1028.description: The Family Cafe is the leading source of information, resources, and networking for Floridians with disabilities. It hosts the largest statewide cross-disability event in the nation, The Annual Family Café, which connects attendees with resources and strategies they need to thrive in their communities. It also provides a platform for state agencies and policy makers to connect with the citizens they serve. The Family Café additionally promotes leadership among youth with disabilities through its Florida Youth Council and supports the development of local family organizations through a Family-Run Organization Movement initiative. This will allow for Floridians to access the connections, resources, and natural supports that The Annual Family Cafe offers on a local level throughout the year. This specific project will support the 29th Annual Family Cafe in June 2027, Florida Youth Council a
1028.purpose: The requested funding will allow The Family Cafe to support and promote the self-sufficiency and wellbeing of Floridians with disabilities. Funds will allow The Family Café to connect Floridians with disabilities and their families with information, resources, and networking opportunities, both through The Annual Family Café event, and on a regular basis throughout the year. The Annual Family Café will connect families with peers, commercial service providers, and public entities to find out wha
1028.activities: The primary activity that will be funded through this request is the 29th Annual Family Café. This three-day event will include approximately 200 breakout sessions; a series of keynote events; The Annual Summit on Disabilities, where attendees can interact with the elected officials and the State Agencies that serve them; and an Exhibit Hall, with a range of providers, partner organizations and private vendors on hand to showcase their services and products for individuals with disabilities. Fun
1028.direct_services: The bulk of the direct service provided by The Family Café comes in the form of training and resource provision through 26.5 hours of total training activity at The Annual Family Cafe as well as training through the Annual Youth Summit. The project also provides direct service to family leaders engaged in the Family-Run Organization Movement through on-site training and assistance in their communi
1028.population: The Family Café primarily serves K-12 students with disabilities or special health care needs and their families. It is also open to other Floridians with disabilities, including transition-age youth. The 27th Annual Cafe in June, 2025 hosted over 14,607 attendees.
1028.outcome: The Family Café makes individuals with disabilities better equipped to flourish in the community. The project will lead to informed families better able to identify resources, engaged youth disability leaders able to lead their peers in transition to independence, and a network of local family-run organizations able to support Floridians with disabilities where they live. The Family Café collects data regarding satisfaction with The Annual Family Café through a survey tool known as the "Report Card.” It offers a means to provide both objective and subjective feedback about the event. A similar survey tool is used to assess the efficacy of the Annual Youth Summit.

2307.description: The State Science and Engineering Fair (SSEF) of Florida – STEM Competition was authorized by the 1957 legislature who authorized the Florida Foundation for Future Scientists (FFFS), non-profit 501c3, to discover scientific and technical talent in the schools of Florida and to encourage the pursuit of careers in STEM. In meeting this obligation, the FFFS has administered the SSEF of Florida for more than 70 years. More than 900 of Florida’s most outstanding middle and high school students advance to this prestigious event after competing in one of 37 affiliated regional science fairs representing all 67 Districts. The SSEF is proudly affiliated with the International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) through the Society for Science, connecting Florida’s young innovators to the global stage. We consider ourselves a contributor to the STEM talent pipeline of Florida's developing technica
2307.purpose: The purpose of the requested funding is to support the continuation of the State Science and Engineering Fair of Florida (SSEF-Florida) beyond the fiscal year 2025-26. The SSEF-Florida has been conducted annually since 1957. The project impacts thousands of students in grades 6-12 who want to do experimental STEM research. Without these funds, we will no longer be able to continue holding the annual event that spans more than 9 months, and involves thousands of hours of dedicated adult volunteer
2307.activities: The SSEF will continue beyond June 2026 in preparation for the event in March 2027. In addition, members of the Board will seek to identify Corporate support so that SSEF can be conducted without legislative support. Effort will be made to develop platforms that will make the operations for the SSEF-Florida to be made more efficient.
2307.direct_services: The citizens of Florida will be able to continue to support the State showcasing of students in STEM Experimental Research. Student participants at SSEF will agree that Floridians appreciate their efforts, just like the achievements of student athletes who compete in State Finals! The citizens will have access to the results of the studies designed to determine the impact of science fair on studen
2307.population: The target population is the students and their teachers in grades 6 - 12 in all 67 districts and their schools (public, charter, private, home, virtual, etc.). There are 37 affiliated regional science fairs representing all districts geographically in the state of Florida. It is expected that 15,000 students and their teachers will be involved in pre- collegiate independent STEM research study eligible to compete at a school, regional, state, and/or national/international science fair.
2307.outcome: It is expected that the SSEF of Florida will increase teacher and student participation in independent STEM research and compete in their school and regional fairs and become winners for the state and international competitions. The SSEF will be able to provide data regarding participation and awards received at all levels of competition with a comparison to other years. Results from an ongoing longitudinal study regarding the impact of the SSEF STEM research on student learning and achievement.

1135.description: After School All Stars (ASAS), our mission is to empower students with the tools they need to thrive both in school and in life. We provide high-quality, year-round academic and enrichment programs—at no cost to families—serving more than11,000 students across Broward, Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, and Orange Counties. By leveraging existing public- school spaces, we maximize resources and direct funding where it matters most: on the students themselves. Our comprehensive out-of-school time services offer rigorous academic support, wellness programs, enrichment activities, and workforce training, ensuring that every student is equipped to succeed.
1135.purpose: To support underserved communities in Broward, Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, and Orange counties, ensuring the continuation of vital programming and services in the areas of academics, health and wellness, enrichment, leadership and workforce training. Our programs are designed to keep students safe and supervised during out-of-school hours while fostering their success both academically and in life. This funding request is essential for the continuation and expansion of our high-quality programs.
1135.activities: The following programs will be provided: Youth employment training and placement services, college preparation classes including test preparation, comprehensive academic programs that support and enhance in-school learning such as intensive tutoring and credit recovery. Programming also includes core comprehensive curriculum such as academic enrichment activities, leadership initiatives and health/wellness programs.
1135.direct_services: Our organization provides direct services to citizens in the following key areas: 1) Workforce Development: Through strategic partnerships with local businesses and community leaders, we enhance youth workforce skills via our Opportunity Jobs Academy, preparing young people for success in the workforce. 2) Community and Neighborhood Safety: ASAS programs play a vital role in keeping youth safe and
1135.population: The target population is K-12 public/charter school students in Broward, Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, and Orange counties.
1135.outcome: 1) Improved On-Time Grade Promotion and Graduation Rates: Our programs are designed to foster academic success, leading to higher rates of grade promotion and graduation. 2) Enhanced School Day Attendance: By engaging students during out-of-school hours, we encourage consistent school attendance and active participation in their education. 3)Grow Youth Workforce Training and Employment by increasing student participation in workforce training to expand employment opportunities. 4) Improved Health and Wellness by offering programs that contribute to their long-term wellbeing.

1904.description: The Town of Windermere seeks funding for design and planning to upgrade the existing outmoded roundabout at 6th Avenue and Main Street. Adding additional lanes will improve traffic capacity, reduce congestion, and enhance overall safety. Both Main Street and 6th Avenue are operating at more than 75% over their designed capacity, resulting in daily backups and delays during peak hours. The project will expand entry and exit lanes, update pavement markings and signage, improve lighting for visibility, and enhance pedestrian crossings. These upgrades will ensure the roundabout can safely accommodate increasing traffic demands while maintaining the Town’s commitment to efficient and reliable transportation infrastructure.
1904.purpose: The requested funds will upgrade the 6th Avenue and Main Street roundabout by adding lanes to improve traffic flow, reduce congestion, and enhance safety. Both Main Street and 6th Avenue are operating more than 75% over their designed capacity, causing daily backups and delays. Upgrades include new pavement markings, signage, lighting, and pedestrian crossings, along with drainage improvements to support stormwater management. These enhancements will increase efficiency, accommodate growing traf
1904.activities: The project will include roadway expansion, resurfacing, and lane additions to improve traffic flow. Activities include installing new pavement markings, upgraded signage, enhanced lighting, and pedestrian crossings for safety. Drainage improvements will support stormwater management. Engineering, design, and construction services will ensure efficient implementation. These upgrades will enhance traffic capacity, reduce congestion, and improve overall safety at the 6th Avenue and Main Street rou
1904.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide citizens with improved traffic flow, reduced congestion, and enhanced safety at the 6th Avenue and Main Street roundabout. Upgraded signage, lighting, and pavement markings will improve navigation and visibility. Pedestrian crossings will ensure safer access for all users. Additionally, drainage improvements will enhance stormwater management, reducing floodi
1904.population: The target population includes Windermere residents, commuters, local businesses, and visitors who travel through the 6th Avenue and Main Street roundabout. This intersection serves as a key access point in the town’s roadway network. The project is expected to benefit thousands of individuals daily by improving traffic flow, safety, and accessibility, ultimately enhancing the overall transportation experience for both motorists and pedestrians in the area.
1904.outcome: These enhancements will increase efficiency, accommodate growing traffic demands and ensure safer access for motorists and pedestrians in the Town of Windermere. Traffic studies.

1039.description: Autism is affecting more of Florida's families than ever before: Today, 1 in 31 children in the U.S. is diagnosed, up from 1 in 150 in 2000. Meanwhile, 85% of autistic adults are unemployed or underemployed. The Bridge to Success (B2S) Program, created by the Boca School for Autism (BSA), provides year-round vocational training and workshops for young adults with autism, through the creation of micro-enterprises. Participants gain skills in product design, customer service, sales, money management, workplace behavior, and self-advocacy, all bolstered by instructors, job coaches, and autism therapy supports. Program funds will also be utilized for transportation to and from on-site job training in the community, with measurable data-driven outcomes that advance independence and employability. BSA is a an award winning institution, co-located in the FAU Research Park, where educators and c
1039.purpose: If awarded, this appropriation will expand the Bridge to Success (B2S) Program at the Boca School for Autism, following a successful pilot. The goal of B2S is to provide year-round vocational training, workshops, entrepreneurship opportunities, and employment pathways for young adults with autism; increase independence; reduce reliance on state services; strengthen Florida's workforce.
1039.activities: The B2S Program will provide vocational training through the creation micro-enterprises in sectors such as food & beverage and hospitality, where participants learn product development, customer service, sales, and financial literacy. The program will also support transportation to job sites, on-the-job training with local employers, workplace coaching, self-advocacy instruction, and specialized entrepreneurship training; program evaluation will track skills gained, employment outcomes, and inde
1039.direct_services: The B2S Program will provide autistic young adults with direct vocational instruction, workshops, job coaching, and workplace readiness training through micro-enterprises and community job placements. Participants will receive hands- on experience, daily coaching, and supported employment opportunities that build independence and prepare them for competitive work.
1039.population: Autism is effecting more of Florida's families than ever before: Today, 1 in 31 children in the United States is diagnosed, up from 1 in 150 in 2000. Meanwhile, 85% of autistic adults are unemployed or underemployed. The target population of the B2S program at the Boca School for Autism is young adults with autism in Palm Beach County and the surrounding areas. Following a successful pilot, the expanded B2S program, if funded, will initially serve 35+ students/year, with the capacity and expecta
1039.outcome: The project will increase employment and independence for autistic young adults by providing year-round vocational training and on-site experience. At least 80% of participants will show measurable gains in workplace readiness, and 50% or more will obtain employment, self-employment, or paid work experience within their first year of program participation. Outcomes will be measured through skill assessments, employment tracking, micro-enterprise revenue, and annual reporting on independence gains.

3574.description: The Lake Clinch Stabilization Project will primarily provide cleaner water to one of Polk County's cleanest lakes. The project involves diverting six stormwater outlets from direct discharge into the lake along Lake Clinch Boulevard to a retention area, reducing sediment and pollutant loading into the city’s public use area and improving overall water quality. Since Hurricane Ian, the park shoreline has experienced significant erosion. While the city received FEMA funds to repair some of the damage, the park’s public use shoreline continues to struggle with ongoing erosion.
3574.purpose: Excessive erosion along the eastern shoreline of Lake Clinch is causing sediment to wash into the lake, which may degrade water quality and impact recreational use of the area. Stabilization of the shoreline is critical to protect the lake.
3574.activities: The erosion appears to be caused but excess stormwater runoff from the east. To address the issue Construction of a curb line along the road and stormwater inlets and pipes to intercept the runoff before it flows down to the Lake; Construction of a stormwater retention pond to attenuate, treat, and control the discharge into the Lake; Paved on- street parking to prevent vehicular traffic on the grass to help maintain the stabilization offered by the grass.
3574.direct_services: The project will directly benefit citizens by improving water quality, reducing shoreline erosion, and enhancing the safety and usability of the Lake Clinch area. Preserve the lake public recreation such as boating, fishing, and swimming. Provide safer, organized on-street parking for visitors. Improve the overall appearance and environmental health of the lakefront area, supporting long-term comm
3574.population: The target population for this project includes residents, visitors, and recreational users of Lake Clinch, as well as property owners along the eastern shoreline. The project is expected to benefit the entire community by improving water quality, shoreline stability, and recreational access. While exact numbers may vary, it is estimated that hundreds of individuals annually will directly benefit from safer, cleaner, and more accessible lakefront areas.
3574.outcome: Expected benefits of this project include reduced shoreline erosion, improved water quality, enhanced recreational opportunities, and increased public safety along the eastern shoreline of Lake Clinch. The outcomes will be measured using the following methodology: Shoreline stability: Periodic surveys and visual inspections of the shoreline to assess erosion reduction and bank restoration effectiveness. Water quality: Monitoring sediment levels, turbidity, and other water quality indicators before and after project implementation. Recreational use and safety: Observations and feedback from lake users regarding accessibility, parking, and overall usability of the lakefront area.

3672.description: PRWC’s mission is to contribute to the survival of native FL wildlife through rescue, rehabilitation and education. PRWC is constructing a $5 million state-of-the-art education center in Punta Gorda to expand educational programming, increase public engagement, and provide greater access for students, families, and visitors. The new facility will allow PRWC to host a more diverse population of wildlife for educational purposes, create interactive learning spaces, and strengthen connections with nearby cultural and tourism destinations. By raising the site elevation and building to hurricane-rated standards, the center ensures the continuity of its education mission even during storms, while providing a safer environment for resident wildlife. We have currently raised $3 million entirely through private donations. State support will help complete this vital project, advancing environmenta
3672.purpose: The requested funds will support the construction and outfitting of Peace River Wildlife Center’s new Education Center, expanding our capacity to deliver environmental education, wildlife conservation programming, and community engagement. The facility will provide dedicated space for interactive exhibits, school and public programs, and volunteer training, reaching thousands more residents, students, and visitors annually. This project strengthens our dual mission of wildlife rehabilitation and
3672.activities: The new Education Center will provide a wide range of programs and services designed to promote environmental education, wildlife conservation, and community engagement. Activities will include interactive educational exhibits, guided tours, school field trips, youth camps, and public presentations focused on Florida’s native wildlife and ecosystems. The Center will also host volunteer training, community workshops, and partnerships with local schools and organizations to expand conservation out
3672.direct_services: The new Education Center will provide direct services to citizens through accessible, hands-on environmental education programs, guided wildlife tours, and interactive exhibits that promote awareness and understanding of Florida’s native species. It will offer school field trips, youth and family learning experiences, and community workshops focused on conservation, habitat protection, and coexist
3672.population: The target population includes residents, students, and visitors of Charlotte County and the greater Southwest Florida region, as well as tourists who visit the area annually. The new Education Center will serve a diverse audience, including K–12 students participating in field trips and school partnerships, families, senior groups, and community organizations seeking environmental education opportunities. With the expanded facility, Peace River Wildlife Center expects to serve more than 80,000
3672.outcome: The expected benefit of the new Education Center is increased public awareness, knowledge, and engagement in wildlife conservation and environmental stewardship across Southwest Florida. By providing interactive exhibits, school programs, guided tours, and community workshops, the project will foster a stronger culture of conservation, inspire responsible behavior toward native wildlife, and support Peace River Wildlife Center’s rehabilitation and education mission. Outcomes will be measured through a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods, including tracking the number of visitors, students, and participants in programs and events; pre- and post-program assessments to evaluate

3531.description: This project supports the City’s recovery from multiple hurricanes and enhances the resilience of its public water infrastructure. Key benefits include: Reliable meter communication during and after hurricanes, even when power is out. Improved storm resilience through sealed, flood-resistant meter assemblies and cellular communication that is not dependent on local relays.
3531.purpose: The City proposes will replace the damaged and outdated mesh AMI system with a modern cellular-based AMI metering system. The new system will allow each meter to transmit usage data directly through secure cellular networks, removing the need for grid powered neighborhood relay points that are easily damaged during storms.
3531.activities: Purchase of new meters and registers as the first phase of a system-wide replacement program.
3531.direct_services: • Improved storm resilience through sealed, flood-resistant meter assemblies and cellular communication that is not dependent on local relays. • Restoration of accurate billing for residents and businesses. • Real-time leak detection and improved water conservation. • Reduced fuel and labor costs associated with manual meter reading. • Improved utility operations and customer service during emerge
3531.population: Punta Gorda Utility Service area serving 47,500 people.
3531.outcome: Resilient accurate water metering. Water meters installed and tested for accuracy.

1437.description: The purpose of this project is to construct an athletic track at Dorsett Stadium in Perry, Fl. The current track at Taylor County High School has deteriorated significantly due to age; rendering it unsafe and unusable for athletic events, physical education classes, and community events. This proposed project will construct a new, regulation grade, all- weather synthetic surface track that meets Florida High School Athletic Association standards for competitive use.
1437.purpose: The funds will be used to construct a new, regulation grade, athletic track with an all-weather synthetic surface. This project will provide a safe, durable, and accessible facility for athletic events, physical education classes, and community use. The goal is to enhance student participation in athletics and expand opportunities for school and community events.
1437.activities: Project activities include the demolition and removal of the existing grass and soil base, installation of a proper drainage and subbase system and construction of a high-quality synthetic track surface that meets Florida High School Athletic Association guidelines. The completed facility will support school athletic practices, physical education instruction, district-level competitions, and community fitness and recreation programs.
1437.direct_services: This project will provide direct access to a safe and modern athletic track for students, staff, and the surrounding community. Citizens will benefit through opportunities for organized youth sports, local athletic events, walking and fitness activities, and community gatherings. The facility will serve as a shared resource promoting health, wellness and engagement across all age groups.
1437.population: The target population is our 997 middle and high school students who participate in athletics, physical education and extracurricular activities. In addition, the estimated number of local youth leagues and community groups annually.
1437.outcome: The expected outcome is a restored, modernized athletic track. Benefits include reduced maintenance costs, increased facility availability for athletics, physical education and community events year round. Outcomes will be measured by: * Completion of project within the project timeline * Number of athletic events successfully hosted on the new surface * User feedback from students, staff and community groups

1438.description: The purpose of this project is to repair, renovate, and strengthen school facilities that sustained significant damage from recent hurricanes, including Hurricane Idalia. Many school buildings suffered roof leaks, water intrusion, HVAC damage, and infrastructure deterioration as a result of storm impact and prolonged exposure to high moisture and wind conditions. These issues have created unsafe and inefficient learning environments, disrupting educational continuity and increasing maintenance demands. By restoring and upgrading these facilities, the district will ensure that students and staff return to a safe, functional, and storm-hardened environment. The project supports the district’s mission to provide uninterrupted, high-quality education and safeguards the community’s investment in public infrastructure by reducing future storm- related repair costs.
1438.purpose: The funds will be used to address critical facility needs, including the repair, renovation, and modernization of aging school infrastructure. The goal is to ensure that all facilities provide safe, efficient, and conducive learning environments for students and staff while meeting health, safety, and accessibility standards.
1438.activities: Project activities include HVAC replacements, plumbing and electrical upgrades, and renovations to classrooms, restrooms, and common areas. Funds will also support safety enhancements such as security systems, lighting upgrades, and emergency preparedness infrastructure improvements.
1438.direct_services: This project will directly benefit students, teachers, and community members by ensuring school facilities are safe, functional, and welcoming environments. Citizens will also benefit through improved access to community-use spaces such as auditoriums, athletic facilities, and meeting areas, supporting broader civic engagement and wellness initiatives.
1438.population: The target population includes approximately 2300 students and 403 total staff members who utilize the facilities for educational, recreational, and civic activities annually.
1438.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved building safety and energy efficiency, reduced maintenance costs, and enhanced learning and working conditions. Success will be measured by facility inspection reports, maintenance cost reductions, stakeholder surveys, and compliance with updated safety and accessibility standards.

1440.description: The Quincy Fire Department (QFD) seeks funding to purchase a new pumper engine. The QFD is in dire need of a new pumper engine with a water capacity of at least 1,500 – 2,000 gallons. Currently, the QFD has two existing pumper engines that are over 20 years old (2002 and 2003) and are constantly in need of repairs which includes not holding needed air pressure. The health and safety concerns for citizens in both Quincy and Gadsden County are of utmost importance. A new fire truck will benefit not only the citizens of the City of Quincy and Gadsden County but will also allow QFD firefighters to be better protected, arrive sooner and be better equipped to handle whatever emergency situations arise.
1440.purpose: The purpose of this funding will be to purchase a new fire engine for the Quincy Fire Department (QFD).
1440.activities: The intended purpose of this funding request is to purchase a new fire engine. This will give the fire department the equipment necessary to answer calls. Quincy is approximately 12 square miles with roughly 8,000 residents. There is a great need for a new truck. In nearly three years the fire department has answered more than 2500 calls.
1440.direct_services: The health and safety concerns for citizens in both the City of Quincy and Gadsden County are of utmost importance. The QFD is in dire need of a new pumper engine with a water capacity of at least 1,500 – 2,000 gallons. The 2 pumper engines we have now are over 20 years old and constantly in need of repairs. One is a 2002 and the other is a 2003. Constant issues with these include not holding need
1440.population: The target population served is expected to be the entire City of Quincy along with supporting neighboring communities with fire service needs.
1440.outcome: The funding outcome can be measured by the number of calls responded to and the length of time it takes to arrive to the calls.

1442.description: The proposed project includes upgrades to the City’s electric substation, located on South Stewart St, which feeds power throughout the City. The substation is currently comprised of antiquated and potentially dangerous components, leaving the citizens of Quincy vulnerable to prolonged outages and endangering workers. The proposed improvements will replace these components, mitigating these risks.
1442.purpose: The proposed project will prevent power outages and will mitigate risk that may be an endangerment to citizens and workers.
1442.activities: Perform a complete battery of tests for the transformer (built in 1990), replace all gaskets, and have it painted, Replace the existing 69 kV circuit switcher with a 69 kV circuit breaker already purchased, Install new 69 kV hookstick switches on the voltage side steel structure, and Install refurbed control building for all relay and control equipment.
1442.direct_services: The substation is currently comprised of antiquated and potentially dangerous components, leaving the citizens of Quincy vulnerable to prolonged outages and endangering workers. The proposed improvements will replace these components, mitigating these risks.
1442.population: The entire city will be impacted by funding to upgrade the electric substation.
1442.outcome: The expected outcome will be a reduction in loss of power for long periods of time through out the service area. This can be measured by pulling an outage report and it being better than past years in the length of time of the power outage.

1331.description: Lift Stations (19,24 & 31) are critical infrastructure of the City's sewer system. Since they were originally constructed, the number of customers both residential and commercial has grown. Lift Stations (19,24 & 31) helps to pump sewage for a number of industrial and commercial buildings, and residential neighborhoods along subdivision cimmunitets and SR 35. The increased sewage flows around the City have resulted in a need to rehabilitate the lift stations to keep up with the demand and replace the run-down components of the station. If these critical lift stations are not rehabilitated, it will result in sewer backups and spillage which would result in a risk to the public health.
1331.purpose: Pump Station (19, 24 & 31) will continue to function as they should and extend the life of those stations as well as all pump stations and sewer lines along the way to the City's Wastewater Treatment Plant.
1331.activities: A contractor will be hired to complete a rehabilitation of the three sewer pump station.
1331.direct_services: Customers will continue to be provided with sewer services with less risk of sewer backups and potential sewer spillage. Increase reliability.
1331.population: All customers who have city utilities and citizens of the city. This will serve approximately 8,000 people.
1331.outcome: The outcome of this project will extend the life of the pump stations and other lines in the city. The outcome is measured by the completion of the project.

1332.description: The City of Belleview is experiencing tremendous growth, which requires larger capacity lines. The City needs additional infrastructure between the Water Treatment Facilities and existing lines to best serve new commercial and residential development. The City will have better pressure and consistency in all water lines. The additional line will help provide fire flow for a potential Big Box store on US 441.
1332.purpose: There has been massive growth in the City of Belleview, new commercial and residential developments are in various stages of planning and building. The construction of this water main will allow this growth to continue without causing issues with capacity and fire flows in the current line, The looping of our system provides reliability and less stress on the exisitng system.
1332.activities: The construction of a 20"/12" water main from SE 119th Street to US Hwy 441 which will eliminate a dead end line and provide better pressure, fire flows and services to citizens and businesses.The additional line will help provide fire flow for a potential Big Box store on US 441.
1332.direct_services: The citizens will receive a more efficient water system. The current water mains If these lines reach capacity new customers cannot be added and there is potential for frequent repairs and road closures to rectify any issues on the aging lines that are currently serving those areas. This may cause traffic issues as US Hwy 441 and US 301 are main thoroughfares serving Marion County, Ocala, Bellevie
1332.population: The City of Belleview serves approximately 8,000 people in the area with water services and approximately 75,000 people driving through Belleview each day on US Hwy 441 and US 301.
1332.outcome: Provide a new water main to relieve capacity issues and fire flows in surrounding lines and create a more efficient system. This will be measured by the completion of the project.

1174.organization: Community Haven for Adults and Children
1174.description: The proposed community center would provide people with developmental disabilities a safe, accessible facility designed to promote independence, social inclusion, and skill development. It offers adaptive recreational programs, vocational training, health and wellness services, cultural activities, and a hurricane shelter. The center fosters community engagement, supports physical and mental health, and provides resources tailored to individual needs.
1174.purpose: A community center on The Haven's 32-acre campus would provide hundreds of people with developmental disabilities a hub that supports the social, educational, recreational, and personal development needs of its participants. Its role is both practical and empowering—designed to help individuals live safe, fuller, more connected, and more independent lives.
1174.activities: Activities and services provided include: Social Inclusion and Connection; Development of Practical and Vocational Skills; Improvement of Health and Well-Being; Empowerment and Advocacy; Family and Caregiver Support; Community Integration; Serve as a Special Needs Hurricane Shelter; A Theater for Creative Expression and Performance.
1174.direct_services: Direct services include life skills training, job readiness & vocational support, social & communication development, recreational & creative programs, educational & cognitive support, mental health & emotional wellness, health & nutrition education, self-advocacy & rights education, family & caregiver resource education, fine arts programs, emergency shelter.
1174.population: Developmentally disabled, Elderly persons, Persons with poor mental health, Persons with poor physical health, Jobless persons, Economically disadvantaged persons, Physically disabled, Preschool students, Grade school students, High school students. Greater than 800 persons are expected to be impacted by services.
1174.outcome: Benefits include enhancing skill development and independence, improving mental and emotional well-being, providing access to tailored resources and support, and offering relief and assistance to families and caregivers. Additionally, incorporating facilities such as a hurricane shelter ensures a safe, accessible space during emergencies, addressing a critical need for safety and security within this vulnerable population. Offering performing arts programs further enriches the centers impact by promoting creativity, self-expression, and confidence, while also providing enjoyable social and therapeutic activities. Methodology to measure outcomes would include use pre- and post- assessments, s

1443.description: ZeroEyes is the industry's leading AI-based weapons detection solution. The software integrates into existing security and surveillance camera systems and sends out a series of alerts when a verified gun is detected via our best-in-class weapons detection algorithms. The ZeroEyes platform is the most proactive and actionable early-warning system on the market, allowing users to "Save time, save lives". ZeroEyes will partner with Florida schools to deploy gun detection software on existing camera infrastructure across the State of Florida to mitigate gun violence.
1443.purpose: The additional funds will allow ZeroEyes to double the number of cameras monitored for guns on campus - creating a safer school environment.
1443.activities: ZeroEyes will add server capacity and begin monitoring double the amount of cameras across the district for brandished firearms, and providing 24/7 human verification monitoring, troubleshooting / maintenance, quarterly software updates.
1443.direct_services: Citizens with children enrolled in the district will benefit with the added layer of protection at their kid's schools, while also making the schools not appear like a heavily guarded facility because the software layer sits on top of the already existing camera infrastructure.
1443.population: The target population includes students, teachers, and staff that work and learn within the district.
1443.outcome: To measure the effectiveness of the ZeroEyes deployment, ZE shall submit a report on the number of guns detected and verified on campus.
