1716.description: Ruth Eckerd Hall serves as a critical partner in public safety, functioning as an emergency command and housing center, hosting disaster preparedness initiatives and supporting law enforcement, and emergency response training. State funding will harden the facility against hurricanes and security threats, ensuring it can continue serving both the community and first responders.
1716.purpose: Ruth Eckerd Hall is a critical public-safety partner, serving as an emergency command and housing center, hosting disaster-preparedness initiatives, and supporting law-enforcement and emergency-response training. The requested funds will replace and upgrade the outdated fire-alarm and HVAC systems and install hurricane-rated glass to protect the public and keep the building safe, code-compliant, and fully operational year-round for both public events and emergency use when crises occur.
1716.activities: Funds will harden Ruth Eckerd Hall so it can function reliably as an emergency command & housing center by upgrading HVAC for operation during outages, replacing the outdated fire-alarm system to be code-compliant, and installing hurricane-rated glass to protect occupants and infrastructure and ensure the building remains usable for law- enforcement and emergency-management trainings.
1716.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from a safe, compliant, and storm-resilient facility during emergencies, including disaster- preparation activities by public-safety agencies. Upgrades also ensure fire safety code-compliance and a secure facility for over 300 performances serving 458,000 patrons.
1716.population: The facility will be secured against future flooding and hurricane force wind damage and potential security threats for use by first responders, community partners and 458,000 patrons from local, national, and international markets who attend Ruth Eckerd Hall events annually and contribute an estimated $144 million in economic activity to the community, including state and local tax collections.
1716.outcome: A safe, code-compliant, storm-resilient facility that can remain open for both cultural use and emergency command/housing. Outcomes will be measured by the number of emergency activations supported, number of trainings hosted, and annual patron and economic impact realized.

1030.description: The Homeownership Opportunity Initiative (HOI) is dedicated to expanding access to homeownership in Central Florida by empowering 200 new homeowner households. Through policy reform, affordable home construction, and comprehensive home-buyer preparation—including financial literacy, counseling, down payment assistance, and coaching—HOI promotes housing stability, builds financial strength, and creates lasting positive impact across the region. The ultimate goal is to implement a regional model that will be replicated statewide upon demonstrated success.
1030.purpose: The funds requested will be used to expand sustainable homeownership opportunities across Central Florida by preparing households for homeownership, increasing the supply of attainable homes, and removing barriers through policy and system change. Specifically, funds will support home-buyer education, individualized coaching, and down payment assistance; strengthen partnerships with builders and developers to create starter homes; and advance policy solutions that make affordable homeownership m
1030.activities: Participants will complete assessments to identify their home-buying needs and be paired with Coaches who guide them, connect them to resources, and provide support. Builders and developers will create starter homes to meet Central Florida's housing demand, while policy recommendations promote innovative, affordable homeownership solutions and remove barriers to owners.
1030.direct_services: Personalized support, offering Housing Counseling and Credit Repair services tailored to participants' needs. Additionally, informational and educational events will empower residents to grasp the initiative, inquire, and navigate the process, further underscoring its impact. Event-related expenses, including marketing, printing, etc. are accounted for as direct service costs.
1030.population: The target population for the Homeownership Opportunity Initiative is first-time home-buyers in Central Florida who are ready or near-ready to purchase a home but face financial and procedural barriers to ownership. The initiative will serve approximately 200 individuals and families annually, providing home-buyer readiness services, guidance, and pathways to affordable homeownership opportunities.
1030.outcome: The Homeownership Opportunity Initiative will expand access to stable, affordable homeownership, strengthen families' financial stability, and support community revitalization across Central Florida. Expected outcomes include increased rates of sustainable homeownership, improved housing stability, and enhanced economic mobility for participating households. Methodology for Measuring Outcomes: Progress will be measured through quantitative and qualitative data collection, including: Number of participants completing homeownership readiness programs. Number of households purchasing homes through the initiative. Number of new attainable homes built or renovated. Tracking participant financial

2424.description: To provide an Evacuation Route that will improve the evacuation times for the City of Cape Coral and Lee County. The project will relieve traffic congestion and provide a missing east-west transportation connection in this area of Lee and Charlotte counties.
2424.purpose: To provide an Evacuation Route that will improve the evacuation times for the City of Cape Coral and Lee County. The project will relieve traffic congestion and provide a missing east-west transportation connection in the area of Lee and Charlotte counties.
2424.activities: Interchange Justification Report; Project Development and Environment Study.
2424.direct_services: Citizens will be provided a new interchange which will alleviate congestion along SR31, SR78, SR80.
2424.population: This project will serve residents of Cape Coral, Lee and Charlotte Counties; roughly 1M in combined population.
2424.outcome: To provide an Evacuation Route that will improve the evacuation times for the City of Cape Coral and Lee County. The project will relieve traffic congestion and provide a missing east- west transportation connection in this area of North Lee and South Charlotte counties. The outcomes will be measured by improved evacuation times and reduced daily travel times.

2857.description: Pinellas County is currently embarking on a $6 M multi-shelter mitigation project, utilizing local funding to harden local schools to maintain and increase sheltering capacity. Two of the sites that are used for special needs residents also need new generators to be able to support basic electrical needs and expand capacity at these locations. Pinellas County is seeking additional funding from the state to support the purchase and installation of two generators to complete the shelter mitigation project. In coordination with the Florida Department of Health – Pinellas County and the Pinellas County School Board, Pinellas County will properly assess and configure each generator to expand uninterrupted electrical service for durable medical equipment, the HVAC system, emergency lighting and cooking facilities at each school. It is estimated that we will need 1.6 megawatt generators or larg
2857.purpose: This Funding will complete our mitigation efforts by providing critical life-sustaining backup power systems for two Special Needs risk shelters. This will provide suitable locations for our approximately 3,000 special needs registrants to maintain the electrical outlets for medical equipment, emergency lighting, the HVAC system, and cooking facilities at each school even when widespread power outages occur .
2857.activities: This will provide uninterrupted power at special needs risk shelters for hurricanes as well as the electrical outlets for medical equipment, emergency lighting, the HVAC system, and cooking facilities at each location even when widespread power outages occur.
2857.direct_services: This will provide uninterrupted power to the electrical outlets for medical equipment, emergency lighting, the HVAC system, and cooking facilities at each location even when widespread power outages occur. This will ensure compliance with state statute, requiring the County to provide risk shelters for special needs populations .
2857.population: Very vulnerable residents who have medical conditions that require equipment to run on electricity. These sites are utilized during hurricane evacuations to provide a safe refuge for those who are at risk due to storm surge and high winds. Our registry currently has approximately 3,000 people.
2857.outcome: This will save lives for medically vulnerable residents by providing a safe option for those people seeking refuge during a hurricane. This can be measured by the number of people who seek shelter and a reduction in indirect storm related deaths, reduced 911 calls, and emergency evacuations after a storm.

2467.description: The Gulfport Senior Center is Gulfport’s trusted leader in providing senior services that empower older adults to live life to the fullest. Many engaged citizens use this facility but the current building is not optimized to provide the needed services. This improvement proposes remodeling and expansion to continue and expand upon the opportunities afforded to the Senior Citizens of Gulfport.
2467.purpose: To improve resources to the senior citizen community.
2467.activities: Design, permitting and infrastructure construction services.
2467.direct_services: Educational, occupational and general interest offerings can be expanded with the additional room.
2467.population: Citywide benefits will be realized through a more engaged senior population.
2467.outcome: Longer lifespans and greater community engagement for senior citizens

2469.organization: Tampa Bay Workforce Alliance, Inc. dba
2469.description: CareerSource Tampa Bay (CSTB) is requesting $1.5 million to invest in a project that provides enhanced training, employment, and supportive services to a minimum of 125 local veterans, transitioning service members, and eligible spouses. The need for services in our community is evident, especially due to the recent hurricanes in the Hillsborough/Pinellas area and the veterans who were displaced from their homes. This additional funding is necessary to fill funding gaps and meet the unique needs of the military community, with a focus on supportive services to veterans with barriers to employment, such as the homeless, disabled, and women veterans, who may have limited access to traditional funding from federal programs. In the previous program year, CSTB served 2,741 veterans, 521 of which faced significant barriers to employment.
2469.purpose: Prior to Hurricanes Helene and Milton impacting the Tampa Bay region during a two-week span in 2024, many veterans were already living in unstable conditions, including homelessness or temporary housing. Funding this program will provide training, employment, and supportive services to a minimum of 125 Hillsborough and Pinellas County veterans, transitioning service members, and eligible spouses with barriers to employment to assist with obtaining or retaining employment, and promoting to a high
2469.activities: Training, employment, and supportive services to veterans, transitioning service members and eligible spouses targeted to meet the unique needs of the military community, with a focus on offering comprehensive supportive services to subgroups with barriers to employment such as homeless, disabled and women veterans, that may have limited access to traditional funding from programs like the federal Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA).
2469.direct_services: Training, employment, and supportive services to veterans, including participant wages during work-based learning experience; supportive services to address barriers to employment, such as childcare stipends, transportation assistance that will enable participants to fully participate in the program and support in their transition to employment; training and education services; and certification c
2469.population: -Veterans, transitioning service members, and eligible spouses. This includes individuals within this population with barriers to employment, such as homeless, economically disadvantaged, jobless, physically disabled, and justice- involved or formerly incarcerated individuals. -125 individuals, with expected sustainability of the program through integration with existing and planned veteran services initiatives.
2469.outcome: The following benefits and outcomes are anticipated: 1) Increase in the number of individuals who enroll in, complete and earn an industry-recognized credential for their selected training program; 2) Increase in the number of individuals who obtain or retain employment, including a position change or wage increase; 3) Increase in the number of individuals who increase their financial security and economic self-sufficiency; 4) Decrease in the number of individuals participating in public assistance programs such as the Welfare Transition Program. Outcomes will be measured by participant surveys and employment and education data, such as training completion and credential attainment, wage rat

2470.description: These funds will be used to harden a gymnasium for utilization as a hurricane risk and step down shelter. This hurricane rated facility with backup generation would expand our current capacity and provide a non-public school facility. This facility services an identified community redevelopment area in one of the poorest areas of the county, and on a day to day basis serves as a school, daycare, and neighborhood community center that is host to many activities and events. On the same campus, Pinellas County has a building fortified with a generator and, through a donation from Duke Energy, the County has built out a kitchen to help support limited sheltering operations
2470.purpose: This funding will increase risk and step down sheltering options for Pinellas County. As a non public school option, this option is ideal for using for smaller storms. Step down sheltering can last for months after a hurricane makes landfall and when schools need to remain operational. This will allow Pinellas to support evacuees before the storm, get public schools reopened quickly, and have a location for disaster survivors to stay temporarily.
2470.activities: Mitigation of the existing facility that can be utilized to serve the community on a daily basis as well as provide for a location for disaster sheltering and supportive services.
2470.direct_services: Risk sheltering during hurricanes, step down sheltering after hurricanes, feeding location, center for disaster recovery services, utilization for community outreach and education for disasters. Distribution site for emergency supplies and services. This site serves as a year-round community center for one of our poorest areas and will be able to expand the daily services provided by partners.
2470.population: The majority of these funds will be directed to these target populations: elderly persons, persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, homeless, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, grade school students, special needs populations, and people who needed to evacuate their homes due to risk or displacement.
2470.outcome: Increased risk sheltering and step down shelter locations and capacity with generator back up. This will reduce the number of days that public schools are used as shelters. Outcomes will be measured by the number of people able to shelter at this location during and/or after a storm. Number of people able to be served post-disaster from this location with supportive services such as mass feeding, distribution of goods and services. Decreased number of days public schools are impacted by serving as a shelter.

2471.description: This project will allow for the construction of the final 2 (out of 10) multi-purpose fields and ancillary facilities (restrooms, concession building, storage, etc.) at the Seminole Junior Warhawks youth sports facility as conceptualized in the County's Unincorporated Seminole Youth Sports Facilities Master Plan. The request will supplement designated Penny for Pinellas capital dollars appropriated for the project as part of the County's CIP program. Once completed, the facility will serve over 2,500 area youth engaged in soccer, lacrosse, and flag football.
2471.purpose: The requested funds will supplement County funds, allowing for the construction of the final 2 (out of 10) multi-purpose fields which will be used for youth soccer, lacrosse and flag football practices, games, and tournaments. Current facilities are inadequate and do not provide sufficient parking, field space, and amenities for concessions, restrooms, etc.
2471.activities: Sports leagues are provided through non-profit program providers under the direction of the Unincorporated Seminole Sports Association, which is the County's designated operating organization created by a special district municipal services taxing unit (MSTU). Construction of the new facilities will be overseen by the County's Public Works Engineering Division and the Parks and Conservation Resources Department.
2471.direct_services: Enhanced youth sports participation, safer facilities, and sports tourism through the construction of new fields and ancillary facilities.
2471.population: The target population is boys and girls ages 3 to 17 interested in participating in youth sports leagues. The facility is expected to serve 2,500+ youth over the course of each year.
2471.outcome: Youth sports facilities and associated programs are shown to increase physical and mental health for youth, provide social engagement, improve player safety, and instill community pride. Outcomes will be measured through participant surveys, increased program registration, and community conversations.

1447.description: The proposed project received half of the needed funding in the last legislative session. However, the City has experienced system failures at this site due to its conditions. If the project is funded in whole, it will ensure that during normal activity usage and during power outages, the system will continue to function as designed. As a result, no contaminants will be released into the surrounding areas. The lift station is located in the Mosquito Creek basin area which flows into the Apalachicola River.
1447.purpose: The City has been experiencing system failures at this site due to its conditions. If the project is funded, it will ensure that during normal activity usage and during power outages, the system will continue to function as designed.
1447.activities: The completion of the lift station rehab project will be concluded with the requested funds.
1447.direct_services: With the completed project, citizens can rely on a functional and dependable sewer system to meet their daily needs.
1447.outcome: The outcome will ensure that this lift station remains in working order.

1448.description: The intent of this request is to upgrade an existing building to serve as an emergency command center and City Hall for the City of Chattahoochee. Upgrades would include, but not limited to, new storm protective windows and doors, new generator with connection, minor room reconfigurations to accommodate meeting areas, HVAC upgrades, new electrical/communication hardware, roof inspection and repairs if warranted, and upgraded carpet, paint, and fixtures.
1448.purpose: The goal of this project is to provide the City a safe and updated emergency command center for the police department, fire department, and City Council as well as an updated City Hall for the citizens of Chattahoochee.
1448.activities: An existing building will be renovated to meet the desired needs of an emergency command center and City Hall.
1448.direct_services: The City currently does not have an emergency command center and the existing City Hall is antiquated and is too small to serve the basic needs of the City. Therefore, this project would provide the citizens with a larger, more convenient City Hall and the Command Center would provide the necessary equipment for the police chief, fire chief, and City officials.
1448.population: The target population to be served is all the residents of the City of Chattahoochee and the surrounding rural Gadsden County residents.
1448.outcome: The expected outcome of this project would be to provide the citizens of Chattahoochee with a newer, larger, and more convenient City Hall and provide a new age command center for the police chief, fire chief, and City officials during a time of emergency.

1075.description: The project involves the design and construction of a new public works building for the City of Anna Maria. The facility will serve as the central operations hub for essential municipal services, including infrastructure maintenance, stormwater management, sanitation coordination, fleet and equipment storage, and emergency response operations. The new structure will replace an inadequate, and significantly damaged from the 2024 hurricanes, existing facility and provide a safe, efficient, and hurricane-resistant space that meets current building and safety standards. This investment will strengthen the city’s ability to maintain public infrastructure, improve emergency preparedness, and ensure continuity of essential services for residents, businesses, and visitors.
1075.purpose: The requested funds will support the construction of a new public works building to replace the existing facility that is currently not secured nor hardened from natural disaster damage in a coastal city. The project’s goal is to restore essential city operations, including infrastructure maintenance, stormwater management, sanitation, and emergency response, in a safe, hurricane-resistant facility ensuring service continuity and community resilience.
1075.activities: Funds will support design, engineering, permitting, and construction of a new public works building to replace the current facility. The hardened building will provide space for infrastructure maintenance, stormwater management, sanitation operations, fleet services, and emergency response coordination, ensuring continuity of essential public services.
1075.direct_services: The project will restore and improve essential public works services for citizens, including road and stormwater maintenance, sanitation, facility repair, fleet management, and emergency response operations. The new building will enable the city to deliver these services safely, efficiently, and without interruption during emergencies.
1075.population: The target population served by this project includes all residents, businesses, and visitors within the City of Anna Maria, as the public works department provides essential services that maintain public safety, infrastructure, and community operations. The new public works building will directly support approximately 900 year-round residents and benefit an estimated 8,000 to 10,000 seasonal visitors and tourists annually through improved maintenance, stormwater management, sanitation, and emer
1075.outcome: The project will provide a modern, resilient public works building to improve infrastructure maintenance, sanitation, stormwater management, and emergency response. Outcomes will be measured by reduced response times, improved service efficiency, compliance with safety standards, and decreased operational downtime during storm events.

1449.description: The proposed project will include replacing the existing forcemain along Congo Road to Bethel Road, (950 LF) and along Bethel Road to Lincoln Drive ( 800 LF). The Watermain will be replaced down A & E Road and Adolphus McMillian Road. (2,600 LF). Water services, valves, fittings, and restoration services will also be included.
1449.purpose: Project will include replacing the existing forcemain along Congo Road to Bethel Road, (950 LF) and along Bethel Road to Lincoln Drive ( 800 LF). The Watermain will be replaced down A & E Road and Adolphus McMillian Road. (2,600 LF). Water services, valves, fittings, and restoration services will also be included.
1449.activities: Waterlines will be upgraded to new PVC pipe material with new valves and fittings as well as new service lines.
1449.direct_services: Citizens will be provided a cleaner more dependable water system for consumption. Also, with upgraded waterlines, fire flow protection will be increased.
1449.outcome: The outcome will ensure that the system remain operational.

1060.description: In 2017 DAS lost their 25-bed emergency shelter during hurricane Irma. We have purchased a property to be renovated as our new shelter. The requested funds will be used for that renovation. The property will house the emergency shelter, outreach offices and administrative offices. These services will provide domestic violence survivors and their families, including pets, safety from abuse and the ability to move forward successfully with safety and independence.
1060.purpose: Emergency shelter and outreach services which will provide safety to survivors of domestic violence and their families and pets.
1060.activities: Emergency shelter and outreach services which will provide safety to survivors of domestic violence and their families and pets.
1060.direct_services: Domestic violence survivors are citizens, but DV is a criteria for services.
1060.population: Domestic violence survivors, their families and pets.
1060.outcome: A safe, accessible shelter will allow victims to rebuild their lives and services will be provided to help improve self- sufficiency. Monitor use of the shelter, satisfaction surveys and case management notes.

2714.description: Our program is the only one in Florida that serves families of unsolved homicide victims, of which there are at least 20,000 in Florida. We provide awareness for the victims and advocacy for their families. We host a database of cases, provide training for establishing cold case units where they don't exist, and provide consulting with experienced cold case detectives.
2714.purpose: A safer Florida by helping solve cold cases. Fewer survivors requiring state funding assistance due to counseling and resolution in their cases. Added jobs for a better economy. An effort by all to assure public safety but getting criminal off the streets. Healing for families of unsolved homicides.
2714.activities: We will hold trainings, speak at conferences and assist in reviewing cold cases for any and all law enforcement agency in the state. We will provide contracted mental health professionals to help families affected by the loss of a loved one to an unsolved homicide.
2714.direct_services: Raised awareness for their loved ones cases. Fresh eyes on the cases. Individual and group facilitated counseling for healing.
2714.population: Victims of crime - specifically families of unsolved homicide victims. With 20,000 unsolved murders in Florida, and each victim averaging 2-4 survivors we have the potential to assist 40-80 thousand survivors. However, realistically we won't have the staff for all of them and will likely serve well over 1,500.
2714.outcome: Safer communities, better mental health for victims' family members. Added jobs. We continue services to these survivors and track employment and mental health progress.

3339.description: A youth intervention program that meets the targeted needs of Nassau County youth by providing effective diversion and intervention programs which include redirection of youth through community service, mentoring and academic assistance to prevent juvenile delinquency. Program services will be provided to youth who are identified as at-risk of becoming involved in the juvenile justice system and are between the ages of six (6) and eighteen (18).
3339.purpose: Effective diversion and intervention for at-risk youth which includes redirection through community service events and mentoring and tutoring sessions to help prevent juvenile delinquency. Nassau County will contract directly with a program director to provide mentoring and tutoring services. The Nassau County Sheriff's Office will administer the community service events.
3339.activities: This program will provide mentoring and tutoring services as well as supervised community service events for at-risk and probation youth.
3339.direct_services: This program is designed to provide a graduated system of community service hours as well as mentoring and tutoring services for at-risk and probation youth to help in preventing juvenile delinquency.
3339.population: At-risk youth between the ages of six (6) and eighteen (18). Approximately 51-100 youth.
3339.outcome: This program is designed to help improve or build self-esteem, life skills, character development, professional skills, peer-pressure, personal development and leadership skills in order to decrease future/repeat criminal behavior. The tutoring services offered will aid in preventing truancy and assist with academic achievement. Progression of the program services can be tracked along with the number of participants that successfully complete the program. On- going assessments of behavior can also be conducted and tracked. This data can be used to determine the Program's overall success and to generate monthly reports for each participant to determine whether truancy has been reduced and aca

2684.description: Thomas Creek borders between Nassau and Duval Counties. The Watershed is historically plagued within Nassau County for flood damage and many repetitive loss properties. Thomas Creek is also the headwaters of the State of Florida designated Nassau River - St. Johns River Marshes Aquatic Preserve. From 2008 to 2018 the County, in collaboration with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection, executed a de-snagging project at a cost of $3,340,000. The de-snagging project only provided short-term relief. From 2019 to 2022 Nassau County partnered with Us Army Corps of Engineers to execute a Planning Assistance to States (PAS) Study. The findings of the 2-year study were presented to the Nassau County BOCC in June of 2022. The study found the only viable long-term solution was to remove structures from the floodplain and return to lands to their natural state. This project will focus o
2684.purpose: In response to the study, Nassau County developed an Implementation Plan. The plan lays out a fifteen (15) year program with phase one representing the first 5-years of the program. Phase one consists of the acquisition, home demolition, and septic system removal of the most vulnerable properties within the Thomas Creek basin, based the Implementation Plan's ranking. This project not only removes septic tanks from the headwaters of the State of Florida designated Nassau River - St. Johns River M
2684.activities: Demolition of homes, septic, and structures along with reclamation as needed of the floodplain. Nassau County BOCC will also acquire the land to maintain the floodplain in its natural state.
2684.direct_services: Remove homes from the repetitive loss areas.
2684.population: Nassau County citizens specifically residents of the Thomas Creek Watershed in Callahan.
2684.outcome: The benefit is a restored floodplain and mitigation of repetitive loss homes. FEMA's cost benefit analysis will be used for each individual home, but the Planning Assistance to States Study reviewed the outcome in comparison to other structural solutions.

2685.description: The requested funds will enable the Town of Hilliard to extend its potable water distribution system along US Highway 1, Eastwood Road, and Henry Smith Road in partnership with Nassau County. These extensions will expand rural water service capacity, eliminate dependence on private wells, improve fire protection and system redundancy, and strengthen pressure and flow reliability to support residential, commercial, and economic development along the US 1 corridor.
2685.purpose: The requested funds will extend the public water system along US Hwy 1, Eastwood Road, and Henry Smith Road. This will enhance the system’s capacity, provide fire protection, eliminate the need for private wells, and complete a vital loop in the distribution network. The improvements will ensure increased water pressure, enhanced flow reliability, and expanded access to safe drinking water for both new and existing customers, supporting the Town’s growth and development.
2685.activities: The requested funds will expand the Town of Hilliard’s water system southward along US Hwy 1 to support the orderly development of lands along the corridor. The project will provide an expanded water supply for fire suppression, eliminate the need for private well installations, and improve the overall reliability and capacity of the water system to meet the community’s growing needs.
2685.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services through the extension of water mains along US Hwy 1, Eastwood Road, and Henry Smith Road. These extensions will improve the water supply for fire suppression, eliminate the need for private well installations, and enhance overall access to safe drinking water for both new and existing residents.
2685.population: All ˜3,000 residents of the Town of Hilliard and residents of the surrounding Nassau County.
2685.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is the elimination of the need for private well installations and the provision of a reliable water supply for fire suppression. Residents along US Hwy 1, Eastwood Road, and Henry Smith Road will be able to connect to the public water system, gaining access to fire protection and safe drinking water. The outcome will be measured by tracking the number of connections made to the new water system, as well as monitoring the reduction in private well usage and the improved capacity for fire suppression in these areas.

2687.description: High-dosage tutoring has proven to be the most effective form of learning intervention. Research from leading institutions shows that high-dosage tutoring provides the targeted intervention that struggling students need to bridge learning gaps, and that it helps teachers by reinforcing what students learn in class. The funds requested will be used to provide evidence-based high-dosage tutoring for up to 600 K-12 Duval County Public School students. The identified students would receive high-dosage tutoring twice a week in small groups of 5 (1 tutor : 5 students) for 40 weeks during the school year.
2687.purpose: High-dosage tutoring has proven to be the most effective form of learning intervention. The implementation of high- dosage tutoring will help to close learning gaps and accelerate student achievement.
2687.activities: These funds will support evidence-based delivery of high-dosage tutoring to identified students in need of learning intervention. The funds requested will be used to provide tutoring for up to 600 K-12 Duval County Public School students. The identified students would receive high-dosage tutoring twice a week in small groups of 5 (1 tutor : 5 students), for 40 weeks during the school year.
2687.direct_services: These funds will support evidence-based delivery of high-dosage tutoring to identified students in need of learning intervention. The funds requested will be used to provide tutoring for up to 600 K-12 Duval County Public School students. The identified students would receive high-dosage tutoring twice a week in small groups of 5 (1 tutor : 5 students), for 40 weeks during the school year. High-do
2687.population: The target population for high-dosage tutoring is students who are struggling academically, such as in math or reading. Students struggling with learning gaps, those at risk of not meeting grade level benchmarks, or those requiring support for standardized tests are often the populations targeted for high-dosage tutoring.
2687.outcome: High-dosage tutoring (HDT) has proven to be the most effective form of learning intervention. The personalized instruction that HDT delivers accommodates unique student needs, addresses specific learning gaps, and ensures students progress at their own pace. High-dosage tutoring is a proven way to improve student learning outcomes. High-dosage tutoring programs generally include pre- and post-program assessments to measure the effect of the academic intervention.

1450.description: Construction of a new K-12 school in Lafayette County. It will be the only public school in Lafayette County. The school district has not received any construction funding from the state since 1996, and that was to add a gymnasium to the existing school. This new school will also consist of an enhanced hardened area that will serve the community as a storm shelter during weather events.
1450.purpose: The requested funds will allow the district to start construction of a new K-12 school.
1450.activities: This funding will allow the district to start the construction process. Construction is a multi year process and the funding will allow the district to get started without causing delays to this very large project.
1450.direct_services: This project will give all the K-12 students in Lafayette county a clean, safe, secure, and up to date school. It will allow the students in this small county to use current technology and give them the same skills as students that graduate from the larger districts.
1450.population: The target population is K-12 students, but the facility will also consist of enhanced hardened areas that will serve the community as a storm shelter during weather events. At the moment the county does not have an emergency shelter.
1450.outcome: There are many benefits and outcomes associated with this project; some of the most important ones will be a better learning environment, updated technology and classrooms, better school safety measures, higher student achievement scores, and increased student confidence.

1717.description: The project will protect 31 pump stations from future flooding and storm events by elevating the electrical equipment at each sanitary sewer pump station. The 31 pump stations were damaged during Hurricane Helene, and are prone to future damage without mitigation. The electrical equipment that will be replaced and elevated includes the meter can, junction box, disconnect switch, remote telemetry unit, and control panel. The following work will be performed: Equipment will be elevated on a new aluminum platform with stairs; New conduit and wires will feed power to the electrical equipment; New electrical platforms will be installed 4 to 5 feet above existing grade and rated for 145-mph wind loads. Bypass pumping will also be required to maintain flow during the work.
1717.purpose: 1. Mitigate risk of future flooding and bring critical infrastructure into compliance with Section 2 e. of Florida Administrative Code 62-604.400. 2. Invest in infrastructure to protect vulnerable pump stations against the 100-year storm event
1717.activities: The electrical equipment that will be replaced and elevated includes the meter can, junction box, disconnect switch, remote telemetry unit, and control panel. The following work will be performed: Equipment will be elevated on a new aluminum platform with stairs; New conduit and wires will feed power to the electrical equipment; New electrical platforms will be installed 4 to 5 feet above existing grade and rated for 145-mph wind loads. Bypass pumping will also be required to maintain flow durin
1717.direct_services: Pinellas County Utilities customers will receive ongoing, uninterrupted sanitary sewer services, even during major storm events.
1717.population: Target population is Pinellas County Utilities (PCU) customers and visitors. The project will ensure that the over 64,000 residents and visitors in the 8,569 acres of PCU's service area affected by these pumps are less impacted by storm events.
1717.outcome: 1. Mitigate risk of future flooding and bring critical infrastructure into compliance with Section 2 e. of Florida Administrative Code 62-604.400. 2. Invest in infrastructure to protect vulnerable pump stations against the 100-year storm event. Outcomes will be measured by tracking progress as each of the 31 lift stations are improved, protected and elevated. Specific measures will include number of lift stations elevated, number of feet raised above existing grade, and rated for 145 mph winds. Post-project performance metrics will include reduced outages due to storm surges during wet weather events.

1234.description: Fostering Our Future (FOF) is a community-based, church-led partnership designed to increase the number of high- quality foster families while safely reducing the number of children who enter foster care. Through its 100 Churches Initiative, FOF mobilizes, organizes, and equips local churches to care for vulnerable foster children as a compassion ministry of the local church, helping them to recruit, train, and support the foster families within their congregation. State funding in FY 2026-2027 would equip FOF's Initiative to scale up foster care family capacity and wrap around services in Central Florida (Orange, Osceola, and Seminole), East Central Florida (Flagler, Putnam, Volusia, Brevard), as well as immediate surrounding counties when resources bleed over. FOF will continue to fund at scale one-third of its operating costs from local communities.
1234.purpose: The funds will expand the capacity of high-quality foster families in our community. Through our Community of Care model, we will recruit, train, equip, and sustain families who are willing to open their homes to vulnerable children. Unlike traditional strategies, our model has proven more effective - recruiting three foster families for every one brought in through the legacy system. Our process, systems, and tools provide families with more than just training; they offer a full circle of suppo
1234.activities: Expansion of the 100 Churches foster care training initiative in targeted communities in a 7-county region which will provide families with more than just training; we will provide a full circle of support to help parents remain engaged and successful in fostering. In addition, we will grow our volunteer base to strengthen wrap-around support for kinship caregivers and the children they care for.
1234.direct_services: Building on last year's program, professionally managed and trained volunteers provide individual caregiver support and help with respite care, meals, items needed for new foster children entering the home, invitations to regularly scheduled events and trainings, self-growth and improvement sessions.
1234.population: The target population served by this project are foster children and foster/kinship families. Over 2,000 individuals are expected to be served.
1234.outcome: The 100 Churches initiative moves children to permanency faster - whether to family members, their parents, or adoption with a 90% foster parent retention rate with zero cases of substantiated child maltreatment.

1907.description: Bluford Avenue is one of Ocoee’s three primary north–south arterials, a designated evacuation route, and the corridor that serves the City’s Emergency Operations Center, City Hall, and Ocoee Middle School, an emergency shelter during storm events. To date, the City has self-funded $9 million in improvements to over the half-mile of Bluford Avenue. Before the project can be started, existing above ground power needs to be moved underground as part of ongoing resiliency initiatives for the City to serve this critical area and evacuation route
1907.purpose: The Bluford Ave. project brings improved roadway, pedestrian, stormwater and underground utilities to the City of Ocoee downtown area. The requested funds are specifically for moving existing overhead power lines underground, which will provide a more storm resilient corridor while also improving the aesthetics of the downtown area. Bluford Ave. is critical to the City's storm response, as it serves as a designated evacuation route, the City's Emergency Operations Center (EOC), and services an e
1907.activities: Bluford Avenue is one of Ocoee's three primary north-south arterials, a designated evacuation route, and a vital roadway serving both the City's Emergency Operations Center and Ocoee Middle School, which functions as an emergency shelter during storm events.
1907.direct_services: Improved sidewalks and bike lanes in the area serving a middle and elementary school enhance public safety and ensure ADA compliance, which in turn boosts both roadway safety and economic growth. The underground infrastructure improvements also include expansion of the City's reclaimed water and sewer systems to reach a greater portion of the population.
1907.population: Bluford Avenue is the primary roadway connecting the City of Ocoee’s downtown area, serving all approximately 50,000 residents of Ocoee and individuals from surrounding areas.
1907.outcome: The Bluford Avenue Project directly serves the City's downtown area by providing improved and enhanced roadway and underground infrastructure to encourage economic development and investment.

1908.description: This project will be to design backup supply to reclaim and infrastructure improvements to allow for continued operation and expansion of the Ocoee Reclaim system. Ocoee’s reclaim system expansion has far outpaced expectations due to the City's proactive expansion program which includes wholesale agreements for additional supply and retrofits. Ocoee is withdrawing in 3.8 MGD of groundwater and supplying 4 MGD of reclaimed water to customers, with 1 MGD of reclaimed water reservation for future reclaim customers. Recently Orange County changed qualification criteria for wholesale rates by increasing the City's cost per 1,0
1908.purpose: Continue to provide and expand reclaim water services.
1908.population: Ocoee residents and businesses with an estimated service area population of 50,000.
1908.outcome: The City's operation of it's robust reclaimed water system aligns with SJRWMD CFWI groundwater conservation mission. This project allows the City to supply over 4 MGD of reclaim water to the entire service area and also continue to expand the system. Groundwater withdrawals are measured and reported to the St Johns River water management District semiannually. Withdrawals and potential environmental impacts are evaluated as part of the City's Consumptive Use Permit and are also used for Central Florida Water Initiate Regional Water Supply Plan.

2131.description: The proposed project will be used to engage a contractor to construct the drainage improvements as proposed. The proposed Green Stormwater Infrastructure project will install a single subsurface detention system located within the open space of the urban park to alleviate the flooding within the park and the densely populated surrounding community. With nearly all of the City currently in a flood zone and already experiencing flooding from both rain and tidal events, the development of the green stormwater infrastructure to address the immediate needs of the project impact area will be another significant step to decreasing the impacts of floodwater from the homes, businesses, and public facilities that are essential to the community.
2131.purpose: The implantation of green infrastructure below the surface at City Park during its redevelopment represents a cost- effective use of tax dollars by providing significant flood protection for the densely populated area. The built-out urban area does not provide many opportunities for new stormwater infrastructure, much less green infrastructure, to be constructed without significant investment and impact on the daily lives of the community. The proposed project can be incorporated into the site c
2131.activities: The completion of the project will provide stormwater management services to the community. The project will increase drainage capacity, decrease the threat of flooding, and enhance surface water quality before it enters the nearby Middle River and AICW.
2131.direct_services: The project will not provide any direct services to citizens.
2131.population: While construction will take place within the boundaries of the park, the impact on the drainage of the surrounding areas will reach in each direction. The defined project impact area consists of densely populated urban development. On each side of the park, there are multi-unit residential developments, commercial and industrial structures, and even a small number of single-family homes. On the southeast side of the park, a large FPL substation exists. The impact area is a financially disadvant
2131.outcome: The project provides a high cost-benefit due to the large area of the community it will protect. The project benefit area contains hundreds of residences, businesses, and multiple critical facilities. These facilities represent hundreds of millions of dollars in property. The personal safety risk of flooding both during an event and after a major storm cannot be measured. The City will be able to measure the effectiveness of the project by monitoring surface water levels and any flooding that might occur. This will be done as part of the City's stormwater management program. The decrease in flooding events from tidal events and heavy rains will be clearly demonstrated.

1235.organization: Habitat for Humanity of Seminole County and
1235.description: Habitat Seminole-Apopka is respectively requesting funding to support the construction of a development featuring 19 single-family homes for ownership that are affordable, sustainable, and transit-accessible. This initiative aims to create an affordable housing community in Sanford, making efficient use of limited land space. By increasing the availability of homes for lower-income earners, we aim to address the urgent housing needs in the area while also creating jobs during the construction process.
1235.purpose: Create an affordable homeownership development in Sanford that will optimize the use of limited space and will create a small community of affordable homes within .02 miles of a bus route, .02 miles from the Sunrail station, 3.5 miles from a grocery store, and 1.1 miles from a pharmacy. It will also create jobs during the construction process.
1235.activities: The funds will allow us to complete the construction that is needed for the raw land that was purchased to increase the affordable housing stock in Seminole County. During the construction period all future homebuyers will increase their financial stability by participating in the Habitat homebuyer program as indicated by: - increasing their credit scores by at least 100 points - increasing their savings by at least $2,500 - maintaining a debt-to-income ratio below 43%
1235.direct_services: Affordable, sustainable, and transit-accessible homeownership opportunities
1235.population: Completion of a construction project in Seminole County that establish additional affordable housing stock for Seminole County's workforce. 50 - 100 individuals are expected to be served.
1235.outcome: Increasing Sanford's stock of affordable owner-occupied homes. When the construction is completed, the homes will be sold to qualified homebuyers. In addition, this project will create approximately 105 jobs while in the construction phase.

2135.description: The program will provide shared housing and wrap-around services to individuals experiencing homelessness with mental health and or substance use disorders. The program helps reduce street homelessness in Fort Lauderdale, which accounts for nearly half of Broward County’s unsheltered population, and offers a scalable model for Florida. By blending housing with behavioral health services, it not only improves community safety and wellness but also provides a pathway to statewide impact by addressing the root causes of homelessness and creating sustainable routes to recovery and permanent housing.
2135.purpose: Expand the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Treatment Housing Program to address the concentration of unsheltered individuals in the city by integrating both substance use and comprehensive mental health services. The initiative will provide shared housing options alongside wraparound supports - including behavioral health care, psychiatric treatment, case management, substance use stabilization, and recovery support - to promote wellness, reduce homelessness, and create lasting pathways to sta
2135.activities: The funds will support shared-housing placements paired with wrap-around services for individuals experiencing homelessness who have mental health or substance use disorders. Activities and services will include behavioral health assessments, case management, detoxification and residential recovery, linkage to medical, legal, and employment resources, assistance with obtaining identification and benefits, housing navigation to promote long-term stability, and transportation support to ensure acc
2135.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services such as individualized assessments, behavioral health and substance use treatment, shared housing placements, and wrap-around supports including case management, recovery housing, and stabilization services. Participants will also receive assistance in obtaining identification documents, applying for benefits like Social Security and SNAP, acc
2135.population: The target population for this project is adults aged 18 and older experiencing homelessness within the City of Fort Lauderdale, with a focus on individuals facing mental health challenges or substance use disorders. Based on prior outcomes and capacity, the program is expected to serve approximately 120–150 individuals annually through housing placements, treatment services, and comprehensive case management that lead to long-term stability and recovery.
2135.outcome: The expected benefit is a measurable reduction in homelessness among adults with mental health and substance use disorders in Fort Lauderdale through stable housing, treatment, and services that foster recovery, wellness, and long- term self-sufficiency. Outcomes will be measured through program data on individuals housed, retained in housing, or reunified with family; completion rates for treatment and recovery programs; referrals to higher levels of care; and successful connection to benefits and resources.

2136.description: This pilot program will enhance emergency response for students in a Emotional/Behavioral Disability (E/BD) program who are experiencing psychiatric crises by ensuring appropriate medical transport. Minor students under the Baker Act who pose no security risk would be transported from designated Broward County Public Schools by Basic Life Support ambulance instead of a police vehicle. This approach aligns the response with medical needs, reduces unnecessary law enforcement involvement, and allows officers to remain available for public safety duties.
2136.purpose: This program will, among other benefits: 1. Reduce the trauma of youth being transported to a hospital during a psychiatric emergency; 2. Increase the cooperation and understanding of the youth being transported, thereby reducing the risk of escalation or resistance to needed medical care; and 3. Increase police officer availability for public safety.
2136.activities: The use of BLS ambulances instead of traumatic law enforcement transportation. The BLS ambulances also include a trained crisis response team and may provide medical care.
2136.direct_services: Continuity of care for minors via: 1) less traumatic transportation, 2) behavioral health services, supports and outreach and 3) behavioral health prevention services and information and referral services.
2136.population: Minor children enrolled in designated Broward County Public School with Emotional/Behavioral Disability (E/BD) programs. This pilot program is expected to serve up to [X] kids, which could increase to over [X] (over 400 in Hillsborough's program) if implemented County-wide.
2136.outcome: It would reduce the trauma of children during a psychiatric emergency, improving their cooperation and decreasing escalation, which also decreases the likelihood of future involvement with the Juvenile Justice and criminal justice systems. This can be measured by analyzing juvenile justice rates for youth that were transported during a Baker Act. Currently, youth in this program who are experiencing a psychiatric crisis necessitating their transportation to a hospital are relegated to being transported in a police car exacerbating their trauma. It would also reduce the burden of police officers having to provide this transport, so the officers can prioritize their duties to ensuring public s

1044.description: West Miami requests increased funding to expand its Senior Hot Meals Program, serving Miami-Dade registered seniors with nutritious congregate and home-delivered meals. Rising costs and growing demand strain current resources, impacting service quality and reach. Beyond meals, the program provides recreational activities, participant screening, transportation, nutrition education, and staffing support. This cost-effective investment aligns with Florida’s goals to support aging in place, reduce healthcare costs, and enhance quality of life for vulnerable seniors.
1044.purpose: The funds will expand and sustain West Miami's Senior Hot Meals Program, ensuring registered seniors receive daily nutritious meals, transportation, and wellness services. The goal is to eliminate wait lists, improve service quality, and support aging in place for vulnerable older adults.
1044.activities: Funds will support daily hot meal delivery (including holidays), transportation to the Senior Center and recreational outings, nutrition education, wellness screenings, and staffing costs for program coordination and oversight.
1044.direct_services: Direct services include home-delivered and congregate meals, transportation for seniors to activities and health events, recreational programming, nutrition education, and personalized wellness assessments - all coordinated through the city's Senior Center staff with community partners.
1044.population: Senior citizen aged persons in Miami-Dade County near and around the City of West Miami.
1044.outcome: The project will improve senior health, reduce isolation, and increase access to essential services. Outcomes will be measured by tracking meals served, participation rates, satisfaction surveys, and reductions in wait lists for services.

1236.description: The Veteran-Led Space Innovation Program empowers Florida veterans to lead the development and commercialization of cutting-edge space technologies. Through technical training, mentorship, and access to shared equipment and laboratory resources, participants turn innovative concepts into viable products and services. The program fosters collaboration with university tech transfer offices and aerospace industry partners statewide, accelerating technology transfer, creating high-tech jobs, and strengthening Florida's leadership in the space and defense sectors.
1236.purpose: The funds will empower veteran-led technology companies to develop and commercialize space-related innovations through technical training and collaboration with industry and university tech transfer offices statewide, accelerating commercialization and strengthening Florida’s leadership in aerospace and defense innovation.
1236.activities: The program will provide veteran-led companies with technical training, mentorship, and hands-on support to develop and commercialize space-related technologies. Activities include prototype development, access to specialized equipment and labs, and collaboration with university tech transfer offices and industry partners statewide. Additional services include business coaching, investor readiness training, networking events, and public demonstrations to connect veterans with the space ecosystem
1236.direct_services: The program will provide citizens with direct access to innovative space technologies developed by veteran-led companies, including wearable health monitors, telemedicine devices, and rehabilitation tools. Citizens will benefit from public demonstrations, STEM workshops, and community engagement events that showcase these technologies. Additional services include educational outreach, training ses
1236.population: The primary target population is veterans across Florida who are interested in entrepreneurship and technology development, particularly in space and defense sectors. Secondary beneficiaries include Florida citizens who will gain access to space-enabled healthcare innovations and STEM outreach programs. The program also engages industry partners, university tech transfer offices, and research institutions, fostering statewide collaboration that supports veteran entrepreneurs while advancing Flor
1236.outcome: The level of benefit will be measured using quantitative and qualitative metrics focused on space technology and health applications. Metrics include the number of veteran-led prototypes developed, technologies licensed, and companies launched.

2308.description: Expand direct services through mobile and sex-trafficking teams to minors and adults, male and female. Expand ability to provide prevention and education services to school districts and local schools.
2308.purpose: Expand direct mobile anti sex-trafficking services to children and adults, male & female. Expand ability to provide prevention and education services to school districts and local schools.
2308.activities: 24 hour mobile crisis intervention services for at risk or identified children, teens and adult victims of sex trafficking that include counseling, case management and survivor led advocacy and support, as well as prevention and education to various populations to include law enforcement, medical providers, hotel and hospitality industry, community leaders and school districts and educational professionals.
2308.direct_services: The mobile crisis intervention teams provide trauma-informed based practices, client-centered modalities specific to trauma as related to sex trafficking, the mobile unit provides 24 hours a day, 7 days a week services of case management, advocacy, and clinical counseling with a team of a Clinician, Advocate and Survivor Mentor, education and awareness trainings for the community.
2308.population: The funds will serve children and adults who are survivors of sex trafficking and those who are at-risk of being trafficked due to identified vulnerabilities. This may include persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, homeless persons, developmentally disabled persons, drug users (in health services), grade school, high school, and university/college students, currently or formerly incarcerated persons,
2308.outcome: The project will improve physical and mental health, enrich cultural experience, improve quality of education, protect the general public from harm (environmental, criminal, etc.), improve transportation conditions, enhance specific individual's economic self sufficiency, reduce substance abuse, and divert from criminal/juvenile justice system.

2472.description: The Empowered to Change Safe Housing Program delivers a 7 -12 month structured comprehensive program that enhances life-changing support through trauma counseling, employment, and education services while living in a home free from all narcotics, alcohol, or abuse. We are 11 years of serving those who suffer from human trafficking, sex trade, addiction, aging out of foster care, the formerly incarcerated, and/or homelessness.
2472.purpose: The goal is to deliver Safe Housing, employment, education, life skills, accountability, and trauma therapy so that broken individuals have the tools to heal, change their lives, and be productive in our communities.
2472.activities: Psych/social evaluation, specific Independent Living Plan (ILP) goal for each individual, employment coaching and placement, educational support, life skills and coaching, trauma therapy and MRT (Moral Reconation Therapy- evidence based).
2472.direct_services: The direct services provided will include a Safe House to live in, trauma therapy, MRT, life skills, employment/job readiness, GED/College guidance, accountability, and life coaching. We also give food, clothing, and bus passes to any participant who needs them.
2472.population: The target population is the vulnerable in our communities who age out of foster care as they are prime targets for human trafficking, survivors of the sex trade, and individuals who suffer from addictions, homelessness, and mental health issues. We serve 200+ people every year.
2472.outcome: The expected benefit is to provide Safe Hosing ie, zero tolerance for illegal drug activity or violence. There are 125 beds in Pinellas County and 153 beds in Florida for any adult 18 years of age and up to receive a minimum of a 7- month program that teaches them to be gainfully employed. Another benefit is that they are employed between 14 and 30 days into the program. One hundred fifty-three people received life coaching, accountability, random drug testing, and house visits. 111-220 have an opportunity to divert from jail time relating to their trauma, ie, sex trafficking, sexual abuse, addiction, or theft.

2859.description: Established in 1959, the Science Center of Pinellas County was the premier science learning location in the U.S. for decades, serving as many as 22,000 children per year. Reactivating it will enable new generations of Pinellas children and families to immerse themselves in STEM learning while building community connections and enjoying family-friendly programming.
2859.purpose: To provide an opportunity for engaging, hands-on emerging technology and science programs that educate and prepare students for the jobs of tomorrow. While partnering with local educators, schools, universities and government, St. Petersburg Foundation will build a center of excellence for emerging technologies that help St Petersburg, and Florida compete in the new artificial intelligence centered economy.
2859.activities: The additional requested funds will be used to reactivate the Science Center and to get the building located at 7701 22nd Ave N, Saint Petersburg. The facility will include an AI Village serving thousands of students and campers a year, an artificial intelligence center of excellence focused on preparing citizens and our region to compete, working space for A.I. startups, companies and groups. A cutting-edge auditorium made for hybrid events and a digital platform that makes facility curriculum
2859.direct_services: The Science Center will be a space where hands-on, discovery-based learning and STEM enrichment fuel inquisitive minds and enthusiasm for all things science. A place where all children, adults, and families can go to observe, analyze, and explore emerging technologies. A coalition of service providers will provide a matrix of programming, events, and classes. The AI Village will serve students dai
2859.population: Children, adults, and the families of Pinellas will be welcome to participate in the programs, events, exhibits, and classes held at the science center. Programming will also provide specific opportunities for day camps and summer camps open to residents and to tourists looking to enroll children in fun and educational activities while visiting Pinellas County. Opportunities for exposure to STEM/STEAM learning and career paths will be especially extended to low - ncome, and disenfranchised youth
2859.outcome: Pinellas has a higher percentage of low-income workers than the national average. Building wealth through higher paying jobs is the path to a better future for the county and the region. Exposing youth to STEM fields at the center is an important first step on a pathway to a variety of career paths that pay well and increase the overall prosperity of the community. Careers in STEM and STEAM have grown 79% since the mid-1990s. These education opportunities will lead students directly into a STEM pipeline of needed labor in the Pinellas market. Students who move into STEM careers out of high school and college make more money than their non-STEM counterparts. Workers with STEM training and ski

1367.description: Citrus Health Network’s Adult Crisis Stabilization Unit (CSU) is open 24-hours-a-day, 7-days-a-week to offer brief, intensive services for individuals who are acutely mentally ill and experiencing a mental health crisis, with the goal of examining, stabilizing, and redirecting them to the most appropriate and least restrictive treatment setting they need. Citrus's Assessment and Emergency Services (AES) Department is open 24-hours-a-day, 7-days-a-week operating as a psychiatric emergency room to ensure that individuals in need of mental health services receive quality screenings, evaluations, and determinations of suicidality. Citrus' CSU and AES services are crucial round-the-clock and emergency mental health services, especially for indigent, uninsured, underinsured, and homeless populations in the South Florida community.
1367.purpose: Citrus Health Network’s Adult Crisis Stabilization Unit (CSU) is open 24-hours-a-day, 7-days-a-week to offer brief, intensive services for individuals who are acutely mentally ill and experiencing a mental health crisis. Likewise, Citrus' Assessment and Emergency Services (AES) Department operates 24-hours-a-day, 7-days-a-week as a psychiatric emergency room offering quality screening, evaluations, determinations of suicidality, and linkage to services. The funding allows the Citrus CSU and AES
1367.activities: Citrus Health Network’s Adult Crisis Stabilization Unit (CSU) is open 24-hours-a-day, 7-days-a-week to offer brief, intensive services for individuals who are acutely mentally ill and experiencing a mental health crisis, with the goal of examining, stabilizing, and redirecting them to the most appropriate and least restrictive treatment setting they need. Likewise, Citrus' Assessment and Emergency Services (AES) Department operates 24-hours-a-day, 7-days-a-week as a psychiatric emergency room of
1367.direct_services: CSU: Brief, intensive services for individuals who are acutely mentally ill and experiencing a mental health crisis. Services offered include the following,as appropriate and clinically indicated: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale Screening, Psychiatric Evaluation, Nursing Assessment and Nursing Services, Medication Management, Individual, Group, Family Therapy, Safety Planning, Care Coordina
