CSU: Project funds will be used to serve 700 individuals, providing 1,065 bed days for uninsured and underinsured individuals in need of crisis stabilization due to a mental health crisis. AES: Project funds will be used to serve 1,000 individuals, providing mental health screenings, evaluations, determinations of sui
1367.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to improve mental health. The specific measures to be used for the CSU are 1.Bed days provided to clients who have an unfunded day of care, 2. Readmission Rate based on clients who had multiple admissions during the time period, and 3. Clients with stable housing situation. The specific measures to be used for AES are: 1. number of clients served who are uninsured or under insured 2. number of screenings and evaluations provided. The outcomes will be measured using Citrus' Electronic Health Records.

1368.organization: Epilepsy Florida, Inc. DBA Epilepsy Alliance
1368.description: FESP is comprised of 5 independent, non-profit epilepsy organizations serving the entire state of Florida. These non- profits provide an extensive range of vital services in local communities for individuals with epilepsy and their families. Core services provided by the legislative program are case management, medical services and prevention and education services. These lifesaving activities help prevent epilepsy in the general population and improves the quality of life for over 500,000 Floridians (including 88,000 children) living with epilepsy while saving the State of Florida money and resources by vastly reducing emergency room visits. The program is proven with 90% of patients reporting fewer emergency room visits once enrolled in the the FESP. There has been an over 86% decline in the FESP Seat Belt Trust Fund ($1.2M less) since 2013-2014 and a cumulative cost of living shortfal
1368.purpose: The funds will provide epilepsy prevention education, early intervention, medical treatment, school trainings, support services, mental health services, referrals and on-going case management to improve the quality of life for the over 500,000 Floridians living with epilepsy and their families while simultaneously saving the State of Florida money and valuable resources. 90% of patients will report fewer emergency room visits once enrolled in the FESP compared to 2.5 visits prior to enrollment.
1368.activities: Medical and diagnostic services, individualized case management, prescription medication assistance, support groups, self- management programs, basic life needs and family support services for over 4,000 individuals with a diagnosis of epilepsy as well as epilepsy prevention and education for the families and patients with epilepsy and the community at large.
1368.direct_services: Medical visits and all diagnostic services including EEG's and MRI's, individualized case management, prescription medication assistance, support groups, mental health services, education and family support services. In addition, epilepsy education has been expanded to provide the community at large with a large focus on public schools since the passing of the 2023 Care of Students with Epilepsy o
1368.population: Over 500,000 Floridians with epilepsy and their families as well as educating the Florida community at large about epilepsy prevention and seizure first aid.
1368.outcome: Benefit: Reduced emergency room visits; improved seizure management measured through an annual client survey. Benefit: Patients will have better understanding and control of their seizures measured through an annual client survey. Benefit: Improved seizure control for many means job and education opportunities measured through an annual client survey.

1334.organization: University of Florida College of Medicine
1334.description: Florida is one of the fastest aging states, with over 25% of its residents projected to be over age 65 by 2030.Preserving brain health and staving off age-related neurological diseases like Alzheimer’s disease, currently affecting over 580,000 Floridians, is critical for reducing personal and financial burdens associated with disability. Through a robust multidisciplinary research infrastructure that includes the Evelyn F. and William L. McKnight Brain Institute, the Norman Fixel Institute for Neurological Diseases, the Center for Translational Research in Neurodegenerative Disease (CTRND) and the 1Florida Alzheimer's Disease Research Center (1FLADRC), the University of Florida (UF) has established a high-impact program of scientific discovery aimed at translating basic discoveries in aging and neurological disease to therapies that benefit patients. These State funds are critical to the
1334.purpose: Through federal grants and its partnership with the state, UF has become a leader of innovation in research on Alzheimer’s and other neurological diseases. Indeed, current estimates indicate UF researchers now hold >$40 million in grants from federal agencies focused on these diseases. These state funds will enable us to bolster this research by supporting critical activities not covered by federal grants. Specifically, the funds allow us to recruit new faculty in key programmatic areas, recruit
1334.activities: These funds provide necessary support for the 1Florida ADRC(https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/alzheimers-disease- research-centers) which is a critical resource for our state, bringing the latest discoveries in the Alzheimer’s field directly to Floridians with the disease. While centered at UF, the 1Florida ADRC is a collaboration between Florida institutions (MSMC, UM, FIU, FAU) focused on making discoveries about effective prevention and, treatment of ADRD their translation to affected Floridians
1334.direct_services: • Participation in Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease research studies and access to the latest discoveries in the field • Access to new clinical trials for novel Alzheimer's and Parkinson's treatments. • Training of the next generation of physicians who will be skilled in treating those affected by Alzheimer’s and other neurological diseases • Bolstering of the state’s biomedical workforce to en
1334.population: The target population is nearly one million Floridians currently living with AD, PD or other age-associated neurological disease as well as those at risk of developing these diseases. In addition, we will serve approximately 250 University students by providing unique and valuable scientific and medical training which is necessary to build a highly skilled workforce in our state.
1334.outcome: • Benefit: Increased access for Floridians to the latest discoveries in the field of brain aging and neurological disease Measured by: Subject enrollment in new research and clinical trials related to Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and other age- related neurological conditions. • Benefit: New discoveries relevant to neurological disease and bolstering Florida’s skilled scientific workforce in Florida. Measured by: New scientific publications, patents issued, technology licensed, and extramural grant awards (all can be collected from publicly available databases). We will also track the number of trainees completing specialized training programs at UF. • Benefit: Public education regarding brain h

1369.description: The Phoenix program offers a comprehensive approach to support survivors of human trafficking, emphasizing stability, safety, and self-sufficiency. The program provides low-demand short-term housing and rental assistance for up to 12 months ensuring survivors have a secure foundation to rebuild their lives. 1. Stabilizing Survivors: Survivors are provided with an immediate, safe environment where they can access care, essential services, and treatment if needed. This supportive space enables them to begin addressing the trauma they've experienced. 2. Facilitating Financial Independence: The program connects survivors to critical resources, including employment opportunities, and benefits, equipping them with the tools necessary to achieve financial stability. 3. Achieving Self-Sufficiency: Survivors receive assistance in securing permanent housing and developing the skills required for l
1369.purpose: The Phoenix Human Trafficking Recovery Program aims to stabilize survivors, prevent chronic homelessness, and reduce re-victimization. CH will meet the existing need by providing victim-centered crisis stabilization services and transitional housing assistance to to help survivors locate & secure housing and obtain economic independence. The program will also assist victims to integrate into their community by coordinating other community services to best meet the victim’s needs.
1369.activities: Residential Services: A Three-Phase Approach Phase 1: Crisis Stabilization services include crisis intervention, housing navigation, nutrition, advocacy, transportation, and counseling. Staff assist with medical appointments, court proceedings, and accessing resources like financial aid, housing, and employment. The average stay is 45 days, (maxof 180 days) tailored to individual needs. Phase 2: Short-Term Assistance- Survivors transition to scattered-site housing, leasing market-rate apartments
1369.direct_services: Support Services: Advocacy: Victim Advocates help survivors secure financial aid, victim’s compensation, housing, employment, healthcare, and other essential resources while advocating for their rights and needs. Crisis Intervention: Staff provide in-person or phone support to develop safety plans and next steps during crises. Supportive Counseling: Confidential, non-judgmental counseling empowers
1369.population: The Phoenix Program supports trafficking victims aged 18 and older, referred by the Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office, other SAOs, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, and law enforcement. These individuals, often homeless or at risk of homelessness, are provided a safe space to access care, treatment, and services while preparing to serve as victim-witnesses in trials against traffickers. Serving approximately 30 individuals annually, the program operates as a state-wide resource, accepti
1369.outcome: Expected Outcomes: Safe, stable housing and independence. Improved self-esteem and reduced vulnerability to exploitation. Increased access to financial, employment, and educational resources. Long-term self-sufficiency through skill-building and resource connections. Measuring Outcomes: Housing Stability: Track the number of participants securing stable housing at program exit. Employment and Income: Measure the percentage of participants gaining employment, completing training, or securing benefits. 2041.description: The Speak Life End Bullying program is a community-based initiative that addresses bullying and youth mental health. The program combines evidence-based resilience learning with digital engagement, providing community organizations and educational entities with access to Speak Life End Bullying, which includes: the film, educator and community leader training, counselor and administrator resources, and 23 lessons aligned with Florida’s Resiliency Standards. Funding will support the expansion of the program beyond school settings through the development of the Speak Life Parent and Community Platform. This will include parent portal design and implementation, security enhancements and community access.
2041.purpose: Requested funds will enable Speak Life to expand the platform to be able to better integrate with existing learning management systems, create complimentary community organization systems and establish a parental platform to include parents in the education process. This will ensure that parents are able to take an active role in the educational programming that focuses on resiliency and mental wellbeing.
2041.activities: Once developed, this platform will be able to integrate with educational entities' learning management system and be a resource for out of school time community providers. Most importantly, the parent portal will create an easy pathway for involvement in the curriculum to better re-enforce the teachings as well as provide greater level of comfort as to what students are learning.
2041.direct_services: The 23 lessons and parent trainings focus on mental health, character development, civic duty, human trafficking, substance use prevention, internet safety, personal responsibility, critical thinking and other pillars of resiliency.
2041.population: School-age students as well as their parents. 120,000 students and parents are expected to utilize the platform in the first full year of implementation after development. That number is expected to grow through expanded adoption, without additional state funding being requested.
2041.outcome: The goal of this project is to facilitate parental involvement to re-enforce the core curriculum and principles of resiliency through a closed loop platform. Through the development of the Analytics and Telemetry phase of the project, Speak Life will be able to identify usage of both the parental access and the community organization access to the platform.

2861.description: To achieve its vision of expanding its educational, programming and exhibition spaces, The Dalí has embarked on a multiyear effort to raise $68 million to renovate and expand its footprint in downtown St. Petersburg. This includes interactive art galleries to spark creativity and imagination, education & conference space to promote innovation, learning & connection, and infinite experiences that attract, educate, engage and delight. Museum renovations (2026-2028) will leverage $25.16M in local support and additional private funding to ignite the imagination of 82% of Museum-goers interested in learning about art in an immersive format while expanding education, program, exhibition and training space for school groups, scholars, innovators and visitors for years to come.
2861.purpose: Museum renovations (2026-2028) leveraging $25.16M in local support and additional private funding to ignite the imagination of 82% of Museum goers interested in learning about art in an immersive format and expanding education, program, exhibition and training space for school groups, scholars, innovators and visitors for years to come.
2861.activities: Renovations will expand The Dali's capacity to serve as a key community and state educational resource through enhanced educational, programming and exhibition spaces; cutting-edge AI, augmented reality and virtual reality exhibits; and state-of-the-art research on creativity, creative problem solving and organizational management for businesses, associations, and non-profits.
2861.direct_services: The expansion will increase the number of Museum annual visitors from 300,000 to 500,000+ over a 10-year period and provide free or reduced admissions for 150,000 children, students, seniors, educators, fire-fighters, uniformed military, veterans, and police. The project is projected to increase the Museum's annual economic impact from $112M to $218M over the next 10 years.
2861.population: The 4.9 million attendees over a 10-year period who will benefit from the Museum's programs. In addition to on-site programming, The Dali brings educational experiences that address Next Generation Sunshine Standards (including critical thinking and reflection, historical and global connection) directly to students in public and private schools, including Title I and home-schooled students, serving as a key educational resource for the community, the state and the world at large.
2861.outcome: An estimated 4.9 million attendees over a 10-year period will benefit from the Museum's programs. Additionally, an independent analysis of visitor profile data (2018-2022) and Museum economic impact projections (2022) determined that The Dalí currently generates $53 million in direct spending and $106 million in overall economic impact annually, with this total $160 million economic impact expected to grow to $3.1 billion by 2034. Outcomes will be measured through visitor counts as well as economic data available.

1909.description: The Town of Windermere seeks funding for design and planning for intersection improvements at Chase Road and Main Street to enhance traffic flow, safety, and accessibility. Both Main Street and 6th Avenue are operating more than 75% over their designed capacity, causing daily congestion, long delays, and unsafe turning movements. The project includes roadway widening, upgraded signage, improved pavement markings, enhanced lighting, and new pedestrian crossings. Drainage enhancements will also support stormwater management. These upgrades will relieve congestion, improve navigation, and create safer conditions for motorists, cyclists, and pedestrians at this key intersection, ensuring long-term infrastructure reliability and access.
1909.purpose: The requested funds will address severe congestion and safety issues at the Chase Road and Main Street intersection. Main Street and 6th Avenue operate at over 75% beyond their designed capacity, causing daily backups and hazardous turning movements. Proposed improvements include roadway widening, upgraded lighting, signage, pavement markings, pedestrian crossings, and enhanced drainage to support stormwater management. These upgrades will relieve congestion, improve safety, and ensure long-term
1909.activities: The project will include roadway widening, installation of upgraded signage, improved pavement markings, and enhanced lighting to improve visibility. Pedestrian crossings will be added to ensure accessibility. Drainage improvements will be implemented to manage stormwater effectively. Engineering, design, and construction services will oversee the project’s implementation, ensuring the intersection’s safety, efficiency, and accessibility for all users, including motorists, pedestrians, and cycli
1909.direct_services: The project will provide improved traffic flow, reduced congestion, and enhanced safety at the Chase Road and Main Street intersection. Upgrades will include better signage, lighting, and pedestrian crossings. Drainage improvements will reduce flooding risks. These enhancements will ensure safer and more efficient travel for Windermere residents, commuters, cyclists, and pedestrians, benefiting da
1909.population: The target population includes Windermere residents, commuters, local businesses, and visitors who travel through the Chase and Main intersection. This intersection serves as a key access point in the town’s roadway network. The project is expected to benefit thousands of individuals daily by improving traffic flow, safety, and accessibility, ultimately enhancing the overall transportation experience for both motorists and pedestrians in the area.
1909.outcome: The project will reduce congestion, improve traffic flow, and enhance safety for motorists, cyclists, and pedestrians at the Chase Road and Main Street intersection. These improvements will also support emergency response access and promote more efficient regional mobility. The outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-construction traffic studies, including level of service (LOS) analysis, travel time data, and crash rate comparisons to quantify safety and operational improvements.

1076.description: Selby Preschool, a program of The Haven, provides comprehensive early education for children ages 1–5. With low ratios & high-quality teachers, classrooms bring together children with & without disabilities, fostering acceptance, empathy & diversity. Students benefit from speech, occupational, physical, aquatic & mental health therapies, adaptive PE, music, art & meals. Families receive training, support & connections to resources. With a waitlist & limited community services available, Selby faces a $379,000 deficit; this grant sustains its life-changing work.
1076.purpose: The Haven’s Selby Preschool seeks state support to continually improve comprehensive early childhood education for 66 children, over half with disabilities. Funding will preserve small class ratios, therapies, and skilled staff, ensuring children of all abilities access high-quality education. This investment supports operations and families, and reduces future costs by giving every child the strongest start in life.
1076.activities: State funds will support activities and services such as comprehensive classroom instruction, therapeutic interventions, and developmental support for preschoolers. Children will benefit from licensed therapy services, specialized teaching strategies, and family engagement, ensuring equitable access to quality early education.
1076.direct_services: Funds will provide comprehensive preschool services including individualized instruction, speech/occupational/physical therapy, small group learning, adaptive equipment use, progress monitoring, and family engagement. These activities ensure children with and without disabilities achieve developmental milestones and school readiness.
1076.population: The target population is children ages 1–5, with & without disabilities, who thrive in an comprehensive early education setting. For over 70 years, Selby Preschool has offered low ratios, skilled teachers, & individualized supports to meet diverse needs. Each year, the program serves 66 preschool students & their families. Beyond education, families gain guidance, resources, & connections with one another—building a supportive community that strengthens long-term success.
1076.outcome: The project will ensure 66 children ages 1–5 receive inclusive, high-quality early education with access to therapies, enrichment, and nutrition. Expected outcomes include developmental growth, school readiness, stronger physical & mental health, and social-emotional skills, while families gain resources & peer connections. Outcomes will be measured through the Ages & Stages Questionnaire (ASQ), CLASS assessments, therapy progress notes, family surveys, and attendance data.

2310.description: Polk State College is requesting $7,576,930 to complete the $51 million Polk State Haines City-Davenport Campus. With $10 million allocated in the 2025 Legislative Session, the College continued construction which began in early 2025, making this final funding is crucial to complete the project in time to open for the Fall 2026 Semester. The campus will drive workforce development, support local industries, and provide essential educational and healthcare training opportunities. Approving this request will ensure the project stays on track and is open to students as early as Fall 2026, benefiting Northeast Polk County’s economic growth and long-term prosperity.
2310.purpose: Construction on the Haines City-Davenport Campus began in early 2025. This final funding allocation is crucial to ensure the project progresses smoothly and opens for students in Fall 2026, preventing any disruption in construction and guaranteeing timely completion. Located in one of the fastest growing areas of Polk County, the Polk State Haines City Campus will increase access to higher education for stakeholders in Haines City, Davenport, Poinciana, and the Four Corners region. In particular
2310.activities: The proposed development will house education and training facilities to support workforce programs with a particular emphasis on Health Sciences and the general education coursework for the Associate in Arts degree. Health disciplines do not work in isolation in a hospital or clinic setting and students at this campus will have the benefit of sharing state-of-the-art technical and training labs while working alongside each other as they would in a hospital setting. Increases in the use of simul
2310.direct_services: Upon completion, the Haines City-Davenport Campus will provide residents with access to essential academic services and the ability to earn an Associate in Arts degree, along with degrees in high-demand Health Sciences fields. The campus will also feature Central Florida’s first interdisciplinary simulation hospital at a public higher education institution, enhancing healthcare training and foster
2310.population: Polk County students and families are the target population for this project with a particular emphasis on those residing within the Haines City, Davenport, Poinciana, and the Four Corners region. Residents within a 10-mile radius of the site are the ideal population to be served and include nearly 3,800 12th graders, which represents 39% of all 12th graders in Polk County, and over 80,000 individuals whose highest educational attainment is a high school diploma or some college/no degree.
2310.outcome: The outcome of this project will be to provide access to higher education to the residents of Northeast Polk County. Outcomes will be measured through increased student enrollment, retention, and completion for Polk State College, and specific increases in these metrics for students who are residents of the Haines City, Davenport, Poinciana, and the Four Corners region.

1087.description: Circles of Care, Brevard County’s nonprofit Community Behavioral Health Center and designated Central Receiving Facility, requests $750,000 to complete facility renovations and safety improvements across its behavioral health campuses. Projects include roof and parking lot replacements, flooring and restroom renovations, HVAC and kitchen upgrades, replacement of patio structures damaged by hurricanes, structural reinforcement of aging exterior walls, and safety enhancements such as ligature-resistant door systems and door-top alarm installations consistent with patient- safety audit recommendations. These renovations will preserve aging facilities, enhance staff and patient safety, extend building life, and modernize clinical and residential environments consistent with state and federal behavioral health standards.
1087.purpose: To modernize and preserve behavioral health facilities serving Brevard County residents by completing targeted structural, safety, and accessibility renovations across Circles of Care’s hospital, residential, and outpatient campuses.
1087.activities: Renovate and improve behavioral health facilities, including roofs, bathrooms, flooring, parking areas, patient safety upgrades, and staff spaces across multiple program sites.
1087.direct_services: The project directly benefits patients, staff, and visitors by providing safe, modern, and compliant treatment and residential environments for mental health and substance use disorder care.
1087.population: Adults and youth receiving inpatient, residential, or outpatient behavioral health services, including Medicaid, uninsured, and indigent populations of Brevard County. Circles of Care serves approximately 12,000 individuals annually.
1087.outcome: Improved facility safety, accessibility, and compliance; reduced maintenance costs; enhanced patient experience; and preservation of essential behavioral health infrastructure.

1088.description: Circles of Care, Brevard County’s nonprofit Community Behavioral Health Center and the county’s designated Central Receiving Facility, requests funding to sustain psychiatric and clinical capacity and complete its transformation to a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC). Through budget proviso language adopted in the 2025 legislative session, the Legislature directed the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) to pursue Federal CCBHC State Demonstration designation for Florida. This appropriation advances that statewide initiative by enabling Circles of Care to expand medication-assisted treatment (MAT), implement primary-care screenings, enhance care coordination across hospitals and primary care, and build data systems for quality and outcome reporting.
1088.purpose: To sustain psychiatric and clinical capacity and complete Circles of Care’s transition to a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic. Funds will expand medication-assisted treatment (MAT) services, initiate primary care screenings, enhance care coordination, and strengthen data systems that support timely access, quality reporting, and for Florida’s forthcoming CCBHC demonstration and PPS reimbursement model.
1088.activities: (1) Retain a board-certified psychiatrist providing care and leadership ambulatory programs. (2) Expand MAT access and continuity of care for opioid and alcohol use disorders. (3) Implement primary care screening protocols (blood pressure, BMI, tobacco use, diabetes risk). (4) Strengthen coordination with local hospitals, primary care partners, and FQHCs. (5) Develop and deploy standardized outcome and quality reporting systems to meet CCBHC standards.
1088.direct_services: Funds will directly support psychiatric evaluation and treatment, medication management, medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid and alcohol use disorders, primary-care health screenings, care coordination, peer and family supports, and follow-up engagement for individuals with mental illness and substance use disorders. These services will be provided to Medicaid and uninsured residents of
1088.population: Adults, youth, and families in Brevard County experiencing mental illness, substance use disorders, or co-occurring conditions. Priority populations include Medicaid and uninsured residents, individuals with opioid use disorder, those at risk of hospitalization or incarceration due to untreated behavioral health conditions, and those at risk for repeated emergency department utilization due to unmanaged medical conditions that are comorbid with behavioral health conditions.
1088.outcome: (1) At least 75% of CCBHC outpatient clients will be seen within 10 days of first contact, unless the client specifically requests an appointment beyond 10 days. Electronic health record (EHR) encounter data will be used to measure the outcome. (2) At least 70% of outpatient clients will annually receive a documented physical health screening. This measure speaks to the positive benefit of the integration of primary care in CCBHCs and the reduction of emergency department visits and reduced hospitalizations. EHR encounter data will provide data to measure the outcome.

1056.description: Promise Fund is advancing a scalable model of community-based healthcare that reduces breast and cervical cancer mortality by breaking down barriers to care. Through outreach, education, and Promise Fund Navigation, women are connected to timely screening, diagnosis, and treatment. Since launching, we have established a county-wide Promise Fund Navigator Network, partnered with local health providers and hospitals, and co-located lifesaving screening and diagnostic services at federally qualified health centers. Today, our Navigators serve women across Palm Beach County including rural communities such as the Glades ensuring access to care close to home.
1056.purpose: Promise Fund is seeking support to expand our breast and cervical cancer screening and navigation program because when cancer is found early, women live longer, healthier lives and communities save millions. Survival rates soar to nearly 99% for breast cancer and 95% for cervical cancer when detected at early stages. 1056.activities: Promise Fund Navigators carry out a comprehensive set of activities to ensure women can access and complete lifesaving care. They guide women through the healthcare system with cultural sensitivity, facilitate scheduling and referrals, and ensure timely follow-up for abnormal findings and treatment. Navigators provide women’s health education to individuals and groups, assist with financial and insurance barriers, and arrange transportation when needed. They track interventions and outcomes, use
1056.direct_services: Promise Fund Navigators break down barriers to care for low-income women in Palm Beach County by providing multilingual navigation and personalized support. They connect women to mammograms, diagnostic mammograms, Pap and HPV tests, and when needed, timely cancer diagnostics and treatment. Navigators ensure each participant has a medical home, assess social determinants of health, and make referra

Black women experience the highest cervical cancer mortality rates and are 40% more likely to die from breast cancer than White women. Hispanic women are most likely to develop cervical cancer and face higher rates of late-stage breast cancer diagnoses. Through our program, more than 800 women will receive Promise Fund Navigation to co

1721.description: The City of Safety Harbor seeks State assistance to improve security and customer service for residents and guests at their local City Hall. The current City Hall lacks adequate security measures to protect staff and ensure continuity of operations. The location needs to up-fit doors and locks, install closed circuit camera systems, replace lighting and windows, install a public address system, and remodel areas of the building that require fortification. Such work will ensure safe operations. Projects are ready for contract.
1721.purpose: Increasing safety for residents, guests, and employees to comfortably conduct local government in a safe atmosphere.
1721.activities: The installed systems will protect citizens and staff as they conduct daily business at City Hall.
1721.direct_services: The installed systems will protect citizens and staff as they conduct daily business at City Hall.
1721.population: The target population includes the residents and guests of Safety Harbor, as well as employees, who utilize City Hall for services. As all city business is conducted through City Hall, the project projects to serve all approximately 16,000 residents of the community by ensuring continuous and safe operations.
1721.outcome: The City will monitor unnecessary closure days, as well as employee leave and retention.

Carver Elementary School, Maggiore Park, and the presence of multiple businesses along the US-1 corridor, where safe pedestrian access is essential.

3547.description: Develop an effluent spray field along the City's existing reuse line. Project includes land acquisition, environmental permitting and site development. A spray field system disperses treated wastewater over land where soil and vegetation naturally filter and further treat the effluent prior to groundwater or surface water infiltration that provides a long-term, environmentally compliant solution for the disposal of treated wastewater. Developing a City-owned spray field will reduce operational risk, ensure regulatory compliance, and enhance wastewater management independence.
3547.purpose: Goal is to secure a City-owned effluent spray field, providing a reliable, long-term, and environmentally compliant method for treated wastewater disposal. The project reduces reliance on third-party contracts and agreements, enhances wastewater management independence, and ensures long-term regulatory compliance.
3547.activities: Funds will be used for land acquisition as determined by engineers, environmental permitting and site development (as funding permits) of an effluent spray field connected to the City’s existing reuse line utilizing and adhering the City's procurement policies and procedures.
3547.direct_services: The project ensures safe, sustainable wastewater disposal, protecting groundwater and surface water quality, supporting public health, and providing long-term environmental compliance for City residents and utility customers. Improves quality of life, health and safety.
3547.population: Target population includes citizenry, residents, visitors, general public, the business community, plus utility customers in neighboring areas that depend on the City’s wastewater system, ensuring service reliability and environmental protection in this Financially Disadvantaged Municipality (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.), located in Hardee County, which is designated as a Rural Area of Economic Concern/Rural Area of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes). Population expected to be served exceeds 25,
3547.outcome: Outcome: Reliable and independent effluent disposal system, reduced environmental risk, and compliance with DEP regulations. Methodology: Measure is regulatory compliance records, number of gallons managed on-site, and reduced dependence on third-party disposal contracts. Completion and certification of the project.

3577.population: The target population is the City of Bartow, which serves as Polk County's Capital City for Regional, Federal and State government operations, offices, agencies, properties and buildings, which are tax exempt that creates a reduction of revenue, which is needed to adequately serve its citizenry; and surrounding communities such as Clear Springs Developments and the Polk State College Advanced Technology Center Campus. Benefit is operation of reliable fire rescue lifesaving truck that is essential to the protection of the general public, first responders, life, health, property including Regional, State and Federal buildings and the environment. Measure is efficient and effective response to emergencies, less expenses for maintenance and fuel costs; improved insurance and ISO rating with delivery and operations of the fire rescue ladder truck.

1099.description: This project will address critical infrastructure needs by replacing aging stormwater conveyance systems with modernized drainage improvements to alleviate flooding and protect property in the downtown core. This project will reduce stormwater discharge to the Coral Gables Waterway. These upgrades will significantly reduce localized flooding in the downtown area, enhancing public safety, preserving economic activity, and improving resiliency for some of Coral Gables’ most heavily used corridors.
1099.purpose: This project will address critical infrastructure needs by replacing aging stormwater conveyance systems with upgraded drainage systems to alleviate flooding and protect property in the downtown core. This project will reduce stormwater discharge to the Coral Gables Waterway. These upgrades will significantly reduce localized flooding in the downtown area, enhancing public safety, preserving economic activity, and improving resiliency for one of Coral Gables’ most heavily used corridors.
1099.activities: The City will be managing the procurement process for this project by retaining the services of a construction contractor to implement designed project improvements.
1099.population: Downtown area residents, commuters, businesses and patrons affected by flooding including approximately 550 properties will benefit directly and indirectly.
1099.outcome: Minimize flooding and flood related damage to Downtown Coral Gables. Provide safe public access to affected areas. This will be measured by the reduction in the number of flooding incidents reported through direct communication and various reporting platforms.

1146.description: Kinship Care Stabilization efforts aims to divert children from foster homes and group homes, reducing their risk of involvement in the juvenile justice system. This program also provides funding for life-skill development and mentorship to prevent delinquency. In collaboration with Citrus, our local Community-Based Care provider, Voices For Children Foundation serves as a vital safety net for families and youth, ensuring support in situations where no other resources are available.
1146.purpose: Kinship Care Stabilization efforts aims to divert children from foster homes and group homes, reducing their risk of involvement in the juvenile justice system. This program also provides funding for life-skill development and mentorship to prevent delinquency. In collaboration with Citrus, our local Community-Based Care provider, Voices For Children Foundation serves as a vital safety net for families and youth, ensuring support in situations where no other resources are available.
1146.activities: Foster Care Navigators and Life Skills Coordinators play a critical role in prevention and intervention efforts to support children in foster care and divert them from involvement in the juvenile justice system. Foster Care Navigators collaborate with kinship caregivers who accept placement of a child to assess their needs and provide essential support, including assistance with furniture, basic necessities, housing, and other resources that help stabilize the placement and prevent disruptions.
1146.direct_services: Foster Care Navigators and Life Skills Coordinators will provide comprehensive direct services to promote stability and prevent justice system involvement for children in foster care. Foster Care Navigators will conduct a thorough needs assessment to develop a tailored plan for each family, ensuring they have access to wrap-around services, service connections, and referrals for resources such as
1146.population: Children in foster care, relative and non-relatives who are caring for children who come into foster care, and youth who are nearing their 18th birthday and set to age out of foster care.
1146.outcome: The goal of this project is to reduce the number of foster youth involved in the juvenile justice system by stabilizing kinship placements, providing tailored support, and engaging youth in strength-based, pro-social activities. Outcomes will be measured by tracking arrests or justice system involvement, conducting needs assessments to connect families and youth with resources, and monitoring academic performance, school attendance, and extracurricular involvement. Progress will also be evaluated through individualized normalcy plans and regular reviews to ensure stability, engagement, and positive development.

1238.description: Construction of a new, 108,134 gsf workforce training building designed to double the number of students trained in the fields of math, science, technology, and various healthcare programs (such as nursing, respiratory therapy, etc) from ~4,500 to ~9,000. Fill large gaps in regional and statewide workforce needs, especially in nursing and other health sciences. Provide a highly-trained and skilled workforce in high-demand, high-skilled, high-wage healthcare areas. The Florida Center for Nursing estimates that 1,000 nurses alone will be needed annually for the next 10 years.
1238.purpose: The construction of a new, 108,136 gsf building to house workforce classrooms and labs designed to double the number of students served from ~4,500 to ~9,000. Fill large gaps in regional and statewide workforce needs, especially in nursing and other health sciences. Provide a highly trained and skilled workforce in high-demand healthcare areas. Jobs will be created during construction, and program grads will be placed into high-demand, high-skilled, high-wage jobs.
1238.activities: The construction of a new, 108,136 gsf building to house workforce classrooms and labs designed to double the number of students served from ~4,500 to ~9,000. The State of Florida previously provided $25 million in state funding for the purchase of land on which this and other buildings will be constructed. Jobs will be created during construction and program grads will be placed in high-skilled, high-demand, high-wage jobs upon graduation.
1238.direct_services: Creation of jobs during the construction phase. Training and placement of grads in high-demand workforce jobs, especially healthcare and related occupations. Placement rates are currently greater than 90%, with a 100% passage rate on nursing licensure exams. Employers will be supported by more well-trained graduates prepared to immediately enter the workforce in workforce occupations experiencing
1238.population: College students, high school dual enrollment students, workers returning to refresh or enhance skills, economically disadvantaged persons, and jobless persons. The number of students served is expected to double from ~4,500 to ~9,000.
1238.outcome: Improved quality of education, improved economic self-sufficiency, increased economic activity, and addressed employer need. Measured by the number and rate of program enrollments, completions, graduates, placement, wages of graduates, and reinvestments by graduates back into the local/regional economy. The project will also result in improved healthcare for the region.

2864.description: Continue the growth of a state-of-the-art digital path cancer program to fuel development of new AI algorithms using big data from patient cohorts. Funds will support purchase of additional equipment and software. Project transforms practice of pathology by creating high- resolution digital images, facilitating remote analysis, seamlessly integrating data and enhanced diagnostic accuracy. These unique data will be linked to additional cancer patient data, including treatment and outcomes.
2864.purpose: Continue the growth of a state-of-the-art digital path cancer program to fuel development of new AI algorithms using big data from patient cohorts. Funds will support purchase of additional equipment and software. Project transforms practice of pathology by creating high- resolution digital images, facilitating remote analysis, seamlessly integrating data and enhanced diagnostic accuracy. These unique data will be linked to additional cancer patient data, including treatment and outcomes.
2864.activities: The modernization of digitizing data will be linked to additional cancer patient data, including treatments and outcomes.
2864.direct_services: Digital Pathology reads and case sign outs for both Moffitt patients and outside consults.
2864.outcome: Creates a hub for cutting-edge research, attracting additional funding, clinical trials and collaborations. Digital pathology is critical for analyzing large datasets and enabling advancements in personalized medicine through the development of novel AI and ML algorithms. Increased frequency and accuracy of cancer detection in Floridians; improved resources for cancer treatment

1079.description: This project will involve a modification to the Pembroke Falls outfall structure that includes the installation of a sluice gate at the connection point into SBDD’s Flamingo Rd canal and the installation of a telemetry control system to allow District staff to operate the sluice gate remotely, as needed. The use of the sluice gate will allow SBDD to lower the lake levels within Pembroke Falls more effectively and much faster than currently exists, thereby creating millions of gallons of excess storage capacity in advance of a major rainfall event. The improvements also include erosion control protections to harden the existing canal embankment that sits adjacent to SR 823.
1079.purpose: Modification to an existing drainage structure that serves the Pembroke Falls Community, businesses, schools, and emergency shelters (3.2 square miles). The modification includes the installation of a new sluice gate and telemetry system which will allow for pre-storm and post-storm drawdown effecting stormwater levels within the lake system and enhancing flood protection and resiliency for the region.
1079.activities: This project will provide a sluice gate, telemetry control system and erosion control for SBDD Basin 13. These improvements will allow for the ability to draw down water levels pre-storm to create increased storage capacity within the lakes and basins across SBDD’s system. This will allow for flood levels to be lower, emergency access routes to remain open and accessible longer, and the time frame that residents may be trapped in their homes and businesses closed due to flooding to be reduced.
1079.direct_services: SBDD will be provided real-time water level monitoring with the ability to provide pre-storm and post-storm drawdowns which will enhance the level of service of flood protection (both stages and duration) for the citizens and businesses within the region.
1079.population: This project will directly impact the residents and the three schools within SBDD Drainage Basin 13 which comprises of 11,268 individuals according to 2020 census data; however, Basin 13 is interconnected with SBDD Drainage Basins 2 & 7 which will also see a benefit of increased storage from this improvement. The total population served by the project is 89,582.
1079.outcome: This project will provide added flood protection within the region. By lowering surface water levels within the interconnected lakes and canal system, SBDD will have the ability to perform a pre-storm drawdown within the SBDD Basin 13 region that cannot be performed at this time. The residents and businesses will benefit from the pre-storm drawdown which will lower the lake levels and provide additional, critical, storm-water storage within the community. The extra storage capacity will account for businesses remaining open longer, returning to work sooner and roadways being negatively impacted later during the storm event and recovering sooner post-storm.

2312.description: FFT is an evidence-based family therapy model designed to increase family engagement, reduce families from going deeper into the Child Welfare system or prolonged stays. The model also reduces the time of out-of-home placements in foster care and increases the percentage of successful reunifications working with both the foster parents and the biological/permanent parents/placement. Additionally, where the parents' rights have been terminated, will stabilize the long term non-permanent placement until child(ren) can be placed permanently.
2312.purpose: The goal of the program is to serve the most at-risk youth and families involved in the Foster Care system. FFT Foster Care has demonstrated that families participating are significantly more successful when the child(ren) are reunited from the foster placement. FFT Foster Care is unique in that it works both with the biological family AND the foster family. The foster families are trained specifically to work with the most challenging population in the Child Welfare system.
2312.activities: FFT in Foster Care is a highly intense intervention that is family-based treatment. The provider's clinicians and case managers are trained to deliver the model with fidelity. All services, including family therapy and case management, are delivered in the home for both the foster and biological/care giver families.
2312.direct_services: Youth and their families along with the foster families involved with the Department of Children and Family Services will receive evidence based and trauma informed counseling services. The model is specifically designed to work with the most challenging families in the Child Welfare system to keep from going deeper into the system and to successfully reunify the family or permanent caregiver.
2312.population: Families involved in the Child Welfare system where the youth have been removed from their families and placed into a foster care environment. The team will be comprised of 1 master's level supervisor, 4 master's level clinicians and 3 bachelor level family specialist that will carry a caseload of approximately 10 to 12 cases at one time. A minimum of 57 families will be served annually.
2312.outcome: Youth and families served by the FFT treatment model will experience a successful transition from foster care to their biological/care giver homes, reducing the number of additional out of home placements. In cases where the rights of the biological family have been terminated, the long term non-permanent home will be stabilized using this model. A Clinical Outcome Measure (COM) is given to the families both at the beginning and the end of the services. All the data is entered into the FFT learning management system that provides the outcome measures such as family participation, engagement rate, and completion rate. Data collected from each family served is analyzed at the end of the fiscal

2313.description: Tri-County Human Services, a non-profit CARF-accredited and licensed substance use disorder and behavioral health service provider for over 40 years, is requesting funding for an additional 20 detox beds for citizens/individuals of Polk, Hardee, and Highlands counties to meet the increasing population demands for these essential healthcare treatment services. The current funding by the Department of Children and Families (DCF) only funds up to 5.5 beds annually. No additional DCF funding is anticipated to meet this current community need. Funding from Polk County match requirement will only fund 4 beds for FY 2026-27. The balance of 10.5 beds will not be funded to sustain and keep these beds available and necessary for the increasing needs of individuals within these communities.
2313.purpose: To meet the increasing needs of Polk, Hardee and Highlands counties to provide on-demand, medical detoxification and Marchman Act services to those individuals suffering from substance use disorders and abuse of alcohol, benzodiazepines and opiates. Tri-County Human Service has been a main service provider of medical detox services in these counties. Our goal is to treat these individuals with the appropriate detox protocols, stabilize them and assist them in seeking the appropriate treatment (r
2313.activities: Services provided are medical and clinical interventions to stabilize the patient, to reduce the immediate impact of the potential overdose of the individual, and initiate a treatment plan to engage the individual to seek further medical and/or clinical assistance in the form of residential or outpatient treatment to address their addiction issues.
2313.direct_services: Direct services include a medical assessment, clinical assessment, treatment plan development discharge planning into the appropriate level of care, as defined in the individual treatment plan, Medication Assisted Treatment (MAT) for those with alcohol or opiate use disorder diagnosis (use of Vivitrol or Suboxone monitored by qualified medical licensed staff), care coordination for high-need/high-
2313.population: The target population are adult individuals who have abused their drug of choice or ingested a drug unknowingly, to the point of endangering themselves and require immediate medical and clinical intervention to stabilize them and reduce the risk of further endangerment to themselves. It is anticipated Tri-County will annually serve approximately 3,650 individuals.
2313.outcome: The requested appropriation benefit will assist in reducing unnecessary admissions into the local emergency department. The outcome will measured by the documented referrals made by the emergency department to our Detox program. Without this funding, there will be increased utilization of our burdened local emergency departments for substance use disorder and behavioral health-related admissions.

1773.description: This project would expand Miami-Dade County Public Schools' Early Childhood Education (ECE) program and open eight (8) new ECE Learning Labs, tied to CTE Teaching Academies, in high schools throughout the district. These programs provide care for infants, toddlers, and prekindergarten students, and provide high school students participating in the Early Childhood Education pathway program with insights into the teaching profession. The additional schools will provide more options for both students and parents.
1773.purpose: The purpose of the funds is to expand the Early Childhood Education (ECE) program and open eight (8) new ECE Learning Labs, tied to CTE Teaching Academies, in high schools throughout the district. These programs provide care for infants, toddlers, and prekindergarten students, and provide high school students participating in the Early Childhood Education pathway program with insights into the teaching profession. The schools will provide more options for both students and parents.
1773.activities: Children will have a nurturing and stimulating preschool environment that will prepare them for kindergarten through developmentally appropriate activities that will help them meet their social, emotional, physical, cognitive, and intellectual developmental needs. High school students will be able to plan, prepare, and execute lessons while being supervised by well-trained staff.
1773.direct_services: Parents of infant, toddler, and preschool children will have more regional options for early childhood education and childcare, reaching more under-served areas. Additional high school students across the district will be able to gain relevant knowledge and skills needed to prepare for postsecondary education and careers in the education industry.
1773.population: The target population includes over 800 preschool children and high school students in the Early Childhood Education pathway program across Miami-Dade County.
1773.outcome: The expected outcome is to equip high school students with the relevant knowledge, skills, and hands-on experience needed to succeed in postsecondary education and future careers, as well as strengthening the teacher pipeline and addressing the teacher shortage. Expanding to more high schools will also increase regional options for parents for early childhood education and childcare, reaching under-served areas. This will be measured through CDA certifications, evaluations, enrollment and graduation rates.

1058.description: The ADAM (Awesome Dads Awesome Men) Fatherhood Mentoring Program is a comprehensive, evidence-based initiative led by Community Based Connections, Inc. (CBCI), which, for 20 years, has been a nonprofit at the forefront of strengthening families in Broward and Palm Beach Counties. The ADAM program (now in its 13th year) supports at-risk, court-involved, and low-income fathers with a clear goal: reconnect fathers with their children, restore family relationships, and achieve economic stability through employment and skill-building (thus strengthening families, ending multi-generational cycles of neglect). The ADAM program provides: evidence-based parenting education, promotion of marriage and family reunification, individualized case management, and, most critically, workforce training pathways that lead to industry-recognized certifications. If funded, this appropriation will allow CBCI t
1058.purpose: This appropriation, if funded, will be used to expand CBCI's ADAM Program to serve 300+ additional at-risk fathers in Broward and Palm Beach Counties. The specific program goals are strengthening father-child relationships, improving responsible parenting skills, and increasing family stability by reconnecting fathers with their children and equipping them with the tools needed to provide emotional and financial support. Through evidence-based parenting education, case management, workforce trai
1058.activities: More than 44% of children in the region are born to unwed mothers, and in many communities, fathers are struggling with joblessness, court involvement, or a lack of support. State investment in the ADAM program strengthens traditional families through the promotion of marriage, reduced reliance on social services, supports reentry and workforce reintegration, and ensures fathers can meet their obligations, financial and emotional, to their children. This initiative aligns directly with the state
1058.direct_services: The ADAM Program provides a continuum of evidence-based services including individualized case management, parenting and co-parenting education using the 24/7 Dad® and Nurturing Parenting Program curricula, family counseling, and facilitated support groups. Participants engage in structured workshops that promote responsible fatherhood, healthy communication, and emotional bonding with their child
1058.population: The target population for the ADAM Program is low-income, court-involved, and at-risk fathers in Broward and Palm Beach Counties, including those reentering society after incarceration, or mandated to complete parenting programs due to child welfare involvement. The project also serves community-based fathers seeking to strengthen their parenting and family relationships. In its 13 years of existence, the ADAM Program has served 1100+ fathers through direct services, and thousands more through c
1058.outcome: The ADAM Program’s ultimate goal is to strengthen traditional families, reduce generational cycles of neglect and absence, and promote safer, more connected communities. 80% of fathers participating will demonstrate improvement in child support payments, parenting engagement, and family stability; at least 200 will receive workforce certifications; and 150+ placed in employment. These outcomes are evaluated using a comprehensive methodology that includes assessments, detailed case management documentation, and participant progress tracking.

1064.description: Funds for the Village South will support 3 additional Crisis Stabilization Unit beds at the Miami Center for Mental Health and Recovery. The Center prioritizes individuals with 5 or more jail mental health (MH) admissions over the past 5 years, a population that also frequently experiences homelessness and substance use disorder (SUD). These beds will enhance public safety, save critical tax dollars, significantly reduce homelessness, and offer a future of recovery for people with MH and SUD.
1064.purpose: Funds for the Village South will support 3 additional Crisis Stabilization Unit beds at the Miami Center for Mental Health and Recovery. The Center prioritizes individuals with 5 or more jail mental health (MH) admissions over the past 5 years, a population that also frequently experiences homelessness and substance use disorder (SUD). These beds will enhance public safety, save critical tax dollars, significantly reduce homelessness, and offer a future of recovery for people with MH and SUD.
1064.activities: The Center includes a receiving facility, an integrated crisis stabilization unit & addiction receiving facility, various levels of residential treatment, transitional housing, day programs, outpatient behavioral health & integrated primary care, dental & optometry services, vocational rehabilitation & employment services, classrooms & educational spaces, and housing assistance, among others.
1064.direct_services: Funds will support 3 additional CSU beds, increasing the total number of beds to 13. The CSU provides residential crisis stabilization services for adults experiencing acute mental health problems on a voluntary and involuntary basis. These beds will enhance public safety, save critical tax dollars, significantly reduce homelessness, and offer a future of recovery for people with MH and SUD.
1064.population: It is estimated that around 730 individuals will benefit from these services. This diverse group encompasses people from all genders, adult age groups, racial and cultural backgrounds, socio-economic standings, as well as varied educational and employment histories. Specifically, our program aims to assist individuals with co-occurring behavioral health disorders (COD), which means they have two or more concurrent conditions. Among these are individuals struggling with mental health challenges,
1064.outcome: The program aims to bring about multiple positive outcomes for its participants. We anticipate that participants will show marked improvements in mental health symptoms and overall mental functioning. Another significant objective is to reduce recidivism by diverting individuals from the criminal justice system. Also, we aim to see decreased recidivism rates among participants during the program and after their discharge. Additionally, we aspire for our participants to remain drug-free and not relapse during their treatment. To gauge the effectiveness of these interventions, we will rely on program data, documenting individual participant progress as recorded by our dedicated staff.

1061.description: The Military to Civilian Statewide Integration Program provides coordinated transition support for service members leaving active duty and relocating to Florida. Through the Florida Veterans Coalition’s partnerships with military installations across the U.S., the program connects transitioning service members with certified community sponsors, statewide veteran resources, and critical services in housing, employment, education, healthcare, and financial stability. This initiative reduces veteran suicide risk, increases workforce participation, and strengthens Florida’s economy by integrating over 2,000+ new veterans & 5,000 veterans and their families annually into communities across all 67 counties.
1061.purpose: The requested funds will expand the Military to Civilian Statewide Integration Program, a coordinated initiative led by the Florida Veterans Coalition that works in conjunction with transitioning service members on installations across the United States. Every service member through this program receives early, structured support through certified VA sponsors and access to housing, employment, education, healthcare, and financial resources. This funding will strengthen FVC across 67 counties, en
1061.activities: Funds will support coordinated transition and suicide prevention services through the Florida Veterans Coalition’s Community Integration Coordinator (CIC) program. Activities include recruiting and training certified VA sponsors under the Veteran Sponsorship Initiative, conducting risk assessments, and connecting transitioning service members to housing, employment, education, healthcare, and financial resources. Regional task forces will coordinate with local VSOs, nonprofits, and county agenci
1061.direct_services: Direct services will be provided to transitioning service members, veterans, and their families through personalized case management, peer sponsorship, and coordinated access to critical resources. Each participant will receive a customized transition plan supported by a trained VA-certified sponsor, connecting them to housing assistance, employment opportunities, education benefits, financial lit
1061.population: The target population includes transitioning service members, veterans, and their families relocating to or residing in Florida. The program focuses on individuals within 12 months of military separation and recently transitioned veterans at higher risk of isolation or suicide. Through statewide coordination and community partnerships, the initiative is expected to serve approximately 1,200 transitioning service members annually, with indirect benefits reaching more than 5,000 veterans and famil
1061.outcome: Funding will enable the Florida Veterans Coalition to expand critical support and coordination services for transitioning service members, veterans, and their families across the state. Outcome measures will include: (1) the number of veterans and service members connected to housing, employment, education, and benefits assistance; (2) the number of individuals participating in suicide prevention, financial literacy, and wellness programs; (3) successful referrals to community and clinical partners for mental health and crisis intervention; and (4) engagement outcomes measured through partner reports, participant feedback, and verified follow-ups to ensure long-term stability and reintegrati

1452.description: This project will allow for the hardening and renovation of the Jefferson County Jail Facility. Jefferson County is a fiscally constrained county, and this is the county's only jail facility. It was constructed in 1998 and has not been renovated in the last 27 years. This project will enhance the facility's efficiency and improve the security and safety for the public, staff, and incarcerated individuals. The scope of work will include painting, replacing, and repairing all plumbing fixtures, metal security doors, locks, gutters, and ventilation systems to improve air quality and prevent further stormwater erosion due to collapsed and broken gutters. It will also include replacing the jail's kitchen exhaust system and upright freezer.
1452.purpose: Hardening and renovation of the Jefferson County Jail Facility. This project will provide a safer and more efficient jail for the citizens, officers and incarcerated individuals during their incarceration.
1452.activities: Renovations and upgrades to the jail facility will include painting the interior and exterior of the jail, new gutters, storm water piping and downspouts, a new ventilation system, new piping and plumbing, including the replacement of shower tiles (floor and wall), a new kitchen exhaust hood and upright freezer, and new detention facility metal doors, locks and replacing the existing hot water heaters with new boilers.
1452.direct_services: Providing a renovated more secure jail facility will ensure the citizens of Jefferson County a safer county by hardening the security of the jail facility.
1452.population: The target population would be persons with poor mental and physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, currently incarcerated persons and drug offenders.
1452.outcome: The expected benefit and outcome of this project with new paint will assist with preventing moisture from seeping in the stone and the general appearance of the facility. New gutters including storm water piping and downspouts will assist with mitigating erosion from storm water, a new ventilation system will provide cleaner air quality which will help prevent the transmission of viruses and illness mitigating both staff and incarcerated individuals from becoming ill. This will also keep staff from missing work with fewer sick days. New metal security doors and new locks will ensure the facility is secured.

1453.description: This project will be for the engineering and construction services to build and furnish an 18,000-square-foot Fire Rescue, EMS, Police, and Public Works headquarters on Town of Cross City owned property located at the northwest corner of NE 210th Avenue and NE 118th Street. The new building complex is immediately adjacent to City Hall and will accommodate police services, emergency services, fire rescue, public works. This new building will improve response times of emergency personal, facilitate ease of communication between departments, and provide a new headquarters for public works which is currently operating out of City Hall. This new facility will also serve as an emergency operations center as needed. The facility will position each entity to meet current standards for public safety buildings and to deliver new and improved public services that were not previously possible for an
1453.purpose: The requested funds will be used to design the Public Safety Facility building including the engineering, permitting, construction, construction management services, and furniture. The Town of Cross City's current public works facility and chief of police office (including the evidence room) is currently housed within City Hall. Due to limitations of the facility and continued population growth, a new building is required. This building complex will accommodate the Police Department, the Town's
1453.activities: The Town of Cross City will execute a contract for engineering, construction, and construction management services to begin constructing the new public works facility during phase II of construction and furnish accordingly.
1453.direct_services: Upon completion of the project, the citizens of Cross City and Dixie County will have improved fire services, police services and improved life, health, safety, and protection of property as a result of more efficient emergency operations and management system.
1453.population: The new public safety facility will service Cross City's 1,800 residents and seasonal visitors. It will also be a resource to Dixie County and its bordering towns and cities, which has a combined population of approximately 18,000 residents. The fire and police departments have mutual aid agreements to provide assistance to neighboring cities in times of crisis and emergency.
1453.outcome: The new facility will provide a place for training, community outreach, policing, and emergency shelters during natural disasters. It will provide improved response times for fire rescue, police and public works support. The benefit is the increased safety of citizens, visitors, and the business community. The outcome will be measured by collecting data on response times, impact of police and fire training activities, and number of residents served. In addition, the facility will include industry standards for safety to protect the health of our emergency responders and also extend the conditional life span of critical fire apparatus and support equipment. The police department will also hav

2453.description: Runway to Hope’s purpose is to ensure that no family has to battle pediatric cancer alone. Our Family Assistance Program supports families who are battling pediatric cancer by actively preventing eviction, car repossession, keeping the lights on, and putting food on their tables. With a pediatric cancer diagnosis, the needs are endless, as one in five families diagnosed are already living in poverty. The goal is to support families through financial assistance with basic needs, including mortgage/rent, transportation costs, utilities, toiletries during their treatment and funeral expenses to lay children to rest when their fight has ended. Additionally, the Total Wellness Program provides holistic support to families, addressing mental health needs, physical well-being and social connections.
2453.purpose: Runway to Hope ensures no family faces pediatric cancer alone. Each year, about 15,000 US children and over 1,000 in Florida are diagnosed, many living in Central Florida. Our Family Assistance Program actively prevents eviction, car repossession and utility shut-offs, while ensuring families have food and access to counseling, support groups and other wellness programs. Funds also cover essential needs such as rent/mortgage, groceries, utilities and funeral expenses, easing the burden of treatm
2453.activities: Runway to Hope's Family Assistance program will continue the direct emergency financial assistance program for constituents to apply to for help with basic necessities and funeral arrangements. Serving approximately 200 families annually, the program also continues providing a holistic total wellness approach to creating a thread of support within our community for pediatric cancer patients and their families through offering mental health support and physical rehabilitation.
2453.direct_services: Requested funding will provide financial assistance and supportive services to children with cancer and their families across seven Central Florida counties. Support covers essential expenses such as housing, utilities, transportation to and from treatment, groceries and funeral costs. It also funds counseling, family therapy, support groups and rehabilitation services, relieving financial strain,
2453.population: Countless lives are touched when a child is diagnosed with pediatric cancer including their immediate and extended family members. Our goal is to support several groups within the pediatric cancer community, including patients, parents, siblings, as well as those who have been affected by the death of a pediatric cancer patient and those who are considered survivors. Runway to Hope serves families across Orange, Seminole, Osceola, Lake, Polk, Volusia, and Brevard counties. An estimated 800 indiv
2453.outcome: Provide resources for gaps in support for our families who are battling pediatric cancer including preventing eviction, car repossessions, keeping utilities on, putting groceries on the table, providing transportation to get to and from treatment, as well as supporting families through the toughest time in their lives when their beloved child passes away so they can lay their soul to rest. The outcome is that no family should battle pediatric cancer alone and this will be measured by the individuals who are served and impacted through one of our programming initiatives.

3553.description: Funds needed for preliminary engineering, design, permitting, bidding, project management/administration, construction observation, engineering during construction, demolition, site development & construction of new two-story, 200-space parking garage to serve the County’s new Multi-Government Complex. Project replaces outdated facilities; ensures sufficient, safe, and convenient parking for citizenry, residents and employees accessing critical public services in this Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO).
3553.purpose: The goal is to construct a modern, two-story, 200-space parking garage that provides adequate, safe, and convenient parking for the County’s new Multi-Government Complex. The facility will replace outdated surface lots, reduce congestion, and support citizens and employees safe, efficient access to essential public services.
3553.activities: To seek contractual services for preliminary engineering, design, permitting, bidding, project management, demolition site preparation, and construction of the parking garage through the County's procurement policies and procedures.
3553.direct_services: Citizens will directly benefit from safe, well-lit, and secure parking that allows easy access to critical County services, including administrative, public safety, planning, and legal offices. The project will reduce traffic congestion, provide convenient access, and enhance public safety in the government complex area.
3553.population: Hardee County, which is a financially disadvantaged community (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.) that is located in a Rural Area of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes), citizenry, visitors, tourists, business community and surrounding areas. Greater than 27,000 expected to be served.

Measured by reduced recidivism and increased economic self-sufficiency, this initiative drives lasting change and safer communities.
