This supports cognitive development, attention span, and overall learning readiness.
1527.activities: The activities and services that will be provided include daily physical fitness and balanced cognitive/motor skills for all students.
1527.direct_services: Funds will build Crossroad Academy's first on-campus playground with safe, age-appropriate equipment, fencing, and surfacing. Students will engage in active play, gross motor skill development, and cooperative activities, promoting physical fitness, social-emotional growth, and a healthy, safe space for the entire school community.
1527.population: The target population is K-12 students living in Gadsden County and the community of Gadsden. This project will serve over 800 people.
1527.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of this project is to provide 75% of Crossroad Academy K-12 students an opportunity to engage in a minimum of 30 minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity daily on the new playground, contributing to improved cardiovascular fitness, gross motor skills, and overall health. The methodology by which this outcome will be measured by student participation and activity level tracking using a combination of teacher/PE staff logs, structured activity schedules, and periodic student surveys.

2328.description: The Heartland Youth Village campus is in need of asphalt removal and replacement that covers 178,119 sq. ft on a large piece of property for existing group homes/foster homes where collaborating partners provide safety, stability and caring relationships to nurture and heal hurting children and teenagers with high needs that have experienced trauma as a result of child abuse and neglect.
2328.purpose: The Heartland Youth Village campus is in need of removal and replacement of the asphalt roadway and parking throughout the campus that covers approximately 178,119 sq. feet where collaborating group home/foster care partners provide safety, stability and caring relationships to nurture and heal hurting children and teenagers in the foster care system with high needs that have experienced trauma as a result of abuse and neglect.
2328.activities: This allows for transportation providers, case managers, and visitors to access homes without safety hazards like potholes, flooding or uneven pavement. It will also create safer walking pathways for youth and staff from the bus stop and throughout the property on the Heartland Youth Village campus.
2328.direct_services: Direct placement services will be provided to children in the foster care system that are placed in a home on the Heartland Youth Village campus that includes supervision by staff/house parents, basic needs, transportation, normalcy activities, and mentoring for high needs youth that are in the foster care system and at-risk or involved with law enforcement or the Juvenile Justice System. Referral
2328.population: The target population served are children in the foster care system that have been removed from their homes in Polk, Highlands or Hardee counties due to abuse, neglect or abandonment. These may include children with poor mental/physical health, homeless, at-risk youth, developmentally delayed, victims of crime, economically disadvantaged, and grade school/high school students. The providers on campus could serve up to approximately 150 children in a 12-month period depending on the permanency pl
2328.outcome: The expected outcomes and methodology are: -Eliminate campus roadway maintenance costs by at least 95% within the first two years due to reduced patching and emergency repairs. This will be measured by tracking and comparing roadway maintenance expenses for the 2 years prior to the asphalt replacement compared to the two years following project completion. - 95% of children in out-of-home care will receive dental and medical services that is measured through the Community Based Care Agency Scorecard established by the Department of Children and Families. - Children will improve their mental health by being referred to mental health providers to receive the appropriate mental health services

2330.description: The Heartland Youth Village campus is in need of significant repairs and renovations for existing group homes, buildings, and on the property where collaborating partners can provide safety, stability and caring relationships to nurture and heal hurting children and teenagers with high needs that have experienced trauma as a result of child abuse and neglect.
2330.purpose: The Heartland Youth Village campus is in need of significant repairs and renovations for existing group homes/buildings where collaborating partners provide safety, stability and caring relationships to nurture and heal hurting children and teenagers in the foster care system with high needs that have experienced trauma as a result of abuse and neglect.
2330.activities: Repairs and renovations will be made to the property and homes to safely operate group homes that house children in foster care that are placed on the Heartland Youth Village campus. These programs serve high needs youth with emotional or behavioral health disorders.
2330.direct_services: Direct placement services will be provided to children in the foster care system that are placed in a home on the Heartland Youth Village campus that includes supervision by staff/house parents, basic needs, transportation, normalcy activities, and mentoring for high needs youth that are in the foster care system and at-risk or involved with law enforcement or the Juvenile Justice System. Referral
2330.population: The target population served are children in the foster care system that have been removed from their homes in Polk, Highlands or Hardee counties due to abuse, neglect or abandonment. These may include children with poor mental/physical health, homeless, at-risk youth, developmentally delayed, victims of crime, economically disadvantaged, and grade school/high school students. The providers on campus could serve up to approximately 150 children in a 12-month period depending on the permanency pl
2330.outcome: The expected outcomes and methodology are: - 95% of children in out-of-home care will receive dental and medical services that is measured through the Community Based Care Agency Scorecard established by the Department of Children and Families. - Children will improve their mental health by being referred to mental health providers to receive the appropriate mental health services based on their mental health needs which is measured by the referrals made to providers, assessments completed by providers, medication management and treatment plans to improve their mental well-being.

1532.description: We are constructing a waste water treatment plant at our regional industrial corridor. Due to increase in costs the construction of the waste water treatment plant is going to exceed the original estimate. This appropriation will help manage the gap in construction funding already received so that the plant stays on schedule.
1532.purpose: This will help offset the rise in construction costs that has occured since the project cost was initially estimated three years ago.
1532.activities: Continued next steps in the construction phase of the Waste Water Treatment Plant and help to avoid delays in getting the project operational so we may support new businesses.
1532.direct_services: Waste water treatment plant will directly serve new businesses at the Regional Industrial Corridor as well as citizens located in the area which are currently on septic systems.
1532.population: Waste water treatment plant will directly serve new businesses at the Regional Industrial Corridor as well as citizens located in the area which are currently on septic systems.
1532.outcome: This will increase and improve economic activity with more businesses, increased revenue for the county, and higher wage jobs. It will create immediate job opportunities for new residents and new jobs for existing residents, and provide a stronger tax base. Installation of a municipal waste water treatment plant would reduce the amount of septic tanks needed to support ongoing projects.

2202.description: The University of Miami Medical Training and Simulation Laboratory (MTSL) has been an important asset to the State of Florida through its development and dissemination of state-of-the-art life-saving training programs in prehospital response, emergency medicine, and surgery for medical, nursing, allied healthcare and 1st responders. The MTSL accomplishes this through the development and use of web-based and mobile multimedia learning systems and simulation technology. The specific goals are to: 1) Create and disseminate advanced prehospital training programs for Florida's first responders; 2) Develop patient simulation training scenarios that enhance hands-on advanced life-saving skills, practiced without risking real patients. These programs will focus on 1) responding to active shooter and hostile events; 2) responding to natural disasters such as hurricanes and floods; 3) supporting F
2202.purpose: The goals are to: 1) Create and disseminate advanced prehospital training programs for Florida's first responders; 2) Develop patient simulation training scenarios that enhance hands-on advanced life-saving skills, practiced without risking real patients. These programs will focus on 1) responding to active shooter and hostile events; 2) responding to natural disasters such as hurricanes and floods; 3) supporting Florida's rural communities by addressing and supporting their unique needs.
2202.activities: Advanced, lifesaving, critical skills for first responders (law enforcement / fire rescue / EMS) to respond to active shooter hostile events and natural disasters (hurricane). Advanced public health and preventive health services skills for fire rescue / EMS to serve as community paramedic.
2202.direct_services: These training programs focus on advanced lifesaving skills and recommend best practices for the pre-hospital management of active shooter/assailant events, natural disasters (hurricanes) and public health and preventive health services for all populations.
2202.population: All Florida residents who are at risk of active shooter/assailant hostile events, and natural disasters (hurricanes), or who required need for prehospital and emergency, and public health services.
2202.outcome: Improvement of knowledge and skills in the response to active shooter/assailant hostile events, natural disasters (hurricanes) and pre-hospital community and public healthcare and services. These will be measured through surveys of 1st responders (law enforcement / EMS); Simulation scenarios, and examinations to assess knowledge and skills.

1378.description: Repaving and grading the non-motorized shared use path adjacent to SR-A1A and installing embedded crosswalk lighting at various points along SR-A1A.
1378.purpose: To increase pedestrian safety by: a) repaving and grading the non-motorized shared use path and b) installing embedded crosswalk lighting at various points along SR-A1A. Following the improvements made to A1A by the FDOT RRR Project, changes in elevation and drainage patterns have led to flooding at several points on the shared use path, creating hazards for pedestrians and cyclists. The proposed project will ensure safe and reliable multimodal transportation along and across A1A.
1378.activities: Shared use path renovation - Elevating the existing walk path to improve drainage and reduce flooding, grading and compacting sub-base material for long-term stability, and repaving with ADA-compliant surfacing. Installation of embedded crosswalk lighting at various points along SR-A1A.
1378.direct_services: Shared use path renovation - Elevating the existing walk path to improve drainage and reduce flooding, grading and compacting sub-base material for long-term stability, and repaving with ADA-compliant surfacing. Installation of embedded crosswalk lighting at various points along SR-A1A.
1378.population: All Town residents and pedestrians from neighboring communities that utilize the shared use path and crosswalks.
1378.outcome: Consistent accessibility of the shared use path and increased visibility when using crosswalks, both of which enhance pedestrian safety. Documenting pre and post construction conditions (flooding intensity and frequency) and tracking the number of safety and health incidents between pedestrians/cyclists and vehicles.

1144.description: The Administration (AD) Building on our Boca Raton campus was built in 1992 and has not had any major remodeling since original construction. Boca Raton is the fastest growing of our five campuses and makes an easy transition for students to transfer to Florida Atlantic University with its co-location. Goals of this remodel include providing our students with the most efficient, systematic, and technologically enhanced process for enrolling, recognizing newer generations of “tech-savvy", digital natives. Safety and security enhancements will also be major considerations in the planning and design phase.
1144.purpose: By remodeling the space, College employees will be able to better serve our students, family, faculty, staff and ensure the safety and security of the population of those entering our campus.
1144.activities: Costs would be directly spent on remodeling the Boca Raton Administration (AD) Building, which houses our student services, ranging from registration, enrollment, counseling, testing, financial and and disability services. Space utilization, technology upgrades and major safety and security considerations will be considered as designing and planning stages occur.
1144.direct_services: An overall better and more efficient experience will be provided for students, families, guests, faculty and staff.
1144.population: All students, families, faculty, staff and general public. Over 10,000 students consider the Boca Raton Campus as their home campus.
1144.outcome: Measurable outcomes may include reduced wait times for student services as well as a smoother transition between service areas. Student, parent, faculty and staff satisfaction should therefore increase in tandem. Ideally, the increase in positive outcomes in the student services area would result in more completions and graduations.

2061.description: Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office will contract for services with a firm with expertise in Forensic Investigative Genetics Genealogy. This funding will help to solve up to 75 cases.
2061.purpose: These funds will be used to conduct testing in active criminal cases or for the purposes of identifying human remains.
2061.activities: Specialized DNA testing and genealogical research to give closure to relatives of victims of homicides as well as identifying suspects in active violent crime cases.
2061.direct_services: Safer community due to alleged criminals being identified and arrested. Families of victims will receive justice for lost loved ones.
2061.outcome: Closure for relatives of victims of homicides as well as identifying suspects in active violent crime cases.

2062.description: This project will restore, maintain, and monitor 21 acres of submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) to the North Fork St. Lucie River, an important tributary to the Indian River Lagoon. The project is based on a successful pilot effort that showed native SAV can establish & spread in the Northern St. Lucie River when protected from grazing pressure.
2062.purpose: The primary goal of this project is to restore and enhance 21 acres of native submerged aquatic vegetation in the North Fork St. Lucie River.
2062.activities: The project will allow for restoration to occur by installing 107,000 native SAV planting units. 525 herbivory exclusion devices will be installed to protect plants from grazers. The project includes a 12 month maintenance program designed to ensure planting unit success.
2062.direct_services: The project will improve water quality, enhance recreational/commercial fishing, and improve the ecotourism industry. Improved water quality means more fish will be available for recreational anglers, increasing local economic activity at bait and tackle shops, restaurants, hotels, etc..
2062.population: The target population are individuals that live and vacation in St. Lucie County. This could impact local residents totaling up to 390,000 people.
2062.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of the project is the restoration and enhancement of 21 acres of native submerged aquatic vegetation in the North Fork St. Lucie River, an important tributary to the Indian River Lagoon.

2145.description: Restoration of the mangrove islands of the Jupiter Narrows north of Cato's Bridge in Palm Beach County in the Village of Tequesta through the construction of a limestone breakwater, limestone toe protections, seabed stabilization, seagrass planting, and mangrove planting.
2145.purpose: Restoration of mangrove islands, improvement of essential fish habitat, improvement of wildlife abundance in the Jupiter Narrows.
2145.activities: This money will fund the construction of breakwaters and other environmental engineering to restore and protect mangrove islands in the lower Indian River Lagoon.
2145.direct_services: Enhanced wildlife recreation areas, improved fisheries, better enjoyment of nature.
2145.population: Floridians in Palm Beach and Martin Counties and those who enjoy the beautiful lower Indian River Lagoon and the Jupiter Inlet area. The impacts extend to millions of Floridians.
2145.outcome: The FDEP is the permitting authority, and it will measure success by showing that manatees, fish, birds, seagrass, mangroves, sea turtles and other wildlife benefit from the restoration, and by showing that Floridians will benefit in terms of improved and protected ecosystem services provided by mangroves and seagrasses.

1150.description: ChildNet is the Community Based Care Lead Agency for Palm Beach County and is responsible for arranging supervision for parent-child visits in the child welfare system. In Palm Beach County, parent-child visitation is generally court ordered three times per week for dependency cases involving a child’s removal from their parent’s care and custody due to allegations of abuse, neglect, and abandonment. ChildNet supports visitation through scheduling, operational coordination, transportation, supervision of the visits, and reports to the court. Due to the high volume of visitation, and the vast size of Palm Beach County, a significant need exists for an expanded visitation space at the current Palm Beach location, along with an additional visitation center in the southern portion of the county to adequately provide the space and geographic accessibility to accommodate the volume of visitati
1150.purpose: The purpose will be to provide a safe and family-friendly environment for parents and children involved in the local foster care system to visit with one another allowing for maintained relationships, attachment, child nurturing, and reduction of trauma. Along with those critical reasons, the ultimate goal is to increase the chances of family reunification as quickly as it is safe to do so. A research study by Davis, Landverk, Newton, and Ganger, "Parental Visiting and Foster Care Reunification,
1150.activities: ChildNet will provide supervised visitation for parent-child visits involved in the child welfare system in Palm Beach County where a child has been removed from the parent's care and custody due to abuse, neglect, and/or abandonment. Service array delivered by Visitation Monitors, Visitation Specialists, and Transportation Specialists will include scheduling visits, coordinating visitation logistics, providing direct in-person supervision of the visits, transporting children to and from visits
1150.direct_services: Direct services to the citizens will include supervision of family visitation, scheduling, transportation, and completion of required reports to the court.
1150.population: Target population includes both children and parents with an open legal dependency case in Palm Beach County and the child(ren) has been removed from the parent's care and custody due to abuse, neglect, and/or abandonment. Ages of the children may range from 0-18; parents may be any age. ChildNet's Palm Beach visitation program will serve 152 children annually.
1150.outcome: Supervised Visitation will be provided for a minimum of 152 children annually (38 children quarterly). At least 80% of target will be achieved each quarter and annually. The measure will be determined by dividing the total number of children who received supervised visitation by the number of program participants.

1391.description: The Firefighter Cancer Initiative (FCI) is a unique program led by the University of Miami Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, which was awarded designation from the National Cancer Institute (NCI). This program aims to understand and address why firefighters are at increased risk of developing and dying of cancer relative to the populations that they serve. FCI supports novel translational research, wide scale education and prevention initiatives, and collaboration with Firefighters to develop and implement practices that can reduce noxious exposures associated with disease.
1391.purpose: The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) has classified the Working group of occupational exposure as a firefighter as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1), on the basis of sufficient evidence for cancer in humans. With this classification, FCI will continue to expand firefighters’ access to cancer screening through our mobile clinic, which provides screenings on-site at fire stations locally; expand access to clinical screenings in remote and rural areas of the state of Florida; provi
1391.activities: Expand research on characterizing firefighter cancer, including volunteer and wildland firefighters as well as expand access to cancer screening and earlier detection of disease through two mobile clinics; expand access for all fire service personnel across the state to education on best practices for cancer risk reduction and prevention strategies, including virtual curriculum and education modules for firefighters and firefighter cancer survivors; and tailored guidelines for subgroups; identif
1391.direct_services: Funds are invested in increasing participation in cancer screening and prevention for cancers overrepresented among active and retired firefighters, including access to these services through a unique mobile clinical infrastructure. Additionally, funds will support the expansion of clinical services to wildland firefighters and firefighters in remote and rural areas. FCI will develop a resource ce
1391.population: The Firefighter Cancer Initiative serves the Florida fire service, both career and volunteer firefighters including fire subgroups (investigators, wildland, trainers and urban search and rescue (USAR)). FCI has engaged over 13,000 in research projects, over 1,000 firefighters have been screened by the FCI clinical team. We anticipate increasing this number by 1,000 in the coming year as well as continuing in our efforts nationally, as FCI leads the national conversation on cancer in the fire ser
1391.outcome: FCI aims to increase the life expectancy of firefighters and their families by better understanding cancer risks related to occupational exposures. FCI research findings will result in developing new safety standards and best practices to reduce firefighters’ increased risk of developing and dying of cancer. Outcomes will be measured in various ways, including number of firefighters engaged; number of firefighters screened for cancer; successful new technologies to monitor exposure; number of tumor specimens submitted to the tumor bank to identify biomarkers and therapeutics; continued analysis of the dataset linking the Florida Cancer Data System with State firefighter data. We plan to incr

2765.description: The Town of Oakland is planning for the next phase of the South Lake Apopka Initiative. This wastewater system extension project known as the "N. Pollard Street Wastewater Extension" is the next step in removing existing septic systems from the south shore of Lake Apopka in our town. The Oakland portion of this plan is to design and construct 11 manholes and approximately 3000 feet of gravity sewer in older parts of the town. The project will also include abandonment of approximately 40 existing septic systems, some relief from wastewater impact fees, and connection to the central sewer. This network will connect to approximately 4500 feet of DEVELOPER FUNDED gravity sewer already constructed that serves 53 new residences, and will also utilize an existing TOWN FUNDED lift station in the effort to minimize costs. Additional extensions to the east and south, adjacent to Lake Apopka, will
2765.purpose: Further elimination of existing septic systems along the southern shore of Lake Apopka, a nutrient impacted water body with a Basin Management Action Plan in place.
2765.activities: Design activities, construction administration activities, and construction of infrastructure.
2765.direct_services: Elimination of new and existing septic systems and some relief from wastewater impact fees.
2765.population: New and existing residents of the Town of Oakland. Approximately 400 to 500 individuals will be served when the overall project has been completed. (Town funding for Lift Station #7, developer contribution (Briley Farms), and this request).
2765.outcome: The expected benefits are creation of construction jobs, elimination of owner-operated septic systems, groundwater quality improvement, surface water quality improvement. Methodology to measure success will include number of construction jobs created, number of septic systems eliminated, and by measuring improvements in the overall health of the Lake Apopka aquatic system and adjacent groundwaters.

1280.description: Agape Network, Inc., based in Miami, Florida, will expand its Re-Entry Program to strengthen comprehensive post- release services for individuals returning to the community from the Miami-Dade County Corrections and Rehabilitation Department and at-risk individuals. Through a holistic, evidence-based model, the program addresses substance use, mental health, physical wellness, and spiritual development to promote successful reintegration and long-term stability.
1280.purpose: Improve Mental Health and Substance Use - Access to timely integrated behavioral health and primary care for uninsured and under-insured low-income residents; increases in medication management; decreases in hospitalizations/institutional settings; and decreases in criminal justice costs associated with involvement in crime/infractions by those experiencing mental illness. Reduce Substance Abuse - Decreases in criminal justice costs associated with involvement in crime/infractions by those exper
1280.activities: Access to Care (uninsured), Chronic Disease Management, Availability of Primary and Preventive Care, Barriers Accessing Continuum of Care, Mental Health and Substance Abuse, Peer Support, High Standards of Care, Supportive Housing, Prevention, Family Involvement, and Communication with the Community and Criminal Justice System.
1280.direct_services: Direct services include: Psychiatric evaluations, medication management, Medication assisted treatment, wellness checks, assisting with job placement, linking to vocational or traditional school settings, linkage to economic resources, Peer support, and individual therapy sessions.
1280.population: Between 51 and 100 persons who are reentering the community following incarceration or jail from State or County correctional facilities, as well as those who are considered at risk individuals.
1280.outcome: Average annual days worked for pay for adults with severe and persistent mental illness (Target: 40 days) Percentage change employed from substance abuse treatment admission to discharge (Target: 10%); Percent change in number arrested 30 days prior to admission versus 30 days prior to discharge (Target: 15%); Percent complete treatment (Target: 51%); Percent with stable housing at discharge (Target: 86%). Address behavioral health disorders (mental health/substance abuse) coupled with chronic disease management to foster better health outcomes leading to reductions is missed days at work and/or unemployment.

1175.description: The Center for Educational Strategy and Innovation will build upon the FAU Lab Schools' success and provide professional development to teachers, administrators and educational leaders at schools throughout Florida, with the goal of supporting the replication of the FAU Lab Schools model across the State of Florida. By empowering educators to engage students in tackling real-world challenges and collaborating on solutions, the Center will foster essential skills like critical thinking and problem-solving while nurturing their creativity and innovation necessary for today's rapidly changing landscape.
1175.purpose: FAU and FAU Lab Schools have developed world-class K-12 educational programs and built state-of-the-art facilities that serve as a blueprint for how to approach education. The new Center will build upon the FAU lab school district's success as a model for K-12 education and provide professional development to teachers, administrators and educational leaders at schools throughout Florida. The goal of the institute is to support the replication of the FAU Lab Schools model across the state.
1175.activities: The goal of the Center is to develop and equip educational leaders and teachers to facilitate project-based, competition-centric learning crucial for preparing students for the challenges they will face in the future. By engaging students in tackling real-world challenges and collaborating on solutions, the Center will teach essential skills like critical thinking and problem-solving by further preparing educators and K-12 leaders to foster these skills in their students.
1175.direct_services: Students, teachers and educational leaders and entire communities will benefit as the Center produces workforce- ready students in fields such as healthcare, engineering, computer science, architectural design, robotics, and artificial intelligence throughout the state of Florida.
1175.population: The target population that the Center will serve includes K-12 teachers, administrators and leaders in the State of Florida, but the individuals served will extend beyond this population to also include the students and families that they serve through the overall improvement in the quality of K-12 education in Florida.
1175.outcome: By expanding the FAU Lab Schools approach throughout Florida, we can measure the tangible benefits of incorporating project-based, competition-centric learning into educational practices and highlight its potential to positively impact student outcomes in grades K-12 for replication. Future model execution will be measured by a robust analytics system utilizing both baseline and post hoc data including school and contextual factors such as student participation, attendance, grade point average, discipline, competitive achievements, and performance on state- standardized assessments (FAST & EOC) in English Language Arts, mathematics, science, and social studies.

2766.organization: United Foundation of Central Florida, INc
2766.description: UFCF-YIEI is a prevention-based, workforce-higher education aligned after-school initiative combating academic gaps, youth violence, and economic immobility across Central Florida. It integrates STEAM, digital literacy, financial resilience, and civic leadership to prepare at-risk youth for Florida’s future workforce and strengthen community safety and prosperity. An expansion of UFCF’s Future Leaders United After-School Enrichment & Mentoring Program. Aimed at reducing youth-related crime and improving college and career outcomes through structured after-school engagement, mentorship, and early workforce exposure.
2766.purpose: UFCF-YIEI is a prevention-based, workforce-higher education aligned after-school initiative combating academic gaps, youth violence, and economic immobility across Central Florida. It integrates STEAM, digital literacy, financial resilience, and civic leadership to prepare at-risk youth for Florida’s future workforce and strengthen community safety and prosperity. An expansion of UFCF’s Future Leaders United After-School Enrichment & Mentoring Program.
2766.activities: Operation of four Youth Empowerment Learning Practicums, each providing hands-on experience in STEAM & Innovation, Financial Resilience & Entrepreneurship, Health, Wellness & Civic Leadership, and College & Career Readiness. Mentoring, tutoring, and service-learning projects integrating community improvement and social responsibility. Family workshops to strength intergenerational stability.
2766.direct_services: Hands-on enrichment, academic tutoring, workforce simulation labs, leadership development, mental-health and wellness sessions, FAFSA and college navigation support, and local service projects improving neighborhood safety and cohesion.
2766.population: Primary: At-risk youth (Grades 6-12) from Title I schools Secondary: Parents/guardians and young adults ages 18-24 Demographics: Economically disadvantaged, minority-majority households in Central Florida
2766.outcome: The project will improve academic performance, career readiness, and economic self-sufficiency among at-risk youth while reducing juvenile involvement in crime. Outcomes will be measured through pre-/post-assessments, academic progress reports, college enrollment and certification rates, attendance data, and community impact surveys.

1662.description: Las Olas Chabad is not only a place of worship for the Jewish Community, but also a place of service open to everyone in the entire community including persons with Autism, developmental, and intellectual disabilities. Their unique location in the heart of town provides a strong sense of belonging and a unique inclusion component for participants training in the Friendship Circle Program. It prepares participants with skills for employment in the community. The Friendship Grill located on Las Olas, and open to the public, provides culinary training and work experience for program participants. Friendship Circle provides assistance, life skills and additional supports to individuals with special needs and their families through social, educational and vocational programming. In addition to helping those in need, the Friendship Circle enriches its network of volunteers by enabling them to
1662.purpose: Hands-on training through our Life Skills and Job Training Program, including real-world experience in the Friendship Grill Restaurant, job coaching, and employment assistance for participants. The Grill, located in the heart of Downtown Fort Lauderdale, connects our students with the community and local businesses while they build transferable skills. Our purpose is to instill self-sufficiency, confidence, independence, and pathways to meaningful employment for adults with autism, developmental
1662.activities: Life skills and Job training program, regular trips to potential employers, generalization of skills in various jobs & environments. Skills training consisting of food preparation, proper use of equipment, inventory, stocking shelves, greeting customers, taking orders, cash register operation, financial literacy, etc.
1662.direct_services: Opportunities for participants to become skilled and receive continued support and training. Strategic partnerships with community members and employers in restaurants, retail, and catering. Promotion of inclusive efforts to hire participants in local and community businesses. Helping participants to become confident, independent, employed and productive.
1662.population: Individuals with Autism and other developmental and intellectual disabilities. We can service 40 developmentally disabled individuals with over 50 volunteers.
1662.outcome: Training and job opportunities, supportive employment placements, and on-campus Friendship Grill experience. Our participants are trained to have the skills necessary to be successful and productive members in both their home and community. We provide support and resources for them to be able to succeed. We track skill development over multiple jobs and environments.

1663.organization: Friendship Circle of Greater Ft. Lauderdale
1663.description: Completion of 11,000 square foot Inclusive Community Center for persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities. It is a place of service open to everyone. A unique locations provides and inclusion component for on the job training in the program and prepares participants with skills for employment and to be part of the community. The building will also include other opportunities for life skills training, and developing skills to receive practical experience in other jobs and therapy.
1663.purpose: To help individuals with disabilities prepare for gainful employment and be part of the community. There will also be a large fully operational kitchen & restaurant for our students to develop skills and receive real life work experience. In addition, the building will contain a sensory room, music center, art studio, exercise room, a beautiful garden & other amenities.
1663.activities: There will be 5 Life Skills & Job Training Classrooms to further grow this very needed program to help individuals with disabilities prepare for gainful employment. There will also be a large fully operational kitchen & restaurant for our students to use to further their skills in receiving real life work experience.
1663.direct_services: Providing the community and families of persons with disabilities and special needs the help they need to continue to work and prosper so all members of their families, no matter what their special needs, can thrive in a safe place they can depend on. Assisting families in need and providing a welcoming place to learn, socialize, volunteer, prepare participants for employment and become more indep
1663.population: Families and persons with special needs, autism, intellectual and developmental disabilities, physically disabled, and those not eligible to receive services from APD or those who are pre-registered and not yet receiving services. We expect to serve an additional 200 plus individuals and their families.
1663.outcome: Individuals with disabilities, who would not likely otherwise become employable or employed because of their physical health, receive training, get jobs and become less dependent on assistance. Participants who attend will complete various age appropriate programs, become more independent, maintain employment within the community, implement life skills to acquire friendships and social independence.

1278.description: This proposal outlines a further enhanced TAP program aimed at closing the skills gap by providing financial assistance and training opportunities for individuals entering or advancing in their careers. The program strengthens the manufacturing workforce by expanding access to standardized, industry-recognized training. Efforts will target the next generation of talent, including unemployed or under-employed individuals, veterans, ex-offenders, high school students, adult-education (GED) learners, and those in career transition or seeking career advancement. The program will emphasize high-demand fields such as aerospace, advanced technology, logistics, and aviation mechanics. Additionally, the talent-attraction component will elevate Florida’s Space Coast manufacturing companies as a premier destination for career growth—helping ensure the industry remains strong, innovative, and econom
1278.purpose: By addressing workforce shortages in critical sectors, the program will drive local economic growth and improve regional competitiveness. It will empower individuals to secure stable, well-paid careers. The cascading effects—higher incomes, reduced unemployment, and stronger local economies—will benefit Brevard County, and the state of Florida, for decades to come.
1278.activities: Activities and services will promote manufacturing careers, highlight high-demand fields such as aerospace, advanced technology, logistics, and aviation mechanics, and support talent-attraction initiatives that position Florida’s Space Coast as a premier destination for manufacturing careers. Collectively, these services will build a stronger, more competitive workforce and enhance long-term economic growth in the community.
1278.direct_services: Access to financial resources for skills-based training with emphasis on attainment of industry certifications that align with existing industry needs and pathways to career advancement for personal prosperity.
1278.population: The project is designed to serve a diverse target population, including the unemployed, under-employed, veterans, ex- offenders, individuals in career transition or seeking career enhancement, non-college-bound youth, GED students, and incumbent manufacturing workers.
1278.outcome: The project's goal is to establish a talent pipeline that not only meets the demands of the local industry but also facilitates career advancement for the target population, enabling them to excel in a high-wage, high-tech sector. Quarterly reports and monitoring will enable ongoing assessment and adaptation of strategies to ensure the project's success in meeting both industry demands and individual career goals.

2883.description: Florida is home to one of the largest veteran populations in the nation, and many of these men and women continue to suffer from persistent symptoms of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) long after completing conventional VA care. Symptoms compromise veterans' ability to work, maintain family stability, reintegrate successfully, and participate fully in community life. These funds would establish a statewide program designed to provide highly specialized upper cervical craniocervical corrective care to 100 Florida veterans suffering from persistent post mTBI symptoms. This initiative directly targets the physiological root cause of chronic mTBI by identifying and correcting structural injury at the CCJ rather than treating downstream symptoms.
2883.purpose: To restore the health, productivity, and quality of life of Florida veterans suffering from mild traumatic brain injury by providing upper cervical care that addresses root neurological dysfunction at the craniocervical junction. The project will serve 100 veterans, collect and publish outcome data, and establish a cost-effective, evidence-based and first-in- the-nation standard of care that reduces long-term healthcare dependence.
2883.activities: Provide precision upper cervical imaging, evaluation, and corrective care for 100 veterans with mild traumatic brain injury. Data on neurological, vascular, and glymphatic improvements will be collected and published to validate a root- cause model of recovery addressing craniocervical dysfunction.
2883.direct_services: Veterans will receive targeted correction of upper cervical misalignment to restore brainstem and neurological signaling, improve cerebral blood flow and glymphatic system function, and reduce chronic post-concussive symptoms such as headaches, dizziness, and cognitive impairment for lasting recovery.
2883.population: 100 veterans with mild traumatic brain injuries.
2883.outcome: Veterans will experience measurable reductions in headaches, dizziness, balance issues, and neck pain through correction of upper cervical misalignment, with restored neurological function, mobility, and postural control demonstrating improved physical stability and performance. Neurological and postural exams, range-of-motion testing using computerized motion tracking, and validated symptom inventories at baseline, 30, and 90 days. Participants will demonstrate improved mood stability, reduced anxiety and sleep disturbance, and fewer PTSD-related symptoms as autonomic balance is restored through improved brainstem regulation, cerebral perfusion, and glymphatic function. Changes in mental he

3307.description: The City of Palm Bay (City) is requesting state appropriations or grant support to provide monetary assistance in continued expansion of the City's fiber infrastructure. As the City aims to comply with NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) standards, the fiber infrastructure expansion would separate the City’s utility and non-utility network infrastructure and establish a continuous underground fiber optic cabling solution to remote City facilities while enriching the overall resident experience. Upon completion, most City facilities will connect to a redundant network fiber ring, eliminating outages due to a single point of failure and reducing recurring local internet service provider communication fees, resulting in a more resilient network. This is Phase 4 of a project previously funded under the Florida Digital Service aimed to enhance cybersecurity and harden critic
3307.purpose: Continued enhancement of the City's cybersecurity network, providing a redundant underground network fiber ring, eliminating outages due to a single point of failure, resulting in a more resilient network and hardened cybersecurity infrastructure.
3307.activities: The City will utilize existing contracts to continue expansion of the fiber network.
3307.direct_services: As a municipal services provider, the enhanced cybersecurity will better secure private information stored on the City's network, as well as, isolate the utilities system to avoid cybersecurity incidents through the City's utilities infrastructure.
3307.population: The general public of Palm Bay, FL. Palm Bay has a rapidly growing population of approximately 148,000 residents.
3307.outcome: The expected benefit and outcome of this project is enhanced cybersecurity to protect the City's operational network and utilities infrastructure, which will safeguard the City and the residents of Palm Bay. This expansion will also provide hardened infrastructure in the event of emergencies, man-made or natural, which will protect the organization and citizen data and reduce the time off-line due to an emergency event or bad actor.

1276.description: State funding will support Seminole County's implementation of Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) by accelerating the transition to a modern, data-driven water system. This technology will enhance operational efficiency, improve leak detection, reduce unaccounted-for water loss, and empower customers to better manage their usage,promoting long- term water conservation. These improvements directly align with state and regional goals for resource conservation, resiliency, and infrastructure modernization. The project includes replacing more than 8,000 water meters connected to potable water systems that influence the minimum flows and levels (MFLs) of Wekiwa Springs,an Outstanding Florida Spring,as well as the Little Wekiva River, the Wekiva River, and Lake Sylvan. The importance of water conservation in these sensitive areas is underscored by Chapter 373, Florida Statutes, which estab
1276.purpose: State funding will help close the remaining financial gap, enabling Seminole County Utilities to accelerate the upgrade of its metering infrastructure technology. This investment will allow approximately 8,000 utility customers to proactively monitor and address leaks, promoting water conservation, reducing water loss, protecting the Upper Floridan Aquifer and Outstanding Florida Springs, improving operational efficiency, and mitigating financial impacts on the utility and its customers.
1276.activities: Installation of upgraded meter reading technology and 8,000 water meters for residential and commercial use within Seminole County's utility service area.
1276.direct_services: The Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) project will provide direct benefits to approximately 8,000 Seminole County utility customers by enabling real-time monitoring of water usage through upgraded smart meters. This technology empowers residents to: Detect and address leaks quickly, reducing costly water loss and property damage. Track daily water consumption through user-friendly digital too
1276.population: The primary population served by this project includes Seminole County Utility customers connected to the County's potable water system. The project will directly benefit approximately 8,000 residential and commercial utility customers through the installation of upgraded smart meters. Indirectly, the entire Seminole County community, more than 475,000 residents, will benefit from improved water conservation, enhanced resource protection, and greater operational efficiency within the County's ut
1276.outcome: The primary outcome of this project is the modernization of Seminole County's water metering infrastructure, resulting in improved operational efficiency, enhanced water conservation, and increased customer engagement. Project success will be measured using both quantitative and qualitative performance indicators, including: Leak detection and response metrics, reduction in average leak duration and volume of unaccounted-for water.Customer participation and behavior data, percentage of customers accessing usage data and reducing consumption. Water conservation outcomes, measurable decrease in per-capita water demand across the utility service area. Operational efficiency metrics, reduction i

2331.description: The Gilmore Outpatient expansion project is the second phase of a two phase project where the three current buildings on the campus will be adjoined to create a single health services complex. Interior and exterior renovations and modifications will occur including installation of a new roof, proper fire suppression, technology, security, electrical, HVAC, plumbing, and emergency generator systems. With the added space, we will be able to hire additional staff and accommodate up to 720 additional clients in the future to keep pace with community growth. Additionally, we will create a single point of access for the security of clients and staff.
2331.purpose: Increase the efficiency, security, and usability of the Gilmore Campus by improving continuity of care and enhancing the client experience of the 200+ individuals the location sees daily. We will create a single point of access for the security of clients and staff and will better serve clients through provision of outpatient therapy and medication management, primary health care, pharmacy services, care coordination, substance use disorder services, and assertive community treatment.
2331.activities: Peace River Center will renovate the Gilmore Campus to expand usable space, adding 12 offices, a community education room, lobby space, and three registration stations. The added space allows hiring three to five licensed therapists and two bachelor’s-level care coordinators, increasing capacity to serve up to 720 additional clients in the future and better meeting community needs.
2331.direct_services: This project allows us to better serve clients through the provision of outpatient therapy and medication management, primary health care, pharmacy services, care coordination, substance use disorder services, assertive community treatment, as well as community education.
2331.population: The majority of the funds requested will serve these target populations or groups: elderly persons, persons with mental illness, persons with poor physical health, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, homeless, persons with substance use disorders, victims of crime, and domestic violence and sexual assault victims. We anticipate serving more than 700 individuals from these target populations or groups.
2331.outcome: Peace River Center (PRC) will improve the behavioral and physical health of individuals receiving outpatient services at the Gilmore Campus. The Gilmore Outpatient Expansion Project will increase usable space allowing for hiring additional staff and providing more services. Outcomes will be measured by tracking client scores from the PHQ-9 and PSC-17 assessments at admission, at intermittent points during care, and at discharge. Physical health outcomes will be documented on client records from the Wellness Clinic on the campus.

2332.description: As the State prepares to adopt CCBHC model, funds will sustain CCBHC services that expand access to evidence- based mental health and substance use treatment. The program enhances care coordination, community engagement, and quality improvement to reduce wait times, close care gaps, and promote health equity. It supports recovery and service continuity.
2332.purpose: Funds will support services that meet Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) standards, enhancing delivery in the catchment area. They will reduce wait times from screening to intake, ensuring timely access. Funds will also improve outcomes for individuals with Serious Mental Illness (SMI), Serious Emotional Disturbance (SED), and Substance Use Disorders (SUD). This request addresses a funding gap from October 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
2332.activities: CCBHC improves access to evidence-based treatment for mental illness and substance use issues, along with their related health and social impacts, in community-based settings. It enhances evidence-based practices through data- driven interventions, which includes care coordination, community engagement, and a model of continuous quality improvement.
2332.direct_services: Care coordination offers direct services to the community aimed at closing gaps in care by improving access to mental health and substance use treatment. This ultimately enhances health outcomes. The initiatives focus on raising awareness, promoting health equity, and building partnerships with community stakeholders to increase access to care and support recovery.
2332.population: The project will serve more than 800 individuals, including elderly persons, individuals with serious mental illness or substance use disorders, those with poor physical health, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, people experiencing homelessness, victims of crime, and survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault.
2332.outcome: The project will improve mental and physical health, reduce substance use and recidivism, and enhance economic stability for 800+ individuals. Outcomes include reduced wait times, timely follow-up, medical screenings, medication- assisted treatment (MAT) with overdose prevention, job support, transportation access, and culturally appropriate care, all measured through data tracking, surveys, and progress verification.

2146.description: Build a program that would strengthen relationships between student government leaders in Florida’s public universities and Israel’s universities. Floridian students would learn about the importance of democracy, Israel’s place in the world, and the dangers of the terror organizations in neighboring countries that seek to cause harm not only to Israel but also to America and anyone who pursues Western values; Operational support for South Florida Regional Intelligence Center that liaises with law enforcement to monitor extremists and potential threats not only to the Jewish community, but for all religious communities and other groups who may be targets; Combat antisemitism by collaborating with Jewish educational nonprofits to provide resources and educational programming to School Boards throughout the State as well as public, private and charter schools; Convene Jewish nonprofits that
2146.purpose: We will combat antisemitism and grow Israel support among politically minded college students and future political leaders; operate a Regional Threat Center that works closely with law enforcement to protect Jewish people and all Floridians who may be targeted by hate groups and hateful individuals; collaborate with public, private and charter schools to combat antisemitism; and convene Jewish nonprofits to reduce duplicative efforts in these spaces.
2146.activities: We will build an educational trip to Israel for top political leaders in student government organizations; provide licensing to research analysts to scour the dark web for extremist activities; and collaborate with educational nonprofits to provide programming to School Boards and schools to combat antisemitism. We will also convene a working committee or board of nonprofits focused on supporting Israel and antisemitism to help govern the Miami Alliance Against Antisemitism.
2146.direct_services: All Floridians will be safer because they will be less susceptible to terror attacks due to the information sharing between law enforcement and the Regional Threat Center. Additionally, K-12 will be safer for Jewish students because of curriculum on the dangers of antisemitism offered to schools throughout the state. And future political leaders in Florida will have had a chance to visit Israel an
2146.population: We have an opportunity to impact millions of Floridians. All Floridians will be safer with more resources monitoring the dark web to prevent extremist attacks. All Jewish students will have an opportunity to be safer in school because of curriculum helping to fight antisemitism. And the Israel education piece will be offered to students in public universities throughout the state.
2146.outcome: Safer citizens; safer public, private and charter school experiences; and student government leaders who better understand the importance of democracy and the conflict in the Middle East.

2333.description: The Community Mobile Support Team (CMST) will work with law enforcement in a collaborative partnership to identify individuals who experienced a mental health crisis and were admitted to in-patient services as a result of a law enforcement Baker Act. These individuals will receive follow up services from CMST staff within 10 days after the Baker Act, which will reduce recidivism and has reduced law enforcement-initiated Baker Acts by more than 10% each year since program implementation.
2333.purpose: Funds will place CMST counselors in local law enforcement substations to reduce Baker Act admissions and provide follow-up within 10 days of discharge. This partnership frees law enforcement (LE) to address other calls while CMST focuses on post–Baker Act care, diverting individuals to community services. Working with the Sheriff's Office and local LE agencies, CMST aims to reduce Baker Act admissions and readmissions in our community.
2333.activities: CMST provides post–Baker Act follow-up, outreach, and crisis assessment. Counselors in law enforcement substations work with officers to assess and de-escalate crises not requiring a Baker Act, connect individuals to needed services, and link them with community-based resources. These efforts divert or prevent Baker Acts while ensuring timely access to appropriate care and resources.
2333.direct_services: CMST provides post–Baker Act follow-up, outreach, and crisis assessment. Counselors embedded in law enforcement substations assist with intervention and follow-up for individuals in crisis, diverting arrests by addressing immediate needs, and connecting people to resources, thus reducing further crises and helping avoid unnecessary Baker Act admissions.
2333.population: The target population served by this project is persons who have been under a law enforcement-initiated Baker Act and persons in crisis that don't require a Baker Act. We expect to serve more than 800 individuals annually.
2333.outcome: Peace River Center (PRC) will improve mental health and reduce recidivism of individuals who were under a Baker Act initiated by law enforcement. The provision of follow up services within 10 days of discharge from a Baker Act has shown decreased suicidality and improved overall mental health, as demonstrated by the Columbia Suicide Risk Assessment and PHQ-9/PSC-17 assessments. In 2024, CMST provided more than 7,400 follow up services to 2,371 people resulting in a 14% reduction in Baker Acts initiated by law enforcement.

2335.description: A $15 million recurring operational investment to support Florida Poly’s growth to 3,000 students by 2030. Funds will expand high-tech degree programs, increase faculty hiring, strengthen student support services, and improve retention and graduation outcomes. This initiative ensures Florida continues producing top-tier STEM graduates who drive innovation and high-wage economic growth.
2335.purpose: The requested operational enhancement will accelerate Florida Polytechnic University’s strategic goal to increase enrollment to 3,000 students by 2030. This investment directly supports Florida’s demand for high-wage STEM talent by expanding programs that yield a high return on state investment, producing graduates whose median salaries and in-state employment rates consistently exceed System averages.
2335.activities: Funds will support the hiring of additional faculty and staff, the expansion of high-demand academic programs such as Aerospace Engineering and Cybersecurity, and the enhancement of student success services including tutoring, advising, and career readiness initiatives. Investments will also be made in laboratory equipment, instructional technology, and other academic infrastructure needed to sustain enrollment growth and program quality. These activities will ensure that students are well-prepa
2335.direct_services: Florida Poly will provide direct educational services to students through high-quality classroom instruction, hands-on research and laboratory experiences, mentoring, and career development programs. These services directly translate into workforce outcomes by preparing graduates for immediate employment in high-wage, high-skill STEM fields. With graduates earning an average salary above $62,000 a
2335.population: The target population includes current and future undergraduate and graduate students pursuing STEM degrees in engineering, computer science, and related applied sciences. The requested funding will directly serve approximately 3,000 students annually once full enrollment is achieved, and indirectly support hundreds of Florida employers that rely on access to a highly trained STEM workforce. This investment benefits both the students who receive direct services and the broader economy that depen
2335.outcome: The expected benefits include a 90 percent increase in annual STEM degree production (to approximately 550 degrees per year), improved four-year graduation rates reaching 60 percent, and retention rates increasing to 85 percent. Outcomes will also include greater in-state employment and wage growth among graduates, reflecting a direct ROI to Florida’s economy. Progress will be measured through established Board of Governors performance metrics, the University’s annual accountability plan, and verified post-graduation employment.

1735.description: The proposed stormwater improvement project in New Port Richey addresses frequent street and home flooding identified in the City’s 2013 Stormwater Master Drainage Plan. Key components include new stormwater inlets at Rio Drive (intersections with Wyoming and Lafayette), over 1,200 feet of various-sized stormwater pipes, an outfall and a baffle box to improve water quality.The project aims to enhance neighborhood resiliency by reducing flood risk during storms and protecting against rising river levels. It also aligns with the City’s Vulnerability Assessment, which highlights this low-lying area near the Pithlachascotee River as especially flood-prone due to sea-level rise and increased storm intensity.
1735.purpose: Goals are to provide an effective and resilient storm water system that improves the accessibility for the local community by ensuring the passage of the right of ways and reducing impacts on private property in the area. While also providing and economically and environmentally sound stormwater management system with the installation of the baffle box The installation of which would greatly reduce adverse impacts both on site and downstream, as a result of concentrated discharges.
1735.activities: The installation of approximately 1,200 linear feet of storm water pipe, inlets, catch basins, baffle box and outfall
1735.direct_services: Installation of necessary drainage infrastructure in an area as determined by the City’s 2013 Stormwater Master Drainage Plan, 10-Year Update
1735.population: Direct impacts of this project will involve the immediate area surrounding the project; approximately 100 residents. Indirectly, the improved stormwater treatment process will serve the entire City as it will improve the water quality of the Pithlachascotee river; approximately 18,000 residents.
1735.outcome: Improved water way conditions Reduce the pollutants such as hydrocarbons, nitrates and liter reaching the local water ways and estuaries; specifically the Pithlachascottee River Generate increase economic activity by improving water quality on local water ways; specifically the Pithlachascottee River Promote water way and estuary tourism by improving water quality on local water ways; specifically the Pithlachascottee River These benefits will be measured through the us of the following: 2013 Stormwater Master Drainage Plan Update. City of New Port Richey Pavement Management Plan Update Annual NPDES Water Quality Report Pasco County Office of Tourism Data

1664.description: Lighthouse Point is a small residential community and faces challenges in securing funding for large projects. Funds will provide for the construction phase of the NE 31 Court Bridge replacement. The bridge is over 50 years old, and has undergone multiple repairs. Due to the extremely aggressive marine environment, the bridge will continue to deteriorate. The NE 31 Court Bridge serves as a single point of access and hurricane evacuation route to many City residents.
1664.purpose: The project will provide funding for the replacement of the NE 31 Court Bridge. The bridge serves as the single point of access and hurricane evacuation route to many residential households. The project includes the total replacement of the existing bridge resulting in a new resilient structure.
1664.activities: The bridge provides the sole access and evacuation route for City residents. A structural failure could endanger lives and leave residents isolated during a severe weather event.
1664.direct_services: Residents living in the island community will benefit from a new, resilient bridge that ensures safe access during significant weather events and eliminates concerns about structural failure due to the bridge’s age.
1664.population: City of Lighthouse Point residents with 25 households living on the island community. Emergency responders will have access these residents via the new bridge, which will allow them to provide emergency services to these residences.
1664.outcome: A new, resilient bridge will be constructed, providing a service life of approximately 75 years under current building codes.

1665.description: This project will improve the level of protection for the existing police station, which houses our first responders 24/7. Currently, the building is not equipped with hurricane-rated windows and doors. Given the City's close proximity to the Intracoastal Waterway, this presents a significant vulnerability. The requested funds will be used to replace all existing windows and doors with hurricane-rated impact systems, ensuring the building's safety against extreme weather events.
1665.purpose: Providing enhanced protection to the existing police department building will allow first responders to remain operational during significant weather events.
1665.activities: This project will provide the police department with improved protection against water damage during significant weather events.
1665.direct_services: The existing building will be protected from hurricane-force winds and flying debris, which will allow first responders to provide uninterrupted services to the residents of Lighthouse Point.
1665.population: The residents of the City of Lighthouse Point will be served by this project, which includes all residential households and commercial establishments located within the City.
1665.outcome: The project will provide the police department with improved protection against water damage during severe weather events. The outcome will be measured by site assessment and observation.

1666.description: Lighthouse Point is a small residential community and faces challenges in securing funding for large projects. The City adopted a Stormwater Master Plan (SWMP) with over $13M in estimated repairs. Funds will be used to construct Priority Area 1, in the north end of the City, identified in the SWMP. To reduce flooding, recommended improvements aim to enhance stormwater management and water quality, as well as roadway conditions and traffic flow.
1666.purpose: Constructing a new drainage system will improve the level of service to the roadway during weather events, reduce street flooding and improve the water quality discharged. The project will provide total reconstruction to the existing drainage system.
1666.activities: This project will mitigate environmental hazards associated with stormwater runoff and improve local surfacewater quality. Ponding stormwater runoff from roadways will be removed, providing safer conditions for vehicle and pedestrian traffic.
1666.direct_services: The project will remove flood waters from roadways, and reduce flood stages and durations. Flooding from rainfall will be mitigated, which will protect persons and property in the residential area.
1666.population: City of Lighthouse Point residents located in the north end of the City.
1666.outcome: The improvements will be supplemented with pollutant retardant baffles to capture sediment from runoff. The outcome will be measured by site assessment and observation including feedback from the community.

1539.description: Carter’s Corner, Inc. is a nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening families and communities through holistic education, athletic engagement and evidence-based support services. We partner with local agencies, sports programs, and families to deliver mentoring, tutoring, life skills training, HIV education and testing, case management, and youth development camps. With funding, Carter's Corner will support the 24:7 Dad A.M. and P.M. curricula and provide training for resilient families focusing on fathers and youths. This is a voluntary, skill-based program designed to equip fathers facing systemic challenges and have children under 18 with the tools to become responsible, and nurturing parents across the Big Bend region.
1539.purpose: The requested funds will support a community-based initiative that equips adult fathers (ages 18 and older) with the tools, training, and mentorship needed to strengthen family bonds, improve economic mobility, and foster responsible parenting. Serving fathers with children aged 24 or younger, the program addresses barriers including poverty, justice involvement, and lack of positive male role models.
1539.activities: Through structured workshops and facilitator-led sessions, participants will engage in evidence-informed modules focused on employment readiness, financial literacy, parenting strategies, and healthy relationship building. Grounded in the principles of Family, Opportunity, Resilience, Grit, and Engagement, this initiative promotes long-term stability and generational restoration for Florida families.
1539.direct_services: Delivered in community settings across the Big Bend region, the program equips fathers with practical parenting, relationship, and workforce skills. Participants engage in guided sessions on fatherhood identity, child development, discipline, and emotional regulation, while also receiving support in employment readiness, financial literacy, and co- parenting. Fathers navigating reentry benefit fro
1539.population: Participants may include young fathers, returning citizens, noncustodial parents, and those engaged in reentry, workforce development, or family reunification efforts. By focusing on fathers who face systemic barriers to stability and engagement, the initiative promotes generational restoration, responsible parenting, and long-term family resilience. The project is expecting to serve 400 to 500 fathers across the Big Bend region including Leon, Wakulla, Gadsden and surrounding counties.
1539.outcome: The 24/7 Dad initiative aims to strengthen father engagement, reduce recidivism, and enhance family stability across the Big Bend region by equipping adult fathers with parenting, employment, and relationship skills. Outcomes will be tracked through pre- and post-assessments, facilitator feedback, and participant surveys, measuring attendance, curriculum completion, employment changes, parenting confidence, and peer engagement.

1658.description: Senior Friendship Centers, a 52-year nonprofit serving older adults in southwest Florida will replace four original commercial elevators installed in the 1980s with modern and reliable units. These elevators are necessary for seniors on walkers, canes and wheelchairs to access services and programs located on the second floor of buildings on two senior campuses.
1658.purpose: Four elevators that are more than 35-years old will be replaced with modern equipment, that is up to code for safety and communications with emergency services.
1658.activities: Once these elevators are replaced, older adults and staff who cannot navigate stairs will have trusted and safe equipment to allow them access to the 2nd floor of the buildings on the two campuses of Senior Friendship Centers.
1658.direct_services: Senior-serving campuses provide health, wellness, enrichment, mental health support and other services. The elevators allow older adults to reach the 2nd floor to meet with a counselor, exercise, participate in programming and receive other supports. When elevators aren't operable or feel unsafe, programming is canceled.
1658.population: Older adults, persons with disabilities, volunteers serving older adults. More than 1,500 persons will be serve, with more than 53,000 visits to the Centers annually.
1658.outcome: Improved physical and mental health, improved access to services, increased cultural and wellness access, and a reduction in falls. Pre- and post-program surveys will measure these outcomes.

3442.organization: The Integrity Group a dba of Blue Sky
3442.description: Providing state agencies with an enterprise-wide solution to enhance current anti-fraud activities by developing a system that aggregates data for review and analysis. The combined data from all agencies administering grants and other public assistance activities will enhance the ability to identify organized criminal organizations and individuals stealing from multiple programs across agencies. The program will identify questionable applications, ease the review process and enhance fraud prevention. Out of a funding of over $229 billion, it is estimated $22 billion was stolen thru fraud, waste or abuse. Recovery of stolen funding is estimated at $4 billion.
3442.purpose: Providing state agencies with an enterprise wide solution to enhance current anti-fraud activities by developing a system that aggregates data for review and analysis. The combined data from all agencies administering grants and other public assistance activities will enhance the ability to identify organized criminal organizations and individuals stealing from multiple programs across agencies. The program will identify questionable applications, easing the review process for analyst.
3442.activities: Enhance current anti-fraud measures currently used by state agencies managing grant programs and other public assistance activities. Establish an enterprise-wide system of data required to identify and analyze suspected cases of fraud by organized criminal activities and individuals. Increased recovery of funding stolen through fraudulent activities; detection and prevention of fraudulent activities; increase the amount of funding available to applicants in actual need of public assistance fundi
3442.direct_services: Prevention, detection, and prompt response to fraud perpetrated against state and federal public assistance programs, thereby, ensuring funding is directed to and for those as intended by legislation and individuals needs.
3442.population: Persons and families in need of public assistance for essential needs.
3442.outcome: Prevention, detection and appropriate response to fraud against public assistance programs. Increase the number of fraud cases identified and prevented. Increase funding available to individuals needing public assistance, through prevention activities and funding claw back activities. Agency reporting of fraud detection and prevention activities comparing previous time period to the current time period. Reporting of funds stolen through fraud, the value of funding recovered by prevention and detection activities.

1571.description: In 2012, the City of Gretna determined its water system lacked sufficient pumping and storage capacity for future demand. The city planned to add a production well, a new well, and two ground storage tanks with pumps. Due to funding limits, the tanks were prioritized first. Funding has been secured for the first tank, now under construction, and the city is seeking support for the second,a 350,000-gallon tank near the I-10/SR-12 interchange. This project is critical to meet growth and demand.
1571.purpose: In 2012, the City of Gretna determined its water system lacked sufficient pumping and storage capacity for future demand. The city planned to add a production well, a new well, and two ground storage tanks with pumps. Due to funding limits, the tanks were prioritized first. Funding has been secured for the first tank, now under construction, and the city is seeking support for the second,a 350,000-gallon tank near the I-10/SR-12 interchange. This project is critical to meet growth and demand.
1571.activities: In 2012, the City of Gretna determined its water system lacked sufficient pumping and storage capacity for future demand. The city planned to add a production well, a new well, and two ground storage tanks with pumps. Due to funding limits, the tanks were prioritized first. Funding has been secured for the first tank, now under construction, and the city is seeking support for the second,a 350,000-gallon tank near the I-10/SR-12 interchange. This project is critical to meet growth and demand.
1571.direct_services: This project will provide consistency in water pressure, fire protection for emergency use, and resilience against future disasters.
1571.outcome: The measurable outcome will be to provide a source of treated water in the event of major storm events or emergencies.

1573.description: The project will be the construction of a hurricane rated primary Fire Station in Taylor County (County). The current station is housed in a WW ll hangar at Perry-Foley Airport (Airport). The Airport has experienced considerable growth the past few years and made numerous improvements with FDOT and FAA funding assistance, the hangar is needed for aviation use.
