1671.description: The project will create a local, sustainable source of sand for the beaches south of Port Everglades Inlet. It is expected to provide 50% of the sand needs for this area, which is the most chronically eroded stretch of beach in the County. It will result in reduced sedimentation into the Port Everglades Inlet. It will reduce the scale, cost, and impact of future beach nourishment events. The project's construction is critical to maintain a resilient shoreline in the area south of the inlet.
1671.purpose: The project will create a local, sustainable source of sand for the beaches south of Port Everglades Inlet. It is expected to provide 50% of the sand needs for this area, which is the most chronically eroded stretch of beach in the County. It will result in reduced sedimentation into the Port Everglades Inlet. It will reduce the scale, cost, and impact of future beach nourishment events. The project's construction is critical to maintain a resilient shoreline in the area south of the inlet.
1671.activities: A sand trap will be constructed just offshore of the Port Everglades inlet, which will trap beach-quality sand for eventual placement on the beaches south of the inlet. Additionally, the project will reduce sedimentation into the Port Everglades federal navigation channel.
1671.direct_services: The project will provide a local sand source for the beaches south of the Port Everglades inlet. Residents and visitors will benefit from the resilient shoreline width that will result from project completion.
1671.population: The target population served by the project is residents and tourists. Approximately 240,000 residents occupy Dania Beach, Hollywood, and Hallandale Beach; an additional 12 million tourists visit Broward County each year, many of whom recreate on the beaches.
1671.outcome: The project will result in reduced sedimentation into the Port Everglades federal navigation channel; physical (multibeam) surveys will be conducted every six months post-construction by the County's Consultant to quantify the amount of sedimentation reaching the inlet. The project will also result in wider beaches south of Port Everglades; physical surveys will be conducted by the County's Consultant to characterize shoreline width.

1397.description: The Town of Surfside seeks state funding to construct stormwater drainage improvements in Focus Area 4, the neighborhood between Hawthorne Avenue and Irving Avenue from 89th to 90th Street. This area experiences recurring roadway and yard flooding due to undersized infrastructure that cannot handle major rainfall events. The project will expand system capacity by upsizing stormwater pipes, adding new inlets and outfalls to Biscayne Bay, and restoring affected roadways and surfaces. These upgrades will reduce flood depths, improve drainage efficiency, and enhance long-term resilience consistent with the Town’s Stormwater Master Plan.
1397.purpose: The project will reduce chronic flooding in Focus Area 4 by increasing stormwater conveyance capacity and adding new outfall connections to Biscayne Bay. These improvements will strengthen the Town’s stormwater system, enhance roadway access during heavy rainfall, and protect nearby homes and infrastructure from flood-related damages.
1397.activities: Funds will be used solely for construction of the stormwater drainage improvements, including installation of upsized stormwater pipes, new manholes and inlets, supplemental outfall structures to Biscayne Bay, and roadway and surface restoration.
1397.direct_services: The project will directly reduce flooding impacts for residents and businesses in the project area by improving stormwater conveyance and roadway drainage, ensuring safer travel and property access during heavy rainfall events.
1397.population: The project serves residents, businesses, and visitors in the Focus Area 4 neighborhood and indirectly benefits the broader Surfside community through improved flood protection and emergency access. The population target is general and >800.
1397.outcome: The expected outcome is reduced flood depth and duration within the project area. Effectiveness will be measured through field observation during storm events, maintenance records, and reductions in resident service requests related to flooding.

1404.description: The Surfside Safe Streets Project will implement neighborhood traffic-calming and pedestrian safety improvements identified in the Town’s 2023 Traffic Study by The Corradino Group. The study documented excessive vehicle speeds and recurring crash patterns along Byron, Carlyle, Abbott, and adjacent streets, where several roadway segments exceed County livability thresholds. The project will construct safety devices such as speed humps, raised crosswalks, neighborhood roundabouts, and sidewalk connectivity upgrades to slow traffic, improve pedestrian mobility, and reduce crashes. These improvements will create safer streets for residents, schoolchildren, and visitors while promoting walking, biking, and neighborhood livability.
1404.purpose: The purpose of the funds is to construct traffic-calming and pedestrian safety improvements throughout the Town of Surfside to reduce speeding, improve walkability, and enhance neighborhood safety. The project will implement measures such as speed humps, raised crosswalks, roundabouts, and new sidewalks to slow vehicle traffic, reduce crashes, and create safer streets for residents, schoolchildren, and visitors.
1404.activities: The project will include the construction of traffic-calming and pedestrian safety improvements such as speed humps, raised crosswalks, neighborhood roundabouts, new sidewalks, roadway striping, and signage. These improvements will be installed at priority locations identified in the Town’s 2023 Traffic Study to reduce speeding, improve pedestrian safety, and enhance walkability.
1404.direct_services: The project will provide safer and more accessible streets for residents, schoolchildren, and visitors by reducing vehicle speeds and improving pedestrian crossings. It will enhance neighborhood walkability, lower the risk of traffic- related injuries, and create a more comfortable environment for walking, biking, and daily travel within the community.
1404.population: The project serves the general population of the Town of Surfside, including residents, schoolchildren, and visitors who walk, bike, and drive within the community. It is expected to benefit approximately 6,000 people by improving neighborhood safety, reducing vehicle speeds, and enhancing pedestrian access throughout the Town.
1404.outcome: The project will reduce vehicle speeds, improve pedestrian safety, and lower the number of traffic-related crashes in residential areas. It will create safer, more walkable streets and encourage active transportation such as walking and biking. Success will be measured through post-construction traffic observations, crash data, and community feedback.

1766.description: The EquiWell Project is a first-in-Florida initiative to prevent homelessness, exploitation, and system cycling among young adults ages 18-24, with priority given to youth exiting foster care at age 18. The project will establish a mixed-use, 200-unit resilient housing campus in Miami-Dade County that integrates permanent affordability through a Community Land Trust model and provides on-site supportive services to stabilize health, housing, and workforce outcomes.The initiative includes a Health & Housing Navigation Center offering trauma-informed behavioral health care, physical health coordination, benefits and legal navigation, and tenancy support to ensure successful placement and retention. In addition, an AI Digital Incubator will operate on-site to deliver workforce training, entrepreneurship development, financial literacy, and technology-driven career pathways that reduce relia
1766.purpose: The EquiWell Project: Advancing Public Health Through Permanent Supportive Housing, Florida's first integrated Health, Housing, and Workforce Resilience Campus, specifically designed to prevent youth exiting foster care from entering homelessness, psychiatric inpatient settings, and the criminal legal system. The goal is to bolster housing stability and safety for our young adults 18-24 by combining supportive housing, mental and physical health services, and an AI-enabled innovation incubator t
1766.activities: The mix-use buildout includes 200 residential technology designed one bedroom lofts with an onsite Health & Housing Navigation Center; embedded with clinical and support services, mindfulness pods for individual/group behavioral healh and trauma informed care, mental health/physical and preventive health navigation support, life stabilization, assitance with (Snap benefits, State issued ID, legal, SSI/SSDI payee support), placement continuity to avoid returns to shelters or street homelessness,
1766.direct_services: This project will provide direct housing placement through rolling admissions for up to 200 young adults who have exited the foster care system. Housing Stabilization & Navigation will include: Intake, placement, and tenancy support for 200 residents. Move-in coordination, retention coaching, and landlord mediation. Assistance with documentation, benefits enrollment, and credit repair.
1766.population: The targeted population served by this project is 200 young adults ages 18-24 who are: at risk youth exiting foster care, LGBTQ+ young adults, economically disadvantaged individuals, homless/displaced, physically disabled, developmentally disabled, etc.
1766.outcome: State investment will convert a high-risk discharge population into a stably housed, working, and clinically supported population, measurably reducing state expenditures on crisis systems while creating a permanent affordable housing resource that can be replicated statewide. Creation of a Permanent, Replicable Housing Asset Site control and pre-development completed to advance to construction financing.Permanent affordability secured through a Community Land Trust structure.Deployment of a replicable blueprint for expansion in other Florida counties. Housing Stabilization for Priority Population: 200 young adults housed at any given time (rolling admissions).Priority placement for youth exi

1933.description: The purpose of this project is to remove 60-acres of muck and flocculant material from the Newton Park area of Lake Apopka (Florida's fourth largest lake) near downtown Winter Garden to improve water quality, navigation, fish and wildlife habitat, recreation, ecotourism, and surrounding property values for thousands of local residents and businesses. Much of the bottom of Lake Apopka is covered by a consolidated muck layer of decayed plant matter and an unconsolidated flocculant layer made up mostly of dead algae. These muck and flocculant layers damage boat engines, are malodorous and aesthetically displeasing, contribute to nutrient overloading and algal blooms, and inhibit recovery efforts for essential submerged aquatic vegetation in the lake which is vital to improving water quality and wildlife habitats, and controlling invasive vegetation. The SJRWMD and the City funded a WSP engi
1933.purpose: The purpose of this project is to remove muck and flocculant material from the Newton Park area of Lake Apopka (Florida's fourth largest lake) near downtown Winter Garden to improve water quality, navigation, fish and wildlife habitat, recreation, ecotourism, and surrounding property values for thousands of local residents and businesses. Submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) is critical to the health and sustainability of an aquatic ecosystem. It stabilizes the sediment, cleans and oxygenates the
1933.activities: Activities will include dredging, transporting, and disposing of muck and flocculant material from the Newton Park area of Lake Apopka, as well as project management, grant management, and third-party validation of work performed. Permitting is underway for the project and permits are expected by or before May, 2026. Construction can commence upon receipt of the permits.
1933.direct_services: This project will benefit the residents, businesses, and visitors of Winter Garden and other communities surrounding Lake Apopka by removing legacy nutrients and muck from the lake that will improve water quality. 1. Improve recreational activities at this public park area 2. Create shoreline depths that can be navigated by boaters 3. Eliminate the presence of malodorous and aesthetically displeas
1933.population: This project is in a densely populated area of downtown historic Winter Garden, home to over 47,000 residents hundreds of businesses, and thousands of weekly visitors. Newton Park is a charming green space This tranquil park area offers a peaceful retreat with lush landscaping, walking paths, and picnic areas. The park is known for its beautiful views of Lake Apopka and amenities like a boardwalk, boat ramp, grills, picnic tables, playground, shaded gazebo, and restrooms. The local community fre
1933.outcome: Expected outcomes include: 1. Nutrient reduction 2. Water quality improvement 3. Improved navigation 4. Improved conditions for restoration of submerged aquatic vegetation 5. Improved habitat for fish and other wildlife 6. Sediment stabilization 7. Enhanced ecotourism, property values, and recreational opportunities including fishing Project engineer, contractor, and SJRWMD will validate lbs. of muck removed, amount of nutrients removed, and other measures that demonstrate water quality improvements.

1405.organization: The Arc of South Florida Inc
1405.description: The funds will support the operation of a comprehensive Culinary Vocational Training Program designed to equip participants with practical, employable skills in baking, food preparation, and restaurant maintenance. This program will offer paid, hands-on training opportunities that prepare individuals for sustainable careers in the culinary and hospitality industries, while also fostering economic growth and job readiness within the community.
1405.purpose: The funds will support The Arc of South Florida Culinary Arts Program, providing hands-on culinary training for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. This program will fund qualified instructors, staff benefits, facility rental, and equipment to teach food preparation, safety, and service skills. The goal is to prepare participants for employment, promote independence, and increase inclusion in the workforce.
1405.activities: The funds will support activities and services including culinary, baking, and restaurant maintenance training in a professional kitchen, life skills and vocational development, supervised daily engagement, and behavioral support for adults with autism, developmental disabilities, and mental illness to enhance independence, employability, and overall well-being.
1405.direct_services: The funding requested will directly support services that empower citizens with autism, developmental disabilities, and mental illness. These services include life skills training, vocational development, employment readiness programs, and individualized support to foster independence, enhance daily living, and promote community integration.
1405.population: The majority of the funds requested will serve 25–30 adults with autism, developmental disabilities, and mental illness. This includes individuals who are developmentally disabled, persons with poor mental health, and economically disadvantaged. Some participants may also be unemployed and in need of vocational training and life skills development.
1405.outcome: The project will improve independence, life skills, vocational readiness, and well-being for adults with autism, developmental disabilities, and mental illness. Outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-assessments, program completion, employment tracking, and feedback from participants, families, and employers.

2889.description: Florida Agriculture & Energy Innovation Initiative is a workforce development program equipping undeserved youth (10–18) and adults (18+) in Orlando, Miami, and Tampa Bay/St. Pete with skills in agriculture and energy investment and installation. It addresses educational gaps and unemployment through hands-on training in urban farming, solar installation, and energy efficiency, fostering American jobs in resilient communities in like Overtown, Parramore, and Sulphur Springs.
2889.purpose: Train 450 under-served youth and adults in sustainable agriculture and energy skills, reducing unemployment and enhancing climate resilience in target communities.
2889.activities: Hands-on workshops in hydroponics, energy installation, and energy auditing; mentorship programs; community garden builds; urban agriculture, energy investing, and certification pathways.
2889.direct_services: Free training sessions, job placement support, and access to community resources for 450 participants in Orlando, Miami, and Tampa Bay/St. Pete.
2889.population: The target population consists of 450 under-served youth (ages 13–18) and adults (ages 18+) residing in economically disadvantaged communities across five Florida counties: Orange County (Orlando/Parramore/Pine Hills/Holden Heights), Pinellas County (St. Petersburg/Sulphur Springs), Hillsborough County (Tampa), Palm Beach County, and Miami-Dade County (Miami/Overtown/Liberty City/Homestead).
2889.outcome: Under-served youth (10–18) and adults (18+) in Overtown, Liberty City, Homestead, Sulphur Springs, Parramore, Holden Heights, and Pine Hills; 450 total. 70% certification/job placement rate, 500 tons atmospheric gas reduced; measured via quarterly DOE reports on enrollment, audits, and economic tracking.

1402.description: The Florida Advanced Technological Education Center (FLATE) is a state-wide center aimed at enhancing STEM education to meet the technician workforce needs of Florida's advanced manufacturing industries. The funds will support pipeline development, professional development for educators, and curriculum support. Activities include maintaining the Manufacturing Matters FL dashboard, developing STEM career curricula, and increasing college enrollment in manufacturing education. These efforts will benefit Florida’s workforce and manufacturing sector.
1402.purpose: The funds requested for the Florida Advanced Technological Education Center (FLATE) will achieve the goal of enhancing STEM education to meet the workforce needs of Florida's advanced manufacturing industries. Specifically, the funds will support pipeline development, professional development for educators, and curriculum support. These efforts aim to increase student enrollment in manufacturing education, improve the quality of education, and enhance the skills and knowledge of Florida’s workfo
1402.activities: The funds will support FLATE by maintaining the Manufacturing Matters FL dashboard, developing STEM career curricula, increasing college enrollment in manufacturing education, offering professional development for educators, and providing curriculum support. These services aim to enhance the skills and knowledge of Florida’s workforce, benefiting the manufacturing sector and the diversification and growth of Florida's economy.
1402.direct_services: The funds will provide direct services to Florida citizens, including maintaining the Manufacturing Matters FL dashboard, developing STEM career awareness curricula, and increasing college enrollment in manufacturing education. Additionally, FLATE will offer professional development for educators, hands-on training, and curriculum support. These services aim to enhance the skills and knowledge of
1402.population: The target population served by the FLATE project includes grade school students, high school students, university/college students, and economically disadvantaged persons. Approximately 20,000 students and thousands of educators are expected to benefit from the project.
1402.outcome: The FLATE project aims to improve STEM education quality and enhance Florida's workforce skills in advanced manufacturing. Methodology: • Monitor student enrollment and completion rates. • Track participation and feedback from professional development activities. • Measure economic impact through surveys and financial reports.

1421.description: Since 2017, the Wilhelmina Foundation has provided textbook stipends for deserving students attending institutions of higher learning. With Bright Futures and other scholarships/financial aid not accounting for textbook purchases, and students having to increasingly take on debt and loans to pay for their education, appropriated funds will allow for the Wilhelmina Foundation to provide additional textbook scholarships to students attending an institution of higher learning.
1421.purpose: If appropriated funds, the purpose of this expansion of the Wilhelmina Foundation scholarship will be to allow for more students to receive textbook stipends who are attending college in the Leon County area. The goal of this expansion will be to provide more access to potential students who may otherwise be unable to afford to attend an institution of higher learning.
1421.activities: Scholarship awards to subsidize cost in academic textbooks.
1421.direct_services: Direct services will be scholarships which allow college students afford textbooks while attending institutions of higher learning.
1421.population: The target population is high school and college students. With the funds, the Wilhelmina Foundation anticipates serving over 400 students in the Leon County area.
1421.outcome: The expected outcome will be an increase in scholarships awarded. This will be measured by the number of scholarships given out compared to previous years.

1406.description: Initiative provides trauma-informed mentoring, arts-based interventions, academic support, SEL development, and workforce readiness training to at-promise youth ages 10–23 in high-need Miami-Dade communities. The program focuses on youth at risk of entering or reentering the juvenile justice system by addressing the root causes of delinquency, including trauma, disengagement, and limited access to safe enrichment opportunities. Through structured pro-social activities, mentoring, and support, youth build resilience, improve behavior, and stay connected to school & community. Serving 200+ youth annually, the initiative is projected to prevent an estimated 30 offenses each year, resulting in $337,000–$450,000 in direct taxpayer cost avoidance based on DJJ cost benchmarks. By reducing first-time offenses & recidivism while improving academic engagement & workforce readiness, the program enh
1406.purpose: The requested funds will expand The Motivational Edge’s Juvenile Justice Diversion, Prevention & Workforce Readiness Initiative to reduce first-time offenses, lower recidivism, and serve 200 at-promise youth with trauma- informed mentoring, arts-based intervention, and workforce skill-building-ultimately decreasing juvenile justice costs and improving community safety.
1406.activities: Wraparound education and mentoring services will be provided to students in grade 2 up to 23 years old, 7 days per week. Activities will include trauma-informed mentoring, arts and education programming (music, lyrical expression, visual arts), academic and SEL support, goal-setting, and workforce readiness training. Services focus on diversion, prevention, skill-building, and ongoing engagement to reduce first-time offenses and recidivism among at-promise youth.
1406.direct_services: The project will provide youth with direct diversion and prevention services, including trauma-informed mentoring, arts- based intervention, academic and behavioral support, SEL development, court-compliance assistance, and workforce readiness coaching-helping reduce offenses, improve stability, and support healthy development.
1406.population: Youth with a history in the juvenile justice system, the lowest 25% performing in school, and youth in foster care are our prime target population. The project serves at-promise youth & young adults ages 10–23 in high-need communities, and youth at risk of entering or reentering the juvenile justice system. Approximately 200 youth are expected to be served annually through diversion, prevention, and workforce-readiness programming.
1406.outcome: • 25–30% reduction in first-time offenses and recidivism among participating youth. Measured through DJJ re-offense data, court-compliance tracking, case management notes, and completion of diversion requirements. • 80% of youth will show improved social-emotional skills and behavioral stability. Measured by SEL assessments, pre/post surveys, attendance logs, and behavior reports. • 75% of youth will demonstrate increased engagement in school and positive activities. Measured through attendance tracking, participation logs, academic reports, and staff evaluations. • 100% of youth will receive career, vocational, or workforce-readiness exposure. Measured through pre- and post-interest surveys

2600.description: The Miami Downtown Development Authority (Miami DDA) is an independent agency of the City of Miami focused on improving the quality of life for stakeholders, residents, and visitors in Downtown Miami through business development, infrastructure and capital improvements. In partnership with the Miami DDA and Miami-Dade County, the City of Miami is rebuilding a 1/2-mile section of one of Florida's most historic Streets in Downtown Miami: Flagler Street. This 4-year project is transforming the City’s historic main street from its current design into a curbless festival street that will attract new businesses, provide larger sidewalks for shopping and dining, install much-needed tree canopy and site furnishings, and upgrade all utilities to allow for new vertical development. Phase E is the fifth and final phase, is approximately 800 linear feet and runs from Miami Ave to W 1st Ave.
2600.purpose: In recent decades, the Flagler Street corridor in Downtown Miami has been in desperate need of renovation and not attractive to potential new development. Thus, specific purpose or goal of this project is to draw more people to the corridor, activate the sidewalks with retail and expanded outdoor dining, and stimulate the vertical development of the historic corridor. Currently there is a $5 million dollar shortfall in the total project budget, and we are requesting additional funding to complet
2600.activities: At the core of Downtown Miami, Flagler Street has been the economic, entertainment and political hub of Miami-Dade County since the City was founded in 1896. In recent decades, the Flagler Street corridor has been in desperate need of renovation and not attractive to potential new development. Thus, specific purpose or goal of this project is to draw more people to the corridor, activate the sidewalks with retail and expanded outdoor dining, and stimulate the vertical development of the historic
2600.direct_services: This project will deliver an enriched pedestrian experience for residents, businesses and visitors with expanded sidewalks, large shade trees, outdoor café dining, improved LED lighting, signage, public art, and seating. Existing drainage systems will also be upgraded to prevent flooding of streets and sidewalks. We aim to improve the quality of life through a safer and more attractive shared spac
2600.population: In revitalizing and improving Flagler Street, the project will fulfill the expectations of over 115,000 area residents, 250,000 workers, and thousands of visitors who desire the advantages of a dynamic urban center. Downtown has emerged as a popular tourist destination with nearly 6 million tourist and visitors. In terms of demographics, the Miami DDA serves a diverse population, with a diversity index of 73.1. The number of households in the Greater Downtown more than doubled between 2000 and 2
2600.outcome: A 2014 economic impact analysis of the Project estimated that reconstruction of Flagler Street would generate approximately 2,080 new direct jobs within five years after reconstruction was completed, along with an additional 1,940 new jobs from indirect and induced economic effects – a total impact of 4,020 additional jobs, resulting in $610 million of gross revenues to local business establishments, $236 million of additional personal income (after tax and adjusted for inflation) for local residents and an increase of $406 million to the County’s Gross Regional Product. The economic impacts were estimated utilizing the South Florida Multi-regional REMI Model, a dynamic econometric model dev

2779.description: The requested funds will support the installation of an ADA-compliant elevator at 26Health’s main facility. The current elevator lacks the capacity to accommodate a stretcher, creating safety and accessibility challenges. Because behavioral health services are located on the fourth floor, patients requiring emergency transport must currently be chairlifted down multiple flights of stairs. The new elevator will ensure safe, efficient, and dignified access for all patients, staff, and emergency personnel.
2779.purpose: The requested funds will be used to install an ADA-compliant elevator at 26Health’s main facility to improve accessibility, safety, and patient flow. The project will ensure equitable access to care for individuals with mobility challenges and strengthen emergency preparedness for all building occupants.
2779.activities: Funds will support design, engineering, permitting, and construction activities for installing a new ADA-compliant elevator. Services will include architectural planning, structural modifications, electrical and safety integration, and inspections to ensure full compliance with ADA, building, and safety standards.
2779.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with improved access, safety, and comfort when receiving care at 26Health’s facility. The new elevator will ensure individuals with disabilities or mobility challenges can reach all service areas, while the new windows will enhance building safety, energy efficiency, and indoor comfort for patients, staff, and visitors.
2779.population: The project will serve patients, staff, and visitors at 26Health’s health center, with a focus on individuals with disabilities, mobility limitations, and seniors. 26Health primarily serves uninsured and under-insured residents across Central Florida. Each year, more than 2,000 individuals receive care at this facility, all of whom will benefit from improved accessibility and safety through the addition of this elevator.
2779.outcome: The project will enhance accessibility and safety at 26Health’s main facility by adding an ADA-compliant elevator. These improvements will ensure equitable access for patients with mobility challenges and create a safer, more comfortable environment for all visitors and staff. Outcomes will be measured through accessibility metrics, such as tracking elevator usage, reduced wait times, and patient satisfaction surveys. Project progress will be tracked through documentation of ADA and building inspection approvals.

1422.description: Design & construct drainage system on NE 94 St from NE 10 Ave & Belvedere Dr to N. Bayshore Dr to prevent ponding/standing water and water intrusion for proper drainage during rainfall events and high tide events as this flooding occurs approximately 1600 ft from the Biscayne Bay aquifer. This drainage system would allow the Village to capture water runoff and assure water quality contaminant predictability within the allowances of the NPDES guidelines before it reaches the Biscayne Bay aquifer.
1422.purpose: To reduce standing water in this area and water intrusion into properties on this street.
1422.activities: This street runs perpendicular to Biscayne Bay. As water recedes, the runoff would not be contaminated with environmental hazards such as oils, chemicals and other hazardous materials.
1422.direct_services: Both pedestrians and vehicular traffic would be able to better traverse the area without having to travel through floodwaters to get to their home.
1422.population: The residents that live on 94th Street in addition to the general public that drive on the roadway.
1422.outcome: The expected outcome is residents will no longer be impacted with standing water on their properties and in the streets as well as intrusion to the dwellings would be minimized measured by flood-free streets.

1771.description: Raise the roadway to an elevation the ensures sustainability and resilience for anticipated future flooding, surpassing the projected flood elevation for future years by reducing flooding and water intrusion for the properties on located on this street during heavy rainfall and high tide events.
1771.purpose: Our precise objective is to raise the roadway to an elevation that ensures sustainability and resilience against sea level rise, surpassing the projected flood elevation for the next 60 years.
1771.activities: This street runs perpendicular to Biscayne Bay. As water recedes, the potential runoff into Biscayne Bay would not be contaminated with environmental hazards such as oils, chemicals and other hazardous materials.
1771.direct_services: Both pedestrians and vehicular traffic would be able to better traverse the area without having to travel through floodwaters to get to their home.
1771.population: The residents that live on 94th Street in addition to the general public that drive on the roadway.
1771.outcome: The expected outcome is residents will no longer be impacted with standing water on their properties and in the streets as well as intrusion to the dwellings would be minimized measured by flood-free streets.

1423.description: Replacing underground fuel tanks with above-ground systems greatly reduces the risk of leaks and soil contamination that can migrate into groundwater and ultimately reach the C7 canal. Above-ground tanks allow for easier inspection, maintenance, and containment in the event of a spill, preventing fuel from seeping into the surrounding environment. This proactive measure protects surface and groundwater quality, helping to preserve the ecological health of the C7 canal & Biscayne Bay Aquifer.
1423.purpose: Prevent impact contamination of underground well.
1423.activities: This is a supply point for day-to-day operations as well as an emergency supply point in the event of a disaster. This project will improve the fuel supply storage for our emergency responders as well as the Village disaster operations.
1423.direct_services: During emergencies, these tanks are utilized for emergency responders including the local hospital, health workers, teachers just to name a few. This upgrade would ensure that we can support other local agencies during an emergency event.
1423.population: The general population surrounding the facility and those properties abutting on the C-7 canal that may potentially have an environmental impact.
1423.outcome: Elimination of any potential environmental contamination to the underground watertable which may seep into the C-7 canal and further into the Biscayne Bay Aquifer measured by well testing.

1769.description: Funds will support the construction of a resilient government complex, which will accomodate police services, building and code compliance, public works, and community services. A modern infrastructure is an essential component in enhacing public safety and trust, operational efficiency, and community resilience. Importantly, the Town is divided by a major State road that serves as the only area evacuation route. Therefore, a new Police Facility will ensure the Town is able to meet the demands of the growth of its community and surrounding County municipalities, particularly in times of crises.
1769.purpose: Funds will support Fixed Capital Outlay activities for planning, engineering design, and pre-construction services leading to construction of the new Town Hall/Police Resilient Complex. The new facility will expand services for residents and surrounding County jurisdictions to ensure public safety. This public safety measure will be achieved by improving response times, providing safer working conditions, expanding services and resources, and increasing community engagement projects.
1769.activities: The Town will execute a contract for planning, engineering and permitting services to move forward with the construction of the proposed facility. The facility will enable the enhancement of public safety services to residents by enabling expedient crime reporting and prevention. It will also support community engagement by providing space for cultural engagement events, educational programming, and family events. Local businesses will be supported by streamlined services for permitting, licensi
1769.direct_services: The new Town Hall/Police Resilient Complex will be a safe haven for citizens to report crime and seek aid. Additional direct services will include rapid response to emergency situations; community services such as fingerprinting and crime prevention; community engagement events; and, victim services and at-risk youth services.
1769.population: The project will serve residents from the Town of Bay Harbor Islands and multiple Miami Dade County municipalities that share access to the surrounding bay waters. The Town's population and neighboring municipalities total approximately 153,000 residents whom the project will serve. Additionally, more than a million seasonal visitors pass through the Islands and rely on public safety services.
1769.outcome: The new facility will accomodate training needs, secure evidence management, more operational staff, community activities, youth programs, and emergency response. Residents, visitors and businesses will benefit from the expansion of services and resources and improved emergency response times. The increase in capacity and resiliency will allow for more jobs measured by new staff hired and additional or expanded services provided to community residents. Programming for at-risk youth will be measured by enrollment numbers.

2780.description: 26Health seeks state appropriations to acquire a portable X-ray machine and ultrasound machine to expand access to essential diagnostic imaging services for uninsured and underinsured patients across Central Florida. As a nonprofit community health center providing integrated primary care, behavioral health, and specialty services, 26Health addresses significant gaps in care for diverse and often marginalized populations. Currently, patients requiring basic radiology services must be referred off-site, creating barriers to timely diagnosis and treatment. The addition of portable X-ray capabilities will enhance continuity of care, reduce unnecessary emergency visits, and improve early detection of conditions such as pneumonia, fractures, and chronic illnesses. This investment aligns with 26Health’s mission to deliver comprehensive, accessible, and equitable healthcare for all.
2780.purpose: The funds will allow 26Health to purchase a portable X-ray machine and ultrasound machine to provide on-site diagnostic imaging for patients who currently face barriers to care. This addition will reduce off-site referrals, improve timely diagnosis and treatment, and enhance care coordination within 26Health’s integrated service model. The project will expand access to essential healthcare and improve outcomes for underserved Central Florida residents.
2780.activities: 26Health will purchase and implement portable X-ray and ultrasound machines to expand its diagnostic capabilities. Licensed medical staff will be trained to operate the equipment, and imaging protocols will be integrated into the electronic health record system. These activities will support timely screening, diagnosis, and follow-up for primary care, women’s health, and urgent care patients.
2780.direct_services: The project will provide patients with on-site X-ray and ultrasound imaging, eliminating the need for external referrals and reducing wait times for diagnostic results. Citizens will directly benefit from same-day imaging that enables faster diagnosis and treatment for injuries, infections, chronic conditions, and early prenatal care needs.
2780.population: The project will serve uninsured, underinsured, and medically underserved residents of Orange, Seminole, and Osceola Counties who rely on 26Health for affordable, comprehensive care. 26Health anticipates serving 240 patients per year. The ultrasound machine has a life expectancy of approximately 10 years, therefore 26Health anticipates serving 2400 individuals through the appropriated funds.
2780.outcome: The project will expand access to diagnostic imaging, leading to faster diagnosis, improved treatment outcomes, and fewer emergency room visits. Success will be measured by tracking the number of imaging procedures completed, reductions in off-site referrals, and patient satisfaction and follow-up data captured through 26Health’s electronic health record system.

1618.organization: United Home Care Services, Inc. d/b/a United
1618.description: The Coming Home Senior Hospital Transition Program offers in-home transitional care for Broward County seniors age 60+ whose needs aren’t covered by LTC Medicaid, Medicare, or other insurance. Designed to support safe recovery after hospitalization, rehab, or nursing home discharge, the program provides nursing, case management, personal care, and home-delivered meals. These services reduce preventable ER visits and hospital readmissions while filling critical care gaps and improving long-term health outcomes. Vulnerable older adults can remain safely at home—where they prefer to be—and maintain their independence.
1618.purpose: Funds will support transitional care services for 90 days to Broward County seniors age 60+ whose services are not covered by LTC Medicaid or other insurance helping them recover safely at home post-hospitalization, rehab, or nursing home discharge. The goal is to reduce preventable readmissions and ER visits by providing in-home nursing, personal care, case management, and nutrition support with home-delivered meals—helping vulnerable older adults remain safely at home and maintain independence
1618.activities: The program will deliver transitional care services including in-home Personal Care Services, Nursing and Case Management assessments, and nutrition support with Home-Delivered Meals. Staff will coordinate with hospitals and families to ensure safe discharge planning and continuity of care at home for uninsured seniors upon hospital, rehab, or nursing home discharge to support recovery, reduce avoidable readmissions, and help them remain safely and independently at home.
1618.direct_services: Direct services include in-home personal care, nursing assessments, case management, and nutrition support through home-delivered meals. Staff coordinate discharge planning with hospitals and families to ensure continuity of care for Broward County residents age 60+ without LTC Medicaid or other insurance who are transitioning from hospitals, rehab centers, or nursing homes to home.
1618.population: The program serves Broward County residents age 60+ whose services are not covered by LTC Medicaid or other insurance and who are transitioning from hospitals, rehabilitation centers, or nursing homes to home. These individuals face significant barriers to safe recovery. The program expects to serve approximately 60 seniors annually, prioritizing those at highest risk of readmission or institutionalization.
1618.outcome: The project aims to reduce hospital readmissions, ER visits, and premature institutionalization among uninsured/underserved Broward seniors age 60+. Expected outcomes include improved health stability, successful transitions home, and better quality of life. Outcomes will be measured by 30/60/90-day readmission and ER visit rates, number of seniors retained at home, and cost savings from avoided hospitalizations. Metrics will be tracked through nursing and case management assessments, hospital data, and client follow-ups.

1349.description: Funds will support design, procurement, installation, and integration of upgraded control systems for the City of Chiefland’s SBR wastewater treatment process. The project will replace aging 25-year-old control panels and electrical components, improve treatment reliability, support compliance with nitrogen limits required under the City’s Administrative Order, and maintain operational performance while funding is pursued and secured for a 1.0 MGD WWTF expansion.
1349.purpose: To upgrade the aging SBR control system at the Chiefland WWTF to maintain reliable treatment performance, improve nutrient removal required under the City’s Administrative Order, and support system operations until the new 1.0 MGD plant is constructed.
1349.activities: Design, procurement, installation, configuration, and integration of new controls, along with testing, startup, and operator training.
1349.direct_services: Improved wastewater treatment reliability, reduced risk of environmental harm, protection of public health, and improved utility service continuity for all customers.
1349.population: Approximately 2,300 City residents, businesses, schools, and critical facilities, along with customers in the service area relying on safe and compliant wastewater treatment.
1349.outcome: The project will help stabilize nutrient removal, reduce treatment disruptions, extend the useful life of existing infrastructure, and protect groundwater and surface waters. Benefits will be measured through effluent TN performance, SCADA data, reduced downtime, and FDEP compliance records.

1600.description: This project will allow Osceola County to advance the construction of 2 ramps at the Waterlin Boulevard Interchange which will provide critical new access to Florida’s Turnpike in southern Osceola County, addressing one of the longest gaps between exits on any U.S. limited access facility, approximately 50 miles between exit locations. This investment will provide immediate congestion relief, improve safety, support regional growth, and generate significant new toll revenue for Florida’s Turnpike Enterprise.
1600.purpose: This project will allow Osceola County to advance the construction of 2 ramps at the Waterlin Boulevard Interchange which will provide critical new access to Florida’s Turnpike in southern Osceola County, addressing one of the longest gaps between exits on any U.S. limited access facility, approximately 50 miles between exit locations. This investment will provide immediate congestion relief, improve safety, support regional growth, and generate significant new toll revenue for Florida’s Turnpik
1600.activities: The Waterlin Boulevard Interchange project will construct a half diamond interchange on Florida’s Turnpike at the Waterlin Boulevard overpass, which is under design and planned for construction in Summer 2026. Construction of the interchange includes providing a northbound on-ramp and a southbound off-ramp.
1600.direct_services: The Waterlin Boulevard Interchange provides a proactive solution to meet near-term demand before the long-planned future Southport Connector or Mildred Bass Boulevard interchanges come online (15+ years out).
1600.population: Current residents of St. Cloud, the Waterlin Mixed Use District, Canoe Creek Reserve, Lake Gentry Landings, and Southern Osceola County will be served by the construction of this project. Over ninety-one thousand (91,000) residential units, forty-five million (45M) square feet of non-residential (commercial/industrial) space, and over five thousand (5,000) hotel rooms are anticipated in this area by year 2040.
1600.outcome: The benefits of the project will be manifested in improved transportation conditions, improved economic activity and job opportunities, diversification of the County's tourism-dependent economy, enhanced individual economic self- sufficiency, less traffic congestion, less stress, improves emergency response times, evacuation route connection, and system reliability.

2204.organization: South Broward Hospital District dba Memorial
2204.description: Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital New Solutions Program will provide community-based direct care services to close service gaps, reduce preventable Emergency Department (ED) visits, manage crises, and avoid placing youth in locked psychiatric units. The program provides ED based initial screening and assessment and same-day admission to treatment. The goal is to provide families with greater access to appropriate interventions for youth with lower risk- stratified behavioral health conditions, strengthen family functioning, and improve overall wellbeing.
2204.purpose: In 2025 Broward County saw a 22% decrease in pediatric Baker Act beds. New Solutions reduces the number of youth needing care in an inpatient hospital setting when in crisis from mental health and/or co-occurring substance use disorders by providing an Emergency Department (ED) based initial screening and assessment and same-day admission to treatment. The program reduces ED visits and hospital admissions while addressing challenges of mental health and substance use disorders.
2204.activities: • Screen youth in the pediatric ED with behavioral health (BH) assessments. • Improve BH functioning of youth identified with lower risk stratified BH conditions through participating in New Solutions. • Provide short-term, recovery-oriented services with a multidisciplinary team proficient in working with youth facing BH challenges. • Strengthen family functioning through education and links with community partners providing health related social needs.
2204.direct_services: New Solutions will provide community-based direct care services to close service gaps, reduce preventable ED visits, manage crises, and avoid placing youth in locked psychiatric units. The goal is to provide families with greater access to appropriate interventions for youth with lower risk-stratified behavioral health conditions, strengthen family functioning, and improve overall wellbeing.
2204.population: New Solutions will serve: 1) 1,400 at-risk youth and their families at its ED; 2) 120 at-risk youth and their families through the community-based New Solutions intensive model; and 3) 1,280 at-risk youth and their families through a behavioral health community outreach and education campaign in conjunction with community agencies.
2204.outcome: 1. Services (financial and medication assistance and care management) will help meet the growing basic needs of Survivors in poverty, improve physical and mental health/wellness, thereby helping Survivors maintain their ability to live independently and avoid premature institutionalization.
2591.purpose: JFCS will provide culturally-relevant, trauma-informed support to 100 aging Holocaust Survivors living in poverty in Duval, St. Johns, Volusia and Flagler counties. Emergency financial assistance, health-related/medication assistance and care management will help meet basic needs, improve physical and mental health/wellness, helping Survivors maintain independence and avoid premature institutionalization.
2591.activities: Two geriatric care managers will provide culturally responsive case management, assessment and coordination of services/resources to Survivors. Care managers will ensure Survivors meet basic needs (housing, utilities, food, prescriptions, health care) through the provision of emergency financial assistance and medication assistance and home-delivered food. To meet linguistic needs of Survivors, one care manager speaks Russian.
2591.direct_services: Citizens will receive case management visits and phone check-ins from their care manager, Services will consist of ongoing assessment, care planning, referral and coordination of resources. Survivors will also receive help, as needed, to meet a growing demand for basic needs - medication costs, emergency financial assistance (rent/mortgage, utilities, other critical basic needs), home-delivered me

(67% of Survivors receiving care management live in poverty). The majority are Russian. Many struggle with dementia, cognitive decline, PTSD and health problems stemming from starvation and abuse endured during the Holocaust. 2591.outcome: JFCS will strengthen the safety net and support network for aging Survivors by providing access to in-home wraparound services to meet their basic needs and mental health needs. In most instances, JFCS is the sole social service/in-home provider working with these vulnerable individuals. We will enter assessment and service plan data into eCR (our EHR system), pulling evaluative reports regularly. Services will help at-risk individuals strengthen their level of functioning and improve their ability to cope with life challenges, building a stronger foundation for self sufficiency. Funding will help subsidize sliding-fee scale counseling services to lower income individuals in the community who do not have Medicaid or health insurance to cover behavioral health services. Funding will also help remove barriers to access, by providing resources such as, but not limited to, bus passes, Lyft transportation to/from sessions and equipment/tablets for telehealth services.
2596.purpose: JFCS will have expanded capacity to provide outpatient mental health and substance abuse counseling, as well as psychiatric services, to lower-income uninsured children, teens and adults in Duval County. Services will help at-risk individuals strengthen their level of functioning and improve their ability to cope with life challenges, building a stronger foundation for self sufficiency. 2596.activities: Licensed and license-eligible therapists will provide outpatient mental health counseling services to children, teens and adults. A Substance Abuse therapist will provide outpatient substance abuse services to teens and adults. Funding will help subsidize sliding fee scale services, provide additional program oversight, expand psychiatric nursing services (provided by a contract psychiatrist and staff ARNP) and help remove barriers to access for uninsured individuals.
2596.direct_services: Clients will receive a bio-psychosocial evaluation, treatment plan, counseling sessions and discharge planning. Sessions will typically be weekly, for up to 4 months. Clients may also receive psychiatric evaluation and medication management services. Additional support to help clients access barrier-free services may include bus passes, Lyft transportation to sessions, necessary equipment/tablets

A growing population in Jacksonville is caught in the middle ...hard working, providing for their families, yet unable to afford counseling. Though lower income, they do not qualify for Medicaid or they lack adequate health insurance for behavioral health care. Caught "in the gap," they can’t afford traditional
2596.outcome: Families are operating in crisis mode, and need accessible, timely, affordable mental health care to cope with chronic stress and trauma, rising family tensions and economic uncertainty. Sliding fee scale counseling is imperative. Funding a Substance Abuse therapist with expertise in working with dual-diagnosed clients and helping families alleviate barriers to participating in counseling is equally critical. This will increase a client 's ability to actively engage in services and improve their wellbeing and functioning. 2338.description: Nurse Family Partnership (NFP) works by having specially trained nurses regularly visit young, first-time parents-to-be, starting early in the pregnancy and continuing through the child’s second birthday. NFP empowers first-time parents to transform their lives and create better futures for themselves and their babies. Expectant parents benefit by getting the care and support they need to have a healthy pregnancy. At the same time, new parents develop a close relationship with a nurse who becomes a trusted resource they can rely on for advice on everything from safely caring for their child to taking steps to provide a stable, secure future for them both. Through the partnership, the nurse provides new parents with the confidence and the tools they need not only to assure a healthy start for their babies, but to envision a life of stability and opportunities for success for both parent a
2338.purpose: The funding will support salaries and benefits to ensure sustainability of Nurse Home Visitor positions at the Broward, Gadsden, Highlands, Hillsborough, Miami Dade, Northcentral, Northeast, Orange, Palm Beach, Pinellas, Southwest , and Treasure Coast sites. The funding will ensure the sites' ability to continue serving the approximate 2,000 families at risk of losing services if positions are not maintained.
2338.activities: Implementation of the Nurse Family Partnership model, an evidence-based, community health program for first-time mothers facing high-risk factors to improve maternal health, child health and development, and enhance individual educational and economic achievement. The funding will be spent to sustain nurse home visitor salaries and benefits for 12 sites serving 30 counties.
2338.direct_services: 1. Care coordination by developing a Care Plan based on an initial assessment and continuously updating it to ensure the client’s needs are met. 2. Assessments & screenings for maternal and child health, child development, mental health, substance use, intimate partner violence, and social determinants of health. 3. Case management to support prenatal care, pregnancy issues, conduct warm hand-offs
2338.population: First-time, high-risk pregnant women who are living in poverty and their babies, as well as Multiparous and Late Registrant mothers through the NFPX Bridge study. Annual mothers and babies expected to be served with full allocation are at least 325. Funded counties will include Alachua, Baker, Brevard, Broward, Citrus, Clay, Collier, Dixie, Duval, Gadsden, Gilchrist, Hendry, Hernando, Hillsborough, Indian River, Jackson, Lee, Levy, Marion, Martin, Miami- Dade, Okeechobee, Orange, Palm Beach, Pin
2338.outcome: Nurse Family Partnership has extensive data, research studies and replication analyses showing the program’s impact over the past 40 years. NFP has repeatedly demonstrated: • 82% increase in labor participation by the mothers • 9% reduction in Medicaid costs and an 11% reduction in Food Stamp costs • 46% increase in father presence and partner stability • 31% reduction in closely-spaced subsequent pregnancies

2597.description: This project involves the construction of a high-quality, all-weather turf field designed to expand year-round athletic and recreational opportunities for students and the surrounding community. The field will serve as a durable, safe space for sports such as soccer, football, and other team activities, reducing weather-related cancellations and supporting increased participation, training, and physical education programming.
2597.purpose: The requested funds will be used to build a durable, all-weather turf field that expands safe, year-round access to athletic and recreational opportunities for students and the broader community. This investment will enhance physical education, support school sports programs, and promote healthier, more active lifestyles.
2597.activities: The turf field will provide a dedicated, safe location for students and public school athletes to participate in sports such as soccer, football, and other team-based activities. It will also support practices, PE classes, conditioning sessions, and community recreation, ensuring consistent access to structured physical activity throughout the year.
2597.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with direct access to a safe, reliable, year-round athletic field for sports, physical education, and recreational activities. It will support school teams, youth leagues, and community programs by offering a high-quality space for practices, games, fitness, and organized events that promote health, engagement, and teamwork.
2597.population: The target population includes economically disadvantaged youth, at-risk youth, and grade school through high school students who rely on safe, accessible spaces for athletics and recreational programming. The project is expected to serve more than 800 individuals annually through school sports, physical education classes, and community-based activities.
2597.outcome: Athletic programs help build confidence in our youth and teach them resilience, discipline, and the value of teamwork. Rather than focusing solely on wins and losses, we measure success by the growth in our students’ character, their commitment to their education, and their conduct on and off the field. Participation in athletics requires students to maintain strong attendance and academic performance, which has consistently resulted in improved daily attendance, better engagement in the classroom, and increased academic effort. These outcomes will be measured through school attendance records, GPA tracking, and student eligibility reports for athletic participation.

1673.description: The Hollywood Marine Public Safety Initiative includes the purchase and outfitting of a multipurpose enforcement vessel with lifesaving equipment, including night-vision goggles, a side-scan radar, and a vessel boarding hook. The purpose of this initiative is to reduce vessel accidents, reduce water violations, enforce derelict vessel laws, and educate the boating community. The City of Hollywood’s marine jurisdiction has recently expanded its northern boundaries to include Port Everglades, one of the world's busiest cruise ports and container ports. Additionally, the patrolled waterway serves as the connection between Broward County and Miami-Dade County.
1673.purpose: The purpose of the Hollywood Marine Public Safety Initiative is to reduce vessel accidents, reduce water violations, enforce derelict vessel laws, and educate the boating community. The purchasing and outfitting of a multipurpose enforcement vessel with lifesaving equipment, including night-vision goggles, a side-scan radar, and a vessel boarding hook will achieve this purpose.
1673.activities: The services provided will be the enforcement of laws, emergency response, and education of the boating public. The City of Hollywood’s marine jurisdiction has recently expanded its northern boundaries to include Port Everglades and serves as the waterway connection between Broward County and Miami-Dade County.
1673.direct_services: The services provided enhance public safety through patrolling waterways, which involves enforcing laws, providing boater education, and responding to emergencies, all of which benefit residents, visitors, and boaters.
1673.population: The target population is the 155,000 residents of the City of Hollywood and the millions of local and national tourists who visit the City and Port Everglades. Since patrol will also occur within Port Everglades, it is important to indicate that Port Everglades is projected to handle over 4.7 million cruise passengers this year. Additionally, the Port reports that 4,000 vessels call at Port Everglades annually, including cruise ships and cargo vessels.
1673.outcome: Improve physical health - reducing accidents and injuries - tracking incidents Enhance/preserve/improve environmental or fish and wildlife quality - reduce the amount of derelict vessels - tracking outcomes of derelict vessels Protect the general public from harm - Increased patrol and education - tracking incidents Improve quality of education - Providing knowledge and skills on safe and responsible boating practices. • Tracking contacts made and educational materials provided

2205.description: Memorial Healthcare System (Memorial) respectfully requests $1 million to expand our capacity to respond to the ongoing overdose crisis through enhanced clinical and care coordination that identifies and addresses the behavioral components of addiction and ensures a warm hand-off to outpatient services. Through MAT, Memorial will provide 200 individuals, including pregnant women, with immediate addiction screening in the emergency department and comprehensive substance use disorder treatment. MAT will also feature an integrated primary care and behavioral health home for 200 persons that provides ongoing recovery support, along with an extensive community outreach and education campaign that targets 1,000 persons at risk of substance use disorder in conjunction with community agencies and harm reduction resources (Narcan Kits).
2205.purpose: Memorial will achieve the following goals: 1) reduce the number of opioid-related overdoses and fatalities in adults, including pregnant women, through screening programs for substance use disorder in medical settings and immediate access to medication-assisted treatment. 2) increase the number of neonates born free of illicit substances; and 3) improve the physical health of adults through an integrated primary and behavioral health home for ongoing recovery support.
2205.activities: 1) an extensive community outreach and education campaign for adults, including pregnant women, who are at-risk of substance use disorder (SUD). 2) screening for SUD within Memorial's medical settings to identify persons in need of addiction treatment services; and 3) care coordination and case management for patients as they transition from addiction treatment services to outpatient services.
2205.direct_services: Direct services include: 1) addiction treatment induction (detoxification) services; 2) medication-assisted treatment (MAT) services; 3) integrated primary care and behavioral health care services; 4) care coordination services; 5) infectious disease treatment; 6) prenatal care services; 7) peer support services; and 8) ongoing recovery support services.
2205.population: 1) 200 adults through its comprehensive SUD treatment program. 2) 200 adults through its integrated primary care and behavioral health home for ongoing recovery support; and 3) 1,000 persons at-risk of SUD through its extensive community outreach and education campaign in conjunction with community agencies.
2205.outcome: Memorial will reduce substance abuse and improve the physical health of adults, including pregnant women in Broward, Miami-Dade and Palm Beach Counties. The methodology for this return on investment includes: The sum of Medicaid reimbursement for an infant requiring a NICU stay (APR-DRG 6253) due to Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome is $30,279 versus $679 for a normal newborn (APR-DRG 6401). For 20 babies born drug-free each year, Memorial could save the state $591,700. The sum of Medicaid reimbursement for an inpatient hospitalization due to opioid complications is $122,624 versus $4,023 for a non-fatal opioid overdose treated in the ED. 2602.description: American Legion Boys State is among the most respected and selective educational programs of government instruction for U.S. high school students. It is a participatory program in which students become part of the operation of local, county and state government. The American Legion Auxiliary sponsors a separate but similar program for young women called Girls State. At both programs, participants learn the rights, privileges and responsibilities of franchised citizens. The training is objective and centers on the structure of city, county and state governments. Operated by students elected to various offices, Boys State and Girls State activities include legislative sessions, court proceedings, law-enforcement presentations, assemblies, bands, choruses and recreational programs.
2602.purpose: The funds will be used to house over 500 boys and 300 girls during Boys State and Girls State programs put on by The American Legion and The American Legion Auxiliary. This will allow the students to attend these programs, which are considered to be one of Florida's premiere citizenship programs for rising seniors.
2602.activities: The requested funds will pay for student housing during Boys State and Girls State.
2602.direct_services: Housing at Florida State University during Boys State and Girls State programs.
2602.population: Approximately 800 high school students will benefit from participating in the programs.
2602.outcome: Florida American Legion Boys State and Florida American Legion Auxiliary Girls State are a unique summertime leadership/government program that does not emphasize classroom lectures and textbook learning. Instead, it focuses on participation and personal experience in a model state, complete with governing bodies and elected public officials. Mirrors structure and operation of a State. The measure has traditionally been to follow up with students and families involved with overwhelming support.

1282.description: The Lucy Project delivers evidence based literacy intervention and professional development directly in schools across Miami Dade County. Through its Structured Literacy model, the program ensures all students, including those with dyslexia and other reading difficulties, receive explicit, systematic instruction aligned to the science of reading. The team works in classrooms year round to provide differentiated instruction, model best practices for teachers, and build school capacity to sustain progress. Each partnership includes professional learning for administrators, summer institutes for teachers, and ongoing coaching that strengthens early reading outcomes, student confidence and builds local capacity.
1282.purpose: Improved early reading outcomes in additional schools. A larger group of pre-K through grade-two students will receive direct Structured Literacy support, and the teachers who serve them will gain the skill and capacity to deliver evidence-based instruction without outside support. The funds allow the model to expand while building permanent school-based capacity so results continue without ongoing external intervention.
1282.activities: Funds will build organizational and school capacity to scale the Lucy Project structured literacy model, codify best practices, and strengthen data systems that support 440 current and 80 additional students while preparing for expansion to additional counties.
1282.direct_services: The project provides year-round structured literacy instruction for kindergarten students, including those with dyslexia and related reading challenges, hands-on teacher coaching, administrative professional development, summer training institutes, and family literacy workshops to improve reading proficiency and help schools sustain success independently.
1282.population: The project primarily serves grade school students, with 520 children reached through direct instruction and capacity building, including 440 students in current partner schools and 80 additional students in the new expansion classrooms. Preschool students are also served through PreK instruction and early foundational support. Because we work in the most economically disadvantaged schools, the population includes economically disadvantaged persons and at-risk youth. The project also provides de
1282.outcome: Outcomes: Improved reading outcomes for PreK through second grade students, with more children reaching grade level through consistent structured literacy instruction. Stronger instructional capacity among teachers and school leaders in underperforming schools, resulting in higher quality daily reading instruction. Earlier identification and support for children with reading difficulties, reducing the number of students who face third grade retention. Methodology: Student progress measured through Accidence and Star Reading benchmarks three times per year. Fidelity of implementation assessed through structured classroom observations.
