1998.description: Drone as First Responder 2.0 (DFR 2.0) is an advanced version of DFR technology that uses automated drone docking stations, enabling rapid, remote, and autonomous drone deployment without the need for human observers on the ground for Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS) operations. This system aims to provide enhanced situational awareness and safety for public safety agencies by reducing costs, expanding operational periods, and allowing for quicker response times, ideally with a single operator overseeing multiple missions. DFR program can reduce costs and expand operational period.
1998.purpose: This can reduce costs and expand operational periods by allowing public safety agencies to reallocate public safety resources.
1998.activities: Can provide a technology-driven approach to increase efficiency and effectiveness when responding to calls for service. When a call comes into the emergency center, dispatchers and pilots can initiate a drone mission to respond to the scene before ground personnel arrive. In less than 90 seconds, teleoperators (and those within a real time information center) can have a visual of an accident scene, crime in progress or even simple calls like parking complaints.
1998.direct_services: This live, real time information can be relayed to field personnel and provide critical updates, such as a suspect leaving a scene and the direction they are headed. It will be particularly valuable and versatile for search and rescue operations, offering aerial perspectives to speed up resource allocation/reallocation, improving situational awareness while providing faster and well informed infor
1998.population: The entire city of Titusville would be the target population, to include residents and visitors.
1998.outcome: Providing a way to give real time updates to increase efficiency and effectiveness while responding to calls for service.

1848.description: The Cities current back-up infrastructure is utilized to secure digital data against unintentional loss and cyber security threats. The system secures data city wide to include public safety, operations, critical infrastructure and City administration. Our current setup is at risk of exceeding its limits in both storage capacity and recovery performance. This project will enhance data recovery capabilities, security and immutable storage for digital resilience. The City is currently seeking funding for a full replacement of the systems, at an estimated cost of $264,000.
1848.purpose: To enhance cybersecurity and data resilience through immutable, physically isolated (air-gapped) backups and verified zero-error recovery, ensuring rapid restoration of city and first responder services and compliance with evolving regulatory standards such as CJIS.
1848.activities: Accommodate the city’s increasing data footprint with scalable storage solutions. Advance to the 3-2-1-1-0 backup model and move beyond the traditional 3-2-1 method by adding both immutable/air-gapped backups for ransomware defense and verified zero-error recovery to ensure data integrity. Improve performance by Reduce Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) from days to hours and Improve Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs) to minutes.
1848.direct_services: Increased cyberware resilience will reduce the risk of service gaps due to cyber attacks and data loss for first responders (Police and Fire) and all city critical infrastructure, such as water, sewer and waste services. Reduced risk of financial impact to city due to loss of critical data leads to reduced financial burden to citizenship.
1848.population: All residence in the City of Titusville. Approx. 49,883
1848.outcome: Key outcomes include faster recovery times (RTOs reduced from days to hours), improved data integrity (RPOs reduced to minutes), resilience against ransomware through immutable backups. These improvements will ensure continuity of public services, safeguard sensitive data, and maintain public trust. Methodology for Measuring Outcomes: Recovery Time Objective (RTO): Track the time required to restore critical systems during disaster recovery tests. Recovery Point Objective (RPO): Measure the age of data restored to assess how current backups are. Immutable Backup Verification: Confirm air-gapped, tamper-proof backups through system logs and integrity checks. Zero-Error Recovery Testing: Condu

1580.description: The program provides accessible, cost effective care to residents, preventing unnecessary emergency room visit by offering same day and walk in access to primary care providers as an alternative to use of the emergency room for non- emergent care. Patients also benefit from utilizing MCR's emergency room diversion locations as additional supportive services such as care coordination, chronic disease management and pharmacy services are available which result in reducing recurring ER visits.
1580.purpose: The program provides accessible, cost effective care to residents, preventing unnecessary emergency room visit by offering same day and walk in access to primary care providers as an alternative to use of the emergency room for non-emergent care. Patients also benefit from utilizing MCR's emergency room diversion locations as additional supportive services such as care coordination, chronic disease management and pharmacy services are available which result in reducing recurring ER visits.
1580.activities: MCR will continue to operate open access to primary medical care at its East Manatee Health Center and Lawton Chiles Pediatric Health Center. Patients in need of a non-emergent medical visit can walk in to the locations or call to obtain a same day appointment. This same day service access will reduce the number of patients accessing the emergency room and ultimately reduce cost to the State.
1580.direct_services: Those accessing ERD services will receive a comprehensive medical visit to evaluate and treat their condition. Diagnosis related to hypertension and diabetes are the top two reasons the walk-in location is accessed. New patient will be referred to a MCR primary care provider to establish a medical home. All accessing services will receive wrap around services as needed and reduced RX pricing.
1580.population: The target population for the ERD program includes Medicaid and low income Uninsured residents who present at the ERD locations
1580.outcome: GOAL: Reduce the cost of avoidable ER visit by offering walk in access. Outcome:1. 75% of the new patients accessing services will be referred to a MCR medical provider to establish a medical home to receive ongoing treatment and management for their condition to avoid possible future ER visits. 2. 90% of the projected number of new and established patient visits will be achieved.1. MCR's electronic health record will be used to track the number of new patients accessing the ERD locations and of those the number who were referred to establish a medical home. Measurement: Use of MCR's electronic health record will provide visit and referral information.

1551.description: This project intends to offer multidisciplinary access to services at historic educational property located in rural and economically depressed Madison County.
1551.purpose: The funds will support the restoration and revitalization of a historic property, transforming it into a multipurpose vocational center available to residents of Madison and nearby communities.
1551.activities: Offer training programs with certification in fields like plumbing, auto repair, barbering, and AC maintenance.
1551.direct_services: Support for veterans, agricultural workers, and early childhood education.
1551.population: The programs are projected to serve a limited number of people, including those seeking help with job training and placement. We anticipate that more than 800 individuals will register for these programs.
1551.outcome: The anticipated benefits include enhanced economic opportunities for clients, an improved quality of life, and a heightened appreciation for the property's cultural and historical significance.

1255.description: Program will focus on addressing the persistent disparities in maternal health outcomes, particularly among uninsured women with chronic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, and obesity. In Manatee County, where 18% of adults are uninsured, pregnant individuals with high-risk medical profiles often lack access to the specialized care required to manage their pregnancies safely. These gaps contribute to elevated rates of preterm birth, low birth weight, and maternal morbidity, disproportionately affecting communities of color and those living in poverty.
1255.purpose: This project will support perinatology services in Manatee County, designed to provide care for uninsured pregnant individuals experiencing high-risk pregnancies. The initiative will address critical gaps in access to specialized care is accessible and integrated with existing OB services provided at MCR Health. Services will focus on on high-risk pregnancies due to chronic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension and racial and ethnic minorities disproportionately at risk.
1255.activities: Improved delivery outcomes will result from the expansion of services and availability. The obstetrician will refer woman who present as high risk to the perinatologist. The perinatologist will identify and treat conditions which result in fetal infant deaths, negative birth outcomes such as low birth weight, the incident of neonatal abstinence syndrome and chronic diseases.
1255.direct_services: Direct services will include comprehensive Maternal Fetal Medicine exam and treatment by a perinatologist for patients referred by MCR Health obstetrical providers. Other services will include ultrasound technician who will perform the ultrasound that is provided to the perinatologist to identify any issues that present which place the child at risk.
1255.population: Services will focus on on high-risk pregnancies due to chronic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension and racial and ethnic minorities disproportionately at risk.
1255.outcome: The cost effectiveness and overall goals of the project will be measured by the outcomes data within the target population. Through analysis of the outcomes data, an improved health status will be realized with the perinatologist involvement in the care of the woman and fetus through better-management of the pregnancy. The data collected will be entered into the computer system. Reports are generated monthly to address the progress made on the outcome measures.

1550.description: The City of Carrabelle proposes a roadway resurfacing project to improve pavement conditions along several key streets in the downtown area. This effort aims to enhance drivability, extend pavement life, and support safe, reliable access for residents, visitors, and local businesses.
1550.purpose: Mill and resurface roads which driving conditions need to be improved.
1550.direct_services: Improved driving conditions and resurfaced roadways.
1550.population: The city of Carrabelle at large and others who utilize these roadways.
1550.outcome: Improved roadway conditions. This will be measured via milling and resurfacing.

1545.description: Funds will purchase one municipal SUV, one municipal pickup truck, and a grapple truck to speed emergency response and debris removal, improve public safety, and boost resiliency. After Hurricane Helene, cleanup was delayed for several weeks while waiting to borrow a grapple truck from Jefferson County. The grapple truck will clear storm debris to restore access quickly, reducing hazards. The municipal pick-up truck will haul tools, materials, and crews for emergency repairs. The municipal SUV will enable Town leadership to assess damage, coordinate operations, and deliver supplies.
1545.purpose: Funds will purchase one municipal SUV, one municipal pickup truck, and a grapple truck to speed emergency response and debris removal, improve public safety, and boost resiliency. The grapple truck will clear storm debris to restore access quickly, reducing hazards. The municipal pick-up truck will haul tools, materials, and crews for emergency repairs. The municipal SUV will enable Town leadership to assess damage, coordinate operations, and deliver supplies.
1545.activities: Activities include acquiring one municipal SUV, one municipal pickup truck, and a grapple truck to improve emergency response and debris removal.
1545.direct_services: The grapple truck will clear storm debris to restore access quickly, reducing hazards. The municipal pick-up truck will haul tools, materials, and crews for emergency repairs. The SUV will enable Town leadership to assess damage, coordinate operations, and deliver supplies. Together, they speed recovery, improve safety, and ensure timely service for residents.
1545.population: Residents of the Town of Greenville (approx. 780) and surrounding unincorporated Madison County.
1545.outcome: Purchasing the vehicles and a grapple truck will speed debris removal, improve emergency access, and reduce hazards after storms. Faster cleanup lowers risks of injury, disease, and stress, while ensuring responders reach residents promptly and safely. Monitor performance during severe weather to determine if staff can reach and clear affected areas faster and more safely, aiming for at reduction in debris removal time compared to previous storm events.

1544.organization: The Sower of the Seed Food Pantry
1544.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1544.description: Sower of the Seed food pantry serves community members that live on limited incomes, with restricted transportation and few local resources for obtaining essential supplies. With grant support, we seek to purchase and distribute shelf-stable food, dry milk, and incontinence supplies—including adult pull-ups and Depends—to our high-need clients.
1544.purpose: Our organization serves vulnerable older adults, over 60 years of age, in rural communities who face significant barriers in accessing basic necessities. Many of our clients live on limited incomes, with restricted transportation and few local resources for obtaining essential supplies. With grant support, we seek to purchase and distribute shelf-stable food, dry milk, and incontinence supplies—including adult pull-ups and Depends—to our high-need clients.
1544.activities: The $25,000 grant will be used entirely to purchase and distribute nutritious shelf-stable food, dry milk, and essential incontinence supplies—such as adult pull-ups and Depends—to help seniors in need.
1544.direct_services: The $25,000 grant will be used entirely to purchase and distribute nutritious shelf-stable food, dry milk, and essential incontinence supplies—such as adult pull-ups and Depends—to help seniors in need.
1544.population: Elderly, peple with poor physical health, economically disadcantaged people, up to 200 people
1544.outcome: As a result of this funding, many seniors experiencing food insecurity and limited access to personal care supplies will receive monthly allotments of nutritious shelf-stable food, dry milk, and adult incontinence products. These services will help improve recipients’ nutrition, overall health, and dignity, allowing them to remain safely and independently in their homes. Impact will be measured by tracking the number of seniors served, the quantity of supplies distributed, and conducting follow-up surveys to assess improvements in food security, physical health, and quality of life among participants. Testimonials and survey results will demonstrate how this support directly addressed urgent

1601.description: This project is to conduct a targeted, one-time removal of shoals and invasive vegetation within Boggy Creek to restore water conveyance to East Lake Tohopekaliga (East Lake Toho).
1601.purpose: To restore water conveyance to East Lake Toho, restore native habitat and improve ecological health, reduce flood risk by re-establishing natural flood conveyance, strengthen watershed resiliency against future development and stormwater impacts, and restore safe navigation and provide management access for agencies.
1601.activities: Design, permitting, and removal of shoals and invasive/nuisance vegetation.
1601.population: The project area includes a diverse population with mixed racial backgrounds and a median household income reflective of the community’s demographics. The project is expected to benefit approximately 10,000 affected individuals.
1601.outcome: The expected benefits include a reduced risk and duration of flooding, as well as improved natural habitats through the reduction of invasive vegetation. The methodology for measuring these benefits will focus on increases in acres of open water, reductions in water levels, and improvements in water conveyance.

1543.description: The requested funding will support ongoing scientific research and public education initiatives designed to improve the health and sustainability of Wakulla Springs. Activities funded will include watershed tours, communication research, student internships, and educational outreach programs that engage the local community and promote conservation. Additionally, the funding will support the development of an educational video and statewide curriculum for Florida students in partnership with the Challenger Learning Center, providing science-based instructional content to the thousands of children who visit the center each year. The project will also address needs identified during its first year of implementation, ensuring that both research and educational programs continue to meet community and ecological goals while empowering citizens to participate in the long-term stewardship of thi
1543.purpose: The funds requested will help protect and sustain Wakulla Springs by supporting scientific research to identify groundwater sources, assess nutrient pollution, and improve understanding of the ecosystem. They will also promote public education and community engagement through watershed tours, internships, educational outreach, and the development of a statewide video and curriculum for students. Overall, the goal is to empower citizens and students to actively participate in conservation and lon
1543.activities: The funds will support activities such as watershed tours, communication research, student internships, and educational outreach to increase public awareness and engagement in conservation. They will also fund the creation of an educational video and statewide curriculum in partnership with the Challenger Learning Center to provide science- based instruction to students across Florida.
1543.direct_services: The appropriation will provide citizens with hands-on educational opportunities through watershed tours, internships, and community outreach programs. It will also offer students access to a statewide educational video and curriculum, delivering science-based information about Wakulla Springs and its conservation.
1543.population: The target population includes students, local community members, and visitors to Wakulla Springs, with a particular focus on the thousands of children who participate in programs at the Challenger Learning Center. Overall, the project is expected to reach several thousand individuals each year through tours, educational programs, and outreach activities.
1543.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is improved health and sustainability of Wakulla Springs, increased public awareness of conservation issues, and greater community and student engagement in environmental stewardship. Outcomes will be measured through participation metrics for tours, internships, and educational programs, feedback from students and community members, and assessment of educational materials’ reach and effectiveness in conveying key scientific and conservation concepts.

2403.description: Due to flooding from Hurricane Milton, the pond walls will be reinforced and deepened to allow for more water retention. The pond is adjacent to an elementary school and several residences. It is critical that this pond be able to retain water to allow minimize the impact to the public school and surrounding residents.
2403.purpose: To mitigate flooding in the surrounding area due to the increase in rain intensity and frequency in an older existing stormwater pond.
2403.activities: Mitigation of potential flooding to private property, school property and public right of way.
2403.population: Elderly, economically disadvantaged, at risk youth, grade school student and the general population.
2403.outcome: If the pond is able to handle the increase in stormwater there will be a lessened likelihood that the school will be closed due to flooding issue that would prevent the school from being open or operating at full capacity. Measurements include: Days closed due to flooding and number of properties damaged by interior flooding.

2420.description: Feeding Florida’s produce incentive program, Fresh Access Bucks (FAB), would like to expand their produce initiative to help bring fresh, nutritious fruits and vegetables to the under-resourced and rural communities that need it most. The FAB expansion program would provide produce incentives to SNAP recipients or food insecure Floridians at specified grocery locations. These grocers would be trained in the disbursement, control and redemption of these dollars in order to ensure proper utilization of the funding. As evidenced by pilot versions of this program, the increase in demand for fresh produce would also create an increase in supply and the economic benefit to the retailers.
2420.purpose: Finding a way to incentivize healthy food consumption by food insecure Floridians is a critical part of supporting and enhancing our state. Hundreds of studies agree that nutritional food can help prevent any number of health issues and food as medicine is widely recognized as good for all communities. The goal is to improve the overall health of the most vulnerable population of our state by increasing access to affordable fresh produce in under-served and rural communities.
2420.activities: The team will be working in conjunction with the retail operational teams around the state to ensure that their customers are aware of the program and the extent of the available benefits. Training on all aspects of the program will be provided.
2420.direct_services: Citizens utilizing SNAP benefits will have immediate access to the supplemental funds expressly for the purchase fresh fruits and vegetables from participating retail locations.
2420.population: The target population is the food insecure customer base of the retail outlets that will be offering the program. Based on historical transaction data, it is expected that over 70,000 people will participate in this program and obtain fresh, healthy food to supplement their SNAP spend.
2420.outcome: The expected benefit is to allow for food insecure Floridians participating in the SNAP program to obtain healthy food in a dignified manner. It is expected that this will improve the health conditions of these citizens. All transactions involving SNAP spend, incentive issuance and incentive redemption will be constantly monitored. This ensures the integrity of the funding issuance process and that all funds were spent as indicated.

1852.description: This request is for the purchase and deployment of Archer 1200 Mobile Vehicular Threat Mitigation Barriers at community events throughout the City of New Smyrna Beach. These engineered barriers will establish a hard line of defense to deter and mitigate the threat of vehicles being used for harm or accidental intrusion at high-attendance, pedestrian-based gatherings. The system will also serve as a critical regional asset, supporting neighboring law enforcement agencies.
1852.purpose: The funding is specifically requested to bolster the public safety posture of New Smyrna Beach and neighboring jurisdictions. This investment will enable the deployment of effective measures for the deterrence and active mitigation of vehicular threats targeting high-density public gatherings.
1852.activities: The entire asset inventory (trailers, barriers, and accessories) will be housed and secured at the New Smyrna Beach Public Works facility. Strategic deployment, managed through detailed operational plans, will establish safe perimeters around public gatherings, effectively shielding critical roadways and pedestrian areas from vehicle-borne threats and accidental intrusions.
1852.direct_services: This initiative provides enhanced safety for citizens attending public events by strategically blocking unauthorized vehicle access to event perimeters, roadways, and walkways. The systems being procured are specifically engineered and tested to mitigate vehicular threats and incidents, ensuring proper function and efficacy.
1852.population: The targeted population includes all residents and visitors attending the numerous annual public events hosted by the City of New Smyrna Beach, totaling thousands of individuals per event. Additionally, the system will serve the populations of neighboring communities by being available as a regional resource to secure their public gatherings.
1852.outcome: The goal is to establish a sustainable, cross-departmental capability for New Smyrna Beach Police and Public Works to deploy vehicular threat mitigation barriers, enhancing safety at public events. We will track deployments by cross- referencing the number of events secured and estimated patron attendance. A lack of vehicular incidents at these events will directly correlate to the effectiveness of the barriers.

1292.description: The Florida-Israel Business Accelerator (FIBA), an initiative of the Tampa Jewish Community Centers and Federation, will continue to grow Florida’s global economy by focusing in 2026 on Israeli innovation in drones, artificial intelligence (AI), and cybersecurity. Partnering with leading Israeli technology companies, FIBA will bring these advanced solutions to Florida’s defense, space, aviation, hospitality, and health tech industries, strengthening competitiveness, fueling innovation, and expanding high-skilled job opportunities across the state. To date, FIBA has partnered with more than 100 Israeli companies, who created over 180 high-skilled direct jobs across Florida. Companies such as XTEND and Ossio are projected to create about 200 additional jobs in the coming years through new facilities in Tampa and Palmetto. Ten companies have successfully exited or gone public, and 46 have e
1292.purpose: FIBA will collaborate with Florida’s defense, space, aviation, hospitality, and health tech industries to identify key technological challenges and match them with high-tech solutions from Israel in drones, artificial intelligence (AI), and cybersecurity. By facilitating the deployment of these cutting-edge technologies, FIBA will help Florida companies improve efficiency, enhance safety, and strengthen competitiveness in both domestic and global markets. The initiative will create high-skilled
1292.activities: FIBA will facilitate partnerships between Israeli technology leaders and Florida businesses through targeted industry workshops, technology demonstrations, curated events, and pilot programs. The initiative will support the integration of advanced drone, AI, and cybersecurity solutions into Florida’s defense, space, aviation, hospitality, and health tech sectors. Activities will include matching Israeli experts with Florida industry partners, connecting companies with potential investors, and as
1292.direct_services: FIBA will deliver Israeli innovation in drones, AI, and cybersecurity to improve the daily lives of Floridians through safer communities, stronger defense systems, smarter transportation, enhanced healthcare, and a more resilient hospitality sector. These technologies will expand high-skilled job opportunities, strengthen local economies, and improve quality of life across the state.
1292.population: Statewide, the population will benefit from the deployment of Israeli technologies in drones, AI, and cybersecurity that enhance operational efficiency, safety, and service delivery across key sectors including defense, space, aviation, hospitality, and health tech. FIBA’s initiative will address concrete challenges such as improving healthcare delivery through AI solutions, strengthening cybersecurity defenses for Florida businesses, supporting advanced systems in defense and space, and streaml
1292.outcome: The project will strengthen Florida’s economy by increasing productivity, safety, and job creation across defense, space, aviation, hospitality, and health tech industries through the integration of Israeli drone, AI, and cybersecurity technologies. Expected outcomes include greater business efficiency, new high-skilled employment opportunities, and enhanced industry competitiveness. Results will be measured by tracking jobs created, companies established or expanded, investment attracted, and efficiency improvements. FIBA will collect and analyze data through partner reporting, pilot program outcomes, and economic impact assessments to ensure measurable statewide benefit.

1853.description: This project would be to dredge the area near the Turnbull Bay Canal Bridge in order to improve water flow into Rose Bay. These efforts would reduce flooding in the local area and City-wide during high rainfall events. Dredging operations would commence after acquisition of necessary permits. The City of New Smyrna Beach is already coordinating with a contractor to acquire permits for this project.
1853.purpose: The requested funds will support dredging near the Turnbull Bay Canal Bridge to restore water flow through the removal of built up sediment, reduce neighborhood flooding, and improve tidal exchange and water quality in Rose Bay.
1853.activities: Construction/Dredging of Turnbull Creek Canal near the Turnbull Bay Canal Bridge.
1853.direct_services: The project will deliver critical flood protection and drainage improvements for residents in New Smyrna Beach, especially during hurricanes and intense rainfall. The improved capacity due to sediment removal will allow for water offshed
1853.population: This project would directly benefit residents near the Turnbull Canal and Rose Bay Area. Additionally, due to improved drainage, this project would also affect the City as a whole. This area has a large percentage of low and moderate income residents that are signficantly affected by extreme weather events.
1853.outcome: The City plans on measuring success through pre and post-construction monitoring of total sediment removal cubic yardage amounts, improvements to the water movement & capacity in the area, and tracking reductions in flood-related reports.

2658.description: The requested funds will be used to expand access to critical developmental resources for students in rural communities across Florida's 2nd District. The funding will enable the launch of 20 camps across 13 counties, serving up to 1,500 students, providing structured mentorship, sports-based leadership training, and mental health support.
2658.purpose: The funding will enable the launch of 20 camps across 13 counties, serving up to 1,500 students, providing structured mentorship, sports-based leadership training, and mental health support.
2658.activities: Multi-tiered program integrating mental health support, cognitive development, and physical wellness. Students receive resilience training, critical thinking development, and sports-based leadership growth.
2658.direct_services: Free on-site mental health support from licensed professionals, skills training, mentorship in leadership and problem solving, and physical wellness educations for over 1,500 students.
2658.population: Grade-school youth across the 13 counties. Up to 1,500 children will be served through the program.
2658.outcome: Physical and mental health improvements, leadership skills for participants, mentoring. These outcomes will be measured with qualitative data points following the program to include surveys and other forms of assessments.

1293.description: The Florida Institute for Pediatric Rare Diseases, established within the Florida State University College of Medicine, will serve as a statewide hub for research, clinical care, education, and advocacy for pediatric rare diseases. The institute will advance the diagnosis, treatment, and support for children and families affected by these conditions. A key initiative, the Sunshine Genetics Pilot Program, will provide opt-in genetic testing for newborns beyond the state's standard newborn screening program. This three-year pilot program will partner with universities, healthcare providers, and genetic specialists to offer early detection, enabling faster diagnosis and treatment. Families will receive comprehensive clinical services, genetic counseling, and support resources to navigate these conditions.
1293.purpose: Funds will support the Sunshine Genetics Pilot Program, a part of Florida Institute for Pediatric Rare Diseases at FSU's College of Medicine, providing opt-in genetic testing for newborns, improving early detection and treatment. Additionally, funds will create the Sunshine Genetics Consortium to facilitate collaboration and data-sharing among researchers and healthcare providers.
1293.activities: The funds will support genetic testing for newborns through the Sunshine Genetics Pilot Program, expanding early detection of pediatric rare diseases. Services will include multidisciplinary clinical care, genetic counseling, and patient advocacy for affected families. The program will also foster research collaboration through the Sunshine Genetics Consortium, collecting and analyzing deidentified data to advance medical knowledge. Additionally, healthcare professionals will receive training to
1293.direct_services: The funding will provide opt-in genetic testing for newborns, offering early detection of rare diseases. Families will receive comprehensive clinical care, genetic counseling, and patient support services. The institute will train healthcare professionals, improving diagnosis and treatment statewide. Through the Sunshine Genetics Consortium, data-sharing will enhance research, benefiting children.
1293.population: The target population for this project includes newborns and children diagnosed with pediatric rare diseases, as well as their families. Additionally, healthcare professionals in the fields of genetics, pediatrics, and rare disease management will be served through training programs. The program aims to serve thousands of newborns in Florida through the opt-in genetic testing during the pilot program. It is expected that hundreds of healthcare professionals will benefit from the training and edu
1293.outcome: The expected benefits of this project include improved health outcomes for children with rare diseases through early diagnosis, reduced healthcare costs via early intervention, and enhanced expertise in rare disease management. Families will receive critical support, and the project will advance research in pediatric rare diseases. Outcomes will be measured by tracking the number of newborns screened and diagnosed, monitoring health improvements through early treatment, evaluating the success of healthcare professional training, and assessing the effectiveness of the Sunshine Genetics Consortium through collaborative research and data sharing.

1530.description: This project will repair/replace the stormwater box culvert passing underneath S Mulberry St. and the open stormwater ditch running alongside the street. These items are failing, causing collapse of the street and erosion of surrounding area. The repair/replacement of these items will allow for the street, which has been closed for more than 12 months, to be repaired and reopened, putting an important connector street back into service. The rehab of this stormwater system will support the proper conveyance of stormwater that runs off of U.S. Hwy 19, mitigating the risk of flooding and decreasing the amount of sediment transfer and deposition into our wetlands.
1530.purpose: Re-opening of important connector street. Street serves as detour route during emergencies and state highway closures but has been closed for more than 12 months because of degraded box culvert running underneath and other infrastructure deficiencies. Proper conveyance of stormwater without the continuing erosion of the area, and decreased transfer and deposition of sediment into wetlands.
1530.activities: Planning, design, construction, and supervision of project by City of Monticello and qualified contracted personnel. Completed project will provide Safe Pedestrian and Vehicular Access, and Proper Stormwater Conveyance.
1530.direct_services: Safe access for pedestrians and vehicles. Proper conveyance of stormwater. Flood resilience.
1530.population: City of Monticello Greater than 2,700 people
1530.outcome: Avoidance of total collapse of important connector street: Safe, structurally sound street once completed. Reopening of important connector street closed for more than 12 months: Safe, structurally sound street. Rehabilitated stormwater infrastructure: Conveyance of stormwater without erosion of soil, bypass of drainage path, or increased deposition of soil in wetlands.

1529.description: Through delivery of its Family Centric Model (FCM), AMIkids wants to engage, empower & strengthen families to break the cycle of juvenile justice involvement. AMIkids developed FCM, a research informed community-based model, in 2016. The model was created to improve family functioning while reducing anti-social behaviors and improve psychosocial functioning of youth. Sessions are provided in the home with all family members and progress through three stages: family bonding & assessment, family development, and family preservation. Using an approved human subject research protocol, the Justice Research Center conducted a randomized clinical trial to measure the model’s effectiveness for 3 years. Results showed that youth who were assigned to receive FCM services achieved greater reductions in defiant, aggressive, and rule breaking behaviors. Parents of youth served in the FCM project repo
1529.purpose: Divert youth who demonstrate criminal risk factors from initial contact with DJJ or from further Department of Juvenile Justice involvement and incorporate family engagement and alliance so that the prevention and intervention services with youth have a long term impact.
1529.activities: The Family Centric model includes three stages of services (Family Bonding and Assessment, Family Development, Family Preservation). A Family Support Specialist provides 10 to 18 sessions with specific skills for families focused on one of three tracks, based on assessed risks and needs: aggression and conflict, healthy relationships and positive use of free time, and effective communication. Services are provided in the home or, when not feasible, in a location convenient for the family within
1529.direct_services: Family Centric Model direct services include in-home services provided by family support specialists, family education sessions, and supportive services including counseling referrals.
1529.population: Target population includes the following: persons with poor mental health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, youth at risk of justice involvement, drug users in health services, grade school students, high school students, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, drug offenders in criminal justice. AMIkids expects to serve 400 students and family members through this program.
1529.outcome: 1. Outcome: # served who reduce anti-social behaviors, improve psychosocial functioning, improve family-functioning. Measure: all students will receive the Community Assessment Tool (CAT) or Prevention Assessment Tool (PAT) assessment, as well as the Family Assessment Device and Childhood Behavior Checklist. 2. Outcome: # of students who complete the program and do not reoffend for 12 months. Measure: AMIkids is required to submit data to FLDJJ to track offenses for 12 months after program completion as well as subsequent placement. 3. Outcome: # of students who successfully complete the program who are not adjudicated for any law offense within 12-months of program release. Measure: Youth w

2656.description: Rehabilitate neglected and deteriorating historic property in Springfield Historic District. The renovated building will (1) ensure historic preservation of key contributing structure, (2) remove source of blight and criminal activity in surrounding park and neighborhood, (3) provide publicly accessible community and archive space for historic neighborhood, and (4) provide office space for small business incubation, resulting in new economic activity and job creation.
2656.purpose: Rehabilitation of neglected and deteriorating historic property in Springfield Historic District. The renovated building will (1) ensure historic preservation of key contributing structure, (2) remove source of blight and criminal activity in surrounding park and neighborhood, (3) provide publicly accessible community and archive space for historic neighborhood, and (4) provide office space for small business incubation, resulting in new economic activity and job creation.
2656.activities: Planning, design, and construction on the property to rehabilitate property into productive use. Rehabilitation includes foundation work, roof work, siding, windows and doors, HVAC, electric, plumbing, ADA, fire, and general code compliance, interior renovations, etc.
2656.direct_services: Funding will be used only for capital expenses. As a result of the renovation, the building will be put into productive use. The rehabilitation will provide a community and archive space that is open to the public, maintained and operated by our nonprofit, and provides research opportunities, cultural enrichment, and historical education services to the community. The project will also remove a so
2656.population: The target population is the surrounding community of the Springfield Historic District, approximately 5,500 people according to the most recent census tract data (Tract 11 and 12). The project will also provide approximately 4-6 offices for small business incubation resulting in new economic activity and job creation.
2656.outcome: (1) Successful rehabilitation of the property into productive use, as measured by certificates of appropriateness and occupancy from the City of Jacksonville. (2) Removal of a source of blight and criminal activity in the community, as measured by blight and crime reports to the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office and Municipal Code Compliance. (3) Creation of publicly accessible community and archive space for research opportunities, cultural enrichment, and historical education services to the community, as measured by the number of individuals accessing these services and materials pre- and post-project. 1603.description: State of Florida recently authorized a new county judgeship to be created in Osceola County. A new courtroom and new judicial chamber are required to accommodate the new position. The funds would allow for the Court to address the increasing number of cases in Osceola County and the Ninth Judicial Circuit.
1603.purpose: Create new chamber space to accommodate a newly created judgeship's caseload.
1603.activities: Increased number of hearings for the growing number cases.
1603.direct_services: This request will expand the residents' of Osceola County access to justice.
1603.outcome: Increasing the court's capacity to hear cases. Tracking the number of cases heard.

1299.description: To ensure all Parkland Park Patrons experience firm, stable, and slip-resistant pathways that meet ADA regulations. This project will renovate hard-surface, nonmotorized trails and necessary accompaniments such as benches, waste receptacles, wayfinding and safety signage, warning tactile strips, and shading landscaping.
1299.purpose: The primary purpose will be to ensure all Parkland Park Patrons experience firm, stable, and slip-resistant pathways that meet ADA regulations.
1299.activities: The project will renovate hard-surface, non-motorized trails and provide necessary accompaniments such as benches, waste receptacles, wayfinding and safety signage, warning tactile strips, and shading landscaping.
1299.direct_services: The City's parks will continue to provide safe pathways.
1299.population: All park patrons will be served, drawing residents from the northwest region of Broward County, expected to exceed 20,000 annually.
1299.outcome: The City will ensure safe, secure, accessible pathways that will result in a reduction of the number of injuries to park patrons. The number of injury incidents will decrease.

1528.description: Transforms unused space in FAMU’s New Pharmacy Building into state-of-the-art research labs supporting STEM and health disciplines. Expands degree production, boosts research productivity, and enhances workforce readiness through hands-on training. Completes remaining floors of the Pharmacy Phase II Building to meet College of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences instructional and research needs while advancing FAMU’s strategic and statewide innovation goals.
1528.purpose: Funds will be used to complete construction of new research and instructional space for the Florida A&M University College of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences. The project will expand laboratory capacity to advance pharmacy education, biomedical research, and workforce development in Florida’s growing healthcare sector.
1528.activities: Funds will support construction, renovation, and equipment installation for modern laboratories and classrooms. These facilities will foster hands-on research, interdisciplinary instruction, and experiential learning that prepare students for licensure, clinical practice, and leadership in pharmaceutical and public health professions.
1528.direct_services: The project will expand training and clinical research opportunities for pharmacy and public health students, enabling them to provide community health outreach, medication counseling, and disease prevention services. It will also enhance partnerships with healthcare providers and expand access to health resources for underserved populations.
1528.population: The project serves FAMU students pursuing pharmacy, public health, and biomedical degrees; faculty conducting applied health research; and Florida communities benefiting from outreach and service programs. The expanded facility is expected to directly serve more than 800 students and faculty annually and indirectly benefit thousands through community health engagement.
1528.outcome: The project will boost degree production in high-demand health fields, increase research output, and strengthen Florida’s healthcare workforce. Success will be measured by higher graduation and licensure rates, growth in funded research and publications, and expanded partnerships and service hours in community health programs.

1376.description: The City of Parkland (City) will initiate a capital project to provide a secure, functional, healthy environment for the firefighters housed in Fire Station 109.
1376.purpose: The primary purpose will be to ensure the health and safety of Fire Rescue personnel. These workers require safe, secure, and healthy environments in which to work and rest. This project makes improvements to Fire Station 109 to ensure the firefighters stationed there are protected from weather-related harm and are provided living quarters that optimize their health and safety, directly benefiting the community they serve.
1376.activities: Reliable, responsive fire rescue service will be provided by this project.
1376.direct_services: Optimizing our fire rescue service directly impacts the lives and safety of our community
1376.population: Residents from the northwest region of Broward County and southern Palm Beach County will benefit from this project due to mutual aid agreements.
1376.outcome: Response time to calls for assistance will meet or be shorter than expected times for a majority of calls. Coral Springs Parkland Fire Rescue measures response time to calls with a goal of averaging 8 minutes or less.

1253.description: The Kellogg Research Building was built over a half century ago and originally housed the Department of Psychology. With the long-since completed Psychology Center, located next to the College of Medicine, the University proposes a major remodeling of the Kellogg Research Building for new occupancy. The current level of research funding achieved by the University is due, in large part, to the condition of the University's physical plant and the levels of service necessary to maintain it. If research funding is projected to increase, then the capacity and capability of the services necessary to support it must likewise be increased. Increases in operational performance, which can be achieved through improvements such as a major remodeling of an important academic building like the Kellogg Research Building make a building that is more efficient to operate.
1253.purpose: Specifically, the renovation would improve research facilities so that faculty and students can better engage cutting- edge technology in their research and will enhance learning environment where students' overall learning experience and engagement would improve. The building currently has zero windows for one which is detrimental to quality of life in the building.
1253.activities: University officials will use funds to complete projects on the lengthy list of necessary structural and mechanical updates required.
1253.direct_services: Renovating the Kellogg Research Building will greatly improve the quality of space for students. Specifically, the renovation would improve research facilities so that faculty and students can better engage cutting-edge technology in their research; enhanced learning environment where students' overall learning experience and engagement would improve.
1253.population: The target population is FSU's 45,000 member student body.
1253.outcome: Improved learning environment for students could be measured through student satisfaction surveys and increased retention rates for the College of Criminology. In addition, we estimate that a better research facility will improve research output measures including research expenditures in this discipline and grants awarded.

1254.description: The Tully remodel project at FSU aims to modernize and expand the facility to enhance academic excellence, research, and innovative teaching. The renovation will include new research labs, teaching spaces, and upgraded recreational and athletic training areas, benefiting students, faculty, and researchers. Funding will support the planning and design phase, integrating advanced technology, ensuring accessibility and safety, and optimizing space for a more effective learning environment.
1254.purpose: Funding would be used to plan and design the Tully remodel which will include new research labs and teaching spaces. The project will support academic excellence, research, and innovative teaching methods, benefiting both faculty and students. Currently Tully houses Sport Management, Sport and Exercise Sciences, Nutrition and Integrative Physiology, and Sport Psychology.
1254.activities: The university will utilize the funds to design and plan to modernize the existing facility, expand available space, integrate advanced technology, ensure accessibility and safety, and effectively manage the project budget for the comprehensive renovation and enhancement of the FSU facility.
1254.direct_services: The funding requested will directly facilitate the provision of improved educational and recreational services to the citizens, including modernized classrooms and research labs for enhanced learning experiences, expanded athletic training facilities for improved sports programs, upgraded recreational spaces for student clubs and activities.
1254.population: The target population served by this project encompasses the diverse student body and academic community of FSU, including current and future students, faculty, and researchers.
1254.outcome: The quality of education will be significantly improved through the integration of modernized facilities, advanced technology, and expanded resources, enabling enhanced teaching methodologies, comprehensive research opportunities, and practical training experiences for students. The quality of education will be measured through various comprehensive metrics, including an assessment of student performance, such as academic achievements, grades, and graduation rates, providing insights into the effectiveness of the educational programs and the overall learning outcomes.

1640.description: This project upgrades safety and security infrastructure at four community re-entry centers through the installation of modern high-resolution security cameras, encrypted two-way emergency communication radios, and electronic access- control systems utilizing staff proximity fobs. These equipment upgrades will enhance staff safety, reduce security risks, improve emergency response times, and strengthen supervision and accountability for individuals transitioning from incarceration back into the community.
1640.purpose: The goal of this project is to increase safety and security at four community-based re-entry centers by modernizing surveillance, communication, and controlled-access systems. The upgraded camera networks, encrypted radios, and electronic access controls will reduce security risks, improve emergency response coordination, and strengthen the safe reintegration process for individuals transitioning from incarceration back into the workforce and community.
1640.activities: This project provides upgraded surveillance, secure facility access management, and improved emergency communication between staff. These systems support safer daily operations, enable rapid response to incidents, and enhance supervision of residents in work-release programming.
1640.direct_services: Citizens benefit through increased facility safety, reduced incidents, and improved re-entry stability for individuals returning to the community. Enhanced supervision and communication help ensure safer reintegration, reduce risks to staff and residents, and support positive outcomes for returning citizens.
1640.population: Currently or formerly incarcerated persons, Economically disadvantaged persons, Drug offenders (in criminal justice), Persons with poor mental health, Persons with poor physical health, Homeless. 500-800 individuals annually across four re-entry centers.
1640.outcome: Protect the general public from harm. Measure: Reduction in safety incidents and security breaches, including fewer unauthorized access attempts, fewer disturbances, and enhanced ability to detect suspicious activity. Method: Review incident reports, response times, and security logs pre- and post-installation to measure improvements in safety and emergency response. Improve mental health Measure: Increased resident and staff perception of safety, which supports emotional stability and reduces anxiety-driven behavioral incidents. Method: Conduct resident and staff safety surveys; review behavioral notes and mental-health incident logs Reduce recidivism Measure: Increased compliance and succe

1674.description: The new Adult Day Care Center will serve patients experiencing Alzheimer's, dementia, and related diseases by ensuring a safe, caring, social environment that provides physical and cognitive stimulation for the participant and respite for the caregiver. An initial funding allocation for build-out and startup operations was approved in the 2025 legislative session. Easter Seals of South Florida, Inc. has been contracted to manage/operate the Hollywood Adult Day Care Program and now with the Center being fully operational in 2026, additional funds are needed.
1674.purpose: The Area Agency on Aging Broward County has identified a gap in dementia-related day care services in Southeastern Broward County. As such, the proposed Adult Day Care Center would serve patients experiencing Alzheimer's, dementia, Parkinson's, strokes, hearing/vision loss by ensuring a safe, caring, social environment that provides physical and cognitive stimulation for the participant and respite for the caregiver.
1674.activities: The Adult Day Care programming will be centered around a structured, safe, caring, social environment that provides physical and cognitive stimulation for the participant. Exercise is a daily activity, along with Brain Games and either music or art therapy. All potential participants are given a mini-mental test so that the staff is aware of their functioning level. This allows for the program to be more client-centered.
1674.direct_services: This 5 day a week Adult Day Care Program, licensed through AHCA, provides socialization, recreation, education, and lunch supervised by a nurse and staffed by trained individual. Adult Day Care also provides respite for the caregivers. This prevents or prolongs the need for costly placement.
1674.population: Individuals with Alzheimer's and dementia related disease, including elderly individuals and those experiencing poor mental/physical health. The Center is expected to serve 25-50 individuals at a given time.
1674.outcome: Clients are able to remain at home longer and are participating in brain stimulating activities and socialization in a structured, safe environment. In addition, caregivers are provided needed respite which allows them to continue their caregiving. Our goal is to encourage participants to participate in physical activities to assure that they don't become more frail. Each client is assessed using the 701B assessment upon intake and annually thereafter which tracks ADL's. By providing daily exercises, such as dancing, chair yoga, chair exercises and other activities, the client is able to maintain a level of flexibility. Each client is given an activity plan upon entry into the day care and p

SOW launched in 2023, brings play & comfort directly to pediatric oncology units at Joe DiMaggio Children’s Hospital, Nicklaus Children’s Hospital & Broward Health. This program includes in-hospital visits with games, crafts & entertainment. In 2025, we opened Sunrise Day Camp SFL, the region’s first dedicated camp for children with cancer & their siblings. We provide a safe, medically supervised camp where kids can build friendships, experience joy & create lifelong memories. In 2026, we’ll launch RISE for adults undergoing cancer treatment, modeled after SOW, providing care & companionship to patients. Sunrise SFL Programs create moments of laughter, friendship & hope for those navigating the chall

The goal is to reduce stress and isolation, build resilience, and enhance overall quality of life for families facing cancer. Sunrise South Florida programs provide healing of the heart and hope, giving children the chance to fully experi

Services include transportation, snacks, specialized staff training and on-site nurses to ensure camper safety. 2)Sunrise on Wheels (SOW) year-round program brings comfort, play and recreation into pediatric oncology units at Joe DiMaggio Children’s Hospital, Nicklaus Children’s Hosp

These include daily recreational camp activities, in-hospital engagement and support, medical supervision, safe transportation, and specialized programming designed to foster joy, connection and resilience. Families also benefit from respite and peace of mind, knowing

Outcomes will be measured locally through surveys of participants, parents and staff, direct observation, attendance and retention tracking, and an annual program review conducted by the Sunrise Association. The Exchange Club Family Center Parent Aide program helps caregivers learn the skills necessary to provide a safe, stable and nurturing environment where children can grow and thrive through a home visiting model removing barriers of transportation and childcare.
3438.purpose: Parent Aide will serve 250 families referred by DCF investigators, CBC prevention service case managers, public schools, and a wide variety of local social services agencies. Any family with a child under the age of 18 is eligible. Our goal is to help parents learn the skills necessary to create, a safe, healthy and nurturing home environment and to deter further intervention from DCF or law enforcement, keep families together and out of the foster care system. The program curriculum focuses on

The Plan includes goals developed by the parents to be completed during enrollments, and curriculum to be covered based on the INA. All services are provided in the home with 60-minute weekly visits for 3 months and bi- weekly for an additional 3-9 months. Pre and Pos

As needs arise, we connect families to HOPE Florida, job resources, therapy, substance misuse treatment, and other community supports.
