2669.description: Jacksonville Arts & Music School (JAMS) aims to expand its What A Leader (WAL) program to prepare middle and high school students with essential leadership training, cultivating confidence, critical thinking, communication, professionalism and relationship development. Through guided mentorship and hands-on learning experiences, students develop strong character, leadership, and a sense of civic responsibility. This expansion will develop a generation of motivated young leaders equipped to excel in college, advance in their careers, and contribute to the strength of Florida’s evolving workforce.
2669.purpose: The purpose of this program is to enhance youth development across five key areas: confidence, critical thinking, communication, professionalism, and relationship-building. Participants will gain the interpersonal and emotional intelligence necessary to succeed in school, post-secondary education, trade programs, and professional environments. The ultimate goal is to cultivate a pipeline of prepared, engaged young leaders who contribute positively to their communities and the broader workforce e
2669.activities: Activities and services are offered year-round and include educational workshops, youth-led projects, professional cohort engagement, and structured programming with weekly sessions. Participants engage with community partners and receive ongoing mentorship to support sustained growth. The program also features an annual What A Leader (W.A.L.) regional competition for middle and high school students, along with the W.A.L. Climb to Success Toolbox to reinforce curriculum knowledge and enhance ski
2669.direct_services: Structured mentorship, leadership training, life skills instruction, and experiential learning activities for students ages 12–24. Participants will engage in workshops, youth-led projects, and hands-on activities designed to strengthen confidence, communication, critical thinking, and professional skills. The program also includes an annual What A Leader regional competition to reinforce learning
2669.population: 500 - 1000 youth annually will be served by this project. Target population s from a diverse socioeconomic backgrounds and students facing hardships linked to poor mental health and at-risk indicators.
2669.outcome: This project will enhance students’ self-awareness, confidence, problem-solving, professional readiness, and social skills. Outcomes will be measured through online course modules, milestone badges, and staff- and community- administered surveys and assessments to track program performance and effectiveness.

3359.description: The R.M. Schulze Family Heart & Stroke Critical Care Center will expand access to state-of-the-art heart and stroke care in SWFL. Clinical trials, research, and technological advancements in these services will improve outcomes, reduce long-term care needs, reduce disability & save lives. The additional operating rooms will expand availability for emergency operations, cardiac & stroke interventions, and improve patient outcomes by reducing wait times to intervention.
3359.purpose: NCH tracks and reports to the state numerous patient data, including volumes, outcomes, and other uniform reported information.
3359.activities: The construction of a state-of-the-art comprehensive heart and stroke critical care center will dramatically elevate the standard of care and improve patient outcomes. This project consolidates numerous complimentary health care services into one location, and eliminates the remaining shared rooms (making all rooms single-occupancy).
3359.direct_services: The increased number of cardiac and stroke operating rooms will reduce time to intervention, saving precious cardiac muscle and reducing brain damage. NCH provides nearly $29mm in direct charity care and these services are included among that amount. Finally, a water well will be included in this project to serve the full campus during emergency events causing loss of municipal water.
3359.population: NCH had 1.4mm patient visits in 2024 and among that, are the residents of SWFL and innumerable visitors to our state, representing expected health care needs.
3359.outcome: NCH tracks patient volumes, outcomes, and other reported data to the state of Florida on the quality of care provided. The facility will increase ongoing research and development of new care technologies and clinical trials to regional residents.

2339.description: Warner University is completing critical upgrades and rehabilitation to its aging wastewater treatment plant and collection/treatment system that will directly mitigate concerns over the system's lifespan raised by engineers. The funding requested will allow for the completion of the project and will ensure continued wastewater services for the campus and over 2,500 individuals among a service area that includes Bok Academy South Middle School, South Lake Wales Church of God, a 50-unit mobile home park, Genesis Point (a retirement community) and multiple single-family homes near Crooked Lake (OFW). There is no public sewer available in the area meaning failure of this system poses a substantial risk to the population in the area and would likely require the introduction of new on-site systems at each residence, business, and on Warner's campus.
2339.purpose: Funds requested will directly provide for the completion of desperately needed sewer improvements that will benefit all Warner students/faculty and numerous private residents in Polk County that depend on Warner to provide sewer services. Warner has historically provided wastewater treatment at no cost to the surrounding area. This community consists of over 2,500 individuals among a service area that includes Bok Academy South middle school, South Lake Wales Church of God, a 50-unit mobile home
2339.activities: Funding will be utilized to complete construction of critical sewer improvements that will result in the continued provision of wastewater services provided to Warner students/faculty and surrounding Polk County residents.
2339.direct_services: Direct services to the citizens include the continued provision of wastewater services on Warner University's campus along with Bok Academy, South Lake Wales Church of God, Genesis Point retirement community, and nearby residential communities who depend on the system.
2339.population: The largest population to be served by this project would be the Warner University community consisting of students, faculty and staff. This could be expanded to include their visiting families, athletic teams, recruits and commuters. The second tier of the population served by this project would be the communities who tie into Warner's wastewater system including the students, faculty and staff of Bok Academy, (well-known Lake Wales Charter school), the members of the South Lake Wales Church of
2339.outcome: Engineers have recommended rehabilitation and upgrade of the existing wastewater treatment system resulting in transmission/treatment capacity of 300,000 gallons per day—sufficient to support more than 20 years of projected growth. This investment would remove a major barrier to growth for Warner University and its surrounding community. Success will be measured through continued campus development, compliance with DEP wastewater standards, and the increase in jobs generated as Warner resumes its growth trajectory. Further, with no public sewer available to surrounding residents and businesses, this project prevents the introduction of new OSTDS near a protected waterbody.

2650.description: The project consists of the relocation and expansion of the Career Connection Center located at FSCJ's Downtown Campus. Funding will be utilized for the design and construction of the relocation of the Career Connection Center from the URC Building to Building B. The new Center will be centrally located on the Downtown FSCJ campus and incorporate efficiencies with additional nearby student services. Career Development staff at the Center will offer students individual career and internship counseling, career assessments, occupational research assistance, matching major and career options, resume and cover letter writing assistance, and workshops. The new Center will also house the career resource library and the Career Center.
2650.purpose: Relocation of the Career Connection Center at the Downtown FSCJ Campus. Funding will be utilized for design and construction of the new Career Connection Center. The new location will expand student support services, like internship and job placements, advisory services, and the Career Closet Boutique.
2650.activities: Funding will allow for the relocation and expansion of the Career Connection Center located at FSCJ's Downtown Campus. Funding will be utilized for the planning, design, and construction to expand and renovate the Career Connection Center space, thereby expanding the services and increasing the number of students served.
2650.direct_services: Career Development staff located within the new Career Connection Center will provide the following services and resources to students: individual career and internship counseling, career assessments, career resource library, occupational research assistance, matching major and career options, resume and cover letter writing assistance, workshops, and a Career Closet Boutique.
2650.population: The target population is FSCJ students, graduates, and community members, including those who are jobless or economically disadvantaged.
2650.outcome: The relocation and expansion of the Career Connection Center at FSCJ will enhance student's economic self- sufficiency by providing assistance and resources to career opportunities. The Center will also improve economic activity by increasing the number of students, graduates, and community members that will be connected to job opportunities within the Jacksonville area, therefore adding to the local workforce. These benefits will be measured by the increase in students, graduates, and community members that utilize the Career Connection Center.

3183.description: Warrior Homes of Collier Co requests $100K grant to support our Zulu Project and these funds would put a roof over the head of Veterans and is only 4% of the overall cost of the finished project.
3183.purpose: The requested funds will allow Warrior Homes to complete critical roof construction at our Zulu Project, enabling the property to open as permanent supportive housing for 10–12 homeless or housing-insecure veterans. This investment directly supports our goal to eliminate veteran homelessness in Collier County by 2026 and ensures the long-term structural integrity and habitability of a residence that will serve veterans for decades to come.
3183.activities: The requested funds will be used to replace the roof of a newly acquired residential property, the Zulu Project, so that it can safely and sustainably house 10 to 12 homeless or housing insecure Veterans. Activities tied to this funding include pre-construction inspection, roof removal and installation, permit acquisition, contractor oversight, and post- construction readiness for occupancy.
3183.direct_services: The funding will allow WHC open Zulu Project by completing a roof replacement, thus creating urgent need to house up to 12 homeless or at-risk Veterans. Once open and occupied the residents will receive the stable housing along with access to support services through existing WHC partnerships. Each Veteran will contribute 30% of their income towards rent, reinforcing both affordability and account
3183.population: Our targeted audience is the homeless or at risk for homeless Veterans. These individuals may be elderly Veterans, with slight mental health issues, and economically disadvantaged Veterans. We expect to house 12 Veterans in the Zulu Project.
3183.outcome: The Zulu Project advances Warrior Homes’ mission to end veteran homelessness in Collier County by 2026. Once the roof is complete, Zulu will open with capacity for 10–12 homeless or housing-insecure veterans, increasing our total to 50 beds across five properties. We expect full occupancy within 30 days and 100% utilization in the first 6 months. Outcomes will be tracked via the Homeless Management Information System (HMIS), lease compliance, and reductions in local veteran homelessness as measured by the annual HUD-sponsored Point-in-Time count. Residents will pay 30% of income toward rent, and all will have access to support services through existing WHC partnerships.

3184.description: It is more than 80 years since the end of WWII, and there are few Holocaust survivors still alive to share their stories with the people of today. As sharing testimony is a valuable tool to connect individuals today with individuals who experience the Holocaust, the Holocaust Museum & Cohen Education Center endeavors to renovate its central classroom space to become an immersive theater in which to share interactive testimonies of survivors. We seek funding to expand the space, install raked-seating (theater style) and high definition screens and immersive audio controls to allow for the use of the "Dimensions in Testimony" technology. This technology allows for real-time conversations with Holocaust survivors so that their stories can continue to inspire positive change for generations to come.
3184.purpose: Since it has been 80 years since the end of World War II and the Holocaust, few survivors remain alive and even fewer are able to continue to tell their stories.. By providing an experience whereas our visitors can interactive with Holocaust survivors through this unique technology developed by the USC Shoah Foundation, we can continue to share their critical stories. Studies have shown that individuals that receive Holocaust education that includes testimony are more empathetic and more apt to
3184.activities: Funding will be used for the architectural plans, permitting, renovation, and installation of necessary improvements and technology.
3184.direct_services: The Museum's yearly 10,000 visitors will be able to have live conversations with Holocaust survivors for years to come.
3184.population: Our target audience are students and educators from southwest Florida, grades 5 through 11, plus local residents, seasonal residents, and tourists. This experience will add a meaningful layer of first-person testimony to our Holocaust education offerings which we provide to area schools to assist in compliance with the State of Florida Department of Education Holocaust Education Mandate.
3184.outcome: As a result of this investment more individuals will hear survivor testimony and gain a greater understanding of what the Holocaust was like on an individual basis. Studies show that hearing survivor testimony can lead to more empathetic, civic-minded individuals who are more liable to speak out on behalf of someone suffering an injustice.

3010.organization: Collier Health Services, Inc., d/b/a Healthcare
3010.description: Healthcare Network's mission is to provide quality primary healthcare to the community. Children learn better in school and adults are better able to work when they have access to the healthcare that they need. The southern portion of Collier County lacks a full-service community based healthcare provider. With this funding Healthcare Network will be able to establish a southern hub to meet the current and ever rising needs of the Southern Naples community.
3010.purpose: Healthcare Network's mission is to provide quality primary healthcare to the community. Children learn better in school and adults are better able to work when they have access to the healthcare that they need. The southern portion of Collier County lacks a full-service community based healthcare provider. With this funding Healthcare Network will be able to establish a southern hub to meet the current and ever rising needs of the Southern Naples community.
3010.activities: Healthcare Network will provide pharmacy, pediatric, adult, dental, and behavioral health services at the location.
3010.direct_services: High-quality primary care services will be provided. Services such as, but not limited to, dental cleanings, behavioral health visits, well-child check-ups, drive through pharmacy services, and many more.
3010.population: Healthcare Network serves all members of the community, but we focus on those most in need. More than 10,000 individuals will be served.
3010.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is increased overall community health and increased access to high quality primary health care services. This will be measured by using data from Healthcare Network's electronic health record, such data points include new patients and total patient visits.

3189.description: The Immokalee Foundation provides a proven career pathway for at-risk students to become SW Florida's workforce in high-demand careers focusing on Business Management & Entrepreneurship, Education & Human Services, Engineering & Construction Management and Health Care. Career exploration begins in middle school, and TIF guidance and support continues to employment. Results include 100% of TIF high school students earn an industry certification and complete a paid internship. 100% graduate high school and enter a college program, get a job in their career field or enter the military. And, 100% of postsecondary TIF students complete an advanced postsecondary certification or college degree, with 86% earning a bachelor’s degree or higher and 95% working in their field of study. Career Pathways is a model program that provides students with critically needed technical and work ethic skills t
3189.purpose: The Immokalee Foundation (TIF) provides a proven career pathway for students in Immokalee to become SW Florida's workforce in high-demand careers focusing on Engineering & Construction Management, Business Management & Entrepreneurship, Education & Human Services, and Health Care. Career exploration begins in middle school, and TIF guidance and support continue to employment, including internships, tutoring, mentors, academic advisors, career counseling, and mental wellness services.
3189.activities: Our services provide after-school and summer programming for students to explore in-demand career fields in Southwest Florida. Elements include career counseling, certification attainment, internships before high school graduation, career action plans, and exposure field trips. Summer camps, in partnership with postsecondary institutions, offer expert instruction and exposure field trips.
3189.direct_services: Funding will enable students in Immokalee to explore in-demand fields and postsecondary options beyond their rural setting. Services include one-on-one career advising, paid internships in their areas of interest, hands-on learning experiences, and transportation to career activities. These initiatives will equip students with the skills and knowledge needed to build a strong regional workforce.
3189.population: The Immokalee Foundation serves a projected 1,300 students annually and has served 18,081 students since 1991. The students we serve are economically disadvantaged, at-risk elementary students, middle and high school youth, and postsecondary students. 100% of these children and youth live in Immokalee, a REDI & RAO community.
3189.outcome: Growing Florida's economy by increasing the number of workforce-ready professionals. A study of the Tampa Bay region by the Helios Foundation shows $1 billion in economic gains if college enrollment increased by 10%. 93% of The Immokalee Foundation's postsecondary students complete their degrees with 87% earning a bachelor degree or higher, thus a state-wide model for building a skilled workforce and growing and expanding Florida's economy.

2990.description: Change the irrigation water source within the Estero Park from groundwater wells to reuse water by extending the reuse water main and installing an irrigation water storage tank.
2990.purpose: The purpose of this project is change the irrigation water source for the Estero Park from groundwater to reuse water from the Lee County Three Oaks Parkway waste water treatment facility.
2990.activities: Extend the reuse water main from Lee County's Estero Recreational Center to the park, connect to the irrigation system, and abandon the existing groundwater wells. The existing wells will be used as a back up irrigation source.
2990.direct_services: This project will not provide direct services to citizens.
2990.population: The general public and environment will benefit from this project via reduced groundwater usage.
2990.outcome: The expected benefit is the reduction is groundwater used for irrigation and the beneficial use of treated waste water for irrigation. This will improve protection of the aquifer. This will be measured by the volume of groundwater will not be pumped.

2991.description: Currently, irrigation along Estero Parkway is supplied via groundwater wells which results in additional strain on the water table. Lee County currently has an excess of reuse water from their Three Oaks Parkway Waste Water Treatment Facility. The project involves extending a reuse water line from the Facility along Estero Parkway, thereby conserving water resources while creating an outlet for treated waste water.
2991.purpose: The purpose of this project is change the irrigation water source along Estero Parkway from groundwater to reuse water from the Lee County Three Oaks Parkway waste water treatment facility.
2991.activities: Construction of a reuse water main along Estero Parkway, connect to the Estero Parkway irrigation system, and abandon the existing groundwater well. The well will be used as a back up irrigation source.
2991.direct_services: Transitioning from groundwater to reclaimed water use reduces utility costs and enhances long-term water supply sustainability. This shift also helps conserve the underlying aquifer, protecting it from over-extraction and ensuring resource availability for future needs of the community and region.
2991.population: All citizens and visitors to the Village of Estero will benefit via reduced groundwater usage.
2991.outcome: The expected benefit is the reduction is groundwater used for irrigation and the beneficial use of treated waste water for irrigation. This will be measured by the volume of groundwater that will not be pumped.

Continued state support will fund academic programming, infrastructure enhancements, renovations for the Polk Science Building, restoration of a Frank Lloyd Wright designed greenhouse, and the Construction Management Program Workshop Lab. These improvements ensure students are well-prepared to meet the evolving needs of Florida’s agricultural industry.
2340.purpose: This funding will be used for capital projects and programs within the college to accelerate Florida’s economic growth and workforce readiness. This funding will expand academic programs in high-demand fields – land and resource management for horticulture and citrus as well as construction management and education – ensuring graduates are prepared for critically needed jobs in Florida.
2340.activities: Activities include: campus visits and tours for FFA high school students to learn more about the new major and the Horticultural Sciences Learning Lab, increased focus on recruiting FL students interested in Agribusiness, additional scholarship funding, engaged learning opportunities with our State's agriculture leaders, and enhancing corporate partnerships throughout Florida for internships and job opportunities. In Polk Science, we will be able to fund needed structural improvements to preserv
2340.direct_services: The state of Florida will benefit from an investment in Agribusiness through FSC's Horticulture, Land, and Resource Management program, a multidisciplinary field of study that builds upon the College's legacy in the Citrus Sciences. This program will address the shortage and bolster the number of qualified graduates needed to fill leadership roles in Citrus, Farming, Ranching, Land, and Resource M
2340.population: The target population includes Florida's current and future high school students who are interested in pursuing careers and leadership roles in agribusiness, horticulture/citrus, land and resource management, finance, and marketing. We anticipate this major will grow, impacting at least 100 high school and college students annually. Additionally, the restoration of the historic Polk Science Building including the rare Wright-designed greenhouse is expected to attract increased campus visitors an
2340.outcome: The expected benefit and outcome of this project is (1) increased numbers of high school students interested in Florida Agribusiness/Citrus; (2) increased numbers of students enrolled in this major or related majors; (3) restoration of aged structures and buildings to become state-of-the-art learning labs well equipped for instruction and research; and (4) improved career outcomes for graduates, who are employed in Florida working in Agribusiness. The methodology we will use include surveys and admissions data for reporting.

1703.organization: Empowered of Central Florida DBA The Rock
1703.description: With $350,000 in state appropriations, the Rock Program will expand services to all middle schools and high schools in Marion & Citrus and Launch in Levy & Sumter counties. This funding will empower thousands of students with essential items, improving attendance, confidence and academic performance. The expanded reach and operational efficiency will ensure no child's success is hindered by lack of basic resources including food, clothing, school supplies, and hygiene products..
1703.purpose: Enhancing Access to Essential Resources Provide under served middle and high school students with essential items such as clothing, hygiene products, and school supplies to improve their self-esteem and readiness to succeed in school and life. Expanding Program Reach
1703.activities: 1. Distribution of Essential Items Provide students with clothing, shoes, hygiene products, school supplies, and other basic necessities to ensure they have the tools to succeed academically and socially. Organize regular distribution events at participating schools and community centers. 2. Outreach and Program Expansion Identify and partner with additional schools, focusing on underserved areas, to expand the reach of the Rock Program. 3.Resource Logistics and Management Improve the storage, i
1703.direct_services: Access to Essential Items Distribute clothing, shoes, and outerwear to students in need. Provide hygiene products, such as toothbrushes, toothpaste, soap, shampoo, and deodorant. Supply school essentials, including backpacks, notebooks, pens, and other learning materials. Improved Access for under severed Communities Bring mobile resource units to rural or economically challenged areas where stude

The program focuses on students in: Economically disadvantaged communities where poverty limits access to basic needs. Rural or under served areas with fewer community support services. Schools with high rates of free or reduced lunch participation, indicating financial hardship. Families experiencing tem

Key outcomes include: Enhanced Student Confidence and Self-Esteem Providing essential resources like clothing and hygiene products empowers students to feel confident and ready to participate in school activities. Improved Academic Performance Addressing basic needs helps students focus on their education, leading to improved attendance, engagement, and academic success. Reduced Financial Burden on Families Supplying essential items reduces the strain on families struggling to meet their children’s basic needs. Increased Acce

1355.description: This pilot program seeks to develop a much needed trained workforce pipeline for Florida's growing shellfish industry through curriculum and field-based internships. Recovering from multiple hurricanes and lack of support mechanisms like insurance, the commercial industry needs investment in labor to continue to rebuild and grow. This program would provide grants to engage commercial industry in a match program to cover partial labor & living costs while training people for employment in a future facing industry that grows Florida's economy.
1355.purpose: Trained workforce that will help grow Florida's shellfish aquaculture industry along with short-term investment in commercial farms to offset labor costs and promote further growth opportunities.
1355.activities: Interns will be recruited to participate in a virtual curriculum learning component and up to 1 year on the job training experience. Graduates of the program will obtain new skills preparing them for jobs within the shellfish industry from working on a boat to processing facility or a hatchery/nursery.
1355.direct_services: No direct services will be provided to citizens. Indirect services include water filtration and improved local water quality because of shellfish aquaculture farms and high protein local food production.
1355.population: The target population includes the broader public and High school, college students, veterans, and individuals looking for employment in aquaculture. Depending on funding 10-15 interns would be trained providing labor to 10-15 commercial operations.
1355.outcome: The benefit and outcome of this project is investment in a trained workforce for Florida's growing shellfish aquaculture industry which contributes to the State's economy through local food production, immense eco-system benefits like water filtration and job creation for rural coastal communities.

2341.description: Funding for the new Police Evidence Shed will allow the Lake Alfred Police Department to move the evidence out of the current location which is not secure and water damaged. Evidence is currently in a shed that is out of space and has water damage due to a leak near the evidence shed. Funding will allow us to build secure evidence building with the space we need.
2341.purpose: Funding for the Police Department Evidence Shed would provide the Lake Alfred Police Department a safe and secure location to store and view evidence.
2341.activities: A secure location to store and view evidence. The current Police Department Evidence Shed is out of space and it has water damage due to flooding.
2341.direct_services: The citizens of Lake Alfred will benefit from having a secure location to store Police Evidence that no longer has the threat of getting damaged by the leak.
2341.population: The members of the Lake Alfred Police Department and any resident who may file a police report, be a victim of a crime, or rely on the Lake Alfred Police Department to handle a case.
2341.outcome: The expected outcome is a bigger and secure Police Department Evidence Building.

2651.description: The Apprenticeship Initiative provides hands-on training through real event planning and game-day operations. Young adults and returning citizens gain workforce skills by helping produce and host sports and community events across North Florida. In partnership with teams, colleges, and organizations, the program creates a pipeline into jobs in sports management, events, and operations. It expands economic opportunity, strengthens Florida’s sports workforce, and supports second-chance talent.
2651.purpose: The Apprenticeship Initiative provides hands-on training through real event planning and game-day operations. Young adults and returning citizens gain workforce skills by helping produce and host sports and community events across North Florida. In partnership with teams, colleges, and organizations, the program creates a pipeline into jobs in sports management, events, and operations. It expands economic opportunity, strengthens Florida’s sports workforce, and supports second-chance talent.
2651.activities: Services include apprenticeship training modules, on-site learning at partner sports venues, mentorship for young adults and returning citizens, career-readiness support, and workshops delivered with professional teams, colleges, and partners. Funds will support hosting sports and community events where participants receive hands-on training in event planning, logistics, and game-day operations.
2651.direct_services: Participants receive hands-on training by helping produce sports and community events, gaining skills in planning, logistics, and operations. Services include mentorship, career-readiness coaching, on-site learning with partner venues, and support such as transportation, uniforms, and needed materials.
2651.population: All young adults, and returning citizens who seek a second chance. The project will serve 20-50 individuals.
2651.outcome: The program will place or prepare at least 10 participants for sports-related employment or internships.70% of participants will complete career-readiness training. Recidivism among participants will remain below 10% within 12 months post-program. At least 75% of justice-involved participants will maintain stable employment or continued training. -Payroll records for event-based roles. -Employment verification from partners. -Internal job-placement tracking. -Case management follow-up at 6 and 12 months.-Employment tracking and partner reporting. -Participant self-reporting cross-verified with re-entry partners.

2415.description: L.E.A.D. aims to create safer, healthier communities and schools through the implementation of substance prevention, anti-bullying education, and violence reduction initiatives. This is accomplished through effective partnerships between Florida law enforcement agencies, school districts and communities working together to educate youth on the harmful impacts of drug misuse, drug related crimes, bullying, and violence. L.E.A.D. instructors provide evidence-based, anti- drug/anti-violence curriculum delivered by law enforcement directly in the classroom to K-12 students.
2415.purpose: This funding request will support the training of up to 500 instructors, including law enforcement and educators, to deliver the evidence-based L.E.A.D. curriculum in the classroom to K-12 students in Florida. Once trained, each instructor will serve four classrooms, educating between 100-150 students per instructor. The goal of the curriculum is to teach K-12 students about substance use prevention, anti-bullying education, and violence reduction initiatives. L.E.A.D. offers evidence-based curr
2415.activities: Funding this request will support the recruitment and training of up to 500 law enforcement and educators to deliver the L.E.A.D. curriculum in the classroom. The scripted curriculum includes both lecture and activities for students to apply the skills they have learned through a lesson structure. The educational program can be individualized to meet the needs of the classroom. The funding will also support an outside evaluator to measure the success and outcomes of the drug, bullying, and viole
2415.direct_services: K-12 students receiving the L.E.A.D. curriculum will learn about the importance of drug, bullying, and violence prevention from trusted law enforcement in addition to the promotion of key resiliency skills. These include goal setting, decision making, effective communication, anger management, conflict resolution, and social competency. This is accomplished through lessons, an age-appropriate appr
2415.population: This funding request will support the training of up to 500 instructors, including law enforcement and educators, to deliver the evidence-based L.E.A.D. curriculum in the classroom to K-12 students in Florida. Once trained, each instructor will serve four classrooms, educating between 100-150 students per instructor. Therefore, this request will support the education of 75,000 to 125,000 students in Florida.
2415.outcome: Florida students that are served through this project will be equipped with the knowledge, skills, behaviors and attitudes necessary to combat drug abuse and drug related crimes and violence. The outcomes will be demonstrated and measured through evaluations which will include pre- and post-test surveys for all K-12 students participating.

2342.description: The City of Lake Alfred Public Library Expansion Project will expand the current library to add new program rooms of varying sizes, an Esports room, increase the number of computers publicly available, and expand the walkway around the Secret Garden behind the library. The project will allow the Lake Alfred Public Library to provide more services to the citizens as well as increase the number of library patrons we can serve at one time. The population in Lake Alfred has increased forty percent since the 2020 Census and the library has seen the growth firsthand. There is often a wait for patrons to use the computers, and the program rooms are not big enough to hold the number of patrons in attendance. Funding to expand the library will allow us to better serve the growing population of Lake Alfred. The City owns the property that the expansion will be built on. The Friends of the Library,
2342.purpose: The requested funds will allow the City of Lake Alfred to expand the Lake Alfred Public Library. The expansion will include the addition of an ESports room, program rooms, room for more computers, new parking, new landscaping, and a walkway through the existing Secret Garden behind the library.
2342.activities: The Lake Alfred Public Library will be able to provide service to more patrons simultaneously with funding for the expansion. At this time the library has a limited number of computers, and patrons often have to wait to access a computer. The expansion will include the addition of new computers so we can better serve our patrons. The library currently has two program rooms that are in high demand. Funding for the expansion will create new program rooms of varying sizes to better accommodate our
2342.direct_services: The City of Lake Alfred Public Library will be able to provide increased access to the public-access computers, increased availability of meeting space, and an increase in Library Programs. The population in Lake Alfred has grown exponentially in the last five years and we have seen that in the increase in attendance in Library Programs. Citizens in Lake Alfred and the surrounding area will benefi
2342.population: The target population served by this project is the residents of Lake Alfred. The 2025 population in Lake Alfred is about 9,000 residents. Each of the residents in the city will benefit from the expanded services provided by the library. The Lake Alfred Public Library is also located within the Lake Alfred CRA and several under-served neighborhoods. The increase in technology services will directly benefit those that might not have access without the library.
2342.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is an increase in services and programs provided by the Lake Alfred Public Library as well as an increase in patrons served by the library. We will be able to measure these outcomes through patron attendance at library programs and circulation numbers.

3040.description: The City of Clewiston is located within the jurisdictional area of the South Florida Water Management District (SFWMD). Secondary and local drainage are the responsibility of the City. The culvert beneath Berner Road has reached it's end of useful life and is in need of replacement. The 36" corrugated metal pipe is old and rusted, and sink holes nearby are due to the piping failure beneath the right of way. The Public Works Department is consistently upgrading the City's infrastructure. The project will replace the existing pipe with 136 linear feet of reinforced concrete pipe, replace the sand/cement endwalls with concrete, and restore the roadway. The project is a material upgrade that will significantly improve the roadway and ensure the culvert performs as designed to convey 2.5" of storm runoff per day.
3040.purpose: A resilient storm hardened facility with sufficient load bearing capacity suitable for a heavily traveled local roadway.
3040.activities: Maintenance of the streets and adequate storm water conveyance during weather events is an essential function of the City of Clewiston, to protect the health and safety of its citizens.
3040.direct_services: Berner Road is a heavily traveled two lane divided road between State Road 27 and Olympia Avenue, a four lane undivided collector road, used by local and regional vehicles.
3040.population: The population of Clewiston, and the Community of Harlem primarily utilize this heavily traveled roadway. The greater Hendry County regional population is approximately 40,000.
3040.outcome: The City of Clewiston is in a fiscally constrained county consistently among the highest unemployment rates in the state of Florida. The expected benefits and outcomes of this project are improved public health, safety and welfare. Reduced loss of life and property, higher prevailing wage rates and increased public sector revenues are anticipated positive outcomes over time and are measurable.

Replacing the four-inch diameter cast iron water main to an appropriately designed eight-inch diameter PVC water main needs to be constructed to meet current National Fire Protection Association guidelines. In 2024, the city procured construction drawings for the Pasadena water main improvement project, to install 1315 linear feet of 8" PVC water main from Deane Duff Street to N. San Pedro Street, along the Pasadena Ave right of way, "looping" the service main to two existing 6" mains at the project endpoints. The proposed water main is located within the Hwy 27 corridor and will provide adequate fire flow to serve the Hwy 27 commercial customers along the project limits. Phase 1 construction began in 2025, and the c
3041.purpose: The requested funds are necessary to ensure adequate potable water supply and meet fire flow requirements for existing properties and future development along portions of the Sugarland Highway corridor. This will allow for improved water service to the affected area and ensure fire protection meets NFPA standards. Water flow capacity will be increased from existing peak 240 gpm to as much as 1000 gpm. Infrastructure enhancements will facilitate commercial development and reduce insurance premium
3041.activities: To achieve adequate fire flow protection for this commercially and industrially zoned area, increasing the water flow capabilities and adding hydrants to the water distribution service is necessary.
3041.direct_services: Increasing the water flow capabilities and adding hydrants to the city water system will greatly reduce risks for loss of life and property during natural disasters. On September 28 2022, as Hurricane Ian winds reached 49 mph, an water flow was insufficient to suppress a structural fire and the building was lost. The fire also endangered several homes nearby necessitating evacuations in the midst
3041.population: The target population to be served by this project will directly include the property owners, businesses and nearby residents along the Sugarland Highway corridor. Indirectly, the entirety of the City of Clewiston will benefit from the enhanced economic development potential created by this project which will boost private investment and the creation of employment opportunities for the entire region. This is a much needed outcome in a financially disadvantaged county & municipality for an area d
3041.outcome: As a result of this project, greater fire protection, and increased public sector revenues resulting from enhanced property values associated with new private investment are anticipated positive outcomes over time and are measurable. Importantly, the requested funding will provide for the much needed improvements in a manner that will allow customer rates to remain affordable in a fiscally constrained community with among the highest unemployment rates and lowest wage rates in the state.

1319.description: The FSU Northeast Campus Academic Corridor will provide a hub for the arts to unite FSU's arts programs from the College of Fine Arts, College of Motion Picture Arts, and College of Music. This facility will provide greater educational value to the students at FSU, as well as K-12 students in the community who will likewise benefit from FSU's arts programs. Additionally, the community will see a benefit not only through an increase in quality arts and cultural events, but also through the improvement of the economy driven by the Corridor.
1319.purpose: The construction of the Northeast Campus Academic Corridor could bring numerous benefits to the students at Florida State and the citizens of the Tallahassee community. First, the building would provide state-of-the-art art instruction to students and provide a venue for a wide range of artistic performances and exhibitions including music, theater, dance, and visual arts.
1319.activities: These funds will facilitate planning and initial construction for the FSU Northeast Campus Academic Corridor that will unite three academic colleges: the College of Fine Arts, the College of Motion Picture Arts, and the College of Music. This will also include space for the FSU "Flying High" Circus, Opening Nights, and the Maggie Allese National Center for Choreography (MANCC).
1319.direct_services: The FSU Northeast Campus Academic Corridor would provide citizens with access to world-class cultural experiences and educational opportunities, which would help build a strong sense of community. This can be measured by attendance at events, feedback from the community, and the variety and quality of programming offered.
1319.population: Target population are university students, K12 students and the general community as a whole, here in Leon county.
1319.outcome: The Northeast Campus Academic Corridor would provide educational opportunities not only for FSU students but also to students in neighboring K12 systems, who often come to campus for performances. This can be measured by the number of students who participate in these programs, and the impact on their knowledge and appreciation of the arts.

1676.organization: Friends of Birch State Park, Inc.
1676.description: The project replaces approximately 3,250 linear feet of failing perimeter fencing along A1A and Sunrise Boulevard. It will remove aging, breachable chain-link fencing and replace it with an 8-foot fully welded aluminum fence that enhances public safety, reduces unauthorized access, protects sensitive wildlife habitat, and improves aesthetics along a key tourism gateway in Fort Lauderdale. The project also includes the replacement of park entrance/exit gates and installation of an app-based smart access control system to safely manage after-hours access for permitted youth groups using the Elks Youth Camp and park volunteers and staff.
1676.purpose: A modern perimeter fence will: • Enhance safety for nearly half a million annual visitors • Improve security for youth programs and after-hours camp rentals • Reduce environmental disturbance caused by unauthorized access • Protect rare habitats including coastal dune lake, mangrove forest, and maritime hammock • Improve the visual character of this iconic coastal state park and adjacent Fort Lauderdale beach
1676.activities: The funds will support removal of deteriorated fencing, clearing of vegetation along the park’s perimeter, installation of 3,250 feet of new 8-foot welded aluminum security fencing, replacement of entrance and exit gates, and implementation of an app-based access control system. These activities will enhance safety, prevent unauthorized access, protect sensitive habitat, and improve the overall visitor experience along the A1A and Sunrise Boulevard corridor.
1676.direct_services: The project will provide safer park access for visitors, improved security for youth groups and families, protection of sensitive wildlife areas, and a more attractive and welcoming A1A/Sunrise Boulevard corridor. Citizens will directly benefit from reduced unauthorized access, enhanced safety during recreation, and a cleaner, better-maintained environment for walking, biking, and enjoying the par
1676.outcome: The project is expected to improve visitor safety, reduce unauthorized access, and protect sensitive wildlife habitat along the A1A and Sunrise Boulevard perimeter of Hugh Taylor Birch State Park. The replacement of deteriorated fencing with secure, 8-foot welded aluminum fencing and upgraded gate systems will enhance the overall safety, environmental protection, and visitor experience. Outcomes will be measured through - Park Ranger and Law Enforcement Reports tracking reductions in trespassing, breaches, and homeless encampments; Environmental monitoring documenting decreases in habitat disturbance along the fence line; Visitor attendance and program participation data showing increased us

1817.organization: Dade County Dental Research Clinic d/b/a
1817.description: Comprehensive, no-cost dental care for homeless individuals — children through seniors. As South Florida’s only provider of restorative care at no charge, Community Smiles provides crowns, bridges, dentures, implants, orthodontics, oral-trauma care, and case management. Their goal is to prevent costly ER use, restore health, and enable employability — a smile is often an employer’s first impression. Triage alone doesn’t repair oral health; this program does. Oral health is tightly linked to primary health: untreated dental disease worsens diabetes control, raises cardiovascular risk, impairs nutrition, fuels chronic infection and pain, and undermines overall care outcomes. For those experiencing homelessness, this care is vital — poor dental health not only drives systemic illness but also creates barriers to shelter, food, employment, and dignity.
1817.purpose: Goals: cut preventable ER dental visits by diverting care to clinics; save taxpayers by offsetting Florida’s >$400M/year ED dental charges (avg $2,657/visit) with $90–$200 office care; achieve =10:1 ROI (every $1 invested saves ˜$10) per ADA/HPI Florida estimates; boost employability—treatment doubles odds of favorable work outcomes; improve primary health by reducing diabetes and CVD risks via periodontal care, integration, and case management; track outcomes and housing/job gains.
1817.activities: Intake/eligibility; exams/x-rays; prevention; restorative (fillings, crowns, bridges), endodontics; prosthodontics (dentures, implant restorations); limited orthodontics; oral surgery/trauma; anesthesia; lab work; dental case management (plans, navigation, reminders, follow-up with partner case managers); patient transport; outcomes tracking and reporting. Oral-health education: Skills-based chairside demos (brushing, flossing, interdental and denture/implant care); fluoride use and caries-risk
1817.direct_services: No-cost dental care for homeless Floridians: diagnostics (exams, x-rays), prevention (cleanings, fluoride, sealants), restorative (fillings, crowns, bridges, root canals), prosthodontics (partial/full dentures, implant restorations), limited orthodontics for function, oral surgery/trauma, anesthesia, lab fabrication/repairs, and dental case management for scheduling, navigation, and follow-up. Plu
1817.population: Target population: people experiencing homelessness across Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, and Monroe counties. We will serve 800–1,000 individuals annually, prioritizing adults and seniors while treating children as needed. Community Smiles — the region's safety-net dental provider — is South Florida's only clinic offering full restorative care at no cost: crowns, bridges, dentures, implants, and oral-trauma treatment. Coordinated with shelters and partner case managers to support jobs & stabi
1817.outcome: Expected benefits: fewer preventable ER dental visits and taxpayer savings; improved employability and chronic disease control; reduced pain/infection; restored dignity. Methodology: track patients, procedures, pain scores, ER diversions, cost avoided, and employability (IDs gained, interview readiness, job starts/retention at 30/90 days), plus housing outcomes; quarterly dashboards/annual reports using baseline/post surveys and hospital data. Compare clinic costs to ED benchmarks to show ROI.

2484.description: The City seeks funding to design and build a new Category 5 hurricane-rated Public Works garage and maintenance facility engineered to exceed Florida Building Code standards with wind resistance up to 200 mph, the hardened structure will protect vital equipment, ensure emergency operations continuity, and preserve City assets—strengthening community resilience against severe weather events. The structure is currently a pre fabricated metal structure with no wind/storm rating at all.
2484.purpose: A hurricane-resistant public works facility enhances community resilience by ensuring uninterrupted essential services. By safeguarding critical infrastructure, it also protects residents from environmental hazards such as flooding, debris, and water contamination.
2484.activities: By keeping the fleet safe and operational, it ensures timely road maintenance, and emergency response, directly improving transportation safety, reliability, and efficiency for the community..
2484.direct_services: Maintenance of infrastructure, manager utilities, support safe road and sidewalk travel for citizens.
2484.population: The target population are all the citizens and business owners in Belleair Bluffs and surrounding areas, tourists, visitors and anyone utilizing our infrastructure either on a daily basis on while traveling through. Our populations approximately 2500 but we serve a broad number of visitors coming inland from the beach communities.
2484.outcome: The benefit and outcome will be the utmost safety and security of our employees and residents of our city. The building is now a manufactured metal building which is not secure or safe. The need for a Cat 5 structure is to protect all our vehicular equipment that can be used for road clearing, tree maintenance and cutting, sidewalk repair and all other ancillary tools, and safety equipment necessary to protect the public and our employees.

1517.description: Hurricane Helene revealed critical vulnerabilities in St. Marks' aging wastewater infrastructure when six lift stations flooded and lost power. The City seeks funding for design and engineering to replace these stations with flood-resistant structures and emergency generators as part of a larger upgrade. St. Marks is preparing an SRF loan application and will leverage the APR funds with the SRF loan to secure resources for completing the full project. Overall, the improvements will address age and condition-related deficiencies, as well as prevent sanitary sewer overflows during future storm events, protecting public health, drinking water quality, and surface water quality (St. Marks and Wakulla Rivers). Investing in these measures can mitigate the costs associated with sewage cleanup and environmental restoration, leading to long-term economic savings.
1517.purpose: The goal is to plan and design for replacements for six aging lift stations with flood-resistant structures, upgraded electrical systems, and emergency generators. These improvements will prevent storm surge infiltration, ensure continuous operation during severe weather, and enhance wastewater system resilience as part of a larger WWTP upgrade project. St. Marks is preparing an SRF loan application and will leverage the APR funds with the SRF loan to secure resources for completing the full pro
1517.activities: Activities include designing and engineering six flood-resistant lift stations with upgraded electrical systems and emergency generators. Services provided will ensure continuous wastewater operations during severe weather, prevent storm surge infiltration, reduce sanitary sewer overflow risks, and improve system reliability for residents.
1517.direct_services: Funding will ensure uninterrupted wastewater service during severe weather by replacing six aging lift stations with flood-resistant designs, upgraded electrical systems, and emergency generators. These improvements protect public health, prevent sewer overflows, and maintain reliable sanitation for residents.
1517.population: The St. Marks Wastewater Treatment Plant provides service to the entire municipality (approximately 275 residents), and 40 commercial accounts.
1517.outcome: The project mitigates sanitary sewer overflows during severe weather, reducing exposure to harmful pathogens and preventing untreated wastewater from entering the St. Marks and Wakulla Rivers and surrounding wetlands. This protects public health, aquatic ecosystems, and water quality. Outcomes will be measured by tracking overflow incidents before and after completion, and monitoring water quality reports for contamination levels.

2343.organization: The Miami Project - University of Miami Miller
2343.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive and memory decline that worsens over time and it is believed to start 20 years before the onset of symptoms. An estimated 16.6% of the residents in MDC have the disease. Statewide, 12.5% of adults over the age of 65 are estimated to have AD. AD kills more people than breast cancer and prostate cancer combined. The Miami Project to Cure Paralysis and the University of Miami Center for Cognitive Neuroscience and Aging and the Departments of Psychiatry, Neurological Surgery, Neurology and Molecular Physiology and Cellular Biophysics have come together to use a multi-factorial and innovative approach for the study of Alzheimer's disease. The diverse backgrounds in this collaborative team leverages the knowledge from different fields of science that can be successfully applied to fulfill our goals of improving
2343.purpose: The purpose of this research is to improve the care of patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) by developing a multi- factorial approach for the study of AD with the goals of 1) Identifying therapeutic targets that are clinically relevant to AD pathogenesis, 2) Developing new therapies for those targets specific for the treatment of AD, and 3) Improving the way patients with AD are diagnosed and how their prognosis is monitored.
2343.activities: The research that will be conducted will be based on highly innovative approaches to gain a better understanding of how the inflammasome contributes to the early stages of AD. In addition, strong preliminary data and the proposed mechanistic and translational set of experiments will allow our multidisciplinary team of experts to advance inflammasome-based therapies to the clinic for the treatment of AD and other age-related neurodegenerative diseases.
2343.direct_services: Currently, no direct services will be provided to citizens. In the future, The Miami Project's goal is to translate this research into FDA approved clinical trials and develop new technology to identify AD sooner in individuals and advance new therapies to treat this disease.
2343.population: The target population served by this project are the more than 6 million Americans are living with Alzheimer's disease. Alzheimer’s disease kills more people than breast cancer and prostate cancer combined. In 2020, COVID-19 contributed to a 17% increase in Alzheimer's and dementia deaths.
2343.outcome: Each project will address specific research questions that are highly relevant to an important scientific problem using established technologies and experimental protocols. During the funding period, progress will be evaluated by written progress reports including qualitative and quantitative data related to the proposed specific aims. These findings will then be submitted to scientific journals for peer review and publication.

2344.organization: Powell Gene Therapy Center at the University
2344.description: The UF Health Center for Advanced Therapeutics has been established to provide and develop gene therapy treatments for rare genetic diseases. Nearly 2 million Floridians are affected by a rare genetic disease. In additional to providing specialized care to these individuals, we have developed an approach to conducting critical Investigational New Drug (IND) enabling studies to advance these therapies in clinical trials. These studies include preclinical efficacy, safety assessments, and manufacturing process optimization. Ultimately, this work will support training gene therapists, ensuring a skilled workforce capable of delivering these innovative treatments and expanding access to life-changing therapies for patients.
2344.purpose: To meet the intended purpose of these funds, we will conduct critical research and development activities to advance gene therapy treatments for rare genetic diseases including Duchenne Muscle Dystrophy, Friedreich's Ataxia, Barth syndrome. This includes: 1) Performing IND-enabling studies, such as preclinical efficacy and safety assessments, to ensure regulatory compliance and readiness for clinical trials. 2) Optimizing gene therapy manufacturing processes to enhance scalability and therapeuti
2344.activities: We will create comprehensive reports for all activities conducted under this project. These reports will document IND- enabling studies, preclinical efficacy and safety assessments, gene therapy manufacturing optimization, workforce training efforts, and translational research progress. The reports will ensure transparency, regulatory compliance, and data-driven decision-making while supporting future funding applications and clinical trial readiness.
2344.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide a transformative impact on public health by developing life-changing gene therapy treatments for rare genetic diseases. These therapies have the potential to cure or significantly improve the quality of life for patients who currently have limited or no treatment options. By advancing these innovative therapies through rigorous research, IND-enabling studies,
2344.population: The target population served by this project includes individuals (children and adults) affected by rare genetic diseases who currently have limited or no treatment options. By developing life-changing gene therapy treatments, this project will provide hope and potential cures for these patients. While the exact number of individuals served will depend on the specific diseases targeted, thousands of patients nationwide could benefit from these therapies as they progress through clinical trials a
2344.outcome: The success of this project will be measured through: 1) Completion of IND-enabling studies, including preclinical efficacy and safety assessments; 2) Regulatory milestones achieved, such as successful Investigational New Drug (IND) submissions to the FDA; 3) Advancement to clinical trials, indicating the readiness of gene therapies for patient testing; 4) Publication of research findings and reports, demonstrating scientific progress and transparency. These metrics will provide quantifiable evidence of the project's impact and effectiveness in advancing gene therapy treatments for rare diseases.

2940.description: The City of Fanning Springs is seeking funding to design and permit a new fire station that can house their added fire trucks, tankers, and train staff. The current fire station cannot house the six fire trucks and two tankers the City Fire Department has and provides no storage for additional supplies or space for training staff. A new fire station is needed to accommodate the growth of the fire department so that they can continue to provide fire risk management services to the surrounding community and counties of Gilchrist, Levy, and Dixie.
2940.purpose: The funds will initiate the first phase of the new fire station by funding the design and permitting.
2940.activities: The design and permitting of the new fire station will ensure that current services can be properly managed and stored safely for long-term use and provide space for growth of the fire department as their service area expands to include the growth of the community and surrounding areas.
2940.direct_services: The new fire station will allow for safe and efficient operation and storage of essential devices and equipment for fire department staff to serve the community.
2940.population: The target population is the entire City of Fanning Springs and the surrounding counties of Gilchrist, Levy, and Dixie. It is expected to serve >800 people.
2940.outcome: The expected benefit will be increased efficiency and proper storage of essential fire department equipment and staff. The outcome will be measured by response times of the fire department and decreased risk of damage from the environment on fire trucks and tankers while not in use.

2347.description: Moffitt Cancer Center is one of only three cancer centers in the United States with a research facility dedicated to precision cancer interception through healthy lifestyle behaviors, the Population Engagement and Research Laboratory (PEARL). Currently, PEARL supports 29 funded research studies. The PEARL research kitchen opened in 2023 and already cannot accommodate additional nutrition studies. We request $300,000 to expand the research kitchen and increase access to cold storage. Funding will not only allow us to conduct more nutrition research studies, but also to do so less expensively by buying and storing food in bulk.
2347.purpose: Funds will allow us to conduct more cutting-edge research to understand the molecular impact of diet and nutrition on cancer prevention and treatment outcomes.
2347.activities: The gold-standard nutrition study is one in which participants eat only study-provided meals. Expansion of the research kitchen will allow for meal preparation and storage space to allow us to conduct gold-standard science.
2347.direct_services: Participation in dietary cancer prevention and treatment studies are open to a wide variety of citizens in Moffitt's catchment area, including people both with and without a cancer diagnosis.
2347.population: The target population are individuals with cancer or at high risk of cancer. Expansion of the kitchen will allow us to increase the number of participants by approximately 1,000 per year, or double our current capacity.
2347.outcome: Research is expected to provide important new evidence about precision nutrition to help people prevent cancer as well as receive maximum benefit from cancer treatment.

2943.organization: Clay County Board of County Commissioners
2943.description: The funding would aid in the construction of a new 911 Communications/EOC Center to support Clay County and regional operations.
2943.purpose: The funding would aid in the construction of a new 911 Communications/EOC Center to support Clay County and regional operations.
2943.activities: Essential communication and dispatch across the Clay County for citizens. Improved Public Safety performance and response. The Co-Located Communications Center will provide synergy inside the centers with the correct communications layout. A radio tower will improve the range of communications.
2943.direct_services: Once constructed, operation of the new facility will direct dispatch of all calls rather than routing of calls from 911 to one of the four secondary Public Safety Answering Points resulting in the expedited dispatch of services. The facility will be a regional resource center for the State, Camp Blanding, NAS JAX, and other partners.
2943.population: The target is the general population of Clay County, Florida.
2943.outcome: Expected Benefit: 1. Decreased time between 911 call and dispatch of assistance by Fire Rescue or Law Enforcement. 2. Improved Coordination for Crisis Response Measurement Methodology: 1. Tracking and resolution of calls 2. Conduct post-incident reviews of large-scale emergencies or drills to assess inter-agency communication, coordination efficiency, and decision-making.

1511.description: Construct 26 new T-hangars and 5 new box hangars that will increase based aircraft, allow more aircraft to be based at the airport, which will result in a steady stream of revenue from aircraft storage fees, boost airport revenue by renting out the new hangars and increase fuel sales. With more aircraft, fuel consumption will rise, driving revenue and stimulate county wide economic activity.
1511.purpose: Construct 26 new T-hangars and 5 new box hangars that will increase based aircraft, allow more aircraft to be based at the airport, which will result in a steady stream of revenue from aircraft storage fees, boost airport revenue by renting out the new hangars and increase fuel sales. With more aircraft, fuel consumption will rise, driving revenue and stimulate county wide economic activity.
1511.activities: We will house 26 new tenants in T-hangars and 5 new tenants in Box Hangars. We currently have a waiting list larger than this.
1511.direct_services: Additional hangar space will be available for lease to both private citizens and commercial entities. By expanding rental opportunities, we are ensuring that individuals who previously lacked access to adequate facilities can now take advantage of the additional space. This supports our community’s aviation needs and strengthens commercial operations.
1511.population: Franklin County residents, 13,330 and surrounding counties.
1511.outcome: Having the additional hangers. We expect overall economic impact to the county by the additional rentals.

2944.organization: Aging True Senior Services of Clay County
2944.description: Green Cove Springs Senior Center is in need of a mobile emergency generator to provide electrical service in the event of an electrical outage. The senior center provides critical services to seniors including hot meals, health and wellness activities, and other services that support seniors in their community. The senior center provides emergency services including hot meals during an emergency - namely weather-related events - following hurricanes, storms, etc. Presently the senior center lacks a generator to provide electrical power during an outage caused by weather-related events, placing seniors at risk as well as the loss of large quantities of food products stored in freezers and refrigerators. The Green Cove Springs Senior Center is licensed and approved as a commercial kitchen and currently produces meals for the Clay County seniors on a daily basis.
2944.purpose: ENSURE the ability to produce meals to Clay county seniors in the event of a power outage, especially following weather-related events and ensure the preservation of stored cold food in kitchen freezers and refrigerators. A mobile generator will ensure continuity of services during both pre and post-storm events and during recovery.
2944.activities: Meal preparation and associated tasks for feeding individuals in emergency situations during a power outage. The mobile generator will ensure the facility has power to operate the kitchen and ensure the continuity of services.
2944.direct_services: The mobile generator will ensure that the senior center is able to continue to provide hot meals to seniors in the event of a power outage. The senior center will also be able to continue other critical services following a hurricane that may cause an extended power outage.
2944.population: Any senior and their family members residing in Clay county and designated by emergency management response center of Clay County.
2944.outcome: Hot food preparation and maintain cold food storage during emergencies when electricity is not available. The outcome will be calculated by the number of hot meals prepared and served.

2948.description: CCUA intends to continue implementation of modern Operations Technology (OT) with Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) Systems with robust cybersecurity. CCUA's implementation of these systems will improve operational efficiency in fulfilling our primary mission of delivering safe, reliable, and cost effective potable water, wastewater, and reclaimed water services. Recent cyber attacks aimed at public utilities require more robust systems to protect public health and safety.
2948.purpose: CCUA intends to use allocated funds for the continued implementation of modern OT, SCADA, and cybersecurity systems throughout CCUA's service area.
2948.activities: CCUA engaged professional engineering consultants, CDM Smith. They developed a master plan for our OT,SCADA, and cybersecurity systems. CCUA budgeted funds for the OT, SCADA, and cybersecurity systems within the CIP. CCUA intends to implement systems consistent with current OT and cybersecurity standards including NIST 800-82, NIST CSF, and ANSI/ISA-62443-3-3.
2948.direct_services: CCUA will use OT, SCADA, and cybersecurity systems to support our primary mission. We work to deliver safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of potable water, wastewater, and reclaimed water services. The funding for cybersecurity advances will allow CCUA to further protect public health and safety by acquiring more robust systems to fight against potential threats.
2948.population: CCUA serves the unincorporated area of Clay County. CCUA currently serves roughly 56,000 customer accounts or 154,560 people (2.76 people per account). CCUA expects the growth in Clay County's population will result in over system expansions and service to over 110,000 customer accounts (303,600 people) over a 20-year planning horizon.
2948.outcome: CCUA intends to increase operational efficiency through the use of OT and SCADA systems. The methodology to measure outcomes from this perspective will be the number of customer accounts per employee. We will also measure changes in after hour call-outs and related overtime costs. Cybersecurity systems will be measured by their prevention of intrusion of unwanted and potentially harmful access by internal and external threats.

2949.organization: Clay County Board of County Commissioners
2949.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2949.description: Capital improvements to the Clay County Fairgrounds may include: (1) Cattlemen's Kitchen & Event Center: Construct an 8,200 sf multi-purpose event center with commercial kitchen. (2) Livestock Pavilion: Construct a 26,000sf livestock barn. (3) Exhibit Halls: Replace roof and wall insulation, new HVAC system and fire alarm systems; lighting
2949.purpose: The proposed improvements are expected to increase the number of events and community participation at the Clay County Fairgrounds, expanding vendor participants therefore leading to rise in attendance and affecting an economic increase. Additionally, more events can be hosted with a higher guest capacity and ultimately a higher quality experience for the public and community.
2949.activities: All improvements requested will go toward creating a higher quality overall total experience for the citizens of Clay County when they visit events at the Clay County Fairgrounds which may include repair/replacement of facilities, or expanding event spaces to hold a higher capacity of guests. The community will feel the impact through increased access and facilities that support event experiences.
2949.direct_services: Direct services may include bigger event spaces, upgraded kitchen facilities as well as infrastructure improvements such as water and sewer which will reduce down time due to leaks and outages. Installed restrooms will accommodate higher number of visitors as would the expansion of meeting areas. HVAC/ lights/technology upgrades would increase visitor comfort and encourage longer stays.
2949.population: The target population served by this project will be the general population in Clay County (As an estimate for 2025, Clay County, Florida has a population of approximately 244,049 residents.)
2949.outcome: The Clay County Fairgrounds is a central location for many educational and agricultural learning opportunities. The improvements would allow for more events in a high quality space that visitors would enjoy and want to revisit. This can be measured by ticket and vendor sales as well as bed taxes. These improvements would increase the capacity for agricultural, equestrian and horticultural education, as well as a variety of other opportunities to support and promote such learning. Visitor counts would measure the level of benefit/outcome of its success as a result of is performance with these new improvements in place.

1608.description: The specific purpose is to expand our Youth Violence Reduction & Workforce Readiness Program. Our facility is the only dedicated teen center serving East Orange County teens, directly addressing the documented need stemming from constantly growing crime rates. Funds will expand capacity for at-risk, economically disadvantaged youth to access a comprehensive workforce readiness program (e.g., career exploration, mock interviews) to foster economic self- sufficiency.
1608.purpose: The goal is to increase access to structured, safe, and skill-building programs that prepare students for post- secondary education, employment, and life beyond high school graduation. Funding will support direct instruction, career exploration, financial literacy, and hands-on learning activities that strengthen critical life skills, improve academic engagement, and reduce youth involvement in high-risk behaviors.
1608.activities: The funds will be utilized for direct services to the youth offering career readiness training, financial literacy, entrepreneurship, life-skills instruction, academic enrichment, and supervised pro-social activities. Services include facilitator-led lessons, hands-on projects, career exploration sessions, and connection to resources that improve youth safety, skills, and future readiness.
1608.direct_services: Youth will receive direct in-person services, including career assessments, workforce readiness instruction, financial literacy training, mentoring, project-based learning, and structured activities that build communication, collaboration, critical thinking, and problem-solving. Programs provide safe, supervised environments and individualized support to help youth plan for long term success.
1608.population: The project serves jobless persons, economically disadvantaged youth, and at-risk middle and high school students ages 11–18. These students face limited access to structured enrichment, career training, and future-planning support. The program will provide direct services to approximately 100 youth annually, offering career readiness instruction, life- skills development, and safe, supervised activities designed to improve long-term education and workforce outcomes.
1608.outcome: The project will improve education, economic self-sufficiency, and reduce juvenile justice involvement. Outcomes include 75% of youth increasing knowledge and identifying a career path while building decision-making and life skills. Progress will be measured through pre/post assessments, Positive Youth Development Index scores, pathway tools, and attendance and engagement tracking.

1320.description: Hispanic Unity of Florida (HUF) aims to strengthen its workforce development strategy aimed at offering clients accessible and meaningful credentials of value, aligned to high-demand occupations, for individuals with diverse skill levels.
