3039.outcome: There are many benefits and outcomes associated with this project; some of the most important ones will be a better learning environment, updated technology and classrooms, better school safety measures, higher graduation rates and student achievement scores, and increased student confidence.

3251.description: Enhanced security for Jewish schools, businesses, and synagogues in Southwest Florida by partnering with Sheriff Offices, police departments and employing a regional security director. Using advanced technology and layered systems, the program prevents and detects antisemitic acts, terrorism, and active shooters, improves first responder awareness, speeds emergency response, and strengthens regional preparedness.
3251.purpose: Enhanced security for Jewish schools, businesses, and synagogues in Southwest Florida by partnering with Sheriff Offices, police departments and employing a regional security director. Using advanced technology and layered systems, the program prevents and detects antisemitic acts, terrorism, and active shooters, improves first responder awareness, speeds emergency response, and strengthens regional preparedness.
3251.activities: Off-duty law enforcement provide visible deterrence and rapid response at all Jewish facilities, while a regional security director coordinates security, training, and emergency preparedness. Security systems, AEDs, and trauma kits enhance first responder collaboration and ensure timely, effective responses to active shooters, terrorism, and other emergencies.
3251.direct_services: Members of the Jewish community will be free to exercise their rights to religious activities and send their children to Jewish schools in peace with knowledge and confidence they are protected by trained and certified off-duty law enforcement officers. Law enforcement will be immediately notified active shooters, acts of terrorism, etc., and will be able to better prepare for such emergencies.
3251.population: Elderly persons, preschool students, grade school students, high school students, university/college students
3251.outcome: Improve physical health by use of AEDs and access to CPR training programs. Improve mental health by providing security and giving Jewish citizens the ability to attend community events with decreased anxiety. Enrich cultural experience- Individuals served by facilities in the area will have safer access to cultural events provided by Jewish facilities in the region. Measured by attendance numbers at these events.

1386.description: The Longboat Key Police Department aims to enhance transparency and accountability in officer-citizen interactions by securing funding for body-worn cameras (BWC). The absence of body-worn cameras poses risks of disputes, evidence gaps, and community trust issues. Implementing BWC's would help mitigate these concerns and improve both officer safety and public trust.
1386.purpose: The project aims to enhance transparency and accountability in officer-citizen interactions by securing funding for body-worn cameras (BWC). The absence of body-worn cameras poses risks of disputes, evidence gaps, and community trust issues. Implementing BWC's would help mitigate these concerns and improve both officer safety and public trust.
1386.activities: By equipping our officers with body-worn cameras, we aim to provide accurate and transparent documentation of interactions with law enforcement and the community. This program aligns perfectly with our commitment to community oriented policing by addressing key areas such as evidence collection, officer training and public trust. This program will help LBKPD meet the highest standards of accountability and service to the community.
1386.direct_services: Body-worn cameras solve our key issues by providing clear recordings of police interactions. They boost transparency, build community trust and ensure proper evidence collection making policing more accountable and professional.
1386.population: All citizens, visitors and residents of the Town of Longboat Key.
1386.outcome: The implementation of the program will be methodical. First, we will begin with a pilot programs in which a select group of officers will test the cameras in daily patrol operations. This phase will enable us to refine our policies based on feedback as well as address technical issues before full deployment. Next we will proceed with a full department-wide implementation which will include training, data management and community outreach showcasing the benefits of BWC's.

1471.description: Nathan Benderson Park is strategically located central to the North Port-Sarasota-Bradenton Metro Area to provide continuity of the operation of essential school, local government services, and intergovernmental coordination during and after major storm events. The building will be built to Threshold Building standards that provide increased wind load capacity in a centrally located area for the regional and in an area outside of designated evacuation zones or mapped flood zones. The facility will serve as a regional evacuation, shelter, recovery facility, staging lineman and food services, mobile hospital setup, etc. In addition to the evacuation functions, the facility will be a county-owned property that offers a number of benefits to the surrounding counties including providing a new 100,000 square foot Indoor Multi-Sports Complex, including, but not be limited to basketball, pickleb
1471.purpose: To provide centrally located facility that can be utilized by the region as an emergency shelter that is adjacent to I-75 and primary evacuation routes. Nathan Benderson Park is an ideal location to invest in to serve as a regional evacuation, shelter, and recovery facility and centralized. It will also serve as a centralized community facility with activities and event spaces accessible to residents and visitors to the region.
1471.activities: The facility will become available during emergency response and post storm events.
1471.direct_services: The facility will be available for government agency emergency response and post storm recovery staging.
1471.population: All residents and visitors of the region. The North Port Sarasota-Bradenton MSA 2022 census tract population is 891,411 people.
1471.outcome: The 2025 Hurricane Season has highlighted the need that Sarasota County has identified for critical hardened infrastructure support space during storm preparation and recovery periods. Nathan Benderson Park is strategically located central to the North Port-Sarasota-Bradenton Metro Area to provide continuity of the operation of essential school, local government services, and intergovernmental coordination during and after major storm events.

1375.organization: Florida Alliance of Boys & Girls Clubs
1375.description: Florida’s Boys & Girls Clubs work with school-age children and youth to explore and develop workplace skills while using evidence-based workforce readiness programs and curricula that encompass a broad range of focus areas, including exploring student interests and passions; developing their employability skills; and applying knowledge to real- world work experiences through internships and apprenticeships.
1375.purpose: The goal is to build tomorrow’s leaders, innovators and problem-solvers by providing workforce readiness programming for youth ages 6 to 18.
1375.activities: Students ages 6 through 18 will have the opportunity to explore careers and prepare themselves for future career success with employability skills. Clubs will also connect teens to real-life work experiences, such as internships and apprenticeships.
1375.direct_services: Florida’s Boys & Girls Clubs will provide school-age children and youth opportunities to explore into their interests and passions; develop their employability skills; and apply their knowledge to real-world work experiences, among other opportunities, through the implementation of approved workforce readiness programming and curricula that encompasses a broad range of focus areas.
1375.population: More than 5,000 school-age (kindergarten through twelfth grade) children will receive high-quality afterschool programs.
1375.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is to engage youth within their communities, schools, organizations, peer groups, and families in a manner that is productive and constructive; recognizes, utilizes, and enhances young people’s strengths; and promotes positive outcomes for young people by providing opportunities, fostering positive relationships, and furnishing the support needed to build on their leadership strengths. The outcome will be measured through the youth's data collected by the local Boys & Girls Clubs, national data, and the analysis from the Clubs' third-party evaluator.

1610.organization: The School District of Osceola County
1610.description: The enhancements requested from the legislature will specifically fund the enhancement of educational and restroom structures along the boardwalk at the SDOC Environmental Center. This enhancement will also supplement the existing classroom space at the head of the boardwalk. The interactive new education spaces along the boardwalk will allow students and the public to learn more about the natural environment in Osceola County, aligned with the life, earth, and physical science standards taught in Florida’s public schools.
1610.purpose: The enhancements requested from the legislature will specifically fund the educational and restroom structures along the boardwalk at the SDOC EC. This enhancement will also supplement the existing classroom space at the head of the boardwalk. The interactive new education spaces along the boardwalk will allow students and the public to learn more about the natural environment in Osceola County, aligned with the life, earth, and physical science standards taught in Florida’s public schools.
1610.activities: An environmental center boardwalk in Osceola County would play a direct role in enhancing, preserving, and improving environmental and fish/wildlife quality by combining conservation science, education, and community engagement.
1610.direct_services: By providing hands on learning with STEM integration, Agricultural literacy, community workshops, cultural connections, career pathways, and public awareness campaigns.
1610.population: All elementary students in Osceola County as well as the general public on the weekends.
1610.outcome: This project can improve agriculture by promoting sustainable practices, offering farmer education, and connecting communities with conservation-based production methods. They act as hubs where science, outreach, and cultural heritage meet to strengthen both farming and environmental stewardship. This project will teach habitat restoration, water conservation and native plant programs. Species monitoring and aquatic ecosystem protections are also outcomes that can be realized.

1612.organization: The School District of Osceola County
1612.description: Create a Safety Security and Emergency Management stand-alone center as a central point of all safety, security and emergency management communications.
1612.purpose: We will convert an existing space within Safety, Security and Emergency Management (SSEM) for three eight-hour shifts that operate as the eyes and ears for the school district.
1612.activities: We currently operate approximately 8,000 security cameras across our school board owned buildings and property. We also operate an online security overlay on our student network, which flags critical situations that would require in school or after-hours wellness checks for students.
1612.direct_services: The number of facilities owned and operated by the school district, as well as the geography of Osceola County, and in the spirit of operating more efficiently with our law enforcement partners, requires a fully operational 24/7/365 security operations center. Our response times will be greatly improved.
1612.population: All students and staff of Osceola County (65,000 students).
1612.outcome: We will measure the results by the improvement in response times in an emergency.

1953.description: The funds provided through this appropriation will be used to purchase the needed heating, ventilating, air conditioning (HVAC) system for the planned Junior Achievement Center to be located in Lake Nona, FL. The Center will host the JA BizTown program, which teaches free enterprise and how an economy works by placing 5th and 6th graders into a simulated town. Annually, 20,000 to 30,000 5th and 6th graders from both Orange and Osceola County school districts intend to send their children to this center.
1953.purpose: The funds provided through this appropriation will be used to purchase the needed heating, ventilating, air conditioning (HVAC) system for the planned Junior Achievement Center to be located in Lake Nona, FL.
1953.activities: The BizTown program to be hosted at this center will introduce 5th/6th grade students to economics and free enterprise via hands-on experience where students apply learned concepts in a lifelike community. Students simulate running various businesses, earn paychecks, open and manage bank accounts, spend their income, and more. The students become full-fledged citizens and consumers by making purchases at other student-run businesses within JA Biz.
1953.direct_services: Junior Achievement intends to establish an Experiential Learning Center in Lake Nona and offer the JA BizTown program, a proven, transformative experiential learning program designed to engage and inspire the approximately 30,000 5th/6th grade students enrolled annually in Orange and Osceola County Public Schools. BizTown is a simulated city environment that teaches free enterprise, career awarene
1953.population: Grade school and high school students. Initially serving up to 30,000 5th/6th grade students per year.
1953.outcome: Students are provided the opportunity build knowledge in free enterprise, financial literacy, work readiness, and entrepreneurship. o 93% of participants indicate that they plan to contribute their skills and interest to make their local community a better place to live. o 85% of participants indicate they learned about at least one career option that they did not know about. o Participants noted the importance of real-life skills, such as customer service, business management, and the workings of economy and market within a community. o 90% of participants agreed that when they are old enough, voting is one way they can contribute to improving their local community. o 83% of participants in

2282.description: The Tampa YMCA is developing a previously vacant lot located at the SW corner of Eagleston Boulevard and Bruce B. Downs Boulevard in Wesley Chapel to build a 45,050 square foot YMCA facility. This new Family YMCA will serve as a hub of activity for more than 40,000 households who live within minutes of this major community resource. This full facility YMCA will include a lap pool and splash pad, athletic fields, gymnasium, wellness center, multipurpose/ community spaces, and playground. Families will have a new place to connect, and collectively, we will build a healthier community for generations to come. In times of hardship, such as after hurricanes, this community center can be used to house emergency response workers and help families recover.
2282.purpose: As our Pasco County community continues to grow, so do the demands for quality health and well-being programs. To help meet these needs, the Tampa YMCA will construct a new health and wellness family center in Wesley Chapel. The new YMCA in Wesley Chapel will include a 40,000 sq ft wellness facility as well as a 30,000 sq ft outdoor aquatic center. More than 40,000 families live within minutes of the proposed site for this new YMCA.
2282.activities: Welcoming, fully accessible environment for people of all abilities/ages in pursuit of healthier lifestyle in quality/effective programs; safe, positive space for youth/teens to build character/values in afterschool/teen/sports programs; Drowning Prevention Programs; evidence-based programs to address chronic disease; gathering spaces for community; and more opportunities for families to bond.
2282.direct_services: YMCA Survivorship & Wellness Program Powered by Moffitt, Parkinson's management programs, Diabetes Prevention Program, Swim Lessons and Drowning Prevention programming, Youth Sports, Teen Leadership programs, Summer Day Camp, Out-of-School Time programming, Senior Wellness programs, Food distribution, community volunteer initiatives, and so much more.
2282.population: Elderly persons, persons with poor physical health, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, physically disabled persons, preschool students, grade school students, high school students, university/college students, cancer survivors, chronically ill community members, families, infants, and the general public.
2282.outcome: The Wesley Chapel Family YMCA will improve physical and mental health. As a community leader in health and wellness, the Tampa YMCA understands the importance of physical activity and a balanced diet. We help improve the community's health and well-being by providing a variety of programs and activities that promote wellness, reduce risk of chronic disease, and help others manage and reclaim their health. We will offer group exercise classes, small-group training, and personal training to community members and offer evidence-based health programs for specific chronic diseases.

2283.description: The project will add one generator to an existing stormwater pump station located on the SE corner of the subdivision, which drains the neighborhood, along with piping to connect the SW and SE ponds. During storms and power outages, the pump-station is no longer operational, causing flooding in the neighborhood. The proposed generator will ensure that the station remains operational during power outages, thus increasing the resilience in the neighborhood and significantly reducing flooding impacts.
2283.purpose: The project will add a generator to an existing stormwater pump station located at the SE corner of Meadowood Estates, along with piping to connect the SW and SE ponds, for a subdivision of 124 homes. During storms and power outages, the pump station is not operational, causing flooding in the neighborhood. The proposed generator and piping will ensure the station remains operational during power outages, increasing the resilience in the neighborhood and significantly reducing flooding impacts.
2283.activities: The funds will be used to install a generator at an existing stormwater pump station, along with piping to connect the SW and SE ponds that will keep it operational during power outages, helping relieve flooding.
2283.direct_services: This project will provide relief to the Meadowood Estates neighborhood.
2283.population: The target population are the residents of Meadowood Estates neighborhood, roughly 400 individuals.
2283.outcome: The proposed generator will allow the stormwater pump station to operate during power outages, reducing the flooding in the Meadowood Estates neighborhood during rainfall events. Methodogy used to measure outcome, will be that the pump is running during power outages. The stormwater pipe between the Southwest and Southeast ponds will provide the connectivity of the ponds and will allow the SW pond to also benefit from the pumping.

2284.description: The funds will be used for the construction of a new Fixed Based Operator (FBO) Terminal Building to stimulate growth in the County. The future development of ZPH and the adjacent Industrial Park will attract new corporate and recreational aircraft operations. FBO operations are projected to create 47 jobs, supporting $3.9 million in personal income and $11 million in sales and creating additional tax revenues for Pasco County.
2284.purpose: The funds will be used for the design and construction of a new Fixed Based Operator (FBO) Terminal Building to stimulate growth in the County. The future development of ZPH and the adjacent Industrial Park will attract new corporate and recreational aircraft operations. FBO operations are projected to create 47 jobs, supporting $3.9 million in personal income and $11 million in sales and creating additional tax revenues for Pasco County.
2284.activities: The construction of a new FBO/terminal building increase capacity and allow the Zephyrhills Municipal Airport to provide a full-service facility offering pilot and passenger amenities (lobby, pilot planning rooms, rental car services, etc.). As corporate and other jet traffic increase, higher levels or FBO/terminal services are required.
2284.direct_services: The increased capacity and services available as a result of the new FBO/terminal building will be able to accommodate the projected operational growth mentioned above.
2284.population: The aviation community and citizens impacted by employment opportunities. Greater than 800 individuals are expected to be served.
2284.outcome: Future development of ZPH and the adjacent Industrial Park will attract new corporate and recreational aircraft operations, including increased jet traffic. FBO operations are projected to create 47 jobs, supporting $3.9 million in personal income and $11 million in sales and creating additional tax revenues for Pasco County. The outcome will be measured by monitoring specific aircraft takeoffs and landings and new airport tenants by the Zephyrhills Municipal Airport. Industrial corridor growth will be determined and monitored by the Planning Department. Coordination with the City of Zephyrhills and Pasco County to determine business and industrial growth.

2286.description: The project expands East Port, Port Tampa Bay’s newest port region. This new public facility will be located on East Bay, immediately across from the port’s main Hooker’s Point. The $37 million project would increase the existing facility, from 18 acres with a 400-foot wharf, to 27 acres with a 675-foot wharf capable of berthing 850-foot+ vessels. It creates 9 additional acres. It includes paving with concrete, site lighting and fire protection. It also lengthens the berth by 275 linear feet with a 43-foot-deep steel bulkhead wall, and it constructs a rail spur. The project will be designed for flexibility, efficiency, economies of scale and environmental integrity, serving mixed cargoes but with special accommodation for aggregates. The project is necessary to accommodate existing demand.
2286.purpose: The project will be designed for flexibility, efficiency, economies of scale and environmental integrity, serving mixed cargoes (containers, forest products (lumber, plywood), steel and aggregates. The project is necessary to accommodate existing demand.
2286.activities: Port operational services including Longshoreman and Trucking.
2286.direct_services: This project reduces supply chain issues which will result in lower costs for products for our citizens.
2286.population: The southwest region of Florida including the following counties - Hillsborough, Pinellas, Pasco, Polk, Hernando, Sarasota and Manatee.
2286.outcome: Lower costs for products to the benefit of the consumer (citizens and businesses). This is due to these products coming to the region by water transportation and not by Trucks coming in from out of state. Water transportation (ocean shipping transport) is the cheapest form of transportation. Cheaper transportation (freight) costs means cheaper total product costs for the ultimate buyer (citizen and business).

2288.description: This project provides rapid, accredited workforce training for veterans—including CDL, construction, logistics, and high- demand trades—combined with mental health support and case management to prevent veteran suicide. By addressing financial instability, joblessness, and lack of career pathways—known drivers of veteran suicide—the program transitions veterans and their families into stable, well-paying careers, reduces homelessness, and strengthens long-term financial independence.
2288.purpose: Florida has the nation’s second-largest veteran population, yet many leave service without the skills, support, or income needed to thrive. Financial stress is a major driver of veteran suicide. This project delivers rapid, accredited workforce training—including CDL and high-demand trade skills—combined with mental health support. Veterans and families move quickly into stable, well-paying careers, reducing suicide risk, strengthening families, and boosting Florida’s economic growth.
2288.activities: OWR partners with accredited training providers, Florida employers, and nonprofits to deliver industry-recognized certifications in CDL, construction, logistics, and skilled trades. Services include outreach, career evaluations, case management, mentoring, required gear, job-placement support, and mental health services to ensure completion and long-term success.
2288.direct_services: Veterans and military families receive a fully supported pathway into high-wage jobs in critical industries. Services include training tuition, case management, mental health support, credentialing, employment placement, and required gear and tools at no cost.
2288.population: Persons with poor mental health, Persons with poor physical health, Jobless persons, Economically disadvantaged persons, Homeless Disabled Veterans. Number to be served: 101-200
2288.outcome: This project will create immediate job opportunities, improve economic self-sufficiency, reduce suicide risk, decrease homelessness, and strengthen family stability. By equipping veterans with CDL, construction, logistics, and other in- demand trade skills, participants typically experience a 100–200% income increase, dramatically reducing financial stress—a major suicide risk factor. Success will be measured using credential completion data, employer wage verification, labor market comparisons, job-placement tracking, PHQ-9 and TSQ screenings, satisfaction surveys, and longitudinal follow-up on employment retention and financial stability.

2296.description: The Florida Aquarium Storm and Flood Protection project will enhance the resiliency of the Aquarium and its economic benefit to the Tampa Bay area. The project's goal is to provide total perimeter protection for the property at 701 Channelside Drive to protect animal habitats and critical life support systems from wind and flood damage.
2296.purpose: The Florida Aquarium Storm and Flood Protection project will enhance the resiliency of the Aquarium and its economic benefit to the Tampa Bay area. The project's goal is to provide total perimeter protection for the property at 701 Channelside Drive to protect animal habitats and critical life support systems from wind and flood damage.
2296.activities: Concrete barrier walls will be built around the perimeter of the Aquarium; entrances will be improved with door flood barriers.
2296.direct_services: This project will provide protection for TFA's infrastructure critical to animal safety and conservation, as well as facilities that provide education to the public.
2296.population: The Florida Aquarium's facility receives 950,000 visitors annually; the majority of visitors are Florida residents.
2296.outcome: The expected benefit is improved protection for future storm and flood events compared to the 2024 hurricanes Helene and Milton. This will be measured by the cost of damages to the facility during the next significant storm/flood event in Tampa as compared to the cost of damages in 2024.

2297.description: The Adoption Support Program in Hillsborough County responds to the vital need for ongoing assistance for adoptive families who have welcomed children from foster care. The adoption journey significantly influences family dynamics and often brings forth challenges that persist long after the legal finalization of adoption. Many children in these families have faced trauma, including neglect, abuse, and exposure to substance abuse, resulting in intricate emotional and behavioral needs. This program is dedicated to providing the necessary support to help families navigate these challenges and foster healthy, thriving environments for their children. The Adoption Support Program provides community-based, trauma-informed services designed specifically for the diverse needs of adoptive families. We connect adoptive families to peer support networks, specialized counseling, and essential commu
2297.purpose: The requested funding will provide adoption support services to adoptive families in Hillsborough County to help stabilize adoptive placement and prevent re-entry into the foster care system. There are currently more than 4,500 adoptive children in Hillsborough County under the age of 18. During the first 7 years of the program, more than 950 families accessed services and serving more than 1200 children. 250 children have accessed intensive services to preserve their adoptive placement.
2297.activities: The adoption Support Program will provide specialized adoption counseling, community support groups, case management, and crisis intervention directly to adoptive parents and children. The program serves approximately 150- 175 new families each year. These services are not currently available in the community or funded through other state funding.
2297.direct_services: Direct assistance and support services to adoptive parents and children to prevent the disruption and dissolution of adoptive placement that result in re-entry into the foster care system. Re-entry in to the foster care system creates a tax payer costs as well as further traumatizes a child potentially resulting in life long challenges including homelessness, domestic violence and other challenge
2297.population: Persons with poor mental health, Persons with poor physical health, Economically disadvantaged persons, At-risk youth, Developmentally disabled, Physically disabled, Preschool students, Grade school students, High school students
2297.outcome: Improve physical health: 1) Placements maintained 2) Less hospital days Improve mental health: 90% of adoptive parents will report improved scores on "The Parent Stress Index" which measures their ability to provide care to children with emotional problems Reduce recidivism: 1) 95% of families participating in services will maintain their adoptive placement with no re-entry into foster care 2) 60% of pre-adoptive placements will not disrupt prior to finalization. Current baseline is 50%

1789.description: Came to Believe Recovery (CTBR), a specialized addiction recovery provider, will conduct recovery retreats throughout Florida partnering with agencies such as local rehabilitation centers, missions, public offerings and the Salvation Army. CTBR will bring their unique and proven curriculum and process to Floridians in need through an innovative 3-day retreat model. The funds will allow Came To Believe, working with others, to reach hundreds of individuals in need of hope and a plan for an addiction-free future. A similar partnership model already exists between the Salvation Army and Came to Believe throughout California and is flourishing and is expected to reach 7,000 men and women in 2025 alone.
1789.purpose: Came to Believe Recovery (CTBR), a specialized addiction recovery provider, will conduct recovery retreats throughout Florida partnering with agencies such as local rehabilitation centers, missions, public offerings and the Salvation Army. CTBR will bring their unique and proven curriculum and process to more than 1,200 Floridians in need with this appropriations request through an innovative 3-day retreat model. We present the program in the same way it was being presented back when it was first introduced. Our founders have a direct connection to one of the first 40 members of AA that helped create the program, so, with firsthand knowledge we have developed and executed successfully on the program. Along with presenting the entire program we o
1789.direct_services: Came to Believe provides a three day in person retreat/workshop with experts brought in to run the program. There are large group and small group sessions over the three days. The 12 steps are taught in a way that allows attendees to continue the process for a lifetime. They are left with a 20-module course curriculum taught by substance abuse staff. Continued support and “practice” of the process
1789.population: The target population includes all people suffering from addiction of all types. Specifically, we are targeting homeless shelters, Salvation Army AC's, and missions. We provide programming to the general public and would like to serve those incarcerated. We would expect to serve between 1500-2000 Floridians.

Liver, stomach and lung ailments are rampant and occur at much higher rates than the general public. Addiction costs the State of Florida between 43-68 billion dollars a year. Addicts average $10-20,000 more in healthcare costs annually. It is estimated that addiction costs each resident of Florida $1,900 a year. Addiction has a profound effect on mental health. Rates of depression, suicide, and anxiety are higher in those suffering from substance abuse. These ailments affect family, work, school, relationships and health. All indi

1322.description: The funding requested will be used for the following: 1) outreach across the state to ensure all individuals with IDD know about and have access to the application process; 2) all prospective residents and their families have one-on-one support during the pre-application, application, and lease up process; 3) all prospective residents receive the training needed to live as independently as possible; 4) relationships in the community are established so programming is set prior to lease up.
1322.purpose: The funding requested will be used for the following: 1) outreach across the state to ensure all individuals with IDD know about and have access to the application process; 2) all prospective residents and their families have one-on-one support during the pre-application, application, and lease up process; 3) all prospective residents receive the training needed to live as independently as possible; 4) relationships in the community are established so programming is set prior to lease up.
1322.activities: Assisting people with disabilities with accessing information about the property and assisting them with the extensive application process; monthly programming including housing stability, financial literacy, community integration, social integration, workforce development; funds for furniture is needed for the area where activities will take place.
1322.direct_services: Prospective residents of Special Compass will be provided with guidance on application process, skill development for independent living, and support service options. Residents will be provided with myriad activities and programming to choose from to increase their independent living and workforce skills and develop healthy relationships both in and out of the Special Compass community.

1322.outcome: Enhancing economic self-sufficiency by: 1)Improved access to support services; 2) Financial literacy education; 3) Personal budget management; and 4) Job training. Skills will be measured using a comprehensive skills assessment tool that will be administered quarterly.

1359.description: PIAG Museum, founded in 2003, is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to bringing art and mindfulness to diverse and underserved communities who often lack access to cultural and emotional-wellbeing resources, especially children and seniors. This grant will empower us to expand our art workshops and mindfulness practices, giving participants opportunities to de-stress, express themselves, and build supportive connections. Our mission is to foster healthier, more resilient communities where individuals feel seen, supported, and inspired through the arts. The project promotes stress reduction, emotional expression, and social connection.
1359.purpose: This grant will empower us to deliver meaningful art and mindfulness programs directly within underserved and diverse communities. By providing creative tools and calming practices, we offer participants a chance to de-stress, express themselves, and build supportive connections with others. The result is a healthier, more resilient community where individuals feel seen, supported, and inspired.
1359.activities: Art workshops for all ages, with emphasis on kids and seniors to boost creativity, reduce isolation, and support well- being. Mindfulness sessions to improve wellbeing. Community art exhibitions in public spaces. Painting masterclasses for all levels participants to encourage artistic growth and connection.
1359.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with direct and free access to hands-on art workshops, mindfulness and stress- reduction sessions, free creative tools, and guided activities that support emotional well-being. Participants will benefit from opportunities for self-expression, stress relief, skill-building, and meaningful social connection. These direct services help reduce isolation, promote resil
1359.population: The target population includes children, youth, adults, and seniors in underserved and diverse communities across Florida. This project will offer accessible art workshops, mindfulness sessions, community events, and outdoor exhibitions to individuals of all ages. Based on projected participation across all program activities, the initiative is expected to directly serve approximately 4,780 individuals.
1359.outcome: The project will increase access to creative activities, reduce isolation, and support emotional well-being for seniors, children, and underserved communities. Participants will gain opportunities for self-expression, connection, and relaxation. Outcomes will be measured through attendance records, participant surveys, and pre- and post-session feedback to assess changes in engagement, stress levels, and overall satisfaction.

1940.organization: Florida Alliance of Boys & Girls Clubs
1940.description: Florida’s Boys & Girls Clubs are a vital partner in advancing the Department of Juvenile Justice’s prevention priorities. This initiative engages at-risk youth in structured, evidence-informed programs that reduce gang involvement, substance misuse, and justice system contact. With over 345 Club sites, including nine on military installations, these programs build resilience, decision-making, and resistance skills through mentoring and positive peer interaction. Program effectiveness will be tracked through youth attendance, service referrals, and DJJ’s Comprehensive Accountability Report (CAR), ensuring transparency and measurable impact across Florida.
1940.purpose: The Positive Youth Development program goals are to promote positive peer interaction, enhance resilience, improve problem-solving and decision-making, raise awareness and resistance skills, and build confidence and knowledge. Ultimately, the goal is to provide young individuals with the tools and support they need to lead healthy, productive lives and resist negative influences such as gangs and substance abuse.
1940.activities: Boys & Girls Clubs will deliver SMART (Skills Mastery and Resilience Training) suite of targeted programs twice weekly to students in kindergarten through twelfth grade. These sessions build essential life skills resilience, decision- making, and problem-solving, through age-appropriate lessons and interactive discussions. Mentoring fosters positive peer relationships, while guided conversations help youth develop awareness and resistance strategies by sharing experiences and learning from one a
1940.direct_services: Qualified staff will deliver prevention programs to Florida youth from low-income families during out of school time. Services include supervised enrichment activities in safe, supportive environments; mentoring and relationship-building with trusted adults; and structured opportunities that promote healthy decision-making, personal growth, and resilience. Programming is designed to reduce risky b
1940.population: Florida at-risk youth in grades kindergarten through twelfth-grade attending the state's Boys & Girls Clubs during out- of-school time; their families; and the surrounding communities. The program will provide at least 277,000 filled program slots.
1940.outcome: The requested funds will strengthen Florida’s Department of Juvenile Justice Prevention programs by supporting initiatives that reduce youth involvement in the justice system and promote long-term well-being. These investments will improve health and educational outcomes, reduce substance abuse and recidivism, and enhance public safety. They will also foster economic opportunity, job creation, and individual self-sufficiency for at-risk youth and their families. Program effectiveness will be measured through youth attendance, referral rates, and DJJ’s Comprehensive Accountability Report (CAR), ensuring transparency and impact across prevention efforts.

2490.description: Pinellas County is currently building a new EMS and fire station in North Redington Beach. This station being constructes serves all three Redington communities (Redington Beach, North Redington Beach and Redington Shores). The current plan is to house a medic unit at this station which will increase response times to medical calls. Unfortunately as a medic unit this will not improve response times to fire related calls. If we were to house a fire suppression unit this would increase response times for both fire and emergency medical calls. Funding for this is not able to be accomplished due to the size of the three budgets.
2490.purpose: Improved response times for fire related calls and emergency medical calls.
2490.activities: Having a fire suppression unit versus a smaller medic unit will allow for an increase in staffing which will in turn improve the quality of care and fire suppression having an extra person staffed.
2490.direct_services: Fire suppression services will be provided to the three Redington communities.
2490.population: Local residents and visitors to the three Redington communities. Approximately 7000.
2490.outcome: Current response times are not ideal and is the reason for this new station being built. We can further improve response times to any 911 emergency call by housing a fire suppression unit there which can respond to either medical or fire calls. This can easily be measured by documented response times through the dispatching system and 911 web based dispatch.

1755.organization: Florida Alliance of Boys & Girls Clubs
1755.description: Opioid Awareness and Prevention Program is a proactive, statewide effort to protect Florida’s youth and families from the devastating impact of substance misuse especially prescription opioid abuse. Through targeted education, community engagement, and prevention programming, the project equips young people and their caregivers with the knowledge, tools, and support systems needed to recognize risks, make informed choices, and build resilience. By expanding access to evidence-based and evidence-informed resources and deepening public understanding of the opioid crisis, this initiative strengthens Florida’s communities, reduces future harm, and lays the groundwork for a healthier, more informed generation.
1755.purpose: This project aims to empower Florida’s youth and families with the knowledge and tools to prevent substance misuse, focusing especially on the dangers of prescription opioid abuse. By deepening understanding of the opioid overdose crisis and expanding statewide prevention efforts, the initiative will build awareness, reduce risk, and strengthen community resilience against addiction.
1755.activities: Clubs will provide programming to raise awareness of substance abuse and misuse with an emphasis on opioids. Programming will be provided weekly to the selected youth with pre- and post-test data to measure student progress. In addition, each Boys & Girls Club will provide a menu of prevention strategies for staff, youth, and families on the Organization's website.
1755.direct_services: Boys & Girls Clubs across Florida will provide hands-on services to help youth and families understand the risks of opioid misuse and how to stay safe. Clubs will lead group sessions that teach kids what opioids are, why they’re dangerous, and how to make smart choices. Youth will learn how to handle stress, avoid peer pressure, and talk to trusted adults when they need help.
1755.population: The target population for the Opioid Awareness is 4,000 students in kindergarten through 12th grade attending the Boys & Girls Clubs. Community outreach and dissemination and marketing quarterly
1755.outcome: This initiative lays the foundation for a healthier, more informed generation of Floridians by intervening early and equipping youth with real-world knowledge to prevent substance misuse. Through weekly programming and community engagement, Florida Boys & Girls Clubs are helping to break the cycle of addiction and build safer, more resilient communities. The program increases awareness of opioid risks among youth and families, strengthens decision- making and refusal skills in high-risk situations, and reinforces protective factors like stress management, and peer resistance. The progress is measured through evaluation, program attendance and dissemination and marketing outreach through part

2492.description: Area 6 road improvements, as per the city's Capital Improvements Project, will consist of storm drain improvements, curb replacement, utility upgrades, and milling and resurfacing of the roadway. Area 6 includes 155th Ave., 154th Ave., 153rd Ave., 1st St., 2nd St., Harbor Dr., and Municipal Dr. This area is mixed use with residential and commercial use and heavily traveled daily. This project area will improve safety of our roadways that are cracking and sinking, improve mobility for those with physical impairments, and improve the commuter experience by having safer roadways available.
2492.purpose: Improving the roadway for residents and visitors. This project will improve the commute for residents, improve drainage, limit stormwater pooling, and beautification of the area.
2492.activities: Milling and resurfacing of the roadway and remove and replace the curbs all to improve quality of life around area 6.
2492.direct_services: Improving the roadway for residents and visitors. This project will improve the commute for residents, improve drainage, limit stormwater pooling, and beautification of the area.
2492.population: Residents and visitors of Madeira Beach.
2492.outcome: Improving residents quality of life, improved mobility for residents and tourists. Methodology would be decrease in commute times by repaving the road and reducing water pooling with the installation of new drainage systems.

2493.description: This funding would allow Madeira Beach Fire Department to buildout an addition that would be utilized as our Emergency Operations Center. Pre and post storm activities would be handled more efficiently and effectively and allow a smoother transition into implementing the Incident Command Structure (ICS). Establishing the ICS has proven to be more difficult due to different branches and sectors not being in the same room or building. During Hurricanes Helene and Milton the need for this EOC was realized. When not utilized during a state of emergency it will function as a multijurisdictional fire department training facility. Both aspects would benefit the Gulf Beaches Fire Group which consists of six fire departments.
2493.purpose: To allow Madeira Beach Fire Department (MBFD) to function at a high level during a state of emergency. MBFD is also the Emergency Manager for Redington Beach and North Redington Beach. All three communities would benefit greatly from a designated EOC with up to date equipment. This will also improve response times since we will be able to stay in the city during a State of Emergency instead of evacuating to an alternate EOC outside of the city.
2493.activities: Having the ability to stay in Madeira Beach during a State of Emergency will allow MBFD to respond to an emergency call rapidly from the new EOC located within the city at our current fire station.
2493.direct_services: Allow MBFD to serve the three communities safely, more effeciently and effectively. In the Emergency Operations Plan we agree to house board members and public works from Redington Beach and North Redington Beach. This has proven to be difficult during a State of Emergency due to a lack of space. Attempting to implement the Incident Command Structure is much more difficult when everyone is not in
2493.population: Residents of Madeira Beach, Redington Beach and North Redington Beach. Approximately 7500 residents + visitors..
2493.outcome: To successfully design and build an addition on to the existing MBFD Station 25 which will be the new Emergency Operations Center. This can be measured by faster response times to all three communities since we will be within Madeira Beach versus our alternate EOC located in a neighboring city off the barrier island. Implementing the Incident Command Structure (ICS) is key to a successful operation as shown in every large scale emergency, natural or man made.

1387.description: The requested funds will be used to purchase three drones and provide any officer training. 2494.outcome: Restores evacuation route for Safety Harbor and residents to access SR 60 Gulf to Bay and eliminates frequent flooding of road. City will be able to measure outcome by seeing elimination of road closures due to flooding of street.

1463.description: This project will improve the St. Armands Circle roadway system, including SR 789, John Ringling Blvd, Blvd of the Presidents, and Fillmore Drive. Planned improvements include upgrades to sidewalks, crosswalks, and curb ramps for drainage; incorporation of speed management feature; resurfacing of travel lanes.
