1778.description: The scope of work for this project includes the replacement and upgrades to the City-owned water and sewer systems along Alton Road, between Michigan Avenue and Chase Avenue, including the installation of a new sanitary sewer pump station in the vicinity of Alton Road and 27 Street. These improvements are critical to protect public health and preserve culturally and historically significant zones that contribute to the State's tourism and economic development.
1778.purpose: The work includes installation of approximately 7,650 linear feet of water main, up to 12-inch diameter, as well as new fire hydrants. in addition, the replacement of sewer line and laterals. These improvements are critical to protect public health and preserve culturally and historically significant zones that contribute to the State's tourism and economic development.
1778.population: City of Miami beach, ,Mid-beach community. Around 20,000 people, comprised of residents, tourists and work-force.
1778.outcome: This project will improve the critical infrastructure.

1779.description: This project will provide Miami Beach residents, tourists and visitors with reliable flood protection, upgraded water and sewer services, & enhanced public safety. Funding will allow the elevation of frequently flooded streets, install new drainage systems, improve water and sewer lines to reduce service interruptions enhance storm water treatment and ensure pump stations remain operational. The funds will support construction activities and public services that directly advance the State's goals of reducing flood risk, improving water quality, and strengthening neighborhood resilience.
1779.purpose: This project will adapt the flood-vulnerable West Avenue neighborhood, making it resilient to future sea level rise and storm related threats. Roads will be elevated by approximately 24 inches, protecting them from high and rising tides. Storm water infrastructure across the neighborhood will be upgraded with new drainage, backup power generators, and larger pipe connections.. A water quality treatment system will filter stormwater, reducing it of pollutants.
1779.activities: The funds will support construction activities and public services that directly advance the State's goals of reducing flood risk, improving water quality, and strengthening neighborhood resilience.
1779.direct_services: This project will provide Miami Beach residents, tourists and visitors with reliable flood protection, upgraded water and sewer services, & enhanced public safety. Funding will allow the elevation of frequently flooded streets, install new drainage systems, improve water and sewer lines to reduce service interruptions enhance stormwater treatment and ensure pump stations remain operational.
1779.population: Residents, tourists, and visitors to the Greater Miami Beach Community. (80,000 residents) and annual tourists.
1779.outcome: This project will significantly improve transportation conditions throughout the West Avenue corridor by ensuring that streets remain safe, accessible, and operational during rain events, king tides, and future sea level rise. Measuring flood reduction performance, water quality improvements, drinking and wastewater improvements, residents quality of life. All metrics will be documented, inspected, and operational reporting.

1752.description: The project involves enhancing stormwater management practices in the project area by implementing engineering strategies to mitigate flooding in the public right-of-way, thereby raising the area's stormwater drainage system, and improving the Level of Service protection for both water quantity and water quality. Project location: NE 15 Street between Biscayne Blvd and Bayshore Drive.
1752.purpose: The goal is to reduce flooding and protect properties on NE 15 Street, from Biscayne Blvd to Bayshore Drive by installing 950 linear feet of exfiltration trenches, 20 drainage inlets, and pollution control structures. The project involves raising the area's stormwater drainage infrastructure to provide a standard level of service to mitigate flooding and increase storage capacity and conveyance. Project location: NE 15 Street between Biscayne Blvd and Bayshore Drive.
1752.activities: Installation of 950 linear feet of exfiltration trenches, 20 drainage inlets, and pollution control structures
1752.population: General—thousands of individuals will be served.
1752.outcome: Mitigate flooding by improving the stormwater drainage infrastructure—measured by decrease in flooding incidents and reduction in the number of flood complaints received.

1862.description: The City has been investing millions of dollars in the hardening of its community with stormwater improvement projects to improve the safety and bolster resiliency efforts, all of which are immediately realized with objective proof of success. These stormwater projects will reduce flooding during sunny day and king tide events which will allow residents and tourists accessibility to their properties and businesses without worry about impacts of flood waters. In addition, with reduced flood waters, property owners and commercial establishments should be able to begin restoring their properties quicker.
1862.purpose: The purpose is to reduce sunny day and king tide flooding within the City to provide better access to all residences and businesses during all times of the day. The projects will also improve flooding during 25-yr, 24-hr storm events.
1862.activities: The construction of pipes, inlets, and filter inserts to reduce flooding. This includes the design, materials, construction, and construction management.
1862.direct_services: Safer, more aesthetic & reliable system. Reduces the risk of limited mobility as a result of storm events/damage. Improve resiliency for power service to the residential and tourist barrier island community. The City of Bradenton Beach has become the staging site for after-storm first responders & FPL crews following the past few hurricane seasons due to the underground work in the South end of th
1862.population: Elderly, residents, businesses, tourists, and students. The City is mostly tourist populated with approximately 80% of the residences being rentals. In fiscal year 2023, 3.8 million visitors generated 2.2 billion dollars in Manatee County.
1862.outcome: The City's residents will benefit from the reduced flooding by having access to their homes and businesses during the majority of days/times, as this should significantly reduce flooding associated with sunny day and king tides and will reduce flooding associated with the 25-yr, 24-hr storm events.

1634.description: FSW is seeking funding to expand our Hendry/Glades Center into a fully equipped hub for applied technologies and agriculture workforce training. With these capital funds, FSW will construct and equip a new facility that supports agrotechnology and agribusiness programs, transforming the center into a regional engine for job creation and skills development. The project will broaden access to education in one of Florida's most rural and underserved regions.
1634.purpose: The purpose of this request is to expand FSW's Hendry/Glades Center into a fully equipped hub for applied technologies and agriculture workforce training. With these capital funds, FSW will construct and equip a new facility that supports agrotechnology and agribusiness programs, transforming the center into a regional engine for job creation and skills development. The project will broaden access to education in one of Florida's most rural and underserved regions.
1634.activities: The Hendry/Glades Applied Technologies Expansion will provide rural SWFL with access to state-of-the-art labs and classrooms for Agrotechnology and Agribusiness. Services include, but are not limited to, dual enrollment, certificates, degree pathways, hands-on workforce training, and partnerships with employers to prepare students for high-demand, high-wage jobs in SWFL.
1634.direct_services: The funding will deliver hands-on workforce training in Agrotechnology and Agribusiness at FSW's Hendry/Glades Center through new labs and classrooms.
1634.population: The target population is college students, including dual enrollment, and adult learners in rural Hendry and Glades counties, who will gain access to applied technology and workforce programs.
1634.outcome: In addition to improving the overall quality of education, and economic activity, this funding will expand FSW's Hendry/Glades Center with agrotechnology labs, classrooms, and precision agriculture tools, which will provide hands- on training in soil science, plant science, GIS, and farm business practices, directly enhancing agricultural production, promoting innovation, and advancing education in SWFL's rural communities.

1768.description: This request provides funding to outfit FSW's applied technology laboratories across multiple campuses with modern equipment, technology, and furnishings. The investment will enhance programs in agrotechnology, non-invasive cardiovascular technology, robotics, engineering technology, and biomedical sciences through state-of-the--art, hands- on training spaces.
1768.purpose: The funds will outfit applied technology laboratories with advanced equipment and instructional technology, creating state-of-the-art spaces that support hands-on training in agrotechnology, non-invasive cardiovascular technology, robotics, engineering technology, and biomedical sciences. The goal is to prepare students for high-demand, high- wage careers in SWFL.
1768.activities: The funds will equip applied technology labs across campuses with robotics systems, biomedical devices, precision agriculture tools, automation trainers, GIS software, and modern furnishings. Services include hands-on workforce training, dual enrollment pathways, and applied learning experiences aligned with employer needs.
1768.direct_services: Citizens will gain direct access to modern applied technology labs and equipment at multiple FSW campuses, offering hands-on training in agrotechnology, robotics, engineering technology, biomedical sciences, and non-invasive cardiovascular technology. Services include certificates, degrees, and workforce programs that prepare students for high-wage, high-demand jobs in SWFL.
1768.population: The target population includes college students, dual enrolled students, recent high school graduates, and adult learners across Southwest Florida. The project will serve a substantial number of individuals by expanding access to applied technology and workforce programs.
1768.outcome: The project will expand applied technology programs across multiple campuses, improving the quality of education with state-of-the-art labs in agrotechnology, non-invasive cardiovascular technology, robotics, engineering technology, and biomedical sciences, while strengthening the regional workforce and boosting economic growth. Outcomes will be measured through growth in enrollment, graduation, and credential attainment in targeted programs, job placement rates, and employer satisfaction.

1635.description: The Yarger Hall building, constructed in 1997, has reached an age where significant updates are essential to meet contemporary educational and safety standards. This project addresses program space changes to existing science labs. The project accommodates changes in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math (STEM) programs. Anatomy and Physiology, Environmental Science and Oceanography, Chemistry, Biology, undergraduate research and classroom spaces will be reconfigured to accommodate additional student stations and improve efficiency of space. The building, which spans 17,982 gross square feet, requires comprehensive improvements to its mechanical, electrical, plumbing, security, and life safety systems to support modern academic needs and maintain a secure environment for students and staff.
1635.purpose: Funds for the renovation of Yarger Hall will be used to modernize and reconfigure science labs and classrooms to support STEM programs, such as Anatomy and Physiology, Environmental Science, Chemistry, and Biology. The goal is to expand lab capacity, improve space efficiency, integrate advanced teaching technology, and create a collaborative leering environment to enhance educational outcomes and workforce readiness.
1635.activities: Funds for Building G will modernize science labs and classrooms to support STEM programs like Biology, Chemistry, and Environmental Science. Activities include reconfiguring spaces to expand lab capacity, upgrading mechanical and safety systems, and integrating advanced teaching technology. The project will create collaborative, flexible learning environments to enhance educational outcomes and workforce readiness, addressing the growing demand for STEM trained professionals.
1635.direct_services: Building G will indirectly provide services to citizens by producing more STEM-trained professionals to meet workforce demands. Enhanced lab and classroom facilities will better prepare students for careers in fields like healthcare, environmental science, and technology, ultimately benefiting the community through a more skilled workforce.
1635.population: This project will serve STEM students by enhancing labs and classrooms to support programs in Biology, Chemistry, and Environmental Science. By preparing graduates for critical roles in healthcare, technology, and science fields, the project will address workforce needs in Southwest Florida. The improved facilities will benefit the community through the development of a highly skilled and job-ready workforce.
1635.outcome: The Building G renovation will enhance STEM education by modernizing labs, expanding capacity, and integrating advanced teaching technology, better preparing students for careers in science, healthcare, and technology. Success will be measured by increased enrollment, higher graduation rates, and workforce placement in STEM fields, ensuring the project meets the growing demand for skilled professionals in Southwest Florida.

1854.description: The Animal Care Center will be on two levels and is targeted to be around 4,500 sq ft. The lower level will be used for animal support functions such as holding, surgery, and food prep. Visitors will be able to enter the building with Wonder Gardens staff to watch and learn about animal diets and health care. The upper level will be used for staff offices, group work spaces, and an open flex room.
1854.purpose: A new Animal care center (ACC) will safeguard the health and wellness of our resident animals and position the Wonder Gardens for future accreditation by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA). The ACC will replace the previous animal kitchen & holding building that was destroyed by Hurricane Ian and is being removed from the property. The current diet kitchen is held in the Administration office building temporarily. The ACC will provide much needed on site safe holding during hurricanes.
1854.activities: Funds will help provide services needed for our animal care, as well as a hurricane shelter for our animal residents, which will indirectly service citizens.
1854.direct_services: Provides opportunity for additional education based off building's purpose, as well as more advanced research opportunities for interns and other interested parties. As well as behind the scenes learning opportunities for guests to see diet prep and medical facilities. It will also support our partnerships with other learning facilities and give them access to opportunities to bring students in.
1854.population: Our guests and our animal residents and staff will all be positively servied by this project. We have over 80,000 visitors annually, from locals to tourists from all over the world that are traveling to SWFL.
1854.outcome: For the animals: Onsite medical treatment when necessary, easier routine checkups, safety during severe weather, protection from physcial harm, better diet preparation for their overall well-being. This will be measured by increased vet exams and detailed record keeping through an online database. For people: overall planning intent is to cluster support functions in the north west section of the 3.45 acre property and create more space for visitor amenities and attractions near some of the existing core attractions. This will improve the overall visitor experience by having less fragmented exhibit sequences and will also help staff to be able to do their work without interfering with the vi

1941.description: Lake Cares, Inc. serves Lake County residents who are food insecure or at risk of or at risk of hunger. We address this important need through targeted programs in an effort to close the gap on hunger in Lake County. With a priority on good health, we promote wellness by providing fresh vegetables, fruit and dairy to clients receiving essential food through our food pantry. To assure those who need essential food the most are able to receive it, Lake Cares distributes food from our main location in Mount Dora as well as seven additional distribution sites where the population of residents who have most need resides. We distribute food in Paisley, Eustis, Sorrento, Tavares, Howey-in-the-Hills, Lisbon and East Mount Dora. Last year, we served 71,377 residents and 1.4 million pounds of food provided 20,000 families supplemental food including fresh fruit, vegetables, dairy and meat. This mo
1941.purpose: The specific purpose or goal of the requested funds to be used toward providing essential food to Lake County residents in need in an effort to lower the rate of food insecurity in Lake County, FL. Lake Cares has recently experienced an increase in requests for essential food with 2,000 individuals receiving food in just 36 hours through one recent distribution held in coordination with Second Harvest Food Bank. We request funds to help provide for these of individuals and families who request o
1941.activities: Needed food will be purchased with the requested funds and provided to Lake County residents from Lake Cares main pantry location as well as 7 distribution sites in Lake County. Clients schedule an appointment to pick up food from Lake Cares Food Pantry. During this appointment, Lake Cares will update the client record and conduct intake to evaluate their need. These funds are requested for the expressed purpose of providing for struggling families with essential food and lowering food insecurit
1941.direct_services: Through this request, Lake Cares will provide essential food to Lake County families and individuals who are food insecure and in need. The requested funds in the amount of $200,000 will assure a minimum of 53,000 individuals are provided a meal. The average meal at home cost in Florida is $3.78. Because we buy food at a more affordable cost, we are able to provide more food to families.
1941.population: The target population served by this project are low-income Lake Country residents who are food insecurity. Lake Cares provided for over 71,000 individuals in 2024 and expect an increase in 2026 due to population growth. The requested funds will provide for 53,000 individuals.
1941.outcome: The outcome of this project is lowered numbers of individuals and families struggling with food insecurity. This change can occur when they receive essential food through Lake Cares.

1709.description: The college is in the middle of the largest workforce program expansion in its history. To support tremendous growth in N. FL and the Ocala metro area, funds will support new and expanded programs in nursing, allied health, agricultural sciences, teacher education, hospitality, business and technology. Ocala was named #3 in the nation for high-earning job growth and #6 in the nation for overall job growth in 2025 by Lightcast.
1709.purpose: The college is in the middle of the largest workforce program expansion in its history. To support tremendous growth in N. FL and the Ocala metro area, funds will support new and expanded programs in nursing, allied health, agricultural sciences, teacher education, hospitality, business and technology. Ocala was named #3 in the nation for high-earning job growth and #6 in the nation for overall job growth in 2025 by Lightcast.
1709.activities: Creation or expansion of workforce ready degree programs, to include program planning, proposals, start-up expenses, employer partnerships, facilities expansion or renovation, faculty and staff hiring and marketing for awareness of these programs.
1709.direct_services: Programs and services will be designed for the working individual to upskill or reskill to meet the unprecedented need for high-skill, high-wage employees locally. The labor market participation rate is declining. It will take targeted strategies and employer aligned training programs to attract individuals to seek training.
1709.population: Citizens of Citrus, Levy and Marion county who need an affordable pathway to a high-skill, high-wage job. Employers in Citrus, Levy and Marion county who need local, job-ready and highly-qualified employees to grow their companies and to support the region and state's critical workforce needs. College of Central Florida's enrollment is projected to grow 15% through 2031, leading to an additional 759 students being served with this funding.
1709.outcome: 1. Improve agricultural production/education through creation of precision agriculture program designed to produce high-skill technicians. This program will be aligned to the statewide critical need to modernize and automate the industry, and to preserve natural resources such as water. Success measured by an enrollment increase of 20%. 2. Improve quality of education by developing/expanding critical workforce training programs to meet specific industry needs in health sciences, allied health, precision agriculture, teacher education, hospitality and tourism, information technology and business. Success measured by specific and measurable targets for number of graduates that are based on lab

1636.description: The Southwest Florida Public Service Academy, which houses the Criminal Justice and Fire Academies, provides state- certified training for future law enforcement officers, firefighters, and EMTs. However, its outdated, undersized bathroom and locker-room facilities, with elementary school–sized fixtures, are unsuitable for adult recruits and detract from a professional training environment. Funding is requested to modernize these facilities with adult-standard fixtures, add a secure vestibule to protect staff, and replace aging police training vehicles, ensuring a safe, functional, and professional setting for recruits and current first responders.
1636.purpose: The requested funds will modernize the Southwest Florida Public Service Academy’s facilities to create a professional, safe, and functional training environment for law enforcement, fire, and EMT recruits, as well as current first responders. Implementing sanitary updates in the outdated bathrooms and locker rooms will meet adult standards and support student needs. Replacing aging police training vehicles and adding a secured vestibule will improve safety, strengthen facility security for staff
1636.activities: The project will renovate the Southwest Florida Public Service Academy’s bathroom and locker-room facilities by replacing outdated, elementary school–sized fixtures with adult-sized showers, toilets, and lockers. It will also include construction of a secure vestibule to strengthen staff safety and the purchase of new police training vehicles to replace aging units. These safety & sanitary updates will be completed through facility improvements and equipment replacement to directly support the A
1636.direct_services: The project will strengthen the training of future law enforcement officers, firefighters, and EMTs, as well as sworn first responders who return for continued education at the Southwest Florida Public Service Academy. By improving the Academy’s facilities and equipment, the project directly supports the delivery of high-quality public safety training programs that prepare recruits and active pers
1636.population: The project serves law enforcement, fire, and emergency medical recruits enrolled in the Southwest Florida Public Service Academy’s training programs, as well as the instructors who lead them. The Academy supports more than 24 law enforcement agencies, providing both initial certification training and continuing education for approximately 4,300 active officers. It also serves over 28 fire departments, offering initial academy training for new recruits and advanced training for more than 3,200 c
1636.outcome: The project will improve the quality, safety, and professionalism of training for future law enforcement officers, firefighters, and EMTs as well as additional training of sworn first responders at the Southwest Florida Public Service Academy. Updated facilities will provide recruits with an environment that meets adult standards and better reflects real-world public safety settings, while new police training vehicles will enhance practical instruction and readiness. The vestibule will provide increased security for staff.

1760.description: The City has been investing millions of dollars in the hardening of its community with the conversion of overhead power lines to improve the aesthetics and safety, generate more tax revenues, enhance commercial growth, and bolster resiliency efforts, all of which are immediately realized with objective proof of success. The entire south end of the City has been hardened by removing all poles and utility lines, which expedited the recovery from storm events at a substantially faster rate. Property owners and commercial establishments were immediately able to begin restoring their properties since power was more quickly made available. FPL found they had less damage to its utility infrastructure since it was buried and protected from the hurricanes. The OH lines prevented redevelopment of pre- firm structures to larger FEMA-compliant structures.
1760.purpose: SR 789/Gulf Drive is the only means for visitors and residents to get on and off Anna Maria Island. Burying lines eliminates weather-related power outages and provides more reliable service and greater resiliency per SB 796 - 366.96, Fla. Stat. Safety and Community Health. Burying lines eliminates fire hazards, accidents, and safety risks from power outages due to downed lines. There have been two house fires and an electrocution from past hurricanes in the City from power lines. Following Hurri
1760.activities: The complete conversion of current aerial facilities to underground. This includes the design, materials, construction, wreck-out of aerial facilities, and construction management. This project will have a dual benefit of creating a corridor of usable property without the need for property acquisition by the FDOT for the Complete Streets Project. The City of Bradenton Beach will acquire all easements and land acquisitions needed for the underground conversion and the impending FDOT Cortez SR789
1760.direct_services: Safer, more aesthetic & reliable system. Reduces the risk of limited mobility as a result of storm events/damage. Improve resiliency for power service to the residential and tourist barrier island community. The City of Bradenton Beach has become the staging site for after-storm first responders & FPL crews following the past few hurricane seasons due to the underground work in the South end of th
1760.population: Elderly, residents, businesses, tourists, and students. The City is mostly tourist populated with approximately 80% of the residences being rentals. In fiscal year 2023, 3.8 million visitors generated 2.2 billion dollars in Manatee County.
1760.outcome: FDOT/FPL will save over $1,000,000 for the work Bradenton Beach will do in preparation for the Cortez Bridge and Complete Streets with relocation of overhead lines, equipment, landscaping obstruction removal and securing of public ROW/Easements. Immeasurable benefit of providing a safe evacuation route from the Barrier Island for Bradenton Beach and Longboat Key along SR 789. Benefit of keeping power on during storm events for a tourist-driven area will increase visitors and tourist dollars to the area. The benefit of removing the power lines from the rights-of-way in very limited real estate (barrier island developed in 1957) provides huge opportunities to install stormwater drainage, wider

2206.description: The Integrated Medication Assisted Treatment Response (iMATR) program is needed to reduce health disparities that have lifelong negative impacts within disadvantaged communities. iMATR will provide high-quality, comprehensive outpatient care for Broward County residents experiencing a substance use disorder. iMATR will provide comprehensive psychosocial/behavioral therapy and pharmacotherapy to address the underlying issues that contribute to the substance abuse and/or co-occurring conditions, as well as expand services for labor/delivery and babies born with neonatal abstinence syndrome. Therapeutic services will aim to support and assist individuals in the acquisition of skills and resources that reduce the risk of relapse, to aid in improving self-sufficiency, and achieving their treatment plan goals. iMATR’s pilot will be implemented under the leadership of Broward Health, who has se
2206.purpose: The Integrated Medication Assisted Treatment Response (iMATR) Enhancement program is needed to reduce health disparities that have lifelong negative impacts within disadvantaged communities. iMATR will focus on general social welfare for all Broward County residents and its goal is to provide high-quality, comprehensive wrap-around services and outpatient care for County residents experiencing a substance use disorder.
2206.activities: Screening and treatment; multidisciplinary diagnostic assessment; nursing assessments; medication for addiction; group therapy; individual and/or family therapy; drug testing; peer support; family support groups; aftercare/continuing care planning; treatment planning; intensive case management; 24-hr pharmacy coverage; enhanced social work; provider education; community prevention outreach
2206.direct_services: Screening and treatment; multidisciplinary diagnostic assessment; nursing assessments; medication for addiction; group therapy; individual and/or family therapy; drug testing; peer support; family support groups; aftercare/continuing care planning; treatment planning; intensive case management; 24-hr pharmacy coverage; enhanced social work; provider education; community prevention outreach
2206.population: Target population - Broward County residents Target number - 500
2206.outcome: By end of project, reach 500 persons belonging to the population of focus. By end of project, enroll 300 (60%) unduplicated participants, defined as per the population of focus To collect data and track the objectives, an Integrated Electronic Health Record (EHR) system will be utilized. EHR data includes demographics, information regarding hospitalizations, and other information typically found in the patient medical record.

2214.description: The goal of the NW 116th Way Drainage Project is to construct a new drainage system, as identified under the Stormwater Master Plan (SWMP). This will include new drainage structures, valley gutters, exfiltration trenches, and other improvements to improve water quality, mitigate flooding hazards, reduce nutrient loading in groundwater, and may ultimately help boost the local economy.
2214.purpose: The goal of the NW 116th Way Drainage Improvement Project is to construct a new drainage system, as identified under the Storm-Water Master Plan (SWMP), which will include new drainage structures, valley gutters, and exfiltration trenches and other improvements to improve water quality, mitigate flooding hazards, reduce nutrient loading in groundwater, and may ultimately help boost the local economy.
2214.activities: The project will result in construction of a new drainage system on NW 116th Way. The proposed improvement will include but is not limited to a) improved roadway conditions and safety: b) mitigated flooding hazards; c) other improvements.
2214.direct_services: The proposed project will serve as a direct investment in the local community and surrounding businesses. An efficient and well-maintained roadway drainage system reduces accidents, enhances emergency responses, and boost economic growth. Also, an improved drainage system will prevent flooding and will give excess water a place to safely transport runoff to an area better suited to hold it. Additi
2214.population: The proposed improvement will enhance the aging infrastructure, water quality, mitigate or eliminate flood hazards, and reduce nutrient loading in surrounding groundwater, and improve local traffic access for Medley residents, commuters and local businesses. The project is expected to serve 800 individuals and over 100 local area businesses.
2214.outcome: The proposed project will enhance the drainage system, which may include but not limited to a) new drains; b) drainage pipes: c) trenches; d) gutters and e) other improvements. The new drainage system will be constructed, which may help improve water flow, improve storm water management, overall water quality, reduce flooding hazards, and reduce property damages and other cost to local business, and local economy.

3102.description: Construction of seawall along sovereign submerged lands to secure United States Coast Guard offshore patrol cutters for the Department of Homeland Security pursuant to a manufacturing contract. Following the completion of the USCG contract, the seawall would help support attracting future contracting work.
3102.purpose: The project will increase and improve economic activity and create specific immediate job opportunities by expanding seawall for outfitting berthing spaces. Includes costs associated with constructing an industrial bulkhead and outfitting basin in Watson Bayou the construction and outfitting of United States Coast Guard offshore patrol cutters which will be constructed, launched, and sea-trialed from Watson Bayou.
3102.activities: Watson Bayou berthing spaces will enable governmental, industrial, and commercial water dependent activities. United States Coast Guard offshore patrol cutters will be docked at this bulkhead while being outfitted with propulsion, navigation, communication, HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, etc., prior to delivery to the United States Dept. of Homeland Security.
3102.direct_services: The University of West Florida Haas Center conducted a financial impact analysis of the work to be performed and concluded that 900 direct jobs and between 3,500-5,000 indirect jobs will be created for each of the up to 20 years of the performance of the manufacturing contract. The direct jobs exceed the average local wage scale in addition to various employment benefits.
3102.population: The citizens of Bay, Gulf, Washington, Jackson, Calhoun, and Walton Counties are the primary counties in which targeted direct-hire employees live. The US Coast Guard vessels will serve as coastal national security assets for the Department of Homeland Security.
3102.outcome: The measured outcome includes the construction of bulkhead and the longterm operation of an outfitting facility. The county’s lessee is willing to commit to keeping 900 direct hires which can be validated by reports filed with the State of Florida.

3103.description: Dredging at the Allanton Basin will support the outfitting berth and deepwater access for United States Coast Guard offshore patrol cutters for the Department of Homeland Security pursuant to a manufacturing contract. Along with the USCG contract, the basin would help support commercial future contracting work.
3103.purpose: The project will increase and improve economic activity, create specific immediate job opportunities, and improve transportation conditions by dredging Allanton Basin.
3103.activities: Allanton Basin dredging will enable governmental, industrial, and commercial water dependent activities. United States Coast Guard offshore patrol cutters and commercial vessels will transport from the Allanton Basin to/from St Andrew Bay, the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, and the Gulf of Mexico.
3103.direct_services: The University of West Florida Haas Center conducted a financial impact analysis of the work to be performed and concluded that 900 direct jobs and between 3,500-5,000 indirect jobs will be created for up to 20 years of the performance of the manufacturing contract. The direct jobs exceed the average local wage scale in addition to various employment benefits.
3103.population: The citizens of Bay, Gulf, Washington, Jackson, Calhoun, and Walton Counties are the primary counties in which targeted direct-hire employees live.
3103.outcome: The measured outcome includes the widening of the Allanton Basin in support of the movements of the 300'+ length United States Coast Guard Offshore Patrol Cutter, United States Army Corp. of Engineer hopper dredge vessels and commercial vessels. All improvements will be conducted in the state's sovereign submerged lands.

3104.organization: Panama City - Bay County Airport and
3104.description: The North Terminal Expansion Program is a result of the expanded growth of the Airport since opening in 2010. In 2009, the final year of the the old airport in Panama City (PFN) there were approximately 312,500 total passengers in 202 at ECP, here are expected to be more than 1.9 million total passengers. This growth has place a great demand on the existing Terminal and infrastructure, resulting in the need for additional space to address the demand. The TEP consists of an approximately 80,000 square foot expansion of the existing Terminal Building to the north of the existing baggage claim area by approximately 315 feet. The North TEP includes relocating the TSA SSCA to the current baggage claim area of the existing terminal building connecting to a new secure vertical circulation area. The existing baggage carousels will be replaced and 3 additional passenger boarding bridges installed
3104.purpose: The TEP includes approximately 80,000 sf of additional terminal and concourse space including but not limited to the Security Checkpoint, Baggage Claim, Holdrooms, passenger amenities and 3 additional gate positions with Passenger Boarding Bridges.
3104.activities: The TEP includes approximately 80,000 sf of additional terminal and concourse space including but not limited to an expanded Security Checkpoint, Baggage Claim, Holdrooms, passenger amenities and 3 additional gate positions with Passenger Boarding Bridges.
3104.direct_services: The Project will create three (3) new commercial air carrier gates leading to a 33% increase in travel options and availability for the Panhandle and travelers throughout the world.
3104.population: The District Airport serves almost 2 million passengers per year all across the panhandles, the state of Florida, the United States and the world. The Project would grow the target population by increasing offerings throughout the world.
3104.outcome: The expected out come will be providing additional and expanded air travel opportunities for residents and guests of our Region. In addition these increased recreational travel opportunities will lead to increases in additional economic development opportunities throughout the Panhandle and helps the region to recruit business relocation to the State of Florida.

3485.description: As the state prepares to adopt the CCBHC model and improve the delivery of behavioral health care in Florida, funding to ensure Child Guidance Center has the ability to continue implementation of the model and thus meet CCBHC certification requirements is imperative. Child Guidance Center is requesting funding to ensure our agency's readiness for CCBHC certification, and the benefits of that certification, once the State of Florida has completed the certification process and added CCBHCs as a provider and service type.
3485.purpose: The purpose of this project is to assist in Child Guidance Center's (CGC) preparation to become a CCBHC Agency when the certification avenue becomes available again. It was the Legislative intent in the 2025-26 budgets of both AHCA and DCF, via budget proviso, to implement the CCBHC model in Florida. CGC's intended use of this funding is to ready itself to take advantage of those benefits allotted to the State of Florida once the State has achieved the necessary parameters to become a CCBHC Stat
3485.activities: These funds will allow CGC to stabilize our current workforce and add specific additional positions, now unavailable due to a lack of funding, that would assist in fulfilling the necessary CCBHC accessibility requirements. These new positions would specifically address CGC's focus on Integrated Care and the expansion of our Immediate Access Clinic, both increasing the ability to serve the Jax/Duval population at an increased capacity via a faster and more effective rate of service.
3485.direct_services: The goal of the national CCBHC project is to increase accessibility to behavioral health services and streamline that access. CGC services under this request would address those goals by (1) stabilizing the CGC Outpatient staffing to allow for increased access to mental health services as well as address the importance of continuity of care, (2) stabilizing and encouraging new internal and consist
3485.population: use, and behavioral health care across the family systems we serve. Our services are available to the Duval County population as a whole. Our clients are funded through Medicaid, State of FL contracts, as well as private insurances as dictated by our staffing model. We serve over 4000 identified child and youth clients, along with their family members, averaging over 12,000 clients annually.
3485.outcome: The benefit of this project will be the preparation for CGC to be included in the benefits of the State of Florida's CCBHC status once that is achieved. The CGC outcome measures will be an increased workforce stability which is directly related to client success and satisfaction. Client response to treatment will be measured through client surveys as well as therapeutic treatment measures via treatment plans, and CFARS and DLA-20 (once implemented) ratings.

3105.organization: Bay County Board of County Commissioners
3105.description: Bay County Fire Rescue (BCFR) requests state assistance to purchase and equip a 100-foot aerial platform truck to strengthen emergency response for Bay County and nearby municipalities. The added platform is needed to meet rising service demands driven by rapid growth and vertical development. The unit will enhance firefighting and rescue capabilities for high-rise, residential, and industrial facilities, provide fleet redundancy for resilience during simultaneous incidents or maintenance, ensure compliance with NFPA 1901 safety standards, and serve as a regional disaster asset under the Statewide Emergency Response Plan.
3105.purpose: This project will strengthen BCFR’s emergency response capacity and ensure reliable service during complex or high- risk incidents. Funding will expand capabilities for elevated access, extended water reach, and specialized rescue operations, including multistory and industrial fires, high-angle rescues, hazmat, and post-disaster response. It enhances protection for dense residential areas, commercial corridors, coastal development, and critical facilities such as schools and hospitals, while su
3105.activities: The requested funds will allow BCFR to expand its ability to respond to complex and high-risk incidents that require elevated access, extended water reach, or specialized rescue operations. Activities supported by this project include enhancing response capacity for multistory and industrial fires, high-angle rescues, hazardous materials incidents, and post-disaster operations such as debris fires and structural collapse. response commitments.
3105.direct_services: This appropriation will enhance fire suppression, rescue, hazardous materials response, and disaster operations for Bay County residents and the millions of visitors who enter the county each year. It supports service demands in rapidly growing coastal and tourism corridors, high-rise lodging, and public venues, and increases capacity to prevent loss of life, reduce property damage, and maintain o
3105.population: The target population includes Bay County’s 185,000 residents, over 5 million annual visitors, and neighboring jurisdictions supported through mutual aid. The project benefits residential, commercial, and industrial areas, and critical facilities such as schools, hospitals, and multiple military installations. It expands elevated rescue and firefighting capacity to meet rapid growth in coastal and high-density zones, supports risk reduction and mitigation for vertical development, and strengthen
3105.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is improved public safety through faster and more reliable emergency response for complex and large-scale incidents. The project will increase firefighting and rescue capacity, reduce response times, and enhance protection for residential, commercial, and industrial areas. Outcomes will be measured using response-time data, NFIRS reports, ISO ratings, and after-action reviews to track performance improvements and overall impact on community safety and service reliability.

3106.description: The North Bay Water Tank and Pumping Station project involves the design, construction, and commissioning of a new 5 million gallon water storage tank and associated pumping station. This critical infrastructure will enhance water supply reliability and capacity to meet the growing demands of Bay County residents, businesses, and industries. The facility will be strategically located at the County's existing North Bay site off of Edwards Road.
3106.purpose: Construction of a new 5 million gallon water storage tank and pumping system will boost water pressure and ensure reliable fire flow within north Bay County.
3106.activities: Design and construction of the needed tank and pumping station.
3106.direct_services: Increased water pressure and adequate flow flow within Northern Bay County.
3106.population: The target population are the citizens of Bay County.
3106.outcome: The expected benefit of the project will be an increase in water pressure to ensure adequate fire flow. The outcome will be measured by utilizing the Bay County water model to determine line pressures throughout the system.

2955.organization: Clay County Board of County Commissioners
2955.description: The CR 218 Project is a holistic initiative primarily designed to enhance roadway safety, environmental sustainability, quality of life, and mobility for the Clay Hill/Middleburg community. The project includes expansion of County Road 218 from two lanes to four lanes in sections with specific work including drainage, sub base and curbing. These are part of a larger countywide effort to improve traffic flow, safety and infrastructure by adding travel lanes, sidewalks and bicycle lanes.
2955.purpose: To address safety concerns, the project will expand to four lanes. Additionally, the project will install a buffered, off- street concrete sidewalk, high-visibility crosswalks, improved lighting, and upgraded traffic signals—measures that target the reduction of fatalities and serious injuries among pedestrians and bicyclists while aligning crash rates with or below state benchmarks.
2955.activities: The County aims to convert the existing two-lane rural roadway into a safe, efficient, and resilient four-lane urban corridor. Key elements of the project include intersection improvements, sidewalk construction, signalization and lighting.
2955.direct_services: These improvements will create a multi-modal corridor that supports walking, cycling, and transit use while fostering economic growth and community resilience. The project’s forward-thinking design ensures that public safety will be enhanced through clearly delineated bike lanes, sidewalks, and crosswalks, delivering lasting value for residents and stakeholders.
2955.population: The target population served by this project is the Clay Hill/Middleburg in Clay County community. The number of individuals expected to be directly served is approximately 72,000, but the project will have a county-wide benefit, as well, for drivers in Clay (240,000+).
2955.outcome: Improved public safety and efficiency in traffic flow for motor vehicles, pedestrians and bicyclists. The construction is designed to yield long-lasting infrastructure minimizing repairs and related costs associated with maintenance.

1611.description: Pathways to Independence is a comprehensive continuum of care program that transforms foster youth from underserved, at-risk youth to healing, thriving, and self-sufficient. Studies show that 40% of Miami-Dade foster youth will experience homelessness by 19, 25% will be in the justice system by 20, and only 3% will earn a college degree. So, in partnership with the State of FL, GHH will provide holistic, wraparound programs and services, including housing, educational support and advocacy, vocational training and career readiness, essential life skills, and enrichment programming to 300 foster youth. We will remove barriers and create opportunities so these students can excel in school, maintain housing, learn life skills, earn employment, avoid incarceration, become independent, and build healthy relationships.
1611.purpose: The purpose of the appropriation funds is to provide direct wrap-around services, programming, and resources to over 300 foster youth who will not be reunified with their families, enabling them to overcome learning loss, master life skills, maintain housing, and become employment-ready. Thereby, creating pathways to high school and college graduation, employment, and independence through GHH's After-School, Career Readiness, Vocational Training, and Camp Independence programs.
1611.activities: GHH will meet the purpose of these funds through our evidence-based programming, created in-house and refined over 10 years, as well as our community partners who are experts in youth development, life skills, career readiness, and vocational training. Collectively, our program curriculum will create measurable, life-changing pathways to independence for foster youth in Miami.
1611.direct_services: GHH's direct services include hands-on, instantly accessible solutions, such as HVAC vocational training and certification, personalized tutoring by certified teachers, job placements at GHH and local small businesses, life skills training and career readiness workshops provided by GHH staff and community partners, as well as one-on-one mentoring to ensure accountability and results.
1611.population: The target population is foster youth ages 10-14, youth transitioning out of foster care ages 15-17, and former foster youth ages 18-25. Most of our foster parents come from low-income to lower-middle-class socioeconomic statuses, and 85% of our students have mental health disorders, including autism. This includes persons with poor mental health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, homeless, grade school students, high school students, university/college students
1611.outcome: The expected program outcome is more self-sufficient foster youth aging out of care and diverted from the criminal/ juvenile justice systems, resulting from improved educational support, housing access, job opportunities, life skills, and physical and mental health services. We measure these outcomes through frequent data collection, including school report cards, attendance records, and feedback from teachers, school counselors, caseworkers, and foster parents, as well as behavioral charts and social-emotional learning assessments that measure social skills, emotional resilience, and stress management strategies, increased leadership roles are measured by the level of involvement in GHH, sc

2957.description: Funds will support design, permitting, and construction of a reclaimed water interconnect between the City of Green Cove Springs and the Clay County Utility Authority (CCUA). The project will allow the City to distribute excess reclaimed water to CCUA for beneficial reuse, reducing surface water discharges, offsetting potable water withdrawals for irrigation, and advancing compliance with Senate Bill 64 (SB 64). The project enhances local and regional water resource management.
2957.purpose: The project will establish a reclaimed water interconnect between the City of Green Cove Springs and the Clay County Utility Authority (CCUA), enabling the beneficial reuse of excess reclaimed water. This will reduce surface water discharges, offset potable water used for irrigation, and advance compliance with Senate Bill 64 (SB 64) while protecting the St. Johns River and enhancing long-term water resource sustainability.
2957.activities: The project will include design, permitting, and construction of the reclaimed water interconnect and associated improvements. Activities will include installation of transmission mains, valves, metering, and controls necessary to convey reclaimed water from the City’s system to CCUA’s distribution network for reuse.
2957.direct_services: The project will provide direct environmental and public health benefits by reducing nutrient loading to the St. Johns River and ensuring sustainable use of reclaimed water. Citizens will benefit from improved regional water management, reduced reliance on potable groundwater, and long-term protection of natural resources vital for recreation, tourism, and quality of life.
2957.population: The project will serve approximately 10,000 residents within the City of Green Cove Springs and the surrounding CCUA service area, benefiting both current and future customers by enhancing regional reclaimed water capacity and reliability.
2957.outcome: Expected outcomes include compliance with SB 64 requirements, increased reclaimed water reuse, and measurable reductions in surface water discharge volumes and nutrient concentrations. Success will be tracked through FDEP and SJRWMD reporting, effluent discharge monitoring, and metered reclaimed water flow data to verify beneficial reuse quantities and system performance.

1424.description: Resistance: Courageous Acts in Desperate Times During the Holocaust Exhibit will teach visitors that there was resistance and victims did not go like "sheep to the slaughter." Did they fight back? After learning the true story of resistance during the Holocaust, the real question that should be asked is "How was it possible that any resistance - spiritual or army - took place? Through this exhibit, we will share that living every moment of every day was an act of resistance, smuggling a loaf of bread, rescuing a torah scroll, chronicling events, taking up arms in streets, forests, death camps and ghettos, such as the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, which in spring of 1943, drew the attention of the world. Remarkably, there was resistance.
1424.purpose: The goal is to create a permanent exhibit for the HDEC that will enrich and enhance the visitor museum experience. In addition, visitors will have the opportunity to learn more about Resistance during the Holocaust.
1424.activities: This exhibit will be a part of the HDEC full museum experience which is open to all visitors and school field trips. In addition, any programs, films, events, and traveling exhibitions at the time will also be available for touring.
1424.direct_services: All citizens will be able to schedule tours of the museum, visit the Library, the Interactive Learning Center, become a volunteer such as a transcriber, audit editor, proofer of the HDEC's globally recognized Oral History Collection of Survivors, Liberators, and Rescuers eyewitness testimonies which to date total 2300+. Visitors will also be able to access the 59,000 eyewitness testimonies from th
1424.population: Visitors of all ages and nationalities are welcome to the museum. The HDEC especially targets students from elementary through college and universities, elderly, Holocaust Survivors and their families, historians, authors, scholars, researchers, representatives of Holocaust museums, locally nationally, and internationally, educators, and legislators. The HDEC anticipates serving over 36,000 individuals.
1424.outcome: The Resistance exhibit will enrich the cultural experience of visitors at the museum by telling the stories of those who fought back against Nazi tyranny. This exhibit will teach visitors that victims did not go like sheep to the slaughter and that there were many forms of Resistance. Visitors will be exposed to the true stories of those who fought back, such as Sam Lato, a Jewish Resistance Fighter who joined the Resistance at 17. He said, "There was Resistance. We did not go quietly. I know the Jews fought back. I was one of them. I was there."

2279.description: The funds will support our mission to heal Veterans facing PTSD, TBI, chronic pain, anxiety, and related challenges. In our first year, we are serving over 70 Veterans monthly and delivering more than 600 free sessions each month using state-of-the-art holistic therapies. Our goal is to provide lasting relief, improve quality of life, and reduce Veteran suicide by addressing root causes rather than relying solely on medication.
2279.purpose: The funds will support our mission to heal Veterans facing PTSD, TBI, chronic pain, anxiety, and related challenges. In our first year, we are serving over 70 Veterans monthly and delivering more than 600 free sessions each month using state-of-the-art holistic therapies. Our goal is to provide lasting relief, improve quality of life, and reduce Veteran suicide by addressing root causes rather than relying solely on medication.
2279.activities: 100% of the funds will go directly to services for Veterans in our community. These dollars will ensure continued access to life-changing therapies such as light, cryo, magnetic, and hyperbaric treatments—provided free of charge—to help heal the physical and mental wounds of those who have served our nation.
2279.direct_services: The funds will support direct therapeutic services for Veterans, including hyperbaric oxygen, cryotherapy, light therapy, magnetic therapy, and 20+ additional advanced modalities. These treatments are provided free of charge, delivering relief from PTSD, TBI, pain, anxiety, and other service-related challenges.
2279.population: The majority of funds will serve Veterans in our community at no cost to them. At this point we service over 70 Veterans monthly and delivering more than 600 free sessions each month.
2279.outcome: Improved physical health for Veterans, demonstrated by reduced pain levels, decreased inflammation, faster recovery from injuries, and increased mobility and stamina as a result of advanced therapeutic services. Additionally improved mental health for Veterans, demonstrated by reduced stress, anxiety, depression, and PTS symptoms, along with improved sleep quality, mood stability, and overall emotional resilience. Measured through confidential pre- and post- session mental health surveys, standardized self-assessment tools, feedback and observations from trained staff, tracking of session attendance and consistency, and Veteran testimonials documenting improvements in daily life and emotiona

1861.description: Due to the City's recent growth, the city and its police department need to keep pace with the influx of added people, drivers, crime, etc. The city would like to update an array of its policing equipment, particularly a new closed-caption camera system and license plate reader system. This system would offer the ability to completely integrate with a CAD system delivering still images and video while police officers are traveling to a call, thus enhancing crime prevention and investigation, crime analysis and intelligence gathering, intelligence sharing with neighboring agencies, and enhanced situation awareness. Sweetwater would also benefit from a closed-caption camera system and license plate reader system. CCTV and LPR offer multifaceted advantages in enhancing security and law enforcement.

Club Challenge is the bridge for this vulnerable population who desire to feel valued by their community and to participate in meaningful life activities that satisfy their personal goals such as: expand their interests and abilities, engage in volunteer service, learn about taking care of themselves, and explore the possibility of work.

2355.description: The Town of Lake Park plans to undertake a traffic safety upgrade project that will result in the creation of an ovalabout (similar to a roundabout, but oval) at a five-way intersection comprising 10th Street, Prosperity Farms Road, and Northern Drive. The traffic update activities will include replacing the traditional intersection with an ovalabout; pavement resurfacing and widening; improving land configurations for enhanced traffic flow; installing durable pavement markings and signage; upgrading sidewalks/pathways; and installing ADA-compliant curb ramps and crossings. This will enhance traffic flow, improve pedestrian safety, and contribute to the functional value of the surrounding community.
2355.purpose: Upgrading traffic safety in the Town of Lake Park by creating an ovalabout (similar to a roundabout, but oval) at a well- traveled five-way intersection will reduce the number of vehicular crashes that occur in that specific area (27 in the past 10 years, 24 of which occurred in the last five years). It will also create traffic-calming benefits by reducing travel speeds, and will increase mobility (as the result of protected crosswalks), and provide residents, local business owners, and visitors
2355.activities: Funded traffic safety upgrades will include constructing an ovalabout at a five-way intersection (replacing the existing traditional intersection) at 10th Street, Prosperity Farms Road and Northern Drive; pavement resurfacing and widening; improving lane configurations for enhanced traffic flow; installing durable pavement markings and signage; upgrading sidewalks/pathways; and installing ADA-compliant curb ramps and crossings.
2355.direct_services: The ovalabout will enhance traffic flow, improve pedestrian safety, and contribute to the surrounding community's functional value. All pedestrian enhancements will be designed to meet or exceed ADA standards, ensuring accessibility for all residents.
2355.population: This project will serve drivers and pedestrians in Lake Park who drive or walk in the area of the planned traffic safety upgrade. This is expected to total thousands of people each week.
2355.outcome: Project benefits include fewer motor vehicle crashes at the site, resulting in fewer injuries. PBSO compiles statistics on motor vehicle crashes and will easily determine the level of improvement. Transportation conditions will be improved in the area of the intersection, including minimizing idling times, reducing congestion, and ultimately improving overall vehicular traffic. This will be measured by observation of the traffic flow in the area of the ovalabout.

2356.organization: Health Care District of Palm Beach County
2356.description: The Health Care District of Palm Beach County (HCD) is seeking state support to purchase a multi-mission helicopter to to efficiently and effectively respond to complex emergencies. There are currently no multi-mission helicopters in Palm Beach County (PBC) with integrated aeromedical, fire, and search and rescue. Currently, PBC must request support from the US Coast Guard for such needs, or request mutual aide from Miami-Dade which requires local government approval. In most instances minutes, even seconds, are paramount to saving lives.
2356.purpose: There are currently no multi-mission helicopters in Palm Beach County that can respond to emergencies through integrated aeromedical, fire, and search and rescue. A multi-mission emergency response helicopter is an aviation asset capable of performing several critical response functions—without requiring dedicated aircraft for each mission type.
2356.activities: Integrated multi-mission aircraft capable of search and rescue, aeromedical and trauma/patient transport, firefighting, law enforcement support, disaster assessment.
2356.direct_services: Example scenarios include: Infrastructure/bridge collapse, wild or urban fires, cruise/boating accidents, natural disaster prep and recovery, industrial accidents, mass casualty transport, missing person or wilderness rescues.
2356.population: Palm Beach County. In the case of a State of Emergency, through mutual aide agreements with the State of Florida, Trauma Hawk would be able to deploy support missions faster and more cost efficiently than current contracted aerial operations.
2356.outcome: To integrate emergency operations into a multi-mission aircraft requires very specific resources. The helicopter must be specifically equipped with features such as hoists, advanced radar, cargo hooks for firefighting equipment, and night vision systems to quickly locate and assist individuals in distress, aid in rescues and firefighting on land, at sea, or in remote or hazardous environments, and provide aeromedical services both on the ground and in flight. The helicopters must have ability to hover steadily, land in difficult locations, and carry supplies making them highly effective for complex rescue operations -- offering a faster and more versatile solution than ground-based teams tha

1780.description: The Help Me Grow Florida (HMGF) system is designed to help the state and communities leverage existing resources to ensure communities identify vulnerable children, link families to community-based services, and empower families to support their children’s healthy development through the implementation of four core components. The four core components include the centralized access point, family and community outreach, child health provider outreach, and data collection and analysis.
1780.purpose: Help Me Grow® Florida (HMGF) connects children and families to the services they need and provides support for families to navigate a complex system of resources. With increased funding, this will allow more children and families to access these resources. Currently, 92% of children and families are successfully connected to at least one health, social, or educational service. 89% of children are served by HMGF before entering kindergarten increasing opportunities for early intervention.
1780.activities: HMGF care coordinators answer questions that parents and caregivers have about their child's development (ages birth-8) and provide follow up to ensure children receive necessary services. Care coordinators average 5 direct follow- ups per family. Care coordinators provide ongoing communication with physicians working with children and families who access HMGF and maintain partnerships with 22 physician champions advocating for HMGF services throughout the state. Providing developmental screenings and comprehensive care coordination with follow-up services to caregivers and child healthcare providers. Conducting child healthcare and early education provider outr
1780.population: Maintaining a centralized access point that links families of young children with sources of support and services to address concerns about their child’s health, development, behavior and learning. Providing developmental screenings and comprehensive care coordination with follow-up services to caregivers and child healthcare providers. Conducting child healthcare and early education provider outreach trainings to educate and raise awareness about child development and the importance of early de
1780.outcome: Providing access to developmental and behavioral screenings for early identification of early childhood and infant mental health concerns that may result in an immediate referral for services, thus reducing the need for costly intervention later on. This will be measured by keeping track of the percent of successful connections to services, percent of parents/caregivers reporting their child’s development, behavior and/or mental health has improved, percent of parents/caregivers reporting that they have access to people they can talk to for advice and emotional support and percent of healthcare providers referring to HMGF.

1691.organization: Young Singers of the Palm Beaches
1691.description: We operate a free after-school music programs for 2300 students in elementary & middle schools in PB County including Belle Glade. With grant funds from the state we can continue to expand the program and serve 2300 additional students. Our programs provide high quality choral education and help to develop teamwork, leadership skills, and foster good citizenship. The outcome is improved literacy skills, improved wellness and mental health, and improved life skills through music.
1691.purpose: We will be able to increase our reach in afterschool music programming to over 25 sites in Palm Beach County and provide enhanced summer programming. We will be able to expand the Middle School program where some of our most vulnerable teens suffer from depression, anxiety and isolation. Introducing these after school music programs will reduce the time spent on screens and social media while building community in person interactions.
1691.activities: Children will receive music instruction before and afterschool and will perform throughout the community.
1691.direct_services: Choirs and community singing events bring together people of all ages and backgrounds. Provides a shared space where diverse experiences blend harmoniously.
1691.population: Elementary and Middle School children in afterschool programs.
1691.outcome: Singing integrates reading, rhythm, and memory—skills closely tied to literacy and numeracy. Encourages focus, discipline, and attention to detail through musical practice. Singing develops auditory discrimination, articulation, and pronunciation. Encourages exploration of language through storytelling, rhyme, and rhythm. Singing encourages imagination, self-expression, and innovation.

Sewer AI will use the data from the field, catalog the data, and complete timely assessments to generate project needs. This will improve data quality, accelerate capital planning, reduce emergency failures, prevent sanitary sewer overflows, and strengthen environmental and regulatory compliance across the wastewater system.
2123.purpose: The funds will modernize WASD's sewer inspection program by optimizing the CCTV reviews and generate risk-based rehab priorities. Sewer AI will use the data from the field, catalog the data, and complete timely assessments to generate project needs. This will improve data quality, accelerate capital planning, reduce emergency failures, prevent sanitary sewer overflows, and strengthen environmental and regulatory compliance across the wastewater system.

By modernizing sewer inspections and enabling faster, data-driven rehabilitation decisions, the project will protect public health, minimize service disrup
2123.population: Residents of Miami-Dade County, benefiting more than 2.8 million people, including the local community within the project area.

2161.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2161.description: This additional shelter initiative, a comprehensive plan that includes new construction, facility upgrades, and expansion, inclusive of furniture, fixtures, and equipment is set to house at least 350 animals. The goal of this long-term solution is to deliver significant fiscal and community health benefits to Miami-Dade County.
2161.purpose: The funds requested will increase the capacity to provide shelter to Miami-Dade County's homeless pet population.
2161.activities: The project will construct new housing facilities for homeless dogs and cats with adoption services, establish a fully equipped veterinary clinic offering spay and neuter services, and develop outdoor enrichment and play areas with ample free roaming space.
2161.direct_services: Miami-Dade County residents will have access to pet adoption and affordable spay/neuter services for dogs and cats through the on-site clinic.
2161.population: The project will serve Miami-Dade County with an estimated population of 2.8 million residents, more specifically, pet owners seeking low-cost veterinary services, individuals and families interested in adoption, and provide refuge for approximately 350 animals.
2161.outcome: The project is expected to increase shelter capacity and improve animal welfare by reducing overcrowding and the need for co-housing. Success will be measured by the average length of stay, number of animals housed, and an increase in volunteer engagement with the new facility.

3533.description: This project will create a welcoming and accessible environment that enables guests of all ages and mobility conditions to fully explore Peace River Botanical & Sculpture Gardens (PRB&SG), participate in special events and educational opportunities, and experience the unique combination of natural ecosystems and created art that PRB&SG offer. Funds will supply the paving for 12K sq feet of pathways that are currently shell or dirt, enabling improved handicap acessiblity as well as making our property more resilient in the face of hurricanes as all paved paths remained in tact and shell/dirt paths eroded in prior storms.
3533.purpose: The funds from this grant will help to improve safety and accessibility for the visitors of PRB&SG. Smooth, paved paths make it easier for people using wheelchairs, walkers, canes, mobility scooters, or strollers to move safely and independently. By improving pathways and with targeted outreach, PRB&SG hope to engage more guests with limited mobility in Garden activities and send a message that everyone is welcome.
3533.activities: PRB&SG has built a solid foundation of dynamic programming, quickly gaining a reputation of being a cultural and educational beacon for our region. Each year PRB&SG host multiple world-class exhibitions and offer a year-round calendar of events and educational courses on topics of hoticulture, conservation, art, and more. Paving pathways will allow all guests to access garden features and programming, rather than being limited to certain areas.
3533.direct_services: PRB&SG are committed to providing free field trips for our Title 1 schools, serving nearly 3500 students annually. We also provide free horticulture therapy sessions to area nonprofits that serve adults with disabilities and comprehensive, free wellness programs for our community. We are members of Museums for All (highly reduced entry for SNAP recipients). Guest Demographics: 52%: local residents
3533.population: While all 30K+ guests and 2K+members will benefit from improved pathways, the target population for this request is those with limited mobility. With 55% of our guests being over the age of 65, and the most likely to fall into this population, we have an increasing number of our residents and visitors that are missing out on our highlighted features.
3533.outcome: The outcome is all guests can traverse our property safely and have access to all facets of exhibits and programming. Our Director of Engagement closely monitors data on general attendance, class participation, feeback surveys, and online reviews to determine quality and effectiveness of each facet of our programming and facility. Our organization has recently won Excellence in Nonprofit Leadership, Community Impact Award, Attraction Hero, Best in FLorida, SWFL Top 6 Boards, and America's Top Hidden Gem on Trip Advisor.

3534.description: The Parent Partner Program seeks to reduce youth Baker Act readmissions in Charlotte and DeSoto Counties through a structured parent peer support model. Trained parents with lived experience—known as Parent Partners—provide empathetic mentoring, system navigation, and practical guidance and parenting skills to caregivers of youth in crisis. Targeting families who are disengaged from treatment or discharge planning, the program focuses on building trust, addressing caregiver stressors, and strengthening post-discharge supports. A team of five Parent Partners and one therapist, supervised by a family-systems–oriented Master’s level therapist, will engage at least 150 families each year through rapid outreach, screening for risk factors such as caregiver trauma and housing instability, and connecting families to resources that promote lasting engagement and reduce repeat crises.
3534.purpose: The goal of the Parent Partner Program is to utilize a parent peer model to decrease repeat youth Baker Acts in Charlotte and DeSoto Counties. This goal will be achieved by improving parental engagement, addressing caregiver needs, and strengthening post-discharge supports. Approximately one-quarter of parents/guardians at CBHC do not engage in treatment or discharge planning. Subsequently, their children tend to cycle back through crisis care.
3534.activities: Identification of youth at high risk for repeat Baker Acts. Screening of parents/caregivers for disengagement, housing instability, trauma history/ACES and review of youth school attendance. Peer Services for Parents by Parents whose children have interfaced with the behavioral health system.
3534.direct_services: This program seeks to engage 200 families, hoping to achieve a 75% engagement rate. It will include rapid engagement strategies immediately following a Baker Act. The primary focus is on engaging parents initially, with the ultimate goal of improving communication between families and the treatment system, leading to better outcomes in the treatment process.
3534.population: Target Populations: Persons with poor mental health, Persons with poor physical health,Jobless persons, Economically disadvantaged persons, At-risk youth, Drug users (in health services) and Drug offenders (in criminal justice)
3534.outcome: Benefit: Improve Mental Health: Measure: Attempting to achieve 75% engagement of parents of high risk families. Methodology: Track number of screenings versus number of engaged family members. Benefit: Reduce Recidivism: Measure: Hoping to demonstrate 20% reduction in Baker Acts for the youth of parents engaged in the Parent Partner program. Methodology: Quarterly Reporting from Electronic Medical Record. Benefit: Demonstrate use of Assisted Outpatient Treatment for high risk families to ensure participation in family therapies.
