2971.organization: Clay County Board of County Commissioners
2971.description: The Clay County Public Safety Complex is designed to include a Multi-Agency Warehouse, Fleet Center, Administrative Building, 911 Call Center, and Training Complex all situated on a new campus. Once operational, the public safety complex will serve the general population by reduced call times and an increased capacity to respond to natural disasters and other emergencies. Funds will help construct the utility infrastructure (i.e. water and sewer lines) necessary to support the complex.
2971.purpose: The Clay County Public Safety Complex is designed to include a Multi-Agency Warehouse, Fleet Center, Administrative Building, 911 Call Center, and Training Complex all situated on a new campus. These facilities will allow for greater coordination between the Clay County Sheriff's Office and Public Safety. Water and sewer infrastructure is essential to keep these critical facilities operational during major disasters and emergencies.
2971.activities: Essential public safety services across the County for citizens. Improved Public Safety performance and response. The Co-Located Communications Center will provide synergy inside the centers with the correct communications layout. Reliable infrastructure is essential to support the long term viability of the Public Safety Complex.
2971.direct_services: Once operational, the public safety complex will serve the general population by reduced call times and an increased capacity to respond to natural disasters and other emergencies.
2971.population: The general population of Clay County is the target population served by the proposed Clay County Public Safety Complex.
2971.outcome: Benefits include: Reduced Response times from both the Clay County Sheriff's office and Clay County Public Safety. Improved operational efficiencies and streamlined operational costs. Expected Outcome/Methodology: Reduction in call times which are monitored by CCSO and Public Safety and tracked using UCR, NIBRS, and NFIRS.

3073.organization: Clay County Senior Services of Aging True
3073.description: Through Aging True’s Meals on Wheels program, eligible seniors receive nutritious, dietitian-approved meals delivered to their homes. The program also links participants to Aging True's network of services, including case management, in home support, and mental wellness support. This project will provide an additional 25,000 meals to the 400 Clay County seniors currently on the waiting list, helping them maintain their health and independence at home. Each delivery dually serves as a brief wellness check to ensure the senior's safety & provides an outlet for personal connection, reducing isolation among those who live alone. The goal of this program is to reduce food insecurity among Clay County's rapidly growing senior population (ultimately improving their health outcomes) while lessening strain on the local healthcare system.
3073.purpose: The Clay County Nutrition Access for Seniors Project will expand the capacity of Aging True's Home Delivered Meals Program to meet the increasing demand for senior nutrition services in Clay County. Currently, 400 older adults are on the waiting list, unable to receive consistent access to nutritious meals, and therefore are at higher risk of institutionalization and even death. The requested funding will allow Aging True to provide 25,000 additional meals to the county, ensuring these seniors r
3073.activities: Funding for this project will support the preparation, packaging, and delivery of nutritious meals to homebound and vulnerable seniors across every zip code of Clay County. Certification specialists will methodically assess and enroll each of the eligible seniors on the waiting list. Meals will be delivered directly to participants' homes on 252 serving days of the year, by trained staff and volunteers, providing not only nourishment but also a vital daily safety and wellness check.
3073.direct_services: The Clay County Nutrition Access for Seniors Project will provide home-delivered meals directly to eligible older adults who are unable to prepare or access nutritious food on their own. Each participant will receive regular deliveries of balanced, dietitian-approved meals that meet one-third of the Recommended Dietary Allowance for seniors.
3073.population: The target population for the Clay County Nutrition Access for Seniors Project includes homebound and nutritionally at-risk adults aged 60 and older residing in Clay County. They live alone, have limited mobility, and lack access to consistent, healthy meals. The project will serve 25,000 meals to the hundreds of seniors currently on the waiting list for home-delivered meals, providing them with regular nutrition, daily wellness checks, and connections to other services.
3073.outcome: Outcomes will be improved nutrition, health, and independence for home-based seniors in Clay County. Participants will experience reduced food insecurity, enhanced physical well-being, and increased social connection. Outcomes will be measured by tracking the number of seniors served, meal delivery data, and participant surveys conducted by Aging True case managers to assess improvements in nutrition access, stability, and self-reported quality of life.

1971.description: The Sarasota, Pasco, and Marion County Sheriff's Office, or police departments in their jurisdiction, will contract with Florida-based private forensic labs who have a minimum of 5 years accreditation in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 and FBI testing standards for high-volume cases, including specialized DNA testing for fired shell casings, firearms, and property crime evidence. Funds may also be used for expedited testing of evidence when appropriate.
1971.purpose: The funds will allow three sheriffs' offices (Sarasota, Pasco, and Marion County) to operate a grant program in their offices, or police departments in their jurisdiction, to contract with ISO/IEC 17025:2017-accredited private DNA laboratories for testing of DNA samples in an expedited or specialized manner. The goal is to show a meaningful reduction in crime by ensuring law enforcement has the resources to properly and quickly test evidence in cases using a technology or technique that is not r
1971.activities: Funds will be used by Sarasota, Pasco, and Marion County sheriffs' offices or police departments in their jurisdiction to contract with accredited private DNA labs to analyze and test evidence when the case in question requires expedited testing or testing using a technology or technique not readily available at a local or state laboratory. Activities include partnering with ISO/IEC 17025:2017-accredited private DNA laboratories with a minimum of 5 years accreditation to conduct expedited or spe
1971.direct_services: The requested funding will enhance case resolution rates and enable law enforcement to effectively process cases that require specialized evidence testing. This will lead to more accurate investigations, improved public safety, and increased justice for victims and their families. Expedited DNA testing will remove repeat offenders from the community, provide a safer community, and reduce crime.
1971.population: The target population includes residents, business owners, and visitors within the Pasco, Marion, and Sarasota county who are affected by crimes. The project is expected to serve all residents directly through enhanced public safety and crime reduction efforts.
1971.outcome: The expected benefit is a measurable reduction in crime through expedited evidence processing. Improved DNA testing capacity will increase case clearance rates, deter repeat offenders, and enhance overall community safety. The private labs contracted will provide the Police Department and FDLE a report no later than one year after receipt of funding, including the amount of funding received, the number of cases tested, and the type of DNA testing performed.

1875.description: The goal is to enhance safety along the Dolan Road corridor, a 2-lane minor urban arterial (local residential road), that serves as a east-west collector for thru-traffic, and the connector for residents walking/biking to school or Village parks. The improvements will upgrade the sidewalk with a multi-use path for safety and better ADA compliance, and provide intersection improvements to slow traffic and enhance driver visibility of pedestrians/bicyclists.
1875.purpose: The purpose of this project is to enhance safety along the Dolan Road corridor, a 2-lane minor urban arterial (local residential road), that serves as a east-west collector for thru-traffic, and the connector for residents walking/biking to school or Village parks. The improvements will upgrade the sidewalk with a multi-use path for safety and better ADA compliance, and provide intersection improvements to slow traffic and enhance driver visibility of pedestrians/bicyclists.
1875.activities: Four (4) vehicle-pedestrian and two (2) vehicle-bicycle crashes have reported since 2017 on this roadway. The proposed improvements will provide a safe pathway for the students on their way to school (G-Star School of the Arts) and residents walking/biking to the Village's parks, ballfields and library. The proposed safety improvements are recommended by the Village's Vision Zero Action Plan to reduce vehicular conflicts to 0.
1875.direct_services: The proposed roadway safety improvements will enhance the safety of pedestrians/bicyclists traveling along the corridor with a separated mutli-use path. Dolan Road does not currently have sidewalks on both sides of the street. There is documented speeding (10-19 mph beyond the speed limit). The proposed safety and "traffic calming" intersection improvements will reduce vehicular speeds and bring b
1875.population: A specific population is not able to be measured because drivers use Dolan Road as an alternate to Forest Hill Boulevard (SR882), and drive at speeds of the major arterial. The vehicular speeds range from 35-44 in the 85 percentile, but the road is posted for 25 mph. The average daily traffic volume is 5000 trips. This is expected to increase as overall volumes in the region increase. G-Star School of the Arts, a charter high school located nearby on Congress Avenue has 693 students. Resident st
1875.outcome: The improvements will provide a safe route for residents who are walking or biking to the park, library and special events. (The Village Municipal Complex with ballfields, tennis/pickleball courts, basketball courts, splash pad water park, playground and library is located on this segment of Dolan Road.) The proposed safety improvements are recommended by the Village's Vision Zero Action Plan to reduce vehicular conflicts to 0. Crash reports will be monitored to evaluate success of this effort.

2974.description: The Cleather H. Hathcock, Sr. Community Center has served the City of Alachua community for nearly 20 years. The aging modular facility currently serves a resident population of 11,000. Is is strategically located in an area of low-to- moderate income households which are able to access the facility by walking or biking and provides a variety of community support services. Funding will be used to construct a new facility that will continue to serve these vital community support services.
2974.purpose: The Cleather H. Hathcock, Sr. Community Center has served the City of Alachua community for nearly 20 years. The aging modular facility currently serves a resident population of 11,000. Is is strategically located in an area of low-to- moderate income households which are able to access the facility by walking or biking and provides a variety of community support services. Funding will be used to construct a new facility that will continue to serve these vital community support services.
2974.activities: The new Cleather H. Hathcock, Sr. Community Center will provide a wide variety of programming and support services to the Alachua community. Programming includes senior-focused activities and resources, youth-based activities, health screening/activities, cultural events, and community support services.
2974.direct_services: The new Cleather H. Hathcock, Sr. Community Center will provide community support services, community programming, health-related activities, and cultural activities. The new facility will be located in an area with low-to- moderate income households to provide ease of access to serve these residents.
2974.population: All residents of the City of Alachua: over 11,000 at the moment.
2974.outcome: Residents will be able to access health-related and physical-related programming; cultural events; partnerships / events with local schools; job-placement and job training assistance. To be measured by number of events and individuals attending/participating will be tracked through attendance logs

1876.description: The purpose is to ensure power resilience via replacement of generators at sewer Vacuum Stations #2 and #3 that are end-of-life (24 and 21 years old respectively. These "Vac Stations" are required to pump sewage from businesses and home into a sewer force main. The geographical service area is flat and sanitary sewer cannot be transmitted via gravity flow. Power loss at these critical facilities will result in sewage backing up into 183 businesses and 500 residences.

These "Vac Stations" are required to pump sewage from businesses and home into a sewer force main. The geographical service area is flat and sanitary sewer cannot be transmitted via gravity flow. Power loss at these critical facilities will result in sewage backing up into 183 businesses and 500 residences.
1876.activities: Replacement of two permanent generators ( 150kw and 200kw) at Sanitary Sewer Vacuum Stations #2 and #3 (each at $500,000)
1876.direct_services: The project will protect the general public from hard as power resilience (emergency electrical service) is provided to two critical components of the Palm Springs Water Utilities, without which may result in loss of sanitary sewer service and back-up of sewage into homes and businesses.
1876.population: The two sewer vacuum stations each serve 500 residents and 183 businesses on the east side of the Village
1876.outcome: The emergency generators are included in critical facility upgrades identified in the Wastewater Master Plan, which have been adopted by the Village Council. Completion of the installation of two (2) generators (150kw and 200kw), with fuel tanks and electrical connections, at the Village's Sewer Vacuum Stations #2 and #3 is the metric.

2975.description: Procurement and installation of a new power transformer, switchgear, and associated protection equipment; construction of a control building with relay panels, SCADA systems, battery banks, and communication infrastructure; and completion of all necessary site work. These expenditures cover equipment purchase, installation, testing, and integration required to expand the substation’s capacity and ensure reliable long-term operation.
2975.purpose: Procurement and installation of a new power transformer, switchgear, and associated protection equipment; construction of a control building with relay panels, SCADA systems, battery banks, and communication infrastructure; and completion of all necessary site work. These expenditures cover equipment purchase, installation, testing, and integration required to expand the substation’s capacity and ensure reliable long-term operation.
2975.activities: The funds will support the activities necessary to advance the project, including engineering & design services, construction documents, procurement of equipment & materials, & installation & testing of systems. These services collectively ensure the project is fully planned, properly constructed, & successfully delivered for operational use.
2975.direct_services: The funding will support the delivery of reliable, safe, and expanded electrical service to the community by improving system capacity, enhancing power quality, & reducing the likelihood of outages. These upgrades will provide more consistent utility performance, faster restoration times during service interruptions, & the infrastructure needed to support future growth & development.
2975.population: All residents and businesses within the City of Alachua: more than 11,000 population currently.
2975.outcome: By improving electrical reliability and increasing system capacity, the project supports business operations, attracts new development, and enables future growth, thereby strengthening overall economic activity in the community. Business growth indicators such as new commercial connections and overall improvements in service reliability metrics can be monitored. Additional measures may include tracking economic development activity, such as new business openings, job creation, and increases in utility demand that reflect expanded economic activity.

2976.description: The purpose of the project is to increase wastewater conveyance capacity and strengthen system reliability by constructing a new force main. This improvement will reduce the risk of overflows, enhance resiliency during extreme weather, protect the environment, and ensure the system can meet current and future demand.
2976.purpose: The purpose of the project is to increase wastewater conveyance capacity and strengthen system reliability by constructing a new force main. This improvement will reduce the risk of overflows, enhance resiliency during extreme weather, protect the environment, and ensure the system can meet current and future demand.
2976.activities: Funds will support engineering, permitting, and construction activities, including pipeline installation, necessary appurtenances, pump station connections, utility coordination, and system testing. These improvements will reduce the risk of overflows and ensure reliable service as the community grows.
2976.direct_services: This project will significantly improve wastewater management by increasing system capacity, enhancing flow efficiency, and adding capacity to the wastewater transmission network.
2976.population: All residents and businesses of the City of Alachua: current population approximately 11,000.
2976.outcome: This project will significantly improve wastewater management by increasing system capacity, enhancing flow efficiency, and adding capacity to the wastewater transmission network. Tracking increased conveyance capacity, fewer sanitary sewer overflows, reduced emergency repairs, and more stable pump station performance. Continued regulatory compliance and less system downtime will also indicate stronger, more reliable wastewater operations.

2977.description: The City of Newberry is requesting funding for Phase 2 of the all-hazard training facility to complete construction of joint training rooms. These rooms will be used by all public safety agencies for multi-scenario preparedness and cross- training, reducing overall training costs through shared facilities and resources, while also minimizing travel time for training. These training rooms are vital for inter-agency coordination and improving emergency response outcomes in alignment with national safety priorities.
2977.purpose: The goal is to construct additional Joint training rooms for multi-agency (police, fire, EMS, emergency system personnel, state) first responders to improve operational efficiency by sharing resources and standardization, disaster preparedness training across agencies with realistic, multi-agency simulations, enhance public safety through coordinated emergency response and support workforce development across disciplines for our Tri-County Region of Alachua, Levy, and Gilchrist Counties.
2977.activities: The multi-agency training rooms will include cross-training and enhanced communication programs for all public safety agencies across our multi-jurisdictional region; Alachua, Levy and Gilchrist Counties that include interagency workshops for emergency preparedness, incident command systems and mutual aid coordination, provide continuing education and certification programs, serve as a hub for regional tabletop and full-scale high-impact events, and provide simulation zones for urban, rural, agr
2977.direct_services: Direct services for citizens include disaster readiness seminars, youth engagement programs, interactive safety fairs, CPR and first aid certification courses, fire prevention and home safety workshops, active shooter and personal safety awareness sessions, explorer programs for police and fire departments, emergency planning assistance for seniors and individuals with disabilities or STEM-focused
2977.population: A combined 87,033 residents from the Tri-County Region of which Levy and Gilchrist County have high poverty rates.
2977.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved ISO ratings for reduction of property insurance for jurisdictions. Response time improvement measured by average time to respond. Interagency Communication measured by number of communication errors or delays during joint exercises. Training completion rates measured by percentage of personnel from each agency receiving completion certification. And cost savings measured by reduced training costs due to shared resources and facilities.

2978.description: This initiative will replace aging, end-of-life cardiac monitors with a single, standardized platform capable of transcutaneous pacing, advanced rhythm analysis, synchronized cardioversion, defibrillation, 12-lead ECG acquisition and interpretation, and secure hospital telemetry, ultimately ensuring that every EMS call over the next decade benefits from reliable care.
2978.purpose: To replace aging, end-of-life cardiac monitors with a single, standardized platform capable of transcutaneous pacing, advanced rhythm analysis, synchronized cardioversion, defibrillation, 12-lead ECG acquisition and interpretation, and secure hospital telemetry, ultimately ensuring that every EMS call over the next decade benefits from reliable care.
2978.activities: Funding will replace Fire Rescue’s aging cardiac monitors with advanced units that provide real-time rhythm analysis, defibrillation, pacing, and vital sign monitoring. Updated monitors ensure reliable, life-saving care and faster cardiac response across all front line rescue units.
2978.direct_services: The goal is to improve Fire Rescue’s cardiac care capabilities by upgrading outdated monitors. New units enhance diagnostic accuracy, enable faster interventions, and transmit data to hospitals, improving survival rates and emergency response efficiency for cardiac patients.
2978.outcome: Benefits: Increase cardiac arrest survival and return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) rates by 10% within 12 months; 100% of frontline rescue units equipped with reliable cardiac monitors for emergency response. Methods: Track pre-hospital cardiac arrest outcomes using Fire Rescue EMS data hospital reports; Equipment deployment audits and quarterly service readiness checks.

2981.description: The City of Waldo seeks funding to replace approximately 530 aging residential and commercial water meters with new Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meters. Many of the existing meters are beyond their useful life and no longer record usage accurately, contributing to an estimated 15–20% annual water loss. This project will modernize the City’s water system, providing accurate, real-time meter data to improve billing accuracy, identify leaks quickly, and reduce water waste. The improvements will conserve a precious resource, increase utility revenue, lower operating costs, and reduce staff time spent on manual readings. For a small, financially disadvantaged community with limited staff and funding capacity, this investment will significantly improve operational efficiency and long-term water system sustainability.
2981.purpose: The purpose of this project is to replace approximately 530 outdated water meters with Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meters to reduce the City’s 15–20% annual water loss, improve billing accuracy, and increase operational efficiency. The upgrades will conserve drinking water, enhance revenue recovery, and reduce staff time spent on manual meter readings, supporting long-term financial and resource sustainability for the small, financially disadvantaged City of Waldo.
2981.activities: Funds will be used for engineering design, procurement, installation, and integration of approximately 530 Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meters. Activities include removing outdated meters, installing new AMI meters and transmitters, connecting the system to the City’s billing software, training staff on system operation, and verifying meter accuracy to ensure reliable service and efficient water use.
2981.direct_services: The project will provide all City of Waldo water customers with accurate and reliable metering, ensuring fair billing and improved leak detection. Citizens will benefit from better customer service, fewer billing discrepancies, and greater awareness of water usage, helping households conserve water and reduce monthly costs.
2981.population: The target population served by this project includes all citizens and businesses within the City of Waldo who receive municipal water service. The City has an estimated population of approximately 824 residents. This project will directly benefit all water customers by improving service reliability, billing accuracy, and conservation of the community’s drinking water supply.
2981.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is reduced water loss, improved billing accuracy, and increased operational efficiency through installation of Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meters. The outcome will be measured by comparing total water production versus billed consumption, analyzing revenue recovery, and tracking reductions in staff time and maintenance costs after system implementation.

2988.description: Funds will support design, permitting, and construction of critical upgrades to the Copper Creek Lift Station, located along North County Road 23A. The project includes new pumps, piping, and wetwell rehabilitation to improve reliability, capacity, and operational safety. These Improvements will allow the lift station to adequately and more reliably serve the Copper Creek and Sands Pointe subdivisions (273 homes / approx 700+ residents), handle future growth from upstream development, and include new concrete access driveway and site access to enhance worker safety and maintenance accessibility along this high-traffic corridor.
2988.purpose: The project will rehabilitate and upgrade the Copper Creek Lift Station to improve pumping capacity, reliability, and operational safety. The improvements will ensure the system can accommodate existing and future wastewater flows, reduce the risk of sanitary sewer overflows, and enhance staff safety during routine maintenance by providing rear access away from N County Road 23A..
2988.activities: Activities will include design, permitting, bidding, construction, and engineering services during construction for the lift station’s wetwell, pumps, piping, valves, electrical/control systems, and site access improvements. The project will replace aging and undersized components and add safety features such as improved driveway access and grade stabilization.
2988.direct_services: The project will provide reliable wastewater collection and conveyance for residents in the Copper Creek and Sands Point subdivisions and the surrounding service area, preventing potential system failures or environmental discharges. Improved accessibility and reliability will enhance service continuity for all users served by the City’s wastewater system.
2988.population: The project will serve approximately 273 homes / approx 700+ residents within the Copper Creek and Sands Pointe subdivisions and surrounding service area, with capacity to accommodate additional/future residential and/or commercial growth along North County Road 23A.
2988.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved wastewater reliability, reduced risk of overflows, and enhanced operational safety. Success will be measured by monitoring lift station performance data, reduced emergency maintenance visits, and elimination of overflow or access-related safety incidents.

2992.description: The goal is to build a new middle school for grades 6 - 8 to replace the current aging facility built in 1965. This new middle school building will provide an updated learning facility and a climate controlled gymnasium for the students, staff and families of Baker County. The proposed design will also provide safer student pick-up and drop-off areas to promote a more efficient traffic flow and reduce traffic congestion around the campus.
2992.purpose: The specific goal of this funding request is to replace the current facilities that house Baker County Middle School. Since its opening in 1965, the building has seen major population in student growth, moving from the original 500 student stations to now over 1,400. The funding will not only create a safer learning environment but also help alleviate major traffic congestion issues caused by parents and buses at arrival and dismissal. These problems now cause SR 121 and SR 228 to be blocked dur
2992.activities: We will offer a high quality instruction to thousands of students in a safe environment. Additionally, we will have new athletic and extra-curricular facilities to service the community as a whole.
2992.direct_services: Citizens of the community will directly be served by building a safe and modern educational facility. The school will service approximately 1,400 students, which equates to roughly 2,800 parents. In addition, athletic fields, school performance space, gym, and cafeteria will all directly provide services to the people of our community.
2992.population: The targeted population for this facility will be students in grades 6 - 8. Target enrollment is 1400 students
2992.outcome: The expected benefit is a brand new, state of the art, facility for the students, parents, employees, and other stakeholders within the community.

3157.description: Bradford County does not currently provide water or wastewater utility service within the County; however, due to interest in expansion of commercial and industrial businesses located on, and near to the Keystone Heights Airport (air access to FL's back-up EOC at Camp Blanding), Bradford County is interested in completing a feasibility study to support a Water and Wastewater Master Plan. The creation of a regional water and wastewater system located at the Keystone Heights Airport Authority would provide water, wastewater and potentially reclaimed water to serve new businesses. This would give Bradford County the opportunity to diversify their economy since they are currently at their millage cap and unable to grow. Completion of this feasibility study will support next steps to provide an economic development boost to Bradford County, while encouraging the growth of the Keystone Heights
3157.purpose: Bradford County, a Rural Area of Opportunity, will complete a feasibility study to develop a Water/Wastewater Master Plan. Currently, Bradford County does not provide water/wastewater utility service within the County. With expanded W/WW capabilities, Bradford County will increase economic development through growing commercial and industrial businesses. The W/WW Master Plan will encompass utility system plans for the Keystone Heights Airport (air access to Florida's back-up Emergency Operations
3157.activities: Completion of a feasibility study to develop a water and wastewater utility system master plan. This will determine phasing of the project.
3157.direct_services: The proposed feasibility study will provide a strategic framework to develop local water and wastewater facilities. This study will guide future investments to enhance utility services for residents. The availability of reliable water and wastewater services will foster economic diversification and allow new businesses to open and contribute to regional growth.
3157.population: The proposed feasibility study will serve over 50,000 people.
3157.outcome: Identifying local needs and feasibility for the improvement of wastewater management through a local and efficient water and wastewater utility. Developing a local water infrastructure will help to diversify the economy and create growth opportunities for local businesses. All will be completed through the feasibility study.

2996.description: This project is for Special Facilities funding to build a new Bradford Middle/Senior High School. A new school of 1463 student stations will be built on the existing site of Bradford Middle School and Bradford Union Vocational Technical School. The project will include demolition of facilities at Bradford Middle School, Bradford Union Technical School, and Bradford High School. Some buildings at Bradford High School will be remodeled for district office use.
2996.purpose: The purpose is to construct a replacement Middle/Senior high school, the only middle/senior high school, in Bradford County. The one school will replace three existing, very old facilities.
2996.activities: The new Middle/Senior High School will allow 7-12 students to have a modern, safe facility with access to high quality instructional services and technical educational programs.
2996.direct_services: Complete funding for construction of a facility to carry out educational programs, including a full range of academic offerings, career and adult educational offerings, and dual enrollment offerings.
2996.population: The proposed project will be 1463 student stations to serve 7 - 12 students.
2996.outcome: This project will result in the replacement of 3 very old and high maintenance schools with one school. The students will receive instruction in a modern facility equipped to meet their instructional or technical education needs. Reducing to one school will greatly reduce the districts overhead cost in administrative and support personnel needed to staff a school. The new school will also result in increased safety for our students and staff.

2998.description: Requested funding will replace outdated radios with new SLERS Phase 2 compliant units, improving emergency communications for Bradford County’s EMS, Fire Rescue, and remaining Sheriff’s Office personnel not covered in earlier funding cycles. It will also support construction of a new permanent SLERS tower to expand coverage. Together, these upgrades will enhance interdepartmental coordination and strengthen public safety services for county residents.
2998.purpose: Funds will replace outdated radios with SLERS Phase 2 compliant radios for Bradford County EMS, Fire Rescue, and remaining Sheriff’s personnel not previously funded, and build a permanent SLERS tower to expand coverage.
2998.activities: Enhanced reliable radio communication services to ensure first responders are able to quickly and accurately provide emergency services to individuals.
2998.direct_services: Improved coordination and strengthened public safety services for county residents.
2998.population: Bradford County citizens, tourists, businesses, and schools.
2998.outcome: Timely and accurate response to requests for emergency and law enforcement services.

3001.description: The funds will go toward much needed improvements to the Bradford County Courthouse. Construction of the Bradford County Courthouse was completed on December 14, 1969, more than 56 years ago. The only time our courthouse has been altered was in 2004 (21 years ago), when two new wings were added to the existing courthouse to provide more office space. The original courthouse is in desperate need of renovations and repairs.

Construction of the Bradford County Courthouse was completed on December 14, 1969, more than 56 years ago. The only time our courthouse has been altered was in 2004 (21 years ago), when two new wings were added to the existing courthouse to provide more office space. The original courthouse is in desperate need of renovations and repairs.
3001.activities: All court functions as well as Clerk of the Court services including, but not limited to, collecting fines and fees, providing legal documentation for records retained by the clerk, administrative orders, child support, civil traffic/infractions, family law, tax deeds and foreclosure sales, jury duty, juvenile, probate and small claims.
3001.population: The target population served would be the elderly, jobless, economically disadvantaged, at-risk youth, physically disabled, students of all grade levels, university/college students, current or formerly incarcerated persons, drug offenders (via criminal justice), and victims of crime. This project is estimated to serve around 800 citizens regularly.
3001.outcome: The courthouse, in particularly the clerk's office, will be more physically secure reducing the chance of any physical harm coming to county employees in the course of their duties. Measurable outcomes will be the absence of any documented instances where employees were either directly or indirectly threatened. Additionally, the courthouse will come into compliance with ADA requirements. Measurable outcomes will be the absence of any ADA complaints.

3005.description: The City of Hampton is seeking legislative support to complete the renovation and rehabilitation of its aging potable water facility, which serves as a critical lifeline for residents and businesses within the community. In Fiscal Year 2024, the City was awarded $550,000 through legislative appropriations toward the originally requested $1.1 million needed to fund design and construction. The project has since progressed into final design and permitting, with construction anticipated to go out for bid in December 2025. The estimated project cost is now projected to exceed the current available funding by $100,000. Due to rising material and labor costs, and ongoing uncertainty in bid estimates, The City is requesting an additional $550,000 in construction funding to fully implement the replacement of Well 1R and the rehabilitation of the water yard facilities.
3005.purpose: The goal is to improve the health, safety and general welfare of the residents and businesses of the City of Hampton. The City of Hampton water system functions as the potable water distribution for residential and commercial customers within the city, with over 200 active connections. The current system provides a primary and secondary water source in case of a well system failure or when a well needs to be taken off-line for repairs and maintenance. The City of Hampton has operated a two-well
3005.activities: Clean, adequate potable water for residents and businesses and fire suppression needs.
3005.direct_services: Clean, adequate potable water for residents and businesses and fire suppression needs.
3005.population: Residents and business owners. The City currently serves 498 residents and businesses, plus about 50 customers outside city limits. Replacing the failing Well No. 1 is critical to sustain service and protect the community’s health, safety, and welfare. Housing affordability challenges are driving more residents and families to relocate to areas like Hampton, increasing demand for safe, reliable water service.
3005.outcome: By providing clean, adequate potable water to the businesses and community. Measured by the yearly DEP Annual Consumer Confidence Report.

3011.description: This project is the preparation of a Stormwater Master Plan (SMP) to develop a comprehensive strategy for managing stormwater runoff. The SMP will identify ways of improving system treatment and detention that will help to prevent or slow runoff during storm events and identify in-city and upstream alternatives to limit surge and peak volumes in Alligator Creek. The SMP will include evaluation of culverts, swales and ditches, retention ponds, wet storage, park space, grass swales, land acquisition, and other alternatives to slow peak runoff. The SMP document will ultimately recommend design and construction projects for managing stormwater runoff.
3011.purpose: The purpose of the project is to prepare a city-wide Stormwater Master Plan (SMP). The SMP will provide recommendations for improving system treatment and detention that will help to prevent or slow runoff during storm events, and identify in-city and upstream alternatives to limit surge and peak volumes in Alligator Creek. The SMP document will ultimately recommend design and construction projects for slowing peak runoff.
3011.activities: The SMP document will include evaluation of culverts, swales and ditches, retention ponds, wet storage, park space, grass swales, land acquisition, and other alternatives to slow peak runoff. The overall objective of the SMP is to provide recommendations improving system treatment and detention that will help to prevent or slow runoff during storm events and identify in-city and upstream alternatives to limit surge and peak volumes in Alligator Creek.The document will ultimately recommend design
3011.direct_services: This project is the development of a SMP document and will not provide direct services to citizens.
3011.population: The target population that will be served by this project is the citizens of the City of Starke. According to ACS 2023 5- year data, the population of Starke is 5,821.
3011.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is recommended design and construction projects for improving stormwater system treatment and detention to prevent or slow runoff during storm events. In-city and upstream alternatives to limit surge and peak volumes in Alligator Creek will be identified.

3014.description: The trucks will be used to pull a Food Trailer and the 32-Foot Utility Trailer that will be used for disaster activations, long-duration deployments, and mutual aid requests.
3014.purpose: These funds will purchase two used 2020–2024 Ford F-350 pickup trucks to support the Columbia County Sheriff's Office deployment responsibilities as part of the Florida Sheriffs Association (FSA) Emergency Task Force Program. Currently, CCSO does not have a dedicated pair of heavy-duty tow vehicles assigned specifically for these task force responsibilities. Relying on shared or repurposed vehicles can delay response times.
3014.activities: The trucks will be used to pull a Food Trailer and the 32-Foot Utility Trailer that will be used disaster activations, long- duration deployments, and mutual aid requests.
3014.direct_services: These purchases will allow for an essential component of statewide disaster response. Currently, CCSO does not have a dedicated pair of heavy-duty tow vehicles assigned specifically for these task force responsibilities. Relying on shared or repurposed vehicles can delay response times, overload existing fleet assets, and create operational inefficiencies during emergency mobilizations.
3014.outcome: Better response to mutual aid events and events and disasters.

3016.description: The County Road 6 bridge is a functionally obsolete bridge that crosses the Suwannee River between Columbia and Suwannee Counties. The bridge serves as an important route for commerce such as logging and local phosphate industries. Without this crossing, there would be a 36 mile gap between crossings in Fargo, Georgia and White Springs, Florida. The bridge also would allow first responders in mutual aid in the event of wildfires.
3016.purpose: A construction of a new bridge over the Suwannee River with the removal of the current bridge along with engineering, permitting and design.
3016.activities: This funding request will allow Columbia County to replace a functionally obsolete bridge that crosses the Suwannee River between Columbia and Suwannee Counties. Without this crossing, there would be a 36 mile gap between crossings.
3016.direct_services: The bridge is important for industries such as local phosphate mining and logging industries as well as a crossing for emergency response and wildfire response in a rural and underserved area.
3016.outcome: Structural integrity of the new bridge as well as traffic count numbers.

3020.description: To secure the generators needed to provide a safe space for veterans and their families during a climate crisis. This will enable us to offer warm meals, cold drinks, and a place to rest. First responders will also benefit from this project. The generators will sustain our food supplies and allow for proper heating and cooling.
3020.purpose: The goal is to provide shelter, food, and rest for veterans and their families--to include first responders--in the event of hurricanes, and climate crises.
3020.direct_services: Food and shelter and companionship during a time of climate disruption.
3020.population: Veterans and their families--and first responders--and members of the surrounding community if needed.
3020.outcome: A safe space to secure food and shelter.

3022.description: The City of Lake City is requesting funding to replace an aging wastewater lift station. The costs are estimated to be $150,000. This shovel-ready project will improve system reliability, prevent overflows, and help support the City's wastewater network. This would ensure reliability across the City's sewer system, impove capacity allowing for more development, and safeguard environmental and public health.
3022.purpose: The funds will be used to replace one of Lake City's aging wastewater lift stations, ensuring reliable service for the wastewater collection system. The purpose will be to decomission the old units and install more reliable modern versions. The goal will be to ensure reliability in the service area and prevent back-ups, which could affect many homes and businesses.
3022.activities: The activities that will be provided for this project will include the disposal of two old wastewater lift station units and the installation of two new units.
3022.direct_services: The direct service that will be provided to citizens as a result of this project will be continuous and reliable wastewater collection for citizens. This is an essential service that is critical to the health of residents and the quality of the environment.
3022.population: The project will serve the residents, businesses, and visitors of Lake City, particularly those in the direct service areas of the lift stations, including up to 65 homes and 12 businesses. This project will also help support the continuous function of the entire wastewater collection system for Lake City's 12,329 residents.
3022.outcome: The project will improve reliability, prevent back-ups, and increase service capacity for the city's wastewater collection system. The methodology by which this outcome will be measured will be the service life of the units, SCADA data monitoring pressures and quantities, and the operational capacity of the new units.

This shovel-ready project will improve system reliability, prevent overflows, and help support the City's wastewater network. This would ensure reliability across the City's sewer system, impove capacity allowing for more development, and safeguard environmental and public health.

The purpose will be to decomission the old units and install more reliable modern versions. 3023.activities: The activities that will be provided for this project will include the disposal of two old wastewater lift station units and the installation of two new units.
3023.direct_services: The direct service that will be provided to citizens as a result of this project will be continuous and reliable wastewater collection for citizens. This is an essential service that is critical to the health of residents and the quality of the environment.
3023.population: The project will serve the residents, businesses, and visitors of Lake City, particularly those in the direct service areas of the lift stations, including up to 65 homes and 12 businesses. This project will also help support the continuous function of the entire wastewater collection system for Lake City's 12,329 residents.
3023.outcome: The project will improve reliability, prevent back-ups, and increase service capacity for the city's wastewater collection system. The methodology by which this outcome will be measured will be the service life of the units, SCADA data monitoring pressures and quantities, and the operational capacity of the new units.

2715.description: Youth Crisis Center is seeking funding for the purchase of a commercial gas 250kW generator for the residential shelter building and the installation of a new roof on the same building plus the youth clubhouse. The program houses up to 34 youth ages 10-17 who are victims of trafficking, abuse, ungovernable, runaway, truant, and homeless. Youth Crisis Center is also the authorized agency for the state to provide physically secure residential services to court-ordered youth who are adjudicated a CINS (Child in Need of Services). This program serves CINS/FINS youth around the state. Each youth will receive life skills training, mental health therapeutic services, a fully-furnished home, parenting skills and support, educational support and monitoring, employment skills training, transportation as needed, case management, access to meals and proper nutrition classes, and access to child care
2715.purpose: When a power outage occurs, a generator for a youth homeless shelter must be able to provide a secondary source of power to ensure the shelter's operations continue. The generator should be functional and capable of meeting the shelter's power demands during an outage. Youth will be able to remain in the space with continued services, including those youth who are court-ordered and cannot leave the program. The program serves up to 34 youth. Additionally, the roof is aging and in need of replace
2715.activities: The generator will be used to have continuous power for the youth homeless and runaway shelter. The 22,000 square foot space serves youth ages 10-17. Youth receive housing, meals, nursing care, mental health care, academic instruction from Duval County Public Schools, recreational activities, and life skills training. The average length of stay is 12 days. Up to 10 youth can be served who are court-ordered for services up to 120 days and must remain in the physically secure program.
2715.direct_services: The residential program is expected to serve over 500 youth who are homeless, trafficked, ungovernable, victims of abuse, truant, and considered a lockout. Each youth will receive: therapy, housing, meals, academic instruction, life skills classes, nursing services and medication administration and oversight, case management, recreational activities to promote prosocial behavior, referrals post di
2715.population: Youth (clients) ages 10-17 who are homeless, truant, victims of trafficking, ungovernable, and victims of abuse. The youth may be experiencing mental health and physical health concerns, poor academic performance in high school or trade school, at-risk of dropping out of school, economically disadvantaged, at-risk of entering the criminal or dependency system, or have been in the delinquency system. The program can serve 34 clients at any given time with the expected length of stay to be two wee
2715.outcome: To improve youth mental health well-being by an improved Personal Wellbeing Index (PWI-SC) score after discharge/completion of services. Each youth will have stable, safe housing as a deficiency can impair one's overall performance in school and work; improved academic performance as evidenced by grades and attendance through onsite academic instruction and assistance; receive a high school diploma or GED if applicable; aid in the prevention of criminal activity, abuse reports, and homelessness; increase the ability to gain self-sufficiency once 18. This program aims to eliminate criminality due to stability; eliminate possible child abuse by providing parenting skills and mental health care

3027.organization: Girl Scouts of Gateway Council, Inc.
3027.description: The Girl Scout Leadership Center will be a 14,000-square-foot leadership and learning hub in Jacksonville. Funds will support construction of a safe, ADA-accessible facility with hands-on education areas, STEM labs, and flexible community space. The Center will expand year-round programs, interactive learning, and affordable overnight experiences for youth across North Florida, especially low-income girls.
3027.purpose: Funds will support renovation of a 14,000-square-foot Girl Scout Leadership Center in Jacksonville. The Center will serve as a regional community asset providing leadership development, STEM learning, volunteer training, and safe program space for youth and families across North Florida.
3027.activities: The Center will host leadership programs, STEM labs, volunteer trainings, day camps, meetings, overnight experiences, and community events. Funds will make possible the construction and outfitting needed to deliver year- round programs for youth and families.
3027.direct_services: Citizens will gain access to safe, ADA-accessible educational and program spaces, hands-on STEM and leadership activities, volunteer resources, and community gathering areas that support youth development and family engagement.
3027.population: The project will primarily serve girls, including at-risk and economically disadvantaged girls in grade school and high school students. Renovations will accommodate individuals with physical disabilities. The Center will also be open to the public for community programs and events. More than 2,000 individuals are expected to benefit from the facility each year.
3027.outcome: The Center will expand access to youth education, leadership development, and STEM programming. Outcomes include increased program participation, improved educational engagement, safer facilities, and expanded opportunities for low-income and underserved youth across North Florida. Program enrollment, attendance records, badge and skill completions, surveys, and facility usage data.

3028.description: The City of Lake Butler seeks funding to design, permit, and construct a new 200,000-gallon ground storage tank with related sitework, piping, and electrical improvements. The project will provide critical system redundancy and resiliency, ensuring uninterrupted water service during maintenance or emergencies, improving fire-suppression capacity, and supporting key institutions such as the hospital, schools, and the Reception and Medical Center while meeting regulatory and capacity requirements.
3028.purpose: To design, permit, and construct a new 200,000-gallon ground storage tank and related sitework, piping, and electrical improvements to provide system redundancy and resiliency for the City’s potable water system.
3028.activities: Project activities include engineering design, permitting, site preparation, construction of the new storage tank, and installation of associated piping, valves, electrical, and control systems, followed by testing and commissioning.
3028.direct_services: The project will provide reliable, uninterrupted drinking water service and enhanced fire protection for residents, businesses, and critical facilities, ensuring adequate water pressure, storage capacity, and system redundancy during maintenance or emergencies.
3028.population: The project will serve all residents and businesses within the City of Lake Butler and surrounding service area—approximately 2,000 residents and major regional employers including the hospital, Union County School District, and the Reception and Medical Center.
3028.outcome: Benefit: Improved water system reliability, fire-suppression capacity, and compliance with DEP storage and permitting standards. Measurement: Verified through system performance data, fire-flow testing, and DEP operating permit compliance demonstrating continuous service and adequate pressure during operational or emergency events.

3074.description: On September 5, 2024, the Special Facility Construction Committee unanimously determined and ranked the Union County School District project for a news elementary school to replace the current aged facility, first in the amount of $88,557,095. For the 2025-2026 fiscal year, the first year of three years of funding was appropriated to the Union County School District in the amount of $29, 519,032. We are requesting for the 2026-2027 fiscal year that the second year of funding be appropriated in the amount of $29, 519, 032.
3074.purpose: A new Lake Butler Elementary School will be built to replace the current aged facility providing improved education facilities for the students of Union County.
3074.activities: A new Lake Butler Elementary School will be built to replace the current aged facility providing improved education facilities for the students of Union County.
3074.direct_services: Elementary aged students will have a new and safe education facility to meet the needs of the growing community.
3074.population: Public school students between the grade levels of Pre-K through 5th grade in Union County.
3074.outcome: The expected benefit is that a new school will be built to serve the students of the community.

3075.description: Union County requests funding to aid in the completion of construction of a new EMS/ fire station that will provide immediate access to emergency service delivery for the population across the region, specifically targeting the residents in the unincorporated area of west Union County and ultimately county wide in an emergency and outside the county on a mutual aid basis.
3075.purpose: Funding will go towards the construction of a much needed new fire rescue station . The building will house fire rescue staff (EMS and Fire fighters) allowing for the delivery of emergency services and reduce the response time on the west side of the county 24/7/365. this side of the county currently does not have a station and the closest station is located approximately 10 miles away. The project previously received $850,000 in FY 21-22 (SF # 1350/SA 2377A).
3075.activities: The fire station will provide immediate access to emergency service delivery for the population across the region, specifically targeting the residents in the unincorporated area of west Union County and ultimately county wide in an emergency and outside the county on a mutual aid basis.
3075.direct_services: 24-hour a day staffing of EMS/firefighters to respond to calls for service in the region. Currently we staff located at a station in lake butler and in Worthington springs. but with the new facility, we will staff a station in the providence area 24/7.
3075.population: All citizens and border county citizens on a mutual aid basis. more than 15000
3075.outcome: The new facility will mark a significant decrease in response times and as a result enhanced level of service in both fire and medical response The Communications Center tracks response times and will will show an immediate improvement based on the closest apparatus response from the facility.

3054.description: The requested funds will support the expansion of the reuse water system in Lehigh Acres to increase reclaimed water availability for irrigation.This project will reduce potable water demand, support community growth, and promote long- term water resource sustainability in the service area.
3054.purpose: The requested funds will support the expansion of the reuse water system in Lehigh Acres to increase reclaimed water availability for irrigation. This project will reduce potable water demand, support community growth, and promote long- term water resource sustainability in the service area.
3054.activities: Increased reclaimed water availability through construction of reuse water mains supports future residential and commercial development and reduces potable water demand, lowering long term utility costs. Reduction in potable water withdrawals and increased reuse irrigation helps conserve regional freshwater and protect natural ecosystems.
3054.direct_services: Citizens will receive reuse water at their residences or commercial establishments such as golf courses or sod farms will receive reuse water for use in irrigation purposes. Governmental entities will also benefit in use of reuse water for irrigation at parks, ball fields, stadiums or other governmental buildings.
3054.population: All residents and citizens of Lehigh Acres and Lee County will benefit from use of reuse water. Increased reclaimed water availability supports future residential and commercial development and reduces potable water demand, lowering long term utility costs.
3054.outcome: Reducing reliance on groundwater withdrawals helps protect the aquifer from over-extraction and saltwater intrusion. Track the number of new reuse connections and compare annual reclaimed vs. potable water usage in utility reports. Measure annual potable water savings (gallons) and increased reclaimed water usage through utility reporting and compliance documents.

1586.organization: Key West Harry S. Truman Foundation
1586.description: Restoration of state owned object(s) and artifacts on display at the Harry S. Truman Little White House by a professionally recognized conservator facility.
1586.purpose: The mission of the Key West Harry S. Truman Foundation and Little White House Museum is to share history of the American Presidency and preserve and protect the Truman Little White House. We need to continue to protect the Little White House and the historic objects on display inside of the house for future generations to learn about and experience this era in our American democracy.
1586.activities: Professional restoration consultants will be sought, followed by approved activities to achieve restoration with the funds.
1586.direct_services: As a result of the project, objects on display at the Harry S. Truman Little White House will be restored for future generations protection and viewing.
1586.population: The target population consists of visitors, all demographics and backgrounds, who choose to visit the Harry S. Truman Little White House. While adult visitation is our primary age demographic, outreach to all age groups is practiced.
1586.outcome: The expected outcome is identification of objects for restoration by a consultant followed by initiation of restoration.

3049.description: Conversion of up to 300 septic tank sewer systems in the Florida Governmental Utility Authority Lehigh Acres service area to an updated sanitation and sewer treatment system. The project area includes lower-income customers, and additional funding woudl significantly redued the financial burden on the switch to the sewer system from septic tanks.
3049.purpose: Septic tanks will be taken out of service helping to prevent groundwater pollution.
3049.activities: Construction of sewer mains and connection of homes to sewer line for collection and transmission of wastewater to collective sewage treatment plant. Wastewater will receive treatment in excess of that provided by septic tanks. Septic tanks will be taken out of service.
3049.direct_services: Sewage treatment will be provided to citizens minimizing maintenence of septic tank systems, minimizing sewage overflows or issues with septic tank systems during flooding or weather events.
3049.population: Residents of Lehigh Acres. Project will take approximately 300 homes off septic tanks so assuming 4 persons per household, approximatelly 1200 individuals will be served and benefit from the project.
3049.outcome: Lehigh Acres is located within a BMAP. A centralized sewer collection, treatment and effluent disposal system allows for the removal of septic tanks which reduces the nutrient loading on the groundwater and surface water. FGUA will communicate with the water managment district for its sampling results in monitoring ground water nutrient loading and improvement as septic systems are taken offline.

3050.description: Expanding the sewer mains in the south section of Lehigh Acres to provide sewer service to 113 parcels including a new elementary school. Specific goals include increased sewer availability within the Lehigh Acres Utility Service Area, abandonment of septic tanks through connection of residential and commercial parcels to a central sewer system, accommodate growth within Lehigh Acres, and support development along the SR 82 corridor.
3050.purpose: Specific goals include increased sewer availability within the Lehigh Acres Utility Service Area, abandonment of septic tanks through connection of residential and commercial parcels to a central sewer system, accommodate growth within Lehigh Acres, and support development along the SR 82 corridor.
3050.activities: Lehigh Acres is located within a BMAP. A centralized sewer collection, treatment and effluent disposal system allows for the removal of septic tanks which reduces the nutrient loading on the groundwater and surface water. A centralized sewer collection, treatment and effluent disposal system attracts commercial development in areas currently limited with only septic tanks.
3050.direct_services: A centralized sewer collection,treatment and effluent disposal funded by this project project provides a system for improving the treated effluent water quality to meet public access reuse standards, providing for irrigation for home and commercial irrigation use such as parks or golf courses. It will also allow residential homes to switch to the sewer system thus helping prevent groundwater conta
3050.population: Expanding the sewer mains in the south section of Lehigh Acres to provide sewer service to 113 parcels including a new elementary school. Also will serve any commercial properties in the area. With 4 persons per household, it will serve a minimum of 452 Lee County residents.
3050.outcome: The Lehigh Acres sewer utility service area is located within a BMAP. Reduction and removal of septic tanks reduces the nutrient loading on the ground water which ultimately flows into the surface water. Monitoring of ground water nutrient removal by review of watermanagment district sampling in the BMAP area and any Dept. of Health sampling and monitoring of groundwater.

3383.description: The Opera Naples Luciano Pavarotti Foundation Arts Center, the cultural anchor for Collier County Bayshore Gateway Triangle CRA’s Cultural Arts Village PUD, will deliver professional opera productions, youth education, artist residencies, outreach concerts, adult enrichment lectures, museum tours, and interactive exhibits. The new complex's theater will be the permanent home of North America’s only winter opera festival, Opera Naples annual “Festival Under the Stars,” along with the future Theater in the Garden and “Casa Pavarotti” national opera museum. State funds will support critical infrastructure work, including site preparation, permitting, utilities, ADA-accessible pathways and parking—enhancing connectivity to nearby community amenities. Designed to drive economic vitality and celebrate artistic identity, this project further enhances Southwest Florida as a nationally recognized
3383.purpose: State funds will support essential site work including permitting, land preparation, utilities, hardscape, ADA-accessible pathways, and parking preparation. These investments will further the infrastructure of the Opera Naples Luciano Pavarotti Foundation Arts Center, home to Festival Under the Stars, North America's only outdoor winter opera festival, attracting over 5,000 attendees annually. The total $60M project will include the future Theater in the Garden and "Casa Pavarotti" opera museum.
3383.activities: Site preparation for the construction of the Opera Naples Luciano Pavarotti Foundation Arts Center.
3383.direct_services: The Opera Naples Luciano Pavarotti Foundation Arts Center will deliver professional opera productions, the Festival Under the Stars, vocal instruction, youth education, artist residencies, outreach concerts, adult enrichment lectures, museum tours, interactive exhibits, and global music heritage programs for all ages.
3383.population: The Opera Naples Luciano Pavarotti Foundation Arts Center is committed to serving a broad and diverse population, including residents of all ages from Collier and Lee Counties, economically disadvantaged and at-risk youth, older adults, and individuals with disabilities. Currently, Opera Naples annually reaches approximately 7,000 audience members through its professional opera and concert productions, and an additional 3,000 K-12 students through in- school Resident Artist outreach and music ed
3383.outcome: The Opera Naples Luciano Pavarotti Foundation Arts Center will deliver transformative benefits in cultural, educational, economic, and community resilience domains. Expected outcomes include increased access to arts and music education, improved physical and mental health through inclusive performances and accessible green spaces, heightened cultural participation and tourism, job creation and regional economic growth. Methodologies for measuring these outcomes encompass tracking annual attendance figures, ticket sales, program enrollment and student outreach numbers, audience and participant surveys wellness and educational assessment tools, event demographic data, employment records, and p

2997.organization: Harry Chapin Food Bank of Southwest Florida
2997.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2997.description: Harry Chapin Food Bank of Southwest Florida seeks $1,000,000 in state funding to support construction of a new food distribution warehouse in Naples, Collier County. The new facility will expand the food bank’s capacity to serve the growing population of SWFL, ensuring that nutritious food reaches families, seniors, and children facing food insecurity. The Naples warehouse will include expanded dry, refrigerated, and frozen storage, additional loading docks, and energy- efficient systems to support safe, efficient distribution of millions of pounds of food each year through a network of agency partners, schools, and mobile pantries. Food insecurity is a challenge in SWFL and the demand for emergency and supplemental food assistance continues to climb.
2997.purpose: The requested funds will enable construction of a new food distribution warehouse in Naples, Collier County, expanding Harry Chapin Food Bank’s capacity to receive, store, and distribute millions of pounds of food annually through a network of agency partners, schools, senior centers, mobile pantries and food distribution programs. This facility will increase efficiency, improve access to nutritious food, and strengthen the region’s ability to respond to rising food insecurity and disaster-relat
2997.activities: Funds will support all activities related to the construction and outfitting of the new Naples warehouse facility, including site development, building construction, and installation of food storage and distribution systems. Once completed, the facility will enable food collection, storage, sorting, and distribution to agency partners, schools, and mobile pantries serving Southwest Florida residents. The warehouse will also support disaster relief operations, volunteer engagement, and nutrition
2997.direct_services: The direct services provided to citizens by this appropriation project will focus on sourcing, storing, and distributing fresh, perishable food to the community. With the increased capacity, we will be able to source and store more fresh food from local farmers—much of which would otherwise go to waste. By expanding our relationships with local farmers, we can not only provide nutritious food to t
2997.population: The target population served by this project consists of individuals and families experiencing food insecurity in Southwest Florida. Approximately 1 in 6 local residents are expected to go hungry at some point this year, with many facing economic challenges such as cost of living expenses—rent, transportation, child care, medical care, and insurance—that outpace their incomes. Hunger is further exacerbated by personal emergencies or natural disasters. The population most affected includes workin
2997.outcome: This project will enhance the Harry Chapin Food Bank's capacity to serve those experiencing food insecurity in SWFL. By expanding capacity, particularly for fresh and perishable items, and strengthening relationships with local farmers, the project will enable the Food Bank to source, store, and distribute more nutritious food, particularly fresh produce and protein. It will increase food distribution from 45 million pounds to over 80 million pounds annually, while also supporting the local economy. Success will be measured by the increase in pounds of food distributed, tracked through our data collection methods. Ultimately, the project will improve access to nutritious food for vulnerable

3055.description: This appropriation request proposes the rebuild, retrofit, and/or repair of major water control structures owned by the Lehigh Acres Municipal Services Improvement District (LA-MSID), in Lehigh Acres, Lee County Florida. The program will provide greater flood protection and water quality improvement for LA-MSID's Orange River Drainage Basin, as well as upstream and downstream water level sensors to better inform LA-MSID staff on required structure operation during a storm event. The improvements will allow LA-MSID staff to safely and remotely adjust the water control level of the structures from anywhere that an Internet signal is available.
3055.purpose: LA-MSID's water control system is generally modernized. However, there are select structures that require modernization, upgrades, and/or major repairs to better mitigate property loss due to flooding. When a storm approaches LA-MSID, the typical system operation includes lowering structure gates to increase upstream storage capacity. Just before the storm arrives, LA-MSID raises the gates to store water upstream and reduce flood levels downstream. This appropriation proposes modernizing five st
3055.activities: Rebuild existing obsolete broad-crest weirs with modern-style weirs including operable gates, programmed operations, and telemetry. Retrofit existing weirs to add operable gates, programmed operations, and telemetry. Repair a weir that has been rendered unusable due to structural damage. The five weir improvements will work together with LA-MSID greater system's operation to create increased stormwater capability, to better prepare and respond to a major storm event for an area that is in dire n
3055.direct_services: The direct service provided to citizens is increased flood protection for the Orange River Drainage Basin in the Lehigh Acres Municipal Services Improvement District.
3055.population: There are 130,176 target individuals within the entire LA-MSID system, and 65,088 target individuals in the Orange River Drainage Basin who will be directly served or benefited by the project.
3055.outcome: LA-MSID will utilize an integrated computer modeling program (MIKE SHE/MIKE 11), that will verify the effectiveness of the project's food mitigation benefit by measuring the draw-down volume prior to the storm and the real world flow data volume following the storm.

2716.description: This funding request is for the construction of six affordable new homes for low-income families or veterans in the new Coastal Haven development on Mayport Road in Atlantic Beach. Without this assistance, the new homeowners might otherwise be unable to purchase a new home. The homes will be financed with a zero-interest mortgage loan thus keeping monthly payments affordable. The prospective homeowners will be required to contribute a minimum of 300 hours of "sweat equity" in the construction of their home. They will also be required to attend workshops focused on financial literacy and home maintenance.
2716.purpose: The goal of the requested funding is the completion of six affordable new homes in Coastal Haven for low-income families or veterans who might otherwise be unable to purchase a new home. The total buildout of the development will be completed in 5-6 years at a total cost of approximately $10 million. Funds from this appropriation request will only be applied to construction of the first six homes.
2716.activities: These funds will cover the construction costs for six homes in Coastal Haven. At least one of these homes is designated for a veteran. Beaches Habitat's construction staff, supplemented by local volunteers, will construct the homes included in this request. It will be necessary to contract with certified and/or licensed contractors for electrical, plumbing, and HVAC services.
2716.direct_services: Each new home will be sold with a zero-interest mortgage to a low-income individual or family. Mortgage payments will be within the budget capacity of the homeowner. In addition, the homeowner will have the benefit of learning about the responsibilities of home ownership and financial literacy in workshops provided by Beaches Habitat for Humanity.
2716.population: The population served by this project are low-income families whose household incomes meet the <80% of AMI (Area Media Income) requirement. Six low-income families (estimated at 4 family members each) will be new homeowners. There is no income requirement for veterans. Beaches Habitat complies with all Fair Housing laws and federal mortgage regulations.
2716.outcome: The expected outcome at the end of this project will be an increase in the amount of affordable housing available in the Jacksonville Beaches. In addition, the six families that will occupy the homes will have affordable mortgages and a more stable economic future. The new homeowners will have the ability to save with a monthly housing burden that does not exceed 30% of their household income. They will also be required to contribute to a Homeowners Association (HOA) that will provide for continued maintenance expenses of their new homes.

2702.description: Assist Jacksonville, State & Federal Parks in Northeast Florida area to be wellness resources for all individuals - including those with addiction issues, physical, mental, medical, and emotional needs. Implement optimum park adaptations to address existing needs. Attempt to replicate some of the features found at the William J. "Billy Joe" Rish Recreation Area.northeast State Park.
2702.purpose: Assist Jacksonville, State & Federal Parks in the Duval area to be wellness resources for all individuals - including those with addiction issues, physical, mental, medical, and emotional needs. Implement optimum park adaptations to address existing needs. Attempt to replicate some of the features found at the William J. "Billy Joe" Rish Recreation Area.
2702.activities: Provide wheelchair access to ramps and elevated boardwalks over wetlands, provide ADA accessible restrooms, access to potable water, parking and path lighting, provide emergency communications and equipment, provide fencing and gates, and provide signage both inside and outside the parks.
2702.direct_services: Therapeutic Healthy Living programs for individuals with addiction issues, social and emotional needs, physical, medical, and rehabilitation needs, those with occupational/physical therapy needs and the general public.
2702.population: Healthy Living environment conducive to therapeutic wellness for all members of the community and visitors to the area.
