2702.outcome: Increased park utilization and program participation that also help address issues of recovery and wellness for community members. Pre and post surveys will be offered to visitors regarding access quality and programming services.

3258.description: The STARability Foundation requests funding to support program expansion capacity within Phase 1 of our Capital Campaign, which is transforming a 42,000-square-foot facility on a five-acre campus in Naples, Florida, into a regional hub for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD). STARability is a leader in providing innovative programs, including the Trailblazer Academy, which offers community-based skill development focused on eight core life skills that promote social inclusion and independence. Staff assess each participant’s abilities and create individualized plans supporting goals such as employment readiness, personal finance, and self-advocacy. When participants are ready to explore career options, our Vocational Services team provides customized training, coaching, and job placement to address barriers to employment. This investment will help triple ou
3258.purpose: Requested funds will support STARability’s phased expansion into a permanent campus, tripling program capacity as part of a $26M initiative with a renovated 42,000-sq-ft center. Serving as a comprehensive regional hub for Southwest Florida, it will include classrooms, labs, a kitchen, sensory and arts spaces, an event hall, offices, and expanded areas for new programs, supportive housing elements, community partnerships, and long-term sustainability.
3258.activities: Funds will support expansion of full-time Trailblazer Academy and center-based programs, delivering life-skills education, vocational training, community engagement, and job placement with coaching. Added staff capacity and adaptive resources will enable three times more individuals with IDD to develop skills, pursue employment, and achieve greater independence in the new permanent facility.
3258.direct_services: As a Florida Department of Education Vocational Rehabilitation provider, STARability will offer direct services such as individualized job training, career counseling, interview preparation, and on-the-job coaching for citizens with IDD. Funding will increase access to these services, helping more individuals secure and sustain meaningful employment.
3258.population: The population served includes: persons intellectually and/or developmentally disabled, persons physically disabled, persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons. We expect to serve between 400-800 people.
3258.outcome: The expected benefits and outcomes of this project include: improving physical health, improving mental health, enriching cultural experience, improving quality of education, increasing/improving economic activity, creating specific immediate job opportunities, and enhancing specific individual's economic self-sufficiency. The methodology by which these outcomes will be measured include assessing individuals in eight life-skill areas outlined by Virginia Commonwealth University, tracking experiences, tracking employment status from job seeker to placement success, and surveying the target population and caregivers.

3535.description: This project will drive economic growth in Southwest Florida by establishing a welding workforce program that supplies skilled talent to manufacturing, aerospace, and related industries. Funds will provide industry-standard equipment and expert instructors, ensuring adults receive hands-on training and AWS/NCCER certifications. By filling critical workforce gaps and attracting new business investment, the program strengthens regional competitiveness and supports long-term economic development.
3535.purpose: The funds will establish a welding workforce program that develops a pipeline of skilled workers to address critical needs in manufacturing, aerospace, and related industries. By equipping adults with hands-on training and industry certifications, the project enhances the regional workforce, meets employer demand, and fosters sustained economic growth in Southwest Florida.
3535.activities: Funds will provide industry-standard welding equipment and skilled instructors to deliver hands-on training, certification preparation, and workforce development services. Adults will gain the technical skills and credentials needed for immediate entry into high-demand industries, ensuring employers have access to a reliable talent pipeline that supports regional economic growth.
3535.direct_services: The project will deliver direct workforce training services to adults, equipping them with advanced welding skills and industry certifications for immediate employment. Citizens benefit through expanded access to high-wage career opportunities, while employers gain a steady pipeline of skilled workers essential to sustaining and growing Southwest Florida’s economy.
3535.population: The project serves adults, veterans, jobless individuals, and economically disadvantaged persons, training 50–100 annually for high-demand welding careers. By creating a steady pipeline of skilled workers, the program strengthens the regional labor force, helps employers fill critical vacancies, and drives economic growth across Southwest Florida’s manufacturing and aerospace sectors.
3535.outcome: The project will expand Southwest Florida’s skilled workforce by preparing adults for immediate welding careers that support the growth of manufacturing and aerospace industries. Outcomes will be measured by enrollment, completion rates, certifications earned, and job placements, along with employer feedback to confirm the program meets regional workforce and economic development needs.

2154.description: The project expands structured youth tennis, fitness, and character development programs that strengthen public safety and health. Funding provides summer and afterschool instruction, equipment, meals, coach training, and community engagement events, ensuring cost-efficient prevention programming that keeps youth active, supervised, and engaged.
2154.purpose: The requested funds will support the expansion of a youth tennis and wellness program designed to increase physical activity, improve social-emotional skills, and provide safe, structured recreation for children and teens. Funding will be used for certified tennis instruction, equipment, court rentals, transportation, program staffing, and participant support services.
2154.activities: Activities include tennis training sessions, fitness drills, coordinated practice schedules, wellness workshops, mentorship circles, and quarterly family engagement events designed to build skills and healthy habits.
2154.direct_services: Direct services include free tennis instruction, supervised recreation, access to equipment, transportation assistance, wellness education, and one-on-one support from trained coaches and mentors.
2154.population: The program serves 6–17-year-olds in underserved communities, prioritizing Title I schools, with an expected annual reach of 150–200 youth.
2154.outcome: Expected outcomes include increased activity, improved tennis skills, stronger confidence, and better social-emotional development. Measures include attendance, pre/post assessments, surveys, and quarterly coach evaluations.

1659.description: The requested funds will expand access and availability of high-fidelity wraparound (HFW) services to support families with children experiencing a behavioral health crisis. Children facing a crisis often encounter delays between the start of the crisis and the initiation of crisis-response services. These delays are caused by limited access or availability, stigma related to behavioral health issues, and inconsistent “warm hand-offs” across providers. Such delays often result in an increased need for higher-level services, such as emergency room visits, CSU, or DJJ programs. Family peer support with High-Fidelity Wraparound enhances engagement and decreases delays in diagnosis and treatment. HFW is a structured, team-based approach involving families, providers, and natural supports to keep everyone connected and involved in the decision-making. The program provides early intervention t
1659.purpose: The requested funds will support services for families with children aged 12 to 17 who are undergoing a behavioral crisis. Community Care for Families (CCF) helps these children and their families achieve stability, safety, and better emotional well-being. CCF is a partnership between the Florida Center for Early Childhood and NAMI Sarasota and Manatee Counties. The Florida Center offers strong clinical expertise, while NAMI provides extensive experience in peer support. The program will address
1659.activities: An individualized team plan tailored to the child and family includes: Engagement (orientation, crisis stabilization, strengths and needs, engagement), Planning (team plan, crisis plan), Implementation (focused on building trust and logistics, updating the plan as needed), and Transition (transferring skills to youth and family, planning for case closure, and follow-up after graduation). Using HFW, a family or parent peer contacts the family within 24 hours to stabilize the situation, using clin
1659.direct_services: A four-part approach helps youth and families learn how to access resources and seek help from others to overcome their challenges. The program’s components are 1) youth and family prioritize needs, 2) natural supports, 3) integrated planning, 4) self-efficacy. High fidelity wraparound, an evidence-based practice, collaborates with families and youth to develop cohesive, personalized support plans
1659.population: The target population includes families and youth aged 12 to 17 at risk in Sarasota, Manatee, and DeSoto counties. There has been a significant rise in at-risk youth entering out-of-home care due to parental inability to cope or willful abandonment. These youth are facing behavioral health crises, and high-fidelity wraparound services intervene early, ideally before the youth requires more costly care. We expect to serve up to 200 youth and families. Youth may be referred by any individual or or
1659.outcome: Teens in crisis and their families achieve stability, safety, and improved emotional well-being within 12 months. Seventy percent of families will experience these improvements, along with a reduction in needs that hinder functioning and an increase in family strengths. Additional goals include a decrease of five or more points in the life functioning domain score within six months of enrollment. The methodology used is the CANS (Child and Adolescent Needs and Strengths). High-fidelity wraparound benefits include increased permanency and stability, decreased residential restrictiveness, improved behavioral and mental health, better academic and early care outcomes, fewer safety issues, and s

1623.description: The Museum of Contemporary Art North Miami (MOCA) will use requested operating funds to support a full year of high- quality exhibitions, education programs, and community services benefiting residents across Miami-Dade County. As the only major cultural institution in a 25-mile stretch between Miami’s Design District and Fort Lauderdale, MOCA provides reliable, year-round access to professionally produced arts programming for 30,000 people annually. The museum’s 30th anniversary season will feature curated exhibitions, public programs, and free or low-cost art classes that expand cultural access for families, students, and seniors. MOCA’s professional staff and teaching artists deliver consistent, measurable outcomes through workshops, camps, lectures, concerts, community events, and school partnerships. State support will ensure MOCA continues providing broad public benefit, strengthen
1623.purpose: The requested funds will strengthen a key piece of North Miami’s civic infrastructure by supporting MOCA’s role as the city’s primary cultural and educational hub. As an anchor institution in the downtown corridor, MOCA activates the public Plaza shared with City Hall and collaborates with local libraries, schools, and the senior center to deliver year- round, free educational and cultural programs. Funding will help the museum meet growing community demand, support stable operations, and contri
1623.activities: MOCA will provide a full season of exhibitions, public programs, and free or low-cost education services for residents of all ages. Activities include year-round art classes, after-school programs, summer camps, senior workshops, community events on the MOCA Plaza, and partnerships with local schools and libraries. The museum will also maintain extended hours for monthly concerts and public lectures, offer guided tours, and continue producing accessible family programs. Operational support ensur
1623.direct_services: MOCA's galleries will be open to the public five days per week (Weds–Sun), offering four major exhibitions and a 30th anniversary permanent collection presentation. The museum will deliver weekly and monthly education programs serving early childhood (ages 1–5), children (6–12), teens (13–17), and adults, including Sunday Stories, Mini-Makers, Teen Art Force, and MOCA Makers. Seniors will receive
1623.population: MOCA’s target population includes residents of North Miami and Miami-Dade County across all age groups, with a particular focus on families, PreK–12 students, teens, young adults, and seniors who rely on free and low-cost cultural services. All 58,906 residents of the City of North Miami receive free admission to MOCA, ensuring full access to exhibitions, programs, and community events regardless of income. The museum and partners with local schools, libraries, community organizations and the se
1623.outcome: The project will expand access to cultural and educational services while elevating the profile of North Miami and the State of Florida through MOCA’s nationally recognized exhibitions, international press coverage, and significant visitation during Miami Art Week. Funding strengthens a key civic asset that provides measurable community benefit, including youth development outcomes shown in national research such as the Wallace Foundation’s findings on youth arts participation increasing wellbeing and academic engagement. MOCA features internationally lauded artists with roots in the community or region, inspiring youth to pursue creative careers. MOCA will measure impact through attendance

2706.description: CAR-T cell therapy research in treating solid tumors will connect Mayo immunologists studying immune activation with engineers designing closed-loop bioreactors and microfluidic platforms integrated into Zephyr’s biomedical payload bays, allowing precise control of nutrient flow and cell–cell interaction during low-gravity exposure.
2706.purpose: CAR-T cell therapy research in treating solid tumors allowing precise control of nutrient flow and cell–cell interaction during low-gravity exposure.
2706.activities: This project will connect Mayo immunologists studying immune activation with FAMU-FSU College of Engineering researchers designing closed-loop bioreactors and microfluidic platforms integrated into Zephyr's biomedical payload bays, enabling advanced testing and development of next-generation therapies under controlled low-gravity conditions.
2706.direct_services: Potential for developing a new therapy method for treating solid tumors.
2706.population: The potential target population is the entire state of Florida.
2706.outcome: This project has a potential of resulting in the development of the first effective CAR-T cell therapy for solid tumors (e.g., Glioblastoma). No comparative therapy exists at the current time.

2100.description: Alma’s Place is a low-lying piece of Town-owned land that was turned into a mangrove conservation area back in the 1980s. The site connects directly to the Loxahatchee River and is influenced by the tides. Over the years, natural flow in the area has been blocked by built-up sediment and the growth of invasive plants. The Town’s restoration project will clear out those obstructions, restore the land to its original elevations, and improve how water moves through the area. These improvements will help reduce flooding in nearby low-lying neighborhoods. The project will also enhance water quality in the Loxahatchee River and help preserve Alma’s Place as a beautiful natural space where native plants, fish, and wildlife can thrive.
2100.purpose: The intended outcome of the project is to improve drainage and flood protection, restore the conservation area and enhance stormwater quality discharged to the Loxahatchee River.
2100.activities: Remove accumulated soil from the natural drainage channel, replace an existing drainage pipe to restore natural water flow, and clear invasive plants from the mangrove conservation area to preserve its natural beauty and scenic character.
2100.direct_services: This project will help reduce regular flooding, restore the conservation area, and improve the quality of stormwater flowing into the Loxahatchee River.
2100.population: This project will benefit the local communities of Jupiter, Tequesta, and surrounding areas of Palm Beach and Martin Counties, as well as the many visitors who enjoy the Loxahatchee River for recreation, wildlife viewing, and its natural beauty. More than 120,000 people live in the communities along the river and its tributaries. The Loxahatchee River is one of only two federally designated Wild and Scenic Rivers in Florida, highlighting its unique environmental and recreational value.
2100.outcome: This project will help protect the community from flooding while improving the quality of stormwater flowing into the Loxahatchee River. By restoring the drainage system and removing built-up soil, the river will benefit from reduced levels of nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, helping keep the water cleaner and healthier. These improvements are recognized as best practices by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection and will also support the Loxahatchee River’s long-term environmental plan, helping preserve this beautiful, nationally designated Wild and Scenic River for generations to enjoy. The Town of Jupiter, Loxahatchee River District, and FDEP will continue to conduct ro

2148.description: The Alternate A1A (SR 811) roadway was installed with a stormwater outfall pipe with direct discharge into the Loxahatchee River Aquatic Preserve, specifically Sawfish Bay, without treatment. This project would install a stormwater quality treatment structure such as a baffle box, to serve as a primary treatment device, capturing sediment, debris, oils, and other pollutants from roadway runoff, thereby reducing nutrient loading and improving water quality within the Loxahatchee River watershed.
2148.purpose: The funds requested will be used to construct a stormwater treatment system (e.g. baffle box)—at a key stormwater outfall discharging into the Loxahatchee River Aquatic Preserve, specifically Sawfish Bay. The primary goal is to improve water quality by reducing the amount of pollutants, sediments, trash, oils, and nutrients entering the bay from roadway runoff. The project also supports regional efforts to reduce pollutant loads to impaired water bodies under the Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL)
2148.activities: Procurement & Contracting - Conducting bidding processes and contracting qualified construction firms to perform the work. Construction - Furnish and install a baffle box stormwater quality treatment structure and ancillary site work. Project Management & Coordination.
2148.direct_services: Cleaner water enhances public health and safety by reducing exposure to harmful pollutants commonly found in untreated stormwater runoff. Additionally, the project will help preserve the bay’s ecology, supporting biodiversity. The project will directly benefit citizens by improving local water quality in Sawfish Bay, a public natural resource.
2148.population: The target population served by this project includes residents, businesses, and visitors in the Town of Jupiter and surrounding areas of Palm Beach County who rely on the environmental, recreational, and economic benefits of Sawfish Bay, Loxahatchee River, and the adjacent Intracoastal Waterway. It is estimated that over 25,000 individuals will be directly or indirectly served by this project, including approximately 18,000+ residents in the immediate service area of Jupiter and nearby communit
2148.outcome: The primary outcome of this project is improved water quality in the Loxahatchee River Aquatic Preserve, specifically Sawfish Bay, by reducing the volume of pollutants, such as sediment, debris, oils, and nutrients which are directly discharged from roadway runoff. Secondary benefits include enhanced habitat protection for marine life, and greater compliance with local, state, and federal water quality regulations.

2098.description: The Town of Jupiter is partnering with Brightline, the operator of high-speed passenger rail service in Florida, to implement a rail corridor safety fencing project that enhances public safety and prevents unauthorized track access on active rail tracks. This project will install approximately 1,200 linear feet of protective fencing along high-risk sections of the Florida East Coast Railway corridor where trains travel at speeds exceeding 80 mph. These areas have been identified due to their proximity to schools, business parks, pedestrian pathways, and dense residential neighborhoods.
2098.purpose: The requested funds will assist the Town of Jupiter in implementing a rail corridor safety fencing project to ensure that all identified high-risk or vulnerable access points along the Brightline rail corridor are secured to prevent unauthorized access of active rail tracks. The rail safety fencing will be installed in vulnerable areas in close proximity to schools, pedestrian pathways, dense residential areas and business parks, that are not currently covered by Brightline’s ongoing fencing pro
2098.activities: Site Assessment and Engineering Design Coordination with Brightline and Florida East Coast Railway Procurement of Materials and Contracted Services Construction of Rail Safety Fencing Post-Installation Monitoring and Evaluation
2098.direct_services: Reduction in unauthorized pedestrian and vehicle crossings at designated high-risk rail corridors due to safety fencing installation. Enhanced public safety near high-speed rail lines. Support for safe routes to school and community facilities. Reduced rail disruption impact on local commuters.
2098.population: The Town of Jupiter has an estimated population of 63,400 residents. This project is expected to directly serve approximately 3% of the town’s population, or about 1,900 individuals, who live, work, or travel daily within close proximity to the targeted rail segments. The project will primarily serve residents living near the Brightline/FEC rail corridor in the Town of Jupiter, with a specific focus on: Children and families near residential neighborhoods; Pedestrians and cyclists who travel alo
2098.outcome: The primary expected outcome of the project is a measurable reduction in unauthorized access to the railway corridor in high-risk/vulnerable areas. This will result in fewer pedestrian trespassing incidents, lower risk of injuries and fatalities, decreased emergency service calls, decrease in rail disruptions, and improved public perception of safety near rail areas.

2149.description: Replace and modernize aging beach access showers, drains, and water fountains along A1A to improve storm water drainage, enhance water conservation, and reduce roadway flooding and maintenance costs. The project supports the State’s coastal resilience and water quality goals while improving visitor safety and beach access infrastructure.
2149.purpose: Poor drainage at several beachfront showers along A1A (a widely used corridor providing access to some of Jupiter's most popular beaches) has led to flooding and runoff issues into coastal dunes. This plan will replace deteriorating showers to improve drainage to reduce runoff, protect water quality, and enhance drainage functionality. Several beach showers along require replacement due to aging infrastructure, constant exposure to harsh beach conditions, and frequent use.
2149.activities: The project will fund design, engineering, permitting, and construction to replace and modernize aging beach side showers, drains, and water fountains along A1A. These upgrades will improve drainage functionality, enhance water conservation, and provide cleaner, more reliable public amenities that better serve residents and visitors.
2149.direct_services: The project will deliver improved public amenities that enhance the user experience and safety along the A1A beach front corridor. Residents and visitors will benefit from modern, well-functioning facilities that reduce standing water, and ensure dependable access to water and drainage systems.
2149.population: The project will serve residents and visitors who utilize the public beach front corridor along A1A, estimated at more than 500,000 users annually. The improvements will support safe, accessible, and environmentally sustainable amenities for all ages while enhancing the Town’s coastal infrastructure.
2149.outcome: This project will enhance the overall functionality of the drainage system along A1A, while improving stormwater management, reducing flooding, and decreasing runoff issues into coastal dunes. Success will be measured with inspections, confirming proper water flow, and through public feedback, regarding improved visitor experience.

1587.description: The objective of the Florida Heiken Children's Vision Program, a division of Miami Lighthouse for the Blind, is to provide comprehensive eye examinations with dilation and prescription eyeglasses, when required, for eligible children throughout the State of Florida to help them succeed academically and improve their overall quality of life. Services are provided at no cost to the families.
1587.purpose: The goal of the Florida Heiken Children's Vision Program is to assure that all financially disadvantaged schoolchildren have access to a comprehensive eye examination including dilation and glasses, if required, to ensure academic success. Following the Florida Statute which sets standards of care, the Program provides an eye examination with dilation so that underlying medical conditions can be diagnosed and appropriate medical referrals made. Prescription glasses are provided. These services a
1587.activities: In 2010, the Florida Heiken Children's Vision Program was registered with the State of Florida, expanding vision health services to low-income children Statewide. In 2024-2025, leveraging FDOH funding with other private funding, 16,494 low-income schoolchildren received a dilated exam and 10,829 received prescription glasses.
1587.direct_services: With current year Florida Department of Health funding our Florida Heiken Children’s Vision Program will continue its eye wellness program Statewide and will provide 6,900 comprehensive diagnostic eye examinations and prescription eyeglasses to disadvantaged children at no cost to the child. Replacement glasses are provided under warranty for 6 months to all eligible students as well.
1587.population: Our Florida Heiken Program serves the economically disadvantaged, at-risk youth, homeless, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, preschool students, grade school students and high school students.
1587.outcome: Based on research funded by the Health Foundation of South Florida, 77% of the Florida Heiken Children's Vision Program participant's parents who responded reported academic improvement after their children received eyeglasses from our eye wellness program at their school. The Heiken Program has developed a Best Practices approach for the delivery of eye care to uninsured schoolchildren.

3084.description: The County's Multi-Agency warehouse will house supplies that support the County's efforts to maintain robust responses to public safety needs. The warehouse will reduce operating costs and protect materials and vehicles associated with the County's first responders.
3084.purpose: The purpose of the funds requested is to construct a multi-agency warehouse in Clay County to house crucial public safety-related supplies and equipment, such as PPE. The warehouse will protect County assets associated with our First Responders, as well as reduce operating costs.
3084.activities: Equipment housed in the warehouse will be utilized to serve public safety needs by organizations such as Clay County Fire Rescue and Clay County Sheriff's Office.
3084.direct_services: County public safety and emergency personnel will use equipment in the warehouse to support community members in various emergency/public safety scenarios.
3084.population: The general population in Clay County is the target population served by this project (236,760).
3084.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is safer and more efficient storage of County equipment that is used to serve the public. This outcome will be measured by the efficiency of the organization and the availability of necessary equipment.

1630.description: Miami Lighthouse Academy, LLC provides services for students who are Blind/Visually Impaired. The Academy provides services for Miami-Dade County Public School Students from K-3rd grade. To qualify to be in the school, students must be legally blind, have peripheral field loss, or have a neurological visual impairment inhibiting vision. The services provided on sight are standard curriculum instruction, braille instruction, assistive technology instruction, expanded core curriculum instruction, and low vision accommodations (such as large print, screen reader technology). The instruction includes teachers of the visually impaired, O & M Specialist, ESE certified teachers, Occupational Therapist, Physical Therapist, and Speech Therapist.
1630.purpose: The Miami Lighthouse Academy will utilize the requested funds, to provide additional services and materials for Kinder-3rd grade students who are blind/visually impaired to be given the expansive supports needed to adapt, modify, and be provided access to the general education curriculum and activities of daily living skills.
1630.activities: Providing educational opportunities for students with visual impairments requires an explicit hands-on approach that implements materials and requires key support personnel. Services include: Direct on site services by Teachers of the Visually Impaired which include braille instruction, low vision adaptations, blind specific curriculum (expanded core curriculum) instruction.
1630.direct_services: Miami Lighthouse for the Blind- in collaboration with Miami-Dade County Public Schools - offers a learning environment for kindergarten, first, second and third grade blind and visually impaired students. Miami Lighthouse is the first vision rehabilitation educational institution using the State of Florida Standards and Benchmarks for Excellent Student Thinking (BEST).
1630.population: Grade school students that are blind or visually impaired, persons with poor physical health, developmentally disabled, physically disabled.
1630.outcome: The Miami Lighthouse Academy provides services for students who are Blind/Visually Impaired who live within Miami- Dade County, Florida. The academy provides services for Miami-Dade County Public School Students who are visually impaired from K-3rd grade.

3108.description: Construction of a fully-enclosed high service water pumping station with redundant controls and power. Goals include improved reliability in daily operations and increased resilience against both natural disasters and man-based threats. A risk and resiliency analysis performed in 2020 on the City's water supply, as mandated in the federal America's Water Infrastructure Act of 2018 law, isolated threat-asset pairings for criticality and economic impacts. This pumping station was one of two highest risk assets due to the long duration and severity of water loss should a threat occur.
3108.purpose: The goal is to provide a more reliable system for the City's eastern service area, specifically to provide for immediate needs in the event of the loss of our eastern supply input from Bay County. The overall project would provide additional capacity and reliability to maintain system pressure. In the event of a natural or man-made disaster, the City's ability to maintain a safe drinking supply and provide for sanitary needs would be significantly enhanced.
3108.activities: Reliable service pressure is critical to provide safe drinking water, to provide water suitable for personal hygiene, and to ensure that fire flows are adequate for the protection of property. The improved level of service would have a direct impact on the flows available to Navy Support Activity (NSA) Panama City which is located in the eastern portion of the City's service area in close proximity to the proposed expansion.
3108.direct_services: All users of the eastern portion of the system will receive a direct benefit due to the increased availability of water for drinking, hygiene, and fire protection. They will also benefit from a potential reduction in precautionary boil water protocols. Additionally, a more secure water supply with a higher resistance to contamination reduces system vulnerability and provides citizens with greater
3108.population: Users on the eastern side of the City's system receive the primary benefit. Panama City Beach's utilities serves a population comprised of an estimated 55,000 permanent residents and equivalent tourist population of 52,685 for a total of 107,685. It is estimated that the target population served by this project is 53,800 persons.
3108.outcome: Improved minimum pressures and supply reserves during peak demand periods will be measured by a review of actual system operating pressures reported via the City's supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system. The general consumer confidence survey will reflect the community's response to the expansion. Various revenue streams will be analyzed to determine the impact on development in the service area which should benefit from the improved service capabilities.

1628.organization: Amigos Together for Kids, Inc. d/b/a Amigos
1628.description: Requested funds will be utilized to implement and expand the Amigos LEAD (Learning, Enrichment & Academic Development) Program, a comprehensive, high-quality after-school and summer initiative designed to provide essential academic support and enrichment opportunities for children and youth, including students with disabilities. This program aims to create a safe, engaging environment where participants can thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. The program serves up to 200 students in grades K-5 during the academic year, offering activities tailored to their developmental needs. These activities will include academic tutoring, STEM-based projects, arts and cultural exploration, and social-emotional learning opportunities. A key feature of the program is its incorporation of youth voice and choice, empowering students to actively participate in their learning experiences. Summer
1628.purpose: Funds will be used to achieve the goal of expanding and enhancing the Amigos LEAD (Learning, Enrichment & Academic Development) Program, a free, high-quality after-school and summer program designed to address educational disparities and provide meaningful enrichment opportunities for underserved children and youth. Specifically, the funds will support the following purposes: 1. Increase Access: Serve 200 students in grades K-5 during the school year and 60 students in grades K-8 during the summ
1628.activities: 200 students during the school year (K-5) and 60 students during summer (K-8) will be provided with homework assistance (school year only), differentiated literacy instruction (DLI) (school year only), field trips, STEM (Coding, Engineering, Cooking & Gardening), Sports (Flag Football, Soccer, Basketball), Art (Visual Art, Theater, Dance), Service Learning Projects. Program is free to participants.
1628.direct_services: The Amigos LEAD After School Program is dedicated to providing a safe, supportive, and enriching environment for children and youth during their out-of-school hours. The program encompasses a wide range of activities designed to promote academic growth, social development, and creative expression. The program's diverse offerings are aimed at catering to individual interests and needs, ensuring tha
1628.population: 200 students during the school year (K-5) and 60 during summer (K-8) in low income neighborhoods of Little Havana, Allapattah and surrounding areas.
1628.outcome: Assessments: • The physical fitness level of students participating in sports enrichment is gauged using the Progressive Aerobic Cardiovascular Endurance Run (PACER) test. • Literacy levels are assessed using the Oral Reading Fluency (ORF) and the Maze assessments. • The qualitative assessment of enrichments is conducted through showcases, performances, and portfolios, allowing students to demonstrate their learning and creative growth.

1822.description: The project entails drainage improvements to sub-basin U35-S, the fourth highest ranked project per the Village's Stormwater Master Plan. The project is approximately 2,700 feet long and runs along SW 112 Street and SW 72 Avenue. It consists of installing approximately 18 inlets, 12 manholes, three control structures, 1,800 linear feet of solid pipe, and 1,500 linear feet of french drain.
1822.purpose: The Stormwater Improvement Project addresses water retention challenges, the impacts of sea level rising, and an aging drainage system causing erosion and inadequate capacity, causing higher storm flooding.
1822.activities: The project entails drainage improvements to sub-basin U35-S as studied in the Village's Stormwater Master Plan.
1822.direct_services: This project will reduce the number of repetitive loss claims and documented home flooding.
1822.population: It will serve the residents of the Village of Pinecrest along sub basin U35-S and the nearby area.
1822.outcome: This project will improve the drainage/water retention in the affected area, reducing the number of claims, damage to homes, environmental impacts, and the safety of residents directly and indirectly affected. Additionally, this project will mitigate the damage after a storm event. The methodology that will be used to measure the outcome is the number of homes without flooding, number of repetitive losses in the area, and flood volume reduction.

2079.description: Purchase of six new modular classrooms to replace current modulars which are outdated and in urgent need of renovation. By investing in new classrooms, school can better support both students and teachers, leading to higher academic achievement and overall educational success.
2079.purpose: New classrooms can significantly enhance the quality of education by providing a safe, comfortable, and engaging learning environment tailored to modern teaching methods. Upgraded facilities with technology-equipped classrooms enable interactive and personalized learning, while flexible, well-designed spaces support collaboration, hands-on activities, and specialized instruction. Additionally, classrooms that foster collaboration and inclusivity help create a sense of belonging, reducing feeling
2079.activities: These funds will help provide 6 updated elementary classrooms.
2079.direct_services: This project will provide Elementary Classes to students in Miami Dade County.
2079.population: The target population consists of approximately 101–200 elementary students in Miami-Dade County each year
2079.outcome: - Classrooms will have updated technology such as smart boards. - Classrooms will have space for collaborate learning and hands on activities. - Classrooms will be designed and constructed to meet the latest safety codes and regulations, ensuring a secure and supportive learning environment for all students. - The classroom environment will be thoughtfully designed to foster collaboration, encouraging interactive and engaging learning experiences that are inclusive of all students.

2156.description: To improve senior health, social engagement, and accessibility in Orlando. Funds will support fitness classes, enrichment trips, sports leagues, and workshops, reducing healthcare costs and enhancing well-being. Transportation assistance ensures mobility-impaired seniors can participate. SEWP aligns with Florida’s public health goals, lowering Medicaid costs, fostering community engagement, and boosting the local economy.
2156.purpose: The Senior Enrichment and Wellness Program (SEWP) will enhance senior health, social engagement, and accessibility by funding fitness classes, enrichment trips, sports leagues, and workshops on technology, finance, and arts. Transportation assistance ensures participation, reducing isolation, healthcare costs, and dependency on Medicaid, while promoting active aging and community involvement.
2156.activities: The Senior Enrichment and Wellness Program (SEWP) offers activities that promote senior health, connection, and well-being. Monthly trips provide cultural and recreational experiences, while weekly wellness classes like yoga, tai chi, and strength training support physical fitness. Senior sports leagues and workshops on technology, finance, and the arts foster active living and lifelong learning. Door-to-door transportation ensures accessibility, helping reduce isolation, encourage active aging,
2156.direct_services: The Senior Enrichment and Wellness Program (SEWP) will provide direct services that enhance senior health, mobility, and social engagement. These include monthly enrichment trips to cultural and recreational sites, weekly fitness classes such as yoga and strength training, and senior sports leagues like pickleball and bocce. Additionally, social workshops on technology, financial literacy, and cre
2156.outcome: The Senior Enrichment and Wellness Program (SEWP) strengthens seniors’ physical health, mental well-being, cultural engagement, and economic empowerment in Orlando. Progress will be measured through health and wellness surveys, attendance tracking, and participant feedback. Data from pre- and post-program assessments, quarterly evaluations, and workshop follow-ups will track improvements in mobility, stress, social connection, and financial confidence. These measures ensure SEWP effectively enhances well-being, fosters engagement, and long term wellness for older adults.

3111.description: Calhoun Liberty Hospital (CLH) serves one of Florida’s most underserved rural regions and was destroyed by Hurricane Michael in 2018. Nearly $45 million in federal, state, and local investment has rebuilt a new 50,000 sq. ft. hospital that reopened in 2025, restoring essential emergency and outpatient services. However, due to the cost of construction, only 8 of 24 planned inpatient beds were included. With the hospital now open and operating at full capacity, this lack of space, forces patients to leave the community and physicians they trust when there are no beds available. This request funds additional inpatient units to restore the hospital’s full capacity as a Rural Critical Access Facility, providing 16 new rooms for rehabilitation, observation, and specialty care—relieving regional strain and completing CLH’s recovery.
3111.purpose: To increase inpatient capacity to its pre-storm 24-bed volume, meet growing healthcare needs by allowing 40% more patients to receive care locally rather than being transferred 45-60 miles to urban hospitals, and ensure operational resilience in one of Florida’s most medically underserved regions.
3111.activities: Construction of inpatient rooms to provide immediate surge capacity for rehabilitation, observation, and specialty care. The infrastructure will be connected to existing hospital utilities and designed for long-term flexibility. The expansion will allow for direct admission from the emergency room where medical care is being preformed. These patients are currently being required to transport to a territory facility due to bed capacities restraints. Increased inpatient beds will allow for additio
3111.direct_services: Enhancement and expansion of services as stated above will improve healthcare accessibility and equity across the region. These will include shorter wait times for a bed/room for those being admitted. Additionally, there will be a reduction in transfers/travel to other hospitals, which will reduce the strain on facilities in Panama City and Tallahassee as well. Specialty care and rehabilitation se
3111.population: The composition of the area consists of multiple socioeconomic factors and challenges found in its rural population, such as 18.9% of the population over the age of 65, 20.3% of individuals living in poverty, and a median household income of $38,568. As with most rural counties, access to healthcare is one of the primary challenges that further compounds these problems. Existing healthcare resources in Calhoun and Liberty County are limited due to capacity issues. This expansion directly address
3111.outcome: Expected Benefit / Outcome • Increased inpatient capacity from 8 to 25 beds. • Capacity available for surge events or mobile specialty use. • Reduction in emergency transfers by 25%. • Enhanced readiness for disaster response and community resilience. Methodology Monthly census, transfer rates, and emergency department diversion metrics will be tracked and reported to the Department of Commerce and the Florida Senate Appropriations Committee.

1979.description: This project will remove and replace outdated tot lot equipment with a new, ADA-compliant playground featuring shaded areas, turf surfacing, and environmentally safe materials. In addition, the adjoining trail will be renovated with new surfacing and ADA-accessible pathways, ensuring safe walking and exercise opportunities for children, caregivers, and seniors. Together, these improvements will enhance safety, accessibility, and recreation. Budget Estimate: $300,000
1979.purpose: To eliminate unsafe equipment and trail hazards by delivering a modern, ADA-compliant playground and walking path. The project will improve child safety, reduce risks of falls and heat exposure, and provide seniors and families with a secure, accessible space for play and exercise.
1979.activities: Activities include removing unsafe playground equipment, disposing of hazardous materials, installing ADA-compliant play structures with shaded areas and turf, and resurfacing the trail for accessibility and safety. These improvements will support programming such as youth playgroups, family activity days, and senior walking clubs, providing safe, structured opportunities for recreation and wellness.
1979.direct_services: Citizens will gain direct access to a safe, ADA-compliant playground and walking trail. Children will benefit from modern, hazard-free play areas, while seniors and families will enjoy shaded, accessible trails that support walking clubs, wellness activities, and intergenerational recreation.
1979.population: The project will serve children ages 1–12, their families, and seniors who use the park for recreation and wellness. The renovated playground and trail will especially benefit children with disabilities and older adults who need safe, accessible spaces for mobility and exercise. Together, these improvements are expected to serve 12,000+ visitors annually, based on park attendance and program participation.
1979.outcome: The project will create a safe, ADA-compliant playground and trail that eliminate hazardous equipment and uneven surfaces. Benefits include reduced risks of injuries and heat exposure, improved accessibility for children and seniors, and expanded opportunities for family recreation, wellness programs, and intergenerational use.

2394.description: The City of North Miami's (City) current network infrastructure requires an overhaul. Outdated physical equipment potentially leaves the City exposed to further security risks. The City has already taken steps to remediate some of these issues by upgrading several systems and software applications to the tune of $415,000. The remaining infrastructure upgrades will allow the City to better take advantage of new technologies and support stakeholders in the community and beyond from multiple locations. The scope of this project spans not only multiple buildings but also several locations. The remaining cost of this project is estimated to be at $700,000.
2394.purpose: The City of North Miami was the victim of a targeted cyber security incident in August of 2024. Unfortunately, outdated physical equipment and security measures left the City exposed. Below is a brief summary of the Cyber Incident: July 2024, Bad actors began surveilling and testing network access and resiliency. August 2024 a full scale breach had taken place. Once the breach was discovered, remediation efforts began immediately. By November 2024, most City systems had been restored and operati
2394.activities: These upgrades will allow for more constituent outreach at multiple locations such as secure payments,and ensuring that secure access to user and organizational data. Improved network access and write speeds and more reliable updates to public services such as WiFi for community members.
2394.direct_services: Updated facilities able to support new technological endeavors such as community Compter Labs, WiFi Service throughout several popular corridors such as the 'Downtown' area and more.
2394.population: Constituents and Stakeholders of the City including staff, elected officials and the public. The City has a population slightly over 60,000 people all of whom are potential benefactors of these upgrades.
2394.outcome: A more robust and resilient data infrastructure allownig the City to more effectively support its constituents.

3112.description: Calhoun County School District is requesting funding for restoration of the track on the Blountstown High School Campus (BHS). The track was built in 2010 and has had some damage as a result of Hurricane Michael. We had extensive damage to that campus and the surrounding grounds of the school. The perimeter fence was almost completely destroyed by trees falling on the fence. The track had minimal damage from the debris, however the equipment that was used to remove debris from the grounds did cause some damage. The track is still usable, but has many significant cracks and some holes that were created by the clean-up. The grounds are currently used for the BHS Track Team to practice and the PE classes housed at the school. Hurricane Michael also required us to permanently combined Blountstown Middle School (BMS) and Blountstown High School on the BHS campus.
3112.purpose: The track at BHS will be repaired and returned to a condition that PE classes (including handicapped) can better use the facility. BHS will be able to hold meets at their home field instead of having to travel to every meet.
3112.activities: Daily PE classes will be better served by the restoration and the school will be able to hold meets on their own field.
3112.direct_services: Families that have students that compete would have more access/ability to attend track meets. The school would be more able to utilize the facility for PE classes.
3112.population: 630 students that attend Blountstown High School presently and all future BHS students. The community would also benefit from the accessibility from track meets that would be held on the BHS field.
3112.outcome: Having the BHS track restored to full use by the school for its intended purpose.

3115.description: The community center in the Town of Altha was completely destroyed during Hurricane Michael in 2018. These funds would greatly benefit the Town by providing the resources needed to complete construction of the new community center. A new community center would not only provide a central location to host various events, but would also serve as an emergency resource center during/after natural disasters. With the latest hurricane vastly impacting our neighboring communities it has become even more important to provide a valuable emergency resource for this community.
3115.purpose: The goal for this project is to give the Town of Altha a community center that they can be proud of and provide a building that is suitable for the needs of the citizens. The CDBG funds that Altha received for the reconstruction of the community center are extremely beneficial but with the ever escalating inflation of construction costs and the restrictions of how CDBG funds can be used, supplemental funding is absolutely critical to provide Altha with a quality community center.
3115.activities: These funds will help with the enhancement of the community center building when it is built with CDBG funds.
3115.direct_services: The Altha citizens do not currently have a community center. This will help provide them with a building to host school events, Boys and Girls Scouts, Voting Center, Council Meetings, Reunions, Weddings, Birthday parties, fundraisers, and a place to help coordinate disaster recovery efforts.
3115.population: The target population is the Town of Altha, over 500 citizens and all other visitors that will use the community center.
3115.outcome: The community center will allow the community to be united with events held to bring them closer together and interact with one another.

2395.description: In 2025, the City Updated its Stormwater Master Plan. One of the short term drainage improvement projects identified is NE 2nd Avenue Court from 121 Street to 135 Street. The primary objective is to alleviate neighborhood flooding conditions from storms up to and including the 5-year storm. The consultant recommends installation of flap gates on the 12 existing outfalls.
2395.purpose: Installation of the infrastructure necessary to address rainwater up to the 5-year storm.
2395.activities: Funds will be used for permitting, materials and labor required for installation of flap gates on existing outfalls, restoration of roadways and swales and Construction Engineering Inspections.
2395.direct_services: Stormwater infrastructure will increase the overall water storage capacity of the basin and help alleviate neighborhood flooding from 3-year and 5-year storms.
2395.population: NE 2 Avenue is the primary access road for approximately 100 single-family houses and serves approximately 400 individuals.
2395.outcome: The project will help alleviate neighborhood flooding from 3-year and 5-year storms. Staff will monitor future storms and measure the impact of major rain events on the neighborhood.

3423.description: The City has issues with excessive inflow and infiltration. Flows at the WWTP increase drastically during wet weather and several lift stations can become overburdened. Several years ago, the City inspected their gravity sewer collection system and found deficiencies to address; however, the costs for implementing these improvements have been restrictive. The City needs financial assistance to bring these necessary improvements to fruition.
3423.purpose: This project will replace or rehabilitate aged infrastructure to prevent stormwater runoff (inflow) and groundwater intrusion (infiltration) from entering the sewer collection system. This will reduce run times at pumping stations, decrease the flow to the wastewater treatment facility, and reduce the likelihood of sewer overflow in the collection system. This will save the City funds for increased operating expenses to pump and treat stormwater as well as attempt to prevent hazardous conditions
3423.activities: The City will procure engineering services for design of the improvements. The consultant will develop plans and specifications that will guide a contractor as they construct the necessary repairs.
3423.direct_services: This project will provide a safer and more reliable sewer system. Operating costs and hazardous situations will be reduced, benefiting the community.
3423.population: This project will serve the northeast quadrant of the City of Blountstown.
3423.outcome: This project will reduce inflow and infiltration (I&I) in the wastewater collection system. This will reduce operating costs and help prevent hazardous overflow conditions in the collection system. The outcome can be measured by the reduction in operating costs and the reduction in overflows.

3086.description: Replacement of 1,200 LF of undersized stormwater pipe, inlets and curbing/roadway as applicable. The pipe is under- sized metal that is prone to failure. The area serves the Clay County Public Works Facility, to which access is critical in the event of a disaster.
3086.purpose: Provide for adequate floodplain management, protect homes, property and provide for personal security during and after a disaster. Protect business activities following a disaster to maintain emergency supplies, economic strength and employment; Protect private and public support systems(infrastructure)during and after a disaster.
3086.activities: Provide for adequate floodplain management, protect homes, property and provide for personal security during and after a disaster. Protect business activities following a disaster to maintain emergency supplies, economic strength and employment; Protect private and public support systems(infrastructure)during and after a disaster.
3086.direct_services: Provide for adequate floodplain management, protect homes, property and provide for personal security during and after a disaster. Protect business activities following a disaster to maintain emergency supplies, economic strength and employment; Protect private and public support systems(infrastructure)during and after a disaster.
3086.population: Governmental, Commercial and largely Residential beneficiaries. The impact will be over 800 properties.
3086.outcome: Flood Mitigation is the outcome. Tracking property claims will be the indication of success of the project.

3087.description: A 3.6 mile leg of the NE FL Trail System that will provide a multi-use trail connecting Spring Park to new Shands Bridge Trail. Approximately half (1/2) a mile of this trail will be constructed over the waters of the St. Johns River. The remaining portions will be constructed along the shoreline. This multi-year project ask includes funding for design, permitting and construction. This project is part of the NE FL Regional Trails Plan as well as the Green Cove Springs Mobility Plan.
3087.purpose: This project will provide recreational opportunities for Citizens as well as a chance to improve their health and well- being. This trail will provide a link to nearby walking, biking, hiking, fishing, equestrian, camping and other recreational activities as part of a regional trails network.
3087.activities: Citizens will be able to walk, bike, and fish directly along this leg of the regional trail network.
3087.direct_services: Citizens will be able to walk, bike, and fish directly along this leg of the regional trail network.
3087.population: The Target Population ia all ages who are looking for opportunities for varying degrees of physical and recreational outdoor activities. 20,000 Plus
3087.outcome: Increased opportunity for exercise, biking, walking, jogging and fishing along the trail. A nature walk along the trail. Also will connect two commercial cores of economic activity with future plans for Reynolds Park. Tracking the utilization of the trail.

1620.organization: A New Start Financial & Social Services
1620.description: For the past three years, our work has strengthened outcomes for justice involved youth and adults by closing mental health and social work gaps, building career skills, and equipping parents with vital support resources. We teach accountability and core values while providing ongoing mentorship to reduce recidivism and help youth succeed. By partnering with DJJ, we strive to enhance public safety by lowering re-offense rates, encouraging safer choices, and supporting stronger community reintegration.
1620.purpose: Our goals are to: 1) Reduce recidivism 2) Promote personal growth 3) Strengthen community safety through moral education, peer mentorship, counseling, and career development linkages, the program transforms confinement into a classroom of change. Our target population is youth between the ages of 10 and 17, at risk youth, and incarcerated adults (previous and present).
1620.activities: These funds will support program operations delivered by our multidisciplinary team of psychologists, social workers, educators, and other specialists to provide mental health care, parent training, career development, and rapport- building activities. They will also strengthen our referral coordination, employment collaborations, and seamless support from jail to probation and beyond.
1620.direct_services: With this funding, we will provide pro bono, comprehensive support to justice involved youth and adults. Services include counseling, substance-abuse support, parental skills training, and one-on-one mentorship. Youth will receive real-world career preparation, opportunities to build trust through sports and other activities, and direct help accessing resources essential to their success.
1620.population: Our target population is youth between the ages of 10 and 17, at risk youth, and incarcerated adults (previous and present).
1620.outcome: Proposed Performance Measure: 70 % of program participants shall achieve or maintain a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher, or will show an increase in their cumulative grade point average, from the first semester or previous year. Proposed Measurement Tool: Report Cards, School Records, homework completed, and teacher assessments Proposed Frequency of Data Collection: Weekly, monthly, and quarterly

2671.description: Funds will expand Bloom Lab, a free after-school agriculture, arts, and entrepreneurship program for under-served youth in Jacksonville’s North Springfield neighborhood. Funding will increase capacity, enhance curriculum, support staff, supplies, and transportation, and grow student-led micro-enterprise. The goal is to build youth skills, food security, creativity, and workforce readiness while strengthening community resilience.
2671.purpose: The North Florida Agriculture and Arts Program will utilize Jacksonville's Phoenix Arts & Innovation District in the Springfield neighborhood in Jacksonville as a community center to provide an agricultural, arts and entrepreneurship training after school program. This after-school program addresses critical challenges facing Jacksonville's under- served youth and will provide a space for students to learn new hands-on skills in agriculture and the arts.
2671.activities: The program serves as a comprehensive after school youth development initiative with three core components: agricultural education and training, arts education, and community market integration. This program will provide after school services for under-served youth in and around the Springfield neighborhood in Jacksonville.
2671.direct_services: Services to be provided include hands-on farming experience, business skills development, digital media and visual arts training, youth-led farmers market operations and business mentorship. This program will complement the nearly $15 million in private and local investment in revitalizing the area and bringing business innovation, arts and culture to this community in Jacksonville.
2671.population: Economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, grade school students, and high school students. Approximately 201-400 expected to be served.
2671.outcome: This project supports under-served youth by enhancing mental health, cultural enrichment, agricultural education, and hands-on skill development. Participants will engage in after-school programs focused on farming, business, and the arts, fostering personal growth and career readiness. Success will be measured through participant retention, periodic wellness assessments, multimedia content creation, farm production tracking, and student progress logs. Partnerships with local organizations and speaker series will further expand learning opportunities and professional development.

3123.description: With the relocation of our school board offices to 307 West North Ave. Bonifay, FL, we have separated our transportation department away from one location. We would like to be able to move the transportation department to our new location also. This would allow for our entire school board operations to be housed at one location. This would also allow us to modernize our building and equipment which is far below standards at this time. We would be able to get all of our fueling stations up to current DEP standards also. We would be able to get rid of an extra property and all of the monetary confines that come with owning commercial property. This move would allow us to save money for our county which ion turn frees up money for the students of Holmes County.
3123.purpose: Having all HDSB operations on one property thus saving money on property and power and sewage and all other expenditures that go along with commercial property. There will be a safer and up to date facility for our transportation department to work at. All DEP standards will be meet with a new facility.
3123.activities: A better work environment for the transportation department. New equipment that will allow for better maintenance of our bus and car fleet.
3123.direct_services: Better maintained buses for the students of Holmes County
3123.population: Directly this project will serve our County offices which is about 30 people but indirectly it will serve all of Holmes County who's children ride buses.
3123.outcome: The expected benefit of this project will be cost savings for the district by having less property to maintain and pay for. Also the electric and sewage savings that are monthly. Being able to take better care of our buses which is a massive investment for us will also be a benefit. We will see these benefits through lower bills and buses lasting for a longer period of time.

3124.description: This is a special facilities project for a new PK-12 school in Ponce De Leon. This project has been through all DOE facilities vetting and has been ranked to be on the special facilities list of projects this year. This is the first time that this form has been asked to be filled out for a special facilities project. The requested amount is #$77,000,000, but the state normally funds these projects over a 3 year period.
3124.purpose: A new updated education facility for the Ponce De Leon community
3124.activities: All activities and services associated with a school will be provided.
3124.direct_services: Education of the children in the community. It will also be used for community events.
3124.population: The children of Holmes County. It will be built for 750 students.
3124.outcome: The enhancement of the education of the children of the Ponce De Leon community. This can be measured through graduations and state testing scores.

2896.description: The Saturday Shoppes Vendor Academy is an interactive program designed to educate small business owners. Phase one covers business fundamentals like social media marketing, e-commerce scaling, and international wholesale, while phase two is on site, at an event and focuses on income generation at markets and festivals, including booth displays, signage, and payment processing. To date, 86 vendors have graduated, with 4 opening brick and mortar stores and 2 transitioning to mobile boutiques. Graduates report and average revenue increase of 74%. The Everyday Shoppes retail academy is a year- long program for graduating and emerging businesses, offering hands on retail experience in our mall retail location. The curriculum focuses on sales strategies, inventory management, visual merchandising, UPC codes, and FDA compliance. Participants benefit from workshops, practical simulations, and me
2896.purpose: The primary objective of this funding is to broaden the reach and impact of Saturday Shoppes and Everyday Shoppes beyond the Tampa bay area enabling us to support a more diverse range of small businesses and vendors. By extending our services to additional zip codes, we aim to empower more entrepreneurs, stimulate economic growth in underserved areas, and offer a wider variety of unique shopping experiences to a larger customer base. This expansion will create new opportunities for local vendors
2896.activities: The funds will support the continued development of the retail space, provide assistance to small businesses, and offer training through the Vendor and Retail Academy. Services include mentorship, workshops on product development, branding, UPC codes and FDA approval, as well as resources for marketing, inventory management, and business operations.
2896.direct_services: Everyday Shoppes include providing Floridian entrepreneurs with retail space to showcase and sell their products. In 2024, all Vendor and Retail Academy participants saw their annual revenue increase by an average of 52%.
2896.population: The target audience for Saturday Shoppes includes emerging entrepreneurs, artisans, and small business owners from diverse and underrepresented backgrounds, such as minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses.
2896.outcome: Saturday Shoppes and Everyday Shoppes offer access to unique, locally-made products, supporting small businesses not found in larger stores. By shopping and participating, civilians contribute to economic growth, create job opportunities, and support underserved areas. The Vendor Academy equips aspiring entrepreneurs with the skills needed to start and grow their businesses. Thriving local businesses help revitalize neighborhoods, improving the overall quality of life. Vendor revenue growth will be tracked, with a target of at least a 74% increase as they graduate from the Academy and move to Everyday Shoppes. Success will also be measured by how many vendors transition to permanent retail l

2114.description: This project includes the complete rehabilitation of four (4) sanitary sewer lift stations with the City. The scope of work required would include upgraded controls and remote monitoring equipment, new electrical equipment and hardware, new/upgraded submersible pumps, discharge piping and valving, wet well repairs and lining, improved lighting and site security in addition to emergency back-up power via generators. Once completed, these improvements will improve resiliency of our sanitary sewer system and increase the chances of eliminating sanitary sewer overflows in nearby waterways and estuaries during Hurricanes and other high rain events.
2114.purpose: These improvements will improve resiliency of our sanitary sewer system and increase the chances of eliminating sanitary sewer overflows in nearby waterways and estuaries during Hurricanes and other high rain events.
2114.activities: Improve overall water quality of nearby water bodies such as the Manatee River, Terra Ceia Bay and the Gulf of America.
2114.direct_services: Reduce the possibility of contamination of streets and general public who might come in contact with untreated water.
2114.population: All 13,000 residents of the City of Palmetto
2114.outcome: The new lift station equipment will improve overall waster management through elimination or reduction of Sanitary Sewer Overflows (SSO's). It will also improve lift station downtime during loss of electricity during hurricanes/natural disasters.

2115.description: The Palmetto Police Department currently relies on Manatee County EOC to administer certain functions for its current 5G Motorola radios. This software would allow the Palmetto Police Department to independently manage these radios.
2115.purpose: Improve the Palmetto Police Departments ability to manage certain features of the dispatch software. Particularly as it relates to our 5G radios being used by the officers and dispatch office.
2115.activities: Purchase, installation and training of new dispatch software.
2115.direct_services: Improve responsiveness for our citizens via more efficient management of dispatch software.
2115.population: All 13,000 residents of the City of Palmetto
2115.outcome: The Palmetto Police Department currently relies on Manatee County EOC to administer certain functions for its current 5G Motorola radios. This software would allow the Palmetto Police Department to independently manage these radios. Improve responsiveness for our citizens via more efficient management of dispatch software. Metrics include: Reduction in time need to make adjustments to software and radio system. Independence---No longer requires the City of Palmetto to rely on the Manatee County to assist with program changes.

1865.description: The proposed public works project involves replacing all existing AMR water meters and backflow prevention devices with new, modern units to enhance system efficiency, accuracy, and safety. The upgraded AMR (Automatic Meter Reading) technology will provide faster, more reliable meter readings, reduce manual labor, and improve billing accuracy through real-time data collection. In addition, the new backflow prevention devices will strengthen public health protections by preventing the reverse flow of contaminants into the potable water supply, ensuring continued water quality and safety for all customers.
1865.purpose: The upgraded AMR technology will provide faster, more reliable meter readings, reduce manual labor and improve billing accuracy through real-time data collection.
1865.activities: The new backflow prevention devices will strengthen public health protections by preventing the reverse flow of contaminants into the potable water supply, ensuring continued water quality and safety for all customers.
1865.direct_services: Improved billing accuracy and public health protections.
1865.population: The entire population of the City which is over 13,000 residents.
1865.outcome: Faster, more reliable meter readings, while reducing manual labor and improving billing accuracy through real-time data collection.

1627.description: In addition to Hurricane Ian, Hurricanes Helene and Milton caused an estimated $1 billion in Sarasota and Manatee counties. The impact of the damage, and long-term recovery, proved to be especially consequential for Sarasota which has experienced a 20% population increase in the last ten years (2013-2023). State funding would match a $7.5M federal grant to establish a building institute in Sarasota County to meet the needs of the community’s long-term hurricane recovery, the demands of the area’s growing population, and provide education, training and specialized trade certifications for a projected minimum of 1,700 students enrolled and 1,600 job placements by 2036. The result will be increased job opportunities, economic revitalization and a strong workforce of skilled builders in Sarasota County and surrounding areas.
1627.purpose: Through a combination of classroom instruction and on-site construction projects, the Institute will provide young participants with the tools they need to succeed. Beginning with a target age range for post-high school (18 - 24), BII’s curriculum will expand to include classes for high school students, incorporating ages 16 - 24. Students who complete the pre-apprenticeship and full-apprenticeship programs will receive applicable certification through the Home Builders Institute.
1627.activities: The Building Industry Institute will provide career training in the in-demand construction trades. Qualified instructors from respective trades will be hired and give students the benefit of their practical experience as well as an understanding of the theoretical basis for their various job applications. Through classroom instruction, hands-on construction training, skill development, and specialized certification construction trades BII will prepare students to contribute to the well-being and

CIPP is a trenchless method that replaces lining of sewer pipes without reducing capacity, without requiring excavation and restoring services to customers faster economically.
1832.purpose: The current system requires frequent and emergency maintenance due to failing joints, root intrusion, blockages and sewer pipe failures , causing service outages and sewer overflows. Cured In Place method (CIPP) is a less intrusive and cost-effective method to improve the life of these assets with minimal disruption to the residents.

Outcomes will be measured by the following performance indicators: Response times, communication effectiveness, coordination and collaboration, technology infrastructure performance, resource utilization, and feedback from the City's management team as well as from other cities that utilize our services.

Project will increase economic activity by reducing total trip length on route by 6-8 minutes, ensuring increased accessibility for existing aviation training, construction material transport and industrial businesses.
