1970.description: The City of Archer requests funding for shovel-ready construction of a septic to sewer project. This is a regional approach to address long standing wastewater infrastructure deficiencies in this underserved community. The City has faced significant environmental and public health challenges from failing septic systems. This project will remove and properly abandon existing septic systems and connect homes and businesses to a new municipal collection system under an interlocal agreement to the neighboring City of Newberry’s regional Advanced Wastewater Treatment Plant. By eliminating major pollution sources and converting to centralized sewer service, the project improves water quality, reduces environmental hazards, and enhances aquifer recharge, delivering critical benefits to Archer residents.
1970.purpose: The specific purpose is for the construction portion of an already designed and permitted project to eliminate Archer's failing septic systems and replace them with a centralized sewer collection system that connects to the City of Newberry’s regional Advanced Wastewater Treatment Plant.
1970.activities: The activity provided is to remove and properly abandon existing septic systems and connect homes and businesses to a new municipal collection system under an interlocal agreement to the neighboring City of Newberry’s regional Advanced Wastewater Treatment Plant.
1970.direct_services: New septic to sewer connections from Archer to Newberry's AWWTF will provide the citizens with adequate functionality and treatment which will in turn reduce reliance on failing and dated septic systems and will diminish environmental harm.
1970.population: The City of Archer's population of approximately 1,140 people as of the 2020 census will be served.
1970.outcome: The expected outcome of the project is the removal and abandoment of septic systems and connection to a new municipal collection system under an interlocal agreement to the neighboring City of Newberry’s regional Advanced Wastewater Treatment Plant. The method to measure this outcome is by tracking the number of septic tanks removed and the number of connections to sewer made.

1969.description: The City of Archer is requesting funds to revitalize its parks and recreation areas by upgrading the splash pad for improved safety and accessibility, renovating Maddox Park baseball fields to enhance play conditions and attract regional events, installing perimeter fencing to secure the park and protect investments, and modernizing the pavilion to provide an inclusive gathering space. These improvements will create a vibrant, multi-use destination that promotes health and wellness, fosters youth engagement, strengthens community bonds, and stimulates economic activity, representing a long-term investment in Archer’s quality of life.

These upgrades will deliver safer, higher quality water service and strengthen public health protections for the community.

A permanent, ADA-compliant restroom will enhance visitor comfort, help promote tourism, and strengthen local businesses by encouraging longer stays and improving the overall experience in the Historic District.

2496.description: McGough Nature Park is one of Largo's most popular destinations for residents and tourists, attracting more than 50,000 visitors annually to enjoy the trails, pier, wildlife, bird sanctuary, and nature center. The park's boardwalk is more than 35 years old and is beyond its useful life. Additionally, the existing boardwalk was constructed before ADA standards. This project proposes to demolish and replace the existing boardwalk with one that is ADA-compliant and constructed to resiliency standards. The proposed new boardwalk will include bumpouts, rest benches, and a walking surface to be able to accommodate everyone who visits the park.

1985.description: NE 191st Street, NE 29th Avenue, and NE 188th Street, referred to as the NE 191 System, are critical east-west connectors in the City that experience high traffic volumes due to their function and their access to important public services, commercial areas, and residential neighborhoods. The project will enhance roadway safety through the installation of improved signage, lighting, pedestrian crossings, and intersection upgrades; increase capacity via lane widening, resurfacing, and turn lane additions; and incorporate stormwater drainage enhancements as a supporting measure to ensure reliable pavement performance during heavy rains. This comprehensive approach will reduce congestion, improve traffic flow, and mitigate accident risks for the over 40,000 residents and 30 million annual visitors.

3169.population: The project serves all residents, businesses, and visitors of Gadsden County, Florida, with a primary focus on communities currently under served by existing fire and rescue infrastructure. 3169.outcome: The goal of this project is to construct a new Gadsden County Fire Rescue Facility to improve emergency response times, enhance public safety, and provide adequate space for modern fire and rescue operations. The new facility will replace outdated infrastructure, accommodate growing service demands, and ensure compliance with current safety and operational standards. This investment will strengthen county-wide emergency preparedness and provide more efficient and reliable fire protection for residents, businesses, and visitors.

1776.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1776.description: A multi-use rural facility supporting: Local agriculture and small businesses, Workforce training and food entrepreneurship, Community gatherings and youth agricultural education, Farmers market and farm-to-table commerce. The 9,000–10,000 sq. ft. Multi-Purpose Agricenter will include a 4,000 sq. ft. event hall for livestock shows, workshops, and community gatherings; a 1,500 sq. ft. commercial kitchen for shared food production; two classrooms totaling 1,000 sq. ft. for agricultural training and youth programs; an 800 sq. ft. office and conference suite; 1,000 sq. ft. for storage, restrooms, and mechanical needs; and a 700 sq. ft. lobby and display area highlighting local agricultural heritage..
1776.purpose: The funds will construct a Multi-Purpose Agricenter to support agricultural development, community events, educational programs, and small business growth, providing a centralized facility that strengthens local agriculture, workforce training, and economic opportunities in Gadsden County.
1776.activities: The funds will construct and equip the Multi-Purpose Agricenter to host agricultural events, educational programs, youth training, and community gatherings. It will provide a commercial kitchen, classrooms, office space, and display areas to support local agriculture, small business development, and community engagement.
1776.direct_services: The Multi-Purpose Agricenter will provide citizens with access to agricultural education, youth programs, community events, and workshops. It will support local entrepreneurs and food businesses through shared-use kitchen facilities, offer spaces for public gatherings, and promote awareness of the county’s agricultural heritage.
1776.population: The project serves all residents, youth, farmers, and small business owners in Gadsden County, as well as visitors attending community and agricultural events. Estimated Number of Individuals Served:Approximately 47,000 residents and additional visitors are expected to benefit from educational programs, community events, and business support services provided by the Agricenter.
1776.outcome: Expected Benefit or Outcome:The Agricenter will enhance agricultural education, support small businesses, and promote community engagement in Gadsden County. Methodology for Measuring Outcomes:Success will be measured by tracking program participation, events hosted, training sessions completed, and usage of the commercial kitchen, using attendance records and program reports.

The work associated with the requested funds will consist of approximately 5,400 LF of 8” gravity sewer, which will connect to a master lift station that will go to construction in the coming months. The expansion will connect approximately 85 homes to centralized sewer. The project is located within the Upper Wakulla River and Wakulla Spring Basin Management Action Plan area (BMAP). As such, it is expected that the nutrient loads discharged from the existing septic systems have an impact on the groundwater and ultimately affect the spring. The proposed project would finalize the design and construct a portion of the necessary collecti
1830.purpose: This project will complete Phase 1 of the process of converting the existing septic systems within the City of Midway to a central sewer collection and treatment system. This project will provide for improved groundwater quality and higher densities to limit urban sprawl.
1830.activities: The City of Midway is located in the Wakulla Springs Basin Management Action Plan (BMAP). As such, it is expected that the nutrient loads discharged from the existing septic systems has an impact to the groundwater and ultimately effects the spring. The proposed project would design and construct a portion of the necessary collection and transmission infrastructure to begin the process of the septic-to-sewer conversion. Not only will this provide for improved groundwater quality, but also higher
1830.direct_services: The City currently has an agreement with Talquin Electric Cooperative to collect and treat wastewater from the commercial corridor within the City. This project will complete Phase 1 of the City’s steps in connecting large residential subdivisions to the existing system.
1830.population: The City currently has an agreement with Talquin Electric Cooperative to collect and treat wastewater from the commercial corridor within the City. This project will complete Phase 1 of the City’s steps in connecting large residential subdivisions to the existing system.
1830.outcome: The benefits of this project are to prevent nutrient loads from being deposited from the existing septic systems. Because of the impacts on the groundwater, the City wishes to continue septic to sewer conversions by funding Phase 1B of this pro

1870.description: The purpose of the project is to storm harden the City of Bradenton's sanitary sewer system by eliminating the existing Lift Station 08 (LS08), originally constructed in the 1930's, and located immediately adjacent to the Manatee River. The finished floor elevation of the lift station is at the same elevation as the seawall, below FEMA base flood elevation. The lift station platform is underwater several times a year during a heavy rain event that is coincident with a high tide. A new submersible pump station will be built approximately 9 feet higher in elevation, safely out of the floodplain.
1870.purpose: LS08 is located in downtown Bradenton, within 12 feet of the Manatee River and serves a 232-acres sewershed with 406 residences, commercial, institutional, and government buildings. A small portion of the sewershed is below the FEMA established base flood elevation; 27 buildings including LS08 are below BFE, the remainder of the buildings continue to have service during the flood events but flow is either bypassed or circulates to the Manatee River. The existing lift station does not meet curren
1870.activities: The funds for engineering design, survey, geotechnical investigation, and other professional services to create a successful project have been encumbered and this application request for funds are specifically for construction. This includes demolition of the existing LS08, bypass pumping during construction, a new code compliant structure, pumps, valves, piping, manholes, electrical power, controls systems, site work, and restoration.
1870.direct_services: Due to the proximity of the lift station to the Manatee River, a loss of its power supply or a mechanical failure may result in overflows from the lift station that mix with flood waters and ultimately release raw sewage into the Manatee River. In addition, interruption in the operation of the lift station can result in the gravity sewer system that flows to it surcharging and potentially back flo
1870.population: LS08 receives sanitary sewer flow from a residential area, some small businesses, and governmental buildings (Bradenton City Hall and Manatee County Administrative offices) in downtown Bradenton and the surrounding area. A total impacted area of 232 acres and 406 buildings will be directly served by the project. Additionally, the greater Tampa Bay and Sarasota Bay communities will benefit from the reduction in sewage overflows to the Manatee River, a critical regional asset.
1870.outcome: The project ensures that the contributory sewer collection system does not surcharge and backflow into residences currently served by LS08, and an eliminates the potential for the release of raw sewage overflows to the environment. The City also anticipates a greater reduction in inflow & infiltration entering the system by moving the station off the river. This outcome can be measured by comparing the downtime and resulting adverse effects of the existing and proposed lift stations during severe wet weather events as well as improved water quality in the river.

1871.description: During the unprecedented 2024 hurricane season, the City's Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) experienced record high influent flows. The WRF treats an average of 6.5 million gallons per day (MGD); The WRF was inundated with peak flows as high as 30 MGD during multiple severe weather events completely overwhelming the capacity of the facility. Of additional concern was that the flow remained elevated at +15 MGD for weeks after each storm passed, while the rainfall worked its way through the City’s collection system. This led to several bypass events where partially treated wastewater was released into the Manatee River. The wet-weather storage upgrade described below will ensure that the facility is adequately equipped for future post-storm recovery. Additionally, the City is currently funding the construction of a 2MG clarifier and an additional filter to add treatment capacity.
1871.purpose: The hydraulic capacity of the WRF has several limiting factors, one of them being off line storage when severe weather events impacts the City. One of the most cost effective ways to provide additional storage capacity while the plant recovers from severe weather is an off line pond (3 million gallons) where partially treated wastewater may be stored for a short duration of time. The partially treated flow can then be sent back through the treatment train to provide complete treatment prior to d
1871.activities: With the severe weather experienced in the City in calendar year 2024, in excess of 150,000,000 gallons of partially treated or untreated flow, was bypassed through the plant or overflowed in the collection system and entered the ecosystem of the Manatee River. The ability to capture and store some of the excess flow in the off line storage pond at treatment plant, gives the plant the opportunity to fully treat the waste prior to being discharged; fully treated waste is of reclaimed quality and
1871.direct_services: The direct service or impact to all citizens in the County is improved water quality in the Manatee River. Fully treated effluent reduces the nutrient load to the river, i.e. nitrogen and phosphorus, which creates an environment conducive to algae growth; and with complete filtration, reduces the suspended sediments in the effluent that can negatively impact the sea grass and fish communities in t
1871.population: The entire county population (+/-400K) is impacted by the water quality in the Manatee River. The effluent discharge from the WRF goes directly to the Manatee River. When partially treated discharge reaches the river, swimming and fishing prohibitions are immediately posted. As a tourist driven market, disruption to the river creates havoc for eco- sports in the county, impacting paychecks for the locals, vacation time and spending for the tourists, and income to the business community.
1871.outcome: The expected benefit is improved water quality in the Manatee River and fewer unauthorized discharges and SSO events. The City is required to report unauthorized discharges and SSO to FDEP, a reduction in volume and number of events reported is the measure of improvement as well as the sampling in the river to show reduce nitrogen and phosphorus levels in the effluent.

1777.description: The DIRSEE Bridge Project provides under-resourced youth in rural areas with comprehensive support to enhance their academic, social, and personal development. The program offers tutoring and educational enrichment, mentorship, career readiness, college and career exposure through tours, health and wellness activities, social-emotional learning, and violence prevention seminars. It also empowers youth to feel safe, valued and equally important as peers in urban and suburban areas, fostering confidence, opportunity, and long-term personal and economic growth.
1777.purpose: These funds will allow DIRSEE to server under-resourced youth in rural communities. The goal is to strengthen academic performance, physical health, mental wellness, and career readiness through mentorship and education. Funds will support fitness and nutrition activities, mental health workshops, tutoring, literacy programs and college tours. The project will also provide laptops, tablets, reading materials, enrichment workshops. Lastly, our goal is to empower youth to feel safe, valued and equ
1777.activities: The purpose of the funds, the project will provide academic tutoring and educational support, mentorship and social- emotional learning, a violence prevention program, career readiness, college and career exposure through tours, health and wellness activities, and enrichment that build skills, resilience, and opportunities for under-resourced rural youth.
1777.direct_services: The requested funding will provide under-resourced rural youth with academic support (tutoring), health and wellness activities, mentorship, career readiness training, college and career tours, and enrichment opportunities to enhance their educational, physical, and mental well-being.
1777.population: We will serve 50-100 under resourced youth in rural areas with deficiencies in mental health, physical health, economically disadvantaged, at-risk youth, homeless, single parent households, grade school and high school students and victims of crime.
1777.outcome: The project will improve educational achievement, mental and physical well-being, career readiness, violence prevention skills, and provide exposure to college and career opportunities for under-resourced rural youth. The outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-assessments, participation tracking in program activities, and feedback from students and mentors to evaluate skill development, engagement, and behavioral improvements.

2084.description: The Town of Fort Myers Beach has been recovering from the catastrophic damage caused to the community during Hurricane Ian. The Town has also suffered damages and impacts from multiple proceeding storm events including Hurricanes Idalia, Helene, and Milton. Although the Town has been working on storm water and potable water improvements prior to the hurricane, the need for additional repairs and improvements has been emphasized emphasized through these natural disasters. The purpose of the project is to complete construction of improvements to the storm water management infrastructure located in and around the Times Square area, with a continued focus on the vital downtown and business district of the Town to alleviate stormwater flooding and address mitigation efforts in preventing future flooding.
2084.purpose: The purpose of the project is to complete construction of improvements to the storm water management infrastructure located in and around the Times Square area, with a continued focus on the vital downtown and business district of the Town to alleviate stormwater flooding and address mitigation efforts in preventing future flooding.
2084.activities: Appropriated funds will be utilized for costs associated with the construction of storm water improvements.
2084.direct_services: Appropriated funds will be utilized for costs associated with the construction of storm water improvements with improved environmental preservation and protection, contaminant reduction, flood control, and disaster mitigation.
2084.population: Prior to Hurricane Ian, estimated 6,000 full-time residents lived on the Island with approximately tens of thousands of seasonal residents and 1 million annual visitors all of which these improvements aim to serve.
2084.outcome: The proposed stormwater mprovements are anticipated to improve environmental preservation and protection, contaminant reduction, flood control, and disaster mitigation. Construction of stormwater infrastructure will protect the public by improving water quality, reliability, system pressures and flows through the replacement of old, deteriorating pipes. Proposed stormwater improvements are anticipated to also improve flooding conditions along Estero Blvd which is the Town's main evacuation route and within the Town's main business district. Measuring outcomes can be achieved through the appropriate permitting agencies and by the Town, as well as decreased flooding levels to the Town's Level

2086.description: The Town of Fort Myers Beach has been recovering from the catastrophic damage caused to the community during Hurricane Ian. The Town has also suffered damages and impacts from multiple proceeding storm events including Hurricanes Idalia, Helene, and Milton. The purpose of the project is to complete repairs and improvements not already funded on the Town-maintained side streets and roads, as well as sidewalks and curbs to promote safe and adequate accessibility throughout the island. Goals include improved environmental preservation and protection, safety and security, and disaster mitigation to provide safe and secure transportation pathways on the island.
2086.purpose: The purpose of the project is to complete repairs and improvements not already funded on the Town-maintained side streets and roads, as well as sidewalks and curbs. Goals include improved environmental preservation and protection, safety and security, and disaster mitigation to provide safe and secure transportation pathways on the island.
2086.activities: Appropriated funds will be utilized for costs associated with construction of road and concrete improvements to promote transportation and accessibility.
2086.direct_services: Appropriated funds will be utilized for costs associated with the construction of improvements with improved transportation and accessibility, as well as addressing disaster mitigation.
2086.population: Prior to Hurricane Ian, estimated 6,000 full-time residents lived on the Island with approximately tens of thousands of seasonal residents and 1 million annual visitors all of which these improvements aim to serve.
2086.outcome: Will protect the public by improving reliability and improved mitigation and resiliency efforts to ensure adequate and safe transportation on Town streets and sidewalks. These elements will be measured by the appropriate permitting agencies and by the Town of Fort Myers Beach.

1835.description: The funds will modernize WASD's sewer inspection program by optimizing the CCTV reviews and generate risk-based rehab priorities. Sewer AI will use the data from the field, catalog the data, and complete timely assessments to generate project needs. This will improve data quality, accelerate capital planning, reduce emergency failures, prevent sanitary sewer overflows, and strengthen environmental and regulatory compliance across the wastewater system.
1835.purpose: The funds will modernize WASD's sewer inspection program by optimizing the CCTV reviews and generate risk-based rehab priorities. Sewer AI will use the data from the field, catalog the data, and complete timely assessments to generate project needs. This will improve data quality, accelerate capital planning, reduce emergency failures, prevent sanitary sewer overflows, and strengthen environmental and regulatory compliance across the wastewater system.
1835.activities: The project will deploy AI-enabled sewer inspection technology to analyze CCTV footage, catalog system conditions, and produce timely assessments that support proactive infrastructure planning. It will automate the generation of risk-based rehabilitation priorities, enable faster and more accurate identification of defects, and reduce the need for emergency repairs, resulting in fewer service disruptions, improved environmental protection, and enhanced reliability of wastewater services for resi
1835.direct_services: This project will provide residents of Miami-Dade County with a more reliable and resilient wastewater system by using advanced AI technology to identify defects earlier, prevent system failures, and reduce the risk of sanitary sewer overflows. By modernizing sewer inspections and enabling faster, data-driven rehabilitation decisions, the project will protect public health, minimize service disrup
1835.population: Residents of Miami-Dade County, benefiting more than 2.8 million people, including the local community within the project area.
1835.outcome: Expected Benefit / Outcome: The project deploys AI-driven sewer inspections that improve coding accuracy to 97% and boost productivity by 91%, accelerating assessments and enabling early identification of high-risk defects. This improves data quality, reduces SSOs and emergency repairs, and strengthens overall system reliability.Methodology: Performance will be measured through year-over-year reductions in SSOs, emergency repairs, and response times, using NASSCO-scored inspections and AI accuracy/throughput metrics.

2245.description: The Women's Cancer Center at the Miami Cancer Institute will be a 155,000 square foot facility dedicated to expanding access to cancer services to women by providing a coordinated patient-centered environment created to meet growing patient demand and physician development needs. Services provided will include benign and high-risk imaging, medical and surgical oncology, plastics and reconstructive and gynecologic surgery.
2245.purpose: Funds requested will support a total construction budget estimated at $188,000,000
2245.activities: Baptist Health South Florida will construct, operate, and maintain the facility
2245.direct_services: The Women's Cancer Center at the Miami Cancer Institute will be a 155,000 square foot facility dedicated to expanding access to cancer services to women by providing a coordinated patient-centered environment created to meet growing patient demand and physician development needs. Services provided will include benign and high-risk imaging, medical and surgical oncology, plastics and reconstructive
2245.population: The target population includes those in our service areas which include Monroe County, Miami-Dade County, Broward County, and Palm Beach County
2245.outcome: The Women's Cancer Center at the Miami Cancer Institute will provide expanded access to cancer services and expanded opportunities for physician training and research.

1775.description: Kids House of Seminole, Inc. is Seminole County's only Children's Advocacy Center. The CAC serves as the single point of contact for child abuse investigations in Seminole County. The Kids House Mental Health Therapy Program is one of four critical programs at Kids House that helps children heal from abuse and neglect.
1775.purpose: The specific purpose that will be achieved by the funds requested is to provide evidence-based mental health therapy services to child abuse victims who present with behavior problems, posttraumatic stress, anxiety, and depression. The goal is to help children overcome complex trauma, heal from abuse and/or neglect, build resilience, and mature cognitively and emotionally.
1775.activities: Services will include quickly identifying abuse and neglect, providing individual therapy sessions to child victims, providing Parent/Caregiver Education and Support.
1775.direct_services: The direct services that will be provided to meet the intended purpose of the requested funds are: advocating for children with other providers, involving caregivers in the child's therapeutic process through education and consultation, utilizing Animal Assisted Intervention, focusing on early childhood trauma/attachment injury, and developing comprehensive treatment planning.
1775.population: Abused and neglected children and their non-offending caregivers. 51-100 individuals are expected to be served.
1775.outcome: Children will heal from the effects of child abuse and neglect. Children will build long-term resilience while enhancing the caregiver's ability to cope and parent their traumatized child.

1949.description: The City of Bushnell is seeking design funding to expand its wastewater treatment facility (WWTF) from 1.2 to an estimated 2 MGD to meet rising local and regional demands. Positioned along a major interstate near the growing Orlando metropolitan area and The Villages, Bushnell is facing rapid development pressure. Without increased WWTF capacity, the City cannot support new residential and commercial growth. This infrastructure upgrade is essential for regulatory compliance, public health, and unlocking economic development through housing, business expansion, and job creation.
1949.purpose: The requested design funding will enable the City of Bushnell to develop a comprehensive, permit-ready plan to modernize and expand its wastewater treatment facility (WWTF) from 1.2 MGD to an estimated 2MGD to address the regional growth and economic expansion into the area. This will address regional infrastructure needs driven by population growth and interlocal agreements, like the existing one with the City of Webster.
1949.activities: To meet the purpose of the requested funds, the City of Bushnell activities will include the design of the WWTF to be modernized and expanded. This project will provide the engineering design of an estimated 2 MGD facility capable of handling regional growth and nutrient removal needs. The project will also include permitting activities to ensure the design is construction-ready and compliant with regulatory requirements.
1949.direct_services: Direct services to residents will not be part of this project.
1949.population: The target population served by the project is the residents of City of Bushnell, population 3,148, and the City of Webster, population 1,631, for a total population served of 4,779.
1949.outcome: The expected outcome of the project is a fully developed, permit-ready design for an upgraded wastewater treatment facility that meets the current and future needs of Bushnell and surrounding communities. The outcome will be measured by the completion of a permit-ready design that meets technical, regulatory, and regional service requirements, including capacity, nutrient removal, and construction readiness.

2247.description: The requested funds will support the expansion of SW 162/NE 18 Avenue into a four-lane corridor from 328 St to 312 St to meet the mobility and safety needs of this fast-growing area of Homestead. The project will improve and enhance roadway infrastructure, traffic flow, pedestrian and bike safety lanes, and the overall resilience of this critical transportation corridor.
2247.purpose: The requested funds will support the expansion of SW 162/NE 18 Avenue into a four-lane corridor from 328 St to 312 St to meet the mobility and safety needs of this fast-growing area of Homestead. The project will improve and enhance roadway infrastructure, traffic flow, pedestrian and bike safety lanes, and the overall resilience of this critical transportation corridor.
2247.activities: The activities and services include the engineering, design, and construction needed to widen SW 162/ NE 18 Avenue to four travel lanes from SW 328th St to SW 312th St; upgrade roadway drainage and safety features; and deliver the infrastructure necessary to improve mobility and enhance multimodal access.
2247.direct_services: The funding will provide citizens with safer, more efficient daily travel through a widened four-lane roadway, and added sidewalks and bicycle lanes that enhance multimodal access. Residents will benefit from reduced congestion, improved emergency response access, safer routes for pedestrians and cyclists, and a more reliable corridor.
2247.population: This project serves the general public. The amount of individuals expected to be served is > 800.
2247.outcome: The project will improve traffic conditions by widening the corridor to four lanes, removing bottlenecking, and creating smoother, more efficient travel. These upgrades reduce congestion, shorten travel times, and provide safer, better- organized movement for vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists. The benefit will be measured by analyzing traffic flow data, monitoring reductions in congestion and travel delays, tracking pedestrian and cyclist usage, and evaluating accident reports post-construction.

1957.organization: United Home Care Services Inc. d/b/a United
1957.description: The South Florida Home Health Workforce Development Program recruits, trains, and places unemployed or underemployed individuals into fast-track careers as Home Health Aides. Participants are trained by Florida's Designated Home & Community Based Teaching Agency to help disabled and older adults 60+ live safely at home. The program will train 200 individuals at no cost, providing a stipend and job placement. With a growing wait list of 180 interested individuals and Home Health Aide jobs projected to grow 25% by 2031, this initiative addresses a critical workforce shortage and strengthens care for South Florida’s aging population.
1957.purpose: The South Florida Home Health Aide Workforce Development Program, as part of UHC’s Learn & Work initiative, strengthens the region’s workforce by training unemployed individuals as Home Health Aides with transferable skills. With national caregiver turnover at 79.2% (2024 Activated Insights Benchmarking Report), UHC’s rate is just 35%, proving the program’s impact. Funding will expand efforts to address staffing shortages and support Florida’s aging population.
1957.activities: AHCA Level II background screening ensuring participants meet requirements to work with the disabled and older adult population. Participants will receive home health training from a licensed Registered Nurse. To ease the burden of cost, the program is free to participants and will provide all didactic materials, books and supplies. Recruitment of participants will be conducted through community outreach via presentations at churches, job and health fairs, local non-profits, through social media
1957.direct_services: Direct services to be provided include home health, basic life support / CPR training plus on-the-job training. Additionally, participants will receive job placement assistance and a Stipend of six-hundred dollars ($600) will be provided to them upon completion of the Program. Participants will obtain Home Health Aide Documentation which is portable for employment in a licensed Medicaid/Medicare A
1957.population: The South Florida Home Health Workforce Development Program will serve 200 individuals. The target population is unemployed or underemployed individuals ages 18 plus seeking training and job placement assistance in the field of home health and long term care. The Program will provide them with the necessary skills to ensure that caregiving tasks provided to disabled and older adults are safely delivered in the comfort of home, home settings or long term care facilities.
1957.outcome: The expected outcome is increased availability of Home Health Aides to serve South Florida’s growing older adult population. Participants will gain meaningful employment, quality training at no cost, and skills to meet community home health needs. With an estimated annual legislative investment of $220,000, the program will train and empower individuals for gainful employment in the home health and long-term care industry. Outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-surveys of those recruited, trained, and successfully placed in jobs.

2056.description: YMCA Family Centers are essential community hubs serving thousands of children and families daily. The YMCA Critical Infrastructure & Life-Safety Initiative will strengthen building safety and structural integrity at YMCA family centers in Orange and Osceola counties. Funds will support roof restoration, building envelope upgrades to prevent moisture and UV degradation, structural and mechanical rehabilitation to improve efficiency, drainage improvements, emergency- readiness measures, and other life-safety system upgrades that protect youth and families, reduce facility risk, and ensure continuity of operations during natural disasters.
2056.purpose: This funding will strengthen YMCA community health infrastructure in Osceola and Orange Counties by supporting structurally sound, code-compliant, and resilient facilities. Improvements will prevent safety hazards, reduce closures, extend facility life, and protect uninterrupted access to drowning-prevention, childcare, wellness, and family programs, ensuring safe, reliable spaces year-round.
2056.activities: Funds will support roof restoration, building envelope improvements to prevent UV and moisture degradation, structural and mechanical upgrades to improve building efficiency, updates to ADA access, emergency response systems, drainage work, and the rehabilitation of essential aquatic systems. These improvements enhance building integrity, protect life-safety, and prevent closures, ensuring YMCA programs operate safely and without interruption.
2056.direct_services: This project will provide safer, more functionally resilient and efficient YMCA Family Centers in Osceola and Orange counties, ensuring continued access to vital programs that support families and promote healthy lifestyles. Childcare, afterschool programs, and summer camp help working families, while wellness programs support aging in place and lifelong health. Water safety programs help prevent
2056.population: The YMCA Critical Infrastructure & Life Safety Initiative will serve children, families, and individuals of all ages who rely on YMCA Family Centers in Osceola and Orange counties for childcare, afterschool programs, summer camps, water safety, wellness, and community support. This project will benefit working families, seniors aging in place, and at-risk youth, ensuring safer, more accessible spaces. Approximately 55,000 individuals will be served annually through these life-safety and facility
2056.outcome: This project will improve safety and community health by strengthening building integrity, reducing closures, and ensuring uninterrupted access to childcare, wellness, drowning prevention, and senior programs. Success will be measured through reductions in safety incidents and closures, improved facility uptime and compliance, and improved health and well-being through increased participant retention and satisfaction measured with qualitative and quantitative data.

1803.description: The Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) & Aviation Training Center Improvements project will modernize and expand the Aviation Workforce Training and Development Center at Tallahassee International Airport (TLH) to support AAM and eVTOL technologies. The project includes facility upgrades, expanded classroom and hangar space, and advanced training technology to strengthen Florida’s aviation workforce, create jobs, and enhance statewide transportation resiliency. These improvements will position TLH as a regional hub for next-generation aviation innovation and workforce development.
1803.purpose: The project will expand and modernize the Aviation Workforce Training and Development Center at Tallahassee International Airport (TLH) to support Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) and eVTOL technologies. It will strengthen aviation workforce training, create high-skill jobs, and position Florida as a leader in next-generation aviation innovation and transportation resiliency.
1803.activities: Activities include designing, constructing, and upgrading aviation training facilities, classrooms, and hangar space at Tallahassee International Airport (TLH). Services will include advanced technical instruction, certification programs, and hands-on workforce training to prepare students and professionals for careers in Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) and eVTOL technologies.
1803.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with expanded access to aviation education and workforce training programs, creating high-skill, high-wage career opportunities in Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) and related aviation fields. It will also support regional economic growth and strengthen Florida’s long-term transportation resiliency.
1803.population: The target population includes high school and college students, job seekers, and economically disadvantaged individuals pursuing careers in aviation and emerging technologies. The project will create new pathways for Floridians to gain advanced technical skills and industry certifications, significantly expanding training capacity and access to high-quality aviation career opportunities across the region.
1803.outcome: The project will expand aviation workforce training and prepare Floridians for careers in Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) and eVTOL technologies, creating high-skill jobs and strengthening the state’s position as a leader in next-generation aviation. Success will be measured by tracking new training program enrollments, certifications earned, job placements, and partnerships established with aviation and AAM industries, demonstrating measurable workforce and economic growth.

1961.description: This project will expand commercial air service at Tallahassee International Airport (TLH) by recruiting new nonstop routes and increasing seat capacity to improve connectivity within Florida and to key regions nationwide. The City will provide a 100% local match, demonstrating strong shared investment. Funding will support airline recruitment, route incentives, and related planning consistent with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Air Carrier Incentive Program guidance, strengthening statewide access, economic growth, and transportation resiliency for the Capital Region.
1961.purpose: The funds will expand air service at Tallahassee International Airport by attracting new nonstop routes, increasing seat capacity, and improving intrastate connectivity to Florida's capital; strengthening economic growth, tourism, and statewide transportation resiliency.
1961.activities: Activities include recruiting and securing new commercial air service routes, increasing flight capacity, and enhancing intrastate connectivity. Services will include planning, marketing, and airspace studies per FAA Air Carrier Incentive Program guidance, along with related infrastructure and equipment improvements at Tallahassee International Airport.
1961.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from expanded flight options, improved statewide connectivity, and greater access to business and leisure travel. The project will create jobs, boost tourism, and strengthen economic opportunities while enhancing transportation efficiency and resiliency for Tallahassee and the surrounding region.
1961.population: The target population includes residents, businesses, government agencies, and visitors traveling to and from Florida's capital region. Expanded air service at TLH is expected to directly benefit approximately one million annual passengers, while indirectly supporting thousands of regional jobs and businesses that rely on efficient, reliable air transportation.
1961.outcome: The project will enhance air service, increase economic activity, and strengthen statewide connectivity by adding new nonstop routes and greater flight capacity, boosting tourism, attracting business investment, creating jobs, and improving transportation resiliency in Florida’s capital region. Success will be measured by tracking new routes, increased seat capacity, passenger growth, job creation, tourism revenue, and overall economic impact.

3128.description: The funds will provide the Sheriff, Fire Rescue, and local law enforcement and 911 dispatch in Jackson County with reliable, P25-compliant, interoperable radio communications. This will improve coverage for coordination within the county, across the region, and with state law enforcement and emergency services during natural disasters, man-made crises, and other critical incidents. The upgraded communications will improve officer safety and enable more effective mutual aid support to surrounding areas.
3128.purpose: The funds will provide the Sheriff, Fire Rescue, local law enforcement and 911 dispatch in Jackson County with reliable, P25-compliant, interoperable radio communications. This will improve coverage for coordination within the county, across the region, and with state law enforcement and emergency services during natural disasters, man-made crises, and other critical incidents. The upgraded communications will improve officer safety and enable more effective mutual aid support to surrounding are
3128.activities: Providing law enforcement Fire Rescue, and 911 dispatch with P25-compliant communications equipment to improve coordination within and beyond Jackson County. The enhanced coverage will enable faster emergency responses, protecting citizens, visitors, and businesses, while also strengthening law enforcement’s ability to prevent crime, reduce harm, and save lives.
3128.direct_services: Direct services provided to citizens are the improvement of communications by law enforcement, Fire Rescue, and 911 providing greater interoperability and safety for first responders, as well as reducing emergency response times, injuries, fatalities, and property damage.
3128.population: The target populations that will benefit from this project are the residents of Jackson County, local businesses, schools, and visiting tourists.
3128.outcome: The expected benefits provided by the implementation of this project include improved communication for first responders with P25-compliant equipment, improving coverage and interoperability, and reduced response times. Outcomes will be measured by tracking response times, incident resolution, and reductions in crime statistics.

3088.description: PLL is an evidence based family therapy model proven to work successfully with youth who are moderate to high risk of re-offending and their families who are involved in the Juvenile Justice system. Program goals include increasing family engagement, reducing recidivism, addressing the trauma in families and safely keeping youth within their own community.
3088.purpose: To provide services to moderate to high risk youth offenders and families that will help them achieve positive & sustainable long-term impacts. PLL is one of the only evidence based models in the country proven to have high family engagement, lower recidivism rates, lower residential placements, & lower reentry into residential placement. Parents are better prepared & equipped to handle the youth coming back home. PLL works with the entire family, so the siblings in the household will also benef
3088.activities: Youth & their families involved in the juvenile justice system will participate in multi-family groups, individual therapy & case management services. PLL teams will travel to residential commitment facilities and family homes. In addition, transportation for youth & families is provided. To maintain fidelity to evidence-based model outcomes, PLL therapist teams will participate in certified PLL training, continuing education, and bi-weekly clinical consultation.
3088.direct_services: Youth & their families involved in the juvenile justice system will receive the following direct services: skills-based training (research indicates that this is the best type of treatment for at risk families), individual & family therapy including family trauma, crisis intervention, & case management services. PLL staff teams will travel to residential commitment facilities, to family homes, and
3088.population: Targeted population to be served are youth 11 - 18 years who are moderate to high risk offenders returning home from a DJJ residential commitment facility or are youth who have recently returned home from a residential facility. This funding will provide for one team serving up to 30 families annually.
3088.outcome: Youth participating in this program will be less likely to to re-enter the juvenile or the adult corrections system. The purpose is to reduce recidivism by keeping youth ages 11-18 years from violating their probation conditions resulting in re-arrest. PLL has a dashboard that tracks the family engagement and success rates. Additionally, PLL does a mental health behavior pre/post outcome at the end of each contract year using the validated instruments of the child behavior checklist and the FACES IV. These results are provided to the service delivery provider and the department.

3133.description: The funds will assist in the expansion of Jackson Hospital's Oncology and Infusion Center, achieving the hospital's goal of improving access to healthcare. The current Oncology and Infusion offices are at capacity, with patient volumes unfortunately growing . In a recent Community Health Needs Assessment, cancer was identified as the #1 health issue and the second leading cause of death in the County. While Jackson County has a higher cancer mortality rate than Florida, the incidence rate is lower compared to the state, which suggests limited access to care. This expansion will alleviate the office's current space constrictions and allow more patients to be seen and treated in their own community, improving access to rural healthcare.
3133.purpose: The funds will assist in the expansion of Jackson Hospital's Oncology and Infusion Center, achieving the hospital's goal of improving access to local healthcare. The Oncology and Infusion offices are at capacity, with patient volumes unfortunately growing steadily. The current offices are unable to accommodate the space needs required to expand the practice, requiring the providers to limit their number of patients. This expansion will allow more patients to be seen in their own community, impro
3133.activities: The funds will increase access to cancer care in a rural community by assisting in the renovation and expansion of Jackson Hospital's Oncology and Infusion Center. The hospital is the only provider of oncology treatment in the county, if not also in the surrounding rural area. The office's infusion services are steadily growing and require more infusion chairs to meet the local need. By expanding oncology and infusion services, the hospital will be able to increase the number of patients requiri
3133.direct_services: More local patients will be able to utilize Jackson Hospital's Oncology and Infusion Center, allowing for increased access to cancer care in a rural community. In the Oncology and Infusion Center's existing space, there is no room for growth to match the steadily increasing community need. This expansion will increase the amount of patients able to be seen and treated locally, which will thereby e
3133.population: Patients of all ages who may require oncology, hematology, or infusion services will be served by expanding Jackson Hospital's Oncology and Infusion Center. It is difficult to estimate the number of individuals expected to be served by increasing the service lines, but conservatively an additional 10-20 patients could be seen a day in the expanded Oncology and Infusion Center.
3133.outcome: Local patients will have better access to oncology, hematology, and infusion services by expanding the existing Oncology and Infusion Center at Jackson Hospital. Data analysis of the current patients requiring oncology, hematology, and infusion services and the patients who require those services after the expansion should show an increase in patients treated and a resulting increase in access to care. There should also be a decrease in cancer mortalities in Jackson County and a larger number of patients utilizing these services.

2012.description: This project will construct a new YMCA at Lake Meade Park in Cape Coral to expand access to youth development, healthy living, and community programs. The facility will provide childcare, after-school and summer learning, chronic disease prevention, senior wellness, swim safety, fitness, and family support services, improving health, education, and quality of life for residents.
2012.purpose: The funds will support construction of a new YMCA at Lake Meade Park to expand access to youth, family, and community programs. The project will improve health, education, and quality of life by providing childcare, youth development, wellness programs, and community services, meeting the growing needs of Cape Coral residents and strengthening families.
2012.activities: The YMCA will provide childcare and early learning programs, after-school and summer youth development, chronic disease prevention and wellness classes, senior fitness and active-aging programs, swim lessons and water safety, family support services, and community outreach and education. These activities promote health, learning, and family stability for Cape Coral residents.
2012.direct_services: The project will provide direct services including affordable childcare, early learning, after-school and summer programs, chronic disease prevention classes, senior fitness and wellness activities, swim lessons and water safety, youth sports, family support services, and community education programs. These services will improve health, learning, and overall quality of life for Cape Coral resident
2012.population: The project will serve children, teens, families, working parents, seniors, and residents seeking health, wellness, and community programs. It will also support low- to moderate-income households needing affordable childcare and family services. The new YMCA is expected to serve several thousand Cape Coral residents annually through its programs and facilities.
2012.outcome: The project will improve health, education, and family stability by expanding access to childcare, youth development, wellness, and community programs. Outcomes will be measured through program participation data, pre- and post- assessments for health and fitness, academic progress indicators, attendance records, and participant feedback to track measurable improvements for Cape Coral residents.

3135.description: The City of Marianna (City) seeks funds for the purchase of a new pumper-engine firetruck and full suite of equipment for said truck. This funding is being requested to replace a 20+ year old fire truck that combined with its age, increased repair costs and the number of days its been out of service is making reliability and the availability of repair parts an issue. And with the City having an MOU with the County for protection services outside the City Limits, updated equipment is necessary to efficiently respond to public safety emergencies.
3135.purpose: Funding for the purchase of a new pumper-engine firetruck with full equipment suite for serving the emergency response needs of the entire City and parts of the County.
3135.activities: This firetruck and associated equipment will serve the needs of all 20,000 citizens of the greater Marianna area which includes the City of Marianna along with area of five miles beyond the City Limits via decreased response times to calls for service and increased safety for all citizens.
3135.direct_services: Increased services and decreased call response times. This will increase the safety and well-being of all those served within the City and parts of the County.
3135.population: Entire population of the City and beyond will be served to one degree or another
3135.outcome: Decreased response times for events requiring emergency response. Increased efficiency with regards to emergency services.

3082.description: The Town of Brooker has a goal to procure a fire tanker (2026 commercial cab 3,000 gallon water tanker) in order to staff a full-time career paid fire station. The Town of Brooker is one of the most rural portions of Bradford County with fire and EMS response taking a minimum of 15 minutes from the closest station. Funding this request will result in shorter response times, greatly expanding and improving the Fire and EMS service to the community. This is a continuation of a previous project.
3082.purpose: The Town of Brooker has a goal to procure a fire tanker in order to staff a full-time career paid fire station. The Town of Brooker is one of the most rural portions of Bradford County with fire and EMS response taking a minimum of 15 minutes from the closest station. Funding this request will result in shorter response times, greatly expanding and improving the Fire and EMS service to the community.
3082.activities: This new response apparatus will be incredibly beneficial to all citizens and visitors of Bradford County. The new apparatus will provide immediate access to emergency service delivery for the population across the region.
3082.direct_services: The new apparatus will be immediately placed into service as a front-line response unit. This apparatus will be capable of delivering thousands of gallons of water, and life-saving equipment.
3082.population: This project will serve the entire population of Bradford County. Approximately 29,000.
3082.outcome: Quicker response times to patients in need of life-saving medical treatment. Improved apparatus reliability and decreased repair costs. This will be measured by response time data, as well as vehicle repair cost data.

2219.description: This project advances coral restoration, marine research, and community education in Miami-Dade County. Funding supports outplanting, reef monitoring, student and volunteer training, and public outreach. It also provides technical and advocacy work to establish a Marine Sanctuary or Protected Marine Area, strengthening local ecosystems and long-term coastal resilience.
2219.purpose: The purpose and goal of this program is to raise awareness of the plight of the coral reefs in Miami-Dade County, work to establish a marine sanctuary or Protected Marine Area in Miami Dade County, and outplant coral in the water off Miami-Dade County to revitalize the coral reef tract in Miami-Dade County.
2219.activities: For the awareness, we plan to host events throughout Miami Dade County as well as continue to finalize our partnerships with Dade County Public Schools and Florida International University to not only certify students as divers but also to create citizen scientist to help promote the plight of the reefs and how the community can help achieve this goal. We also work with marine stakeholders in the community for the development of a National Marine Sanctuary and/or Protected Marine Area to allow r
2219.direct_services: We plan to work with Miami-Dade Public Schools to certify students as divers to enable them to become citizen scientists to help with coral out plantings, monitoring, cleaning the corals as well as assist in raising awareness for importance of coral reefs to our community. The ability to have reduced insurance costs through reduced storm surge and tidal activity generated by a healthier reef syste
2219.population: The target population are the residents of Miami-Dade County and visitors to the county. By creating a thriving and robust coral reef system again, all residents will be served with lower insurance rates and the ability to enjoy more ecological activities in the marine environment. Additionally, revenue generated for state and local businesses and governments as a result of eco-tourism emanating from tours of the reef will also be a benefit to all who live in the community.
2219.outcome: The ultimate outcome will be a robust and healthy reef system and a return of a biodiversity to current reef system in Miami-Dade County. This will be measured by monitoring the growth of the coral reef system coverage over the current substrate as well as monitoring the different species of marine life and their numbers as it returns to the coral reef off the shores of Miami-Dade County. Secondarily, we will also monitor the insurance rates with specific reference on the impact of storm surge on the rates offered and work closely with the state to ensure all affected see the benefits in the insurance premiums.

3092.organization: University of Florida Board of Trustees
3092.description: The UF Mobile Outreach Clinic (MOC) has been a cornerstone of healthcare access in North Central Florida since 2010, delivering free, high-quality medical care and social service coordination to uninsured individuals. MOC eliminates traditional barriers to care by providing medical services in retrofitted vehicles with exam rooms and laboratory space. MOC provides primary care services to Alachua, Levy, Gilchrist, and Dixie Counties, as well as an OB/GYN mobile unit, serving pregnant and postpartum women in maternal health deserts of North Central Florida. As a truly mobile program, we are able to serve locations that are often unreached by traditional medical care including sites for unsheltered individuals and communities with poor transportation access. This legislative request seeks funding to replace our current primary and rural mobile units with 2 new mobile units. These new vehic
3092.purpose: The funds will be used to purchase 2 replacement mobile health units. One mobile unit will replace a 30 year old, non- wheelchair accessible remodeled blue bird bus that has increasing maintenance costs and cannot be safely driven outside of Gainesville city limits. The other mobile unit will replace a single exam room, non-wheelchair accessible sprinter van that lacks external power with a two exam room mobile unit that has an external power plug-in. Both new mobile units will be wheelchair acc
3092.activities: Both mobile units will be sourced from Mission Mobile Medical with a completion date of services 180 days from order date and Mission Mobile Medical will provide ongoing maintenance and technical services as well as a 10 year warranty on both vehicles.
3092.direct_services: MOC provides weekly comprehensive primary medical care including chronic disease management, acute care, laboratory monitoring, cancer screening and follow-up, and robust care coordination all at no cost to people who are uninsured or underinsured in our North Central Florida catchment area. Care coordination provides referrals and ongoing monitoring to ensure connection with social service agenci
3092.population: Our patient population consists of uninsured and under-insured residents of North Central Florida who lack access to primary care medical services. We currently treat 2500 patients each year and this project will allow us to increase that total to approximately 3000 patients per year.
3092.outcome: This project will increase the accessibility of primary care for residents of North Central Florida. Many counties in North Central Florida (including Levy and Dixie) have some of the worst patient: provider ratios in the U.S. We measure our patient visit numbers each year and can monitor the increase in visits and services every year. We also know that our services help reduce ED visits and hospital readmissions as we help with transitions of care from the ED and hospital and also treat conditions in our clinic that lead to ED and hospital admissions when unaddressed.

2158.organization: Before & After A/C Pilot Program Corp.
2158.description: The Before & After air-conditioning pilot program will install energy-efficient air-conditioning systems in select a Florida Department of corrections facilities including Everglades, Homestead, and Miami correctional institutions. The project addresses the urgent need for climate control in the sleeping dorm areas including the two-man cells. This initiative serves as a model for modernizing Florida correctional infrastructure while promoting energy efficiency, reducing heat related health risks, and supporting humane living and working environments.
2158.purpose: The Before and After A/C Pilot corporation is requesting $450,000 to launch an air-conditioning pilot program at three Florida correctional facilities: Miami correctional institution, Everglades correctional institution and Homestead correctional institution. This program will install energy efficient air-conditioning systems in dormitory and in two- man housing areas that currently lack cooling. The goal is to reduce extreme heat exposure, improve living and working conditions, and pan melt a s
2158.activities: Funds will support the installation of energy efficient air conditioning Systems at selected correctional facilities, including site assessments, wall fabrication, and electrical preparation. Services include contracting license HVAC professionals, purchasing and installing mini split units, and monitoring temperature and energy performance. Additional activities include training staff and volunteers on equipment maintenance, data collection for program evaluation, and reporting outcomes to demo
2158.direct_services: The project will provide safer, healthier, and more humane living and working environments within Florida correctional institutions. By installing air-conditioning systems, the program directly improves physical and mental well-being for incarcerated individuals and staff, reducing he related illnesses and stress. The project also benefits the public by supporting a more stable, efficient correcti
2158.population: The project serves incarcerated individuals and correctional staff at Everglades, Homestead, and Miami Correctional Institutions. These facilities house approximately 4,500 inmates and employ around 900 staff members. The program will directly benefit both groups by improving environmental conditions, health, and safety within the facilities, while also indirectly benefiting families and communities through enhanced well being and reduce strain on medical and correctional resources.
2158.outcome: The project will improve physical and mental health by reducing extreme heat exposure for inmates and staff, leading to fewer heat -related illnesses, better sleep, and enhanced morale. It will also improve facility efficiency and safety. Outcomes will be measured through temperature and humidity monitoring, health and incident reports, staff and inmate surveys, and energy usage data comparing pre-and post installation conditions to evaluate program success and scalability.

2085.description: Bonita Beach Road is the City’s gateway access point from Interstate 75 and the eastern access point to the City’s downtown area and beaches. Improvements will consist of a signature fountain with flagpoles. Flagpoles will feature the US Flag, the State flag, and the City of Bonita Springs flag. Select landscaping will include mature canopy trees, signature palm trees with shrubs, hedges and ground cover, and irrigation and accent lighting. The total project cost for the improvements is $2,038,000.
2085.purpose: The Bonita Springs gateway feature will provide well defined entry way into the community, the downtown area and the beaches. It will provide a well-defined wayfinding feature to the community.
2085.activities: The installation of flagpoles, a fountain, canopy trees, palm trees, shrubs and ground cover with irrigation along with entry signs will enhance the way into Bonita Springs.
2085.direct_services: The installation of the aesthetics improvement project will provide tourists from out of state and in-state a clearly define way into Bonita Springs.
2085.population: Tourists from out of state and in-state. The City anticipates serving more than 10,000 residents and visitors a month as a result of the proposed improvements.
2085.outcome: The Bonita Springs gateway feature will provide a more defined wayfinding into the community. Traffic counts to the beaches and the downtown area. Survey on the City's website referencing the access to beaches and downtown.

2220.organization: Families First of Palm Beach County
2220.description: Behavioral Health Services and Supports and case management services for an additional 150-180 children on the waitlist and their families. School based and crisis supports. First six sessions reduce long term risk factors by 20% with every $1 invested in children's behavioral health resulting in $7 cost savings in uncompensated care and criminal justice. Supported by Sheriff's Department, Schools, and Agencies who refer cases.
2220.purpose: Behavioral health and case management for children and their families on waitlist for services. Many referred by agencies, schools, or other providers. Reduce mental health and criminal risk-factors, reduce abuse and neglect, improve likelihood of successful societal participation for at-risk children.
2220.activities: Behavioral health services for children and families including parenting classes and supports to help keep families together and reduce short- and long-term risk factors for children such as substance abuse, violent criminality, poor academic performance, suicidality, and mortality. Every $1 spent saves state $7 in future uncompensated care and criminal justice.
2220.direct_services: Individual Behavioral Health and Case Management Services for children and their families. School Based Supports and Crisis Response. Six-therapy sessions reduce risk factors by 20% with improved results with continued services.
2220.population: At-risk youth, people with poor mental health, economically disadvantaged, students, and victims of crime. Additional 150-180 children and their families on waitlist expected to be served.
2220.outcome: Reduction of mental health and criminal risk factors and attainment of treatment goals determined via assessments, recorded in electronic records, data will be populated and reported to ME. Expected reductions of abuse and neglect and ER visits.

2087.description: Project components include the installation of an enclosed stormwater drainage system in order to construct a 10-foot wide multi-use path on the west side of the roadway and a new 6-foot wide sidewalk on the east side of the roadway. Additional improvements will be the curb and gutter, irrigation and landscaping, street lights, along with the resurfacing of the roadway and a possible roundabout at Shangri-La Road and Paradise Road.
2087.purpose: The focus is to reduce/eliminate standing stormwater by converting existing open swales to a closed drainage system. The closed drainage system will allow for an extended multi-use pathway along the street for improved safety for pedestrian and cyclists along the roadway.
2087.activities: The proposed stormwater and roadway improvements will increased safety along the new multi-use path, speed control for motorized vehicles, improved roadway lighting, modern stormwater infrastructure to reduce or eliminate flooding. The completed project will reduce vehicle accidents as well as pedestrian accidents with the improvements to pavement condition and new lighting and signage.
2087.direct_services: Reduced standing stormwater ponding during strong storm events, along with a multi-use pathway for pedestrian/bicyclists to safely walk and bike away from the motorized vehicles.
2087.population: The residents in Bonita Springs and surrounding areas. The City expects to serve 10,000 persons per year.
2087.outcome: Improved safety for motorists, pedestrians and cyclists. Increased safety of the new multi-use path, speed control, improved roadway lighting, and signage. The completed project will reduce vehicle accidents as well as pedestrian/cyclists accidents with the improvements to pavement condition and new irrigation and landscaping.

2011.description: The funds will be used to design and construct improvements at the Del Prado WWTF to increase capacity, enhance treatment, and ensure permit compliance. The project will reduce sanitary sewer overflows, improve nutrient removal, and support continued reliable wastewater service and environmental protection for the growing North Fort Myers area.
2011.purpose: The funds will be used to design and construct improvements at the Del Prado WWTF to increase capacity, enhance treatment, and ensure permit compliance. The project will reduce sanitary sewer overflows, improve nutrient removal, and support continued reliable wastewater service and environmental protection for the rapidly growing Lee County- North Fort Myers area.
2011.activities: Expand sewer treatment capacity and increase resiliency during severe weather events to eliminate/reduce sewage seepage, reduce the nutrient loading in stormwater, groundwater & surface water & mitigate the risk of red tide to the area.
2011.direct_services: The wastewater treatment plant will be expanded to accomodate tremendous growth ocurring in Lee County and will protect citizens from overflows of wastewater which can be a public health concern and cause other health concerns such as red tide
2011.population: All of the population of North Fort Myers and will benefit all the citizens of Lee County by providing additional wastewater treatment capacity thus helping to maintain water quality and reduce nutrient loading.
2011.outcome: Expand sewer treatment capacity and increase resiliency during severe weather events to eliminate/reduce sewage seepage, reduce the nutrient loading in stormwater, groundwater & surface water & mitigate the risk of red tide to the area.

2013.description: The requested funds will support the expansion of the reuse water system in North Fort Myers to increase reclaimed water availability for irrigation. This project will reduce potable water demand, support community growth, and promote long-term water resource sustainability in the service area.
2013.purpose: The project will construct improvements to the reclaimed water system, including expansion of the reuse distribution network, installation of supporting infrastructure, and system upgrades to deliver additional reclaimed water for irrigation.This project will reduce potable water demand, support community growth, and promote long-term water resource sustainability in the service area.
2013.activities: These activities will increase reuse availability and reduce potable water use in the service area.Increased reclaimed water availability through construction of reuse water mains supports future residential and commercial development and reduces potable water demand, lowering long term utility costs. Reduction in potable water withdrawals and increased reuse irrigation helps conserve regional freshwater and protect natural ecosystems.
2013.direct_services: Citizens will receive reuse water at their residences or commercial establishments such as golf courses or sod farms will receive reuse water for use in irrigation purposes. Governmental entities will also benefit in use of reuse water for irrigation at parks, ball fields, stadiums or other governmental buildings.
2013.population: All residents and citizens of North Fort Myers and Lee County will benefit from use of reuse water. Increased reclaimed water availability supports future residential and commercial development and reduces potable water demand, lowering long term utility costs.
2013.outcome: Reducing reliance on groundwater withdrawals helps protect the aquifer from over-extraction and saltwater intrusion. Track the number of new reuse connections and compare annual reclaimed vs. potable water usage in utility reports. Measure annual potable water savings (gallons) and increased reclaimed water usage through utility reporting and compliance documents.

2014.description: In response to one of the State of Florida's initiatives, this project converts up to 300 septic tank sewer systems in the FGUA North Fort Myers service area to an updated collective sanitation and treatment system.The project area includes lower-income customers, and additional funding would significantly reduce their financial burden.
2014.purpose: The project is focused on improving water quality and sanitation in the FGUA North Fort Myers service area by transitioning septic tank sewer systems to a more modern and reliable treatment system. This is beneficial not only for residents but also for the surrounding environment, particularly the Caloosahatchee Basin and Estuaries, which are impacted by excessive nutrient loading.
2014.activities: Construction of sewer mains and connection of homes to sewer line for collection and transmission of wastewater to collective sewage treatment plant. Wastewater will receive treatment in excess of that provided by septic tanks. Septic tanks will be taken out of service.
2014.direct_services: Sewage treatment will be provided to citizens minimizing maintenance of septic tank systems, minimizing sewage overflows or issues with septic tank systems during flooding or weather events.
2014.population: Residents of North Fort Myers. Project will take approximately 300 homes off septic tanks so assuming 4 persons per household, approximatelly 1200 individuals will be served and benefit from the project.
2014.outcome: North Fort Meyers is located within a BMAP. A centralized sewer collection, treatment and effluent disposal system allows for the removal of septic tanks which reduces the nutrient loading on the groundwater and surface water. FGUA will communicate with the water management district for its sampling results in monitoring ground water nutrient loading and improvement as septic systems are taken off line.

3136.description: These funds will be used to demo/clean-up a dilapidated & abandoned retail center damaged/destroyed by Hurricane Michael, paving the way for development of the site. his property was devastated by Hurricane Michael in October 2018. This once thriving retail center is now abandoned and dilapidated. The City of Marianna proposes to buy this property, partner with a private developer who will develop this space to a retail center in accordance to the needs of the community and eventually assume full ownership.
3136.purpose: These funds will be used to demo/clean-up a dilapidated & abandoned retail center damaged/destroyed by Hurricane Michael, paving the way for development of the site.
3136.direct_services: Increased quality of life based on the clean-up of this dilapidated three acre site
3136.population: Marianna along with Jackson and the surrounding Counties
3136.outcome: The redevelopment of this space into a retail center that will revitalize parts of the City of Marianna, providing jobs and increased the City's tax base.

3143.organization: Ocean City Wright Fire Control District
3143.description: The Ocean City Wright Fire District currently houses, responds with, and maintains the only 100 foot platform aerial firefighting apparatus in Okaloosa County. That apparatus is aging and is in need of refurbishment.
