The goal of this funding is to enhance current fire service capability in Okaloosa County by refurbishing dated and aging equipment with new components to increase reliability of this critical equipment. This refurbishment project has been chosen for fiscal responsibility.
3143.purpose: The Ocean City Wright Fire District currently houses, responds with, and maintains the only 100 foot platform aerial firefighting apparatus in Okaloosa County. That apparatus is aging and need of refurbishment. The goal of this funding is to enhance current fire service capability in Okaloosa County by refurbishing dated and aging equipment with new components to increase reliability of this critical equipment. This refurbishment project has been chosen for fiscal responsibility.
3143.activities: Citizens in communities throughout the panhandle and state of Florida will be the recipients of emergency response from highly trained professional firefighters operating the most advanced technology available.
3143.direct_services: Citizens will receive reliable fire service response including elevated rescue capabilities, rescue from multistory occupancies on fire, and high angle rope rescue emergencies. Additional elevated fire streams for extinguishment provide tactical advantages not available from other types of firefighting apparatus.
3143.population: Fire service professionals and the citizens of the communities they protect. These individuals include local citizens and citizens statewide through mutual aid agreements.
3143.outcome: This project will be used to protect and rescue citizens during fire and a multitude of other emergencies. It will protect an area that has a high concentration of military personnel, retired veterans, and a high traffic tourist area. The level of benefit is measured by the availability of reliable and updated firefighting technology. Emergencies cannot be predicted, therefore, our measurement is preparedness.

3149.description: A local- custom designed neuro-diverse playground offers a safe, inclusive space with sensory-friendly equipment to support children with autism and neuro-diverse disorders. It aims to enhance sensory, motor, social skills, and emotional well-being, helping children engage, relax, build confidence, and improve their overall development and quality of life. We worked with Edwin Watts ( to design a putting green portion of the playground,(one example of the partnering local businesses) spotlighting the history of our county (home of the special olympics & golf gold medalist, Patrick Rosser and Michael Embry, 2025 Special Olympic Athlete Award Winner).
3149.purpose: This neuro-diverse playground offers a safe, inclusive space with sensory-friendly equipment to support children with autism and neuro-diverse disorders. It aims to enhance sensory, motor, social skills, and emotional well-being, helping children engage, relax, build confidence, and improve their overall development and quality of life.
3149.activities: The custom designed/built playground and equipment will help to develop and improve the sensory, motor, social skills and emotional well being of the children (and subsequently including but limited to tunnels, putting greens and rock climbing( teaching concentration and patience skills), plus hand- eye coordination. The difference in the child's behavior will greatly improve the structure of each family as they see the difference proper developmental activities and skills education makes in the
3149.direct_services: Developmental and coping skills training in addition to physical skills improvement.
3149.population: 101-200 individual students (each school year) will be served however, as the school grows ( already moving into a new larger campus facility with more expansions planned).
3149.outcome: ASHA knows this funding will significantly improve the quality of life and developmental opportunities for neuro-diverse children in our community . The new playground will attract families seeking specialized educational resources, boosting community growth. Supporting this initiative aligns with our commitment to inclusive, innovative, and supportive educational environments. Detailed records will track the additional new student enrollments based on the addition of these opportunities the academy offers families in our community. Also the improved developmental skills will be tracked by the staff and admin of the Academy and reported to the funding agency.

3151.description: Improve an unpaved connector between State Road 85 and CR Hwy 2 in Laurel Hill, utilized by local residents, agricultural and silvicultural vehicles with potential for increased traffic volume. Millside Road scored near the top of Okaloosa County's "Dirt to Pave" matrix and was listed among impaired sites in the Yellow River Watershed in Alabama and Florida, in a 2010 FWC Report. Improvements include paving, guardrails, road and crosswalk striping and reflective pavement markers, traffic signage, and establishing ROW for 3 miles between SR 85 and Steel Mill Creek Road. Okaloosa County is seeking a state appropriation of $1.5 Million dollars for the Millside Road "Dirt to Pave" project.
3151.purpose: To improve an unpaved connector between State Road 85 and CR Hwy 2 to enhance stability and safety of the road and road conditions, and protect from sediment erosion that negatively impacts the Yellow River Watershed.
3151.activities: Construction and construction engineering and inspection services.
3151.direct_services: The project will include paving of the dirt road with additional right-of-way. guardrails, striping and reflective pavement markers, traffic signage and pedestrian crosswalk striping to enhance public and vehicular safety. Dirt to pave will also improve water quality by eliminating sediment runoff into wetland areas, as identified in the Yellow River Watershed Alabama and Florida 2010 FWC report.
3151.population: Millside Road is the connector between two major highways in the northern portion of the County and will serve local residents, and commercial agricultural and timber businesses.
3151.outcome: Benefits of the project include increased stability and safety of road conditions in general, especially during and immediately after heavy rain and major weather events. Regular maintenance of the paved road will proactively ensure safer driving conditions and continued use not impacted by flooding and wash-outs due to major weather events.

1815.description: The funds will support Miami Arts Studio 6-12 @ Zelda Glazer (MAS), a magnet school for the performing and visual arts, created due to a lack of access for students talented in the arts. MAS offers a high-quality and extensive academic and arts curriculum encompassing middle school and high school level programs in visual art, digital art, dance, music, theater, broadcasting, and entertainment law. in addition, MAS hosts a Saturday orchestra program for local elementary students in grades 3-5.
1815.purpose: The funds will support Miami Arts Studio 6-12 @ Zelda Glazer (MAS), a magnet school for the performing and visual arts, created due to a lack of access for students talented in the arts. MAS offers a high-quality and extensive academic and arts curriculum encompassing middle school and high school level programs in visual art, digital art, dance, music, theater, broadcasting, and entertainment law. in addition, MAS hosts a Saturday orchestra program for local elementary students in grades 3-5.
1815.activities: Miami Arts Studio 6-12 @ Zelda Glazer (MAS) offers a high-quality and extensive academic and arts curriculum encompassing middle school and high school level programs in visual art, digital art, dance, music, theater, broadcasting, and entertainment law. In addition to our magnet programs in grades 6-8, MAS hosts a Saturday orchestra program for local elementary students in grades 3-5.
1815.direct_services: Miami Arts Studio 6-12 @ Zelda Glazer offers a program of academic and artistic studies which shall be available to talented middle school and high school students. These skills are transferable to the cultural capital of Miami-Dade County as well as to the robust visual and performing arts industry workforce. Cultural experiences and performances are offered to the community for no or low cost.
1815.population: Over 800 elementary, middle, and high school students throughout Miami-Dade County Public Schools.
1815.outcome: The expected benefits and outcomes of this project include enriching the cultural experience, improving the quality of education for students, and increasing access for students talented in the performing and visual arts to receive high- level, performing arts and entertainment industry–focused educational opportunities. These outcomes will be measured using documentation of performances, enrollment statistics, competition awards, scholarship awards, college acceptances, program materials, expert contracts, and disbursement/expense reports.

1814.description: Mental health treatment and crisis intervention is provided to those at-risk of suicide and/or significant emotional distress. The 2023 Community Health Needs Assessment ranked mental health as Miami-Dade's #2 priority with 11% unable to access needed services. A dedicated team of trauma-informed counselors addresses safety needs and ensures life-saving resources are accessible to all persons served regardless of ability to pay. Clinical approaches utilize best practices with integrated supports for improved quality of life and self-sufficiency. Crisis and suicide prevention counseling is available 24/7/365. Person-centered services empower individuals and families to achieve goals in physical/mental health, education, economic self-sufficiency, and justice diversion. Achievements are measured through CFARS/FARS assessments and improvement in functioning.
1814.purpose: Funds will provide mental health counseling and treatment and community crisis response for those at-risk of suicide and/or significant emotional distress. A dedicated team of trauma-informed counselors from JCS, a faith-based agency, address safety needs and ensure life-saving resources are accessible to persons served. Clinical approaches utilize best practices and involve integration of supports for improved quality of life and self-sufficiency. Achievements will be demonstrated by the number
1814.activities: Professional social services and clinical staff are trained to deliver counseling services to children, adolescents, adults, elders, and families in trauma-informed care and evidence based practices to address crisis and mental health difficulties. Crisis counseling will be available 24/7/365 and addresses immediate threats to ensure safety and stability. Care coordination ensures individuals are assessed and referred to appropriate levels of care and follow up is conducted. Mental health counse
1814.direct_services: Direct services provided to citizens includes 24/7/365 access to a suicide prevention crisis counselors trained to deescalate the situation and take action to ensure safety and stability. Care coordination protocols also assess the severity of a crisis, determining the appropriate level of care, and coordinating with first responders, emergency services, or mental health professionals. Individual
1814.population: The target population includes: older adults, persons with poor mental health and/ or poor physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, homeless, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, substance abusers, preschool and grade school students, high school students, university/college students, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, drug offenders (in criminal Justice), and victims of crime. Approximately 75,000 calls will be answered, assessed an
1814.outcome: This project aims to reduce rates of suicide, enhance mental health access, decrease reliance on emergency services, reduce unsafe and unhealthy behaviors, and improve quality of life and self-sufficiency of persons served. It will improve individual stability and well-being through culturally-competent, trauma-informed counseling and coordination of care. Outcomes will be tracked by monitoring call volume, response effectiveness, client referrals, and improvements in daily functioning. Metrics include the number of diverted emergency responses, engagement in follow-up services, improvement in functioning, and quality of life measures, all of which can be calculated to demonstrate cost avoid

1813.description: To provide Transitional Housing, including support services, for homeless persons with special needs being discharged from Jackson Health Systems (JHS), the public hospital. Including homeless persons identified through data sharing with JHS who present with serious mental illness, substance abuse or medical disabilities coming from the correctional health, hospital ER or crisis. Persons placed are currently enrolled in the Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) and high utilizers of the services rendered by the public hospital.
1813.purpose: Reduces homelessness and utlization of the public health system.
1813.activities: To provide Transitional Housing with supportive services for homeless persons with special needs being discharged from Jackson Health Systems (JHS), the public hospital, including homeless persons identified through data sharing with JHS who present with serious mental illness, substance abuse or medical disabilities coming from the correctional health, hospital ER or crisis. Persons placed are currently enrolled in the Homeless Management Information System and high utilizers of the services re
1813.direct_services: Case management and care coordination to connect clients with resources like housing, employment, healthcare, and financial assistance. Continuing primary care and behavioral health care; supportive housing and housing navigation. On site services include beds, hygiene facilities, meals, clothing, etc.
1813.population: Homeless persons with special needs being discharged from Jackson Health Systems (JHS), the public hospital, including homeless persons identified through data sharing with JHS who present with serious mental illness, substance abuse or medical disabilities coming from the correctional health, hospital ER or crisis. Persons placed are currently enrolled in HMIS and high utilizers of the services rendered by the public hospital.
1813.outcome: Pre and post intervention data provided by Jackson Health Systems indicates a 50% reduction in admissions. 8% of participants increase employment income per HMIS.

1810.organization: University of Miami Miller School of Medicine
1810.description: The Miami Project to Cure Paralysis has assembled an international team of scientists, physicians and therapists and is the nation's premier investigative program conducting cutting-edge discovery, translational, and clinical investigations targeting brain and spinal cord injuries. This involves moving promising new research in the areas of neuroprotection, cell therapy, drug discovery, rehabilitation, and neuromodulation approaches to clinical application in humans. Our comprehensive quality of life programs addresses issues like neuropathic pain, bladder and bowel function, cardiometabolic health. Discoveries made at The Miami Project have been successfully translated to clinically relevant models of brain and spinal cord injury thus providing essential proof-of-concept data to determine future human studies. This research has the potential to be translated to treat other neurological
1810.purpose: Miami Project to Cure Paralysis scientists, physicians and therapists conduct carefully designed research move promising neuroprotective, cellular therapies, drug discoveries, advanced rehabilitation and neuromodulation strategies, neuropathic pain, cardiovascular disorders, and mental health approaches to clinical application for those suffering from traumatic brain and spinal cord injury, concussion, and other neurological diseases including Parkinson’s disease, MS, and ALS. In addition, the f
1810.activities: The research that will be conducted includes basic science to further understand the pathophysiology of neurological disorders, translational research necessary to move these basic discoveries forward to clinical application and our clinical trials which are testing these therapies in research subjects to determine their safety and efficacy. The Miami Project has established a successful pipeline for the translation of new discoveries to the clinic that has already resulted in significant improv
1810.direct_services: Individuals who qualify for our clinical trials will be enrolled and able to participate in our research studies.
1810.population: The target populations served by this project are billions people living in Florida and throughout the United States who are currently living with a spinal cord injury, peripheral nerve injury, traumatic brain injury, concussion, and other neurodegenerative diseases and disorders such as ALS, Muscular Sclerosis, Alzheimer's disease, dementia, stroke, Parkinson's Disease amongst others.
1810.outcome: Each project will address specific research questions that are highly relevant to an important scientific problem using established technologies and experimental protocols. During the funding period, progress will be evaluated by written progress reports including qualitative and quantitative data related to the proposed specific aims. These findings will then be submitted to scientific journals for peer review and publication.

2632.description: The City of Belle Isle Police Department is requesting funding to replace two aging marine patrol vessels and acquire one side-by-side utility vehicle to enhance emergency response and waterway safety operations on the Conway Chain of Lakes. These assets will improve patrol efficiency, expand search and rescue capabilities, and strengthen disaster response readiness. Florida’s recent hurricanes and flooding events have shown the critical need for dependable marine resources. The upgraded equipment will ensure the Department can protect residents, support environmental enforcement, and assist other communities statewide during recovery efforts. This project promotes public safety, preserves surface water quality, and helps maintain a safe, welcoming environment for tourism and recreation.
2632.purpose: The requested funds will replace two aging marine patrol vessels and add a side-by-side utility vehicle to enhance the Belle Isle Police Department’s ability to protect the Conway Chain of Lakes and surrounding community. These upgrades will improve law enforcement efficiency, emergency response, and environmental protection while ensuring readiness to assist statewide during floods, hurricanes, and other major emergencies.
2632.activities: The funds will support law enforcement patrols, search and rescue operations, environmental enforcement, and disaster response on the Conway Chain of Lakes. The new vessels and side-by-side will allow officers to conduct regular waterway safety checks, respond quickly to boating accidents or flooding, and assist with statewide recovery and mutual aid missions when requested.
2632.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from enhanced safety and faster emergency response on the Conway Chain of Lakes and surrounding areas. The new vessels and side-by-side will allow officers to respond more quickly to distress calls, conduct water rescues, enforce boating and environmental laws, and protect residents and visitors during severe weather or flooding events.
2632.population: The project serves both local residents and the many visitors who come to enjoy the Conway Chain of Lakes for boating, fishing, and recreation. By improving patrol capability and emergency response, the project enhances safety for all who use the waterways while supporting tourism and providing a secure, well-maintained environment for community and visitor activities.
2632.outcome: The project will enhance public safety, environmental protection, and disaster readiness on the Conway Chain of Lakes. Upgraded marine vessels and the side-by-side will improve emergency response times, reduce boating accidents, and strengthen the Department’s ability to assist during hurricanes and flooding. Success will be measured through response time data, incident reports, environmental compliance records, and documented mutual aid participation.

1966.description: This program serves individuals with developmental/intellectual disabilities. JARC partners with local businesses to provide on-the-job training for participants. They work side by side with the employees of the business. This not only provides the individual with opportunities for community integration and employment, but also educates the community on the abilities of individuals with special needs. This program began in Palm Beach County and has now expanded into Broward County.
1966.purpose: Funds will secure community-based employment training for individuals with intellectual disabilities and autism. With a goal of employment, individuals with special needs will reduce their dependence on government subsidies.
1966.activities: JARC will work with local businesses to secure partnerships for the community-based employment training. Individuals with intellectual disabilities and autism will receive job coaching services.
1966.direct_services: On the job training at local businesses. This will be completed with supervision from trained Job Coaches to maximize the potential for independent employment.
1966.population: Support to the families of the individuals receiving services. The program has grown every year, and currently provides services to 85 individuals and their families.
1966.outcome: A minimum of 30 participants will receive training in how to develop a resume and how to interact in a job interview. With a goal of community-based employment, a minimum of 6 individuals will become employed by the partner businesses. Outcomes will be measured by the number of partner businesses and the number of individuals employed.

1796.description: The High Flood Swift Water Rescue Program will enhance the City of Boynton Beach Fire Department’s ability to respond effectively to natural disasters, flooding emergencies and storm surge events statewide. The program will establish a comprehensive high flood swift water response system, ensuring the safety and well-being of the community during extreme weather conditions. By procuring the specialized equipment, it will enable the fire department to navigate flooded areas, perform rescues, and deliver critical supplies to affected individuals and families. The High Flood Swift Water Rescue Program will play a critical role in protecting lives and property in these high-risk scenarios, providing rapid response capabilities deployable statewide. This initiative aligns with the commitment to public safety, disaster preparedness, and community resilience, addressing a critical need in the f
1796.purpose: The High Flood Swift Water Rescue Response Program will have a 50/50 cost share. Funding will assist in procuring the vehicle and vessels needed for rapid response capabilities for swift water rescue missions in the City and statewide during natural disasters that are prone to flooding and storm surge events. The unit will consist of a High-Water Rescue Vehicle along with a double-stack trailer carrying both rigid bottom metal and inflatable rescue boats deployable for natural disasters and to p
1796.activities: The City will establish a comprehensive High Flood Swift Water Rescue Response program as a statewide resource. Personnel will complete 40 hours of comprehensive training increasing our response capability. Conduct life saving rescue missions statewide ad provide transportation of essential needs to area inaccessible. All training and operating costs will be provided to ensure reliability and readiness. The Fire Department will provide the necessary personnel, training and operating costs to ens
1796.direct_services: The deployment of the High Water Rescue Unit and watercraft during flooding events to rescue stranded individuals and families. The ability to transport essential supplies, such as food, water, and medical aid, to areas inaccessible due to flooding. The ability to assist in evacuation of residents from high-risk zones to safe locations. Ability to collaborate with local and state emergency managem
1796.population: Serving the City of Boynton Beach, Florida—a coastal city with a population of approximately 80,000 that is vulnerable to flooding and storm surges. Would be readily available as a statewide resource. The target population would serve but not limited too a diverse group such as the elderly, physically disabled, persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, jobless, economically disadvantaged, at-risk-youth, homeless, preschool through college students, and the general popul
1796.outcome: To be in a state of preparedness as a statewide resource for protecting lives, property, and ensuring community resilience during extreme weather events. The percentage of all fire department personnel that complete the 40 hour comprehensive High water Flood Response System training on implementation will be the methodology to determine the state of preparedness. The percentage of personnel trained will show the state of readiness and the fire department's ability to respond to all High Water Rescue Events.

2160.description: The Samaritan Resource Center (SRC), a walk-in homeless resource center, partners with University of Central Florida (UCF), CareerSource Central Florida, Valencia College, Goodwill Industries, and others to provide training and education for jobs in high-demand sectors like hospitality and healthcare. This program empowers individuals, including working, underemployed individuals, to transition from homelessness to stability while filling workforce gaps and strengthening the economy. Orange County leadership supports this program, alongside leaders of the local faith community. We have also expressions of support from our corporate supporters including AdventHealth and Aspire Health Partners, as well as partners like UCF, CareerSource Central Florida, Valenica College, Goodwill Industries, and Second Harvest Food Bank.
2160.purpose: Samaritan Resource Center, in conjunction with its workforce and education partners, will address two critical needs: helping individuals experiencing homelessness gain employment and stability while also addressing unfilled, higher- wage job openings in our region.
2160.activities: Funding will provide skills training, upskilling, housing assistance, job placement, and case management, empowering individuals to transition from homelessness to stability while filling workforce gaps and strengthening the economy. Our education and workforce partners will provide training for jobs in sectors like hospitality and health care, where millions of higher-wage roles remain unfilled.
2160.direct_services: Funding will directly assist 50-100 homeless individuals in East Orange County by providing case management to address challenges and support long-term stability, enabling them to secure sustainable employment while contributing to the local economy. This offering reduces burden on local crisis resources for the homeless, including law enforcement, while empowering individuals.
2160.population: 50-100 homeless individuals in East Orange County are expected to be served by this initiative.
2160.outcome: 1. # of participants connected with mental health resources: Employment provides individuals with a sense of purpose and accomplishment, which can boost self-esteem and overall wellbeing, having a positive impact on mental health. We will partner with mental health providers to ensure the progress and stability of those we serve. 2. Increased or improved economic activity: We will have our own internal database as well as the local Continuum of Care's HMIS system to measure progress in training, employment outcomes, employment retention and obtaining housing. This will be measured by Samaritan Resource Center's data collection, training partners’ enrollment data, and the local Continuum of C

2162.description: We are committed to offering an affordable Summer Camp to Central Florida families, where the children can explore and discover their human potential. The program aims to bring awareness to children in our communities and familiarize them with civic responsibility and participation. The program staff works hard to inspire resilience, curiosity, and a sense of “yes we can” in the participants and their families.
2162.purpose: Provide a summer camp for the community at no cost. We are committed to offering an affordable Summer Camp to Central Florida families, where the children can explore and discover their human potential. The program aims to bring awareness to children in our communities and familiarize them with civic responsibility and participation. The program staff works hard to inspire resilience, curiosity, and a sense of ownership and agency in the participants and their families.
2162.activities: Summer will be completely free serving the community. The program will include leadership development, outdoor activities, and educational opportunities within the American culture.
2162.direct_services: Summer camp for Osceola and Orange County residents
2162.population: Hispanic Community. We plan to serve from 50 to 120 families.
2162.outcome: Our program instills a sense of personal responsibility in the youth, encouraging them to be stewards of our environment and to become positive contributors to their communities. With the Latino population in Orange County having grown steadily in recent years, our mission is to provide a place where all youth can immerse themselves in Latino arts and culture. This allows them to connect across racial and economic divides, fostering unity in the protection of our communities and environment.

2163.description: Our focus in this program is to celebrate the American culture of the people of Florida, uplifting local talent and providing an opportunity for networking and a market for vendors from across the region. With support from the State of Florida, we’ll be able to expand our impact by building strong communities with rich history and culture celebrating our neighborhoods, and networking about opportunities for advancement in business, the arts, education, and health.
2163.purpose: The engagement program are hosted at no cost. The events include community partnerships, leadership and education opportunities.
2163.activities: Provide different opportunities for the community such as assistance programs, career opportunities, networking events, and education opportunities.
2163.direct_services: education and connection regarding resources around leadership development using education activities.
2163.population: Both Orange and Osceola residents. Around 200-500 individuals will be served.
2163.outcome: The methodology will be measured by attendance rate and community awareness of certain assistance in the county.

3158.description: This project expands wastewater capacity in North Okaloosa by installing a new sewer main parallel to I-10, from Okaloosa Lane to the Shoal River Ranch Water Reclamation Facility (SRRWRF). It will divert flow south of Hwy 90 to SRRWRF, freeing up capacity along Hwy 90 East for future development. Upsizing this main would also provide alternate flow from the eastern side of Crestview, relieving the City's system and plant. It creates an opportunity to partner with FDOT to decommission an aging package plant at an I-10 rest area. Constructed in-house to reduce costs, this septic to sewer initiative supports regional growth and improves water quality by shifting future development to public sewer. It complements the SRRWRF’s role as a regional facility and represents a significant infrastructure investment for North Okaloosa.
3158.purpose: The requested funds will support construction of the Interstate 10 Sewer Transmission Main, expanding wastewater capacity and the potential for regionalization of wastewater treatment in North Okaloosa. The new infrastructure supports population and economic growth, environmental protection, public well-being, and job creation. It improves wastewater management and helps safeguard surface and drinking water quality.
3158.activities: To meet the intended purpose of these funds, the County will construct a new sewer transmission main along the northern boundary of the I-10 corridor using in-house forces. Activities include site preparation, material procurement, easement acquisition on private parcels, potential coordination with FDOT for right-of-way access, and installation of the transmission main from Okaloosa Lane to the SRRWRF. The project also includes a potential collaboration with FDOT to decommission an aging packag
3158.direct_services: This project will directly benefit citizens by expanding access to reliable public sewer infrastructure, reducing reliance on septic systems. It will support future residential and commercial development by increasing wastewater capacity, improving environmental protection, and enhancing water quality. The upgraded system will reduce the risk of septic failures, protect groundwater, and promote he
3158.population: The target population includes residents, businesses, and industrial users in North Okaloosa County, particularly those near the Shoal River Industrial Park site and surrounding residential and commercial development areas. The proposed project is currently planned to reroute wastewater flow from 500-550 residential units (townhomes and multi family residences) along Okaloosa Lane which house up to 1,350 residents, at the County's current population of 2.66 persons per household.
3158.outcome: The project will increase regional wastewater transmission capacity, enabling future residential and commercial development, reducing reliance on septic systems, and improving environmental protection and water quality. It will also relieve pressure on existing infrastructure, contributing to long-term sustainability and public health. Outcomes to be measured by the following: - Volume of wastewater diverted to the SRRWRF - Number of new connections enabled by the proposed transmission main - Increase in available capacity within the Hwy 90 East County and City of Crestview collection systems - Reduction in septic system usage within the service area

3160.organization: Community Solutions of the Emerald Coast
3160.description: One Hopeful Place (OHP) seeks funding to construct a new facility that will provide restrooms, showers, a commercial kitchen, and a dining area to serve individuals sheltered in its 48-bed emergency facility as well as vulnerable members of the community during times of crisis. This addition will strengthen OHPs capacity to meet basic needs, enhance shelter operations, and ensure safe, sanitary, and dignified care for those experiencing homelessness or displacement during emergencies.
3160.purpose: This project will fund the construction of The Gathering Place, a new multi-purpose facility on the One Hopeful Place campus designed to expand essential infrastructure, increase service capacity, and strengthen community response during times of need. The building will feature restrooms, showers, a commercial kitchen, and a dining area to serve individuals housed in OHP’s 48-bed emergency shelter, as well as unsheltered residents and vulnerable community members seeking assistance during extrem
3160.activities: The Gathering Place will function as a community service hub offering daily meal preparation, hygiene access, and emergency operations support. The commercial kitchen will prepare and serve meals for shelter residents and community outreach programs, while the restrooms and showers will provide essential sanitation for participants and guests. The dining area will also serve as a multipurpose space for meals, volunteer engagement, community meetings, and partner agency collaboration during cold-
3160.direct_services: Citizens will gain access to vital day-to-day services such as meals, showers, restrooms, and safe space for support during emergencies. The facility will directly serve individuals experiencing homelessness, those temporarily displaced by weather, and community members participating in outreach or recovery programs. These direct services will promote health, safety, and a sense of belonging for h
3160.population: The project will serve adults experiencing homelessness, low-income individuals in crisis, and community members impacted by severe weather or emergencies. It is estimated that The Gathering Place will serve over 900 individuals annually through meal service, hygiene programs, outreach initiatives, and emergency shelter activation. The facility will also support collaborative programming with local agencies to meet emerging community needs.
3160.outcome: The project will result in a fully operational facility that expands OHP’s reach and strengthens community resilience. Expected outcomes include increased service capacity, improved public health and sanitation, and greater access to essential resources for vulnerable populations. Success will be measured through HMIS data, internal service tracking, partner agency reports, and documented community usage, ensuring accountability and measurable impact across all programs served by the facility.

2900.description: This project begin the restoration and stabilization of 3,000 feet of natural habitat that currently protects Harbour Island residents. The shoreline will be shaped and stabilized in a manner that reduces shoreline degradation and increases natural habitat.
2900.purpose: The goal of the project is to restore the natural marine buffer that protects the Harbour Island community and the adjacent shipping channel from damage caused by flood events.
2900.activities: Implement nature-based solutions that blend erosion control with habitat restoration, enhancing the natural ecological health of the shoreline.
2900.direct_services: Direct services include flood impact protection and an increase in natural habitat.
2900.population: A total of 4,423 residents of the Harbour Island community will benefit from the project.
2900.outcome: Improved natural habitat and a reduction in scouring of a natural buffer. Monitoring of sediment erosion will be documented in the construction completion reports.

2164.description: The program's primary goal is to mitigate financial risk and dependence on public assistance for at-risk populations in Orange County, thereby improving their economic self-sufficiency. Funds will be used to provide comprehensive financial literacy education, including individualized counseling and structured workshops on budgeting, saving, debt management, and responsible credit use.
2164.purpose: The goal is to mitigate financial risk and dependence on public assistance for the at-risk population and improve the economic self-sufficiency of participants in Orange County.
2164.activities: Delivering financial education curricula in structured cohorts. Providing individualized financial counseling to each participant to develop customized budgets, debt management plans, and savings strategies.
2164.direct_services: The key direct service is personalized financial mentoring and coaching provided by certified counselors. This includes support in opening bank accounts, understanding credit reports, and accessing asset-building resources.
2164.population: The target population includes: Persons with poor mental health, jobless persons, drug users (in health services), and victims of crime.
2164.outcome: Expected Outcome 1: 70% of participants adopt a key behavior change (e.g., sticking to a budget, opening savings). Methodology: Behavior Change Survey (3-6 months after the program). Expected Outcome 2: 35% of participants report a decrease in perceived financial stress levels. Methodology: Stress Perception Surveys (Likert scale) before and after the program.

2177.description: The City of Tallahassee seeks to establish a state-of-the-art Law Enforcement Training Facility alongside the Tallahassee Police Department Headquarters Building. This training facility will provide law enforcement officers with the essential resources needed to maintain skills, prepare new recruits for real-world challenges, and learn techniques and strategies in a controlled environment. The Facility, spanning over 37,000 square feet, will include a Firearms Training Simulation Room, a Defensive Tactics Room, and a Physical Agility Room.
2177.purpose: The goal of the facility will be to have better trained officers and thereby increase public safety in the community.
2177.activities: The funding will be used to construct the 37,000-square foot training facility, which will include a Firearms Training Simulation Room, a Defensive Tactics Room, and a Physical Agility Room.
2177.direct_services: Services provided to citizens will be better trained officers that will improve community safety and savings on training expenses of the department.
2177.population: The general public of the City of Tallahassee will be served by this project, approximately 200,000 individuals.
2177.outcome: Through construction of this facility, the public will have better trained officers, and the department will have the ability to more effectively recruit and retain officers. Data from use of force interactions can be used to compare outcomes prior to and after the construction of the training facility. The position vacancy rates will demonstrate recruitment and retention success.

1963.description: This funding will enable installation of a hyperlocal flood monitoring sensor network and data intelligence platform, as has been achieved in other locations around the state. This platform benefits the public at large, as well as strengthens capabilities for real-time emergency management for ground-truth data to enable alerts, proactive road closure. water level and flood data sets empower actionable mitigation for infrastructure protection planning and vulnerability assessment response.
1963.purpose: This funding will enable installation of a hyperlocal flood monitoring sensor network and data intelligence platform, as has been achieved in other locations around the state. This platform benefits the public at large, as well as strengthens capabilities for real-time emergency management for ground-truth data to enable alerts, proactive road closure. water level and flood data sets empower actionable mitigation for infrastructure protection planning and vulnerability assessment response.
1963.activities: The project allows for installation of 25 new real-time, self-contained, water level and inundation sensors around Live Oak, at sites prioritized by local government officials and in consultation with state agencies and NWS forecasters. Comprehensive maintenance, telemetry, cyberinfrastructure, and data analytics are all-inclusive and guaranteed.
1963.direct_services: Citizens benefit directly by filling gaps in data availability and through publicly available data and alerts, as well as from enhanced emergency operations support during flooding events, and ability to make data-informed decisions for longer-term planning of mitigation and adaptation to flooding events.
1963.population: The project will target the population of the greater Suwannee County service area serving approximately 45,000 people with real time flood information during heavy rain events or natural disasters through a real time sensor network and internal/public dashboard to inform government and public decisions.
1963.outcome: A real-time flooding intelligence platform empowers Emergency Operators to make better, data-driven decisions for road closures, evacuations, and first responder activities, as well as provide longer-term data for management decisions for infrastructure protection (bridges, roads, buildings).Densification of a surface water level sensor network assists with real-time operations of pump stations, as well as planning for future water management needs. Measurable through direct website and mobile app engagement analytics.

1827.description: The purpose of this project is to drill a replacement well for the Riversink water system. The current second well in Riversink does not supply quality water. A new replacement well will ensure a reliable and backup water source for the growing community in Wakulla County.
1827.purpose: The project will provide high quality water and capacity for the community.
1827.outcome: The project will provide high quality water to the community. This will be measured by the annual water quality report sent to Talquin Members of the water system.

1805.organization: Dixie County Board of County Commissioners
1805.description: In FY 2022-23, Dixie County was appropriated funds for two fire stations (SF1577 and SF 1578). Through cost-cutting measures, the County spent under budget on the Old Town Fire Station (SF 1578). Due to increased construction and equipment costs, the EOC Fire Station has outstanding needs. The savings of $289,026 from Old Town Fire Station (SF 1578) can be used to complete critical public safety needs for the EOC Fire Station (SF 1577). The County requests the remaining funds from the Old Town Fire Station (SF 1578) revert and be reappropriated to the EOC Fire Station Addition (SF 1577).
1805.purpose: In FY 2022-23, Dixie County was appropriated funds for two fire stations, (SF 1577/HB 3749 and HB 3751/SF 1578). Through cost-cutting measures, the County spent under budget on the Old Town Fire Station (SF 1579). Due to increased construction and equipment costs, the EOC Fire Station has outstanding needs. The savings of $289,026 for Old Town Fire Station can be used to complete critical public safety needs for the EOC Fire Station (SF 1577).
1805.activities: These funds will be used for repaving the parking lot, implementing erosion control measures, furnishings for the station and office areas, and equipment.
1805.direct_services: The completion of the EOC Fire Station will allow efficient and quick response of services to citizens.
1805.population: Dixie County, thousands of individuals will be served.
1805.outcome: Completion of the EOC Fire Station allows for critical safety needs of citizens to be fulfilled. Efficient and quick response of services will be a benefit.

1807.organization: Dixie County Board of County Commissioners
1807.description: The funds will be for design and engineering of the renovation and expansion of the Dixie County Tax Collector’s office. The expansion will allow the tax collector to meet the growing needs of the County and provide streamlined services for the residents of Dixie County. Additionally, increased office space will result in the tax collector’s office serving more residents.
1807.purpose: The funds will be for design and engineering of the renovation and expansion of the Dixie County Tax Collector's office. The expansion will allow the tax collector to meet the growing needs of the County and provide streamlined services for the residents of Dixie County. Additionally, increased office space will result in the tax collector's office serving more residents.

1826.outcome: Requested funds will support Dixie County in a phased approach of making critical improvements and equipment purchases for their solid waste transfer station. The increased efficiency of the solid waste transfer station can be used to measure the outcome.

1794.purpose: Continue to provide family caregivers with in-facility respite day care, case management and caregiver training and support services. The Day Care services allow family members to work while their loved ones with Alzheimer's Disease, Dementia and Memory Loss Disorders are provided with positive and stimulating activities and programs in a safe and secure environment.

We are anticipating serving at least 30 caregivers and 30 clients for a total of 60 individuals due to the increasing aging population and the number of individuals being diagnosed with dementia and memory loss.
1794.outcome: The expected benefit and outcome of this project is for the clients to receive both physically and mentally stimulating activities and programs in a loving and nurturing environment by improving their quality of life. These services allow caregivers to be able to continue to work in knowing their loved ones are in a safe and secure environment. The services decrease the caregivers' burdens and stress as they learn to cope with caring for their loved one and receive a break through the respite and caregiver training and support services. 2025.description: Beautify and secure the walkway and street ends on the North and South side of Pier Park. The improvements will support pedestrian safety, traffic flow and infrastructure as well as beautifying the street ends in conjunction with the transformation and revitalization of the park into an upscale, resident friendly, publicly accessible beach establishment containing restaurants, retail, wellness, pool deck and beach operations. Funds will assist in harmonizing the location & Beachwalk improvements.
2025.purpose: The funds will be used to beautify and secure the walkway and street ends on the north and south sides of Pier Park. These improvements aim to enhance pedestrian safety, improve traffic flow, upgrade infrastructure, and create a more visually appealing space. The project is part of the larger revitalization of Pier Park into an upscale, resident-friendly, publicly accessible beach destination with restaurants, retail, and beach operations.
2025.activities: The project will involve construction and infrastructure improvements to enhance the walkways, crosswalks, street ends, and lighting. It will integrate pedestrian-friendly designs with connectivity improvements between the park, the Beachwalk, and surrounding areas, making the area more accessible and safer.
2025.direct_services: The project will provide increased public access and connectivity, making it easier and safer for pedestrians and cyclists to navigate the area. The improvements will reduce congestion, enhance pedestrian safety, and support a more vibrant and welcoming environment for both residents and visitors.
2025.population: The project will serve residents of Miami Beach, local businesses, and visitors/tourists. The enhanced walkways and pedestrian areas will benefit a diverse group of people, including homeowners, renters, business owners, workers, and tourists. The project is expected to serve both residents and visitors who frequent the area.
2025.outcome: Improve pedestrian and bicycle safety through enhanced walkways, lighting, and traffic flow management. Increase tourism and economic activity by making the area more attractive and accessible, drawing more visitors to Pier Park and nearby businesses. Enhance urban connectivity and cultural engagement by creating a seamless connection between the Beachwalk, Pier Park, and surrounding neighborhoods. Beautify the streetscape with upgraded infrastructure, making the area more inviting and aesthetically pleasing.

2556.description: The requested funding will go towards the construction and renovation of the Venice Theatre that was heavily damaged in Hurricane Ian.
2556.purpose: Venice Theatre, one of downtown Venice's oldest businesses, needs support to restore itself as an economic driver of Downtown Venice. Hurricane Ian caused millions of dollars of damage to the Venice Theatre thus ceasing much of its operations. As a center for volunteer engagement for those of all ages, the loss has cost millions to not only Venice Theatre but the entire Venice community and economy. The goal is to make Venice Theatre whole again
2556.activities: The funding will allow for the Venice Theatre to continue to provide theatrical productions, classes, and volunteer engagement to residents and visitors to the region.
2556.direct_services: The Venice Theatre is a center for volunteer engagement, which provides educational opportunities, quality of life, and mental health opportunities for all ages. This funding will not only provide immediate employment opportunities but will generate tax revenue for the state and local economy. The loss, due to storm damage, has cost millions to the Theatre and local economy.
2556.population: The Venice Theatre serves all ages from school age children to retired adults. The Theatre serves thousands of visitors and residents every year.
2556.outcome: Venice Theatre tracks the number of actors, volunteers, and students participating in hours of auditions, rehearsals, productions, set- and costume building, and classes/camps, which provides a physical and educational outlet for the volunteers. In partnership with the EDC of Sarasota County, Venice Theatre will track the economic impact and jobs coming into the economy as a result of this investment.

3161.purpose: Reduction in roadway management expenses incurred by Healing Hoof Steps, a 501c3 organization. Reduction/elimination of damage to vehicles driven by clients, staff, volunteers and residents. Future development activities

3185.description: The goal of this project is to improve traffic flow and safety on Stahlman from the Azalea to US 98. This project will include the study, design and construction of improvements to the Stahlman/Azalea intersection, adding a traffic signal at the Palmetto/98 intersection and moving of the pedestrian crossing on Highway 98 near Palmetto to the Palmetto/98 intersection. These improvements will help mitigate the impacts of the completed Crosstown Connector on the Stahlman/98 intersection.
3185.purpose: These improvements will help mitigate the impacts of the completed Crosstown Connector on the Stahlman/98 intersection. Projects benefits will include less traffic congestion, better traffic flow, and better connectivity.

3186.description: Undergrounding the aerial utilities on Highway 98 from the west boundary of city limits to the intersection of Airport Boulevard will help residents, businesses, highway users and pedestrians. Highway 98 is a major thoroughfare for visitors and residents with ingress & egress on and off the peninsula. Falling tree limbs, high winds, and heavy storms are just a few of the things that frequently cause utility disruptions and destroy overhead lines. Burying lines eliminates weather-related power outages and provides more reliable service. Undergrounding utility lines eliminates fire hazards, accidents, and safety risks from power outages due to downed lines.
3186.purpose: The conversion of existing aerial to underground provides the ability to promote a safer and more reliable system. Thus, limiting the shut-down or limited access as a result from weather-related events. Furthermore, safety and community health; burying lines eliminates fire hazards, accidents, and safety risks from power outages due to downed lines.
3186.activities: The complete conversion of currently aerial facilities to underground. This includes the design, materials, construction, wreck-out of aerial facilities, and construction management.
3186.direct_services: Safer, more aesthetic and reliable system. Reduces the risk of limited mobility and loss of electricity as a result of storm events/damage.
3186.population: Undergrounding the aerial utilities on Highway 98 from the west boundary of city limits to the intersection of Airport Boulevard will help residents, businesses, highway users and pedestrians. Approximately 7,433 customers are served by the three feeder electrical service lines that would be undergrounded as a result of this project.
3186.outcome: Undergrounding utility lines eliminate fire hazards, accidents, safety risks, and power outages due to downed lines. The City is located on a island and is vulnerable to power outages caused by high winds from tropical storms and hurricanes. Residents who receive power from the underground lines will still have power after a major storm because the lines are buried.

Additionally, the program provides outreach and education to increase awareness of nonprofit and community resources to address needs and close service gaps.

Assistance requests - referred by military leadership or community partners - are vetted to confirm they are emergencies and that no other funding exists. Financial support may cover housing, medical/mental health needs, transportation, food, and similar essentials, with payments made directly to vendors.

3190.description: Funding to renovate the building currently housing City Library and Commission Chambers. The Commission chamber moved to a new city-funded building, allowing library expansion. Modern libraries need increased electric and other high- tech adaptations to meet community expectations. Funds will address ADA compliance, flooring, insulation, ceiling tiles, and infrastructure upgrades, safety improvements, and furniture to improve accessibility, safety, and service for all ages.
3190.purpose: Infrastructure and accessibility improvements to Valparaiso Community Library building.
3190.activities: Funds will create safe, accessible library spaces, allowing children and teens to read, attend programs, participate in tutoring, and explore maker activities, while adults have areas for quiet study, meetings, and technology use. Updated restrooms, sinks, windows, and circulation desks ensure all patrons can fully access resources and services.

This alternative connector road will relieve traffic on Highway 98 by creating better traffic flow and increasing connectivity. This project will include the construction of a .3 mile section of roadway, sidewalks, and storm water facilities.

3194.description: This family center will be the hub of our Parent Aide program, a peer-reviewed, research based in-home services plan which has been developed through the auspices of the National Exchange Club. This program provides in-home services to families with children from birth to 17 years old. The families are selected through referrals from agencies like the Department of Children and Families and the parents must agree to participate. The Parent Aide works with the family to mitigate risk factors for abuse: enhancing parenting skills, increasing child safety, and fostering social connections among families.
3194.purpose: This family center will be the hub of our Parent Aide program, a peer-reviewed, research based in-home services plan which has been developed through the auspices of the National Exchange Club. Parent Aides with Bachelors' level degrees are trained in evidence-based Parent Aide model and curriculum by the National Exchange Club's Director of Prevention. Parent Aides will provide weekly 60-90 minute visits to families who voluntarily enroll in the program for a period of 6 - 12 months. Referrals
3194.activities: Bachelors' level Parent Aides will be trained in evidence-based Parent Aide model and curriculum by the National Exchange Club's Director of Prevention. Parent Aides will provide weekly 60-90 minute visits to families who voluntarily enroll in the program for a period of 6 - 12 months. Referrals are accepted from DCF investigators, lead agency case managers, community schools/agencies, self-refers
3194.direct_services: Using Evidence-based curriculum designed for working with families at-risk of child abuse and neglect we provide 18- 24 hours of instruction over a 6-12 month period, in the family home. Referrals will be accepted from DCF, the CBC case managers, agencies, schools and self-referrals from 4 counties in NW FL, for any family with at least one child under 18 who is deemed at-risk for abuse/neglect.
3194.population: Jobless persons, Economically disadvantaged persons, At-risk youth, Homeless, Physically disabled, Drug users (in health services), Preschool students, Grade school students, High school students, or any family with a child under the age of 18 years may be referred to this voluntary program.
3194.outcome: To keep families together and prevent Children from going into the foster care system. This program will be measured with evidence-based curriculum and will be monitored by DCF. Parent Aide serves 13 counties in Florida through 5 Exchange Club agencies who have served Florida for over 35 years. By adding this agency, it will allow these evidence-based, outcome driven and much needed services to families in NW Florida where Parent Aide is currently unavailable. DCF has monitored outcomes of this program in the Jacksonville area for the past 15+ years, and over 97% of all Parent Aide graduates have no confirmed report of abuse or neglect within one year of case closure.

3195.description: Funding will allow for the finished design and construction of a deep-water discharge for Four Prong Lake in Destin. This former dune lake is found within a closed-basin and has no natural or engineered primary spillway. The project will consist of the construction of a weir and discharge pipe that will convey floodwaters to the Gulf of America. The ACOE permit has already been secured.
3195.purpose: Four Prong Lake is the low point in a closed drainage basin, meaning that during and after heavy rains, stormwater runoff from both residential and commercial properties, as well as FDOT's Right-of-Way (US98-SR30), is directed to the lake where it has no natural outlet (former dune lake). The lake's water elevation would then continue to climb threatening private residences with flooding. The estimates of impacted properties below is based on a lake elevation of 9 and 10 feet.
3195.activities: The design the proposed weir and deepwater discharge piping will allow the lake to be maintained at a controlled and predictable level, mitigating the threat to, and potential losses of, residential properties.
3195.population: The target population for this project will be residents and property owners within three residential developments, Destiny, Destiny East, and the Beach Villas at Destiny. At a lake elevation of 9 feet, thirty-four single family residential properties will be protected against the threat of flooding by the installation of these measures . 3195.outcome: This is a flood mitigation project. Success will be measured by the lack of flooded properties.

2207.description: The Miami-Dade County Homeless Trust is seeking to acquire and convert existing properties in Miami-Dade County to serve as rental housing for vulnerable households, including disabled adults and senior citizens.
2207.purpose: Safe, affordable permanent rental housing for disabled adults and seniors experiencing homelessness.
2207.activities: Acquisition and renovation of housing for disabled adults and seniors.

This project supports Governor DeSantis’s goal to become number 1 in the nation in workforce education by 2030 by ensuring that working-age adults have a high-value certificate, degree, or training experience. Last year, the legislature appropriated the first 5M to the project.
3197.purpose: With a goal to increase the employability of area residents and meet the workforce needs of area businesses, the Workforce Innovation Training Center seeks to address the labor market skills needed today and in the future by connecting employers to a highly skilled workforce.

3200.organization: North Walton Rural Hospital, LLC dba North
3200.description: 100% of the funds requested will be used to establish a breast disease screening, diagnostic, and treatment program at North Walton Doctors Hospital. The funds will be used to purchase a 3D Mammography machine and provide one-year operational startup costs to hire a Breast Specialist/Surgeon and clinical staff . There is no nearby breast mammogram or dedicated breast treatment clinic within 30 miles. Mammography is currently recommended for Women from age 40 - 50 years old depending on their risk factors. Repeat screening is recommended every 1-2 years depending on risk factors as well. A dedicated clinic will also be established to fully evaluate any abnormal mammogram findings via 3D stereotactic biopsy, and to treat any diagnosed breast cancer with surgery, radiation, and/or chemotherapy.

Comprehensive diagnosis breast treatment will be seamlessly provided if there are abnormal findings on mammography.
3200.direct_services: 3D mammogram for suspicious breast cancer, 3D stereotactic biopsy for definitive diagnosis, and comprehensive breast treatment with radiation, surgery, and/or chemotherapy if warranted.

3200.outcome: Decreased incidence of advanced or untreated breast cancer. We will create a database that tracks the percentage of women who are getting mammograms as recommended, the incidents of advance her untreated breast cancer, and the mortality rate associated with breast cancer. We will also track the number of mammogram, biopsies, and surgical procedures perform as part of this program.
