This can be measured by reports and surveys of residents who have sustained damage to their property via flooding. Benefit: to improve transportation conditions and economic activity.

2409.description: The Veteran Housing and Homelessness Intervention Program provides street outreach, case management, and transitional housing assistance to homeless and at-risk veterans and their families in Brevard County. The program prevents and ends homelessness among veterans, improving their quality of life and saving costs for the local area. Services are delivered by skilled staff and volunteers who collaborate with the VA and other housing agencies. The program’s benefits include improved health, increased economic activity, enhanced self-sufficiency, and reduced social and personal impact of homelessness for veterans and their families.
2409.purpose: The funds requested will be used to achieve the specific goal of preventing and ending homelessness among veterans and their families in Brevard County by supporting outreach, case management, and transitional housing services. Based on recent performance, the program is expected to serve approximately 500 individuals, including veterans and their dependents. Without intervention, these individuals face a high risk of remaining in or entering chronic homelessness, which costs Florida an average
2409.activities: The program will deliver targeted street outreach to locate and engage unsheltered veterans, intensive case management to resolve housing crises for those at imminent risk, and transitional housing assistance to stabilize homeless veterans and their families. These services are designed to rapidly connect veterans with housing resources, financial support, and long-term stability, leveraging partnerships with the VA and local providers.
2409.direct_services: The appropriation project will directly provide access to VA healthcare and mental health services, basic needs such as food and camping gear, enrollment in housing programs and resources, financial aid and guidance, and transitional housing options to homeless and at-risk veterans and their families.
2409.population: The target population includes homeless and at-risk veterans and their families residing in Brevard County. Based on historical performance and current trends, the program expects to serve approximately 500 individuals, including 350 veteran households. This includes elderly veterans in HUD-VASH housing who are at risk of losing their vouchers due to inspection failures, as well as low-income veterans facing eviction due to rising housing costs.
2409.outcome: The expected outcome is a measurable reduction in veteran homelessness and housing instability in Brevard County. Outcomes will be tracked using HMIS data, intake and exit assessments, and follow-up surveys. Key metrics include the number of veterans who avoid or exit homelessness, access healthcare and mental health services, secure stable housing and employment, and report improved well-being. Economic impact will be calculated using the average annual cost of homelessness in Florida, projected to exceed $3.8 million in savings.

1874.description: The Suwannee County School District, through RIVEROAK Technical College (RTC), is requesting funding to establish the Suwannee Manufacturing at Riveroak Technical Hub (SMART Hub). The goal is to provide students with transferable, sustainable workforce skills and to support local industries, particularly in manufacturing, food processing, and semiconductor building. The project will enhance the state and local infrastructure, driving economic growth in these industries. Suwannee County is also a member of the Space Florida Consortium, emphasizing its commitment to advancing technological innovation. The SMART Hub programs will follow state technical center criteria and focus on advanced manufacturing career pathways, including: 1) Production, 2) Manufacturing Production Process Development, 3) Maintenance, Installation & Repair, 4) Quality Assurance, 5) Logistics & Inventory Control, and
1874.purpose: Funding will be used to build a new classroom and laboratory facility for industrial career and technical education programs including Advanced Manufacturing and Production Technology at Riveroak Technical College. This will be done in an effort to meet the workforce needs of local and regional employers and entice future industry to move into the area due to the generated workforce pipeline.
1874.activities: Educational programs provided will meet the workforce needs of multiple employers, offering students a broad skill set and experience with diverse equipment. The Advanced Manufacturing program offers several career certificates designed to equip students with the essential skills to enter the manufacturing workforce.
1874.direct_services: Advanced Manufacturing and Production Technology will result in earned industry credentials recognized by industry. Citizens will demonstrate competencies required by employers to be hired as Skilled Maintenance Technicians.
1874.population: The postsecondary career certificate will be offered to the public through Riveroak Technical College, the state technical college serving adults ages 16 years and older in Alachua, Columbia, Dixie, Gilchrist, Hamilton, Lafayette, Madison, Suwannee, and Taylor Counties. Programs will be open to interested and eligible adults and dual enrollment high school students. Targeted recruitment activities will include individuals from non-traditional people groups i.e. women, unemployed, underemployed,
1874.outcome: Increase postsecondary educational opportunities and increase job placement in manufacturing and production fields leading to high-wage careers. Outcomes will be measure by program completion rate, certification pass rate, and job placement rate, labor market data from FloridaCommerce, CareerSource, and Suwannee Economic Development Office.

2117.description: Renovation of a facility to permanently house the Fresh Start program, which provides reentry, rehabilitation, and support services to formerly incarcerated individuals. The facility will serve as a centralized hub for job training, mental health and substance abuse services, and case management.
2117.purpose: To provide a permanent facility for the Fresh Start program, supporting reentry and rehabilitation services for formerly incarcerated individuals.
2117.activities: Facility renovation, program space buildout, and infrastructure for service delivery.
2117.direct_services: Job training, mental health and substance abuse treatment, case management, and reentry support.
2117.population: Formerly incarcerated individuals. Economically disadvantaged persons. Individuals with behavioral health needs.
2117.outcome: Reduced recidivism, increased employment, and improved community reintegration. Methodology: Program tracking, employment placement data, and recidivism rates.

1958.description: The Veterans Resource Hub (“The Hub”) is a transformative, county-led initiative designed to serve as a central point of connection for area veterans, their families, and the broader community. It will offer access to direct services and referrals from governmental and nonprofit partners, while the Memorial Park will honor veterans’ sacrifices through educational installations and outdoor event space.
1958.purpose: To establish a centralized Veterans Resource Center that integrates healing, reintegration, and self-sufficiency services for veterans and their families.
1958.activities: Direct services and referrals Skills-building and reintegration programs Community engagement and events Memorial installations
1958.direct_services: Veterans and families will receive coordinated access to services, reducing travel and improving outcomes.
1958.population: Veterans Economically disadvantaged individuals Persons with mental health needs General public (for community events)
1958.outcome: Improved access to services, reduced fragmentation, enhanced community inclusion. Methodology: Service utilization tracking, employment outcomes, event participation.

1992.description: Design, land acquisition (if needed), and construction of a replacement bridge for Bridge #134055 on Singletary Road over a branch of the Myakka River in Manatee County. The project addresses aging infrastructure and supports the County’s broader bridge maintenance and replacement program.
1992.purpose: To replace a structurally aging bridge and ensure continued safe transportation access for residents, emergency services, and commercial traffic.
1992.activities: Bridge design, permitting, land acquisition (if needed), and construction.
1992.population: General public Commuters Emergency responders Commercial vehicles
1992.outcome: Improved transportation safety and reliability. Methodology: Engineering inspections, traffic flow analysis, and maintenance reports.

1993.description: Continuation of the design of the Fort Hamer interchange.
1993.purpose: Evacuation route, traffic relief, allows for east west connector.
1993.activities: Continuation of the design of the Fort Hamer interchange.
1993.direct_services: Citizens will be provided an interchange which will help alleviate traffic problems.
1993.population: This project will serve residents of Hillsborough, Manatee, and Sarasota counties; roughly 2.5M in combined population.
1993.outcome: The project will provide a safe alternative for residents. The outcome can be measured by a traffic study.

2118.description: Funding will support a new psychiatric and addiction facility in Manatee County. As the county's only comprehensive behavioral health provider, Centerstone serves over 17,000 individuals annually through our inpatient, residential, and outpatient services. Our existing 101-bed facility is home to a 41-bed inpatient hospital, 30-bed CSU, and 30-bed Level II Residential Substance Use Unit - built in the early 1980s, it now requires major repairs due to age and usage. Centerstone plans to construct a new behavioral health treatment facility that will provide a safer, more efficient care environment and allow for future service expansion. This funding will further develop architectural plans and appropriate environmental/ land studies.
2118.purpose: The funds will be used for the design phase for construction of a new inpatient facility designed to significantly enhance behavioral health and substance use treatment services. This new facility will address the increasing demand for comprehensive care for patients in Manatee County and surrounding areas, providing a safe and supportive environment for individuals in need of specialized inpatient care. The goal of this investment is to foster long-term recovery and improve patient outcomes.
2118.activities: Once the hospital is built, it will expand the capacity for treatment. The facility will offer critical services that are currently limited, improving access to care for those who struggle with mental health and substance use challenges.
2118.direct_services: Once the hospital is built, it will expand the capacity for treatment. The facility will offer critical services that are currently limited, improving access to care for those who struggle with mental health and substance use challenges.
2118.population: The target population is for those who struggle with mental health and substance use challenges.
2118.outcome: The goal of this investment is to foster long-term recovery, improve patient outcomes, and reduce the strain on emergency services, ultimately contributing to the overall well-being and health of the community. This will be measured through the number of patients served, and the number of beds that are utilized.

2120.description: This comprehensive and statewide program, which is highly responsive to state and national priority recommendations, is designed to support Florida’s efforts to curb rates of opioid-related addiction and deaths by: (1) Increasing the capacity of Florida’s healthcare workforce and other key service delivery systems to appropriately prevent and treat opioid use disorders and dependence; and (2) Increase community awareness of the risks associated with opioid misuse and addiction.
2120.purpose: It is the goal of this program to contribute to Florida's efforts to reduce opioid misuse behaviors and opioid-related mortality and morbidity through targeted professional training and community-based educational interventions.
2120.activities: - Train primary care & other health professionals to prevent/manage/reduce opioid misuse in high-risk communities and populations including youth, the elderly, veterans, the homeless, and individuals with behavioral health needs. - Enhance opioid use curriculum of health professions students and residents in training - Promote evidence-based opioid misuse screening & intervention strategies at health care, social service, school clinics, faith-based organizations, and other targeted sites with l
2120.direct_services: -Health professionals and health professions students will be more informed about evidence-based opioid use disorder identification, treatment and prevention. -Social workers, educators, peer counselors, school counselors, community health workers, caregivers, and other service providers will be trained and equipped to detect, intervene with, and refer to services individuals with real or potentia
2120.population: Persons with poor mental and/or physical health, physically disable persons, drug users, at-risk youth, the elderly, grade school students, high school students, college students, jobless and homeless persons. It is estimated that 500 health professionals and 1,100 health professions students from multiple disciplines and 4,000 individuals in communities impacted by opioid misuse statewide will be served.
2120.outcome: AHEC will: 1) Provide systems-based support to at least 25 primary care sites and 25 community-based organizations around the state - particularly in high exposure risk communities - to enhance pain management services, reduce the risk of opioid misuse, and identify and treat opioid misuse. AHEC will track systems enhancements at targeted primary care delivery sites and community based organizations. The State will be able to assess increases in treatment outcomes and reductions in opioid misuse morbidity and mortality. 2) Provide community-based education programs to a minimum of 500 health professionals, 1100 health professions students and 4000 individuals throughout the state to increase

2408.description: The funds will launch a community-led network to grow hatchery-reared spotted seatrout and other sportfish to larger, more resilient sizes for release in estuaries where recovery is most needed. The project will also repair and enhance natural resource monitoring infrastructure to track progress toward fisheries replenishment benchmarks using marine mammal health indicators, strengthening sportfish recovery and coastal economies.
2408.purpose: This funding will support development of a community-based fish grow-out program that partners with local anglers and organizations to raise juvenile sportfish to sizes that increase their survival after release. It will also upgrade research and monitoring facilities to better evaluate sportfish recovery and track ecosystem conditions through improved marine mammal health assessments.
2408.activities: This project supports state priorities by strengthening Florida’s coastal fisheries and enhancing the effectiveness of the State’s new fish hatchery and revitalized replenishment program. By engaging community partners in fish grow-out and improving the infrastructure needed to track fisheries and ecosystem recovery, the initiative advances responsible resource management and helps ensure healthy, sustainable fisheries for Florida’s coastal communities.
2408.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with expanded opportunities for hands-on participation in community-based fish grow- out and stewardship programs, as well as improved recreational fishing opportunities resulting from enhanced sportfish abundance. It will also support public education and outreach on coastal ecosystem health, including access to updated information from enhanced marine mammal and
2408.population: The project will benefit recreational anglers, coastal communities, and local businesses that depend on healthy sportfish populations. It will also serve community partners participating in fish grow-out activities, as well as state and federal agencies who rely on accurate marine mammal and ecosystem health monitoring to inform responsible coastal resource management.
2408.outcome: Expected outcomes from the full project include increased post-release survival of hatchery-reared sportfish, expanded community participation in fisheries management, and improved tracking of fisheries and ecosystem recovery based on marine mammal health monitoring. Outcomes will be measured through FWC fishery-independent monitoring, volunteer participation records, and analysis of marine mammal health and stranding metrics collected through established monitoring programs.

2366.description: We are requesting funding for the completion of a Real-Time Crime Center (RTCC) within the North Palm Beach Police Department. This will include equipment, (cameras, screens, speakers, etc) software, and installation costs.
2366.purpose: Purpose or goal would be to enhance situational awareness and improve response effectiveness by integrating live data sources—such as cameras, license plate readers, GPS, and analytical software—in order to provide officers with actionable intelligence before and during incidents.
2366.activities: The funds will be utilized in the purchase of equipment, software, and installation costs to complete the RTCC.
2366.direct_services: These funds will be utilized towards completion of a RTCC for the Department. This will directly impact citizens with an enhancement to public safety, security and crime prevention.
2366.population: The target population is general, the entire population of North Palm Beach can be served by this project approximately 13,000 residents. This would also serve the adjacent communities and their local police force who may be searching for a subject traveling through North Palm Beach.
2366.outcome: The expected benefit of this project would be improving public safety through faster response times, better crime prevention capabilities, and more effective and efficient use of data and technology to support officers in the field to either assist with problem area analysis or apprehension. This will be measured by comparing performance measures such as clearance rates, time to arrest and prevention and intervention prior to and after the completion of the RTCC.

2027.description: This program provides funding for the acquisition of critical infrastructure for a multi-use affordable housing project. Funding will be utilized to construct the necessary utilities and infrastructure to support the development of a multi-use affordable housing project that will benefit the community socially and economically.
2027.purpose: Funding for the acquisition of critical infrastructure for a multi-use affordable housing project. Funding will be utilized to construct necessary utilities and infrastructure to help with the development of a multi-use affordable housing project that will benefit the community both socially and economically.
2027.direct_services: The Infrastructure improvements will allow for the preparation of development of affordable and workforce housing.
2027.population: Elderly persons and economically disadvantaged persons.
2027.outcome: The benefits including enriching cultural experience and increasing and improving economic activity. Measurable goals for each aspect of the multi-use project will be established before the project is complete, including—but not limited to—the number of jobs created, average wages for those jobs, and the amount of private investment to start businesses.

2357.description: This project will be for a pavement preservation program focusing on extending the life of existing roads through timely preventive treatments like seal coats, thin overlays, and minor repairs. The program schedules regular road condition assessments to prioritize treatment areas, ensuring efficient use of resources and minimizing costly repairs in the future.
2357.purpose: The specific purpose of the funds is to extend the life and improve the condition of local roads through timely pavement preservation treatments, preventing major deterioration and costly repairs. On-going pavement preservation of local roads will improve safety and transportation conditions, as well as boost economic activity for the Village of North Palm Beach.
2357.activities: Activities will include regular road condition assessments, application of preventive maintenance treatments like seal coats and overlays, and quality engineering oversight to ensure effective and durable results.
2357.direct_services: Direct services to citizens include safer, smoother roads with fewer potholes and disruptions, leading to improved travel conditions and reduced vehicle maintenance costs.
2357.population: The target population is all residents and businesses within the Village of North Palm Beach who use the road network, potentially serving tens of thousands of people who live, work, or traverse through the Village.
2357.outcome: The funds will support construction and renovation efforts to apply specialized preservation treatments, enhancing road durability through advanced engineering and proven maintenance techniques. Engineering oversight will ensure these activities meet high-quality standards, using modern methods and equipment to improve pavement performance and extend service life efficiently.

2358.description: Provide improved ADA access to the municipal dog park.
2358.purpose: Provide improved ADA access to the municipal dog park.
2358.activities: Install an ADA compliant concrete walkway at the dog park.
2358.direct_services: Provide improved ADA access to the municipal dog park.
2358.outcome: The benefit would be improved access to the park. The outcome will be measured by the replacement of the current walkway to an ADA compliant walkway through linear feet.

2374.description: Upgrade existing obsolete control panels and instrumentation equipment at the existing Water Treatment Plant (WTP), perform an overall evaluation of the existing instrumentation and controls (I&C) components, SCADA system, and review considerations for Cybersecurity based on EPA guidelines at the existing WTP. Consideration will be given for the provision of spare I/O modules, fiber/ethernet ports and spare conduits for the overall design. The WTP processes currently includes ten (10) existing raw water supply wells (3 on-site hard-wired wells, 1 off-site hard-wired well, and remote radio monitoring of 6 off-site wells), aeration, dual media filtration, backwash pond, clearwell, ion exchange softening, anion exchange, disinfection, two (2) ground storage tanks, and high service pumping systems. The existing WTP control system includes a Main Control Panel (MCP) within the Control Room (A
2374.purpose: Upgrade existing obsolete control panels and instrumentation equipment at the existing Water Treatment Plant (WTP).
2374.activities: Perform an overall evaluation of the existing instrumentation and controls (I&C) components, SCADA system, and review considerations for Cybersecurity based on EPA guidelines at the existing WTP.
2374.direct_services: Distribution of potable water in a safe, stable and reliable manner.
2374.population: Residents, visitors and business owners totaling approximately 13,000.
2374.outcome: Improved communication between the upgraded instrumentation and controls with the upgrades made at the Water Treatment Plant.

2376.description: This project is for full restoration of a canal which will include removing significant debris, dredging to restore proper cross sections, bank stabilization, and other water quality improvements. The restoration will increase stormwater capacity, conveyance, protect property, prevent localized flooding, and improve water quality.
2376.purpose: This project will restore a major canal that is in severe disrepair to increase stormwater capacity and conveyance which will help to protect property, prevent localized flooding, and improve water quality.
2376.activities: Significant debris removal, bank stabilization, and dredging to restore proper cross sections to increase capacity and improve water quality.
2376.direct_services: The project will protect nearby roadways and the property of residents and businesses adjacent to the canal, improve water quality draining into state waters, and overall enhance flood prevention throughout the city with increased stormwater capacity.
2376.population: Both the immediate neighborhoods and businesses adjacent to the canal and residents citywide. The 62,000 residents of Palm Beach Gardens.
2376.outcome: Flood prevention, improved water quality, and increased stormwater capacity. The outcome will be measured by cubic yards of debris/sedimentation removed, feet of canal bank stabilized, and increased stormwater conveyence.

2663.description: The Cox Science Center and Aquarium is expanding its facility to include approximately 75,000 SF of new space including a new public aquarium, new exhibit galleries, and new STEM education facilities. The project will serve more than 1,000,000 visitors annually including more than 100,000 local school children, residents of the state, and tourists.
2663.purpose: The funds requested will be used to construct new science center facilities in order for the Cox Science Center and Aquarium to expand its ability to provide STEM education programs and services to its target market of more then 3,000,000 residents.
2663.activities: The direct services provided to citizens include science center exhibit and planetarium experiences, educational programs, STEM skills training, job skills training, and early childhood learning programs.
2663.direct_services: The direct services provided to citizens include science center exhibit and planetarium experiences, educational programs, STEM skills training, job skills training, and early childhood learning programs.
2663.population: The target population includes residents of the following counties: Palm Beach, Broward, Martin, St, Lucie, Glades, Henry; students served by the School District of Palm Beach County, and tourists to the Greater Palm Beaches region.
2663.outcome: 1) The expanded CSCA will be the most attended cultural institution in the Greater Palm Beaches Region. This will be measured by attendance reports compiled by the Cox Science Center and Aquarium. 2)The expanded Cox Science Center and Aquarium will be the leading provider of out-of-school STEM programs to the School District of Palm Beach County. This will be measured by program reports compiled by CSCA and the School District of Palm Beach County. 3)The expanded Cox Science Center and Aquarium will add jobs and increase economic output in Palm Beach County through its expanded operations. This will be measured through payroll reports, tax collections, and visitor spending reports. 4) The ex

2377.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2377.description: Restoration Bridge International operates as a food rescue and redistribution logistics agency, recovering surplus perishable inventory from retailers and growers to redistribute to those in need. We bridge the gap between abundance and need by supplying partner agencies/organizations with food and hosting 20–25 direct distribution events each month throughout Palm Beach County. Our monthly distributions are done in partnership with the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office and target low income, low access communities where the need is greatest.
2377.purpose: Reduce hunger and food insecurity in Palm Beach and neighboring counties by distributing donated and rescued food commodities to residents in need in their communities.
2377.activities: Funds will directly support the operational logistics of food rescue, covering essential costs such as refrigerated transport, fuel, and cold storage management. This infrastructure enables RBI to recover surplus inventory and execute 20–25 monthly distribution events to feed families throughout Palm Beach County. RBI also supplies food to our partner agency network enabling them to serve niche populations difficult for us to reach directly such as homeless, veterans, single mothers, the elderly
2377.direct_services: The project will provide immediate nutritional assistance to food-insecure citizens through the execution of 20–25 mobile food distribution events across Palm Beach County each month. Additionally, it ensures consistent access to fresh, high-quality perishables for vulnerable families by leveraging RBI's logistics network to supply local partner agencies.
2377.population: This project primarily targets under-served populations and households struggling with food insecurity. We estimate impacting 1.5 million individuals throughout Palm Beach County through our direct distribution events and partner agency network.
2377.outcome: The primary benefit of this project is a direct reduction in hunger and food insecurity among vulnerable households in Palm Beach County. To measure this outcome, we will utilize a methodology that strictly tracks the total number of pounds of food distributed through our logistics network. Additionally, we will record the specific number of families and individuals served at each distribution event to quantify the program's reach and effectiveness.

2353.description: The requested funds will support the design and construction of wastewater system improvements north of Hillsboro Boulevard between Lyons Road and NW 39th Avenue. The project will expand system capacity, serve existing development, and enable septic-to-sewer conversions, improving public health, groundwater protection, and long-term utility reliability. The area it will serve contains several developments, a business and a large private school.
2353.purpose: Expand system capacity, serve existing development, and enable septic-to-sewer conversions.
2353.direct_services: Provides safe, accessible outdoor space for public events, civic engagement, community programs, and gatherings.
2353.population: The City of Coconut Creek has a population of around 58,000 - it's anticipated that visitors from surrounding jurisdictions will also benefit from greater access to the memorial art installations, including a one-of-a-kind Holocaust Memorial that will be installed in January 2026.
2353.outcome: Increased wastewater system capacity and elimination of septic systems in the project area; reduction in potential nutrient and bacteria seepage from septic and aging municipal systems into groundwater; and expanded capacity and redundancy in wastewater infrastructure serving the area. Measured by: Monitoring flow and groundwater quality, number of properties connected to City sewer and reduction of septic system usage, system modeling, and compliance with state reliability standards.

2080.description: The wastewater system within the City is aging and the City is conducting inspection and rehabilitation of wastewater conveyance structures to reduce inflow and infiltration issues related to deterioration of existing structures. State funds will be used to expedite the rehabilitation process to minimize the potential of environmental hazards caused by aging infrastructure, which could negatively impact the existing impaired water body: the C-14 Canal.
2080.purpose: Reduce inflow and infiltration issues related to deterioration of existing structures. State funds will be used to expedite the rehabilitation process to minimize the potential of environmental hazards caused by aging infrastructure, which could negatively impact the existing impaired water body: the C-14 Canal.
2080.activities: Inspection and rehabilitation of the wastewater conveyance structures to reduce inflow and infiltration issues related to deterioration of existing structures and to mitigate environmental hazards caused by aging infrastructure.
2080.direct_services: Environmental preservation; protection of the C-14 canal; improved groundwater and surface water quality; improved wastewater management.
2080.population: Thousands. This project is citywide and the City has a population of around 58,000
2080.outcome: Preserve quality of the environment; protection of the C-14 canal; improved groundwater and surface water quality; improved wastewater management. Measurements based on the number of wastewater overflows and breaks are reported annually as part of the NPDES permit.

2073.description: Venice Theatre, one of downtown Venice’s oldest businesses, needs support to restore itself as an arts education center and economic driver. Hurricane Ian wreaked havoc on Venice Theatre operations. Funds will be used to rebuild the Raymond Arts Education Center's four classroom studios to serve the area's students, from pre-k through college age.
2073.purpose: Venice Theatre, one of downtown Venice’s oldest businesses, needs support to restore itself as an arts education center and economic driver. Hurricane Ian wreaked havoc on Venice Theatre operations. As a center for volunteer engagement for those of all ages, the loss has cost millions to not only Venice Theatre but the entire Venice community. The goal is to make Venice Theatre whole again.
2073.activities: The funding will allow for the Venice Theatre to continue to teach theatrical productions, classes, and volunteers.
2073.direct_services: The Venice Theatre is a center for arts education, which provides volunteer engagement, quality of life, and mental health opportunities for all ages. This funding will not only provide immediate employment opportunities, but will generate tax revenue for the state and local economy. The loss of due to storm damage has cost millions to the Theatre and local economy.
2073.population: Venice Theatre has programming targeted to populations of all socio-economic levels and has historically served approximately 120,000 patrons annually. When operating at full capacity attendance is expected to rise at least 20% to approximately 144,000 patrons annually.
2073.outcome: By restoring Venice Theatre as one of the economic drivers of downtown Venice and south Sarasota County, it will stimulate the local economy and raise the artistic standards and opportunity for the area. We can measure this by surveys and box office receipts.

2090.description: The City of Clermont reclaimed water system serves over 6,500 homes. This 3-million-gallon storage tank will be critical part of the reclaimed system by storing additional reclaimed water that would otherwise be directed to the rapid infiltration basins. This additional reclaimed water will serve to keep additional off the potable water system for irrigation.
2090.purpose: Increase availability of alternative water supply by storing more reclaimed water.
2090.activities: Land purchase and construction of storage and pumping facility.
2090.direct_services: Use reclaimed water for irrigation in lieu of potable water.
2090.population: The residents of Clermont and surrounding communities.
2090.outcome: Increase storage of reclaimed water for irrigation use. Measure storage before and after project.

2091.description: Purchase land to construct a water treatment facility. This site will help improve system redundancy to an area of the city that that will have a significant economic and healthcare impact in the area and support safe, clean drinking water across the service area along with providing additional system redundancy to a neighboring utility provider in emergency situations through a interconnect between the two water systems.
2091.purpose: Purchase land to construct a water treatment plant.
2091.activities: Acquire land to construct a water treatment plant
2091.direct_services: Increase reliability of fire protection by reducing the amount of fire hydrants that are out of service during water breaks, reduction in service interruptions to the potable water supply for residents in the service area by providing and additional source of water. Provide additional water source to a neighboring utility provider through an interconnect during emergency situations.
2091.population: Potable water users in the southern area of the city's utility service area. Approximately 30,000 individuals.
2091.outcome: Increase reliability of fire protection by reducing the amount of fire hydrants that are out of service during water breaks, reduction in service interruptions to the potable water supply for residents in the service area by providing an additional source of water. Provide an additional water source to a neighboring utility provider through an interconnect during emergency situations. evaluate data for number of residents and hydrants out of service during water main breaks in the area prior to and after construction of the future water treatment plant.

2093.description: The City of Clermont (City) seeks funding to construct a joint public safety training campus serving both the Fire and Police Departments. The project will transform City-owned property at 400 12th Street into a regional hub for emergency responder training featuring a multi-story training tower, classroom and simulation building, defensive tactics and vehicle operations pad, and shared training environments. The facility addresses a critical gap: both departments currently rely on borrowed or out-of-county training grounds, limiting frequency, realism, and safety. This project allows for consistent, integrated, and accredited training that meets CFAI (FIRE) and CFA (Police) accreditation standards.
2093.purpose: Develop a permanent, shared training facility that allows Fire and Police personnel to train safely and frequently within Clermont, supporting CFAI (FIRE) and CFA (Police) accreditation, regional preparedness, and reduced liability through modern, scenario-based instruction.
2093.activities: Design, construct, and operate a comprehensive training campus offering live-fire exercises, law-enforcement tactical simulations, EMS training, command-level drills, and joint disaster-response operations for Clermont and partner agencies.
2093.direct_services: While training-focused, the facility directly enhances public safety by ensuring firefighters and police officers are
2093.population: All Fire and Police Department personnel from the City of Clermont (approx. 200 employees), plus mutual-aid and regional partners across Lake and Orange Counties. Estimated annual participation: 300–500 first responders.
2093.outcome: The facility will provide a safe, permanent location for live-fire, defensive tactics, and joint training that enhances responder readiness and public safety. Expected results include an increase in annual training hours, full CFAI/CFA compliance, a reduction in on-duty injuries, and improved multi-agency and regional coordination. Outcomes will be measured through training-hour and certification data, comparison of injury and incident trends before and after opening, accreditation audit results, and documentation of joint exercises and evaluations demonstrating operational improvement.

2094.description: Clermont’s Wellness Way and Olympus corridor is experiencing rapid growth with thousands of homes, schools, medical, sports, and commercial facilities. The area is beyond the reach of current stations, creating 6–10-minute response gaps that endanger residents. Fire Station 5 will close this gap, ensure NFPA 1710 compliance, protect billions in investment. Using State Support and Federal SAFER-funded staffing the city will provide 24/7 fire and EMS coverage for South Lake County and Clermont.
2094.purpose: Construct a permanent fire station to eliminate 6–10-minute response delays, ensure equitable service coverage, and meet NFPA 1710 deployment standards for the Wellness Way corridor.
2094.activities: Design and build the facility to house an engine company, future rescue unit, command office, community meeting space and law enforcement sub-station; deliver fire suppression, ALS EMS, technical rescue, and law enforcement services to a currently under-served region.
2094.direct_services: Provides 24/7 emergency fire, medical, and Law Enforcement response for residents, schools, and businesses in Clermont and South Lake County, reducing property loss, injuries, and fatalities.
2094.population: Residents, workers, and visitors within the Wellness Way and Olympus corridor and southern Lake County (approx. 8,000 residents initially, growing to 20,000+ by 2030).
2094.outcome: The project will eliminate 6–10-minute emergency response delays in Clermont’s fastest-growing corridor, improving cardiac-arrest survival rates, limiting fire spread beyond the room of origin, and ensuring compliance with NFPA 1710 deployment standards. The station will protect over $1 billion in new development, improve insurance ratings, and expand regional surge capacity for major incidents. Performance will be measured using CAD and NFIRS response- time data, QA/QI medical outcome tracking, insurance loss comparisons, and ISO evaluation metrics to verify measurable improvements in life safety, property protection, and resilience.

2058.description: Powerhouse Youth Project provides on-campus and off-campus training with the goal of preparing the youth population for work-force readiness. Each youth will receive personal and career development guidance, be provided a career assessment through the DISC profile enabling the participant to identify the potential career paths that are possible and then have access to a mentor in a chosen career.
2058.purpose: The goal is to secure and prepare the youth population for work-force readiness within each local community. The funds will be used to create an operational team within the organization that can implement this goal by creating relevant classroom experiences, personal and career development including connecting the youth to a career mentor.
2058.activities: Powerhouse Youth Project will provide on-campus and off-campus training with the goal of preparing the youth population for work-force readiness. Each youth will receive personal and career development guidance, be provided a career assessment through the DISC profile enabling the participant to identify the potential career paths that are possible and then have access to a mentor in a chose career. A professional career panel of industry experts will be available to participants providing stude
2058.direct_services: Powerhouse will provide career and personal development training for youth, ages 14-24 who engage within the program. Adults and senior citizens will also be provided training on mentorship and provided an opportunity to give back within each community served.
2058.population: The target population served by this project is youth ages 14-24 including at-risk students who are currently in high school or participating in alternative schools. Approximately 2,000 individuals are expected to be served.
2058.outcome: The expected outcome is the development of students to enter the workforce including increased awareness of potential careers and job opportunities and the process to acquire them. This will also result in an increase of mental health and awareness of the strategies for overcoming obstacles and barriers for achieving a desired career path. These can be measured by pre/post student surveys, participation in the career DISC assessment, and engagement levels with mentors during follow-up of each student.

3539.description: Since 2013, Links to Success has provided college and career prep programs for students in Desoto County where economic hardships and limited resources create significant barriers. With 21% of residents living below the poverty line and only 11.6% holding a bachelor's degree (compared to 31.5% statewide), many face major challenges in achieving success. To expand our impact, we have established a family resource center. Our goal is to strengthen educational and economic outcomes in Desoto County by providing comprehensive multi-generational programming for students and families, launch an Early Learning PreK Readiness Bag Program, and renovate our family empowerment center to support collaborative learning and confidential client services.
3539.purpose: To strengthen educational and economic outcomes in DeSoto County through comprehensive student and family programming, early learning readiness supports, and facility renovations enabling expanded confidential services and collaborative learning.
3539.activities: College and career prep workshops, youth empowerment programs, parent leadership academy, PreK readiness bag distribution, family navigator services, confidential client consultations, and community convenings.
3539.direct_services: Free programming for students and families, PreK readiness bags, confidential family support, early learning videos, case management, and academic/career readiness workshops.
3539.population: Economically disadvantaged persons At-risk youth Preschool, grade school, high school, and university/college students General community members benefiting from family support and early learning interventions
3539.outcome: Improve quality of education Measures: Pre- and post-program assessments regarding postsecondary preparation Workshop attendance FAFSA completion rate (DeSoto) High school graduation rates Acceptance into a postsecondary institution Method: Data will demonstrate increases in the listed indicators, stronger resource connections, and improved outcomes for families.

2121.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2121.description: The Florida Plastic Degradation Assessment will develop the first scientific method to measure and rank how much common plastics break down under actual Florida conditions. The Assessment will help the State identify which plastics break down the fastest in our environment. The goal is to reduce microplastics and nanoplastics that are appearing everywhere. Once microplastics enter the water system, they persist; settling into sediments, passing through water systems, oysters and fish, and eventually reach humans.
2121.purpose: This Florida Plastic Degradation Assessment will develop the first scientific method to measure and rank how much common plastics break down under actual Florida conditions. Florida needs a clear way to identify which plastics break down the fastest in our environment. Microplastics and nanoplastics are appearing everywhere. Once they enter the water, they persist. They settle into sediments, pass through water systems, oysters and fish, and eventually reach humans.
2121.activities: Many products labeled as environmentally friendly degrade quickly, but this only accelerates their transformation into nano/microplastics. These particles spread through ecosystems and are impossible to eliminate. Materials that remain intact and can be recovered release far fewer particles. FPDA addresses the need to significantly decrease micro- & nano-plastic pollution at its source.
2121.direct_services: Reducing high shedding plastics protects: drinking waters, fisheries and seafood safety, oyster, clam, and finfish aquaculture, water clarity and tourism, coastal property values. A ranking system provides Florida with the information needed to shift away from high-shedding plastics and promote stronger, more effective alternatives.
2121.population: Coastal communities are the primary beneficiaries of the study, but reduced plastics in the water system will benefit all Floridians.
2121.outcome: Many products labeled as environmentally friendly degrade quickly, but this only accelerates their transformation into nano/microplastics. These particles spread through ecosystems and are impossible to eliminate. Florida needs to change the conversation. Materials that remain intact and can be recovered release far fewer particles. These are the materials that lessen pollution at its source. A Florida plastics ranking system provides Florida with the information needed to shift away from high-shedding plastics and promote stronger, more human environmentally healthy alternatives.

2460.description: The requested funds will expand the Figgers Digital Healthcare Access Program. The program deploys Figgers Health tablets for at-risk youth and seniors, fostering holistic well-being. These tablets integrate mental, physical, and behavioral health components, comprehensively addressing diverse health needs. The project seeks to enhance health outcomes and provide crucial support for vulnerable demographics.
2460.purpose: The requested funds will expand the Figgers Digital Healthcare Access Program. The program deploys Figgers Health tablets for at-risk youth and seniors, fostering holistic well-being. These tablets integrate mental, physical, and behavioral health components, comprehensively addressing diverse health needs. The project seeks to enhance health outcomes and provide crucial support for vulnerable demographics.
2460.activities: Participants will receive secure tablets with accessibility features and digital literacy training. Activities include hands- on workshops on using technology safely, accessing telehealth and education platforms, and preventing online fraud to promote independence and digital inclusion.
2460.direct_services: The program will directly provide 4,500 Floridians with modern tablets and personalized digital literacy instruction. Services include device setup, telehealth access training, online safety education, and ongoing support to ensure safe, confident technology use.
2460.population: This project will serve at-risk youth and seniors and other vulnerable populations. This program will provide 4,500 Floridians with modern tablets and personalized digital literacy instruction.
2460.outcome: This project will increase the use of telehealth services for medical appointments, reduced isolation, improve emotional well-being among participants, and increase access online services and employment tools. These outcomes will be measured by pre- and post-program surveys assessing connectivity and health indicators.

2028.organization: DR DOCTOR TEACH ME HOW TO FISH
2028.description: This program is an artificial intelligence education and workforce readiness program serving both collegiate and high school students. At the collegiate level, it provides hands-on, applied AI experiences through industry-aligned projects and professional mentorship that strengthen technical skills and prepare students for technology-driven careers. At the high school level, it introduces foundational AI concepts and applied learning, within the first-year student teams are participating in President Trump’s Presidential AI Challenge and additional AI development project competitions, giving students sustained exposure to real-world problem-solving and emerging technologies.
2028.purpose: The funds requested will support the launch of an artificial intelligence education and workforce readiness program designed to prepare students for careers in the growing AI and technology sectors. The program’s goal is to build a sustainable talent pipeline by providing college students with applied, industry-aligned AI experiences while introducing high school students to foundational AI concepts and real-world applications.
2028.activities: Our organization will use the funding to plan, administer, and deliver a structured artificial intelligence education program serving collegiate and high school students. Program activities include designing and managing industry- aligned, project-based AI learning experiences; coordinating professional mentorship and instructional support; and facilitating applied learning pathways for college participants. At the high school level, activities include implementing foundational AI instruction an
2028.direct_services: The appropriation project will deliver direct educational and workforce readiness services to students through structured artificial intelligence training and applied learning opportunities. Services include hands-on AI instruction, project-based skill development, facilitated mentorship, and guided exposure to real-world technology applications. High school and college students will receive organ
2028.population: The target population served by this project includes high school students and college students with an interest in artificial intelligence, technology, and workforce readiness. The program is expected to directly serve approximately 100 - 200 students, with capacity to scale in future years as additional cohorts, partnerships, and learning opportunities are added.
2028.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is increased student readiness for AI- and technology-related education and careers through strengthened foundational knowledge, applied technical skills, and real-world project experience. Participants will gain exposure to collaborative problem-solving and industry-relevant applications of artificial intelligence. Outcomes will be measured through participant enrollment and completion rates, evaluation of student project deliverables, pre- and post-program skill assessments, and feedback from mentors or instructors.

2401.organization: University of Florida College of Education
2401.description: The Florida K-12 AI Education Task Force convenes education stakeholders to identify and establish pathways to enhance AI literacy, data privacy, and safety for Florida K-12 students, educators and schools. It aims to increase quality assurance, improve access to professional learning, and initiate research and accountability infrastructure. The Task Force is composed of school districts; public, private, and charter schools; colleges and universities; EdTech companies; industry leaders; parent groups; and teachers. It is committed to empowering stake-holders by harnessing the transformative potential of AI while prioritizing safety and privacy for everyone.
2401.purpose: To provide quality assurance recommendations for AI tools used by schools, improve access to professional learning about AI, update AI guidance documents and associated web resources, support districts in revising policies related to AI, and initiate research and accountability infrastructure for AI use in K-12 schools.
2401.activities: Convene stakeholders to identify the best ways to achieve the above. Stakeholders include task force members representing school districts, public, private, and charter schools, colleges & universities, EdTech companies, industry leaders, parent groups, and teachers. Develop and provide guidance and web resources on adaptable, practical strategies for safe AI integration into FL schools. Provide opportunities for professional learning on AI for teaching and learning. Provide technical assistance
2401.direct_services: Provide professional learning opportunities for families, educators, and district leaders to enhance their ability to safely integrate AI into FL schools.
2401.population: The professional learning, guidance, and resulting policies and initiatives will ultimately serve the K-12 students of FL and educators, including over 2.8 million public school students and thousands of private school students.
2401.outcome: Families, educators, and district leaders will enhance their ability to safely integrate AI into FL schools, as measured by pre- and post-tests associated with the provided professional learning. School districts, charter school providers, individual charter and private schools will improve their existing district and school policies to include AI-related components based on best practices and provided guidance from the task force.

2421.description: Queen Esther's Place is a faith-based foster home dedicated to providing a safe, nurturing, and transformative environment for girls ages 13-18 in Alachua County, Florida. Operated by Fresh Start Ministries, the program offers stable housing, life skills training, educational support, and emotional healing for young girls who have experienced trauma, neglect, or displacement. With a foundation rooted in christian values. Queen Esther's Place fosters personal growth, self-sufficiency, and spiritual development through structured mentorship, counseling, and community engagement. The home's holistic approach ensures that each resident receives the care, resources, and guidance need to thrive emotionally and academically and socially.
2421.purpose: The long-term goal of Queen Esther's Place is to empower and equip young ladies in foster care with the skills, confidence, and support necessary to break cycles of instability and build successful, independent futures through a stable nurturing environment. The program aims to foster personal growth, educational achievement, and emotional resilience, ensuring that each resident is prepared for adulthood by providing mentorship, life skills training, and faith- based guidance. Queen Esther's Pla
2421.activities: Queen Esther's Place provides a comprehensive range of activities and services designed to support the personal, educational, an emotional development of young girls in foster care. These include stable housing, individualized case management, academic tutoring, and college or career readiness programs. Residents receive life skills training in areas such as financial literacy, cooking, and job preparedness, along with access to professional counseling and trauma-informed therapy. Faith-based me
2421.direct_services: Queen Esther's Place directly benefits the Alachua County community and surrounding areas by providing a safe, stable, and supportive home for young ladies in foster care, reducing homelessness and juvenile delinquency rates. By equipping these young ladies with the essential life skills, education, and emotional support needed. The program fosters self-sufficiency, leading to more productive and
2421.population: Queen Esther's Place serves adolescent/teen age girls ages 13-18 in the foster care system, particularly those who have experienced trauma, neglect, or instability in Alachua County, Florida. This project specifically targets young ladies who are at risk of aging out of the foster care system without the necessary life skills, education, or support to transition successfully into adulthood. Many of these girls have faced emotional, physicial, or psychological challenges and Queen Esther's place
2421.outcome: The expected outcome of Queen Esther's Place is to empower young ladies in the foster care system to achieve stability, independence, and personal growth by providing them with a safe home, education, life skills training and emotional support. Success will be measured through key performance indicators, including high school graduation rates, college or vocational program enrollment, job placement, and overall self-sufficiency upon leaving the program. Additional metrics will include improvements in mental and emotional well-being will be tracked through trauma- informed assessments, mentor reports, and goal tracking tools which are provided.

2768.organization: So You Want Your Name In Lights
2768.description: These funds will help our organization expand services provided to at-risk youth (ages 10 - 21) residing in underserved communities by implementing youth mentoring services that help them develop character, confidence, leadership, discipline, self-esteem, and positive life skills. The organization will be able to secure a van to transport youth to receive essential weekly mentoring services. This support ensures equity of access and will help maximize the program's positive impact. Vetted drivers, who have undergone background checks, will be assigned to handle this responsibility. We have been providing youth services since 2019. The mission of this organization is to enhance the quality of life for community residents by implementing mentoring activities for at-risk youth, providing educational support, and engaging in performing arts projects.
2768.purpose: The specific goal is to reduce crime and recidivism. The purpose is to further support the mission of this organization which is to improve the quality of life for community residents by implementing weekly at-promise youth mentoring activities, educational support, and performing arts projects. Clients include at-risk and juvenile justice-involved youth (ages 10 - 21).
2768.activities: The intended purpose of these funds is to expand and continue to conduct existing workshops to include, but not limited to, financial literacy, entrepreneurship, healthy lifestyles, life skills/etiquette training that are non-duplicated in public school settings. Art-related activities include drumming for mental health, audio tech, songwriting (critical thinking) paired with piano lessons, visual art, film media art, music recording production, talent showcase performances, and field trips.
2768.direct_services: Direct services include, but not limited to, employability skills, gang resistance, social responsibility, human trafficking, police/community relations, parenting skills, school re-entry, assist with job search, individual/group mentoring, referrals for tertiary education (career/college tours), and referrals as needed, i.e. counseling, mental health professional.
2768.population: Target populations are youth/young adults ages 10 - 21 who may or not may be juvenile justice-challenged, residing in underserved, under-resourced communities in Orange County, Florida. Total number of individuals served up to 100.
2768.outcome: EXPECTED OUTCOME: #1 - Reduce recidivism/Divert from Criminal/Juvenile Justice System (80%), and #2 - Enhance age-eligible individuals' economic self-sufficiency by obtaining jobs while preparing for careers/college, and/or business ownership (30%). METHODOLOGY: #1 - Complete job training, career/college preparation, business development workshops; and #2 - Conduct on-going monitoring of referrals, attendance records, and follow-up contacts.

2514.description: A new perimeter fence and generator will improve shelter safety and resilience, maintaining safe conditions for animals, staff, volunteers, and visitors. The fence will allow for controlled entry, preventing unauthorized admittance and ensuring that the property remains secure. The generator will provide reliable power to ensure continuous care, critical veterinary support, and proper sanitation and climate control for animals sheltered onsite during and following emergencies resulting in a power outage. These upgrades will harden the shelter, support rapid recovery, and position SPCA Tampa Bay to better serve the community.
2514.purpose: Shelter safety and preparedness in the event of an emergency are SPCA’s top priorities. Procurement and installation of a secure perimeter fence and generator will prevent unauthorized access to the facility, protecting staff and animals, and ensure that essential back-up power is available for the entire facility in an emergency. These upgrades will harden the shelter, support rapid recovery, and position SPCA Tampa Bay to better serve the community.
2514.activities: Without adequate electricity back-up, the facility is greatly compromised when power goes out. Lifesaving veterinary care cannot happen. Vaccines requiring refrigeration risk spoilage. Lift stations fail, preventing sanitary disposal of waste. Without proper climate control, lighting, and security fencing, the health and safety of people and animals onsite is threatened.
2514.direct_services: New fencing will prevent unauthorized visitors from routinely gaining access to the 10-acre property through a gate intended for staff and volunteers, creating a security risk for people onsite, as well as animals housed at the shelter. A generator will allow the facility to function effectively in providing essential services to the community in the event of an emergency.
2514.population: 70 shelter staff, over 300 shelter volunteers, and over 8,500 animals that have been surrendered by their owners, along with injured wildlife, served by SPCA each year. Additionally, SPCA Tampa Bay partners with shelters and animal welfare organizations across the state to support families and animals in emergencies and natural disasters, providing housing for pets not permitted in emergency shelters, as well as providing shelter for the animals of first responders during natural disasters.
2514.outcome: The installation of a secure perimeter fence and generator will strengthen the shelter's ability to protect animals, staff, volunteers and the community. Success will be measured by tracking key indicators such as security incidents, power outage impacts, number of animals sheltered during emergencies, and other metrics.

2108.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2108.description: Construction of a new agricultural complex to replace the existing facility that is undersized and was substantially damaged due to Hurricane Helene. The new facility will be a 170ft by 250ft covered arena along with a new 7,000ft climate-controlled exhibition and education building. This facility will be situated on over 40 acres purchased by the County.
2108.purpose: The County’s intent is to construct a 170ft x 250ft new, covered arena along with a new 7,000 sq. ft. climate-controlled, multi-purpose exhibition and education building
2108.activities: The new facility can be utilized for livestock events, rodeos, farmers markets, car shows, community/civic events, and an emergency response staging area during natural disasters.
2108.direct_services: The County and its partners will be able to offer activities centered on promoting agriculture and educating the public about agricultural activities.
2108.population: The general public will be the target population with the number of individuals served greater than 800.
2108.outcome: The project will ensure that future generations of residents have a facility where they are able to understand the lifestyle and educational value of agriculture and experience the paramount role that this industry plays in feeding America. Furthermore, events at this facility will bolster small businesses, encourage additional economic growth including vertical integration within the agriculture sector, and support and encourage careers in agriculture.

2730.organization: Community Health Centers of Pinellas / DBA:
2730.description: Community Health Centers of Pinellas, Inc. dba Evara Health operates 19 healthcare centers across Pinellas County, serving over 62,000 patients annually through more than 228,000 visits. To address Florida’s healthcare workforce shortage, Evara established the Evara Health Institute (EHI) in 2023. In just 18 months, EHI has become the largest healthcare apprenticeship program in Florida, enrolling over 200 apprentices in Medical Assisting, Dental Assisting, Pharmacy Technician, Behavioral Health Technician, and Limited Scope Radiology programs, with more than 90% of graduates employed immediately upon completion. EHI targets unemployed and underemployed residents, offering affordable training at half the cost of comparable programs and has secured over $300,000 in scholarships. Evara proposes to renovate 10,000 square feet of existing space to launch a Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) and
2730.purpose: The purpose of the proposed project is to expand training facility necessary to: - Launch an LPN program. - Establish bridge programs for Medical Assistants and Pharmacy Technicians into nursing degree programs. - Expand Evara's existing Limited Scope Radiology Technician program into a full Radiology Technician program.
2730.activities: Evara will complete renovation of the currently Vacant 10,000sq. feet in EHI building to expand clinical space where students gain hands-on experience alongside Evara provider staff, classrooms for didactic training, and laboratories for technical skills development.
2730.population: The target population for the proposed program are residents of Tampa Bay Area looking for the advancement opportunities in medical field or unemployed and underemployed members of the community. Evara projects to graduate the total of 150 students, within five new or expanded programs, in the first year of operations. These numbers will grow to eight programs and 240 graduating students annually by the third year of operations.
2730.outcome: The funding will allow us to simultaneously address two major community needs: 1) Launch an LPN program to mitigate the statewide nursing shortage. 2) Create a reliable pathway to a successful medical career for the residents of Tampa Bay region and, thus, improve economic stability of the community. The program reduces healthcare workforce shortages and strengthens hospitals, nursing homes, and safety-net providers. The outcomes will be measured through the data on number of EHI graduates and obtaining of the post- graduation employment. Evara will be utilizing methodologies and standards of the State of Florida Department of Education.

2039.description: The proposed project will develop and implement a comprehensive facility digital twin to support more effective management of airport infrastructure. Funding will be used for detailed planning, data collection, and deployment of the digital twin system. This initiative will improve preventive and predictive maintenance in alignment with s. 332.007, F.S., ensuring that facilities are maintained proactively, safely, and in accordance with state requirements.
2039.purpose: The goal of this project is to establish a facility digital twin that enables proactive, data-driven maintenance, improves energy and operational performance, and provides a long-term foundation for informed asset management and capital planning.
2039.activities: The project will include detailed planning, data collection, and deployment as well as ongoing framework for managing the system including change management of the digital twin system.
2039.direct_services: The increased efficiencies and reduction in operating/capital costs associated with the implementation of a digital twin will allow for the savings to be realized during the yearly budgeting process.
2039.population: The over three million passengers a year, the over 400,000 residents of Seminole County, and the tenants and users of the airport will benefit from the efficiencies and savings associated with the project.
2039.outcome: The expected benefit of the project is a reduction in downtime of facility items, maximizing the useful life of equipment and facilities at the airport, and increased safety. These items will be tracked as well as the life of the equipment/facilities.

3181.description: The Health Sciences building will allow FGCU to continue to expand capabilities in research, teaching, practice, and enrollment in strategic ways to meet the unique needs of Southwest Florida. FGCU is embedded in its community and responsive to public/private partners that provide direct services to patients as well industries producing medical devices to promote the health and well-being of the region’s residents. Public health concerns that threaten the region such as comorbidities, access to care, healthy living, the emergence of new diseases, and health literacy are also a focus of interest. These foci have the potential to significantly increase external research funding and impact the community. In addition, FGCU also intends to address the needs of the senior living community and the special challenges faced with a rapidly aging population.
3181.purpose: FGCU is a major supplier of the health professions workforce for the region’s large and ever-growing healthcare industry. Specialized and dedicated teaching, technology, and research labs are critical components in the successful education of future practitioners. The discovery, testing and application of new therapies by faculty and students provide the nexus pivotal to improve the lives of millions of people living in Florida and beyond. These labs will meet the unique needs of multiple health
3181.activities: In the last decade, FGCU has doubled the size of its enrollment in the Marieb College of Health and Human Services. It must continue to expand the ability to meet the demand for baccalaureate through doctoral practitioners in a variety of health fields. FGCU is poised to meet this demand but a lack of space impedes additional growth in our programs. Moreover, the health professions continue to evolve in complexity, both in terms of the technology involved in healthcare delivery, educational tech
3181.direct_services: It will improve graduation rates, retention rates and provide a skilled workforce for the healthcare industry. Further, it will develop partnerships through research and promote innovative opportunities for the advancement of technology and specialized skills within the healthcare industry.
3181.population: University students with over 16,500 students served.
3181.outcome: The addition of the Health Sciences facility will help address long-term institutional goals such as: • Regional sustainability (meet the healthcare needs of the region’s growing population) • Economic diversification (support a key regional industry) • Enhanced research productivity (develop alternative treatment strategies through applied research) • Meet the demand for Healthcare jobs (provide a highly educated workforce)

3182.description: FGCU has consistently emphasized environmental stewardship, integrating it into the university's mission, programs, and academic core. Dating back to 2008, FGCU and Babcock Property Holdings identified a shared interest in resiliency and began discussions about forming a partnership in Charlotte County. These discussions have laid the groundwork for a partnership where FGCU will create a learning community focused on resiliency and best practices, in collaboration with Babcock Ranch.
3182.purpose: Resiliency through service-learning and internships: Students will gain practical experience in resilient and best practices through service-learning and internship opportunities by working with local organizations and industries focused on resiliency, fostering career-readiness and a commitment to environmental stewardship while sharing information with our Southwest Florida community. Additionally, the Charlotte County hub will will include agribusiness and better serve our five county region.
3182.activities: Research initiatives, field experimentation, and scholarly pursuits. Additionally, the development of graduate degrees, courses of study (including early college programs and degree completion options like FGCU Complete), certificate offerings, service-learning opportunities, internships, co-ops, and community outreach programs.
3182.direct_services: It will improve graduation rates, retention rates and provide a skilled workforce. Develop partnerships through research and industry to promote environmental stewardship and resiliency with community outreach.
3182.population: University students with thousands of student served.
3182.outcome: Strengthen academic and workforce alignment with curricula that meet our regional demand, respond to industry trends, include transferable skills and empower students to pursue involvement to gain hands-on work to deepen the connection to the community. Metrics: FTIC Four Year Graduation Rates; Retention and % of Bachelor’s Graduates Employed $40K+. State University Performance-based Metrics.

2665.description: This project involves the construction of a redundant sub-aqueous wastewater force main crossing from the with the associated apertures of the Intracoastal Waterway (connecting the barrier Island to the mainland) near Atlantic Boulevard in the City of Pompano Beach. The redundant main that would provide emergency capacity in the event of failure of the current primary transmission line, provide a mechanism to switch flows for maintenance of the primary transmission line and provides additional conveyance capacity for population growth. The sub-aqueous segment spans approximately 900 linear feet and is connected to Master Lift Station 12, which services the entire barrier island from Hillsborough Inlet south to Commercial Boulevard. The area and infrastructure is at high risk of corrosion and material degradation due to saltwater impacts.
2665.purpose: Provide redundancy, service reliability and additional capacity of wastewater conveyance system utilizing 24-inch wastewater force main crossing under the Intracoastal Waterway (connection from the barrier island to the mainland).
2665.activities: Construction of new sub-aqueous pipeline with appropriate apertures and integration with Master Lift Station 12 (formerly Lift Station 21).
2665.direct_services: Ensures continued wastewater service to residents and businesses on the barrier island from Hillsborough Inlet to Commercial Boulevard in case of primary line failure.
2665.population: Approximately 20,000 residents and businesses of the barrier Island (Lauderhill by the Sea, portions of Pompano Beach).
2665.outcome: Key benefits ensure a vital backup system to prevents service outages and sewer backups if the primary transmission line fails or is in need of maintenance as well as future growth capacity. The outcome will be measured through reduction in emergency maintenance events and restored dual-line system capacity.

1986.description: The Senior Program will support high quality, low-cost events and nutrition for seniors. The program will provide weekly activities through shuttle bus transportation, credentialed and courteous staff services, social interaction, recreational outings, health fairs, exercise and nutrition. This program will minimize service delivery gaps for our senior population who may suffer from depression, anxiety, loneliness and other ailments that plague our elderly residents. The majority of this population is low-to-moderate income Seniors that have limited resources, and desire to be active members of this community.
1986.purpose: The goal is to minimize service gaps for our seniors who may suffer from depression, anxiety, loneliness and other ailments. This program will enhance the quality of life of our participants by providing much needed activities and services. According to the National Council on Aging (NCOA), studies show senior programs provide numerous benefits in 2025, including improved physical and mental health, reduced healthcare costs, and enhanced social connections. Participants experience lower rates of

The program will provide direct services to seniors in the program. Participants will have opportunities to bond and congregat
