The program will provide weekly activities through shuttle bus transportation, credentialed and courteous staff services, social interaction, recreational outings, health fairs, exercise and nutrition. These Seniors will experience a better quality of life, than if they stay in isolation without the opportunity to en
1986.population: Senior residents ages 60 years and older are the target population for this program. With the funding request, we have the capacity to provide direct services and serve approximately 100 Seniors.
1986.outcome: We expect the outcome to be a safe environment for Seniors to participate in holistic activities within our program. Direct services will be provided. This outcome will be measured by attendance records and participant surveys. By providing a comprehensive program that meets service gaps for Seniors, we can assist them with obtaining a better quality of life. The program can also assist any participants who have experienced loss. We will also provide referral services as needed or when appropriate.

2666.description: The City of West Park is in need of assistance to address the issue of truancy and crime prevention within South Broward. The City's surrounding schools have displayed multiple risk factors including, but not limited to suicide, truancy, juvenile crime, teenage pregnancy, alcohol and drug abuse, and other negative behavior patterns. According to the Association for Supervision and Curriculum Development (ASCD), these factors can lead to the detriment of a student’s capacity to envision or achieve success. As part of the City’s commitment to provide quality Youth Programming that will deter truancy, bullying and other negative behavior among school-age children, funding is being requested to support after school and summer programming. Early intervention is essential to preventing and deterring negative behavior and any potential for crime.
2666.purpose: The City of West Park is in need of assistance to address the issue of truancy and crime prevention within South Broward. Students with the community's schools have displayed multiple risk factors including, but not limited to suicide, truancy, juvenile crime, teenage pregnancy, alcohol and drug abuse, and other negative behavior patterns. Early intervention is essential to preventing and deterring negative behavior and potential for crime. According to the Afterschool Alliance, after-school pro
2666.activities: Early intervention is essential to preventing and deterring negative behavior and any potential for criminal activity. Our low-income, at-risk community is seeking support that will create a positive impact on students. Support is needed for this community outreach for crime prevention and anti-bullying. We will also provide services for tutoring, physical education, cultural enrichment, field trips and nutrition, etc.
2666.direct_services: As part of the City’s commitment to providing quality Youth Programming that will deter truancy, bullying and other negative and adverse behavior among school-age children, funding is being requested to support after school and summer programming,. In addition, there will be a production of a skit that will feature the City and students as actors. The Youth Advisory Council will be peer mentors.
2666.population: Youth within the community that maybe at-risk for suicide, truancy, juvenile crime, teenage pregnancy, alcohol and drug abuse, and other negative behavior patterns.
2666.outcome: We expect the outcome to be a safe environment for students to participate in holistic activities within our program. Direct services will be provided. This outcome will be measured by attendance records, report cards, participant surveys. By providing a comprehensive program that meets service gaps for at-risk youth, we can keep them on tract for a better future.

2668.description: The Pearly Express Mobile Dental Program combines oral and behavioral health services to deliver whole-person, evidence-based care directly to underserved communities. Operating from a mobile dental unit, BCOM provides preventive and restorative dental care alongside behavioral health screenings using the PHQ-2 tool to identify early signs of depression. Patients who screen positive are connected to BCOM’s behavioral health providers for follow-up and treatment. This integrated model expands access, reduces barriers, and improves overall health outcomes by bringing comprehensive, patient-centered care to neighborhoods where it is needed most.
2668.purpose: The funds requested will support the implementation and expansion of BCOM’s Pearly Express Mobile Health Program, designed to deliver integrated comprehensive oral and behavioral health services directly to underserved communities. Funding will be used to operate a mobile dental unit, support experienced oral health team, and integrate behavioral health screening tools such as the PHQ-2 into routine dental care. This investment will enable BCOM to identify depression early, provide preventive an
2668.activities: Funds will support the Pearly Express Mobile Dental Unit, expanding oral and behavioral health services for underserved Broward County residents. The unit will provide preventive and restorative dental care, use the PHQ-2 for depression screening, and connect patients to BCOM’s network for follow-up improving access, prevention, and community health.
2668.direct_services: The appropriation funds the Pearly Express Mobile Dental Unit, providing dental and behavioral health care to 300 underserved Broward residents. Services include exams, cleanings, sealants, fillings, and PHQ-2 screenings with referrals to BCOM’s care network. By serving schools, housing sites, and communities, the project expands access and improves health outcomes.
2668.population: Many of these individuals live in federally designated Health Professional Shortage Areas (HPSAs) and face barriers such as cost, transportation, and lack of insurance. During its first year, the program will deliver preventive and restorative dental services to approximately 300 individuals through community-based mobile outreach. As capacity grows, BCOM anticipates reaching over 600 residents annually, improving access, reducing preventable dental disease and strengthening oral health outcomes
2668.outcome: Benefits include increased annual dental visits, reduced untreated decay and emergency room use, and better coordination between dental and behavioral health services. Success will be measured through a data-driven evaluation process using BCOM’s electronic health record (EHR) to track patients served, services provided, and treatment outcomes. Additional measures include patient satisfaction surveys, quarterly data reviews, and annual Uniform Data System (UDS) reporting. These methods ensure accountability and demonstrate measurable improvements in access, prevention, and overall community health.

2399.description: Hamilton School for Classical and Civic Education, established by the 2022 Legislature, supports teaching/research regarding ideas, traditions, texts that form the foundations of Western/American civilization. Project: Continued rehabilitation of a historic Infirmary Building (a basement and 3 floors) housing the Hamilton School. Project scope includes additional substantive reconfiguration of current space &/or substantive changing types of BOG space categories.

2399.activities: Home for the Hamilton School, a new university-wide academic unit at UF.
2399.direct_services: UF renewed commitment to civic debate in an intellectually diverse community to support/challenge one another. Programmatic Outcomes: new curricular offerings; lectures/debates/symposia on matters of public importance; expanded civics resources/teacher training; increased focus ideas, traditions, texts forming the foundation of Western/American Civilization.
2399.population: Thousands of grade school students, high school students and University of Florida students. The school also provides training to Florida citizens and K-12 teachers.
2399.outcome: Core purpose of the Hamilton School is to help students (K-20) develop the knowledge, habits of thought, analytical ability, and character to be citizens and leaders in a free society. Measures to include development of programming/training related to civic education/values of open inquiry/civil discourse to support K-20. Reported Coordination/Activities with UF Hamilton School, FSU Institute of Politics, FIU Adam Smith Center and School District curation/implementation of Portraits in Patriotism.

2072.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2072.description: The goal of the aquaculture technology development and transfer initiative is to launch a targeted program aimed at rapidly advancing and implementing sustainable land-based marine aquaculture operations utilizing emerging technologies on Florida farms & ranches. The focus also includes workforce training designed to facilitate the transfer of information and adoption of new products and processes in Florida commercial agriculture operations.
2072.purpose: The goal of the Initiative is to launch a targeted program aimed at rapidly advancing and implementing sustainable land-based marine aquaculture operations utilizing emerging technologies on Florida farms & ranches. The focus also includes workforce training designed to facilitate the transfer of information and adoption of new products and processes in Florida commercial agriculture operations.
2072.activities: In close collaboration with FDACS, Mote will administer a marine aquaculture technology transfer grant and training program directly supporting Florida farmers & ranchers to develop self-sustainable aquaculture operations on their land.
2072.direct_services: Establish an education, extension and training platform to transfer technology to local commercial farmers & ranchers for successful land-based saltwater aquaculture operations. Identify opportunities for business and industry collaborations and socialize next steps to position the industry for private sector investment.
2072.population: Farmers and aquaculture producers: Creating direct aquaculture related jobs and economic growth for Florida. Including seafood consumers, the initiative will benefit people throughout southwest Florida.
2072.outcome: This Initiative transfers new, efficient, and sustainable techniques for Florida fish production. Activities will be conducted in closed land-based recirculating water systems and includes the transfer of emerging technologies and processes for Florida commercial aquaculture operations. Number of grants executed as pilot commercial-scale facilities on Florida farms & ranches.

2249.description: The specific purpose of the funds being requested is to support the implementation and expansion of the Reach Out and Read program, which promotes early childhood literacy and language development by integrating books, anticipatory guidance, and shared reading into pediatric primary care well-child visits to support caregivers in fostering early literacy and healthy relationships. The funds will be used statewide, with a particular emphasis on reaching undeserved and rural communities in Florida.
2249.purpose: The specific purpose of the requested funds is to strengthen early childhood development by integrating the evidence- based Reach Out and Read model into pediatric care. This will be achieved by providing training to medical providers, and residency programs, developmentally appropriate books to children, offering parents guidance on shared reading, and using books for developmental surveillance during well-child visits, fostering improved literacy, relational health, and long-term well-being fo
2249.activities: The funds will support the implementation of the evidence-based Reach Out and Read model. Activities and services include training clinicians to deliver literacy guidance, providing developmentally and culturally appropriate books during well-child visits, educating parents on the importance of shared reading, and using books for developmental surveillance. These services foster early literacy, strengthen parent-child relationships, and support healthy child development.
2249.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services to families with children from birth to age 5 by integrating the evidence-based Reach Out and Read model into pediatric care. Clinicians will distribute developmentally appropriate books during well-child visits, educate parents on the importance of shared reading for early literacy and development, and use books to assess developmental milest
2249.population: This project targets pediatric providers, residency programs, and families with children from birth to age 5, with a focus on under-resourced communities, high Medicaid populations, and rural areas. In Florida, it currently promotes early childhood development and literacy through pediatric care, reaching over 600,000 well-child visits and approximately 300,000 families annually. With strong community support, the program operates in 281 pediatric clinics across 40 counties, creating a meaningfu
2249.outcome: The project aims to improve early literacy, strengthen parent-child bonds, boost school readiness, and support healthy child development. It reduces toxic stress and fosters cognitive, social, and emotional well-being, particularly in rural areas. Outcomes will be tracked via clinician observations, parent-reported reading, milestone assessments, and evaluations of book distribution and literacy guidance. ROR is the only pediatric-based literacy model endorsed by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), validated by 20+ peer-reviewed studies.

2122.description: Harbor58 is requesting nonrecurring state funding to support the development of a transitional housing campus for youth aging out of foster care. Each year, young adults exit the foster care system without stable housing, family support, or sufficient resources, placing them at high risk of homelessness and unemployment. This project will construct a purpose- built campus providing safe, stable housing for youth ages 18–22 as they transition into independent adulthood. State funds will be used exclusively for fixed capital construction costs, including site preparation, residential unit construction, and related infrastructure, and will not be used for salaries or ongoing operations. Upon completion, the campus will serve up to 12 residents at a time, with new cohorts served approximately every 18 months, while ongoing operations and supportive programming will be sustained through priva
2122.purpose: The purpose of this project is to increase access to safe, stable transitional housing for youth aging out of foster care, reducing homelessness and improving long-term outcomes related to education, employment, and self-sufficiency.
2122.activities: The project will construct a dedicated transitional housing campus that provides safe housing paired with access to supportive services, including life skills development, employment readiness, financial literacy, and mentorship.
2122.direct_services: Youth aging out of foster care will receive stable housing in a supportive environment designed to promote independence, personal responsibility, and successful transition into adulthood.
2122.population: The target population is youth aging out of foster care, ages 18–22, who are at high risk of homelessness.
2122.outcome: Expected outcomes include increased housing stability, improved employment and educational engagement, and reduced risk of homelessness. Outcomes will be measured through program participation data, housing retention rates, and participant progress toward individualized transition goals.

3540.description: Purchase of a fire Ladder truck for DeSoto County Fire/Rescue to replace an existing ladder truck that is frequently out of service making it unreliable to use in rescue and firefighting operations. There is no market for the current truck for resale. The Fire Ladder truck provides an extendable ladder and bucket to access multi-story facilities or to direct firefighting to high flame fires.
3540.purpose: Purchase of a reliable first response firefighting ladder truck for public safety and first responder safety.
3540.activities: Equipment level of service and operational reliability.
3540.population: The DeSoto County Fire/Rescue department services the entire County and the City of Arcadia as the sole provider of service. The County also has mutual aid agreements with the neighboring counties of Charlotte and Hardee counties.
3540.outcome: Vehicle response time and time in service will be the measurement data to evidence the new equipment is serving the intended purpose of providing for the protection of people and property from fires.

3541.description: Land acquisition for replacement of the County Jail and Sheriff's Office Administrative Office Complex. The current jail facility does not meet current jail standards and has many maintenance problems as the original jail was constructed in the early 70's, and added onto in the early 90's. The facility does not meet the operational needs of the Sheriff's Office and is inefficient and costly to operate based on the physical condition and layout. The project is to acquire a site suitable for the replacement of the Jail and Administrative Complex that meets statutory location requirements. Acquiring the land now will allow the County to secure a site while it is available and to provide for site specific planning and design services. A conceptual design has been completed this past year and has determined 12-15 acres is necessary to construct a facility and account for expansion, parking an
3541.purpose: To secure property for the future replacement of the Jail and Administrative Sheriff's Offices
3541.activities: Currently, purchase of property to ensure we have a suitable and available site.
3541.direct_services: Community benefit, while not specifically to provide a direct service to the citizens outside of the planning and facility replacement.
3541.population: Law enforcement and corrections staff, incarcerated individuals and their families, and the general public from a planning perspective.
3541.outcome: Acquisition of a suitable property that meets the needs and location requirements provided by law.

2223.description: The project is to acquire a Rapid Deployment Communication System (RDCS), also known as Communication on Wheels or COW) and a fixed spectrum analyzer to establish resilient, uninterrupted emergency communications and advanced threat detection capabilities in Miami-Dade County, safeguarding hundreds of thousands of people during large scale events. The spectrum analyzer will be used to triangulate the position of unauthorized radio frequency transmissions.
2223.purpose: These funds directly enhance public safety and emergency response, providing critical communication infrastructure that protects citizens and visitors during mass gatherings. This includes acquiring a Rapid Deployment Communication System (RDCS, also known as Communication on Wheels or COW) and a fixed spectrum analyzer. The spectrum analyzer will be used to triangulate the position of unauthorized radio frequency transmissions. These upgrades aim to maintain secure and reliable communications a
2223.activities: Funds will cover acquisition and deployment of RDCS mobile communication units and fixed spectrum analyzer systems at key locations. These activities will support real-time emergency coordination, manage large crowds, detect security threats like unauthorized drones, and ensure reliable communication among all public safety agencies during the event.
2223.direct_services: Citizens and visitors will receive enhanced public safety protections with faster emergency responses, effective crowd management, and real-time threat detection. The improved communication infrastructure will enable law enforcement, fire rescue, EMS, and transit agencies to coordinate efficiently, ensuring a safe environment day-to-day and during mass gatherings.
2223.population: The target population is the 2.8 million residents in Miami-Dade County and thousands of visitors for major events hosted in the County.
2223.outcome: The project’s benefit is a secure, safe environment with improved emergency response and prevention of security disruptions such as rogue drones or signal interference. Success will be measured by monitoring communication system reliability, emergency response times, and security incident reports before, during, and after event activities through interagency evaluations.

2225.description: Reconstruction of NW 117th Avenue will accommodate the realigning and improvement of the intersection with NW 34 St. This new intersection will be a key to a new ramp to the Turnpike expressway. The works along NW 117 Ave include curb and gutters, drainage improvements, new pavement, striping, lighting, signage, sidewalk, relocation of the mass arm at NW 25 St, and installation of new traffic signal on NW 34 St. and NW 117 Ave due to the new construction of the NW Turnpike ramp.
2225.purpose: The NW 117th Avenue reconstruction will realign and upgrade the intersection at NW 34th Street, creating a critical connection to a new Turnpike expressway ramp. Improvements along NW 117th Avenue include new curb and gutter, upgraded drainage, pavement and striping, lighting, signage, relocation of the mast arm at NW 25th Street, and a new traffic signal at NW 34th Street.
2225.activities: Funds will be spent to improve NW 117 Ave from NW 25 St to NW 34 St, the redesigned intersection with NW 34 St, where a new mass arm, signal head, and sidewalks will help pedestrians safely cross the area. The existing mass arm at NW 25 St will be relocated.
2225.direct_services: The Project includes roadway improvement, stormwater drainage, new signage and street lighting, sidewalks and new mass arm and signal head at NW 34 St. This will increase vehicular and pedestrian safety, and improvement in cargo transportation and its incorporation into the Turnpike Expressway and will also serve as a mitigation initiative to help prevent flood related losses.
2225.outcome: This project will reduce flooding and ponding along the roadway, improving safety and reliability during major storms when issues are typically not visible but still impactful. The installation of new street lighting and sidewalks will enhance visibility, expand walkability, and significantly improve pedestrian safety. Additionally, with the construction of the new Turnpike ramp, a new traffic signal is essential to manage increased traffic flow and ensure safe movements; a warrant study has already confirmed the need for this signal.

2227.description: The City of Doral will provide POTUS/dignitary security details at and around the Trump National Doral Resort, a venue that routinely hosts U.S. and international dignitaries and attracts large crowds, protesters, and supporters.
2227.purpose: The goal of this project is to secure overtime funding for expenses incurred by the Doral Police Department during President of the United States (POTUS) and dignitary-related events at the Trump National Doral Resort. The funding allows the Department to recover costs associated with providing security support to federal agencies during elevated national-security operations.
2227.activities: The City of Doral will provide POTUS/dignitary security details at and around the Trump National Doral Resort, a venue that routinely hosts U.S. and international dignitaries and attracts large crowds, protesters, and supporters.
2227.direct_services: Funding provides enhanced public-safety measures during POTUS/dignitary visits, ensuring a secure environment for residents, visitors, and businesses while supporting federal protective operations.
2227.population: President of the United States and other dignitaries, ensuring a secure environment for them and for the general public.
2227.outcome: POTUS/dignitary overtime funding supports enhanced public-safety measures during high-risk events, ensuring a secure environment for residents and visitors.

2228.description: This project delivers direct educational and supportive services to economically disadvantaged individuals, at-risk youth, first-generation college students, and victims of crime. The program provides academic tutoring, college-readiness and navigation support, essential school supplies, and safe, structured summer programs that keep students engaged in a supervised learning environment. By combining year-round academic support with out-of-school enrichment, the program strengthens educational outcomes, promotes stability, and reduces risk factors associated with crime and economic hardship in underserved communities.
2228.purpose: The purpose of the funds requested is to provide direct, practical support that improves educational success and stability for economically disadvantaged individuals, at-risk youth, first-generation college students, and victims of crime. Funding will support tutoring, college-readiness and navigation assistance, essential school supplies, and safe, structured summer programs. These investments strengthen academic outcomes, support college access and persistence, and reduce risk factors associat
2228.activities: The program will provide academic tutoring and college-readiness support for first-generation college-bound students, supply essential school materials and backpacks to at-risk youth, and expand structured summer camp programming with safe, supervised, and enriching activities. Together, these services keep students engaged, strengthen academic performance, and provide critical support to families.
2228.direct_services: Funding will deliver direct support to local families and students by providing academic tutoring, college-readiness guidance, and essential school supplies for at-risk youth. It will also fund safe, structured summer programs that give students a supervised place to learn, grow, and stay engaged while school is out. These services offer immediate, hands-on help to residents.
2228.population: The project serves economically disadvantaged individuals, with a strong focus on at-risk youth and students across multiple age groups, including grade school, high school, and university/college students. It also supports victims of crime by providing services and programs designed to promote safety, stability, and positive educational and personal outcomes.
2228.outcome: The project is expected to reduce juvenile recidivism and improve public safety among participating youth. Success will be measured by year-over-year decreases in repeat juvenile offenses using police incident data and law enforcement reporting, along with lower arrest and school disciplinary rates and more positive interactions with law enforcement. Academic progress will be evaluated through regular review of report cards, standardized test scores, attendance, and graduation rates.

2229.organization: Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida
2229.description: The funds will support a scientific study to document regional reference conditions and identify phosphorus-driven ecological thresholds needed to guide restoration in the Everglades. By analyzing degraded periphyton communities—now detected across large areas of wetland—this project will generate the data necessary to understand ecosystem impacts, prevent further decline, and inform targeted restoration strategies that protect overall habitat health, including fisheries.
2229.purpose: Degraded periphyton has been detected across dozens of square kilometers of wetland through monitoring by the National Park Service's SFCN (NCRA 2021). Impaired periphyton communities associated with persistent above- ambient P exposure in the Everglades are known to lead to cascading consequences harming ecosystem health, including fisheries (Gaiser et al. 2006). This study documents regional reference conditions and P-driven ecological thresholds to effectively plan restoration in the area.
2229.activities: Utilize a flow-through flume design, modeled after the flume study designed by Florida International University (FIU) for establishing protective P criterion for Everglades National Park (Childers et al. 2001). A flow-through flume design offers several key advantages over a mesocosm design. First, flow-through flume designs enable enrichment to occur in a mixing area (in our case, 2-m long).
2229.direct_services: To provide a phosphorous target that protects the WERP wetlands of the BICY from an imbalance in the natural populations of aquatic flora or fauna. We anticipate results from experimental P additions in the BICY to be similar to those in other regions of the Everglades (Gaiser et al. 2005, 2006). This data will aid policymakers and scientists to protect an Outstanding Florida Water.
2229.population: Users of Florida's public lands, South Florida's fisheries, and ecotourism. More than 1m visit/year.
2229.outcome: By determining the resilience of the ecosystem to the introduction of phosphorous from new sources previously outside of the Big Cypress Basin, appropriate targets for policymakers and system operators can be set, preserving the ecosystem health of, and therefore the health-supporting outcomes of interacting with an ecologically intact public land. We will measure this by establishing a scientifically supported numerical P-loading threshold at which ecosystem health significantly declines.

2126.description: The Home365 – Veteran Housing Initiative provides stable transitional housing, case management, and coordinated support services for veterans experiencing homelessness or housing instability in Northeast Florida. LOVE365 INC will offer safe housing units, daily living supports, and individualized service plans to help veterans stabilize, rebuild, and transition into permanent housing. The program prioritizes veterans at the highest risk, including those recently displaced, disabled, or exiting institutional settings.
2126.purpose: To provide safe transitional housing and supportive services for 20–50 veterans annually, reducing homelessness and supporting long-term stability.
2126.activities: Transitional housing placement, Daily living supports, Case management, Transportation assistance, Mental and behavioral health referrals, Employment and benefits navigation, Permanent housing placement assistance.
2126.direct_services: Direct shelter, food, case management, crisis stabilization, and housing navigation for veterans experiencing homelessness or housing instability.
2126.population: Homeless veterans Disabled veterans Economically disadvantaged veterans Recently displaced veterans Number served annually: 20–50 veterans
2126.outcome: Expected outcomes include: providing transitional housing for 20–30 veterans annually; completing individualized housing stability plans for each participant; supporting at least 75% of veterans in achieving measurable progress toward employment, benefits access, or stability goals; and transitioning at least 50% of participants into permanent or long-term housing. Progress will be measured through intake and exit records, case management documentation, monthly housing occupancy reports, and verification of service connections and housing placements.

2232.description: The City of Hialeah is pursuing funding for the removal of invasive and non-native tree species located in public rights- of-way, with the intention of replacing them with native Florida tree species. Invasive, non-native trees can disrupt local ecosystems, outcompete native vegetation, and contribute to long-term degradation of green spaces. These species often spread rapidly, posing threats to local plants and wildlife. They can be introduced either intentionally for landscaping purposes or inadvertently through various human activities. Once they establish themselves, these invasive trees can dominate landscapes, diminish biodiversity, and modify ecological functions. Notable examples of invasive tree species include the Australian Pine (Casuarina equisetifolia), Brazilian Peppertree (Schinus terebinthifolia), and Chinese Tallow (Triadica sebifera), all of which are recognized for the
2232.purpose: Removal of invasive and non-native tree species located in public rights-of-way, with the intention of replacing them with native Florida tree species. Invasive, non-native trees can disrupt local ecosystems, out-compete native vegetation, and contribute to long-term degradation of green spaces. These species often spread rapidly.
2232.activities: The City of Hialeah is pursuing funding for the removal of invasive and non-native tree species located in public rights- of-way, with the intention of replacing them with native Florida tree species. Invasive, non-native trees can disrupt local ecosystems, outcompete native vegetation, and contribute to long-term degradation of green spaces. These species often spread rapidly.

Invasive, non-native trees can disrupt local ecosystems, outcompete native vegetation, and contribute to long-term degradation of green spaces. These species often spread rapidly.

2233.description: The City of Hialeah looks to replace its current water meters to an automated water meter reading system. Automated Meter Reading (AMR) would provide increased billing accuracy, reduced costs, and improved efficiency for both customers and the City of Hialeah Water & Sewer Department. It eliminates manual errors, estimated bills, and the need for meter readers to visit properties, which also enhances customer privacy and employee safety. For customers, AMR can provide detailed consumption data to help manage consumption use, while the Water & Sewer Department can better detect usage and leaks remotely. Moreover, AMR eliminates billing errors from manual readings and removes the need for estimated bills based on past usage.
2233.purpose: With an AMR system you would be looking at more accurate bills, reduced costs, convenience and privacy, faster leak detection, reduced labor costs, improved efficiency, increased accuracy and overall better customer service to the consumer.
2233.activities: The City of Hialeah Water & Sewer Department would oversee the complete installation and then operation of the automated water meters system with project management and administration. This will include communication hardware and network. Software and data management systems. Labor and contractor services. Testing, calibration, and quality assurance. Moreover, training and education, maintenance and ongoing support for the system.
2233.direct_services: To enhance the reliability of the city's water services and modernize the infrastructure, the City of Hialeah Water & Sewer Department would upgrade or replace 10,000 of the existing water meters that connect our customers' homes and businesses to the water system. Once complete, the meters will enable the city to implement an AMR system, which will provide more reliable and accurate service to me
2233.population: The City of Hialeah is the sixth largest city in the State of Florida, second largest in Miami-Dade County. We expect to service approximately 30,000 residents.
2233.outcome: An AMR would provide increased billing accuracy, reduced costs, and improved efficiency for both customers and the City of Hialeah Water & Sewer Department. It eliminates manual errors, estimated bills, and the need for meter readers to visit properties, which also enhances customer privacy and employee safety. For customers, AMR can provide detailed consumption data to help manage consumption use, while the Water & Sewer Department can better detect the usage by its customers. Moreover, this will help in reducing the municipal bureaucracy and overhead.

2724.description: The Hillsboro Inlet connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Intracoastal Waterway. It lies between the City of Pompano Beach and the Town of Hillsboro Beach. The inlet provides critical access to commercial/recreational boaters. Severe wave energy causes shoreline erosion and sediment to drift into the channel compromising navigation and the foundation and concrete footers of the shoreline's lighthouse. Funds would be used to install shoreline stabilization structures and nature-based solutions to stop erosion, improve navigation, prevent flooding of adjacent homes and businesses, protect the foundation and concrete footers of the historic Hillsboro Inlet Lighthouse, enhance shorebird and turtle nesting sites, and significantly reduce the need for and high cost of continual dredging of the inlet by the Hillsboro Inlet District.
2724.purpose: The Hillsboro Inlet connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Intracoastal Waterway. It lies between the City of Pompano Beach and the Town of Hillsboro Beach. The inlet provides critical access to commercial/recreational boaters. Severe wave energy causes shoreline erosion and sediment to drift into the channel compromising navigation and the foundation and concrete footers of the shoreline's lighthouse. Funds would be used to install shoreline stabilization structures and nature solutions to stop ero
2724.activities: Wave modeling study, engineering, design, permitting, manufacturing and installation of shoreline stabilization devices, and scientific monitoring
2724.direct_services: Project funding will provide safe access to the lighthouse for visitors, control erosion which will help retain sand on the beach for recreation, improve navigational access for boaters, protect the area from flooding to protect area homes and businesses, and reduce dredge-related expenses for the Hillsboro Inlet District (a local taxing special district).
2724.population: Target population includes residents and visitors of Broward County, City of Pompano Beach, Town of Hillsboro Beach, the Hillsboro inlet, and the lighthouse.
2724.outcome: Project benefits include erosion control, sediment stabilization, improved inlet navigation, enhanced recreational beaches, flood control, improved structural stability of the lighthouse infrastructure, enhanced fish, wildlife and seagrass habitats, and the reduced cost of dredge and beach renourishment operations by the Hillsboro Inlet District.

2796.description: The City of West Palm Beach is taking a proactive approach to shift the future of its water supply from reliance on surface water to an alternative water supply – the Floridan Aquifer. A first step in this multi-year program is to implement a pilot study for process evaluation and validation of RO membrane performance. The pilot testing will be used for water quality analyses and studies that will evaluate corrosion control and blending strategies within the water distribution system. Use of this information will inform preliminary engineering and design.
2796.purpose: The specific purpose is to complete the reverse-osmosis(RO) pilot testing and associated studies for the Project, which will help the City of West Palm Beach determine the best treatment method(s) for use of Floridan Aquifer water. The City is taking a proactive approach to shift from reliance on surface water supply to an alternative water supply, as they are concerned with how current source waters will be impacted by future climatological changes, including weather patterns and quality issues
2796.activities: The purpose of the funds is to complete a RO pilot testing and associated studies. The activities that will occur as a result of the pilot project are: • Develop additional source water quality data necessary to support full scale design and evaluate freshened Floridan Aquifer source water affected by the ASR well. • Calibrate process modeling against actual operating data and validate design criteria for the membrane system. • Characterize membrane cleaning frequency and cleaning efficiency. •
2796.direct_services: The RO pilot testing and associated studies will support the City of West Palm Beach in shifting its water supply from surface water to an alternative water supply. As a result of the RO pilot testing and studies, and the future construction of a new alternative water supply facility that uses Floridan Aquifer water, citizens will have a more resilient potable water supply.
2796.population: The project will provide water to individuals within the City's water service area, and via a special franchise agreement, to the Towns of Palm Beach and South Palm Beach. The total target population served is estimated at more than 120,000 customers.
2796.outcome: The expected benefit of the project is the basis for preliminary engineering, design, and construction of a reliable alternative water supply source for the City of West Palm Beach. This will be measured in million gallons per day of available potable water, as well as by measuring the water quality of potable water from the Floridan Aquifer.

2361.description: The Old Okeechobee Rail Safety Intersection Improvements project includes the removal of a half rail crossing, realignment of Old Okeechobee Road and Parker Avenue, and installation of a new traffic signal system. The project addresses long-standing safety issues identified in the Jefferson Terminal District Rail Safety Improvements Study (2023), which recommended a new signal and partial crossing closure to reduce train-vehicle conflicts and improve intersection operations. The City of West Palm Beach entered into an agreement with the South Florida Regional Transportation Authority (SFRTA) in 2023 for trackwork and track signal design and permitting.
2361.purpose: The purpose of this project is to improve safety and traffic operations at the Old Okeechobee Road and Parker Avenue intersection by removing a half rail crossing, realigning the roadway, and installing a new traffic signal system. These improvements will reduce vehicle-train conflict points, prevent near-miss incidents, and enhance overall intersection efficiency.
2361.activities: Activities include construction of the roadway realignment, installation of a new traffic signal system coordinated with the South Florida Regional Transportation Authority (SFRTA), and reconstruction of the rail crossing. The project also includes pavement restoration, ADA-compliant sidewalks, and updated signage and striping to improve driver awareness and safety.
2361.direct_services: The project will provide safer and more reliable access for motorists, pedestrians, and cyclists using Old Okeechobee Road. By eliminating unsafe turning movements and reducing vehicle queuing near the rail crossing, the project will directly enhance public safety, traffic flow, and connectivity to nearby residential, commercial, and industrial areas.
2361.population: The target population includes motorists, residents, and local employees traveling through the Old Okeechobee corridor. Approximately 1,000 daily users will directly benefit from improved safety and reduced congestion, while the broader community benefits from enhanced emergency response times and reduced rail-related traffic incidents.
2361.outcome: The project will result in fewer vehicle-train near-miss incidents, reduced traffic congestion, and improved intersection level of service. Outcomes will be measured using pre- and post-construction traffic counts, crash data, and operational analyses following FDOT and FRA standards. Additional performance metrics will include queue length reduction and average vehicle delay improvements.

2378.description: The West Palm Beach Fire Department has a regional hazardous materials response team, serving not only the City of West Palm Beach, but surrounding areas of Palm Beach County such as Palm Beach, Riviera Beach, Palm Beach Gardens and more. The requested package includes a chemical analyzer (FTIR, Raman), a foam / vapor dispersion trailer and a mass decontamination set. The combined package will address the rapidly evolving chemical, biological, industrial, and terror-related threats.
2378.purpose: The purpose of this haz mat package is to expand our chemical/ WMD detection ability by purchasing a Combined FTIR and Raman spectroscopy with Smart Spectral Processing (SSP) as well as a mass decontamination and foam trailer for mass vapor suppression. This new equipment would allow firefighters to rapidly suppress vapors from a chemical or WMD incident, analyze the product and decontaminate any exposed persons. The package would be used in over 10 of the 15 National Planning Scenarios (HSPD-8)
2378.activities: Firefighters will receive specialized training on the new equipment upon delivery, and department policies will be updated accordingly. The analyzer and vapor suppression trailer will be maintained on a scheduled basis by a contracted vendor. Firefighters will perform daily operational checks to ensure the analyzer is charged and fully functional. After any deployment or training use of the trailer or decontamination equipment, disposable supplies will be replenished, equipment inventoried, and
2378.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from, faster identification of hazardous substances during emergencies, quicker and more effective decontamination of exposed individuals, improved public safety through rapid vapor suppression to prevent the spread of toxic chemicals, and finally protection during large-scale incidents, including chemical attacks, fire as a weapon, or drug-related threats like fentanyl expos
2378.population: The target population served by this project includes: Residents of West Palm Beach, as well as surrounding communities in Palm Beach County and across Florida, who may be impacted by chemical, biological, or WMD-related incidents. Visitors and tourists in high-traffic areas, public events, and transportation hubs. Vulnerable populations, including individuals in schools, hospitals, nursing homes, and other care facilities. First responders and public safety personnel, who will benefit from enha
2378.outcome: This project will directly contribute to saving lives, minimizing environmental impact, and restoring public safety more efficiently during high-risk incidents. The effectiveness of the project will be measured using a combination of quantitative and qualitative metrics, including: Response Time Metrics compared to national standards; Reduction in injuries or fatalities in hazmat-related incidents, Training and Readiness Evaluations, Frequency and results of drills using the new equipment, Performance assessments during multi-agency exercises and After-Action Reports (AARs).

3802.description: Three independent assessments were conducted between 2015 - 2020 with all consultants rating the integrity of the current 100,000-gallon storage tank as in “poor” condition, lacking potable water capacity to meet current and future needs, and lacking capacity for fire flow protection. Replacement of the current 100,000-gallon water storage tank with recommended 260,000-gallon water storage tank will increase capacity, meeting all future potable water needs as well as fire flow protection.
3802.purpose: Ensure adequate water supply for consumption and fire protection.
3802.activities: Replacement of current water tank at water plant.
3802.direct_services: Water supply for consumption, irrigation, and fire protection.
3802.outcome: FDEP water supply quality and pressure standards for water utilities.

2379.description: The existing Water Treatment Plant (WTP) is obsolete due to the inability of the technology to meet increasingly demanding water quality objectives, in particular the U.S. EPA's recent regulations for Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) known as "Forever Chemicals. The requested funding will help pay for the membrane treatment and concentrate disposal infrastructure that is required to meet existing and emerging water quality standards.
2379.purpose: The elimination of Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and other contaminants from the raw water supply to provide safe drinking water and adequate fire protection.
2379.activities: A new water treatment plant with supporting facilities to provide safe drinking water and adequate fire protection.
2379.direct_services: Contaminant free drinking water and fire protection.
2379.population: The target population is 43,192 customers (2020 population estimate) and this project will also benefit hospitals, public safety facilities, schools, and commercial and industrial users.
2379.outcome: The potable water system will be free of contaminants and will be tested regularly by an accredited testing laboratory.

2365.description: The Connections High School & Vocational Center is purchasing its current building along with the adjacent property. This expansion will double our capacity and is located in the economically disadvantaged central area of Palm Beach County, where the need for vocational training is greatest. This request seeks funds for renovations to transform the facility into a fully equipped vocational center. Renovations will include accessible classrooms, training labs, sensory- friendly workspaces, and adaptive environments tailored to individuals with autism and related disabilities. The center will serve more than 140 individuals annually, with the capacity to expand. By preparing participants with job skills, workplace readiness, and independence training, the project will address the critical gap in employment opportunities for individuals with autism.
2365.purpose: The requested funds will expand service capacity, enhance employment readiness, and promote long-term independence for adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities, with particular focus on individuals with moderate to severe needs and those in underserved communities. Funds will support the renovation and equipping of a facility to enlarge the Adult Vocational Program, ensuring the creation of fully accessible training areas and workspaces dedicated to vocational instruction, employa
2365.activities: The project will renovate and outfit the facility used by the Connections Adult Program, transforming it into an accessible and specialized vocational training environment. With expanded capacity, the program will deliver job skills training, instruction in essential life skills, and guided opportunities for community integration. These activities will directly benefit adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities by strengthening pathways to independence, employability, and community
2365.direct_services: Through the renovated and equipped facility, the Connections Adult Program will deliver daily, hands-on vocational training, job readiness instruction, supported employment opportunities, and comprehensive life-skills education. These direct services will address employment barriers and foster self-sufficiency for adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. The project emphasizes reac
2365.population: Through the renovated and equipped facility, the Connections Adult Program will deliver daily, hands-on vocational training, job readiness instruction, supported employment opportunities, and comprehensive life-skills education. These direct services will address employment barriers and foster self-sufficiency for adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. The project emphasizes reaching individuals with moderate to severe disabilities, increasing access to critical programs that b
2365.outcome: The project will expand access for over 140 adults with moderate to severe autism annually, improving employment outcomes, increasing independence, reducing reliance on public assistance, and strengthening families and communities. It supports state goals of workforce growth and economic diversification by preparing individuals for employment. Outcomes will be measured through enrollment and completion tracking, employment rates, life-skills and workplace readiness assessments, participant feedback, and longitudinal tracking of sustained employment and independence.

2381.description: Funding will go towards revitalizing the community asset in the financially-disadvantaged community and surrounding region with the goal of increasing services provided to residents. Specific upgrades will include a picnic shelter and expansion of the existing restroom facility, parking lot expansion and resurfacing, basketball court resurfacing and covering, walking track resurfacing along with exercise and additional playground.
2381.purpose: Funding will go towards revitalizing the community asset in the financially-disadvantaged community with the goal of increasing services provided to residents. Specific upgrades will include a picnic shelter and expansion of the existing restroom facility, parking lot expansion and resurfacing, basketball court resurfacing and covering, walking track resurfacing along with exercise and additional playground.
2381.activities: Services provided include recreational, educational, and social activities, which will be provided to residents and members of surrounding communities in the region.
2381.direct_services: Athletic events, exercise classes for the community, better public green spaces for residents, and festivals that are attended to by both residents and members of surrounding communities in the region.
2381.population: The City of Mangonia Park residents and members of surrounding communities throughout the county and the region. Over 4,000 people.
2381.outcome: Improved physical and mental health outcomes for residents, additional municipal services provided to citizens, lower crime rates due to more positive and structured activities being offered, as well as more general usage of the Addie Greek Park by Floridians. These outcomes will be measured by surveys, data collection, and other qualitative data markers.

2364.description: Funding will go towards GGI's program that includes mental health services and assessments, which are provided before individuals are admitted into the shelter. The program collaborates with various agencies, including the South Florida Behavioral Health Network and the PBC Health Care District, to expand services and provide the necessary support. Ongoing support from Gulfstream Goodwill post-discharge will ensure access to therapy, medication management, transportation, and insurance.
2364.purpose: Funding will go towards GGI's program that includes mental health services and assessments, which are provided even before individuals are admitted into the shelter. The program collaborates with various agencies, including the South Florida Behavioral Health Network and the Healthcare District, to expand services and provide the necessary support. Ongoing support from Gulfstream, post discharge, will ensure access to therapy, medication management, transportation, and insurance.
2364.activities: Mental health services and assessments to those being processed by GGI as well as their families.
2364.direct_services: Direct services to be provided include therapy, medication management, transportation, and insurance for patients enrolled in the GGI behavioral health service program.
2364.population: Those experiencing homeless and their families. Over 800 individuals are expected to be served.
2364.outcome: Mental health assessments by professionals, eventual housing for those in the program. Recidivism rates and qualitative assessments from professionals such as surveys and interviews.

2363.description: To fund the training component of a comprehensive initiative that will provide credentialed vocational training through Palm Beach State College (PBSC), the Palm Beach County School District, and other partners that can be completed in 13-15 months for 400+ unemployed, underemployed, homeless, or formerly homeless Palm Beach County residents, empowering them to achieve economic self-sufficiency and contribute to local economic growth.
2363.purpose: To fund the training component of a comprehensive initiative that will provide credentialed vocational training for 400+ unemployed, underemployed, homeless, or formerly homeless Palm Beach County residents, empowering them to achieve economic self-sufficiency and contribute to local economic growth.
2363.activities: Launch industry-recognized programs in high-demand sectors (construction, healthcare and technical trades), modeled after CAPB’s proven training model. Provide connection to safe, supportive housing for trainees, removing barriers to attendance and employment. Housing requirement is enrollment and passing grades for participants in a credentialed program.
2363.direct_services: Access to credentialed vocational programs, learning guides, essential trade tools, and technology upgrades to improve access and efficiency in program delivery. Match funding will provide case managers to enroll participants in PBSC or other partner 13-15 month programs and provide a connection to housing, job coach/employment consultants to connect individuals with partner employers, provide res
2363.population: This program targets unemployed, under employed, formerly homeless, currently homeless residents in Palm Beach County. Over 400 individuals are expected to be served.
2363.outcome: Economic mobility- increased wages and economic stability - collection of employment and wage data. Pre and post assessment surveys to assess skills, confidences, employment and increased wages. This survey data will be tracked along with Quality Assurance reviews.

2946.description: Xcel Mentoring Network is establishing the Xcel Headquarters to support and expand its mobile workforce development program. This permanent base will securely house all of our 28-foot mobile training units and equipment, ensuring operational stability and readiness. With this infrastructure, we can scale career expos, technical training, and mentorship beyond Palm Beach County into underserved regions across Florida. The headquarters will serve as a launchpad for statewide impact—preparing youth for meaningful careers and strengthening Florida’s future workforce.
2946.purpose: The funds requested will be used to establish the Xcel Headquarters, a permanent base that secures our mobile training units and equipment, enabling stable operations and future expansion. This infrastructure will allow Xcel Mentoring Network to scale its workforce development program beyond Palm Beach County, delivering career expos, technical training, and mentorship to underserved communities across Florida. The goal is to strengthen the state’s talent pipeline, increase youth employment, and
2946.activities: The funds will support activities and services that expand Xcel Mentoring Network’s mobile workforce development program. These include secure storage and maintenance of mobile training units, hosting career expos and technical training events, and delivering hands-on mentorship to youth across Palm Beach County and beyond. The headquarters will also serve as a hub for industry partnerships, program coordination, and regional outreach, ensuring scalable, high-impact service delivery aligned with
2946.direct_services: The appropriation project will directly provide hands-on workforce development services to Florida citizens through mobile training units housed at the new Xcel Headquarters. These services include trade-focused classes such as electrical, plumbing, HVAC, welding, and carpentry, as well as specialized pathways in architectural design and 107 drone pilot license. Youth will gain access to career ex
2946.population: The target population for this project is youth ages 13 to 25, with a focus on underserved and underrepresented communities across Florida. Through the establishment of the Xcel Headquarters and expansion of our mobile training program, we aim to serve approximately 1,000 youth per county. As the program scales beyond Palm Beach County, this model allows us to reach thousands of young people annually with hands-on training, mentorship, and career readiness services.
2946.outcome: The target audience for this project is youth ages 13 to 25, with a focus on underserved communities across Florida, aiming to serve approximately 1,000 participants per county. The expected outcomes include increased technical skill development, certification attainment, improved access to employment, internships, and continued education in high- demand industries. Outcomes will be measured through enrollment and completion tracking, credentialing data, post- program on career and education pathways, and feedback from partners and participants. Impact reports will consolidate these metrics to evaluate progress and guide future improvement.

2935.description: The University of Florida Diabetes Institute (UFDI) has pioneered studies defining the genetic and risk factors of diabetes and is recognized nationally and internationally for its leadership in diabetes research, prevention, and care. Through a deep understanding of how diabetes develops and changes over time of the disease, the UFDI is advancing research on diabetes progression and prevention while leading innovative clinical trials that translate scientific discoveries into personalized therapies. To extend these efforts statewide and solidify Florida’s position as a global leader in diabetes, the UFDI requires state financial support to establish a patient focused initiative and a novel AI-driven platform that will accelerate the development of new, targeted treatments designed to help the immune system work properly or restore healthy cells.
2935.purpose: This proposal will reinforce the University of Florida as the epicenter for diabetes innovation, combining patient- centered care, advanced data science, and personalized therapeutics to transform outcomes for Floridians. By strengthening clinical capacity, accelerating research discovery, and expanding statewide access to personalized care, UF will drive measurable improvements in health, reduce long-term healthcare costs, and attract new public and private partnerships. In doing so, the State
2935.activities: Certified Diabetes Educators will provide diabetes management education and treatment options. Mental health resources will be made available to patients. An AI-enabled Discovery Platform will be built to to develop targeted, effective, and safer treatments for individuals with diabetes and speed implementation of clinical trials in both T1D prevention and intervention.
2935.direct_services: Certified Diabetes Educators will work with patients and providers to provide diabetes management education and treatment options. Mental health resources developed by diabetes behavioral medicine and psychology specialist will be made widely available. Increased number of clinical trials will be implemented based on scientific findings.
2935.population: Floridians with type 1 diabetes and those at risk. There is an estimated 210,000 individuals in Florida it is estimated that 2-3 times this number are at risk.
2935.outcome: Improved treatment options due to personalized interventions, increased clinical trial options, and data driven simulate therapeutic responses and disease trajectories conducted before clinical application on patients. Reduce diabetes distress in patients, including adults and children, as well as families and caregivers of those living with diabetes. Outcomes will be measured by disease progression, reduced HbA1c levels (a long-term measure of blood glucose control), reduced hospitalizations and emergency department (ED) visits. The number of new treatments and therapies developed from the AI-driven Discovery Platform will be reported.

3095.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3095.description: The Youth Sports Facilities Program supports youth development by hosting sports events that help shape future athletes and community leaders. It is one of the county’s largest youth-focused programs, providing critical support and opportunities for young participants. The proposed restroom facilities will replace temporary portable toilets, offering a cleaner, safer, and more private amenity for program participants and visitors.
3095.purpose: The funds will be used to enhance the comfort, safety, and overall usability of the Gilchrist County Youth Sports Facility through the installation of a permanent restroom facility. This improvement will provide a cleaner, more sanitary environment for youth sporting events held throughout the year. The project supports the county’s commitment to maintaining safe, functional, and accessible public facilities for both residents and visitors.
3095.activities: The project will include male and female restrooms along with changing tables. Activities include procurement of materials, engineer, contractor, and inspection to ensure compliance with safety and building standards.
3095.direct_services: The project will provide a safer, more comfortable public facility for citizens attending youth sporting events.
3095.population: The project will serve Gilchrist County residents, visitors, youth organization and event participants. The youth sporting events hosts an estimated 20,000-25,000 individuals annually, all of whom will benefit from the improvements.
3095.outcome: The expected outcome is improved comfort, safety, and increased usage of the facility throughout the year. Success will be measured by: An increase in events and attendance after installation. Positive feedback from community groups and event organizers.

3083.description: Services will be provided to youth ages 3-5 years old who are enrolled in Head Start and public school VPK programs. Students will receive mental health screening, assessment, treatment planning, mental health services, classroom supportive care, training to faculty in the area of infant mental health, wellness screenings and referrals, family therapy, and screenings for development disorders. Understanding early childhood mental health is essential for creating inclusive programs, as it supports the emotional, social, and cognitive development of young children. This awareness enables early identification of potential challenges, ensures timely support, and fosters nurturing environments where all children can thrive. By prioritizing mental health, programs can promote positive relationships, reduce stress, and help children build the lifelong skills they need for success by building ke
3083.purpose: This funds requested will expand mental health therapy, behavioral intervention, and early learning support for preschoolers in Head Start and VPK programs, improving school readiness and reducing behavioral incidents across St. Johns and Clay Counties. Early intervention saves long-term costs by reducing later behavioral crises, special education referrals, and juvenile justice involvement. This program delivers high impact, low-cost services that stabilize families.
3083.activities: Therapists will provide individual, group, and family therapy as well as provide supportive care to their assigned Head Start class/center/VPK classroom. Each youth will receive an evaluation, assessment, treatment planning, mental health therapy and psychiatric services, health and wellness screening and referrals, and training to children and families.
3083.direct_services: Services will be provided to youth ages 3-5 years old who are enrolled in Head Start and public school VPK programs. Students will receive mental health screening, assessment, treatment planning, mental health services, classroom supportive care, training to faculty in the area of infant mental health, wellness screenings and referrals, family therapy, and screenings for development disorders.
3083.population: This project will serve youth ages 3 to 5 who are enrolled in Head Start and public school VPK programs across St. Johns and Clay Counties. The target population includes children experiencing poor mental health, developmental delays, behavioral challenges in the classroom, and those who are economically disadvantaged or otherwise at risk. Because these challenges often extend beyond the child, the program also supports families and classroom faculty by providing training, screenings, and interv
3083.outcome: This project will improve physical and mental health for preschoolers by providing screenings, therapy, and early intervention services. Physical health outcomes will be measured through family follow-through on medical and dental appointments and children’s progress on developmental milestones. Mental health outcomes will be measured by attendance at therapy sessions, reduced behavioral incidents, improved Personal Well-Being Index scores, and regular review of individualized treatment plans. The project will also enhance classroom quality by reducing disruptive behaviors and strengthening school readiness. Teacher reports, disciplinary data, and classroom attendance will be used to measure

3032.description: ECS4Kids will grow our Summer Bridge program in Clay and Duval, and expand it into Baker County. Growing the Summer Bridge program in these three counties will provide an additional 7 weeks of early learning services to 200 of the counties' most vulnerable children, ages 3-5. Children enrolled in the Summer Bridge program are immersed in learning-rich environments with individualized instruction to increase developmental gains and prepare them for kindergarten. Parents benefit from no-cost summer childcare to support their continuous employment and family stability, whereas educators benefit from 7 additional weeks of pay.
3032.purpose: The funds will support ECS4Kids’ Head Start Summer Bridge program for North Florida, providing 200 at-risk preschoolers in Baker, Clay, and Duval counties with 7 extra weeks of learning resulting in demonstrable learning gains in literacy, math, and physical skills, improving their ability to succeed in kindergarten. Parents benefit from summer childcare to support their employment and family stability while educators receive 7 weeks of additional pay, improving teacher pay and staff retention.
3032.activities: Preschoolers will receive individualized instruction in literacy, math, and physical development delivered by highly qualified teachers in stimulating indoor and outdoor settings. Children will have two nutritious meals plus a snack daily. Learning will extend beyond the school day with at-home learning supported by our Hatch learning platform, books, and activities. Parents will benefit from childcare for the full school day with no-cost before and after school options to support employment.
3032.direct_services: 200 children will increase their school readiness with 7 weeks of enriched education aligned with Florida’s Birth to Five standards, using both in school and at home learning to directly address summer learning losses. Nutritious meals are provided to combat summer food insecurity. Low-income parents will receive no-cost full day extended childcare to support employment. Teachers will receive addi
3032.population: Summer Bridge will serve 200 of the counties' most vulnerable children, ages 3-5, and their families. All of the children in the program live in poverty. Many of our children also have developmental disabilities, live in single parent households, or have other adverse childhood experiences (ACES).
3032.outcome: This project will enhance school readiness in our youngest learners, with demonstrable results in literacy math and physical skills, preparing them for academic success. Academic success is directly correlated to reduced rates of juvenile justice involvement. School readiness is measured by increased scores in literacy, math and physical domains utilizing pre-and-post scores on the Hatch learning platform. Families also benefit from increased workforce participation, access to education, and/or job training, driving local economic growth. Teachers benefit from 7 additional weeks of income.

2840.description: The Children’s Initiative provides trauma-informed pediatric and family services that close the gap between insurance reimbursements and the true cost of care. The program integrates medical visits, behavioral therapy, developmental screenings, care coordination, parent support, and crisis intervention for at-risk children across Northeast Florida. Children receive evaluations, therapy, follow-up care, and referrals, while families receive resource navigation, case management, and support for housing, and early intervention. The Initiative also offers school and community outreach to identify concerns early and stabilize families. State funds will sustain essential services—including therapists, care coordinators, supplies, and travel—that ensure timely mental health care, improved well-child visits, reduced crises, and stronger family functioning for more than 800 children and caregiver
2840.purpose: The requested funds will close the gap between insurance reimbursements and the actual cost of providing trauma- informed pediatric, behavioral health, and family stabilization services. The goal is to expand access to therapy, developmental screenings, care coordination, and crisis support for at-risk children and families, ensuring timely intervention and preventing escalation of behavioral, developmental, or social concerns.
2840.activities: Funds will support trauma-informed therapy, developmental and behavioral assessments, medical follow-up coordination, parent support, crisis intervention, school and community outreach, resource navigation, and case management. Services include licensed therapeutic care, care coordination, home/school visits, family support supplies, and outcome evaluation.
2840.direct_services: Children will receive therapy, developmental screenings, behavioral health assessments, medical follow-up coordination, and referrals to specialty providers. Families will receive case management, housing and support, crisis intervention, and linkage to community and early-intervention resources. Outreach and care navigation will be provided both onsite and in school/community settings.
2840.population: The Initiative primarily serves economically disadvantaged children, youth with behavioral or developmental needs, victims of trauma, and families facing instability across Duval, Clay, Nassau, and St. Johns Counties. More than 800 children and caregivers are expected to be served annually.
2840.outcome: Expected outcomes include: Improved mental health with a reduction in behavioral crises Increased well-child and follow-up visits Earlier identification of developmental and behavioral concerns Improved school attendance and academic stability Greater family stability through coordinated case management Reduced emergency utilization related to unmet behavioral health needs Measurement methods: Pre/post assessments, EMR data, attendance and screening records, provider reporting, case management documentation, satisfaction surveys, and outcome tracking dashboards.

2718.description: Funds will be utilized to continue services to reduce suicide deaths and attempts by providing same-day access to outpatient mental health services for teens, adults, and veteran/military/first responder at high risk for suicide and family members concerned about the safety of a loved one. Same day services include crisis support, mental health recovery peer support, and outpatient therapy funded by Here Tomorrow. Outpatient therapy is provided within one to two days with an option for virtual or in-person therapy with a State of FL licensed therapist. The program is designed to engage people who are at high-risk for suicide and have not yet decided to seek professional help. Since mental health conditions are typically chronic and require management over time, our program involves staying connected with the service recipients and families over the course of an entire year.
2718.purpose: Funds will expand mental health services across Northeast Florida, embed peers in hospital psychiatric units, and receive 988 warm handoffs. This growth will further reduce suicide deaths and attempts among teens, adults, and military/first responders—data show our peer-based model saves lives. By offering same-day outpatient access for individuals in crisis and concerned family members, Here Tomorrow fills a critical gap where no such immediate help currently exists.
2718.activities: Here Tomorrow provides same-day crisis support 365 days a year through certified peer specialists and licensed therapists. Outpatient therapy is offered within 1–2 days, in person or virtual. Our no-cost, no-wait program includes a full year of peer support. Peers in psychiatric units educate and enroll patients into our 365-day model, cutting readmissions by half since 2023. 988 warm-transfers callers to us for ongoing support.
2718.direct_services: Here Tomorrow addresses the top shared priority across all five NE Florida counties: lack of access to mental health care. Through an innovative non-clinical model, peer sessions support individuals in crisis. We serve diverse communities across Jacksonville, the Beaches, Middleburg, and St. Augustine, and offer no-cost suicide prevention services to all Florida residents 365 days a year. Median h
2718.population: The target population served by this project is adults, teens, and veterans/military/first responders in our community who are experiencing hopelessness and are at risk for suicide. In addition, family members in our community who are worried about the safety of a loved one in a mental health crisis or who may be at high risk of suicide are also served. Since opening in 2021, we expect to serve over 3,000 people by the end of the 2026-2027 Fiscal Year.
2718.outcome: Outcomes measured: • Completion rate of those enrolled in services • % reporting improved quality of life • Readmission rate of service recipients vs. total Baptist Health psychiatric admissions

2719.description: A). advancing entrepreneur education in high school/college programming testing w/existing businesses B). capacity building to increase taxable sales revenue and increase utilization of local vendors. 3 components to the program: (1) technology leading entrepreneur education to prepare business owners, (2) advancing entrepreneurial education in rural communities, and (3) assist entrepreneurs in leveraging artificial intelligence for business growth.
2719.purpose: A). advancing entrepreneur education in high school/college programming testing w/existing businesses B). capacity building to increase taxable sales revenue and increase utilization of local vendors. 3 components to the program: (1) technology leading entrepreneur education to prepare business owners, (2) advancing entrepreneurial education in rural communities, and (3) assist entrepreneurs in leveraging artificial intelligence for business growth.
2719.activities: Apply remote work and established AI strategies to assist small businesses; Management and practice of remote customer service by electronic or other means; Any other relevant business practices as companies evolve to a hybrid workplace model; Online/in-person training registrations, simulation event completions and customer development plans. Applying agentic AI teams to upskill participants and employees of non-entrepreneur organizations which allows us to scale support.
2719.direct_services: Entrepreneur education and simulation activities toward business growth. Online/In person training registrations, simulation event completions, customer development plans, and business model validation submissions.
