Pitch contest with opportunities, Supplier/vendor contract opportunity, Access to capital showcase (loan applications, pitches, and loans) to grow small business activity. Asset buildin
2719.population: The target population served by this project are aspiring entrepreneurs in rural and urban areas, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, University/College students, and currently or formerly incarcerated persons. We average over 300 applications per cohort every six months.
2719.outcome: Assessments and proven learning strategies. Cohort programming has been best way to scale small business participation. Pitch opportunities with suppliers. The vertical integration of AI allows a State-Compute-Prescribe model to accelerate education, formation, strategy, planning, and commerce opportunities.

3324.description: The number of septic tanks in the city has been reduced since 2000 from 400 to about 46, including about 33 in the Marshside area, a low-lying area subject to coastal flooding. The goal is to eliminate those septic tanks and connect the homeowners to central sewer services. This will help protect the salt marsh ecosystem and surface waters from nutrients and bacteria leaching from septic tanks by providing a resilient, dependable means of sewage disposal.
3324.purpose: The number of septic tanks in the city has been reduced since 2000 from 400 to about 46, including about 33 in the Marshside area, a low-lying area subject to coastal flooding. The goal is to eliminate those septic tanks and connect the homeowners to central sewer services. This will help protect the salt marsh ecosystem and surface waters from nutrients and bacteria leaching from septic tanks by providing a resilient, dependable means of sewage disposal.
3324.activities: - Planning, permitting, design and engineering - Construction of sewer line extensions - Septic tank abandonment and connection to the municipal sewer system - Backfilling and restoration
3324.direct_services: - Resilient and reliable sewer service capable of accommodating routine flooding conditions - Elimination of failed septic tanks contaminating area surface waters - Protection of public health from bacteriological contamination - Increased property value - Improved water quality
3324.population: The population of Atlantic Beach will be served by the project through the protection of our natural waterways from contamination. An estimated 75 specific residents will be moved from septic systems given the 33 residences with septic tanks in the Marshside area, which is prone to coastal flooding.
3324.outcome: Septic systems can release pollutants into the groundwater and adjacent surface waters if they are not properly maintained or if they fail. Sewer systems collect and treat wastewater in a centralized facility, which reduces the risk of environmental contamination. Water quality will be tested for contamination and be compared to historical data.

2707.description: The upper end of the Hopkins Creek drainage basin is essentially landlocked and during severe storm events area homes can flood and roadways become impassable. This project entails construction of an offline stormwater mitigation pond on 2 acres of City-owned property in this drainage basin providing for stormwater storage and water quality treatment.
2707.purpose: Construct a stormwater mitigation pond that will provide protection to 92 structures from a 25-year storm event as well as provide drainage improvements during a mean annual and 10-year storm event. The pond will also provide for water quality benefits.
2707.activities: - Clearing of City-owned land - Construction of a stormwater mitigation pond - Development of the area not used for the pond as a passive park - Backfilling and restoration
2707.direct_services: - Protection from severe rainfall events - Resilient and robust stormwater management system capable of accommodating routine flooding conditions - Increased property value - Improved water quality
2707.population: The population of Atlantic Beach will be served by the project through area streets remaining passable during severe storm events. An estimated 210 specific residents live in structures that will be protected from flooding by this project.
2707.outcome: Protection of 92 structures from a 25-year storm event as well as significant drainage improvements during a mean annual and 10-year storm event. The pond will also provide for water quality benefits. The reduction in flood height and duration attributable to this project will be measured after severe storm events. Water quality will be tested for nutrient and fecal coliform reduction and be compared to historical data.

2709.description: This project consists of approximately 2,900 feet of an 8 foot wide concrete multi-use trail on Sailfish Drive between Atlantic Boulevard and Plaza that will connect an existing multiuse trail to local businesses.
2709.purpose: The goal of this project is to connect an existing multiuse trail to local businesses and provide improved pedestrian and bicycle safety.
2709.activities: Construction of an 8 foot wide multiuse path on Sailfish Drive connecting local businesses on Atlantic Boulevard to an existing multiuse trail on Plaza.
2709.direct_services: Safe and convenient connectivity for pedestrians and cyclists between an existing multiuse trail and local businesses.
2709.population: The overall target population is the general population, but geared toward children. Several thousand citizens living in the vicinity of this project will be served by this trail.
2709.outcome: Protect the general public, and especially children, from harm by creating safe protected multiuse trail. Improve physical health of citizens by encouraging more walking and cycling. Usage monitoring and accident statistics will be utilized to measure outcomes.

2303.description: The requested funds will be used to expand the successful One Water Florida campaign, which is a statewide education program to help educate the public regarding potable reuse and how it can help Florida meet future water demands as an alternative water supply. The One Water Florida campaign is being followed by many Florida Utilities, and additional education will help Florida Citizens understand the importance of recycled water and integrated water management in this One Water movement. The sum of $500,000 shall be appropriated for the fiscal year 2026-2027, to the Southwest Florida Water Management District through the Department of Environmental Protection for projects dedicated to the implementation of and the public education regarding direct and indirect potable reuse (“recycled water”) throughout the State of Florida, which shall be developed cooperatively with WateReuse Florida.
2303.purpose: Only half of the available reclaimed water in Florida is being beneficially reused by utilities. By educating the public that potable reuse is safe and protective of the environment, utilities may be able to implement potable reuse and avoid wasteful discharge of reclaimed water as it will become a source for potable water supply. Also, by creating new supply, there may be less reliance on traditional groundwater and surface water supplies, which provides benefits to the environment. The benefic
2303.activities: The first phase of this campaign included a successful statewide survey to understand the current view of potable reuse in Florida. From the baseline survey, an education campaign associated with potable reuse was developed and implemented via social media platforms, a State website, and video clips. Information developed included a fact sheet; media op-eds; speaking points to share with the public and elected officials; graphical messages for use in print and public media; two information video
2303.direct_services: As this request is for the implementation of a statewide education campaign, there are no direct services being provided to citizens by the appropriation project.
2303.population: The target population is the citizens of the State of Florida with the message being developed based on the results of the baseline study. As this is an education campaign, there are no individuals that are expected to be served.
2303.outcome: By educating the public that potable reuse is safe and protective of the environment, utilities can develop projects that better utilize their wastewater and expand the water pie, thus potentially decreasing future water wars between utilities, as well as utilities and other water users, due to a deficit of traditional groundwater and surface water supplies. Besides ensuring that the activities are completed (fact sheet and messaging developed, purchase of media, etc.), a method to determine the success of the education campaign may be the increase in beneficial use of their reclaimed water by utilities. The success of the education program may also be measured by the number of potable reuse

2305.description: Sharks off the coast of Florida can take or damage fish during catch (referred to as “depredation”). This is a growing problem for recreational fishermen and tourism revenues with some affected stakeholders suggesting there is a shark overpopulation when the issue is more likely related to a learned shark behavior and increased media attention. This project will implement electromagnetic tools to greatly reduce this behavior without impacting the gamefish or sharks.
2305.purpose: Sharks off the coast of Florida can take or damage fish during catch (referred to as “depredation”). This is a growing problem for recreational fishermen and tourism revenues with some affected stakeholders suggesting there is a shark overpopulation when the issue is more likely related to a learned shark behavior and increased media attention. This project will implement electromagnetic tools to greatly reduce this behavior without impacting the gamefish or sharks.
2305.activities: Mote researchers will engage with the recreational & commercial fisheries sectors throughout the state to socialize the benefits of depredation deterrent devices. This effort will protect Florida shark populations and the economic benefits of recreational and commercial fishing.
2305.direct_services: Mote will work closely with the recreational and commercial fishing industry to introduce depredation deterrent devices while collecting important scientific shark population information. This will provide targeted shark species protections while allowing normal fishing activities.
2305.population: Recreational and Commercial fishing industry and related tourism operations (e.g. hotels, restaurants). Estimated to be more than 1,000 individuals positively impacted.
2305.outcome: Researchers will engage with the recreational/commercial fisheries sector throughout the state to socialize the benefits of depredation deterrent devices. This effort will protect Florida shark populations and the economic benefits of recreational and commercial fishing. The methodology will be determined by the number of events conducted via a FWC grant agreement.

2306.description: The funds being requested will be used to expand and deliver the Associate in Science Degree in Artificial Intelligence. In order to reach this goal, the program will need new classroom resources and technology that will provide a leading edge educational experience and provide up to date instruction. In addition to the physical lab enhancements, the funds will be used to train and develop learning activities.
2306.purpose: The funds being requested will be used to expand and deliver the Associate in Science Degree in Artificial Intelligence. In order to reach this goal, the program will need new classroom resources and technology that will provide a leading edge educational experience and provide up to date instruction. In addition to the physical lab enhancements, the funds will be used to train and develop learning activities.
2306.activities: Citizens will receive high quality instruction from faculty and facilitators at Hillsborough College, in an emerging field of study. Students will learn about the use of artificial intelligence in business and prepare to become IT or business employees.
2306.direct_services: Citizens will be able to study artificial intelligence and specialize their technology based career on this area of growth. These courses will be available virtually as well as on campus, to citizens who wish to earn a degree or certification in these fields.
2306.population: College age and older individuals who have an interest in this career path. The program will serve over 800 students.
2306.outcome: Measuring student enrollment and retention in these fields. Using HC enterprise software to investigate job opportunities and salaries.

2309.description: Establish a Workforce Education Center (WEC) to provide education and economic development opportunities for Eastern Hillsborough Co. The facility will mediate critical instructional space shortages and function as a comprehensive training center for high wage careers in the healthcare, business, and technology fields.
2309.purpose: Establish a Workforce Education Center (WEC) to provide education and economic development opportunities for Eastern Hills. Co. The facility will mediate critical instructional space shortages and function as a comprehensive training center for high wage careers in the healthcare, business, and technology fields.
2309.activities: The center will provide workforce training and job placement services for high wage occupations, as well as a space for large-scale training and professional development opportunities for local industry. The center will offer a full scope of student services, including advising, financial aid, veterans' services, counseling and career resource.
2309.direct_services: The center will be a multi-function, multi-use space for instruction, workforce training, local stakeholder development, and community events and programming. The center will also serve as a hub for high-value, non-profit agencies to increase public access to services like job placement, food and nutrition support, and childcare.
2309.population: Elderly persons, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at risk youth, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, veterans, grade school students, high school students, university/college students, currently or formerly incarcerated persons.
2309.outcome: The center will be a multi-function, multi-use space for instruction, workforce training, local stakeholder development, and community events and programming. The center will also serve as a hub for high-value, non-profit agencies to increase public access to services like job placement, food and nutrition support, and childcare. This will be measured by usage rates and enrollment.

2334.description: Solo Parent is a 501c3 committed to making a transformational difference in the lives of single parent so they can raise healthy, well-equipped kids. Solo Parent empowers single parents by unlocking their emotional, spiritual, and physical potential. Through their tailored programs and nurturing community, they address and embrace their unique needs and challenges, transforming adversity into strength – guiding families and their children on a path toward healing and sustained success. The funds will go towards tailored programs, educational materials, and free resources to help single parents go from surviving to thriving, ultimately setting them and their families on a path to success.
2334.purpose: To make a transformational difference in the lives of single parents so they can raise healthy, well-equipped children. They will empower, support, and give community to the lives of single parents residing in Florida, including, but not limited to, veterans, members of the FL National Guard; law enforcement officers; first responders; and individuals in high- stress occupations. The funds will go towards tailored programs, educational materials, and free resources to help single parents go from
2334.activities: Online Intensives - to provide education and tools to navigate the challenges single parents face Weekly Support Groups - to provide a supportive community for single parents to share experiences, gain emotional support, and develop a sense of belonging. Coaching- to provide personalized guidance to single parents. Digital Resource Library- access to content, articles, webinars, and courses.
2334.direct_services: Provide single parents in high stress careers and throughout Florida with resources that focus on their physical, emotional and spiritual needs, as well as, connect them to one another in authentic support communities.
2334.population: Single parent veterans, members of the FL Army National Guard or Air National Guard; law enforcement officers; first responders; individuals in other high- stress occupations; single parents who are employed by the state of FL and/or referred by their employer, a non-profit, or a church. Target population- over 800 single parents in Florida.
2334.outcome: Improve the well-being of single parents in high stress careers and throughout Florida with resources and community so they can excel at the dual demands of solo parenthood and service/career. This will be measured by surveying participants. 95% of participants who have utilized the Solo Parent Program report feeling more empowered and less isolated, and 100% of families who utilize the program report no incidents of suicide, substance abuse, or incarceration.

2712.description: Vision Is Priceless will bring essential vision healthcare services—including vision screenings, comprehensive eye exams, and prescription glasses—to children in Northeast Florida through our Sight in Schools Children’s Vision Program. The overarching goal of our Sight in Schools Program is to eliminate treatable vision problems for students so they can have a better chance at success at school, and in life. Additionally, our school-based vision program helps ensure that all students, regardless of socioeconomic status, have access to vision care—a vital component of primary healthcare. This reduces disparities in academic performance and overall health outcomes, which can amplify long- lasting change in the community.
2712.purpose: The Sight in Schools Children’s Vision Program brings vital vision healthcare services—including vision screenings, comprehensive eye exams, and prescription glasses—to children in Northeast FL. We work to eliminate treatable vision problems for students in Title 1 schools so they can have a better chance at success in school, and in life. Good vision is vital for academic, social, and emotional development. Untreated vision issues hinder learning and make navigating daily tasks challenging.
2712.activities: Our objectives for the Sight in Schools Program during the 2026-2027 year are to: • Conduct 35,000 vision screenings for children, enabling the early detection of eye diseases and vision issues. • Provide 3,000 comprehensive eye exams for K-12 students in Northeast Florida, with the goal of eliminating treatable vision problems.
2712.direct_services: Over 35,000 children will receive vision screenings, which are vital for the early detection of vision issues and eye diseases. Through our Sight in Schools Mobile Vision Program, our licensed optometrist provides comprehensive eye exams directly on school campuses using our Mobile Vision Clinic. We target low-income K-12 students, with a focus on Duval and Clay counties, who otherwise go without
2712.population: For our school-based eye exams, we focus on low-income K-12 students in Northeast Florida public schools (with a focus on Duval and Clay counties), who are at greater risk of missing out on essential eye care. Our target population for vision screenings includes children aged 3 to 18 in Northeast Florida (Duval, Baker, Clay, Nassau, and St. Johns counties). Annually, we provide screenings to over 35,000 children across the First Coast in preschools, child development centers, and private, and in
2712.outcome: Addressing vision issues removes barriers to academic success, enabling students to reach their full potential and improving the effectiveness of efforts to boost grade-level reading proficiency. Higher academic achievement in school often leads to pursuing higher education, access to a wider range of career opportunities, and ultimately improving long-term health and socioeconomic prospects. We measure program impact by tracking screenings, results, follow- ups, eye exams, glasses prescribed, referrals, and clinics held, along with demographic data to target under served areas. Weekly reports monitor progress. Surveys conducted 90 days post-clinics and feedback from students and staff asses

2711.description: Extension of Town of Callahan water lines to Northeast Florida Fair grounds, providing municipal potable water, and protecting public health. Installation of potable water to fair site, additionally benefiting the University of Florida Agriculture Extension building and the Nassau County school board maintenance building.
2711.purpose: Potable water supply to a currently under-served area. Reliable and clean drinking water for the overall benefit of public health. All while providing water to a site than can be used for economic development.
2711.activities: Construction of water lines to service a currently under-served area of Nassau County
2711.direct_services: Clean, safe, municipal potable water supply to an area that is currently not serviced.
2711.population: Residents of Nassau County and surrounding areas. Thousands of residents in the immediate service area.
2711.outcome: Enhancement of fair grounds site for future economic development to be tracked in future years. County wide benefit of clean and safe water supply. Water usage data to track measurables.

2423.description: ECS4Kids will grow our Summer Bridge program in Alachua, and expand it into Marion and Lake counties. Growing the Summer Bridge program will provide an additional 7 weeks of early learning services to 300 of the counties' most vulnerable children, ages 3-5. Children enrolled in the Summer Bridge program are immersed in learning-rich environments with individualized instruction to increase developmental gains and prepare them for kindergarten. Parents benefit from no-cost summer childcare to support their continuous employment and family stability, whereas educators benefit from 7 additional weeks of pay.
2423.purpose: The funds will support ECS4Kids’ Head Start Summer Bridge program for Central Florida, providing 300 at-risk preschoolers in Alachua, Lake, and Marion counties with 7 extra weeks of learning resulting in demonstrable learning gains in literacy, math, and physical skills, improving their ability to succeed in kindergarten. Parents benefit from summer childcare to support their employment and family stability while educators receive 7 weeks of additional pay, improving teacher pay and staff retent
2423.activities: Preschoolers will receive individualized instruction in literacy, math, and physical development delivered by highly qualified teachers in stimulating indoor and outdoor settings. Children will have two nutritious meals plus a snack daily. Learning will extend beyond the school day with at-home learning supported by our Hatch learning platform, books, and activities. Parents will benefit from childcare for the full school day with no-cost before and after school options to support employment.
2423.direct_services: 300 children will increase their school readiness with 7 weeks of enriched education aligned with Florida’s Birth to Five standards, using both in school and at home learning to directly address summer learning losses. Nutritious meals are provided to combat summer food insecurity. Low-income parents will receive no-cost full day extended childcare to support employment. Teachers will receive addi
2423.population: Summer Bridge will serve 300 of the counties' most vulnerable children, ages 3-5, and their families. All of the children in the program live in poverty. Many of our children also have developmental disabilities, live in single parent households, or experience other adverse childhood experiences (ACES).
2423.outcome: This project will enhance school readiness in our youngest learners, with demonstrable results in literacy math and physical skills, preparing them for academic success. Academic success is directly correlated to reduced rates of juvenile justice involvement. School readiness is measured by increased scores in literacy, math and physical domains utilizing pre-and-post scores on the Hatch learning platform. Families also benefit from increased workforce participation, access to education, and/or job training, driving local economic growth. Teachers benefit from 7 additional weeks of income.

3409.description: The Construction Inspection Training Program is designed to prepare participants with the technical knowledge, regulatory understanding, and practical skills required to effectively inspect construction projects in compliance with state and local building codes. The program provides comprehensive instruction in construction methods, materials, safety standards, plan reading, quality control, and documentation procedures, with an emphasis on real-world applications. Through classroom instruction and hands-on training, participants learn to identify code violations and ensure workmanship meets approved specifications.
3409.purpose: The funds received for the Construction Inspection Training Program will be utilized to enhance workforce skills, foster economic development, and ensure the quality and safety of construction projects. The primary purpose of this program is to provide comprehensive, hands-on training to individuals aspiring to become certified construction inspectors, equipping them with the technical expertise, regulatory knowledge, and practical experience necessary to excel in the field.
3409.activities: The Construction Inspection Training Program will provide structured classroom instruction in construction codes, safety standards, inspection techniques, and regulatory compliance, combined with certification exam preparation and supervised field-based training. Participants will receive hands-on experience conducting inspections, reviewing plans, and preparing reports, ensuring they develop practical, job-ready skills aligned with industry and regulatory requirements.
3409.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services to citizens by increasing access to qualified construction inspectors who help ensure buildings are safe, code-compliant, and constructed to approved standards. Through improved inspection capacity, residents will benefit from safer homes and commercial spaces, reduced construction defects, faster inspection turnaround times, and greater prote
3409.population: The target population for this project includes 25–50 individuals seeking industry-recognized training to enter or advance in the construction inspection field, including those pursuing new career opportunities, professional skill enhancement, or certification required for employment. Participation will be open to all eligible applicants based on objective criteria such as interest in construction inspection, baseline qualifications, and commitment to completing the program.
3409.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is the development of a skilled pipeline of qualified construction inspectors capable of ensuring code compliance, improving construction quality, and enhancing public safety across residential and commercial projects. Success will be measured through participant completion and certification rates, pre- and post-training competency assessments, job placement or advancement outcomes, and feedback from employers and regulatory agencies regarding inspector performance and inspection accuracy.

2425.description: Pace Center for Girls in Lee County provides academics, counseling, and therapy to at risk girls in middle school and high school. The project will allow Pace to upgrade and remodel our current facility which will increase capacity and allow us to provide the environment needed for education and healing. Upgrades will be focused on enhancing safety, security, health and wellness in the school and therapy programs.
2425.purpose: Requested funds will be used for capital improvements to enhance the safety and security of our aging school facilities and improve the health & wellness of the students we serve. Pace purchased and remodeled our current building in 2013 with the help of a robust capital campaign. Since then, we have invested tens of thousands of dollars in additional repairs, upgrades, and remodels to expand our capacity and continue meeting the growing need for mental health and academic services for girls in
2425.activities: Requested funds will be used for capital improvements to address lingering damage from Hurricane Ian and enhance the safety and security of our aging school facilities. Activities include construction and building upgrades to improve the security of the learning environment for our girls, replacing HVAC clean air intake units, installing an outdoor recreation space, and expanding dedicated space for our Reach therapy program to serve more girls.
2425.direct_services: Funding will support direct services to at-risk girls ages 11-17, who are facing challenges such as academic failure, family instability, or victimization, by providing a safe and secure facility to continue offering an evidence-based model of services that integrates education, counseling, life skills training, and advocacy to help girls achieve academic success and well-being.
2425.population: Each year, Pace serves approximately 150 middle and high school girls, ages 11-17, who reside in Lee County. Students exhibit a minimum of three of the seventeen risk factors identified by the Department of Juvenile Justice which may include academic failure, truancy, and family instability. Other risk factors include physical, emotional or sexual abuse, neglect, mental health disorders, early sexual activity, and prior arrest history.
2425.outcome: This project will enable us to sustain and increase the capacity of our existing programs that provide critical mental health services, academic support, and substance abuse intervention resources that help girls to increase their resiliency and develop the skills to lead productive and engaged lives in the community. Success will be measured by the completion of the proposed projects which will result in enhanced safety and security measures and improved health & wellness at our facility.

2434.description: The Cape Coral Evacuation Route Improvements - NE 24th Avenue project will widen and extend about 2.75 miles of road from State Road 78 to Del Prado Boulevard North, creating a key four-lane evacuation route. With new roundabouts, sidewalks, paths, and lighting, it’s designed to reduce congestion and enhance safety—providing an additional essential, evacuation route corridor for residents during hurricanes while supporting Cape Coral’s rapid growth.
2434.purpose: The Cape Coral Evacuation Route Improvements - NE 24th Ave Project will widen and extend about 2.75 miles of road from State Road 78 to Del Prado Boulevard North, creating a key four-lane evacuation route. With new roundabouts, sidewalks, paths, and lighting, it’s designed to reduce congestion and enhance safety—providing an additional essential, evacuation route corridor for residents during hurricanes while supporting Cape Coral’s rapid growth.
2434.activities: The Cape Coral Evacuation Route Improvements - NE 24th Ave Project will use project funds to widen and upgrade 2.75 miles of road, optimize intersections, and add sidewalks and bike lanes—creating a vital new hurricane evacuation route. This will enhance traffic flow, safety, and connectivity, helping protect Cape Coral residents and improve transportation for all users.
2434.direct_services: Cape Coral Evacuation Route Improvements - NE 24th Ave Project will provide Cape Coral and Lee County citizens with safer, faster, and more reliable travel by creating a new four-lane evacuation route along the NE border. Residents will benefit from reduced congestion, safer intersections with roundabouts, and enhanced walking and biking options, improving daily mobility and emergency readiness.
2434.population: The project will serve Cape Coral and North Fort Myers residents. Thousands of Lee County residents will be served by the project.
2434.outcome: Cape Coral Evacuation Route Improvements - NE 24th Ave Project will widen and extend about 2.75 miles of road from State Road 78 to Del Prado Blvd N, creating a key four-lane evacuation route. With new roundabouts, sidewalks, paths, and lighting, it’s designed to reduce congestion and enhance safety—providing an essential, escape corridor for residents during hurricanes while supporting Cape Coral’s rapid growth. These benefits can be measured by tracking reductions in traffic accidents and injuries, analyzing changes in traffic flow and congestion, monitoring usage of new pedestrian and bike facilities, collecting community safety feedback, and comparing public safety data before and after

2435.description: This project will construct a new YMCA at Babcock Ranch to provide early learning, youth development, sports, wellness, preventive health programs, swim lessons, and community gathering space for one of Florida’s fastest-growing communities. The facility will support working families, promote healthy living, and strengthen community connections through accessible programs for all ages.
2435.purpose: The funds will support construction of a new YMCA at Babcock Ranch to expand access to youth, family, and community programs. The project will improve health, education, and quality of life by providing childcare, youth development, swim lessons, wellness programs, and community services to meet the growing needs of Babcock Ranch residents.
2435.activities: Activities and services will include youth development programs, early learning and childcare, family and senior programs, health and wellness classes, aquatics and swim lessons, community outreach, and recreational programming. The facility will provide accessible space for residents to engage in healthy living, social responsibility, and programs that support strong families.
2435.direct_services: Direct services will include affordable childcare and early learning; youth development programs; sports and recreation activities; swim lessons and aquatics safety; health and wellness classes; senior and family programs; and community outreach services. The YMCA will provide year-round programs that support healthy living, youth development, and community engagement for Babcock Ranch residents.
2435.population: The project will serve children, families, and seniors living in Babcock Ranch and surrounding areas. The YMCA is expected to serve more than 5,000 residents annually through childcare and early learning, youth development, sports and recreation, swim lessons, health and wellness programs, and community services.
2435.outcome: The project is expected to improve health, education, and quality of life for Babcock Ranch residents by expanding access to childcare, youth development, sports and recreation, swim lessons, and wellness programs. Outcomes will be measured through program enrollment, participation rates, swim-lesson completions, childcare capacity utilization, health and wellness assessments, and annual community impact reports.

2436.description: The purpose of the program is to facilitate the operation of a statewide telecare support network that provides community outreach, consultations, and care coordination for women who are challenged with unexpected pregnancies. The program shall: (a) encourage healthy childbirth; (b) support childbirth as an alternative to abortion; (c) promote family formation;
2436.purpose: The program shall provide direct services, supports, social services case management, and referrals to biological parents of unborn children and biological or adoptive parents of children under the age of two years.
2436.activities: 1. Nurse counseling 2. Care plan coordination 3. Connection to state and local services 4. Connection to local pregnancy resource centers 5. Access to licensed social workers 6. Delivery of program virtually.
2436.direct_services: (a) Development of a care plan, resources, and supports for program participants to address identified needs. (b) Referrals to appropriate local resources including, without limitation, state and federal benefits programs and local charitable organizations. (c) Assistance in applying for state and federal benefits programs. (d) Assistance in accomplishing elements of the care plan.
2436.population: 1. Parents of unborn children 2. Adoptive parents with children under the age of 2 3. Parents with children under the age of 2 Expected indivuals served 2,667
2436.outcome: 1. Women choosing to move forward with their pregnancy 2. Healthy pregnancy outcomes..babies born +5.5 lbs, moms giving birth after 37 weeks, moms getting post partum care, moms connected to ob-gyn care un first tri mester 3. Care plans created to link women and families to locval and stat resources.... enrollment in state programs, progression from where they were when they entered to program.

2433.organization: Lee County Board of County Commissioners
2433.description: We are requesting funding for design and construction phase services of the Medical Examiner Facility which serves Lee, Hendry and Glades counties. Rapidly expanding caseloads for both routine and emergency services exceed the capacity of the current facility. The project will add 22,000 square feet of morgue and administrative space, increasing capacity and improving efficiency to meet the growing demand.
2433.purpose: The request is to fund professional design and construction phase services for an addition of approximately 22,000 sqft. to the morgue and administrative areas of the Medical Examiner's Office serving Lee, Hendry and Glades Counties.
2433.activities: Lee, Hendry, and Glades counties are facing rapidly expanding caseloads for both routine and emergency services which exceed the capacity of the current facility. Funding will allow for services to be conducted in a timely manner expected by our residents.
2433.direct_services: Improvements to Medical Examiner's Office serving Lee, Hendry and Glades Counties to expedite services to residents.
2433.population: The majority of funds will benefit no specific group. The number of individuals expected to be served are greater than 800 people.
2433.outcome: The expansion of the ME's Office will increase capacity for the three counties served. The rapidly expanding caseloads for both routine and emergency services exceed the capacity of the current facility. This will be measured by the improvement in case management times.

2430.description: The Student Career Preparation & Innovative Partnerships facility will serve as a centralized hub dedicated to preparing students, traditional or non-traditional, for an ever-evolving workforce in the region and state. In accordance with strategic plan goals, Florida Gulf Coast University looks to build tomorrow’s workforce by creating more career exploration, workforce readiness opportunities and employer-driven micro credentials. These represent employer desired skills.
2430.purpose: Enhances Career Exploration and Development: The facility will provide resources, mentorship, and real-world learning opportunities for all students to explore career paths, make informed decisions, and build their professional network. By offering micro credentials the facility caters to students and professionals to upskill. It will serve as a hub to ensure learning outcomes meet workforce demands.
2430.activities: The new facility will provide a dedicated space for the implementation of targeted academic preparation programs designed to support incoming high school graduates in bridging the gap between secondary and postsecondary education. Additionally, through state-of-the-art career exploration and workforce readiness programs FGCU will equip students with the skills and experiences needed to thrive.
2430.direct_services: It will improve graduation rates, retention rates to provide a skilled workforce.
2430.population: University students with thousands of student served.
2430.outcome: Strengthen academic and workforce alignment with programs and curricula that meet our regional demand, respond to industry trends, integrate alternative credentials, include transferable skills and offer flexible degree lengths and delivery. Metrics: FTIC Four Year Graduation Rates; Academic Progress Rates and % of Bachelor's Graduates Employed and Earning 40K+ or continuing their education. State University Performance-based Metrics.

2428.description: Originally designed under the assumption that FGCU would remain a small, commuter-centric institution heavily reliant on online instruction, Reed Hall's infrastructure hasn't adapted to accommodate the transformation into a residential university with over 16,000 students. Currently, the building doesn't efficiently utilize classroom, laboratory, and office space, and requires redesigning and construction to meet the essential needs of students while optimizing precious university resources.
2428.purpose: Originally designed under the assumption that FGCU would remain a small, commuter-centric institution heavily reliant on online instruction, Reed Hall's infrastructure hasn't adapted to accommodate the transformation into a residential university with over 16,000 students. Currently, the building doesn't efficiently utilize classroom, laboratory, and office space, and requires redesigning and construction to meet the essential needs of students while optimizing precious university resources.
2428.activities: Classroom and lab instruction. Office space as needed for faculty and staff for better student accessibility.
2428.direct_services: By redesigning this space and increasing the utilization of classroom and lab instruction, FGCU will provide students with more class offerings and laboratory availability. This will improve graduation rates, which will invigorate the workforce with highly skilled employees.
2428.population: University students with over 16,500 student served.
2428.outcome: Fosters collaborative learning opportunities that provides dedicated spaces for group work, discussions, and peer interactions, faculty interactions, while enhancing teamwork and learning comprehension. Creates more space to house a growing Honors College and provides learning labs for communications program. Innovate teaching and learning to offer students a distinctive educational experience for a competitive advantage and enhance collaboration between faculty and students to promote critical thinking. State University Performance-based Metrics.

LENA will partner with ELCs statewide to support low-performing classrooms, minimizing staff resource impact. The five-week program uses classroom- and child-level data from LENA’s technology, strengths-based coaching sessions, and research-based strategies to support teachers. Program participation has been shown to improve CLASS scores, reduce challenging behaviors, increase teacher job satisfaction and retention, increase language and literacy assessment scores, and improve kinderg
2239.purpose: LENA Grow is a professional learning program for teachers that enhances the language environment in SR and VPK classrooms statewide. Based on research evaluations, implementing LENA Grow will achieve increased CLASS scores, accelerated literacy and language assessment scores, increased kindergarten readiness, and improved teacher job satisfaction and self-efficacy in SR and VPK classrooms. Independent evaluations of LENA Grow have shown statistically significant increases in teacher-child intera
2239.activities: The funds will support ELCs statewide to implement LENA Grow, including contract recruitment and coaching support SR and VPK classrooms. LENA Grow is a 5-week, evidenced-base program that uses data from LENA technology, classroom- and child-level reports, weekly strengths-based coaching sessions, and research-based strategies to help teachers increase quality teacher-child interactions in daily classroom activities. Funding will empower ELCs to deliver critical support to low-performing SR and V
2239.direct_services: The LENA Grow professional learning program will be implemented in SR and VPK classrooms statewide, as will program evaluation measures. Teachers in these classrooms will receive access to LENA technology and the data it provides, as well as strength-based coaching and printed and digital resources. Children in these classrooms will benefit from their teachers' participation, with increased langua
2239.population: The target population for this project includes more than 350 SR and VPK teachers participating in the LENA Grow program. At least 2,500 infants, toddlers, and preschool children in SR and VPK classrooms, along with their parents and caregivers, will benefit from the teachers' participation. Dual language learners and children with unique abilities, language delays, and challenging behaviors are expected to significantly benefit from the program.

Prior evaluation has shown this change to result in higher quality, responsive interactions and accelerated assessment scores. Additionally, 80% of participating teachers will experience increased job satisfaction, efficacy, and confidence. LENA Online captures participant data and provides classroom, site, and agency-level reports. Teachers receive an anonymous end-of-program survey, and the results are integrated into the program's profile on LENA Online. As avail

2179.description: MTC is requesting support from the state of Florida to support behavioral, educational, and employment programs to prepare Gadsden Correctional Facility residents for release into the community by improving their ability to live independently and successfully post-release. Funds will be used to install a boxx modular to serve as a classroom for the Shaping Success program. Associated costs would include site preparation and utilities installation.
2179.purpose: Funds will be used to support behavioral, educational, and employment programs to prepare inmates for release into the community by improving their ability to live independently and successfully post-release. Funds will be used to install a boxx modular to serve as a classroom for the Shaping Success program. Associated costs would include site preparation and utilities installation.
2179.activities: The funds are being requested to support a systematic approach to effective re-entry programming, including gender- responsive services, intensive case management, positive behavior management, and training in computer coding for incarcerated individuals.
2179.direct_services: With this appropriation, MTC will provide incentives, tablets with educational content, and intensive case management software for the Shaping Success for Reentry program for women. We will also use this funding to create a dedicated classroom space for re-entry. Finally, the funds will allow us to invest in technology to support our coding program.
2179.population: We will serve 400 incarcerated individuals through this project, helping prepare them for successful reentry into their communities.
2179.outcome: Developing the social/emotional, and technical skills that are the focus of both Shaping Success for Re-entry and the coding program will empower residents to be more employable, at higher wages, more quickly. The outcomes will be measured in several ways, including at minimum: program participation, number of mental health referrals, disciplinary infractions, percent of program completions/certifications, inmates' satisfaction/perception, incentive/sanction grid usage and staff feedback. Number of individuals obtaining employment, together with wage data, within 3 months and 6 months of release.

3145.description: Fresh Foundations equips at-risk youth and prime-age adults with industry-recognized skills, certifications, and paid work experiences that lead to sustainable employment and entrepreneurship. Participants engage in workforce readiness training, mentorship and wraparound support services addressing barriers such as transportation, childcare, and financial instability. The program boosts economic self-sufficiency, reduces unemployment, and strengthens the workforce pipeline in high-demand sectors.
3145.purpose: The funds will be used to expand and strengthen workforce development and economic mobility services for economically disadvantaged prime age adults and at-risk individuals by providing industry-recognized training, certifications, paid work experiences, and supportive services that lead to sustainable employment and increased earned income. The project will improve job readiness, reduce barriers to employment, and connect participants to high-demand career pathways, while strengthening the loca
3145.activities: Workforce readiness training, industry credential preparation, paid work experiences and internship stipends, career coaching and job placement, wraparound supports including transportation stipends and program supplies.
3145.direct_services: The project will provide direct workforce development and economic mobility services to citizens, including job readiness training, industry-recognized skills training and certifications, paid work-based learning opportunities, career coaching, and job placement support. Participants will also receive supportive services such as mentorship, case management, and referrals to transportation, childca
3145.population: The project will serve economically disadvantaged prime age adults and at-risk individuals, including unemployed and underemployed adults, at-risk youth, and individuals facing barriers to employment such as limited work experience, low income, transportation challenges, and other economic hardships. The project is expected to directly serve approximately 100-150 individuals through workforce training, certifications, paid work experiences, and supportive services.
3145.outcome: Expected outcomes include increased job readiness, credential attainment, and employment or income-generating placements. Outcomes will be measured using enrollment and completion data, certification records, employment verification, and follow-up tracking at 30, 60, 90 and 180 days.

2544.description: Elderly Hot Meals Program--This program aims to provide for the provision of a daily nutritionally balanced meal to the elderly. These meals are served at either a congregate site or home delivered. The program provides transportation to and from the center, breakfast, lunch, nutrition education, and activities that promote both cognitive and physical health as well as fine motor skills. Center staff provides social services such as translations, the completion of applications for services, and guidance. The program also provides telephone assurance which entails phone calls between center staff and the elderly to insure that all needs are being met.
2544.purpose: The goal of the program is to provide a daily healthy meal to the elderly participants in our community in either the form of a visit to the sites or through a delivery carrier for those who are unable to visit a site. A daily balanced provision of a meal coupled with nutritional education will establish a strong core value to living a healthier and longer life. The City of Hialeah Garden has over 200 participants and continuing to serve our special population is of the utmost importance.
2544.activities: This program aims to provide for the provision of a daily nutritionally balanced meal to the elderly. These meals are served at either a congregate site or home delivered. The program provides transportation to and from the center, breakfast, lunch, nutritional education, and activities that promote both cognitive and physical health.
2544.direct_services: Service provided with funding will be utilized for----Hot meals, both breakfast and lunch, transportation to and from congregate meal site, home delivered meals, nutritional education, and activities to promote both cognitive and physical health as well as fine motor skills. Finally, for telephone reassurance which includes calling clients and making sure that all needs are being met.
2544.population: Residents of Hialeah Gardens age 60 and over.
2544.outcome: Elderly residents are given an opportunity to have two full healthy meals a day and are also able to interact and socialize with other seniors.

2545.description: A proposed three-floor parking facility designed to provide secure vehicle staging, emergency deployment readiness, and integrated training space for law enforcement personnel. This initiative aims to enhance operational efficiency by ensuring that police and emergency vehicles are strategically positioned for rapid response while also incorporating dedicated areas for officer training and equipment storage.
2545.purpose: This facility will serve as a multi-purpose hub for police personnel, providing a secure parking structure for law enforcement vehicles, dedicated training areas, and an emergency staging zone for rapid deployment during critical incidents. By integrating essential resources into one strategic location, this facility will enhance operational efficiency, readiness, and response times for public safety effort.
2545.activities: To provide secure parking spaces for law enforcement vehicles, including patrol cars, emergency response units, and specialized vehicles. To create dedicated emergency staging areas that facilitate quick mobilization of law enforcement and emergency vehicles in response to critical incidents. To establish training zones and readiness spaces within the garage to enhance officers’ tactical skills, crisis management, and vehicle operations. To contribute to overall public safety by enhancing the la
2545.direct_services: Citizens will experience faster, more coordinated emergency responses in situations such as natural disasters, public safety threats, and major accidents. The facility’s emergency staging area ensures law enforcement and emergency vehicles are readily available and quickly deployed, minimizing delays during critical moments. The presence of a state-of-the-art facility dedicated to readiness ensure
2545.population: The facility will serve hundreds of law enforcement officers, providing them with a dedicated, centralized space for vehicle staging, training, and operational readiness. This will enhance the efficiency, effectiveness, and safety of officers across the region. Additional emergency response units (such as fire departments, EMS, and specialized tactical teams) who may need to coordinate with law enforcement for large-scale events or disasters. The entire community benefits from quicker emergency
2545.outcome: Faster deployment of law enforcement and emergency vehicles during critical incidents, reducing response times in emergencies. Law enforcement vehicles will be securely stored, regularly maintained, and mission-ready at all times. Improved law enforcement coordination during major incidents (natural disasters, active shooter situations, civil unrest, etc.).

2176.description: Pace Manatee is building a new facility to replace the outdated, original structure built in 1996. This new building will allow Pace to serve more girls, increase programming options & improve services through interactive classrooms. Enhanced security will create a safe learning environment. Pace opened in Manatee County in 1989 and has a strong history of creating positive change in our community.
2176.purpose: This funding will be used to complete Pace Manatee's new building which will: 1) increase the capacity to serve more girls, 2) add additional classrooms & improve technology, 3) Increase support services with the launch of the Reach Program, a full Health Clinic and an industrial kitchen for on site meal preparation, 4) improved safety and 5) more meeting spaces & offices.
2176.activities: The activities & services provided are: 230 days of instruction with quality education, case management, individual & family counseling, REACH therapy, hot breakfast & lunch every day, school health clinic and community volunteer activities.
2176.direct_services: Direct services include 230 days of education for girls who otherwise would not be in school combined with linkage to community resources & life skills development to help create positive, contributing citizens.
2176.population: The target population served are at-risk girls aged 11-18 years old, including those with poor mental health and are economically disadvantaged. Pace Manatee expects to serve 101-200 girls.
2176.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of this project is to enhance currently provided prevention services that are proven to divert the target population from the juvenile justice system by reducing recidivism, and improving the target population's mental health and quality of education. Pace Manatee's outcomes are measured via DJJ's accountability ratings, DJJ's Juvenile Justice Information System (JJIS), and data points regarding the number high school graduations and teen pregnancies.

Initiative is a statewide workforce development program designed to prepare underserved youth and young adults (ages 16–25) for high-demand, high-wage industries including construction, architecture, aviation, technology, and engineering. This appropriation supports 150 participants annually, providing classroom instruction, industry exposure, job coaching, and employment placement. The program leverages an existing partnership between the City of Miami Gardens and Workforce Readiness Advancement & Placement, Inc. (WRAP), which previously trained 80 youth using Formula 1 (F1) allocation funds. Florida's long-term economic strength depends on a skilled workforce capable of sustaining growth in infrastructure, aerospace, aviation, and technology. 2173.population: The C.A.A.T.E. Initiative intends to serve 150 youth and young adults between the ages of 16-25 during the funding year.

2592.description: The David Schaecter Holocaust Education Initiative supports statewide Holocaust education through teacher training, student programming, educator resources, curriculum development, public programming, and activities aligned with Florida’s Holocaust Education Mandate. Funds honor Holocaust survivor David Schaecter by advancing remembrance and education in all 67 school districts, engaging over 100,000 students and visitors annually while combating antisemitism, bigotry, and hatred.
2592.purpose: Funds will support the David Schaecter Education Initiative at the Holocaust Memorial Miami Beach, honoring Holocaust survivor David Schaecter’s lifelong dedication to remembrance and education. The initiative advances Holocaust education statewide through teacher training, student programs, and curriculum aligned with Florida’s Holocaust Education Mandate, engaging over 100,000 students and visitors annually.
2592.activities: Programs, resources, lessons, and training for educators and students; docent-led tours; Holocaust survivor testimony; educational resources; volunteer training; Holocaust Education Week; student advocacy programs; and statewide community events.
2592.direct_services: Tours, survivor and descendant testimony, student advocacy training, teacher training, volunteer instruction, educational resources, statewide Holocaust Education Week programming, and community commemorations.
2592.population: Elderly persons, Grade school students, High school students, University/college students. Greater than 800.
2592.outcome: The David Schaecter Holocaust Education Initiative will improve mental health, enrich cultural experience, enhance safety, increase educational quality, and expand tourism and economic activity. Survivors who share their testimonies experience increased emotional wellbeing and a sense of purpose. Students and visitors gain deeper cultural and historical understanding, leading to enriched educational outcomes aligned with Florida standards. Expanded programming increases visitor numbers, supports local economic activity, and strengthens statewide awareness of antisemitism, bigotry, and racism. These benefits will be measured through pre- and post-visit surveys, educator and student evaluation

2629.description: The design will address critical space deficiencies at Volusia County's east side judicial facilities, which currently lack 76,500 SF of court space and 27,630 SF of administrative space. The project will validate space requirements through 2045, develop three conceptual design options (including Foxman expansion, Henderson enhancements, and/or new construction), and provide construction documents addressing security deficiencies, ADA compliance issues, and operational inefficiencies.
2629.purpose: The design will address critical space deficiencies at Volusia County's east side judicial facilities, which currently lack 76,500 SF of court space and 27,630 SF of administrative space. The project will validate space requirements through 2045, develop three conceptual design options (including Foxman expansion, Henderson enhancements, and/or new construction), and provide construction documents addressing security deficiencies, ADA compliance issues, and operational inefficiencies.
2629.activities: Preliminary design will provide necessary details for project management.
2629.direct_services: There are no direct services to citizens.

2629.outcome: Preliminary design will provide necessary details for project management.

2491.description: The Florida Local Government Information Systems Association (FLGISA) Critical Infrastructure Resilience Program strengthens the security and reliability of essential public infrastructure operated by Florida’s cities, counties, and special districts. Through the FLGISA, the program provides direct assistance, training, coordination, and resources to help local governments prevent, detect, respond to, and recover from cyber threats and technology disruptions. Funds will be used exclusively for member support, with minimal administrative overhead, to enhance protection of critical systems such as water, emergency services, and communications. This initiative safeguards citizens, ensures continuity of essential services, and strengthens Florida’s overall cyber resilience and public safety.
2491.purpose: The purpose of this funding is to strengthen the cybersecurity, resiliency, and operational continuity of Florida’s critical infrastructure systems operated by local governments. The goal is to assist Florida’s cities, counties, and special districts in preventing, detecting, responding to, and recovering from cyber threats and infrastructure disruptions that could affect essential public services such as water, transportation, emergency response, and administrative operations. This initiative w
2491.activities: The funds will be used to support a range of flexible and adaptive activities that may include, but are not limited to: - Providing technical assistance, training, and awareness programs for local government IT and operational staff. - Facilitating regional and statewide collaboration and information sharing related to cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and best practices. - Supporting the development and implementation of cybersecurity assessments, resilience planning, and incident response exerci
2491.direct_services: While the project’s services are delivered through local government entities, citizens will benefit directly through improved protection of essential public services, including public safety, emergency communications, water and wastewater systems, and local government operations. Enhanced cybersecurity and resiliency reduce the risk of service disruptions, financial losses, and data breaches that
2491.population: The target population includes all Floridians who rely on local government services. The project directly serves Florida’s local government IT departments, system operators, and leadership across FLGISA’s member organizations, comprising approximately 340 local governments statewide. Indirectly, the initiative benefits the state’s entire population by helping ensure the continuous and secure delivery of critical infrastructure and community services.
2491.outcome: Expected Benefits and Outcomes: - Improved cybersecurity readiness and response capabilities among local governments. - Reduced risk and impact of cyber incidents affecting critical infrastructure. - Enhanced coordination and information sharing among local government entities. - Increased awareness and adoption of best practices in infrastructure protection and resilience. Methodology for Measurement: - Pre- and post-initiative self-assessments or surveys of participating local governments. - Tracking of participation levels in training, assessments, and collaborative programs. - Collection of performance metrics such as incident response times, number of participants trained, and adoption

2789.description: The Nonprofit Insurance Coalition (NIC) is a 501c3 nonprofit, that has been approved as an insurance Trust through the Office of Insurance Regulation and is in the final stages of approval. There has been precedent set with assisting in capitalization. The Florida Children Coalition (FCC) received $3 million in 2007 to start an insurance trust. Unfortunately, nothing was done by the FCC to form the trust and in 2009 the money was given back to the State. NIC can have an immediate impact with diversifying, leveraging purchasing power by size, and ultimately attracting other carriers into the market. NIC needs to be capitalized before entering the market. Money saved due to a reduction in cost for in all lines of insurance, including, property, liability, and health is funding that can be re-allocated to increase the quality and quantity of direct services for children and families.
2789.purpose: To fund the start up of the Nonprofit Insurance Coalition (NIC) first year of operation as an insurance trust. The purpose of NIC is to bring competition to the insurance market for non-profit organizations and reduce the cost of insurance premiums in order to re-allocate funding to direct services for children and families in Florida by increasing purchasing power for a collective group of organizations.
2789.activities: The capital will be used to fund any claims submitted in the first year of the Nonprofit Insurance Coalition (NIC) insurance trust.
2789.direct_services: NIC will be providing property and casualty insurance coverage as well as health benefits to Florida non-profits that operate in the social service sector.
2789.population: The target population is Florida 501c3 nonprofits operate in the social service sector such as child welfare, juvenile justice, senior services, homeless shelters, mental health and substance abuse, and workforce development.
2789.outcome: The expected benefit is a reduction to insurance costs in the non-profit sector as well as providing Risk Management and Loss Control / Safety services to members of NIC as well as providing risk reduction services for non-members to reduce their risk and assist in their eligibility for coverage.

2790.description: This shovel-ready project will convert a 488-acre former farming area into natural meandering streams and native wetlands to fill a remaining habitat gap in an otherwise continuous wildlife corridor connecting 8,000 acres of nature preserves to form a habitat expanse supporting wildlife and recreation crossing two watersheds that drain to Hillsborough Bay. Project will significantly reduce nutrient loads to Tampa Bay and form a native aesthetic in a densely populated area for outdoor activities.
2790.purpose: This shovel-ready project will convert a 488-acre former farming area into natural meandering streams and native wetlands to fill a remaining habitat gap in an otherwise continuous wildlife corridor connecting 8,000 acres of nature preserves to form a habitat expanse supporting wildlife and recreation crossing two watersheds that drain to Hillsborough Bay. Project will significantly reduce nutrient loads to Tampa Bay, and form a native aesthetic in a densely populated area for outdoor activities
2790.activities: This property, once restored, forms a native Florida aesthetic in an otherwise densely populated and growing part of the County, forming natural areas valued by the community with hiking, cycling, bird watching and other outdoor activities. Part of the northern corridor that the project ties to has become an internationally-recognized mountain bike destination bringing tourism to the County.
2790.direct_services: Creation of shared public recreation spaces that will allow residents and visitors to enjoy outdoor activities and engage with nature inside the Florida Wildlife Corridor.
2790.population: Target population is the general public of thousands of residents and visitors to Hillsborough County.
2790.outcome: Project completes, connects, and restores the Florida Wildlife Corridor. It provides consistent passage for wildlife, reduces nutrient loads to Tampa Bay improving water quality, enhances fish and wildlife habitats and biodiversity, and provides recreational green spaces for walking, biking, and other outdoor activities improving ecotourism and associated revenues.

3129.organization: Academy at the Farm Charter School
3129.description: The funds will be used to construct a permanent middle school building at Academy at the Farm, replacing temporary modular units. This project will provide safe, durable facilities that meet modern educational standards and support long- term growth for students and the community.
3129.purpose: To construct a permanent middle school building to replace temporary modular units, providing safe, long-term facilities that support quality education and growth for students.
3129.activities: Funds will support construction of a permanent middle school building, including classrooms, administrative spaces, and core facilities. This will provide students with a safe, modern learning environment, support expanded educational programs, and replace temporary modular buildings.
3129.direct_services: The project will provide students with safe, permanent classrooms and educational facilities, enabling high-quality instruction, expanded programs, and improved learning outcomes for the community’s children.
3129.population: The target population is middle school students in grades 6–8 at Academy at the Farm Charter School. Approximately 350 students will be served by this project.
3129.outcome: Expected Benefit/Outcome: Students will have access to a safe, permanent middle school facility that supports high- quality instruction, expanded programs, and improved learning environments. Methodology for Measurement: Success will be measured by student enrollment and attendance, academic performance, program participation rates, and the transition from temporary modular classrooms to a permanent facility.

2595.description: Renovation of two facilities in Key West, Florida, owned by the Monroe County School District (MCSD): Reynolds School (1316 Reynolds St.) and Bruce Hall (1310 United St.) for use as administrative facilities. Renovation of these facilities would permit MCSD to vacate its current administration building at 241 Trumbo Road for the purpose of developing that property for affordable workforce housing for MCSD teachers and educational support personnel at no cost to MCSD through public-private partnership. Through renovation of these properties, MCSD will utilize existing local resources to address one of its biggest challenges to effective operation of schools: decreasing levels of staff attrition caused by the distinct lack of affordable housing in the lower keys area.
2595.purpose: Making the property at 241 Trumbo Road, Key West, Florida, available for development of affordable workforce housing to support local teachers and other district employees at no cost to MCSD via public-private partnership. Renovation of the Reynolds School and Bruce Hall facilities will utilize existing local resources to permit relocation of the MCSD administration team from the Trumbo Road facility, allowing the property to be developed into affordable workforce housing.
2595.activities: The requested funds will be used to retain the services of one or more firms to renovate the Reynolds School facility, which will accommodate relocation of the MCSD Maintenance Department, and the Bruce Hall facility, which will accommodate relocation of the MCSD Administration Department. Relocation of both Departments to Bruce Hall and Reynolds School properties will allow MCSD to vacate the property at 241 Trumbo Road, making the property available for development of affordable workforce hous
2595.direct_services: Monroe County students and families will benefit from recruiting and retaining highly qualified teachers in Monroe County schools when affordable housing in no longer an issue, which will in turn lead to better academic outcomes.
2595.population: The project is expected to serve Monroe County School District employees, economically disadvantaged persons, and at-risk youth as the Reynolds School site will be used in part for Adult Education and/or Alternative Education. These target populations will benefit from the increased availability of affordable housing in the Key West area for teachers and other district employees. The proposed affordable housing development is expected to contain 150 dwelling units. Therefore, it is expected that
2595.outcome: Completion of this project is expected to enhance teacher and employee recruitment for MCSD by reducing the high cost of living in the Lower Florida Keys via development of affordable workforce housing at 241 Trumbo Road. This outcome can be measured by a reduction in the total number of applicants who reject employment with MCSD due to lack of affordable housing, reduction in the total number of vacant employment positions with MCSD, as well as a reduction in the total number of applications for state or federal housing assistance submitted by MCSD employees.

2535.description: The funds will be used to construct 150 units of attainable housing in Key West, FL. Employees of the Monroe County School District will be given priority, followed by other employees of the local and state government and essential service personnel.
2535.purpose: Construction of 150 units of attainable housing in Key West, FL.
2535.population: Employees of the Monroe County School District, Local and State government employees, and essential service personnel.

3651.description: The Town of Eatonville requires a new public safety facility. This request is for funding for a staffing study, needs assessment, and pre-design study with cost estimates to determine the feasibility of a new combined facility.
3651.purpose: The Town is in need of a new public safety building. The current police department building has reached its useful life, and a new facility is needed to address the needs of a modern public safety facility.
3651.activities: A staffing analysis, space needs, predesign, and cost estimate are needed to evaluate the requirements of the new facility.
3651.direct_services: Law enforcement, fire, and EMS; emergency operations center (EOC)
3651.outcome: The staffing study information enables us to make current and future projections of spatial needs. The estimate will help decision-makers better understand the costs, allowing for more informed future financial planning.

In the last year, we have assisted over 25,000 individuals. These funds would allow us to expand our outreach to reach a minimum of 100,000 veterans, first responders, and their families.

The program promotes healing, self-expression, and community engagement, allowing veterans to heal, while providing follow-on care.

This project directly addresses this state priority by serving 400 seniors annually through a holistic, cost-effective model. 2659.organization: City of Delray Beach / Delray Beach Police
2659.description: The Delray Beach Police Department is currently building a real-time center in an effort to identify offenders, deter and reduce crime, increase officer safety, and improve the overall quality of life for the residents and guests. Financial assistance is needed to add license plate recognition cameras to entrance and exit points into and out of the City of Delray Beach. In addition, add live-view CCTV cameras with playback capabilities in strategic locations that will act as a force multiplier in deterring, reducing and solving crimes. The goal is to get CCTV cameras in heavily populated areas, city parks, around schools, and other locations that are identified as "hot spots" or places of interest.
2659.purpose: Cameras and other technological equipment will be purchased for the City's Real Time Crime Center.
2659.activities: This equipment will be used to monitor various locations in the City to prevent crime, to have video to help solve crimes, and to have evidence to prosecute criminals.
2659.direct_services: The City will be safer for all residents, property owners, and visitors.
2659.population: All 66,000 residents of the City as well as all businesses and visitors.
2659.outcome: Crime reduction and an increase in the percentage of crimes solved.

2631.description: The City has a well documented interest in extending Runway 9-27 to 7,500 feet in length for 10+ years. Although the larger, long-haul category of business jets does not yet provide daily operations at the airport (in accordance with FAA and FDOT criteria), the City still has an interest to extend the runway to support local and regional economic development initiatives. Need: To extend Runway 9-27 from 6,000 feet to 7,500 feet in length, through a 2-phase development plan.
