Measured by tracking new activity. Improve economic activity: Revenues will be increased as more airplanes will continue to this airport because of the location and extended runway. The airport will be being able to accommodate the non-stop flights from throughout the country. This will be measured by tracking the increase use. Employ two to four more individuals creating job opportunities.

2819.description: This program combats antisemitism and strengthens the safety, empowerment, and inclusion of Jewish students on Florida campuses through a comprehensive model of education, advocacy, leadership training, and community engagement. By reducing fear and isolation, it supports student mental health and builds emotional resilience, while cultural programming—such as educational events, Shabbat gatherings, and interfaith initiatives—fosters Jewish pride, community connection, and cross-campus understanding. Hands-on learning in leadership and civic engagement further enhances students’ academic development and personal growth.
2819.purpose: Support efforts to combat antisemitism and promote the safety, empowerment, and inclusion of Jewish students on Florida campuses through education, advocacy, leadership training, and community engagement. We will build campuses that are secure, respectful, and unified.
2819.activities: The Rabbis and congregations will deliver student advocacy training, leadership development, educational initiatives, campus cultural and community events, and Shabbat and holiday programming to strengthen safety, Jewish pride, and inclusion across Florida campuses.
2819.direct_services: The Rabbis and congregations will provide direct services including student advocacy and leadership training, rapid response to antisemitic incidents, educational and cultural programs, safety resources, and partnerships with campus and community organizations to promote safety, inclusion, and Jewish pride across Florida campuses.
2819.population: High school students and University/college students. Over 1000.
2819.outcome: The ACT program strengthens student mental health by reducing fear and isolation through education, advocacy, and community support. It enriches cultural experiences by fostering Jewish pride and connection through events, Shabbat gatherings, and interfaith programs. It also enhances education by providing hands-on learning in leadership, advocacy, and civic engagement that builds essential skills for academic and personal growth. Outcomes will be measured through surveys, participation data, and student feedback to track improvements in wellbeing and engagement.

3486.description: This project strengthens Northeast Florida’s crisis response system by modernizing the technology that supports 211 and 988 services. More than 60,000 individuals in crisis contacted these services last year. The requested funding will upgrade core technology to allow callers to access immediate, coordinated assistance without navigating multiple agencies. The project will transform a fragmented system into a seamless, intelligent service navigation network, improving both short-term crisis response and long-term stability for vulnerable residents across the region.
3486.purpose: The purpose of this project is to modernize and integrate crisis response technology supporting 211 and 988 to ensure individuals in crisis receive timely, coordinated, and effective assistance. By creating a closed-loop referral system, the project will improve service navigation, reduce duplication, strengthen partnerships, and improve outcomes for individuals and families facing urgent needs.
3486.activities: The project will improve physical health, mental health, public safety, transportation access, economic activity, job creation, and individual economic self-sufficiency. Outcomes will be measured through database and telephony systems that track call volume, caller demographics, needs by zip code, referral completion rates, service outcomes, transportation usage, employment connections, and successful crisis resolutions using closed-loop referral tracking.
3486.direct_services: Direct services include basic needs navigation such as emergency housing and shelter referrals, utility and rental assistance navigation, food access, transportation assistance, childcare and family support, financial assistance and budgeting, suicide prevention and de-escalation, mental health crisis counseling, immediate connection to mental health support, and navigation of veteran-specific ser
3486.population: Target populations include elderly persons, individuals with poor mental or physical health, jobless and economically disadvantaged individuals, homeless individuals, students, veterans, and families in crisis. Expected number served: More than 800 individuals annually.
3486.outcome: The project will improve physical health, mental health, public safety, transportation access, economic activity, job creation, and individual economic self-sufficiency. Outcomes will be measured through database and telephony systems that track call volume, caller demographics, needs by zip code, referral completion rates, service outcomes, transportation usage, employment connections, and successful crisis resolutions using closed-loop referral tracking.

3600.description: There is an immediate need to repair/restore canal 3 bank and implement erosion control to protect the canal from pollutants that are harmful to water quality and flood control. Funding will address flood control-improved conveyance to reduce flooding and improve water quality before it enters the primary canal water bodies. The project will work to bring the city into full compliance with the water quality goals of its MS4 NPDES Permit. The project will address flood management and improve water quality in the City through infrastructure improvements to the Canal 3 Stormwater Conveyance and Water Quality Improvement Project.
3600.purpose: There is an immediate need to repair/restore canal 3 bank and erosion control to protect the canal from pollutants that are harmful to water quality and flood control. The project will include canal bank repair, stabilization, and erosion control. It will be a local effort to enhance flood management resiliency and improve water quality in the City of Lauderdale Lakes through infrastructure improvements to the Canal 3 Stormwater Conveyance and Water Quality Improvement Project.
3600.activities: The project scope will include canal bank repair and/restoration, stabilization, and erosion control.
3600.direct_services: The project scope will include canal bank repair and/restoration, stabilization, and erosion control. These services will enhance the quality of life for over 5,000 residents in the Oriole Estates Community as well as the water quality in the area.
3600.population: City of Lauderdale Lakes residents and region
3600.outcome: The project will address Flood Control-Improved conveyance will reduce flooding, and Water Quality-will improve water quality before entering primary canal water bodies,Resiliency-improving results of future extreme weather events. This will be measured by the elimination or reduction in the rate of bank loss. Project can bring the city into full compliance with the water quality goals of its MS4 NPDES Permit.

2742.description: Phase I of the project consists in the replacement of existing outfall pipes and installation of automatic sluice gates at 4 locations where City canals connect to the C-13 Canal. The proposed gates will alleviate flooding in canal zone 2, and 3 while implementation of the proposed skimmers will minimize the migration of floatable contaminants, debris and vegetation from the C-13 to the City canal network and vice versa. In addition, 8 water level stage recorder will be installed at strategic locations within Canal Zones 2, and 3 to help better operate the proposed gates.
2742.purpose: Phase I of this project replaces existing outfall pipes and installs automatic sluice gates at four City canal connections to the C-13 canal. These gates will alleviate flooding in canal zones 2 and 3, while the skimmers will minimize contaminant migration between the C-13 and City canals. Eight water level stage recorders in canal zones 2 and 3 will be installed to help better operate the gates.
2742.activities: This project will alleviate recurring flooding in canal zone 2, and 3 and increase water quality of the City canal network.
2742.direct_services: Reduced flooding and increased canal's water quality
2742.outcome: Reduced flooding and increased water quality in the city's canal network

2746.description: The City of Lauderhill Lift Station 48 Rehabilitation Project will upgrade aging wastewater infrastructure that has been in operation for over 30 years. The project includes replacing pumps, motors, electrical panels, and structural components to improve reliability, efficiency, and environmental compliance. These improvements will extend the system’s service life, reduce sewer overflows, and protect public health and water quality in alignment with state environmental priorities.
2746.purpose: The rehab of Lift Station 48 is essential to ensure reliable wastewater conveyance, protect public health, and maintain compliance with state and federal environmental standards. The project will replace deteriorated components that have exceeded their service life, improving system reliability, energy efficiency, and capacity to support continued urban growth. This investment will also mitigate the risk of sewer overflows and environmental contamination, directly aligning with DEP goals.
2746.activities: The project will fund the rehabilitation of Lift Station 48, including design, permitting, construction, and installation of upgraded mechanical, structural, and electrical components. Activities include replacing pumps and motors, upgrading control systems, and restoring the wet well to DEP standards to improve reliability, prevent sewer overflows, and ensure uninterrupted wastewater service to residents and businesses in the service area.
2746.direct_services: The project will provide residents and businesses with reliable wastewater collection and conveyance by eliminating service interruptions, reducing sewer overflows, and improving environmental and public health protection through modernized lift station infrastructure.
2746.population: This project will serve the general populations of Lauderhill residents.
2746.outcome: Improve cost effectiveness, reduce maintenance repairs, reduce sewer overflows into the street, and to improve operational effectiveness within the Lift Station. The City’s Utilities Department will track flow efficiency, pump run times, and maintenance logs pre- and post-construction to measure system performance improvements. The level of benefit will be measured by increased efficiency of wastewater flow which is critically low due to aged system requiring a temporary back-up system.

2747.description: Safeguarding the embankment of the primary distribution canal that supplies our pump stations from erosion or destabilization is vital for the safe and efficient transport of stormwater. Any failures of the canal embankment in these critical canals could result in catastrophic flooding due to the inability to effectively pump out the stormwater. Seawalls, which are man-made barriers, are designed and engineered to minimize erosion caused by water and are considered the highest level of protection. The City's Public Works and Engineering Departments are in ongoing communication with the South Florida Water Management District (SFWMD) regarding potential funding pathways and will continue to pursue all available avenues to support this project.
2747.purpose: Safeguarding the embankment of the primary distribution canal that supplies our pump stations from erosion or destabilization is vital for the safe and efficient transport of stormwater. Any failures of the canal embankment in these critical canals would lead to catastrophic flooding due to our inability to pump out the stormwater. Seawall’s which are man-made barriers are designed and engineered to minimize erosion caused by water and are considered the highest level of protection.
2747.activities: The funding requested will directly support the protection and stabilization of the canal banks along the primary distribution canal that feeds our stormwater pump stations. By constructing engineered seawalls, this project will ensure the safe and efficient movement of stormwater through the canal system, preventing erosion and potential embankment failures.
2747.direct_services: These improvements provide direct benefits to citizens by reducing the risk of catastrophic flooding, protecting homes, businesses, roadways, and public infrastructure from storm-related damages. The project will enhance community resilience, maintain reliable stormwater drainage operations, and safeguard public health and safety during heavy rainfall and storm events.
2747.population: The project serves residents, businesses, and institutions in Lauderhill’s stormwater service area—specifically those whose properties are protected by the primary distribution canal system. This includes neighborhoods adjacent to or downstream of the canal, where the embankment's structural integrity affects flood control capacity, roadway stability, and public safety. The project therefore benefits the entire municipal population that relies on the continuous operation of the canal and pump sy
2747.outcome: The project stabilizes and protects the primary canal embankment supporting the City’s stormwater conveyance and pump station network. Engineered seawalls and erosion-control prevent canal bank failure, preserve hydraulic capacity, and reduce flood risk. These improvements will extend the life of critical stormwater infrastructure, ensure uninterrupted pump operation, and enhance public safety for 75,000- 80,000 residents during storms. Post-construction inspections, hydraulic performance data, and ongoing erosion monitoring confirm structural stability and flow capacity. The City will track maintenance and emergency response reductions, as well as water-level and pump-performance data durin

2748.description: This project is to provide security protection and a safe environment to all employees and visitors of City Hall, along with the elected officials of the City when they are conducting business in City Hall. The project will be comprised of the addition of ballistic glass, doors, and other measures that are designed and recommended by a security consultant. The funds will be used to enhance security measures and controls such as improving technology, emergency signage, cyber infrastructure to better protect against threats.

2748.direct_services: By making these changes to all formats of security City Hall will become a more secure facility as well as making the customer and resident data (payment information, other personnel information) received in the course of City business more secure.

2748.outcome: All occupants of City Hall will feel more relaxed and at ease knowing that they are protected by the added security measures. The benefit can be measured by surveys given to the visitors and employees and of City Hall.

2752.description: The requested funds will be used to purchase foreclosed and/or vacant properties in the City of North Lauderdale. These properties will be rehabbed and offered with down payment assistance to first time home buyers. This will enable City to provide high quality, affordable homes for low-income and workforce families.

These properties will be rehabbed and offered with down payment assistance to first time home buyers. This will enable City to provide high quality, attainable homes for low-income and workforce families.

2752.direct_services: The funding will provide attainable homeownership opportunities for low-income and workforce families addressing critical housing needs in the city.
2752.population: The general population and economically disadvantaged persons are the target population of this project.
2752.outcome: To increase homeownership to our low-income working families and by doing so reduces the financial burden, mental stress by providing positive impact on our community and the local economy in general. The number of families that become homeowners will be used to measure outcome.

Stat. 1001.216, by studying the conditions affecting black men and boys and providing recommendations to improve their well-being. Such research will be on issues such as education, health, incarceration, and economic conditions.

2757.description: Broward Community & Family Health Centers, Inc. (BCOM) will launch the EmpowerMOMS Health Program, integrating high-quality, community-based maternal support services into our existing prenatal and perinatal care system. The program aims to improve maternal outcomes, particularly for women managing chronic conditions. Key components include Doula support for high-risk mothers, interactive culinary and nutrition education classes to promote healthy lifestyles, and concierge transportation through Uber Health to reduce access barriers. By combining clinical excellence with supportive services, EmpowerMOMS will address medical and social determinants of health, ensuring mothers receive, culturally responsive care throughout pregnancy and beyond.

Directly supporting about 150 students annually through weekly tutoring, summer enrichment, and year-round literacy initiatives, plus 500+ parents and community members through quarterly workshops and community-wide resource sharing, the project integrates academics, mentoring, and cultural connections with critical family resources.

Funding will allow the CEA to serve additional students and families, strengthen literacy outcomes, and enhance coordinated school and community-based support that address whole-child educ
2758.activities: Project MPACT will provide a continuum of evidence-informed academic and enrichment services, including free weekly afterschool tutoring, a 7-week summer learning program, in-school literacy and enrichment activities at partner schools identified as underperforming, and quarterly family engagement opportunities. Programming is designed to support academic growth, student resilience and well-being, mentorship, and culturally responsive learning through coordinated school and community partnership
2758.direct_services: Direct services include free weekly afterschool tutoring and homework support, literacy intervention and differentiated academic instruction, mentorship and enrichment activities, a 7-week summer camp experience, and community-based events in partnership with local other literacy focused, STEM, and faith-based organizations. Students also receive free instructional materials, books, academic incen
2758.population: The target population includes students and families across six Broward County public schools and surrounding communities, primarily those residing in District 32 and neighboring areas. Project MPACT prioritizes students and families who may face economic hardship, limited access to enrichment opportunities, and lower educational attainment. Approximately 650 individuals, including students, parents, and caregivers, are expected to be served annually through school-based and community-wide progr

Through intentional partnerships with faith-based organizations and local community organizations that share aligned goals, the project leverages trusted community institutions to increase participation, reinforce positive academic behaviors, and provide wraparound supports that extend beyond the classroom. Services improve quality of life, reduce abuse and neglect, allow families to maintain jobs. 80% of children with environmental delays (common in NWFL) who attend Capstone in early childhood go on to a regular kindergarten or elementary.

2537.description: Walk Off Charities is a Jacksonville based nonprofit with a mission to provide opportunities, resources, and access to the game of baseball and softball for any youth that desires to learn or play. Through various programs, events, and activities we aim to give underserved youth opportunities they may not have had otherwise. With increasingly growing programs and needs, the purpose of requesting these funds is to allow us to expand our reach across northeast Florida to impact even more youth.

This program also provides job opportunities within the local community that it serves as well as internship positions. 2740.description: YPI developed by North American Family Institute (NAFI) is a nationally recognized evidenced informed prevention and intervention program bringing law enforcement and youth together in a structured, relationship-building format over the course of 5 days; designed to address fractured trust, reduce conflict and promote safer more connected communities. Department of Homeland Security considers YPI a promising practice; featured in the Wall Street Journal and Police Chief Magazine. Need for YPI has been identified by local law enforcement based on daily statistics and interactions. Over the course of 20 years, results from independent research by John Jay College of Criminal Justice has shown YPI can lead to a reduction in crime and documented positive attitudinal shifts participants in cities. Train-the-Trainer model consists of 4 one-week training sessions to train and certify police off
2740.purpose: The Youth & Police Initiative program breaks down stereotypes between youth and police by having youth and local PD officers interact in a non-crisis setting. The program starts with a five-day intensive YPI program where both parties examine and discard their stereotypes and negative perceptions of each other. It is followed by various mentoring opportunities for graduates to further build trust with local officers. 4 local PD to build internal capacity to sustain the program after the initial
2740.activities: Local youth and officers participate in a five-day intensive program followed by several mentorship opportunities including a combination of one-on-one and small group programs, utilizing existing programs available through local partners who agree to be a part of the program. Four one-week training programs will be implemented - up to six locals will become certified trainers.
2740.direct_services: The copyrighted curriculum is both didactic and experiential. Sessions include ice breakers, team building, public speaking, group process, goal development and scenario role play. Focus is given to deescalating problem behavior and understanding respective points of view. As youth and police participate they develop beliefs which strengthen protective factors against violence and conflict.
2740.population: As previously stated, the Train-the Trainer program will be utilized to train and certify up to six selected local law enforcement officers within each of the participating departments and communities over the course of four YPI training cohorts (total of 24 certified trainers). This local capacity-building program will allow each of the participating communities to implement YPI indefinitely at a very low cost. The Train-the-Trainer model includes four YPI cohorts with up to 15 youth during eac
2740.outcome: The expected benefits for participating local officers and local youth are to achieve positive attitudinal changes resulting in opportunities for sustained relationships between officers and youths that reduce community conflicts and ultimately juvenile crime. These outcomes are based upon independent research and statistics from over ten studies. A professor from John Jay College of Criminal Justice will be contracted to collect data from each cohort through pre and post surveys and follow-up interviews to measure shifts in attitude of both youth and police regarding safety, trust, understanding and willingness to positively engage.

2635.description: A partnership between The Shul of Downtown/Brickell and Groot Hospitality to establish a Kosher Culinary Training and Certification Program grounded in Jewish tradition. The program trains individuals aged 16+ for skilled jobs in kosher culinary and hospitality fields, providing hands-on experience, certification, and job placement to promote workforce growth and cultural inclusion.
2635.purpose: To expand certified Kosher culinary training and employment opportunities in Florida’s hospitality sector through hands-on education and certification.
2635.activities: Provide culinary and hospitality training, Mashgiach Kosher Certification, food safety certification, and professional job placement services.
2635.direct_services: Hands-on kitchen experience and instruction with culinary staff; Food Handler and Kosher certifications; training in operations and service management.
2635.population: Economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, and high school students. Estimated individuals served: 200–400
2635.outcome: The program will create job opportunities in Florida’s kosher culinary and hospitality sectors by providing hands-on training, certification, and job placement for participants. It will enhance economic self-sufficiency through workforce readiness and promote cultural understanding by preserving Jewish culinary traditions. Participants will gain confidence, stability, and purpose through structured learning that supports both personal and professional growth. Program success will be measured through job placement rates, employer feedback, completion data, and participant surveys evaluating progress and satisfaction.

2636.description: This project will sustain and expand the LiveMore 365 Program, a wellness & care-management initiative that enhances the physical & mental health of individuals living with chronic conditions. The program focuses on reducing disability, preventing hospital readmissions, & empowering participants to take an active role in managing care. Funding will support daily operations, essential equipment, & program enhancements that strengthen long-term health outcomes. With a notable influx of Jewish residents relocating to the Aventura area, this investment will also help meet growing community demand and ensure equitable access to high-quality health and wellness services.
2636.purpose: This will sustain the LiveMore 365 Program, which improves the physical and mental health of individuals with chronic conditions by reducing disabilities, preventing readmissions, and empowering participants to manage their care. Funding will support daily operations and essential equipment to strengthen program impact. With a significant influx of Jewish residents moving into the Aventura area, this investment will help meet rising community demand.
2636.activities: Livemore 365 provides exercise programs for individuals with chronic conditions (cancer, diabetes, heart disease), health assessments to track progress, nutrition and stress management education, and disease self-care guidance. Staff lead daily activities to improve physical and mental health and prevent hospital readmissions.
2636.direct_services: The program provides structured exercise sessions for individuals with chronic conditions, personalized health assessments, education on nutrition, stress management, and disease self-care, and one-on-one support from trained staff to help participants manage their health, reduce disabilities, and prevent hospital readmissions.
2636.population: Persons with poor mental health, Economically disadvantaged persons, Persons with poor physical health. 300 people.
2636.outcome: The project will improve participants physical health by increasing mobility, strength, and stamina, strengthen disease management by reducing symptoms and slowing progression, & enhance mental well-being by decreasing isolation, stress, and anxiety. Outcomes will be measured through participant feedback forms, interviews, satisfaction surveys, & by tracking attendance, engagement, and documented health improvements. The program will monitor social connections formed and overall participant progress to evaluate success.

2637.description: This project will modernize the facility's diagnostic capabilities by replacing outdated X-ray and ultrasound equipment with advanced imaging technology. The initiative includes the purchase, installation, and maintenance of upgraded diagnostic systems designed to improve early detection, maternal health care, and overall patient outcomes. By investing in state-of-the-art equipment, the project will strengthen the quality and reliability of clinical assessments for women and expectant mothers.
2637.purpose: To provide timely and accurate diagnostic imaging for women and babies by replacing outdated X-ray and ultrasound equipment. The new ultrasound machine will improve breast cancer detection and monitor healthy fetal development, ensuring low-income women receive essential care that protects their health and their babies’ wellbeing.
2637.activities: The project will replace outdated X-ray and ultrasound equipment with modern diagnostic technology to enhance early detection and maternal health care. Activities include purchasing, installing, and maintaining upgraded imaging equipment; training clinical staff on new diagnostic protocols; and expanding access to high-quality imaging services for women and expectant mothers.
2637.direct_services: X-ray and ultrasound services will be provided for low-income residents in South Florida.
2637.population: Elderly individuals; persons with poor mental or physical health; economically disadvantaged individuals; people experiencing homelessness; individuals with physical disabilities; preschool, grade school, and high school students; and university/college students. 1000 screenings.
2637.outcome: The new equipment will increase diagnostic accuracy, reduce wait times, and provide 1,000 additional screenings and assessments each year, improving early detection and maternal health outcomes. The level of benefit will be measured by tracking the number of low-income residents who receive X-ray and ultrasound services through the upgraded equipment.

2647.description: Provide uninterrupted power services to campus security-safety/environmental systems of a 100,000 sq. ft. facility that support operations of: 3-active schools (Pre-K, K-5, Sport-Specialized Schools), Jewish Community Center, a Neurodiverse Adult and Child Training Center, Adult Learning, Senior programming, a Holocaust Memorial Resource & Education Center directly supporting Orange-Seminole County area residents and often Central Florida. Actively supporting area Emergency First Responders (Police, Fire-Rescue) by serving as an "as needed" staging center during multi-day extended critical incidents, during-post hurricanes (all-hazards) when power infrastructures are compromised. Funding assistance will provide support necessary for installation of comprehensive generator back-up power system that ensures previously described programs/services remain operational when power services are i
2647.purpose: Provide uninterrupted power services to campus security-safety and environmental systems that support operations to: 3 schools, Jewish Community Center, Adult Learning, Senior programming, Holocaust Memorial Resource Education Center) directly supporting 2-counties area residents. Actively supporting area Emergency First Responders (Police, Fire-Rescue) serving as an "as needed" staging/first responder multi-day center during extended critical incidents / hurricanes (all-hazards) when power infr
2647.activities: A selected contractor/integrator will design/engineer a natural gas-based back-up power generation plan that will supply 3-transformers and then submit an engineering design plan to City/County permitting. Upon permitting approval, contractor will then install & integrate GREEN-FUELED Natural Gas-Based campus-wide Rapid Emergency Back-Up Power-Generator System. *Note that campus is natural gas-fed for existing systems. Contractor will additionally provide formal testing of the system and trainin
2647.direct_services: Funding will directly afford ability to provide services to 3-schools, a Jewish Community Center, Adult Learning Programming, Senior Programming, Neurodiverse Adult & Children Training Center and Special Community Events for Orange and Seminole County area residents. Project will actively support area Emergency First Responders providing an "as needed" Area Staging Center & First Responder Housing
2647.population: Residents of Orange & Seminole Counties will be directly served by this sustainment project as well as those throughout Central Florida who frequent the Holocaust Memorial Resource and Education Center. Specifically, 1500 residents who are campus student-families/members, and the 51,000 Jewish residents of Central Florida who are served by varying Shalom Orlando support programs throughout the Greater Orlando area.
2647.outcome: Please note that this campus hosts (3) active schools. The ability to drop a child off at pre-K, K-5 or Brooke House Academy schools affords families to go to work in lieu of staying home with their children. This directly affects family's ability to maintain income/self-support. This does not include the 200+ campus staff members gainfully employed as primary service members, nor does it include staff of the (2) Neurodiverse Training-Counseling programs & Center. This sustainment project benefits the gainfully employed families dependent on their child's school's ability to remain open, staff to be working and training/counseling programs to train neo diverse adults for the workplace. Measu

2648.description: Harm reduction and raising awareness for mental health, specifically addiction. This program focuses on saving lives and educating the community about the dangers of fentanyl by providing personal education and lifesaving technology. The goal is to decrease the number of fentanyl and opioid related deaths, which has already claimed over 1 million American lives in the past decade.
2648.purpose: Improve physical and mental health. Educate the community about the dangers and safety measures of illicit drugs. This directly reduces overdose and drug use, which will save lives. Reduce substance use and educate on the dangers of illicit drugs and prevent individuals from ever starting drug use.
2648.activities: Funds will support the large-scale distribution of Overdose Prevention Kits designed to detect and prevent overdose and overdose-related deaths. Each kit includes five fentanyl test strips and two units of naloxone, paired with clear, evidence-based educational materials on overdose recognition, response, and harm reduction. Largest Heart will educate and equip individuals by distributing 50,000 or more kits annually across five counties through college campuses, high-traffic community events, s
2648.direct_services: Educate the general public, including first responders and law enforcement, by equipping them with the knowledge and tools to make well-informed decisions to reduce overdose, hospitalizations, and deaths. Provide 50,000 + Overdose Prevention Kits at events, community partnerships, and through the mail. Equip our community with the life- saving tools to prevent opioid and fentanyl overdose and deat
2648.population: The target population for this project includes individuals at elevated risk of opioid overdose and substance-related harm, including individuals with substance use and co-occurring mental health disorders, and community members impacted by the opioid crisis, with a particular focus on underserved, high-risk populations such as young adults, college students, individuals recently released from incarceration, and those experiencing housing instability. Through expanded harm-reduction education, o
2648.outcome: The simple answer: saving lives. The expected outcomes of this project include reduced overdose risk and substance- related harm among individuals served; increased access to life-saving overdose prevention tools; improved knowledge of overdose recognition and response; and strengthened community capacity to prevent overdose-related fatalities across the five-county service area. Outcomes will be measured through standardized data collection and performance tracking, including the number of unduplicated individuals served; overdose prevention trainings completed; naloxone kits and fentanyl test strips distributed; self-reported overdose reversals; and pre- and post- training knowledge assess

2633.description: CEO Financial Literacy Academy provides financial literacy education, workforce readiness, employment skills, and re-entry support to underserved youth, families, and returning citizens. Funds will expand budgeting/credit training, job-readiness workshops, employer partnerships, healthcare navigation, and diversion/re-entry services to increase employment, financial stability, and economic mobility across Miami Dade County and Florida.
2633.purpose: The funds will expand CEO Financial Literacy Academy’s financial literacy, workforce readiness, and re-entry support programs that equip underserved youth, adults, and returning citizens with the essential skills needed to achieve financial stability and long-term economic mobility. The goal is to increase employment, improve credit outcomes, reduce recidivism, and strengthen participants’ ability to successfully budget, save, manage debt, access banking, and transition into sustainable career p
2633.activities: Services include financial literacy classes (budgeting, credit building, banking, investing, debt management), workforce development workshops (résumé building, interviewing, professionalism, soft-skills training), re-entry support (case management, employment placement, identification assistance), diversion programming, college and career readiness activities, employer partnerships, job placement assistance, certification pathways, youth mentorship, transportation support, and healthcare naviga
2633.direct_services: Direct services include financial coaching, credit rebuilding support, budgeting assistance, job placement, employability training, career pathway planning, youth development workshops, re-entry and diversion support, access to banking and financial tools, career tours, mentorship, and one-on-one case management. These services are provided in person, online, and through community partner sites to
2633.population: Target populations include underserved youth ages 13–24, low-income families, individuals facing financial hardship, returning citizens, adults needing workforce training, and residents of high-poverty neighborhoods in Miami-Dade County and surrounding areas. The project will serve an estimated 100–200 individuals annually, with a focus on communities lacking access to financial education, employment resources, and stability-building services.
2633.outcome: Expected outcomes include increased employment, improved credit scores, reduced debt, increased financial literacy, decreased recidivism, greater access to banking, and higher levels of workforce participation. Outcomes will be measured using pre- and post-assessments, credit score tracking (with consent), employment placement data, income improvements, attendance logs, case management progress notes, certification completions, employer feedback, and 3-, 6-, and 12- month follow-up evaluations. These metrics ensure accountability and demonstrate measurable financial and workforce gains.

2755.description: The mission of FAU's SeaTech campus is to provide an environment for advanced engineering research and technology development aimed at solving problems in the ocean. The campus has a seawall that is located adjacent to the Stranahan River and is in critical need of repair. This seawall, which experiences frequent boat wake activity from passing vessels, serves for berthing of BoatUS vessels as well as a platform for FAU students to conduct their research. The funds would repair widespread cracking and breaks, as well as address corrosion of the seawall in multiple areas identified as being in critical condition.
2755.purpose: To repair the needs of the structural condition of the seawall located at FAU's SeaTech Campus in Dania Beach, located adjacent to the Stranahan River. This seawall, which experiences frequent boat wake activity from passing vessels, serves for berthing of BoatUS vessels as well as a platform for FAU students to conduct their research. The funds would repair widespread cracking and breaks, as well as address corrosion of the seawall in multiple areas identified as being in critical condition.
2755.activities: Repairing the seawall ensures the safety, stability, and continuity of the research environment at SeaTech. A secure seawall protects research facilities, equipment, and vessels from erosion, flooding, and storm impacts; conditions that are essential for conducting high-quality marine and coastal research, advancing both academic and research collaborations and technology development opportunities
2755.direct_services: This activity provides a direct service to citizens by generating research that supports safer coastal communities. The marine and coastal work conducted at the Seatech campus results in technologies and applications that help protect Florida's shorelines, improve environmental monitoring, support sustainable fisheries, and strengthen disaster preparedness.
2755.population: The project primarily serves Florida Atlantic University SeaTech Campus students, faculty, and researchers in engineering, as well as industry and government research partners who rely on the waterfront facilities for education and applied research, while also benefiting the surrounding Dania Beach community of about ~33,000 residents. Approximately 70 students annually, along with dozens of faculty, staff, and research collaborators, are directly served, with broader indirect benefits to the en
2755.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is the protection and long-term resilience of the FAU SeaTech Campus waterfront infrastructure, ensuring continued access for education, research, and vessel operations while reducing risk from erosion, storm surge, and sea-level rise for both the campus and the surrounding Dania Beach community. Outcomes will be measured through engineering inspections and performance assessments of the repaired seawall, continued uninterrupted campus and research operations, and post-construction monitoring of shoreline stability and infrastructure integrity over time.

3585.description: Her Song offers comprehensive care for victims of human trafficking, including victim outreach, care coordination, and long-term residential survivor care.
3585.purpose: Her Song offers comprehensive care for victims of human trafficking, including victim outreach, care coordination, and long-term residential survivor care.
3585.activities: Victim outreach efforts focus on reaching into the jails and prisons as well as reaching survivors within our community to help meet survivors right where they are, coordinate care to address individual needs, and provide long-term residential care services.
3585.direct_services: Citizens impacted will be survivors of human trafficking, providing trauma-responsive victim outreach, holistic care coordination, and long-term residential survivor care to assist in rebuilding lives and discovering their worth.
3585.outcome: Providing trauma-responsive victim outreach, holistic care coordination, and long-term residential survivor care to assist in rebuilding lives and discovering their worth. The outcome will be measured by the number of victims served and reintroduced into society.

2754.description: The requested funds would allow for the design, construction, certification and permits to build a sewer system extension to serve 30 commercial properties along the main corridor in the City, as well as retire antiquated septic systems that currently serve these properties. Sewering the area will enable tenants to comply with county mandates, allowing them to renew their licenses to operate in the city. The area is bounded by Northeast 162-163 St from Northeast 18 -21 Avenue, in North Miami Beach.
2754.purpose: This project is a septic to sewer conversion project benefiting 30 commercial properties bounded by Northeast 162- 163 streets and form Northeast 18-21 avenues.
2754.activities: Design , permitting and construction of the expansion of the sanitary sewer system to abut these properties currently on septic systems.
2754.direct_services: Extending the sewer system to their property, connecting them to City sewers and abandoning their septic systems.
2754.population: Commercial businesses. approximately 200 businesses and a population of approximately 400-800 employees.
2754.outcome: The economic growth of the currently stagnant status can be measured with the number of Business Tax Receipt or Licenses in this very area. Also the diversity of the types of businesses opening in this corridor can be measured after this project is completed. Growth in this area , as a result of this project's improvement will ultimately create more job opportunities in this sector. Preserve environmental water quality of the nearby Biscayne Bay as well as the water quality of the Biscayne Aquifer.

2753.description: The Highland Village community was originally developed in the 1940’s. In 2004, stormwater system improvements were constructed in the area. However, due to the low elevation of the area/ property, occasional high tide and limited pervious swale spaces, the community has a history of flooding cases during heavy rainfall and king tide events. The funding will assist with the study and construction of a long-term sustainable solution for Highland Village.
2753.purpose: The specific purpose of the requested state funding is to reduce flooding in the Highland Village neighborhood by implementing critical stormwater infrastructure improvements. This funding will support the design, permitting, and construction of drainage enhancements aimed at addressing long- standing flooding issues that have impacted homes, streets, and public safety during heavy rainfall events. The project will increase system capacity, improve water flow, and reduce the frequency and severi
2753.activities: The scope of work includes the installation of backflow preventers to stop water from reversing into the neighborhood during heavy rain events, as well as increasing system capacity by adding new drainage pipes to improve overall flow.
2753.direct_services: This project will directly address persistent flooding issues that impact residential areas as well as key community assets, including the Highland Village Park and Community Center. By mitigating flooding, the project will improve the usability, safety, and long-term preservation of these public spaces, ensuring they remain accessible and functional for residents year-round. In addition to protec
2753.population: The target population is Highland Village area with approximately 3,790 individuals to be served.
2753.outcome: Flooding will be reduced in the Highland Village. After construction is completed, we will perform a study, every 5 years, to make sure the area is not flooding like it use to.

3067.description: The Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County seeks support to upgrade and expand its aging campus-wide security camera system, which is more than 10 years old and operating beyond its intended life cycle. The current system relies on outdated servers and cameras, which no longer meet modern safety standards. As a result, the Center has identified outdoor camera blind spots and coverage gaps in areas where incidents have occurred, limiting the ability to assist local law enforcement with investigations. This project will modernize critical public safety infrastructure by replacing obsolete equipment, expanding camera coverage to approximately 185 cameras, eliminating blind spots and extending video retention from 30 to 60 days. The upgraded system will also enable secure, controlled access for local police and the U.S. Secret Service during high-profile events, s
3067.purpose: The purpose of the requested funds is to replace obsolete security infrastructure and expand camera coverage to improve public safety, strengthen emergency response coordination and support real-time collaboration with law enforcement agencies. Specifically, the project aims to replace a failing, decade-old system and servers, expand camera coverage, eliminate known outdoor blind spots, extend video retention from 30 to 60 days, enable secure access for local police and federal partners, includi
3067.activities: Funds will support the purchase and installation of new security cameras in high-traffic, outdoor and vulnerable campus locations, the integration of cameras into the Center's centralized security monitoring system, and upgrades to data storage and system redundancy to ensure reliable footage retention. These activities will upgrade the Center's safety infrastructure and align it with best practices for large public venues.
3067.direct_services: The project directly benefits the public by providing enhanced safety and security for patrons attending performances and free community events, safer environments for K–12 students, teachers and families participating in arts education programs, improved emergency response during large-scale events and peak visitation periods and increased confidence for residents and tourists visiting downtown M
3067.population: Since the Arsht is open and accessible to the public, this project serves a broad population who utilize the campus, including Miami-Dade County residents and visitors, schoolchildren and educators participating in arts education programs (over 80,000 students annually), families attending free and low-cost community programming, employees, artists and volunteers working on campus, seniors, individuals with disabilities and other vulnerable populations.
3067.outcome: Collectively, the following expected outcomes of the project strengthen downtown Miami as a safe, vibrant destination for residents and visitors alike. Expected outcomes include increased campus safety and reduced security incidents, faster detection, response and resolution of incidents, enhanced coordination with law enforcement during emergencies, greater public confidence in attending events at the Arsht and improved protection of a major cultural and economic asset.

2634.description: The Institute for Freedom in the Americas supports curriculum and exhibitions at the Freedom Tower to narrate the story of the search for freedom, explore the plight caused by communism, and educate future generations on its historical, cultural, and societal impact. It fosters freedom through civic engagement, global dialogue, and a Fellowship program for students to learn from Latin American leaders via academic studies, workshops, and interactions with leaders from the Western Hemisphere. Established in 2024 under Florida Statute 1004.89, it advances democracy and human rights.
2634.purpose: The specific purpose of the Institute for Freedom in the Americas is to educate and inspire future generations by narrating the search for freedom and examining the societal impacts of communism. Through its curriculum, exhibitions, and Fellowship program, the Institute aims to preserve the historical significance of the Freedom Tower, foster civic engagement, and empower emerging leaders from Latin America and the Caribbean to advance governance, human rights, and democratic values in the Ameri
2634.activities: The funds will support developing curriculum and exhibitions at the Freedom Tower to explore the plight caused by communism. The Institute will offer a Fellowship program featuring academic studies, hands-on workshops, and mentorship from leaders in governance. Additionally, it will host events, foster global dialogue, and build partnerships to advance democratic principles and civic engagement across the Americas.
2634.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services to students, including access to educational programs, exhibitions, and resources at the Freedom Tower. It will also offer a Fellowship program with academic studies, hands- on workshops, and mentorship opportunities, empowering students to engage with democratic principles, governance, and civic leadership. These services will prepare student
2634.population: The target population of 2.8 million residents in Miami Dade County in addition all students throughout the State of Florida.
2634.outcome: The project aims to foster understanding of freedom and democracy, highlight the Freedom Tower's significance, and empower future leaders. Outcomes will be measured through attendance records, participant surveys, Fellowship enrollment, alumni success tracking, and pre- and post-program evaluations.

2640.organization: Jacksonville Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma
2640.description: JAC DST will implement its Five-Point Programmatic Thrust of Educational Development, Economic Development, International Awareness and Involvement, Physical and Mental Health, and Community Awareness and Involvement to empower 800 at-risk youth and economically disadvantaged residents in Duval County. Through comprehensive educational programs, mentorship, and leadership development initiatives, the project aims to improve academic achievement, build self-confidence, and prepare youth to become engaged, informed leaders within their communities.
2640.purpose: The goal of JAC's DST Five-Point Programmatic Thrust of Educational Development, Economic Development, International Awareness and Involvement, Physical and Mental Health, and Community Awareness and Involvement is to empower 800 at-risk youth and economically disadvantaged residents in Duval County through educational programs, mentorship, and leadership development to improve academic success, build confidence, and prepare youth to become engaged leaders in their communities.
2640.activities: The project provides mentoring, college and career readiness, health education, and leadership development. Activities include financial literacy, wellness training, scholarships, health fairs, and voter registration. For 79 years, it has helped economically disadvantaged Duval County residents achieve educational and social advancement.
2640.direct_services: Funding will support direct services for 800 at-risk youth and economically disadvantaged Duval County residents, including mentoring, educational workshops, financial literacy, health screenings, career readiness, college tours, and civic engagement. Services will be delivered through school partnerships and outreach to promote whole-person development.
2640.population: The project will serve 800 at-risk youth and economically disadvantaged persons in Duval County.
2640.outcome: The primary outcome of this project is improved overall well-being among participants, demonstrated through healthier lifestyle habits, greater emotional resilience and mental health awareness, and measurable academic gains such as higher GPAs or completion of grade-level benchmarks. This outcome will be achieved through a comprehensive methodology that combines wellness programs, mental health workshops, peer support activities, and educational interventions such as tutoring, mentoring, and college readiness sessions.

2721.description: State governments asked to donate to the Military Women’s Memorial (MWM) in tribute to women who have served/are serving. Each state that donates is listed on the MWM Honor Roll of States. In the 1990's, thousands of women veterans/volunteers successfully garnered financial support from their states for MWM, meeting with state legislators, governors, and staff to promote state legislation authorizing donations, special state grants and donations from Governor's Funds. Florida was the FIRST state to contribute to the Military Women's Memorial in July 1990 and again in August 1999 for a total of $115,999. Florida contributed the the LARGEST sum of any state in support of the STATE DONATION PROGRAM. Now, 25 years later, the Memorial endeavors to update the technology and digital outreach to Florida women veterans and educational entities.
2721.purpose: Conduct significant outreach and education in Florida highlighting the service and courage of Florida's servicewomen - past and present. Encourage the next generation of Floridians to also reach for the stars with extensive marketing of the Memorial's educational program entitled "One Small Step for Women: American Servicewomen in the Space Race."
2721.activities: Capital Funds will be used for the stunning visitor experience upgrades at the Military Women's Memorial. Florida will receive top tier recognition as one of the states that has contributed the most. Renovation Designs provided by Gallagher & Associates - the firm that designed the World War Two Museum in New Orleans. https://gallagherdesign.com/
2721.direct_services: Funds will be used to highlight military women in Florida and the National Registry. Goal is to add at least 1,000 new stories in National Archive. MWM's Living Legend Proclamations will be presented to Florida's women veterans that reach the age of 100. Collaborate with Elected Officials to participate in these local "hometown" good news stories. Memorial Staff will attend numerous events in Flor
2721.population: The target population is K-12 as well as adults of every generation! Visitors to the Memorial at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery are in excess of 250,000 annually and more than 200,000 visit the website for the education materials and 360 degree virtual tour - https://virtual-tours.womensmemorial.org/
2721.outcome: Increase America's recognition of military women - from the Revolutionary War to today. The State Challenge of "Strive for 500" encourages EVERY state to assist in adding at least 500 new women's stories into the Memorial's nationally acclaimed REGISTER. In 2025, Florida added 684 new stories - but with this funding we can achieve more than 1,000 in 2026!

2801.description: The City of Daytona Beach Shores is a small coastal community on the Volusia County barrier island bordered by the Atlantic Ocean on the east and the Halifax River on the west. This project involves purchasing a mobile stormwater infrastructure unit to allow the quick removal of debris and blockages from underground infrastructure lines through a non-destructive, soft digging method reducing the risk of underground utility damages. The unit will be used throughout the city and county to enhance public safety before, during, and after storms and rain events.
2801.purpose: The funds will be used to obtain a mobile stormwater infrastructure unit to allow for quick removal of debris and blockages from underground infrastructure lines. The unit employs a non-destructive, soft digging method to reduce the risk of underground utility damages and will be used throughout the city and county to enhance public safety during storms and rain events.
2801.activities: The mobile stormwater infrastructure will be used to provide preventative maintenance and response to the city's stormwater system prior to and after a hurricane, tropical storm or other flood event.
2801.direct_services: The mobile stormwater infrastructure will be used to provide preventative maintenance and response to the city's stormwater system prior to and after a hurricane, tropical storm or other flood event.
2801.population: The residents, businesses and visitors of Daytona Beach Shores will be positively impacted by this project. The number of individuals expected to be served includes the residential population of approximately 5,200 along with an additional 5,000 to 10,000 visitors.
2801.outcome: The expected benefit of this project will be to minimize flooding from hurricanes, tropical storms or other flood events. Success will be measured by the number of retention ponds and linear footage of stormwater pipes cleaned prior to storms and reduced damage of local structures from flooding due to removed blockages.

2802.description: Hurricane Milton brought severe rainfall and surface flooding to Lake Helen between October 5 and November 2, 2024, causing significant damage to local infrastructure. Roads along Church Street and Pennsylvania Avenue experienced embankment erosion, culvert and channel failures, and heavy sediment deposition, compromising safe access for residents and emergency services. This appropriation will fund critical repairs to damaged roadways, upgrade drainage systems, and stabilize embankments to restore reliable transportation routes. These improvements will also enhance resilience against future flooding events, protecting public safety and reducing long-term maintenance costs. By addressing structural vulnerabilities and improving stormwater management, this project ensures Lake Helen's infrastructure can withstand extreme weather and maintain essential connectivity for the community.
2802.purpose: Restore safe and reliable transportation routes in Lake Helen by repairing storm-damaged roads, upgrading drainage systems, and stabilizing embankments. These improvements will reduce flood risk, protect public safety, and enhance long-term infrastructure resilience against future severe weather events.
2802.activities: The project will deliver comprehensive engineering design, construction services for roadway repair and drainage upgrades, embankment stabilization, and project oversight to ensure resilience and public safety.
2802.direct_services: This project will provide citizens with safe and reliable transportation routes, improved flood protection through upgraded drainage systems, and enhanced public safety during severe weather events.
2802.population: Lake Helen has a population of approximately 2,800 residents, and when factoring in commuters, emergency services, and local businesses, the project is expected to directly benefit over 3,000 individuals by restoring safe and reliable infrastructure.
2802.outcome: The project will deliver restored transportation routes, improved drainage, and enhanced flood resilience, with success measured by completed repairs, increased drainage capacity, and reduced flood incidents verified through engineering inspections and post-storm performance data.

2803.description: Properties along Canal Avenue in Oak Hill, FL have been impacted by past hurricane event, most recently by hurricanes Ian and Milton. Additionally the during those events and other intense rain events the Canal Avenue gets inundated from runoff on the north side of the road. The improvement along Canal Avenue will address drainage deficiencies along the north side of Canal Ave and establish a drainage connection to the properties on the west end of Canal Ave.
2803.purpose: Improve the drainage along Canal Avenue from US 1 to River Road. The improvements will reduce the building flood risk at the west end of Canal Avenue near US1 and reduce the risk of road over topping at the east end of Canal Avenue. The project will be achieved by creating a drainage connection to the isolated properties at the west end of Canal Avenue and installing a cross-drain at the east end of Canal Avenue. The existing culverts along the length of Canal Avenue will also be replaced.
2803.activities: Services and activities include the construction of drainage improvements along Canal Avenue from US1 to River Road
2803.direct_services: These improvements will benefit the surrounding area adjacent to Canal Avenue by reducing the risk of property and building flooding. The project will also improve the safety of driving on Canal Avenue by reducing road inundation during storm events
2803.population: The targeted population is residents and businesses adjacent to Canal Avenue, estimated to be over 20 properties. In addition, the project will provide a benefit to users of Canal Avenue by improving the safety of traveling on Canal Avenue during rain events
2803.outcome: The project will reduce the risk of building flooding and make Canal Avenue more safe by reducing flooding that over tops the road. After construction is complete the area will be monitored during storm events to evaluate the effectiveness of the improvements.

2844.description: Fire Station 18 is an essential investment for the City of Fort Myers (City). Designed to fill an emergency response deficit within the jurisdiction, the addition of this facility would decrease corridor response times by as much as 50%. The station would remain an environmentally efficient investment within the City and support key initiatives to ensure responder health and cancer prevention treatments. Fire Station 18 will also support a multi-jurisdictional response.
2844.purpose: The funds will be used to establish a needed public safety facility and fill an emergency response deficit eithin the jurisdiction.
2844.activities: Additional fire protection services would be established at the facility, which would continue to serve an unreached corridor within the City of Fort Myers.
2844.direct_services: Fire protection and suppression service, continued hazmat and public safety protection, and efficient responses to natural disasters.
2844.population: The City of Fort Myers, specifically ward 6 will benefit from this project. However, the City of Fort Myers participates in a multi-jurisdictional response within the region which extends to 10 counties within southwest Florida. This increase will allow for extended multi-jurisdictional response to occur.
2844.outcome: Decrease in response times will measure the increased safety and protection of residents within the city.

2811.organization: Villages of South Florida Autism, Inc.
2811.description: Development of a shared living community for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, consisting of up to four 6-bedroom homes designed to provide greater autonomy than traditional community-based group homes and maximize self help/independent living skills. The development of this program on the site of an enriched independent living community addresses federal mandates to transition individuals with IDD, from facility-based settings to community based settings, while providing vocational, educational, and recreational enrichment, inclusion, and opportunities to enhance connectedness, integration, and self sufficiency within the community.
2811.purpose: The requested funds will support the creation of an Assisted Living Facility designed to meet the unique needs of adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD). Our goal is to provide 24/7 supervision while fostering independence and complying with federal mandates aimed at transitioning individuals with IDD from facility-based settings to community-based ones. In doing so, we aim to offer educational and recreational enrichment, promote inclusion, and create opportunities for en
2811.activities: A) Predevelopment activities may include but not limited to survey, architecture, engineering, permitting, funding applications, and other pre-construction activities. B) Construction activities may include but not be limited to Site Preparation, Excavation, Grading, Structural, Window and Door Installation, Plumbing, Electrical, HVAC Systems, Insulation, Drywall and Ceiling Installation, Flooring, Cabinetry and Fixtures Installation, Interior and Exterior Painting, Safety System Installation (F
2811.direct_services: Services will include 24/7 Supervision as needed, daily living skills assistance and training, Residential Habilitation services, educational enrichment, on-site recreational activities, and planned activities such as shopping, dining out, going to movies and other recreational and leisure opportunities to enhance connectedness, integration, and self sufficiency.
2811.population: Individuals served by this funding will include 24 adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities who require 24/7 supervision but who will benefit from living in an environment that maximizes their potential for independence and self determination.
2811.outcome: This project will develop best practices strategies to ensure residents are provides with a safe and secure environment and receive the training they require to maximize their self-help/independent living skills. This project will be programmatically designed to maximize opportunities for community integration and improve the quality of life of its residents.

2922.description: Law enforcement officers are routinely exposed to high-decibel environments from firearms training to tactical operations that can cause permanent hearing damage and degrade situational awareness. The Soundgear Shield is state of the art active hearing protection that prevents hearing loss and enhances communication.
2922.purpose: The funds will be utilized to provide state of the art hearing protection to sworn law enforcement officers in Florida Sheriff's offices. Use of hearing protection can reduce the risk of hearling loss.
2922.activities: The funds will be utilized to provide state of the art hearing protection to sworn law enforcement officers in Florida Sheriff's offices.
2922.direct_services: Sworn law enforcement officers will receive state of the art hearing protection on a first come first service basis. Noise is a significant hazard for LEO and first responders. 71% of officers report hearing loss compared to just 15% of adults. Limiting the risk of hearing loss and auditory injuries is critical for health and readiness of Florida's law enforcement officers.
2922.outcome: Sworn law enforcement officers will receive state of the art hearing protection on a first come first service basis. Noise is a significant hazard for LEO and first responders. 71% of officers report hearing loss compared to just 15% of adults. Limiting the risk of hearing loss and auditory injuries is critical for health and readiness of Florida's law enforcement officers hearing loss. This will ultimately save the state money in healthcare costs.

2846.description: The Calusa Nature Center houses the largest open green space in the City of Fort Myers. A pinnacle area for outdoor recreation and participation, the City has begun a comprehensive restoration project that would repair trails and boardwalks for safe, multi-modal recreation and continued utilization of this City-owned green space for years to come. The investment from the state would support the reconstruction of the boardwalk to allow for safe trail usage through the nature preserve.
2846.purpose: The funds will be used to reconstruct a debilitated boardwalk which is an essential component of outdoor recreation in the city's largest green space.
2846.activities: The funds will be used for design and construction to ensure resident safety and connectivity with trails.
2846.direct_services: Citizens will be provided with increased opportunity for outdoor recreation consistent with the State of Florida's Outdoor Recreation Plan.
2846.population: Residents and visitors of the City of Fort Myers who engage with recreational opportunities provided by the Calusa Nature Center and Planetarium.
2846.outcome: The reconstruction of the boardwalk will provide additional 1,776 feet of safe passage to the City of Fort Myers trail network.

2847.description: In line with the State’s efforts to eliminate surface water discharge and to serve the rapidly expanding Fort Myers population, the City is expanding the Central Wastewater Treatment Plant from 6 million gallon per day (mgd) reclaimed water production facility to an 11 mgd facility. In addition to a new filter feed pump station, upgrades to the existing chlorine contact basin, and new piping, the new installation will be capable of treating all influent flows to a high-level disinfection and filtration.
2847.purpose: The project will increase the reliability of the City’s Advanced Waste Water Treatment Facility ability to aid in eliminating the surface water discharge from the facility and make up to 8.0 mgd of additional reclaimed water available to offset potable water demands for irrigation and industrial use. This project is essential to the City of Fort Myers to provide adequate wastewater resiliency for the community. The project will mitigate bacteriological hazards that may come with improper wastewa
2847.activities: Essential infrastructure advancement that will increase the capacity of the water production facility to 11 mgd.
2847.direct_services: The expansion of reclaimed water production capacity will provide increased water supply for irrigation and make more of the City’s potable water available for critical use. Improving the operational capacity of wastewater systems, including the construction and installation of resilient wastewater infrastructure is crucial to protecting people and the environment.
2847.population: The direct beneficiaries of this project are the 59,075 utilities customers that currently utilize this system.
2847.outcome: The project will directly benefit Low to Moderate income area within the City of Fort Myers providing critical infrastructure advancements to an area which is 54.8% LMI. This will be measured by the amount of LMI homes that are connected to the waster water system.

2925.description: This initiative, led by the Lauderhill Police Department, aims to reduce violent crime, strengthen investigations, and improve community safety through the purchase and deployment of fixed automated License Plate Readers (LPRs) at key intersections. The project will enhance real-time crime data sharing, emergency response times, and inter-agency collaboration. It will directly benefit over 800 residents, including at-risk youth, crime victims, and economically disadvantaged populations. The project emphasizes measurable outcomes such as reduced crime rates, improved citizen safety perception, and increased public trust.
2925.purpose: The primary goal of the LPD's Violence reduction initiative is to reduce rising violent crime in the City, and increase its capacity to investigate, prosecute and prevent its recurrence to keep its residents safe and provide justice to victims and survivors. Specifically, the purchase of License Plate Readers (LPRs) will increase public safety, investigative capabilities, and crime prevention. LPRs provide real time alerts, increase situational information, track suspects and identify criminals.
2925.activities: It is the mission of the LPD to enhance the quality of life of its citizens and keep them safe. The proposed funds will provide direct and indirect services to the citizens by increasing emergency response times, deterring criminal activity, provide enhanced safety in neighborhoods and roadways, and conduct effective and timely investigations to take dangerous criminals off the streets.
2925.direct_services: The Citizens will have enhanced security and peace of mind to live fuller lives to pursue their goals without worrying about their immediate safety. LPRs can identify and track suspect vehicles in real time, deterring criminals. Citizens will be directly protected from burglaries, assaults, abductions using vehicles; prevent car thefts; and effectively locate missing or abducted persons timely.
2925.population: All residents of the city of Lauderhill.
2925.outcome: Reduce crime in the City of Lauderhill, assist neighboring law enforcement agencies and increase citizen safety, improve their quality of life, and bolster public trust. The LPD Crime analyst maps crime details by type, number, recurrence, hotspots, etc. The baseline data of established parameters will be compared at regular intervals, after deploying the License Plate Readers at strategic locations that are a deterrent. Enhanced public trust and citizen perception of safety will be measured via surveys administered at HOA meetings, PTA, or religious gatherings.

3263.description: The Homosassa River Restoration Project (HRRP) is aimed at restoring, protecting and preserving the water quality and critical habitat in our Outstanding Florida Waterway. The project continues to focus its strategy to restore, protect, and preserve the ecosystem through eelgrass restoration. As a result of our restoration, the Homosassa River is one of the few areas in the United States to have the manatee thriving as a result of a surplus of eelgrass.
3263.purpose: These funds will restore a critical habitat that is designated as an Outstanding Florida Waterway. This project will also help local governments and agencies to meet a variety water quality improvement mandates (SWIM plans, BMAP plans, Comp plans, etc.) through the reduction of phosphorus and nitrogen
3263.activities: The majority of the funds are spent on vacuum removal of the detrital material (muck/lyngbya), installing plants (SAV), then monitor and maintain the SAV and cages for a full year after the installation. A project evaluation study from a third party biologist is performed to confirm that sufficient substrate removal occurred to insure plant survivability post restoration. The study will provide an assessment of restoration success or impairment through a statistical analyses of pre and post rest
3263.direct_services: The tourism industry is one of the largest economic drivers in the region. The loss of Water Quality (clarity) associated with current conditions and degrading habitat conditions could potentially cause a collapse of this economy. Improvements proposed by this project will help to improve and maintain condition's for which residents, local, regional, national, international tourists come to expect
3263.population: The citizens and the economy of the State of Florida , Citrus County, and Homosassa. Citrus County enjoys > 500,000 local,national and international visitors per year, which contribute a significant amount in sales tax and tourism related jobs
3263.outcome: The anticipated outcome is the overall improvement in the water quality and a thriving ecosystem as demonstrated by our project study performed pre and post restoration by an independent biologist

3264.description: This local funding initiative request is for the construction of the Halls River Road Multi-Use Path, which is a paved asphalt path, varying in width from 6 to 12 feet along Halls River Road in Homosassa. If funded, this approximately 3.2 mile path will enhance pedestrian and bicyclist safety, improve multi-modal connectivity, and support continued economic growth in Citrus County. This path will serve as a critical linkage between multiple residential communities and key local destinations, including restaurants, retail centers, and commercial establishments located along the corridor.
3264.purpose: This Local Funding Initiative Request will be for the construction of a paved asphalt multi-use path along Halls River Road in Homosassa, FL. This path will originate at South Riverview Circle and will travel 3.2 miles until finally terminating at U.S. Highway 19 where it will connect with another recently constructed multi-use path along that highway. This will serve as a major linkage between multiple residential communities and key local destinations, including restaurants, retail centers, an
3264.activities: The requested funds will be used for CA/CEI/Testing Services as well as construction of a multi-use path along Halls River Road.
