The Florida Department of Transportation will also oversee and manage the construction process with the goal of providing a safe, accessible, and dedicated facility for pedestrians and bicyclists, thereby enhancing multi- modal connectivity.
3264.direct_services: With the construction of the above described multi-use path, Citrus County residents and tourists will be able to realize improved roadway safety and additional bike/pedestrian facilities.
3264.population: The target population served by this project is all of Citrus County's more than 160,000 residents as well as tourists. As mentioned above, this multi-use path will link multiple residential communities with key local restaurants, retail centers, and commercial establishments located along the corridor. Thus, the completion of this project will promote active transportation options, improve roadway safety, and foster economic development through improved access to local businesses.
3264.outcome: If funded, this project would come with numerous benefits for residents, such as improvements to physical health, improvements to mental health, improvements to transportation conditions, improvements to economic activity, increases in area tourism, and increased protection of the general public from harm by allowing pedestrians to utilize a separate transportation facility from the road. These benefits can be measured through analyzing changes in traffic crash data as well as collecting data from users both before and after construction of the path.

2835.description: Implement and deploy a statewide educational technology inventory dashboard and clearinghouse. Provide clarity and transparency to students and families of all technology being used that has accesses to their student personally identifiable information (PII). Flag any student data privacy or security vulnerabilities with tools being used in school districts. Provide real time access for parents and guardians to public dashboard of all educational technology products being used. Provide financial ROI analysis of educational technology tools being used in public school districts.
2835.purpose: Implement and deploy a statewide educational technology inventory dashboard and clearinghouse. Provide clarity and transparency to students and families of all technology being used that has accesses to the students personally identifiable information (PII). Flag any student data privacy or security vulnerabilities with tools being used in school districts. Provide financial ROI analysis of educational technology tools being used in public school districts.
2835.activities: - Real time inventory dashboard of all technology tools being used in Florida public school districts - Technologies that present data privacy and security vulnerabilities and risk for students - Financial ROI analysis of usage and cost of technology tools being used in public school districts
2835.direct_services: - Real time inventory dashboard of all technology tools being used in Florida public school districts - Technologies that present data privacy and security vulnerabilities and risk for students - Financial ROI analysis of usage and cost of technology tools being used in public school districts
2835.population: Public education students, parents and guardians, public education administrators, executives, teachers and support staff.
2835.outcome: Identify education technology tools that present data privacy and security risks, reduce spending on duplicative technology tools, ROI analysis on education technology tools.

3498.description: Convert and expand an unused building into a 3200 square foot transitional housing facility on Refuge House property. It will offer two kitchens, a communal living area, two dining areas, two large family dorms, and six bedrooms with shared bathrooms. The building will be designed to meet the trauma related mental health concerns of women and children who have experienced violence. The program will be designed to address symptoms of Post Traumatic Stress Disorder and will provide a therapeutic environment for children with trauma induced sensory processing disorder. All aspects of the architecture provide for special needs children, and a sensory calming room will be available for those with Autism and ADHD. There will be a designated group counseling room for adults and a play therapy room for children. We will construct a new playground for outdoor recreation. This project will serve r
3498.purpose: Renovation and expansion of a residential building that will add 20 new beds for victims of domestic and sexual violence. Building design will be trauma informed and will meet the needs of neurodivergent children with sensory friendly accommodations throughout. The building will offer counseling rooms, living areas, and shared bathrooms. Group therapy room for children. The goal is to decrease the risk of future victimization and prevent homelessness for women and children. Specialized care for
3498.activities: Renovation and expansion of a residential building that will add 20 new beds for victims of domestic and sexual violence. Building design will be trauma informed and will meet the needs of neurodivergent children with sensory friendly accommodations throughout. The building will offer counseling rooms, living areas, and shared bathrooms. There will be a new play ground for outdoor recreation.
3498.direct_services: Safe shelter for 6 months. Wrap around support services for families who have experienced violence. Special focus on the needs of children who have witnessed and experienced abuse and to provide extensive resources for the parent to improve the well-being of the family. Therapy, counseling, case management, job readiness, vocational assistance, parenting support. On-site tutoring for children.
3498.population: The target population is women and children who are at risk of harm and homicide while fleeing from domestic violence. We anticipate that 160 people will receive safe housing and supportive services annually.
3498.outcome: Outcome is to provide safe transitional housing with expanded intake availability. Outcomes will be measured by completion of renovating an existing building to include dorm style sleeping areas for large families and women without children, an additional kitchen and eating area, and expanded living area, and the addition of six new bedrooms with shared bathrooms. The building will be designed with the needs of adults and children who are experiencing Post Traumatic Stress Disorder, and will be sensory friendly for special needs and nuerodivergent children.

3496.description: Recovery Community Centers (RCC) are innovating and delivering a variety of peer recovery support services, building a lasting physical presence in communities. Recovery coaching, telephone recovery support services, all-recovery meetings, and other services are being organized and delivered by trained volunteers and/or paid staff. A growing network of recovery community centers are home to these services as well as a place for community-wide sober social activities, workshops, meetings, and resource connections. This center will link individuals to resources that support their successful community-based recovery. The goal is to unite community partners in one place to reduce the negative effects of untreated mental health and substance use disorder in adults and children. The building will help fill the gap in services, which has been recognized by the WellFlorida Community Health Asses
3496.purpose: Hernando County BOCC has donated land and has agreed to do all the site work and engineering for the property and provide a 6,000 sq ft. pad ready site for the building. Construction costs to include but not limited to designing, planning, engineering, building materials, labor, appliances, furniture and fixtures.
3496.activities: Individual mentoring, support groups, education classes, community awareness training, workforce development, housing assistance, resource and referral services for individuals and family members of adults and youth living with mental illness and substance misuse disorders. In addition, an internships program for those interested in becoming State Certified Recovery Peer Specialists.
3496.direct_services: Certified Recovery Peer Specialists (CRPS) will work with individuals to establish self sufficiency goals. Other community partners will have office space to bring housing, employment and other much needed support services to participants all under one roof.
3496.population: The target population is 40% of Hernando County residents living with mental illness and substance misuse disorders approximately 72,000 residents plus their family members. We currently impact about 4,500 people each year and plan to double that with the expansion of services.
3496.outcome: Improve mental health, improve quality education, improve transportation conditions, increase economic activity, enhance specific individual's self sufficiency, reduce recidivism, reduce substance misuse and criminal/juvenile justice diversion. These outcomes will be measured through quarterly assessments.

2947.description: The Desire Foundation Inc. is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit rooted in service, equity, and community empowerment. Founded in 2020 from a grassroots movement , the organization works to combat food insecurity, improve nutrition access, and support under served families; particularly those living in Central Florida’s food deserts. Through hands-on programs, community partnerships, and a volunteer-driven model, we provide nutritious food and essential resources to individuals facing systemic barriers. To strengthen our infrastructure and expand our capacity, we are seeking operational support for critical staffing, operational and transportation needs. These needs will include the purchase and operation of a delivery truck with insurance and fuel and the purchase of two commercial refrigerators. These resources are vital to sustaining daily operations and ensuring consistent nutritious, fresh, food
2947.purpose: The Desire Foundation Inc. is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit combating food insecurity and improving nutrition access for families in Central Florida’s food deserts. We provide nutritious food and essential resources through community partnerships and volunteer-driven programs. We seek operational support for key staffing and a delivery truck to sustain daily operations and ensure consistent food distribution to underserved families.
2947.activities: TDF will expand food access in Central Florida’s food deserts through weekly pantry distributions, volunteer coordination, community outreach, and distribution of meals, groceries, and essentials. Funding for key staff and a delivery truck will support reliable food transport and increase our capacity to serve more families. Two commercial refrigerators will support storage of perishable items.
2947.direct_services: The appropriation will support weekly pantry distributions and other essentials and expanded outreach in underserved neighborhoods. Staff will provide volunteer coordination and resource navigation, ensuring families in Central Florida’s food deserts receive consistent support and improved food security.
2947.population: The majority of the funds requested will serve a broad and diverse target population, including elderly individuals; persons with poor mental and physical health; jobless and economically disadvantaged individuals; at-risk youth; people experiencing homelessness; individuals with developmental and physical disabilities; drug users receiving health services; preschool, grade school, high school, and university/college students; currently or formerly incarcerated individuals and drug offenders wit
2947.outcome: The program aims to improve both physical and mental health outcomes for participating families. By increasing access to nutrient-dense foods, families will be able to reduce hunger-related symptoms such as fatigue and skipped meals, lower risk factors for diet-related conditions, and support healthier weight and overall physical well-being. In addition, consistent food distributions and home-delivered resources will help reduce stress and anxiety associated with chronic food insecurity, supporting improved mental and emotional health, greater stability, and an increased ability to focus on work, school, and daily responsibilities. The Desire Foundation will measure these outcomes through a

2968.organization: Better Living Solutions Recovery Center, LLC
2968.description: The project will expand a successful 25/26 project to include additional counties, magnify workforce expansion, enhance provider case investigation, and modernize parent, caregiver, and practitioner engagement. The project focuses on children experiencing trauma-induced behavioral health and eating disorders in North Florida (14 counties) with expansion to four additional NW Florida counties, the majority are rural. The project will offer: 1) Enhanced workforce through additional graduate level intern supervision in four clinical areas. 2) Intensive health and behavioral health practitioner support to primary care, behavioral health providers, and other professionals, and including case staffings to assist in client management. 3) Parent, caregiver, school, and practitioner engagement for at-risk youth using a learning/resource collaborative platform.
2968.purpose: Raise awareness and connect services for children experiencing trauma induced behavioral health and eating disorders in 18 counties (most rural). Programs will include: 1) Expanded access to education and resources for parents/caregivers, practitioners and schools with of at-risk children in crisis including rural areas. 2) Enhanced practitioner support and collaboration for complex cases. 3) Workforce expansion including additional graduate intern supervision - interns will also deliver service
2968.activities: 1) Free education and resource flatform targeting parents/caregivers, practitioners and schools with of at-risk children in crisis including rural areas. 2) Enhanced practitioner support and collaboration for complex child trauma and eating disorder cases. 3) Workforce expansion through collegiate and professional intern supervision for practitioner workforce expansion to serve at-risk children and families. Interns will also deliver services.
2968.direct_services: Behavioral health services will be provided by the graduate level interns during their internships and after completion. The proposal covers graduate level intern supervision, not intern wages. Workforce need is evidenced by the University of South Florida launched a BH workforce dashboard showing significant need in NW Florida. The project also includes child case collaboration the importance of
2968.population: The target population includes school aged children (K-12) who may be experiencing behavioral health issues or eating disorders in the initial 14 counties, plus 4 new counties. The approach includes working with parents (through support groups), educators, health care providers and others who interact with children (through outreach and education), as well as graduate level interns in clinical areas that will serve this target population. Expected populations include children in poor mental or p
2968.outcome: Parents, professionals, and educators will learn the importance of integration of medical, nutritional and behavioral health care for sustained recovery with the goal of assessment of all three areas by providers. All parents served will be given a brief and anonymous survey to assess their child's physical and mental health. The project will include data collection regarding waitlists for BH services to demonstrate the need to expand the workforce, creating awareness for parents and professionals to identify and seek help to prevent child crisis. MH clinicians will collaborate with schools for IEP & 504 accommodation meetings when requested by guardian. The intern program will offer more in

2731.description: CMA attracts visitors from throughout the state, US and worldwide, driving tourism and generating substantial economic impact for Florida. A significant portion of our facility has outlived its use, is deteriorating due to deferred maintenance and hurricanes, no longer able to welcome the public. Funds will allow us to demolish and rebuild, welcoming new sea life habitats. The educational programs, conservation efforts, and scientific research benefit the community and add new visitors.
2731.purpose: CMA attracts visitors from throughout the state, US and worldwide, driving tourism and generating substantial economic impact for Florida. A significant portion of our facility has outlived its use, is deteriorating due to deferred maintenance and hurricanes, no longer able to welcome the public. Funds will allow us to demolish and rebuild, welcoming new sea life habitats. The educational programs, conservation efforts, and scientific research benefit the community and add new visitors.
2731.activities: Rescue, rehabilitation and release of marine life is the mission of Clearwater Marine Aquarium. These funds will provide renovation and activation of space that cannot be utilized due to its deterioration. Once complete, the aquarium will use the space to house rescued animals, educate visitors and further the work of conservation of marine life. CMA hosts over 300,000 guests.
2731.direct_services: This space will be used for human and animal interaction as well as a recreational space for children and families designed to reduce stress, improve mental health, promote family interaction and child education/stimulation, conduct and promote marine and environmental conservation, and educate the public on the rescue, rehabilitation and release of marine life.
2731.outcome: Improve Mental Health- Provide stress relief for autistic and neuro-diverse populations; reduce stress and improve visitor well being; improving social connection and well being through nature engagement. Measured by pre and post micro studies, measuring time on site and in sensory friendly spaces, track return visits to restorative places. Enrich Cultural Experience: Increase access to a conservation focused cultural asset, increased knowledge of global environments, species conservation, and their cultural connections. Measured by tracking attendance; Knowledge checks and surveys; Improve quality of education: Visitors gain measurable knowledge of science and conservation topics; Improved

3611.description: Our Corner Respite Program is a community-based initiative that provides safe, structured, and developmentally appropriate respite care for children with autism, ADHD, developmental delays, and other neurodivergent or behavioral support needs. The program supports both children and their families by offering reliable out-of-school care that promotes social, emotional, and behavioral skills development in an inclusive environment by providing consistent, predictable programming that prioritizes child safety, emotional regulation, and caregiver relief.
3611.purpose: The purpose of the funds requested is to help expand operations for Our Corner Respite Program, a structured, community-based respite care service designed to support children with neurodivergence, developmental differences, and related support needs while providing relief and stability for working families and caregivers. The funding will enable the program to maintain safe staffing ratios, provide reliable after-school care and transportation, and deliver consistent, high-quality services that
3611.activities: Funds will support daily after-school respite programming, including supervised care, structured enrichment activities, homework support, and social-emotional skill development. Services will be delivered by trained staff maintaining a 1 staff to 3 student ratio, with additional 1:1 support provided as needed. The program will also provide transportation from school to the program site using a program-owned van, staff training, program oversight, compliance monitoring, and ongoing evaluation to
3611.direct_services: Direct services provided to citizens include safe, supervised respite care for children; structured enrichment and recreational activities; social-emotional and behavioral support; homework assistance; and reliable transportation from school to the program site. Families and caregivers directly benefit through increased access to affordable, dependable care that allows them to maintain employment,
3611.population: The target population includes children with autism, ADHD, developmental delays, and other neurodivergent or behavioral support needs, as well as their families and caregivers. The program will serve children during out-of-school hours, prioritizing families who lack access to affordable, high-quality respite services. The program has a maximum capacity of 15 students at a time, with the ability to serve approximately 30–45 children annually, depending on enrollment patterns and length of partic
3611.outcome: Expected outcomes include reduced caregiver stress, improved child social-emotional regulation, increased consistency in after-school supervision, and improved family stability. Outcomes will be measured through attendance records, staffing ratio compliance, incident reports, caregiver feedback, and documented child progress notes maintained in the program’s electronic health record system. Program leadership will review data regularly to monitor service quality, safety, and effectiveness and to support continuous improvement.

3424.description: The proposed project consists of constructing an 3.25-mile road and 2-mile utility corridor that runs parallel to Hwy 98, west of Hurlburt Field and north of Florosa Elementary and the Florosa Fire Station. The project purpose and goal is to alleviate traffic on US 98, improve access and traffic flow, and provide military access to Hurlburt Field via a proposed west gate. A PD&E study is underway, and the funds requested would provide for the design phase of the project.
3424.purpose: Design and permitting for 100% project construction plans.
3424.direct_services: Design of roadway and utility corridor to provide congestion relief to US 98 and military access to Hurlburt Field via a proposed west gate.
3424.population: The 50,000 averaged daily users of US 98 in western Okaloosa County.

3612.description: The Miss Black Florida USA Scholarship Pageant is a statewide leadership and scholarship program that supports young women’s academic success, personal growth, and mental well-being. The program combines mentorship, professional development, and community service with a focus on emotional resilience, self-confidence, and mental health awareness. By addressing stress, burnout, and access to supportive resources, Miss Black Florida USA empowers participants to succeed academically and serve as advocates for wellness within their communities.
3612.purpose: The purpose of the funds requested is to support the statewide implementation and expansion of the Miss Black Florida USA Scholarship Pageant as a leadership, scholarship, and mental wellness initiative. Funding will support programming that promotes emotional resilience, self-confidence, stress management, and leadership development for young women, while increasing access to scholarships, mentorship, and supportive resources that address mental health challenges and personal development needs.
3612.activities: Funds will support leadership development workshops, mental health and wellness programming, mentorship opportunities, scholarship administration, and statewide pageant and educational events. Activities include workshops focused on emotional resilience, self-esteem, coping skills, stress management, and professional development, as well as community service initiatives and participant engagement events. Programming will be delivered through structured sessions, facilitated workshops, and coordi
3612.direct_services: Direct services provided to citizens include access to leadership training, mental health and wellness education, mentorship, scholarship opportunities, and community engagement programming for young women across Florida. Participants benefit from structured programming that supports emotional well-being, academic and professional growth, and confidence building. Communities benefit through increa
3612.population: The target population includes young women and girls across Florida, particularly those who face financial, social, or systemic barriers to educational and leadership opportunities. The program is expected to serve approximately 100–150 participants annually, including contestants, scholarship recipients, and individuals engaged through leadership, wellness, and community outreach programming.
3612.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved emotional resilience, increased self-confidence, enhanced leadership skills, and greater awareness of mental health and wellness practices among participants. Additional outcomes include increased access to educational resources and scholarships. Outcomes will be measured through participant surveys, attendance records, program completion data, scholarship distribution tracking, and qualitative feedback collected following workshops and events. Program leadership will review data regularly to assess effectiveness and guide continuous improvement.

3214.description: The current development of over 5,000 single-family homes north of Highway 20 in Freeport has led to demand for a second Wastewater Treatment Plant north of Highway 20 on property purchased by the City of Freeport. The demand for sewer service to those homes under construction necessitates the immediate construction of a 500,000 GPD WWTP on the property that was purchased in 2021. The City is currently waiting on design completion.
3214.purpose: A new wastewater treatment plant is needed to accommodate the tremendous growth in Freeport. A new, more efficient wastewater system is needed to meet the growth demands of the City.
3214.activities: A new wastewater treatment plant will allow for growth over the new 20-30 years and the increased capacity will improve overall wastewater management.
3214.direct_services: The funding will be used for construction of 500,000 GPD sewer plant buildings.
3214.population: The general population of the City of Freeport and their service area is the target population and is greater than 800 individuals.
3214.outcome: More residents will be able to live in the City due to the increased capacity offered by the new wastewater treatment plant. This impact will be measured by the population growth of the City of Freeport.

3034.description: Expand Holocaust Heroes Worldwide TRIBES Project to provide comprehensive weekly support to Holocaust Survivors living in Broward, Miami-Dade, and Palm Beach counties. Funding will provide social engagement programs, trauma- informed companionship services, and proactive health management to reduce loneliness and depression among survivors. Each TRIBE consists of 4-5 volunteer families providing weekly phone calls, monthly in-person visits, essential deliveries (groceries, medication), and companionship support. With this continued funding, we will maintain current services and reduce our waitlist to serve additional survivors.
3034.purpose: Funding will provide social engagement programs, increase companionship and support to survivors via the TRIBE Project. Over the last seven years, we have built a large volunteer community that has enriched the lives of more than 150 Holocaust survivors. With this funding we will be able to reduce our wait list
3034.activities: Providing social engagement and trauma-informed volunteer companionship services to Holocaust survivors to combat loneliness and depression via the TRIBES Project. Each survivor will receive weekly essential services from TRIBES volunteers
3034.direct_services: TRIBES Project volunteers will provide practical, emotional core services of weekly phone calls, monthly in-person visits, make essential deliveries (groceries, medicine, etc.), while also providing companionship, family-structure and cultural connections. Community events will be geared towards Survivors.
3034.population: The target population includes elderly persons, persons with poor mental health, and persons with poor physical health. Expected to serve more than 101-200 individuals.
3034.outcome: Improve physical health, mental health, enrich cultural experience, and improve quality of education to combat anti- semitism. HHW will provide quantitative tracking of Tribe volunteer key details and periodic reports on activities with Survivors; Tribe members structured weekly reporting; number of Survivors participating in community events; along with anecdotal information collected in Tribe member reports, as well as voluntary testimonials from volunteer family members and Survivors themselves.

3218.description: A new water storage tank and well is needed to ensure sufficient water is available for all existing and future uses of the City’s water system. The expanded infrastructure will enhance resiliency, prepare for future demand and is needed for additional storage, fire protection and sustaining sufficient water pressure.
3218.purpose: A new water storage tank and well is needed to ensure sufficient water is available for all existing and future uses of the City’s water system. The expanded infrastructure will enhance resiliency, prepare for future demand and is needed for additional storage, fire protection and sustaining sufficient water pressure.
3218.activities: Construction of a new water storage tank and well.
3218.direct_services: The project will provide drinking water and fire protection water during emergencies to both residential and commercial expansion to the eastern part of the City.
3218.population: The general public is the target population including homes and businesses that are being constructed on the East side of the City. This number is expected to be greater than 800.
3218.outcome: Ensure a continuous supply of water for all existing and future uses of the City’s water system. The impact will be an observable increase in access to residential and commercial users.

3219.description: Active shooters are targeting our most innocent and vulnerable citizens. Criminals know schools throughout our state are "soft targets." This program will train, equip, and prepare Florida's law enforcement community to respond to active shooter events. The program will include live scenario training to ensure our law enforcement officers are prepared in the event of an active shooter emergency. This program will provide curriculum for HR/Active Shooter and past performance training for law enforcement and SWAT. The program should take place at a facility that bust be ITAR compliant, possess an active Florida State ATF License, possess an active Federal ATF License, and have authorized air space for weaponized drones training (up to four hundred AGL)
3219.purpose: This program will provide curriculum for HR/Active Shooter and past performance training for law enforcement and SWAT. The program should take place at a facility that must be ITAR compliant, possess an active Florida State ATF License, possess an active Federal ATF License, and have authorized air space for weaponized drones training (up to four hundred AGL)
3219.activities: Full training facility access and instruction delivered by veteran Special Operators to conduct active shooter response courses. On site lodging, targets, ammunition, UTM bolts and ammo, range supplies, role players, and all other requirements to conduct the most realistic active shooter scenarios available. Participating departments shall be chosen by FDLE on a first come first serve basis.
3219.direct_services: Active shooters are targeting our most innocent, most vulnerable citizens. Criminals know schools and other locations in our state are "soft targets.." This program will help train, equip, and prepare Florida's law enforcement community to respond to active shooter events. The program will include live scenario training to ensure our law enforcement officers are prepared in the event of an emergen
3219.population: Florida Law Enforcement Officers and School Resource Officers. Between 100-200 Officers.
3219.outcome: Law enforcement will be better trained to deal with active shooter situations. This will create a safer community.

3220.description: Holmes County has struggled for several years with an inmate population at or near capacity. Therefore, additional infrastructure is needed to assist with these demands. In addition to needing more space for inmates, the Sheriff intends to expand the drug treatment and rehabilitation services that is offered for inmates re-entering the community.
3220.purpose: Holmes County has struggled for several years with an inmate population at or near capacity. Therefore, additional infrastructure is needed to assist with these demands. In addition to needing more space for inmates, the Sheriff intends to expand the drug treatment and rehabiliation services that is offered for inmates re-entering the community.
3220.activities: Design and construction of the infrastructure needed for 64 beds of 2 man cells. This would also allow for an infill of another 64 beds by adding cells along with major infrastructure tie ins.
3220.direct_services: The expansion will improve the safety and health conditions for inmates and Sheriff’s Office staff. Continuing to provide rehabilitation services will also help those inmates re-entering the community.
3220.population: The general population will be served and over 1,000 individuals will be served.
3220.outcome: Expansion of the jail infrastructure will be able to serve the needs of our citizens and acccommodate the growth of the County. They will observe an increase in the number of inmates receiving these services.

3221.description: The County has identified the need for additional emergency equipment to assist in the response and recovery from natural disasters. The equipment includes skid steers, trailers, generators and pumps needed to provide the County tools to respond to emergencies.
3221.purpose: The County has identified the need for additional emergency equipment to assist in the response and recovery from natural disasters. The equipment includes skid steers, trailers, generators and pumps needed to provide the County tools to respond to emergencies.
3221.activities: Acquiring this emergency equipment will better prepare the County to respond to emergency events.
3221.direct_services: Residents of the County will be able to receive critical emergency services following severe weather events.
3221.population: The general public including residents of Holmes County will be served and this number is expected to be greater than 800.
3221.outcome: Purchase of emergency equipment will equip the County to respond to critical emergency events and better protect residents during these events. The impact will be measured by a more effective response and quicker recovery from major weather events.

3223.description: The purchase of new emergency equipment for the Chipley Police Department is needed to replace outdated and unsupported equipment. This equipment will enhance training capabilities and effectiveness of the Police Department by reducing crime and increasing community safety.
3223.purpose: The purchase of new emergency equipment for the Chipley Police Department is needed to replace outdated and unsupported equipment. This equipment will enhance training capabilities and effectiveness of the Police Department by reducing crime and increasing community safety.
3223.activities: This new equipment with new technology will enhance the Police Department’s ability to perform their duties. This includes training capabilities and overall effectiveness.
3223.direct_services: Residents within the community will receive services that are more effective and improve the overall quality of life for all residents.
3223.population: The general population will be served by this project and is expected to exceed 800 people.
3223.outcome: Improvements will increase law enforcement effectiveness and safety for the community and officers. This will be measured by improved response times and an overall reduction in crime.

3225.description: To extend the sewer system to Northwest Florida Community Hospital, the only hospital in this Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO), to ensure that adequate healthcare can continue to be provided. The existing sewer service is inadequate and improperly located to support the expansion of the hospital. The project will also serve existing homes and businesses that will be able to better access this newly provided sewer capability.

The existing sewer service is inadequate and improperly located to support the expansion of the hospital. The project will also serve existing homes and businesses that will be able to better access this newly provided sewer capability.
3225.activities: The existing sewer system will be extended to serve a larger area in this Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO).
3225.direct_services: Enhanced sewer capabilities that ensure adequate healthcare to Northwest Florida Community Hospital and houses and businesses in the area.
3225.population: The target population is the people around the Northwest Florida Community Hospital; many individuals are expected to benefit from this expansion.

3228.description: Florida Public Media, a non-profit association of 24 public radio and public television stations operating statewide, is seeking $2M in funding to update and maintain critical broadcasting infrastructure and technology equipment.
3228.purpose: Florida Public Media, a non-profit association of 24 public radio and public television stations operating statewide, is seeking $2M in funding to update and maintain critical broadcasting infrastructure and technology equipment. These funds will allow stations to stay on the air 24/7 to provide life-saving information and communications to audiences throughout the state.
3228.activities: Distribution through traditional broadcast channels, social media, and the Florida Storms app of important public safety communications and information during severe weather, hurricanes, and other emergencies.
3228.direct_services: Up-to-the minute weather information, timely reports from the Storm Center, state and local emergency offices, and local news coverage before, during and after an event or emergency.
3228.population: Anyone impacted by natural disasters and other emergencies. Services are provided statewide, individuals expected to be served would exceed 1 million.
3228.outcome: The updates on natural disasters and other emergencies by Florida Public Media's 24 stations provide vital safety information to Florida's residents to hunker down and/or evacuate during an emergency situation saving countless lives. Stations also provide reliable evacuation, road conditions, and closure information during a catastrophic event, providing this information improves traffic flow. The methodology to measure outcomes is provided through an annual report of coverage & services delivered and our ongoing partnerships with state agencies.

2848.description: The goal of the Comprehensive Care Model (CCM) is to provide an interdisciplinary team of professionals who can provide a comprehensive treatment approach for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder. The specific combination of therapies will depend on the specific child's deficits. Likewise, the specific areas of impairment will inform the clinical services. Some individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder have difficulties associated with changes in routine or changes in environments and often have a need for predictability. Regardless of which services a client receives he or she will be familiar with the staff and environment at DNA Comprehensive Therapy.
2848.purpose: Participants will acquire many necessary and valuable skills that will provide immediate job opportunities that will otherwise be unavailable to them. Including but not limited to eye contact, self regulation, and communication.
2848.activities: Counseling, Psychiatry, Occupational Therapy, Speech Therapy and Behavioral Analysis.
2848.direct_services: Counseling, Psychiatry, Occupational Therapy, Speech Therapy and Behavioral Analysis.
2848.outcome: Helping children develop necessary skills to establish healthy, age appropriate peer relationships. Learn to engage with other children and experience social acceptance. Behavior Assessment System for Children, Behavioral and Emotional Rating Scale, Pediatric Symptom Checklist.

3463.description: Endeavors will expand access to mental health and wellness services for veterans and their families in Pensacola, home to nearly 49,000 veterans with a high demand for services ranging from PTSD, depression, and substance abuse care to career training and services navigation. The program will offer a range of services to improve overall wellbeing in the five domains of Mind/Body, Financial Strength, Purpose/Growth, Connection, and Spirituality. We will measure improvements in quality of life, suicide reduction, stability and engagement using respected assessment tools.
3463.purpose: Fourteen percent of Escambia County residents are Veterans with a high demand for services ranging from PTSD, depression, and substance abuse care to career training and services navigation. Endeavors will establish a behavioral health and wellness program for Veterans and their families in Pensacola that improves their overall wellbeing in the five domains of Mind/Body, Financial Strength, Purpose/Growth, Connection, and Spirituality.
3463.activities: Health and wellness services for veterans and their families, to include wellness assessments, case management, fitness and nutrition counseling and classes, use of wellness room, massage, wellness app, and medication management. Endeavors will match the state's appropriation through a combination of leadership time and direct operational funding.
3463.direct_services: Through the appropriations project, Endeavors will provide the following direct services: 1. Evidence-based counseling for veterans, and their families. 2. Suicide-risk screening using the C-SSRS and wellness outcomes using Q-LES-Q-SF. 3. Holistic wellness services (Wellness Model: Mind-Body, Connection, Purpose, Spirituality, Financial Strength). 4. Alternative therapies. 5. Case management and p
3463.population: Endeavors will serve veterans and their families reaching 101-200 individuals annually. Escambia County’s ~49,000 veterans face limited access to low-cost mental health care long wait lists, and high demand for trauma-informed care. The project also supports spouses and dependents experiencing deployment-related stress and individuals seeking holistic, non-clinical services that improve sleep, mobility, mood regulation, and community connection.
3463.outcome: Endeavors utilizes key performance indicators such as industry standard assessments; participation and engagement rates; and client feedback to measure outcomes. We use Salesforce, PowerBI, and an Electronic Health Record (EHR) to ensure confidential, rigorous data collection and quality assurance. Measurable outcomes include: - Improved mental health and functioning measured by Q-LES-Q-SF. - Reduced suicide risk measured by C-SSRS screening trends and safety-plan completion. - Increased access to care measured by reduced wait times from request to first appointment. - Improved stability and family functioning measured through case-management outcomes. - Greater participation in wellness and

3473.description: West Florida Historic Preservation, Inc.'s mission is to become the forefront leader in history, arts, and culture in Northwest Florida. We do this by managing 30 state owned historic properties in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties. Many of these properties are museums which include a 34-acre archeological site, historic farmstead, general history museum, a fine arts museum, a children's museum, a multicultural center, an archives and research center, and a historic village with living history programs. These resources serve as a cultural heritage tourism engine attracting over 200,000 visitors and 15,000 schoolchildren annually. Locally we receive support from both Escambia County and the City of Pensacola, however our state-owned heritage tourism sites are in need of additional funding support for maintenance and preservation in addition to general operations.
3473.purpose: The funds will be used for continued maintenance and operation of the 30 state-owned historic properties that the organizations manage in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties. Many of these properties are museums and include a general history museum, a fine arts museum, a children's museum, a multicultural center, an archives and research center, and a historic village with living history programs. These resources serve as a cultural heritage tourism engine attracting over 200,000 visitors annually.
3473.activities: Among our myriad programs, we offer self-guided art and history exhibits, guided house museum tours, living history programs, and special programs like our ever-popular Ghost Tours and our Art Academy for Autism. Our school programs are among the best in the State and we draw over 15,000 schoolchildren to Historic Pensacola Village from across Northwest Florida and South Alabama.
3473.direct_services: The project will deliver STEAM-focused educational programming in the form of school field trips for grades K-12, adhering to Florida's Next Generation Sunshine State Standards; public programming includes lectures, tours, seasonal programs, and hands-on interactive activities for children; and continued maintenance and preservation of a popular and significant community historical resources.
3473.population: Our Museums and Archaeological sites are multi-generational resources that provides education and outdoor recreation to both local citizens (K-12 school age, young adults, middle-age, and senior community) and out-of-town visitors. We host over 200,000 visitors annually from over 28 states with a breakdown of roughly 42% local citizens from the tri-county area and 58% out of town guests. Annually we host over 15,000 schoolchildren.
3473.outcome: The project will increase visitation to the historic sites. Visitor counts will be taken to track visitor numbers and compare to currents numbers.

3330.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3330.description: The building of a multi-use facility will continue to improve and grow the Florida Agriculture Center & Horse Park Authority, increasing the disaster relief footprint and expanding the variety of events hosted by the park. The FACHPA has proven to be a vital site in times of disaster relief, not only as an animal-safe evacuation site but also as a level 1 logistical support area and a distribution site for food, water, and supplies.

The FACHPA has proven to be a vital site in times of disaster relief, not only as an animal-safe evacuation site but also as a level 1 logistical support area and a distribution site for food, water, and supplies.
3330.activities: Activities include: educational, recreational, agricultural, and emergency management. Examples include (but are not limited to) equine competitions, youth rodeos, cross country and athletic events, compost research, historic event reenactments, car shows, Christmas light displays, educational events, Polo matches, concerts, and K9 displays and training.
3330.direct_services: Services for citizens include (but are not limited to) recreation, safety, housing, emergency management, and education.
3330.population: The population served by the FACHP includes both Florida residents and tourists, as well as school-aged students, student athletes, historic event reenacters, emergency management personnel and others.
3330.outcome: The expansion of the FACHP will increase events related to equine athletics, historic event reenactments, protection for humans and animals during hurricane events, and with more events tourism will grow in the surrounding areas.

3176.description: A youth re-entry and workforce readiness initiative that empowers justice-impacted and at-risk young men (ages 12–24) in Alachua County to transition away from violence and incarceration toward employment, education, and community restoration. Program components include daily mentorship, trade and job-readiness training, work experience, community service, transportation assistance, life-skills development, and cultural/educational exposure trips.
3176.purpose: To reduce youth recidivism while increasing employment, education, and community engagement among justice- impacted youth.
3176.activities: To reduce youth recidivism while increasing employment, education, and community engagement among justice- impacted youth.
3176.direct_services: Hands-on mentorship and paid workforce experience for youth ages 12–24 affected by the justice system or violence.
3176.population: At-risk youth, jobless persons, high school students, currently/formerly incarcerated individuals, and drug offenders; serving 100 participants per year.
3176.outcome: Improved employment and job readiness tracked through employer verification and program records. Reduced recidivism monitored via justice database compliance records. Enhanced mental health and life skills measured via pre/post surveys and mentor observations.

3654.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3654.description: Funding would be used to purchase a new Air Compressor/Purifier to replace our current aged system that is quickly reaching its end of service life. Air Compressor/Purifiers provides safe re-supply of breathing air needed to refill empty Self Contained Breathing Apparatus to protect fire and emergency services personnel during confined space, firefighting, rescue, hazardous materials incidents, CBRN terrorism incidents, and other types of operations where respiratory hazards can or do exist.

2833.description: The goal of the ESB Young Leaders Program is to provide a blended educational approach to equip students for careers and opportunities in business and entrepreneurship. The program will help youth as they progress from students to professionals and contribute to meeting the growing demand for skilled workforce members throughout Miami. Youth participants in the program will exit with practical competencies such as digital & technical skills, employee readiness and leadership skills.
2833.purpose: The goal of the ESB Young Leaders Program is to provide a blended educational approach to equip students for careers and opportunities in business and entrepreneurship. The program will help youth as they progress from students to professionals and contribute to meeting the growing demand for skilled workforce members throughout Miami. Youth participants in the program will exit with practical competencies such as digital & technical skills, employee readiness and leadership skills.
2833.activities: The services being provided will impact youth ages 15-25 as well as educators via curriculum development, professional development sessions, course creation, and mentorship.
