2807.description: The Florida Rising - Dual Enrollment Nursing Pipeline initiative will bridge the funding gap between state dual enrollment rates and private institution costs, enabling high school students to complete 24 credit hours toward a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) degree.
2807.purpose: The appropriation’s purpose is to expand Bethune-Cookman University’s School of Nursing to address Florida’s critical nursing shortage. Equally, this program will establish a Dual Enrollment Nursing Pipeline Program to enable high school students, primarily from underserved communities, to earn college credits toward a nursing degree and enter the workforce more quickly.
2807.activities: The funds will be used to expand and enhance Bethune-Cookman University’s School of Nursing to meet Florida’s growing demand for qualified healthcare professionals. Activities and services funded through this appropriation will include expansion of nursing simulation and skills Laboratories, hiring of additional qualified nursing faculty to reduce student-to-instructor ratios, student scholarships, and licensure support enabling high school juniors and seniors to earn college credits toward a nu
2807.direct_services: The B-CU Rise, Dual Enrollment Nursing Program will cultivate a dual enrollment pipeline with Daytona Beach area high schools, allowing students from underserved populations to complete prerequisite nursing coursework while in high school, begin clinical rotations immediately upon full-time enrollment at B-CU, and, more importantly, earn a Bachelor of Science in Nursing degree within 3 years of hi
2807.population: Florida High school juniors and seniors, particularly from underserved and economically disadvantaged communities, who will participate in the Dual Enrollment Nursing Pipeline Program. This program will allow them to earn college credits toward a nursing degree while still in high school, accelerating their entry into Florida’s healthcare workforce.
2807.outcome: The B-CU Dual Enrollment Nursing Program will increase annual nursing enrollment by 25%, resulting in 40 additional students each year and over 100 new graduates annually to address Florida’s projected nursing shortage by creating a direct employment pipeline. This program Supports state goals by increasing Florida post-secondary graduates and improving retention rates. Enrollment data will be used to Track nursing program enrollment and completion rates via university records and Florida Department of Education reports.

2808.description: Bethune-Cookman University (B-CU) is seeking to continue the campus safety efforts by designing and implementing a comprehensive security and access control system across campus. The requested funding will be used to meet increased infrastructure needs by modernizing building access, improving emergency response coordination, and strengthen campus safety for over 3,000 students, faculty, and staff members at BCU.
2808.purpose: Bethune-Cookman University (B-CU) is seeking to continue the campus safety efforts by designing and implementing a comprehensive security and access control system across campus. The requested funding will be used to meet increased infrastructure needs by modernizing building access, improving emergency response coordination, and strengthen campus safety for over 3,000 students, faculty, and staff members at BCU.
2808.activities: Funding provided through this appropriation will provide direct safety, security, and emergency response services to students, faculty and staff, campus visitors, and surrounding community members who live and work in the regions near B-CU through the installation of comprehensive, technology-based security and a building access control system.
2808.direct_services: The proposed upgrades will ensure the students, faculty and staff, and regional residents are safe and protected during day-to-day activities, community events, and more.
2808.population: There are no specific groups to be targeted with this project as enhancement to university security infrastructure will ensure the safety of students, faculty and staff, and citizens of Daytona Beach who may live in close proximity to the campus. It is anticipated that over 800 individuals will be served by the funding.
2808.outcome: The expected benefits and outcomes include an improvement to the quality of education for students enrolled at B-CU and an improvement to public safety in the Dayton Beach area. By strengthening the security of the university and technological infrastructure, students will feel safe in secure while on campus during instructional hours and on-campus living. Residents in the central east Florida region will be able to rely on the university's security notification system to stay abreast of nearby security threats. These metrics will be determined by quarterly safety surveys to be issued to students, faculty and staff, and regional residents.

3245.description: Project Development and Environment Study for the City of Lynn Haven's Fire Station 3 which will add an additional Fire Station for the city improving call response times. They city has recently acquired the land in which this fire station will be constructed and is now ready to begin the planning and design process for this project.
3245.purpose: Deisgn and permit Fire Station 3 for Emergency Response for the City of Lynn Haven and surrounding areas.
3245.activities: Survey, design, and permit an addition Fire Station.
3245.direct_services: Fire and emergency medical response to the residents in the eastern part of the city.
3245.population: All 21,000 residents and businesses of Lynn Haven will receive an impact from this additional station by improving response times and ultimately allowign the city to have more fire staff to serve and respond to the residents.
3245.outcome: Response times to emergency calls, ultimately this will be measured and help improve ISO ratings.

3247.description: Regional Stormwater Facility with passive recreation amenities. Stormwater wetland facility will help in the treatment of a 300-acre watershed area, alleviating flooding and standing water issues on the east side of Lynn Haven, Florida.
3247.purpose: Provide a 30-acre storm water facility that will help treat storm water, eliminate structural flooding, and alleviate standing water in roadways of approximately 300-acres.
3247.activities: Passive recreation to include walking trails and an observation piers as well as tying two parts of the city together allowing residents walkability to one of the City's largest ball fields and recreation facilities.
3247.direct_services: Storm water relief from flooding for the immediate vicinity and passive recreation for all Lynn Haven residents.
3247.population: All of Lynn Haven's 21,000 residents and surrounding communities will benefit from this project through the passive recreation side and the residents that live in the vicinity of the 300-acre watershed will benefit directly from this project by alleviating their flooding issues and eliminating standing water.
3247.outcome: One measurable goal will be the nutrient/sediment removal that is being discharged to a water body currently and what it will be after constructing this treatment facility. Showing a reduction of nutrients will be a measure of success for this project. Another measurable goal to show success is the current number of flooded structures in this area presently and the number of structures after this facility is built and having storm water diverted to it.

3360.description: In 2024 the Town of Sewall's Point completed its Vulnerability & Resiliency Study. This project will raise the town's main 1-mile corridor to 3.00 NAVD elevation and construct stormwater swales and treatment areas for the removal of harmful pollutants prior to discharge into the Indian River Lagoon and the St. Lucie River Estuary (during 12-hour tidal cycles).
3360.purpose: This project will raise the Town's South Sewall's Point Road roadway to a 3-foot elevation and construct stormwater swales and treatment areas for the removal of harmful pollutants prior to being discharged to the Indian River Lagoon and the adjacent St. Lucie River Estuary during tidal cycles.
3360.activities: South Sewall's Point Road is the Town's only collector road and evacuation route. This project is a critical transportation asset as it will elevate the Town's major roadway, reducing flooding, allowing residents to access their homes during flooding events, depart during an emergency. Lastly, the project includes construction of stormwater swales and treatment areas that will remove harmful pollutants before release into the Indian River Lagoon.
3360.direct_services: On 12/20/24 the Town submitted its Flooding & Sea Level Rise Vulnerability Report Water tests analyses and updated its BMAP water quality restoration plans. By raising the roadway and upgrading the aged infrastructure, this project will restore the health of the surrounding environment, while also improving fish and wildlife that live in the area's adjacent surficial waters.
3360.population: The stormwater treatment and flood protection benefits residents by reducing flood risks, improving water quality in local waterways, creating more green spaces, enhancing property values, providing recreational areas and generally improving the quality of life in this community by mitigating pollution from runoff water, ultimately protecting public health and the environment. This project significantly benefits the Town's entire population of 1,991 residents.
3360.outcome: Sewall's Point seeks state funds to raise the Town's main corridor 3 feet to eliminate storm flooding to 70% of the Town's neighborhoods. Funding will permit the Town to construct a weir, retention ponds and nutrient removal baffle box outfalls before runoff enters the Indian River Lagoon.

3279.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3279.description: The Agricultural Technology & Workforce Education Initiative will provide industry-grade Controlled Environment Agriculture units to 150 classrooms across the state of Florida. Farm-Ed’s AI-powered, data-driven program combines technology, data dashboards, professional development, and standards-aligned curriculum. Aligned for K-12th classrooms, the goal is updating agriculture classrooms to reflect the changing future of agriculture careers and support workforce development.
3279.purpose: The goal of the Agricultural Technology & Workforce Education Initiative is to provide industry-grade Controlled Environment Agriculture units to 150 classrooms across the state of Florida. Farm-Ed’s AI-powered, data-driven program combines technology, data dashboards, professional development, and standards-aligned curriculum. Aligned for K-12th classrooms, the goal is updating agriculture classrooms to reflect the changing future of agriculture careers and support workforce development.
3279.activities: The Agricultural Technology & Workforce Education Initiative will provide 150 AI-powered Grow Chambers to classrooms, access to a Data Dashboard, 36 standards-aligned curriculum supplements, and AEST Agricultural Biotechnology Specialist certification exams. It includes teacher training, ongoing support, consumables, and technology integration to enhance STEM and CTE education.
3279.direct_services: The initiative will provide over 5,000 students with access to hands-on agricultural learning, real-time data analysis, and 36 curriculum modules aligned with industry standards. Those students will earn AEST Agricultural Biotechnology Specialist certifications, preparing them for future careers in agriculture, biotechnology, and STEM. 150 teachers receive training and support throughout.
3279.population: The target population to be served are grade school students, high school students, economically disadvantaged persons, and at-risk youth. We are expected to serve over 15,000 learners across Florida.
3279.outcome: Students are prepared for entry-level roles in agricultural biotechnology and related fields through certification in the AEST Agricultural Biotechnology Specialist program. Students earning AEST certifications gain credentials linked to an average 20% wage increase in biotechnology and agriculture roles, addressing skills gaps in high-demand industries. We will track the number of AEST certifications earned and compare certification rates with those of non-participating schools.

3456.description: District leadership has recognized the need for an intensive setting to better serve ESE students whose needs exceed current self-contained classrooms. SESI will bring Okaloosa County School District innovative approach to special education, behavioral support, and student development. The proposed In-District Program will provide intensive individualized instruction in 4 classrooms serving approximately 100 K-8 students, delivered in alignment with each student's IEP, 504 plan, or other support plans.
3456.purpose: District leadership has recognized the need for an intensive setting to better serve ESE students whose needs exceed current self-contained classrooms. SESI will bring Okaloosa County School District innovative approach to special education, behavioral support, and student development. The proposed In-District Program will provide intensive individualized instruction and a proven behavior support system, delivered in alignment with each student's IEP, 504 plan, or other support plans.
3456.activities: SESI emphasizes learning and embracing the culture of all educational partners. SESI will partner with the Okaloosa County School District to enhance the district's continuum of special education and behavior support services by implementing a highly structured therapeutic classroom(s).
3456.direct_services: SESI proposed the following services: 1. Incorporation of a therapeutic environment throughout the school day with trained behavioral staff. 2. Ongoing instruction for students on core behavioral norms. 3.On-site, full-time social worker providing individual and group counseling. 4.Guided Group Interaction sessions to encourage open conversations about mental health and well-being. 5. Designated s
3456.population: There will be four classrooms created. Serving approximately 40-48 students (K-8). Cumulatively serving approximately 100 students throughout the school year.
3456.outcome: A therapeutic environment will be maintained throughout the day with trained behavioral staff reinforcing key behavioral norms. A full-time social worker will provide individual and group counseling, with Guided Group Interaction supporting mental health discussions. A soft-space room will allow structured breaks, while Live School tracks stamina, soft-space use, behavioral events, and referrals.

3466.description: Increased Utilities capacity is required to accommodate future campus development. Future growth as envisioned in the next 10 years through the 2021-2031 Campus Master Plan will require implementable expansion of the Central Utilities Plant (CUP), as planned new facilities are added, or with renovations to existing buildings that are not currently served by the existing CUP. Construction of a Satellite Central Utilities Plant and associated infrastructure to support future campus growth. This is a Multi-year Project having a total project cost of $28,000,000, with prior/current Phased Funding. After a review of the plans and the operational capacity for the University there was a determination made that expanded capacity is needed to serve faculty/students/staff. The existing campus infrastructure system has limitations. The associated infrastructure required to support implementation of
3466.purpose: Scope is for Construction of a new Satellite Central Utilities Plant and associated infrastructure. Each capital project as identified in the University’s Capital Improvement Plan (and the 2021-2031 CMP) will require increased CUP capacity for heating and cooling. The existing Central Utilities Plant (CUP) is at TOTAL maximum delivered capacity. The existing plant, located on the Northwest side of campus, does not have physical space for expansion, nor pumping capacity or utility infrastructure
3466.activities: A new expandable facility is proposed for the Satellite Central Heating and Cooling Plant which will be located on the South Side of the existing campus in the general area of future priority projects. The layout and configuration of the satellite plant will be designed to allow for future increase in size and capacity to accommodate future service loads. The new satellite CUP will require associated infrastructure including necessary storm-water management; sewer, water, electrical, communicati
3466.direct_services: Campus Improvement and maintenance. The Satellite Central Utilities Plant facility is to be designed to accommodate future campus development within the next 10 years, with the potential for future expansion in order to serve aspirational growth of UWF for the next 30 years plus.
3466.population: University Students, Faculty and Staff: 15,000+ students, 2,000+ faculty and staff
3466.outcome: Additional utilities plant capacity is required to accommodate future campus development. The project will contribute to the overall enhanced climatic environment for campus occupants, and will allow for future campus growth. When constructed the new satellite plant will be tied into the existing piping distribution loop system to operate in conjunction with the existing multi-component heating and cooling plant; with operations controlled as climatic conditions warrant through seasonal temperature fluctuations.

2809.description: The project is to provide stakeholders a data driven decision-making tool to optimize traffic flow and address transportation needs by analyzing current conditions, forecasting future congestion, and implementing forward-thinking solutions. By continuously analyzing real-time traffic data, the system identifies irregularities that could contribute to congestion or potential accidents, using predictive modeling informed by historical trends.
2809.purpose: The goal of the project is to provide stakeholders a data driven decision-making tool to optimize traffic flow and address transportation needs by analyzing current conditions, forecasting future congestion, and implementing forward-thinking solutions. By continuously analyzing real-time traffic data, the system identifies irregularities that could contribute to congestion or potential accidents, using predictive modeling informed by historical trends.
2809.activities: Municipal stakeholders will be able to see what the impact on travel time delays would be for events such as lane- closures, events, etc. that would impact volume, flow and capacity. Over time, this tool allows for understanding the impact of developments around the area on congestion and travel time delays.
2809.direct_services: The tool will provide an ROI calculator based on calculations of cost of delay for the corridor. The ROI calculator will allow the user determine what the return on investment is going to be for infrastructure projects that would reduce travel time delay and congestion on the roadway. Stakeholders will be able to make data driven decisions to better improve the traffic congestion for the citizens.
2809.population: University students and the general public.
2809.outcome: Employ advanced analytics and forecasting to predict traffic impact based on speed and volume, and consequently travel time delays, etc. to provide a what-if scenario analysis tool that enables decision-makers to assess the anticipated impact of developments and the anticipated impact of changes to traffic demand on travel time delay and, therefore, congestion.

2793.organization: A National Salute to America's Heroes, LLC
2793.description: This national signature initiative brings back the true spirit of Memorial Day honoring the men and women of our military and those that have paid the ultimate sacrifice on behalf of our freedom. The project supports recruitment, boosts morale, fosters patriotism and reconnects the military with the American public through engagement and exposure. The project showcases Florida’s commitment to our military while redefining Memorial Day as a time of gratitude, progress, and unity.
2793.purpose: This national signature initiative brings back the true spirit of Memorial Day honoring the men and women of our military and those that have paid the ultimate sacrifice on behalf of our freedom. The project supports recruitment, boosts morale, fosters patriotism and reconnects the military with the American public through engagement and exposure. The project showcases Florida’s commitment to our military while redefining Memorial Day as a time of gratitude, progress, and unity.
2793.activities: This event is free to the public generating community spirit, revenue for the businesses and showcases the community at large including the State of Florida in a positive light. It generates military recruiting interest, boosts morale, and reconnects our military with the American public.
2793.direct_services: The funding will be utilized for the production and marketing of this signature event that brings back the true spirit of Memorial Day. There is no better time than Memorial Day to pay tribute to the men and women of our military and those that have paid the ultimate sacrifice on behalf of our freedom. Memorial Day was the only holiday in America that did not have a signature event prior.
2793.population: This free event attracts entire population creating a wholesome family oriented patriotic experience.
2793.outcome: Showcasing all branches of the US Military and educating the public on the importance of our military protecting our country and our freedom. High-speed aerial demonstrations, elite Special Operations capabilities, exercises, and breathtaking parachute team performances—all showcasing the strength, skill, and dedication of our Nation’s Armed Forces. On site displays, showcasing equipment, free to the public, allowing opportunity to meet the men and women from all branches of our military and thank them for their service.

3474.description: This is a Revert and Reappropriate request from the previous 2025 session (Identifier LFIR: 2987). Funds will be used to generate several high-quality theatrical performances, subsidize children's theatre education as well as retrofitting aspects of our historic building in downtown Pensacola. These funds would provide operational support and critical infrastructure to sustain and expand our community theatre's mission.
3474.purpose: This is a Revert and Reappropriate request from the previous 2025 session (Identifier LFIR: 2987). Funds will be used to generate several high-quality theatrical performances, subsidize children's theatre education as well as retrofitting aspects of our historic building in downtown Pensacola. These funds would provide operational support and critical infrastructure to sustain and expand our community theatre's mission.
3474.activities: Grant funding will enable our community theatre to deliver a wide range of artistic, educational, and community- focused services. Operating support will sustain year-round productions, educational classes for youth and adults, community outreach events, and volunteer programs that foster creativity and cultural engagement. This will further strengthen our capacity by supporting critical upgrades.
3474.direct_services: Accessible Theatrical Productions, Youth and Teen Education Programs, Adult Workshops and Community Classes, Volunteer and Community Engagement Opportunities, Arts Access for Underserved Populations, and Free or Low- Cost Community Events.
3474.population: Elderly Persons, Persons with poor mental health, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, grade school students, high school students, university/college students, and currently or formerly incarcerated persons. Expect to serve AT LEAST 800 individuals.
3474.outcome: Community theatre contributes to improved physical health by engaging participants in regular movement, coordination, and hands-on activity through rehearsals, performances, and volunteer roles. Evaluation will be measured on attendance, registrations, and patron participation. Surveys are distributed for all programs post- execution. Community theatre significantly enhances the overall mental health of our community by providing accessible, inclusive, and creative spaces for emotional expression and social connection. Participation in theatre—whether onstage, backstage, or as a volunteer—reduces stress, builds confidence, and fosters a sense of belonging through meaningful collaboration. Th

2932.description: Reconstruct Boca Ciega Dr. - Boca Ciega Dr. is a vital roadway serving 8,000 residents, and countless visitors, in our community. The existing pavement is in poor condition, and the reclaimed water infrastructure frequently fails, causing leaks and service disruptions. The roadway and associated infrastructure have exceeded their useful life, making reconstruction critical for safety, reliability, and community access. This project will involve full roadway reconstruction, including base restoration and asphalt paving, replacement of curbs, and the addition of sidewalks to enhance pedestrian safety. Aging utility services, including the reclaimed water system, will be replaced, and modern signage and pavement striping will be installed. The project will also incorporate improvements to the stormwater system to reduce flooding and enhance drainage. Together, these improvements will restor
2932.purpose: To reconstruct Boca Ciega Drive between 75th and 87th Avenues, replacing deteriorated utilities and pavement to improve safety, mobility, and economic vitality. The project addresses chronic reclaimed-water and sanitary service leaks that contribute to potholes and roadway degradation while enhancing storm drainage, walkability, and landscape appeal
2932.activities: Replace aging reclaimed water and sanitary sewer mains. Install new storm drainage infrastructure and curb systems. Reconstruct roadway base and asphalt surface per FDOT standards. Add traffic calming, crosswalks, sidewalks, and pedestrian pathways for safety. Include landscape and irrigation improvements.
2932.direct_services: Enhanced pedestrian and bicycle safety. Improved roadway reliability and aesthetics. Reduced flooding, potholes, and service disruptions. Improved accessibility to Corey Avenue business district, promoting local commerce.
2932.population: Residents and visitors along Boca Ciega Drive, including approximately 300 properties in the residential corridor north of the Corey Avenue district. Indirectly benefits local businesses and tourists accessing downtown.
2932.outcome: Reduced roadway maintenance calls (City work order tracking pre- vs. post-construction) Reduced reclaimed-water and sewer leaks (Annual system loss reports and repair logs) Improved pedestrian & traffic safety (Speed and crash-rate comparison before/after) Increased downtown economic activity (Sales tax and business occupancy trends)

3302.description: The Pass-a-Grille area relies on an aging wastewater system of gravity mains, laterals, manholes, and cleanouts that convey flow to a single pump station for treatment off-island. An independent I&I study and the City’s Asset Management Plan identified extensive infiltration from tidal groundwater and pipe deterioration. The project will repair and replace compromised segments, reducing I&I, chloride intrusion, and system failures while improving efficiency and environmental compliance
3302.purpose: Reduce I&I in Pass-a-Grille wastewater system to improve reliability, reduce chloride levels, and protect water quality.
3302.activities: Repair and replace lateral service lines, gravity mains, and manholes; rehabilitate cleanouts; install watertight components.
3302.direct_services: Reliable sanitary sewer service for residents and businesses; prevention of sanitary sewer overflows.
3302.population: Historic Pass-a-Grille neighborhood (south of 21st Ave) > 800 people.
3302.outcome: Measure reductions in I&I flow and chloride levels, verify system performance improvements through CCTV and meter data.

2952.description: This program serves Florida's K-12 students and the aerospace industry ecosystem at large by helping to fill the aerospace workforce gap with a specific focus on Aerospace related disciplines. Our goal is to inspire students to pursue studies in STEM, to increase career awareness and access to career opportunities within the aerospace industry, and to prepare them to accept positions within the workforce. This will also provide the aerospace industry with prepared and skilled individuals.
2952.purpose: The requested funds will support a program that prepares Florida's K-12 students for careers in aerospace by inspiring interest in STEM, expanding career awareness, and developing the skills needed to enter the aerospace workforce. This initiative aims to help close the aerospace workforce gap and supply the industry with well-prepared, skilled professionals.
2952.activities: High school students and educators will work with STEM Education Specialists to engage in aerospace-related coursework and hands-on activities. Students will meet face-to-face with major aerospace organizations about internships, apprenticeships, and job opportunities.
2952.direct_services: Direct services include hands-on STEM activities, facilitated networking sessions, career panels, and one-to-one introductions to aerospace professionals and recruiters, including those hiring students from high school CTE programs.
2952.population: Over 800 high school students throughout Miami-Dade County Public Schools.
2952.outcome: This initiative seeks to increase the education of the aerospace industry missions and programs, and awareness and career preparedness of participants by 80%. This program seeks to inspire students to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering and math, and increase interest by >50%. Students and educators will be provided a survey regarding missions and programs, as well as career awareness and preparedness, prior to and after their exposure to the program. Survey results will provide qualitative and quantitative data.

3512.description: Here's Help provides residential substance abuse treatment services to adults and adolescents in Miami-Dade County. The funding helps to meet community demand for these services. Here's Help has a long track record of successful treatment outcomes. Here's Help has been very successful in transitioning the lives of those that have been treated; from having low self-esteem, habitual school issues and involvement in the criminal justice system, to becoming productive citizens.
3512.purpose: Individuals with substance abuse and co-occurring disorders have been diverted from a life of criminal justice involvement to leading a drug free life, continuing their education, and becoming a productive citizen.
3512.activities: Individual, group and family therapy sessions, as well as educational / vocational courses that enhance the individual's ability to be a confident, well adjusted and skilled person.
3512.population: Residential adolescents and adults with substance abuse and co-occuring issues. Most are criminal justice referrals. About 100 residentials clients are served annually in the residential program.
3512.outcome: That 70% of the persons served will positively complete the program and 90% enrolled in school at discharge. Successful completion is determined by a person served being 100% drug free and completed 75% of their treatment goals.

3059.description: Florida Memorial University is seeking to enhance the current degree offerings through the Department of Aviation and Safety by updating antiquated technology in order to prepare students for career success in Florida's aviation workforce. Funding will be used to acquire quality equipment, strengthen current industry partnerships, and provide additional certification pathways for students.
3059.purpose: The purpose of this project is to prepare students for career success in a competitive job market and enhance internship and apprenticeship programs with both local and national employers, including our current partnerships with the FAA and Miami International Airport. FMU is seeking to strengthen industry partnerships which will allow us to align our curriculum with workforce demands and develop professional certification programs will further increase students' job readiness and employability.
3059.activities: The requested funds will be used to increase degree and career pathway opportunities in aviation to meet the growing workforce needs. Specifically, funding will allow for the establishment of dual enrollment and talent pipeline programs with local high schools and technical institutions, the creation of industry-aligned certification programs, and other educational and career programs.
3059.direct_services: Funding supports outreach to populations in Miami-Dade County and other neighboring areas. Programs may include wraparound services such as academic and career mentoring and one-on-one career advising with certified aviation career specialists.
3059.population: The target population of this project will largely include university students. It is projected that the project will serve about 400 to 800 students.
3059.outcome: There are several expected benefits or outcomes of the enhancement of the aviation classrooms on campus which include, but are not limited to, the improvement of education quality. By enhancing classrooms and equipment such as modern aviation technology and simulators, students will gain quality, hands-on training to deepen their comprehension of the industry. This method will be measured through the application and placement for internship and apprenticeship opportunities. FMU will track the number of students enrolled in the program as well as the number of students who complete the certification process.

2831.organization: Florida Alcohol and Drug Abuse Association
2831.description: The federal Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) strongly advocate for the use of medication-assisted treatment as a best practice approach to serve individuals with alcohol and opioid use disorders. Program funds community treatment providers for provision of substance abuse screening, medical assessments/lab work and extended-release naltrexone medication injections for individuals with alcohol and/or opioid abuse or dependence throughout the state that are court- involved, criminal justice-involved, or at-risk for involvement with the court system due to prior histories or current substance use activities. Services are delivered through a statewide network of 60 providers from Pensacola to Key West.
2831.purpose: In response to the opioid epidemic and the ongoing problem of alcohol abuse/dependence among Florida's citizens, the program facilitates recovery from substance abuse, lowers rates of opioid overdose, and reduces costs to society for employment issues, high-cost healthcare utilization, and criminal justice/court involvement related to opioid and alcohol use disorders.
2831.activities: The program funds substance abuse screening/evaluation, medical assessment, and extended-release medication injections to help uninsured or under-insured individuals with alcohol and/or opioid dependence recover. The program enhances retention/completion rates for outpatient, residential, and other forms of psychosocial treatment.
2831.direct_services: Clinical screening to diagnose alcohol and/or opioid use disorders; medical assessments/lab work to determine fitness of patients to receive medication and continue with maintenance protocols; and, medication administration for dosing extended-release injectable naltrexone every 3 to 4 weeks until cessation of the medical protocol as determined by the physician.
2831.population: The non-recurring funds enable the program to serve 151 patients who are court-involved, criminal justice-involved, or at-risk for court/criminal justice involvement and present with alcohol and/or opioid abuse and dependence problems through the provision of clinical screening, medical assessment/lab work, and extended-release injectable naltrexone medication.
2831.outcome: The program's outcome performance measurement is that at least 60% of individuals receiving extended-release injectable naltrexone services will successfully complete or remain actively engaged in psychosocial treatment for alcohol and/or opioid use disorders at time of discharge from services. Performance is calculated by dividing the numerator, which is all individuals successfully completing or still actively engaged in psychosocial treatment at time of discharge from medication-assisted treatment (MAT) services by the denominator, which is all individuals discharged from MAT services.

3613.description: The requested funding amount will be used to reimburse child welfare provider agencies who were not paid by Embrace Families prior to their contact with the DCF being withdrawn. 2836.organization: Boys & Girls Clubs of Martin County
2836.description: Funding will support construction/fixed capital outlay of a state-of-the-art Boys & Girls Club in Hobe Sound, FL. Once constructed, this 28,000 sq. ft facility will offer over 100 full and part-time employment opportunities; out-of-school programs in academics, health & nutrition, mentoring & life skills, sports & recreation, college access, workforce development, and the arts; workforce certification programs that lead to immediate gainful employment; provision of 50,000+ meals annually; and free out-of-school childcare for families.
2836.purpose: Funding will support capital construction costs to build the facility.
2836.activities: Proctor Construction is the General Contractor for this capital project.
2836.direct_services: Once constructed, the facility will offer over 100 full and part-time employment opportunities; out-of-school programs in academics, health & nutrition, mentoring & life skills, sports & recreation, college access, workforce development, and the arts; workforce certification programs that lead to immediate gainful employment; provision of 50,000+ meals annually; free out-of-school childcare for fa
2836.population: Annually, over 1,500 children, teens, and adults residing primarily in Martin County, but inclusive of some Palm Beach and St. Lucie County residents, will directly benefit from the out-of-school programs and the workforce certification programs that will be offered at this facility.
2836.outcome: Some benefits include: Improved physical health measured by the PACER fitness test administered at the beginning and end of the school year; Improved academic performance in English Language Arts and Math measured by school assessment data; Completion of workforce certification courses and job placement measured by attendance data, curriculum completion and assessment scores, and employment secured; Improved knowledge of the dangers of drug/alcohol use measured by pre-post test; Improved behaviors at home and school measured by risk assessment score and parent surveys.

3062.description: Funding requested will support renovations to nine (9) high school auditoriums across Miami-Dade County Public Schools, including upgrades to lighting, audiovisual systems, equipment, curtains, wiring, and other infrastructure improvements. These enhancements will create modern, multipurpose spaces for student assemblies, performances, and community events, expanding access and engagement in under-served areas.
3062.purpose: Funding requested will support renovations to nine (9) high school auditoriums across Miami-Dade County Public Schools, including upgrades to lighting, audiovisual systems, equipment, curtains, wiring, and other infrastructure improvements. These enhancements will create modern, multipurpose spaces for student assemblies, performances, and community events, expanding access and engagement in under-served areas.
3062.activities: Renovations will include upgrades to lighting, audiovisual systems, equipment, curtains, wiring, and related infrastructure across nine (9) high school auditoriums. These improvements will create modern, multipurpose spaces that support student programs and community events.
3062.direct_services: Students will have increased opportunities and access to Visual and Performing Arts programs in newly renovated auditoriums with updated systems and equipment. These spaces will also provide the community access for town hall meetings, college and career fairs, local performances, and other public events.
3062.population: Over 800 high school students throughout Miami-Dade County Public Schools are expected to be served.
3062.outcome: Renovated auditoriums will provide enhanced spaces for students and community members to participate in educational and artistic activities. Improved lighting, sound, and staging will support school and community events that promote cultural enrichment by supporting creativity, community engagement, and an appreciation for the arts within a safe, modern environment. Documentation of performances/presentations/exhibitions hosted in the auditorium will be collected.

2817.description: Since 2013, the FPREN StormCenter has served the state of Florida during numerous disasters including hurricanes, floods, severe weather outbreaks, and other public safety events. Funding will allow the FPREN StormCenter to expand statewide television programing, while being accessible on all media platforms. Funds will also support a public safety/emergency management reporter and updates to the Florida Storms mobile app to include video and live streaming of crisis situations, while providing real time communications from state & local authorities.
2817.purpose: Funding will allow the FPREN StormCenter to expand statewide television programing, while being accessible on all media platforms. Funds will support a public safety/emergency management reporter who will work directly with state & local authorities to ensure vital information is accessible on a free platform for all Floridians. The FloridaStorms mobile app will be updated with video and live streaming of crisis situations, while providing real time communications from state & local authorities.
2817.activities: FPREN provides a 24/7 public safety reporting service available to all Floridians on free over the air broadcast radio and television in addition to digital (website) and social media coverage, through various platforms such as “X”, Facebook, etc. in addition to the free Florida Storms mobile app.
2817.direct_services: On top of the core FPREN services, the enhanced content that will be provided through all media platforms will include dedicated reporting and updates on public safety and emergency management issues and initiatives, daily reporting and communication efforts supporting agencies at the local, county and state levels and enhanced television products.
2817.population: The target population will be any Floridian impacted by a natural disaster or other emergency situation. Services are provided statewide, so the anticipated number of individuals expected to be served could reach roughly the population of Florida (~23 million).
2817.outcome: FPREN provides updates on emergency situations to residents statewide, regardless of income due to the platform being free of cost. This important service ensures that messaging from state and local authorities reaches all Floridians. For FPREN's efforts educating the public, we have been nationally recognized for over 10 years as a public resource for Floridians statewide during emergency situations. An annual report is also commissioned each year to determine statewide outreach impacts.

3309.description: The WeRestore Facilities Project by Ocean Rescue Alliance International will expand Florida’s statewide network of marine habitat restoration and aquaculture facilities dedicated to cultivating coral, oysters, mangroves, and seagrass. These facilities serve as living laboratories and a collaborative space supporting restoration, education, and resilience programs that enhance water quality, protect coastlines, and restore biodiversity. In addition to expanding a restoration task force this facility will explore blue economy development. The requested funds will be used to expand infrastructure, supplies, and equipment including coral propagation tanks, mangrove nurseries, oyster and seagrass cultivation systems. The project directly supports Florida’s marine restoration initiatives.
3309.purpose: The WeRestore Facilities Project will expand statewide aquaculture and restoration facilities to grow and deploy coral, oyster, mangrove, and seagrass species that restore Florida’s marine ecosystems, improve coastal resilience, and support economic and environmental sustainability. The project will increase native species production capacity, enhance water quality, and strengthen natural storm protection systems. This facility will serve as the first co-working restoration aquaculture facility
3309.activities: The WeRestore Facilities Project will expand statewide aquaculture and restoration facilities to grow and deploy coral, oyster, mangrove, and seagrass species that restore Florida’s marine ecosystems, improve coastal resilience, and support economic and environmental sustainability. The project will increase native species production capacity, enhance water quality, and strengthen natural storm protection systems. This facility will serve as the first co-working restoration aquaculture facility
3309.direct_services: The project will provide environmental education, volunteer opportunities, and workforce training in restoration techniques for Floridians. It will also directly benefit coastal residents by improving water quality, reducing erosion, and protecting property through living shoreline and reef restoration. These services contribute to safer, cleaner, and more resilient coastal communities.
3309.population: Target populations include coastal residents, students (K to college), environmental volunteers, and local workforce trainees. Over 10,000 individuals statewide are expected to benefit annually through education programs, training, and community engagement, with millions of Floridians indirectly benefiting from improved coastal resilience, water quality, and ecosystem services.
3309.outcome: The WeRestore Facilities Project is expected to deliver measurable ecological, economic, and social benefits to Florida’s coastal communities. By expanding restoration capacity, the project will restore more than 10 acres of marine and shoreline habitats and produce over 20,000 coral, oyster, mangrove, and seagrass species annually. These efforts will improve water quality, enhance biodiversity, and strengthen natural coastal defenses against erosion and storm surge. The project’s outcomes will be measured through a combination of scientific monitoring and performance tracking, including turbidity and nutrient-level testing, biodiversity surveys, third party.

2931.description: This project will reconstruct key roadways to enhance connectivity to and around UF Health Hospital, improve and expand critical drainage infrastructure, and restore access to the headwaters of Hogans Creek. The improvements are designed to increase mobility, reduce flooding risks, and support long-term creek and watershed restoration efforts. Additional funding is required to complete the planned bridge construction and associated drainage components.
2931.purpose: Reconstructed roads to provide enhanced connection at UF Health Hospital, accommodate improved drainage infrastructure, and open up the headwaters of Hogan's Creek. Additional funding will be needed for construction of the bridge and drainage infrastructure.
2931.activities: The project will provide improved access to UF Health medical complex and reduce historical flooding along Hogan's Creek. It will open the creek to recreational usage as part of the Emerald Trail multi-use path network.
2931.direct_services: Traffic flow will be improved by connecting and straightening a disjointed street network around the UF Health medical complex. Pedestrian facilities will be added as well as street lighting. Recreational usage of Hogan's Creek, currently not possible, will be accommodated in preparation for the City's related Emerald Trail project.
2931.population: The general population will be served with more than 800,000 residents and visitors served.
2931.outcome: The project will provide safer, more efficient access to the UF Health medical complex and added pedestrian facilities will be provided. Lastly, the project will result in reduced flooding of Hogan's Creek.

2913.description: Funds will be used to serve the growing number of Palm Beach County residents facing chronic food insecurity. Our goal is to reach 200 households below the Asset Limited Income Constrained Employed (ALICE) Household Survival Budget threshold, which is the bare minimum of cost of household basics to live and work in the current economy (United Way 2025). During our intake assessment for food assistance, we may learn if the person needs mental or other service referrals to restore stability.

Food program clients have access to a care manager who assists in addressing the current need and root cause of financial instability and refers them to wraparound services if needed.

2913.outcome: All clients receiving food assistance gain relief from strained household budgets struggling to meet basic expenses such as housing, utilities, and insurance. The program also provides items not covered by SNAP such as household cleaning supplies and personal care products. Food distribution will be measured by financial value and weight and tracked through PantrySoft software. Clients who opt for agency counseling or other mental health services are tracked through Welligent Electronic Health Record software. 2914.description: This funding will enhance disaster response and recovery capabilities with the installation of backup generators at critical County facilities. In the event of power outages caused by storms, hurricanes, or other emergencies, these facilities will serve as comfort stations, points of distribution for water and essential supplies, logistical staging areas, and other critical functions identified in the County’s Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan.
2914.purpose: This funding will enhance disaster response and recovery capabilities with the installation of backup generators at critical County facilities. In the event of power outages caused by storms, hurricanes, or other emergencies, these facilities will serve as comfort stations, points of distribution for water and essential supplies, logistical staging areas, and other critical functions identified in the County’s Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan.
2914.activities: Installation of backup generators at critical facilities to support emergency operations.
2914.direct_services: This project will strengthen the County’s emergency preparedness, public safety, and community resilience, ensuring that residents have access to vital services and support during power outages and other disaster events.
2914.population: This project will benefit residents and visitors of Leon County.
2914.outcome: This project will facilitate the expanded use of county-owned facilities to support Leon County's emergency response efforts following a disaster. This outcome will be measured by conducting an updated vulnerability analysis for the community, as identified in the Leon County Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan and the Tallahassee-Leon County Hazard Mitigation Plan.

2927.description: Horizon Communities Corporation would like to continue to operate in their current 4 institutions. This would include teaching REEFS, Quest, and computer labs in each facility. The funding used would provide for office space for Horizon Employees, computers for the labs, books and materials, and monetary compensation for employees. Courses will be taught to more than 800 incarcerated men and women. A reentry facility will be obtained to provide housing and employment to graduates of the Horizon program, that are released from the Department of Corrections
2927.purpose: Social and emotional awareness and life skills training will be taught to over 800 incarcerated men and women, preparing them to live responsibly with others. Also, the acquisition of a reentry facility that will provide housing for those released from the Department of Corrections custody.
2927.activities: Dorms are created into communities that learn how to behave in socially acceptable ways, improving behavior and promoting public safety.
2927.direct_services: Programs offered through Horizon Communities are Quest, REEFS, and Computer Labs. Also, Conscious Discipline, victim impact, and restorative justice principles have shown the outcome of restoring self-esteem, responsibility and productivity to inmates while they are incarcerated and once, they are released. This serves not only the inmate but also the citizens in the community to which they re-ent
2927.population: Incarcerated men and women are served by this project. More than 800 men and women are expected to be served during this fiscal year.
2927.outcome: Horizon dorms have helped prisons to be safer for both security staff and the inmates housed there. Disciplinary Reports, contraband, and assaults are recorded by the Department of Corrections. These incidents have been reduced every time Horizon has entered a prison, and it is believed that this will continue. Also, recidivism rates are measured, and Horizon has a recidivism rate of 5.4% after 26 years of operation. The reentry facility will provide funds to help future ventures by Horizon in an effort to relieve the burden of state funds.

Wallace Road to the south of State Road 61. The second segment is from the Wakulla County line to L.L. Wallace Road. This project is currently #4 on the local MPO's Roadway Priority List.

2936.direct_services: This project will provide a direct benefit to the citizens of Leon County and those traveling through Leon County by improving transportation system level of service, including relief in traffic congestion and ensuring dependability of the roadway as an evacuation route.
2936.population: The majority of funds will benefit no specific group with the general population expected to be served by this project.
2936.outcome: Widening of Crawfordville Road (US 319) to accommodate the high average daily traffic volume. This outcome will be measured through improved traffic conditions and enhanced safety.

3025.description: This project seeks $500,000 to complete critical security enhancements at the Leon County Courthouse as recommended by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement and the Leon County Sheriff’s Office to provide a safe and secure environment for all courthouse users. Planned improvements include security screening system and security camera upgrades, new access controls, and other physical security measures to promote public safety.
3025.purpose: To achieve the intended purpose of enhancing courthouse security, the funds will be used to upgrade the security screening system to ensure safe entry for all visitors and staff. Security camera systems will be upgraded or expanded to enhance monitoring, incident detection, and evidence collection, while additional physical security measures will be installed to prevent unauthorized access.
3025.activities: To achieve the intended purpose of enhancing courthouse security, the funds will be used to upgrade the security screening system to ensure safe entry for all visitors and staff. Security camera systems will be upgraded or expanded to enhance monitoring, incident detection, and evidence collection, while additional physical security measures will be installed to prevent unauthorized access.
3025.direct_services: This project will provide resident with direct public safety services by ensuring the Leon County Courthouse is a secure and protected environment. Visitors will benefit from safe and efficient entry through upgraded security screening, protection from unauthorized access via enhanced access controls, and increased monitoring and rapid response capabilities through improved security cameras.
3025.population: All users of the courthouse will benefit from this project.
3025.outcome: Enhanced public safety and security at the Leon County Courthouse.

3037.organization: The Florida Center for Early Childhood, Inc.
3037.description: The Florida Center for Early Childhood requests $2.5 million in recurring funds to expand its existing Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD) Clinic into a Statewide FASD Center of Excellence, aligning with the Federal FASD Respect Act, unanimously supported in the Senate. Building on over a decade of state-supported work in Sarasota County, Pensacola, and statewide contracts, this project will strengthen Florida’s capacity to prevent, identify, and treat the effects of prenatal alcohol exposure. FASD is the leading cause of preventable developmental disability in the United States, affecting as many as 1 in 20 school-aged children. Despite this prevalence, most children remain undiagnosed or misdiagnosed resulting in costly outcomes across education, behavioral health, and juvenile justice systems. The Florida Center’s proposed Center of Excellence will serve as the state’s hub for pre
3037.purpose: Goal is to enhance FASD Clinic services and expand them into a Statewide Center of Excellence, aligning Florida with the objectives of the federal FASD Respect Act, by coordinating efforts in prevention, identification, diagnosis, treatment, and ongoing support for individuals affected by prenatal alcohol exposure. The primary goal is to establish a comprehensive and sustainable statewide model for FASD services, thereby reducing the long-term social, educational, and healthcare costs.
3037.activities: Services to include: diagnostic assessments, medical consults, psychological evaluations, educational support, training, public awareness, mental health and other therapies. Additionally, it will implement 5 core components of a Center of Excellence, consistent with the Respect Act: Prevention & Identification; Clinical Services & Access; Workforce Development; Advocacy; and Research.
3037.direct_services: The requested funds will support direct services including: -Comprehensive diagnostic/intervention services for children and families -Support groups, family counseling, care coordination -Public education and prevention campaigns to reduce prenatal alcohol exposure These services will expand access statewide ensuring Florida’s readiness to integrate Respect Act provision into practice.
3037.population: The majority of funds will serve: Persons with poor mental health Economically disadvantaged families Children with developmental and behavioral challenges due to prenatal exposure Women of child bearing age receiving substance use prevention education Professionals in health, education, justice, and child welfare systems requiring FASD training At-risk youth and families impacted by intergenerational substance use and trauma The project will serve 800 individuals.
3037.outcome: Improve physical health: Increased identification and referrals for treatment; Increased education to medical professionals on the impact of alcohol on health. Improve mental health: Reduction in behavioral issues among diagnosed children; Pre- and post-assessment tools (e.g., BASC-3) Improve quality of education: Increased school stability and performance; Collaboration with DOE and local school data Reduce substance abuse: Reduced prenatal alcohol use rates; Healthy Start/DOH screening data Divert from criminal/juvenile justice system: Reduced involvement of undiagnosed FASD youth; Data from DJJ and DCF case reviews Respect Act Readiness: Florida recognized as a model for statewide FASD co

2915.description: Leon County Public Works currently lacks dedicated staging and operations site for emergency response and recovery efforts. As a cornerstone of the County’s emergency response and recovery infrastructure, improvements to the Public Works building will provide a secured space that remains remain fully operational under extreme weather conditions, with centralized availability of equipment and resources to coordinate life-safety, debris management, and infrastructure restoration efforts.
2915.purpose: Critical resiliency upgrades to Leon County’s Public Works building will meet an existing need for a dedicated staging and operations site for public works emergency response and recovery efforts. Improvements include hardening of key building systems to sustain hurricane-force winds and extreme weather conditions allowing the site to be utilized for prestaging staff and equipment
2915.activities: A dedicated staging base for recovery operations during emergency events will support the County's facilitation of the prompt provision of emergency response and recovery efforts to the public.
2915.direct_services: Improvements to the Public Works building will provide a secured space that remains remain fully operational under extreme weather conditions, with centralized availability of equipment and resources to coordinate life-safety, debris management, and infrastructure restoration efforts.
2915.population: All Leon County residents will benefit from this project.
2915.outcome: Improvements made to establish a dedicated staging and operations site for emergency response and recovery efforts will provide benefits such as faster restoration of roads, utilities, and public facilities minimizing community disruption and economic loss following emergencies. Overall, the project will enhance the County’s emergency preparedness, improve public safety, and strengthen long-term community resilience against future emergency events.

3294.description: The funding will be used for the first phase of the design and construction of the new USF Health Translational Research Institute (TRI) facility, which will be a state-of-the-art research facility and allow USF to significantly grow its research portfolio and annual R&D expenditures focused primarily on healthcare and disease prevention and treatment. This facility is slated to be the anchor of a mixed-use development on the Tampa campus, referred to as the Fletcher District, which will be transformational for USF and will help to further elevate and drive economic development in the Tampa Bay area.
3294.purpose: In 2023, USF accepted an invitation to be a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU) demonstrating its impact as one of the nation's most research-intensive institutions. The funds will be used for phase one of the design and construction of the new USF Health Translational Research Institute (TRI) facility, which is expected to be the largest freestanding research facility in USF's history. The TRI will allow USF to continue to significantly grow its research portfolio going for
3294.activities: The current main research hub for USF Health on the Tampa campus is an outdated 1970s research facility which is out of wet lab space. The TRI will provide basic and pre-clinical research cores and laboratories for hundreds of biomedical researchers, and it will allow for the recruitment to Florida of additional highly sought after principal investigators that are conducting state-of-the art medical research and clinical trials in other states.
3294.direct_services: Once built, TRI’s interactive, technologically-rich setting will bring together scientists from all disciplines to ensure efforts to improve diagnosis, prevention and treatment of a range of illnesses, including emerging infectious diseases, neurodegenerative, stroke, cancer, metabolic, and heart disease, placing Tampa Bay and Florida at the forefront of medical innovation and research and cutting
3294.population: USF researchers, physicians, and students are the target population for the project. However, all Floridians, and especially elderly persons, persons with poor physical health, the developmentally disabled, physically disabled, and Floridians suffering from diseases and chronic illnesses will benefit from the work conducted within this new cutting edge research facility. USF has over 50,000 students and 15,000 employees, including more than 1,000 faculty engaged in research.
3294.outcome: The TRI facility will support researchers, graduate students, clinicians and other students and integrate knowledge from studies at multiple levels. The new TRI facility will include space for testing laboratories, core shared instrumentation facilities, clinical trials, a vivarium, and specialized laboratories. Expanded educational and new research capabilities are essential to understanding the fundamental biology underlying human health and disease. Success will be measured by an increase in overall annual R&D expenditures and health research.

2924.description: The FSU Dental School Planning project is focused on developing a comprehensive plan for a new state-of-the-art dental education facility. This planning effort will assess space and infrastructure needs, programmatic requirements, and design considerations to ensure the facility supports advanced dental education, research, and patient care. The project will result in detailed planning and engineering documents that provide a clear roadmap for construction, helping to guide the creation of a modern, efficient, and fully functional dental school. By addressing these foundational needs, the project will enhance the quality of education, expand healthcare services, and benefit students, faculty, and Florida residents.
2924.purpose: The funds will support comprehensive planning and engineering for a new state-of-the-art FSU dental school, establishing a clear roadmap for construction that supports advanced dental education, research, and patient care.
2924.activities: The funds will support planning activities including space and infrastructure assessments, programmatic analysis, and the development of architectural and engineering documents needed to design a modern dental education, research, and patient care facility.
2924.direct_services: The project will expand access to dental care services for Florida residents through future clinical training facilities while improving the quality of care delivered by dental students and faculty.
2924.population: The target population includes dental students, faculty, and Florida residents who will receive dental care services through the future facility. Once operational, the project is expected to serve hundreds of students and faculty annually and thousands of Florida residents through clinical care.
2924.outcome: The expected outcome is a fully developed, construction-ready plan for a modern dental school that supports high- quality dental education, research, and patient care. Success will be measured by completion of comprehensive planning, architectural, and engineering documents that meet accreditation standards and guide efficient facility development.

3306.description: In 2021 the Piney Point facility in Manatee County suffered a significant failure of the walls which contained water used in the processing of materials at the site. The breach created an state emergency which required a immediate response in order to protect public health and safety. Work at the facility continues to this day. This project involves the mobilization of various pumps, heavy equipment, supplies and personnel to assist in mitigating the NGS-S breach at Piney Point.
3306.purpose: Aversion of a major disaster and protection of surrounding residents lives and business's livelihoods through flooding minimization and resource protection.
3306.activities: Pump installation and monitoring, fortifying of drainage impoundments, clearing and blocking various conveyance pipe systems, procurement of various materials and equipment necessary for general site conditions.
3306.direct_services: Aversion of a major disaster and protection of surrounding residents lives and business's livelihoods through flooding minimization and resource protection.
3306.population: Several thousand residents and business employees in the immediate vicinity of the phosphogypsum stack. Residents of the greater Manatee/Hillsboro County region and all recipients of natural gas served by the pipeline that comes in close to the phosphogypsum stack.
3306.outcome: Aversion of a major disaster and protection of surrounding residents and businesses. The benefits of the project will be measured by the successful containment of contaminated water in cells at the Piney Point facility.

3066.organization: Florida Coalition on Donation dbs Donate Life
3066.description: Donate Life Florida seeks funding to support the creation and launch of a comprehensive statewide education and outreach initiative aimed at increasing organ, eye, and tissue donor registrations. Backed by comprehensive research, this campaign will target a diverse statewide audience across multiple demographics.
3066.purpose: Conduct research to shape attitudes toward donation, influence campaign messages, and address barriers to organ donation in certain demographic groups. Modernize the organ donor registry to improve user experience, ensure mobile responsiveness, and provide ADA accessibility. A comprehensive media campaign will inspire Florida's citizens to enroll in the donor registry, while website enhancements will facilitate enrollment and deliver essential information.
3066.activities: 1) Pre- and post-campaign surveys and research among different demographics to assess before campaign launch; 2) Modernization of the Joshua Abbott Organ and Tissue Donor Registry; 3) Statewide media, public relations and marketing campaigns including outreach to multiple demographics ; 4) website and donor registry upgrade/overhaul.
3066.direct_services: Through targeted media, marketing and public relations campaigns, the registry and website enhancements, and specific outreach to designated audiences, these dollars will show a demonstrated increase in enrollment on Florida’s donor registry, which will directly lead to more lives saved through organ and tissue donation, which means more lives saved through organ transplantation.
3066.population: Funding will support a statewide multimedia campaign that will target specific demographic groups. In particular, high school students will be a key target group. The campaign will serve well over 800 individuals.
3066.outcome: 1) Increased registry enrollment, including demographic data will be tracked using data from Florida's DHSMV and direct registrations to the Donate Life Florida registry. 2) Positive media engagement reactions will be monitored through platform analytics, impressions, and website traffic. 3) Increased traffic to the enhanced website will also be tracked via platform analytics.

2912.description: The Dyslexia Awareness Professional Learning Training builds foundational knowledge and understanding using a powerful dyslexia simulation, identifies common characteristics of dyslexia and explores targeted instructional practices and high value accommodations. The Learning Ally Dyslexia Awareness Training meets state dyslexia training requirements and can train educators, administrators and families. The training complements Learning Ally's Audiobook Solution which serves 101,032 students in the state of Florida.
2912.purpose: Learning Ally developed the Dyslexia Awareness Professional Learning Series as a comprehensive, research-based training designed to ensure educators have the knowledge and tools needed to support students with dyslexia and other language-based learning differences. Each module is updated annually to reflect the most current evidence, instructional practices, and state guidance, ensuring that teachers receive training aligned with evolving best practices in literacy instruction.
2912.activities: We are currently partnering with the Florida Department of Education (FLDOE) to support targeted schools identified by BEES as most in need of additional resources and training. This professional learning aligns with Florida’s Building Resiliency Through Evidence-Based Literacy Practices framework and supports educators in implementing structured literacy approaches, in accordance with Florida Statute requirements and state-approved literacy initiatives. The Dyslexia Awareness training for Educa
2912.direct_services: Learning Ally developed the Dyslexia Awareness Professional Learning Series as a comprehensive, research-based training designed to ensure educators have the knowledge and tools needed to support students with dyslexia and other language-based learning differences. Each module is updated annually to reflect the most current evidence, instructional practices, and state guidance, ensuring that teach
2912.population: The target population for the project are Florida educators and administrators, the goal is to provide this training to 1500 educators which is double the educators we were able to impact this previous year with the training. We worked closely with FLDOE through this collaboration, we aim to strengthen instructional capacity, improve literacy outcomes, and ensure that students with dyslexia in Florida receive the high-quality, evidence-based interventions they need to thrive.
2912.outcome: The Dyslexia Awareness Training builds foundational knowledge and understanding using a powerful dyslexia simulation, identifies common characteristics of dyslexia and explores targeted instructional practices and high value accommodations. The Learning Ally Dyslexia Awareness Training meets state dyslexia training requirements and can train educators, administrators and families. We will measure outcomes through educator surveys and usage metrics tracking growth of academic success program utilization.

2906.description: The YMCA of the Suncoast, in partnership with the Pinellas County School District, is seeking funding to co-locate a YMCA facility on their property in the mid- to north Pinellas County area. This initiative is designed to enhance community well-being by providing a full-service YMCA that will serve as a vital resource for youth, adults, seniors, and families throughout Pinellas County.
2906.purpose: Locating a YMCA within an underutilized portion of school property will maximize the use of public space while creating a vibrant community hub. The goal is to provide accessible programs that promote youth development, healthy living, and family engagement, serving individuals of all ages. This partnership will strengthen community connections, support lifelong learning and wellness, provide safe spaces for youth, and ensure the facility benefits the widest possible audience.
2906.activities: The co-located facility will deliver a complete suite of YMCA programs and services that intentionally advance youth development, promote healthy living, and strengthen community connections. It will provide teen engagement, safe spaces for youth, learning support, early education, after-school care, fitness, sports, senior wellness offerings, and inclusive, engaging, family-centered activities. Additional community services, such as volunteer opportunities, special events, and support programs,
2906.direct_services: The co-located facility will deliver a complete suite of YMCA programs and services that intentionally advance youth development, promote healthy living, and strengthen community connections. It will provide teen engagement, safe spaces for youth, learning support, early education, after-school care, fitness, sports, senior wellness offerings, and inclusive, engaging, family-centered activities. A
2906.population: The co-location of a YMCA within a Pinellas County school will serve the broader mid- and north-Pinellas County community, providing programs and services for individuals and families of all ages. This includes children and teens seeking enrichment and recreational opportunities, adults and older adults pursuing health and wellness programs, and families looking for safe, affordable, and accessible activities. By offering a full range of services, the YMCA will support the well-being, growth, an
2906.outcome: This project is expected to transform underutilized school space into a vibrant, full-service YMCA that benefits the entire community. It will provide accessible programs that promote youth development, academic enrichment, health and wellness, and family engagement. By repurposing existing facilities, the project maximizes community resources, strengthens social connections, supports lifelong learning and healthy living, and creates a safe, inclusive hub where individuals of all ages can learn, grow, and thrive.

3624.organization: Supportive Equity Connections of Tampa Bay
3624.description: The RISE (Reach, Inspire, Support, Empower) Youth Development Program provides trauma-informed support to at-risk youth ages 10–18 in Pinellas County, Florida. The program addresses academic challenges, mental health needs, and limited access to consistent mentorship. RISE offers weekly mentoring, individualized case management, and academic support to improve school engagement and overall stability. Workforce readiness is provided in partnership with CareerSource Tampa Bay through job readiness training, apprenticeship opportunities, and employment pathways. RISE operates in six-week cycles and currently serves 25 youth, with additional youth on a waitlist. This project will allow the program to remain consistent and sustainable, supporting continued service delivery and positive youth outcomes.
3624.purpose: The purpose of the requested funds is to maintain consistent and sustainable delivery of the RISE Youth Development Program by supporting core staffing, program operations, and workforce readiness activities. The funding will ensure continued access to mentoring, case management, academic support, and employment preparation services for participating youth.
3624.activities: Funds will support weekly mentoring sessions, individualized case management, academic support coordination, workforce readiness training, apprenticeship and employment preparation activities in partnership with CareerSource Tampa Bay, youth engagement activities, and program coordination necessary to ensure consistent service delivery.
3624.direct_services: Direct services include mentoring, case management support, academic engagement assistance, workforce readiness training, job preparation activities, apprenticeship and employment exposure, and referrals to supportive services for youth and their families.
3624.population: The target population is at-risk youth ages 10–18 residing in St. Petersburg and surrounding areas of Pinellas County. The program is expected to serve approximately 25-35 youth annually, with additional youth supported through referrals and waitlist engagement as capacity allows.
