3624.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved school engagement, increased workforce readiness, strengthened life skills, and improved overall stability among participating youth. Outcomes will be measured through attendance tracking, participation records, academic engagement indicators, workforce readiness milestones, case management documentation, and periodic program evaluations.

3625.organization: The Children's Museum of Tampa, Inc, dba
3625.description: Funding will enable Glazer Children's Museum (GCM) to complete the final design and planning for a first-floor renovation and exhibit expansion. This renovation will create a new and engaging entry for families and allow for the construction of a new 3000 square foot permanent exhibit, as well as a dedicated rotating exhibit space. The renovation will also increase accessibility for those with disabilities and create more functional space for school visitors.
3625.purpose: Funding will enable Glazer Children's Museum (GCM) to complete the final design and planning for a first-floor renovation and exhibit expansion. This renovation will create a new and engaging entry for families and allow for the construction of a new 3000 square foot permanent exhibit, as well as a dedicated rotating exhibit space. The renovation will also increase accessibility for those with disabilities and create more functional space for school visitors.
3625.activities: The renovation will double the amount of space on the museum's first floor dedicated to exhibition and programming, create a more accessible and streamlined entry, as well as increase family/companion restroom space, which is a necessity in a museum that serves young children.
3625.direct_services: The Glazer Children's Museum creates high quality play experiences for young children and their families, as well as over 22,000 students and educators each year. The museum offers daily programming, high quality exhibits, as well as in depth programming for children birth-10 and their families and caregivers.
3625.population: Developmentally disabled, economically disadvantaged, physically disabled, parents, teachers, caregivers, preschool students, grade school students. >800 expected to be served.
3625.outcome: Improve physical and mental health, enrich cultural experience, and improve quality of education.

3282.description: Existing chapel to be demolished and a new prototype chapel will be built on the Main Unit.
3282.purpose: This project will demolish the existing Sumter CI Main Unit chapel which has been condemned as unsafe and will design and construct a new Main Unit chapel building.
3282.activities: This project will include demolition activities of the existing chapel as well as some minor site work, various construction activities and project management services, architectural and engineering design activities and approval and permit services.
3282.direct_services: Citizens will be provided with a modern facility that will provide religious services for all faiths for the Sumter CI inmates, staff, visitors and volunteers. This facility will also provide general purpose institution meeting space.
3282.population: The direct target population that will be served by this project is the Sumter CI Main Unit inmates (current capacity 1,551 males) and the Sumter CI Work Camp (current capacity 350 males). Indirectly the Sumter CI staff, visitors and volunteers will also be served by this project.
3282.outcome: Both the Main Unit and Work Camp inmates will receive improved religious services and activities due to adequate and modern facilities. Inmate spiritual health may improve with resulting reduced recidivism. Additional inmate dormitory space will be made available when temporary chapel activities are moved to the new chapel. Chapel and staff retention may improve due to modern working conditions. These outcomes may be measured by staff retention and recidivism.

3501.description: Funds support the construction of new headquarters facility to support CCR's programs, including CCR School, a year- round early education center providing ALICE and homeless families with high-quality care; developmental screenings/intervention through the Wellness and Early Intervention Program; and an outreach program providing early educators with specialized trainings, coaching, and higher education pathways to improve their classrooms.
3501.purpose: The funds requested are to support construction of new headquarter facility. As such, we would anticipate that, if awarded, funds would be administered through a reimbursement arrangement. If construction is not completed as required, then we suggest no reimbursement. If the award were an advance payment, then we would suggest full restitution of any funds awarded if the work was not completed in accordance with the agreement.
3501.activities: Funds support the construction of new headquarters facility to support CCR's programs, including CCR School, a year-round early education center providing ALICE and homeless families with high-quality care; developmental screenings/intervention through the Wellness and Early Intervention Program; and an outreach program providing early educators with specialized trainings, coaching, and higher education pathways to improve their classrooms.
3501.direct_services: The state-of-the-art campus will significantly benefit CCR's programs by increasing enrollment by 64%, expansion of therapeutic services, the addition of training spaces for early educators and become a hub for connecting families with services to foster growth and stability.
3501.population: ALICE and homeless families, More than 4,500 children and over 300 teachers were impacted by CCR programming last year.
3501.outcome: CCR utilizes research based approaches to support our outcomes child development and kindergarten readiness. CCR has prior outcome data available upon request. CCR School Outcomes: Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ) measures developmental milestones, Environmental Screening Questionnaire (ESQ) measures home environment and access to care, CLASS measures classroom quality. Outreach: CLASS measures teacher retention and progress toward degree attainment and certification renewals

3377.description: City staff requests $600,000 of the estimated $1.2 million in design services for what is expected to be $12 million needed to implement the critical infrastructure improvements in the River Park East neighborhood, encompassing approximately 3,350 centerline feet of roadway. The City has funding available to initiate progressive design-build at 10%. The requested funding will address major resiliency and hardening challenges identified in the Kimley-Horn Multi-Basin Assessments Report, which highlighted the area's vulnerability to severe weather, frequent flooding, and interruptions to essential life-sustaining services such as water, sewer, and solid waste. The project will include the rebuilding and renewal of the 60-year-old wastewater, water, fire hydrant, and stormwater networks, along with the installation of pump stations. These improvements will increase resilience, reduce floodi
3377.purpose: The project will include the rebuilding and renewal of the 60-year-old wastewater, water, fire hydrant, and stormwater networks, along with the installation of pump stations. These improvements will increase resilience, reduce flooding risks, and harden criticial infrastructure through modern reliability engineering--ultimately protecting public health and safety while extending the service life of these essential systems.
3377.direct_services: Needed to implement critical improvements in the River Park East neighborhood, encompassing approximately 3,350 centerline fee of roadway.
3377.outcome: Rebuilding and renewal of the 6-year-old wastewater, water, fire hydrant, and stormwater networks, along with the installation of pump stations. These improvements will increase resilience, reduce flooding risks, and harden critical infrastructure through modern reliability engineering--ultimately protecting public health and safety while extending the service life of these essential systems.

3283.description: The Florida Department of Education will choose 6 schools to expand the Guardian Angel Program. The students at these news campuses, like their peers from the previous allocation, will be protected by an innovative drone program designed to stop school shooters immediately.
3283.purpose: As an expansion to the initial pilot program, additional schools will be onboarded with the object to create extra layers of school safety and aid students in their learning environment.
3283.activities: Expanded deployment of the active shooter response system designed to respond quickly to threats of violence and active events on school campuses.
3283.direct_services: Schools are soft targets for active shooters. This program will increase response times should an active shooter event occur. The program will assist first responders by ensuring a school shooters can either be neutralized or mitigated providing law enforcement with a better opportunity to stop the incident.
3283.population: Students, parents, teachers, and school administrators.
3283.outcome: The program will create extra layers of school safety and aid students in their learning environment. We will measure reduction in violent events to occur. Increase response time and threat intervention success rates. Surveys assessing law enforcement, staff, student and parent perceptions of safety before and after implementation.

3476.organization: South County Mental Health Center, Inc.
3476.description: South County Mental Health Center (SCMHC) is a private not for profit behavioral health provider in Palm Beach County (PBC). The enter has been in continuous service to PBC for 50 years. We operate 35 crisis stabilization unit (CSU) beds in Delray Beach and 16 beds in Belle Glade. The purpose of this request is to support safety issues at the Delray CSU facility. The building housing both CSU I and CSU II, is 35 years old and in need of a completely new door locking system and a nursing station upgrade for both units. Both needs are critical in ensuring client and staff safety.
3476.purpose: SCMHC is requesting funding to increase security and safety measures. Our nursing stations have open access, potentially providing patients access to critical equipment, records and the nursing office which houses the medications. The proposed nursing renovations will limit access to personnel only, eliminating any potential for harm or danger. Our locking system is no longer supported, resulting in manual access. The proposed system will increase efficiency for rapid emergency response and egre
3476.activities: CSU services include activities aimed at the reduction of acute emotional crisis to ensure the safety of an individual. The services we are providing are for patients experiencing a mental health crisis who are in need of a safe, secure and locked environment to protect them from themselves and others. Requested funds will ensure a safer environment by restricting access to vulnerable areas.
3476.direct_services: Direct services (de-escalation assessment) can be enhanced by reducing the time spent on having to redirect patients from elopement attempts, accessing vulnerable areas on the CSUs, altercations with others or retrieving dangerous materials from self-harm or harm to others. The more efficient locking system and the secured nursing stations will address the safety insecurity on the crisis units.
3476.population: The target population to be served: People with poor mental health, economically disadvantaged persons, homeless, university/college students and currently or formally incarcerated persons. Up to 800-1000 individuals are expected to be served.
3476.outcome: The benefit/outcome of this project is to reduce the number of incidents such as elopements, destruction of property or staff/client injuries. The measure will be a new locking system and more secure nursing stations will reduce elopements, property damage and staff/patient injuries by 10%. The method for measuring the benefits or outcome will be a decrease in internal incident reports and invoices from property replacement due to destruction.

3305.description: Project will replace the outdated community building with a modern facility that better serves recreational and programmatic needs. It will include a multipurpose room, concession area with covered seating, restrooms, storage, office/custodial space and outdoor terrace. Improvements include upgraded accessibility, native landscaping and integration with existing tennis courts. Infrastructure upgrades include new sewer connection, LED lighting, HVAC systems and a lightning protection system.
3305.purpose: Project will replace the outdated community building with a modern facility that better serves recreational and programmatic needs. It will include a multipurpose room, concession area with covered seating, restrooms, storage, office/custodial space and outdoor terrace. Improvements include upgraded accessibility, native landscaping and integration with existing tennis courts. Infrastructure upgrades include new sewer connection, LED lighting, HVAC systems and a lightning protection system.
3305.activities: The City will oversee design firm and construction company to deliver the project
3305.direct_services: Area and City residents will receive a safe, modern community space for educational, cultural and recreational purposes.
3305.population: Target population is the residents of the City of South Miami.
3305.outcome: The outcome of this project will be a new safe, modern community space that will serve educational, cultural and recreational purposes.

3310.description: The City completed an inspection that indicated the existing 48-inch culvert located over Broad Canal along SW 58th Street between SW 63rd Court and SW 57th Drive is structurally deficient and needs to be replaced. The project is in the best interests of the State of Florida as its residents and visitors will benefit from the improved roadway system. The repair is critical to the deteriorating culvert presents an immediate risk to public safety. The design work is 95% completed, however the project still needs to be permitted. It is expected that construction will commence in 2026. The total cost of the project is $500,000.
3310.purpose: The replacement of this culvert is critical not only for regular access to the area, but also for ensuring that the Broad Canal remains accessible in the event of emergencies. The current deteriorating condition of the culvert presents an immediate risk to public safety, and the completion of this project is essential to guarantee that emergency vehicles, residents, and first responders can traverse the area without obstruction or risk of further structural failure.
3310.activities: The City will oversee design firm and construction company to deliver the project
3310.direct_services: Area and City residents will receive a safe and functioning roadway system for daily transportation needs and recreational purposes
3310.population: Residents of the immediate area will benefit the most due to their proximity to the bridge. However, it is also expected all City residents and visitors will benefit from the improved roadway system. It is also important to highlight that since access is limited to waterways, having this access point is critical for repair.
3310.outcome: The project will repair a failed culvert and roadway. This will allow safe transportation and access for area residents and citizens of the City at-large. The plan will be permitted and inspected by various permitting agencies ensuring compliance with all necessary requirements. Construction shall be overseen by engineer on record.

3325.description: The Reconstruction of the St. Johns River Northbank Bulkheads is a multi-year, City-funded, initiative focused on protecting and enhancing the Northbank riverfront. The project includes stabilizing and raising the existing bulkheads to preserve adjacent public and private riverfront properties, improving shoreline resilience, and supporting expanded recreational access to the St. Johns River. This reconstruction is essential to enabling the development of the public Hanz Tanzler Marina and strengthening long-term waterfront infrastructure for the community.
3325.purpose: Reconstruction of the St. Johns River Northbank Bulkheads is a multi-year project primarily funded by the City to preserve Riverfront properties (both public and private), raise bulkhead caps and provide for improved recreational access to the river. This segment of bulkhead will support construction of the public Hanz Tanzler Marina.
3325.activities: The project will provide improved storm resilience, improved pedestrian riverfront access and provide for construction of the adjacent public-access Hanz Tanzler Marina.
3325.direct_services: Improved storm resistance. Reduced flooding from high tides. Better pedestrian and boat access along the riverfront.
3325.outcome: The project will strengthen storm-related flood resistance along the Northbank, resulting in fewer occurrences of high- tide and storm-driven flooding on adjacent downtown streets. It will also enhance pedestrian and boating access to the riverfront, creating a more inviting and usable public space. These improvements are expected to increase pedestrian activity along the downtown riverfront and support greater boat traffic to the future public-access Hanz Tanzler Marina, which is planned for construction following completion of the bulkhead project.

3248.description: Funding will allow the City of Panama City to support large industrial growth. Currently, the City is limited in capacity to pr ovide additional water distribution and fire flow to the Port of Panama City's future economic development sites. The requ ested funds will be used to engineer, acquire property, and construct a 5 million gallon water storage tank. This will also support large housing developments which support Tyndall Air Force Base's needs as the base continues its build out. T his is a joint project between Port Panama City, Bay County Board of Commissioners, and the City of Panama City to co ntinue to contribute to the success of Port Panama City’s Intermodal Distribution Center. This will also support broader d evelopment of Panama City North and unincorporated Bay County, which is expected to see tremendous growth in the n ext 20 years.
3248.purpose: Funding will allow the City of Panama City to support large industrial growth. Currently, the City is limited in capacity to provide additional water distribution and fire flow to the Port of Panama City's future economic development sites. The requested funds will be used to engineer, acquire property, and construct a 5 million gallon water storage tank. This will also support large housing developments which support Tyndall Air Force Base's needs as the base continues its build out.
3248.activities: The requested funds for this proposed project will allow the City of Panama City to start the project with design, engineering and permitting.
3248.direct_services: Increased fire flow, volume and pressure necessary for further development of the Intermodal Distribution Center resulting in increased development and job opportunities and life safety for industry and residents.
3248.population: All residents of the city and county who live or work in the area of the port. 200,000+
3248.outcome: Increasing available fire flow, pressure and volume will allow for continued economic development in the form of advanced manufacturing. Without additional water storage capacity future expansion of Port PC's industrial Park will be limited until water distribution deficiencies are addressed. Improved fire flow, volume and pressures. Increased expansion of industry at Port PC's Intermodal Distribution Center.

3284.description: Continued education and training are vital to the services provided for public health and safety. Hernando County (County) Public Safety departments do not have the adequate training facilities available and must travel out of the County for their training needs. The departments have been working on identifying appropriate land and funding to construct facilities that can accommodate the ongoing training needs of their staff since 2012. While numerous training facilities are in other areas of the state, it means our public servants are not available to respond timely or effectively due to the distances away from Hernando County. It also requires cooperative and sometimes complex scheduling. A suitable facility should be constructed to accommodate continued training requirements as well as provide new fire rescue and law enforcement candidates a proper environment and facilities to learn
3284.purpose: The training center will be utilized for fire, emergency medical services and law enforcement for training of their personnel to prepare them for their jobs of protecting and caring for the citizens of Hernando County. Having the training center within the County alleviates the necessity to take personnel out of the county to train. This leaves them available, if needed, to respond to calls.
3284.activities: The funds will be used for design, engineering and construction of the shared facility by Fire, EMS and law enforcement. By designing a shared compound with fire, emergency medical services, and law enforcement will be beneficial and cost effective by sharing the facility.
3284.direct_services: The funds will be used for design, engineering and construction of the shared facility by Fire, EMS and law enforcement. By designing a shared compound with fire, emergency medical services, and law enforcement will be beneficial and cost effective by sharing the facility.
3284.population: The entire Hernando County population of 224,551. Anyone within the County who calls on fire, EMS or law enforcement will benefit from the skills of personnel from all agencies.
3284.outcome: Funding will provide for the construction of the facility which in turn allows for training to be accomplished in County. Training will be measured by the success of law enforcement, firefighters and paramedics in the field while responding to the citizens.

3165.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3165.description: This funding will support positions and equipment within UF/IFAS for dedicated clam research based in Cedar Key and will work collaboratively with industry across the state to solve real world problems in the shellfish culture process. Farm- raised shellfish are a $44+ million industry in the state of Florida. Currently there is a lack of capacity and expertise to address challenges like mortality events and genetics that hinder the commercial industry from growing.
3165.purpose: These funds will increase in-state research capacity to be able to address challenges faced by Florida's shellfish aquaculture industry. Funds will directly support research position(s) dedicated to ongoing clam research studying mortality events and envirnomental factors that are preventing commercial industry growth and long-term sustainability.
3165.activities: This research position(s) will be based in Cedar Key and work hand in hand with clam farmers to tackle and solve research problems that impact the long-term viability of Florida's clam industry. Priority research topics include factors influencing summer mortality of shellfish, options for selective breeding of cultured clams, and understanding and mitigating environmental stressors that are hampering this industry.
3165.direct_services: There will be no direct services provided to citizens but outcomes of the project will produce data and valuable information for shellish farmers and industry stakeholders.
3165.population: Hundreds of clam farmers across the state will benefit from this project along with regional economies that depend on this industry. While the immediate focus of the research capacity will be on issues impacting Cedar Key the position(s) and the research will support clam aquaculture across the state and serve as a hub for expertise to help commericial industry.
3165.outcome: The short-term outcome of this project is that dedicated research capacity for clams will begin to answer commercial industry questions around summer mortality, selective breeding, and clam culture challenges that are currently constraining this industry. This will support innovation and resiliency within the clam industry statewide. The long-term outcome is that Florida will have the research and data necessary to help our shellfish aquaculture industry be competitive and remain a significant economic driver in our coastal communities.

2966.description: The requested funds will support workforce innovation & career development for individuals with intellectual and developmental differences, empowering these individuals to achieve meaningful employment, enhance economic self- sufficiency, earn competitive wages, and contribute to their community. Programs will improve quality of education by enhancing vocational training in career tracks, increase economic activity by preparing individuals to fill workforce gaps, and create job opportunities.
2966.purpose: The requested funds will support workforce innovation & career development for individuals with intellectual and developmental differences, empowering these individuals to achieve meaningful employment, enhance economic self- sufficiency, earn competitive wages, and contribute to their community. Programs will improve quality of education by enhancing vocational training in career tracks, increase economic activity by preparing individuals to fill workforce gaps, and create job opportunities.
2966.activities: The funds will support the innovative Career Campus and Triumph Industries programs for individuals with intellectual and developmental differences. Career Campus offers vocational and work readiness training in specific career tracks, industry certifications, internships and on-the-job training. Triumph Industries provides paid employment and wrap- around services.
2966.direct_services: Services will provide individuals with access to person-centered direct services, including career-focused education through Career Campus, paid employment opportunities at Triumph Industries, work readiness training, job development services, and mental health and well-being support. These services promote self-determination, economic self-sufficiency, and community integration.
2966.population: The target population served by this project is individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD), many of whom also experience economic disadvantage, poor physical health, and poor mental health. The project primarily serves young adults and adults who are transitioning into or seeking sustainable employment and greater independence. Through workforce innovation and career development services, approximately 75 individuals are expected to be served during the funding period.
2966.outcome: The expected outcomes of this project include improved physical and mental health, enhanced economic self- sufficiency, and increased workforce participation for individuals with IDD. Participants will gain job skills, employment readiness, and access to meaningful work opportunities that support long-term independence. Outcomes will be measured through program enrollment, job placement data, income and employment status tracking, and participant assessments related to health, confidence, and self-sufficiency.

3626.description: The Florida Youth Pathways to Healthcare Careers Pilot Program is designed to strengthen students’ understanding of healthcare work, expand interest in high-demand fields, and build readiness for future training.
3626.purpose: This pilot project expands Florida’s healthcare workforce by giving middle and high school students hands-on exposure to healthcare careers. The pilot connects underserved students to hospitals, clinics, labs, and training spaces to explore roles and build foundational skills. It creates a clear pathway from early exposure to CTE health academies, dual enrollment, or entry-level certifications.
3626.activities: The Florida Youth Pathways to Healthcare Careers Pilot Program gives students structured exposure to healthcare careers through site visits, hands-on demonstrations, CPR and basic first-aid training, career modules, skill-building workshops, and interactive sessions with healthcare staff. Students also receive guidance on CTE health academies, dual enrollment, and certification pathways to help them move into Florida’s healthcare pipeline.
3626.direct_services: The program is designed to strengthen students’ understanding of healthcare work, expand interest in high-demand fields, and build readiness for future training.
3626.population: The target population to be served by this project includes elderly persons, person with poor physical health, economically disadvantaged persons, grade school and high school students. Between 100 and 200 individuals are expected to be served.
3626.outcome: Improved physical and mental health will be realized as student participants will be exposed to healthcare careers and professional exploration while encouraged and prepared to enter the pipeline of healthcare workers needed for Florida citizens' access to healthcare and growth in the healthcare workforce and measured through attendance rosters, student/parent/program surveys and evaluations. Economic activity will improve or increase as students pursuing health-related education pathways feed into Florida’s high-demand healthcare workforce as measured through longitudinal tracking. Immediate job opportunities will be created by students earning CPR training or completing introductory module

3250.description: Rehabilitation of a bridge on Frankford Ave. critical to First Responder access to residents and industry. Residents, Suzuki's R&D facility, the Department of Homeland Security, the Bay County Medical Examiner's office all rely on this bridge to access their businesses, offices, and homes. This bridge has an estimated 5 years left on its current lifespan. Rehabilitation of the bridge will increase that to 15-20 years.
3250.purpose: Rehabilitation of a bridge on Frankford Ave. critical to First Responder access to residents and industry. Residents, Suzuki's R&D facility, Department of Homeland Security, the Bay County Medical Examiner's office all rely on this bridge to access their businesses, offices, and homes. This bridge has an estimated 5 years left on its current lifespan. Rehabilitation of the bridge will increase that to 15-20 years.
3250.activities: Design and construction of the improvements include but are not limited to design, permitting, surveying, construction and CEI. Enhancements will include a prefabricated pedestrian bridge.
3250.direct_services: Funding would extend the life of the bridge 15-20 years and allow for safe transit of pedestrians. This will maintain critical access to Suzuki and allow for an expansion project which will create above market rate jobs. Rehabilitation and enhancements will allow for First Responder access to industrial sites, neighborhoods and DHS and Medical Examiner offices.
3250.population: All residents of the city and county who live or work in the area. 5,000+
3250.outcome: Rehabilitation and Enhancements of the bridge will allow for a longer life of the bridge and add safe pedestrian access. These improvements will extend the life of the bridge from 5 years to 15-20 years. Extending the bridge's life will allow for the expansion of Suzuki's R&D facility, which is one of two facilities globally. It will also allow Suzuki to expand and develop the second phase of the facility. Additionally, it will better enable future advanced manufacturing development possible on adjacent vacant property. Structural evaluation. Job creation and development.

3253.description: These funds will go toward the acquisition of 1.7 acres of waterfront property at the NE foot of the Shalimar Bridge in Okaloosa County. The property is one of the few undeveloped waterfront properties in south Okaloosa County and provides beautiful views from Hwy 85/Eglin Parkway and the entrance to Garnier's Bayou. After acquisition the property would be turned into a community park serving residents and visitors alike. This will compliment the Town and County park project across the water on the SE foot of the Shalimar Bridge.
3253.purpose: Waterfront property will be preserved for public use and recreational enjoyment. This property sits at the mouth to Garnier's Bayou, is heavily treed and provides a beautiful vista into the Bayou. The County purchased the property on the opposite side of the bridge, which was a blighted, homeless encampment, and is making it a nice wayside park at the entrance to the Town of Shalimar.
3253.activities: The acquisition of the property and multiplication of the State funding with at least a 3-1 local match for the acquisition and subsequent development of the property in a community asset. The County will handle the purchase, acquisition and subsequent development of the park property with its resources and staffing. The Town or the County will maintain the property in prepurtity.
3253.direct_services: Public recreation and the preservation of open space on the waterfront, at a highly visible location at the entranceway to Garnier's Bayou and directly on Eglin Parkway. Available public waterfront property is a scarce commodity and has almost completely disappeared in our County. Although Okaloosa County has taken tremendous steps to acquire many of these properties and preserve this space, it ne
3253.population: The targeted population will be all residents of (220,000+) and visitors to Okaloosa County, which, in total, is in excess of one million annually.
3253.outcome: The acquisition of the property and development of the park property by the Town of Shalimar and Okaloosa County. The park will have parking, bathrooms, dockage, pavilions, trails, open space, and fishing.

3167.description: The completion of a new U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) office at the Port of Fernandina. The current building has been deemed inoperable, and without a new building CBP could cease operations in Fernandina and the Port could lose its "Port of Entry Designation". The port of entry designation allows the Port of Fernandina with CBP to carry out customs and immigration operations including conducting inspections, processing immigration documents, and to collect duties and taxes.
3167.purpose: The completion of a new U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) office at the Port of Fernandina. The current building has been deemed inoperable, and without a new building CBP could cease operations in Fernandina and the Port could lose its "Port of Entry Designation".
3167.activities: The port of entry designation allows the Port of Fernandina with CBP to carry out customs and immigration operations including conducting inspections, processing immigration documents, and to collect duties and taxes.
3167.direct_services: By keeping the Port of Entry designation, the Port can continue to be an economic driver in Northeast Florida and be used as a tool to attract more businesses and high paying jobs to the region.
3167.population: Statewide and regional impact to the general public. (Ensuring public safety as an immigration enforcement hub, economic benefits of an active port and the jobs it provides to the local economy).
3167.outcome: Continued business and economic impacts for the region. Partner with the Nassau Co. Economic Development Board and Nassau County to track business inquiries that inquire about the port and its operations.

3427.description: FNCAC is Florida’s accredited State Chapter and membership organization for Children’s Advocacy Centers (CACs). We are responsible for advancing the CAC model statewide, strengthening local CACs through training, technical assistance, and development, and administering funding to support their operations. CACs coordinate a trauma- informed, multidisciplinary response to child abuse and crimes against children, working closely with law enforcement, DCF, and the judiciary. They also provide advocacy and mental health services to children and families, and lead prevention efforts through education and outreach. This project will provide pass-through funding to support member CACs in the implementation of the CAC Model and advance FNCAC’s Growth & Development Plan to address service gaps and improve program evaluation throughout the state.
3427.purpose: The requested funds will directly support the continued delivery and enhancement of services for child victims of abuse across Florida. Specifically, this project will: Provide pass-through funding to local CACs to sustain critical victim services, especially in light of recent decline federal funding. Support FNCAC’s Growth & Development Plan, which focuses on identifying service gaps, improving program evaluation, and strengthening statewide capacity. Ensure that CACs can maintain a coordinate
3427.activities: FNCAC will oversee and support the work of Florida’s CACs by administering pass-through funding, monitoring performance, and providing technical assistance. As part of our Growth & Development Plan, we will continue the analysis of statewide service gaps data, and identifying benchmarks to strengthen the CAC network. Local CACs will continue to coordinate and lead Multidisciplinary Teams (MDTs) in their communities, ensuring a trauma-informed response to child abuse cases. They will provide dire
3427.direct_services: FNCAC will meet directly with stakeholders in phase 2 of its Growth & Development Plan. All agencies will provide training & orientation to DCF, LE, SAO, and other investigative and service providers. CACs will provide core services which include: Medical /Psych Evaluations, Forensic/Specialized Interviews, Advocacy, Mental Health, Case Review, and Prevention/Education & Outreach to child victims,
3427.population: The target population for this project are child-victims of abuse and their families, multidisciplinary partners such as law enforcement, state attorneys offices, mental health professionals, etc., and local community stakeholders. CACs report serving over 25,000 children in 2024.
3427.outcome: Sustain and strengthen the delivery of services to child victims and their families. Project will help maintain essential operations, address service gaps, and improve the quality and reach of victim services—particularly in communities impacted by reductions in federal funding. Outcomes will be measured through a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods: Monthly financial and programmatic reports submitted by CACs to FNCAC, including service delivery data and expenditures. Monitoring and compliance reviews conducted by FNCAC to ensure adherence to grant requirements and service standards. Outcome Measurement System (OMS) surveys, administered by CACs in accordance with National C

3168.description: Fernandina Beach is a 200-year-old city located on Amelia Island between the Atlantic Ocean and the Amelia River. The City's Downtown Historic District consists of a flourishing downtown commercial district bustling with shops, restaurants, breweries, cultural sites, and 60 blocks of expertly preserved Victorian-era homes. In 2023, 78.7% (815,174) of Amelia Island's 1,035,800 visitors ranked the Historic District as a "Top Activity Enjoyed," scoring higher than even the Island's beaches. Fernandina Beach's downtown Historic District has an aging street-scape with deteriorating landscaping, failing lighting, uneven and mismatched sidewalk materials, insufficient ADA components and weather-related damage. The Historic Fernandina Beach Downtown Streetscapes Restoration and Preservation Project will improve pedestrian access and local tourism which generates over 25% of Nassau County jobs, w
3168.purpose: Travel publications consistently rank Amelia Island one of best island and beach destinations in the U.S. In 2023, Amelia Island tourism contributed nearly $1 billion in economic impact, employed over 25% of Nassau County, FL residents, and provided over $342 million in wages to Amelia Island employees. Historic Downtown Fernandina Beach, a business and residential district populated with Victorian-aged business structures and homes, was ranked a favorite activity by 78.7% of Amelia Island visit
3168.activities: Historic Downtown Fernandina Beach is comprised of over 60 blocks of Victorian-era buildings listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The Historic Downtown is bustling with restaurants, shops, cultural activities, churches, and landside and waterside tours. At 200 years old, significant restoration activities have been designed to preserve the City as one of Florida's most desirable residential, business, and tourism economic engines. The Historic Fernandina Beach Downtown Streetscape
3168.direct_services: This project will provide physical protection of persons and property. Additionally, this project will preserve specific immediate job opportunities for local residents. Tourism is Nassau County's largest job creator, creating over 25% of all jobs and paying 38% of all sales taxes. Given that 78.7% of Amelia Island visitors ranked visiting the historic Fernandina Beach downtown as one of their fav
3168.population: Residents, visitors, businesses and workers are the target population. Fernandina Beach has 13,647 residents. Amelia Island, on which Fernandina Beach is located, attracted 1,035,800 visitors in 2024 and of those, 815,174 reported that visiting the Historic Downtown Fernandina Beach was a favorite activity, even more than local beaches. Beyond seasonal tourism, Fernandina Beach hosts recurring cultural events and festivals that bring hundreds of thousands of additional visitors - and tourism rev
3168.outcome: The benefit of the Historic Fernandina Beach Downtown Revitalization and Critical Infrastructure Improvement Project will be preservation and construction improvements of historic Downtown Fernandina Beach, a business and residential district populated with Victorian-aged business structures and homes which hosts cultural events and festivals that attract hundreds of thousands of visitors each year. Additionally, the Downtown is also home to the Port of Fernandina, the CSX railroad, and WestRock and Rayonier Mills, all of which generate over 1,000 local jobs. The outcome of this impact can be measured through pre-and-post comparative data about tourism and citizen satisfaction surveys.

3431.description: This project enhances safety, cleanliness, and functionality in Okaloosa County’s Forensic Pre-Trial Unit and Behavioral Wellness common areas through the installation of durable, non-porous flooring. The upgrade supports therapeutic programming, daily operations, and staff-client interaction in high-use spaces, promoting efficiency, hygiene, and a secure, recovery-focused environment.
3431.purpose: Expanding on a donation from a generous community member last year that created a full kitchen at the Forensic Pre- Trial Unit (FPTU), this request seeks funding to install non-porous flooring in the FPTU kitchen, common areas, and in the Behavioral Wellness Program common areas improving safety, cleanliness, and functionality for individuals and staff in a secure behavioral health setting.
3431.activities: This flooring upgrade supports daily meal prep, group activities, and/or frequent staff-client interaction in high-traffic areas. New flooring that resists wear, reduces noise, and promotes hygiene with a seamless, non-porous surface while offering long-term durability, safety, and easy maintenance in a demanding environment is ideal for both spaces. In total this project will cover approximately 6,050 sq ft. of floor space.
3431.direct_services: The requested funding will directly support essential daily services for individuals served in the Forensic Pre-Trial Unit and Behavioral Wellness Programs. This includes safe meal preparation, therapeutic group activities, and structured staff-client engagement in shared spaces. These services promote stability, routine, and recovery in a secure behavioral health setting.
3431.population: This project enhances a behavioral healthcare environment with modern, durable flooring that promotes a welcoming, non-institutional atmosphere while reducing allergens, mold, and bacteria. It supports individuals facing mental or physical health challenges, economic hardship, homelessness, or criminal justice involvement, fostering dignity, safety, and recovery in shared treatment spaces.
3431.outcome: High-quality, non-porous flooring improves infection control, reduces slip hazards, and withstands heavy use, lowering long-term maintenance costs. Its seamless surface promotes hygiene, minimizes noise, and enhances overall safety and comfort while creating a more stable, professional, and therapeutic environment for clients and staff in a high-traffic behavioral healthcare facility.

3428.description: Fixed Capital Outlay funding will be used to build a two-story transitional housing facility on a cleared site. It will serve individuals completing the Forensic Pre-Trial or Detoxification Programs, and those experiencing homelessness, including veterans and people with disabilities. This project promotes stable transitions to permanent housing while reducing recidivism, homelessness, and costly ER, hospital, and jail visits across Okaloosa County and surrounding areas. A previous appropriation of $850,000 was approved. Since that time, the project is a tear down and rebuild due to the hazardous conditions of the structure. The cost of demolition, and work already completed to renovate the building, as well as payment of two architectural and engineering plans impacted the original appropriations to the point where there is not enough current funding to build the much-needed transitiona
3428.purpose: Fixed Capital Outlay funding will be used to finish building a two-story transitional housing facility on a cleared site. It will serve individuals completing the Forensic Pre-Trial or Detoxification Programs, and those experiencing or at-risk for homelessness, including veterans and people with disabilities. The goal is stable transition to permanent housing. Return on investment includes reduced recidivism in ERs, hospitals, jails, and lower homelessness in Okaloosa County and nearby areas.
3428.activities: The facility will house up to 11 individuals, providing stable, transitional housing with a clear path to permanent placement. Residents will have access to Bridgeway Center, Inc. programs and services that support long-term housing stability and self-sufficiency.
3428.direct_services: This facility will provide safe, stable, short-term housing. Residents will be required to work or have a source of income, pay rent, and cover personal expenses such as food and laundry. This self-sustaining model promotes responsibility and supports the transition to permanent housing.
3428.population: The funds requested will serve 25-50 individuals annually. These target individuals, populations or groups may include persons with poor mental health, economically disadvantaged persons, individuals experiencing homelessness, substance users (in health services, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, and/or drug offenders (in criminal justice).
3428.outcome: The transitional housing program in Okaloosa County aims to provide stable housing, access to food, healthcare, and employment support to reduce homelessness, improve mental and physical health, and lower criminal justice involvement. It fosters cultural inclusivity and community safety while promoting workforce readiness. Outcomes will be measured by reduced homelessness, decreased recidivism, improved employment rates, and lower reliance on public crisis systems, aligning with Florida's priorities for stronger, safer communities.

3418.description: This project seeks to remodel the existing athletic facility structure for Pasco High School and purchase necessary equipment for those expanded facilities. In doing so the project will provide additional opportunities for physical education at Pasco High School through the improved athletic facilities.
3418.purpose: These funds are to provide a quality athletic training facility for Pasco High School. Updating the facilities will increase the physical education capabilities for the school as well as provide benefits for the school's athletics.
3418.activities: All services related to physical education for students at Pasco High School and the training student athletes.
3418.direct_services: High school athletics is a part of the education process for students and high school athletics provides significant community benefits beyond student training. This project will provide increased access for students at Pasco High School to athletic competition and other physical education opportunities.
3418.population: Students at Pasco High School will be served by increased physical education options and athletic opportunities, and the greater Pasco County community will also benefit from the existence of these athletic facilities.
3418.outcome: Standard student progress and success measures will be utilized as directed in state law.

3069.description: Saving/ renovation of the historic Oneida Bungalow Court. All 24 houses are in an accelerated rate of disrepair and extensive work to be saved from demolition. This money will be utilized for infrastructure work to make the houses safe and habitable, roof, plumbing, AC, electrical, windows and doors.
3069.purpose: To stabilize and make the houses safe and habitable. To ensure the houses are renovated and modernized but keep the work done to the Secretary of the Interiors Standards for historic preservation on all exteriors.
3069.activities: In ground and in house plumbing, new electrical service, houses rewired, new roofs, Central heat and air, roofs, doors and windows, foundation repair.
3069.direct_services: Affordable housing, safer cleaned up neighborhood, greater opportunity for businesses in the area, cultural and historical landmark saved.
3069.population: Anyone currently living in the neighborhood and newcomers to the area.
3069.outcome: The property will be locally landmarked and protected from demolition and the area will be totally rehabilitated and preserved. Residents will have a nice clean, safe community to live in.

3177.description: Requested funds provide 2-year start-up investments and seed money to build the infrastructure needed to expand nursing education, enhance simulation and clinical training, strengthen NCLEX support, and build on our already high retention rates. These investments establish essential leadership and innovative learning tools, enabling JU to scale programs and produce more practice-ready nurses who stay in the workforce.
3177.purpose: Requested funds provide 2-year start-up investments and seed money to build the infrastructure needed to expand nursing education, enhance simulation and clinical training, strengthen NCLEX support, and build on our already high retention rates. These investments establish essential leadership and innovative learning tools, enabling JU to scale programs and produce more practice-ready nurses who stay in the workforce.
3177.activities: JU will use these funds to strengthen Florida’s nursing workforce through targeted educational and clinical training activities. Investments include expanding simulation capacity, hiring additional simulation staff, and increasing inter- professional training to enhance clinical readiness. JU will launch a new NCLEX Success Center, expand faculty development, and provide more robust student support to improve licensure outcomes. Funds will also support instructional design and AI specialists to
3177.direct_services: Graduates from JU's accelerated nursing programs will provide direct health care and treatment to the citizens of Florida from traditional floor nurses, to virtual nurses and within critical areas of high need including, palliative care, rehabilitative care and cancer care and will retain at the bedside at a higher rate than other programs in the State of Florida.
3177.population: The citizen's of Florida will be the ultimate beneficiaries of the program and would number in the tens of thousands.
3177.outcome: This project is expected to increase the number of practice-ready nurses, raise NCLEX pass rates, and strengthen bedside retention, directly improving workforce stability and staffing ratios. Outcomes will be measured through NCLEX pass and program completion rates compared to Florida and national averages, along with robust multi-year retention tracking. Bedside retention will be evaluated at 1, 2, and 3 years, building on JU’s proven results: Mayo Clinic cohorts retain at 100% and 72%, and Baptist Health cohorts range from 70% at three years to 100% at one year. These metrics demonstrate long-term workforce impact. Workforce improvements will also be assessed through partner- reported staf

3481.description: To address a critical shortfall in resources necessary for the care of forensic mental health patients in the state of Florida. Ensuring continued access to essential services including psychiatric evaluation, treatment, and secure housing for individuals who have been court-ordered to receive mental health services due to involvement with the criminal justice systems. Maintaining staffing levels, meeting regulatory standards and upholding the safety and well-being of both patients and staff.
3481.purpose: To address a critical shortfall in resources necessary for the care of forensic mental health patients in the state of Florida. Ensuring continued access to essential services including psychiatric evaluation, treatment, and secure housing for individuals who have been court-ordered to receive mental health services due to involvement with the criminal justice systems. Maintaining staffing levels, meeting regulatory standards and upholding the safety and well- being of both patients and staff.
3481.activities: 24-hour 7-days per week supervision, psychiatric mental health services, educational substance abuse programs and progress groups, medication management, supportive, therapeutic, enrichment, and companion services, activities of daily living, independent living skills services (assistance with ambulation, bathing, dressing, eating, and grooming)
3481.direct_services: 24-hour, 7-days per week supervision, psychiatric mental health services, educational substance abuse programs and progress groups, medication management, supportive, therapeutic, enrichment, and companion services, activities of daily living, independent living skills services (assistance with ambulation, bathing, dressing, eating, and grooming)
3481.population: Elderly persons, Persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, homeless, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, current or formally incarcerated persons, drug offenders in criminal justice, victims of crime, adult individuals legally represented by a court appointed public guardian, severe mental illness
3481.outcome: Addressing a critical shortfall in resources necessary for the care of forensic mental health patients, Ensuring continued access to essential mental health services. Methodology will be the documented number of fully funded placements.

2950.description: Resiliency education curriculum and wellness platform designed by educators, for charter school students, in accordance with Florida standards. Alaia has taken the State of Florida Resiliency Education Standards and created research-backed lessons that foster character development, emotional, physical, and mental well-being, and proactive problem-solving skills.
2950.purpose: The requested funds will bring resiliency education, wellness practices, and character development to charter school students across the state. Our educator-curated wellness platform enhances social-emotional learning and mental health support, ensuring successful academic performances. By equipping students with essential tools for growth, Alaia fosters resilience, whole-person well-being, and success both in and out of the classroom.
2950.activities: Students will enroll in the program and access the structured curriculum focused on resilience and wellness. Through our interactive platform, they will engage in guided exercises, reflections, and skill-building lessons. Schools will track participation, engagement, and outcomes using built-in analytics.
2950.direct_services: Resiliency education curriculum with hundreds of lessons rooted in national and state standards, wellness, happiness, sleep and physical activity tracking methods.
2950.population: Charter school students of the state, this can include persons with poor mental health, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, currently or formerly incarcerated persons.
2950.outcome: Improved mental health, improved physical health, improved quality of education, and improved development of emotional regulation strategies. All of these outcomes lead to improved academic performance and overall personal development. By engaging in structured wellness practices and character-building exercises, students will develop healthier coping mechanisms, habits, increased self-awareness, and stronger interpersonal skills. Our program will track student participation and progress through our curriculum as well as the platform’s analytics.

3096.description: The Youth Summer, Camera, Action! program requests $150,000 to deliver an affordable, creative, and educational summer experience for children and families across Central Florida. This initiative ensures that young people — regardless of income — have access to safe, structured, and enriching activities during the summer months. The program blends creativity, education, and personal growth, offering workshops and activities in acting, arts and crafts, sports, reading, music, and environmental science. Through these experiences, children learn teamwork, problem-solving, and civic awareness — all while having fun in a nurturing and inclusive environment. Under the guidance of trained mentors and educators, participants will develop self-confidence, leadership, and a sense of community responsibility. The program also provides opportunities for youth mentors and junior counselors to gain pa
3096.purpose: The funds requested will support “Summer Camera Action,” a youth-centered summer program designed to provide hands-on training in film, photography, digital media production, and storytelling. The primary goal of this project is to empower young people through creative education, equipping them with technical skills, artistic expression, and workforce readiness tools that prepare them for future careers in Florida’s growing film and digital media industries.
3096.activities: Film and Media Workshops: Instruction in camera operation, lighting, editing, scriptwriting, and production. Project-Based Learning: Youth will produce short films, documentaries, and digital content reflecting their communities. Career Exploration: Guest speakers and field trips to local studios and media companies. Life & Workforce Skills: Communication, teamwork, and leadership training. Showcase Event: Public screening and exhibition of student work to celebrate achievement and community eng
3096.direct_services: Meal assistance during program days. Certificates of completion All services are directly delivered to participating youth and their families, with community members benefiting from the final public showcase.
3096.population: Target Population: Youth ages 6–15 from low- to moderate-income families, with a focus on at-risk and underrepresented populations in media and the arts. Projected Participation: Approximately 120 youth participants per summer session
3096.outcome: Increased youth engagement in positive, skill-building summer activities. Strengthened community pride Reduced risk of summer learning loss and juvenile delinquency. Methodology: Pre- and post-program surveys assessing skill gains, confidence, and engagement. Attendance and completion rates. Community feedback surveys from parents and attendees of public showcases

3323.description: The signalization upgrade project along Tamarind Avenue from Fern Street to Banyan Boulevard will install new traffic signals at Datura Road and at the Fern Street Extension Project. The newly installed traffic signals will be equipped with video detection systems and fiber communications. This upgrade enables real-time monitoring, automated signal timing, and enhanced emergency coordination, improving daily traffic flow and hurricane evacuation capabilities. The project aligns with Smart Cities initiatives.
3323.purpose: The funds will modernize traffic signal infrastructure along Tamarind Avenue (Fern Street to Banyan Boulevard) by installing two new smart traffic signals equipped with video detection and fiber communications. This will enhance traffic management capabilities, improve emergency response coordination, and support efficient hurricane evacuation operations in alignment with Smart Cities technology standards.
3323.activities: The project will include: (1) procurement and installation of two traffic signal systems at Datura Road and Fern Street Extension; (2) integration of video detection technology for real-time traffic monitoring; (3) installation of fiber optic communications infrastructure; (4) programming and calibration of automated signal timing systems; and (5) integration with existing emergency management and traffic operations centers for coordinated response capabilities.
3323.direct_services: Citizens will receive improved traffic flow management reducing congestion and travel times along Tamarind Avenue, enhanced safety through responsive signal timing based on real-time conditions, faster emergency vehicle response through coordinated signal prioritization, and more efficient hurricane evacuation routing with remotely managed signal controls during emergencies.
3323.population: The target population includes all motorists, pedestrians, cyclists, and emergency responders utilizing Tamarind Avenue between Fern Street and Banyan Boulevard. Based on average daily traffic counts, the project is expected to serve approximately 17,000 vehicles per day along with residents in the surrounding neighborhoods who benefit from improved emergency access and evacuation capabilities.
3323.outcome: Expected outcomes include: reduced average travel time (measured through before/after travel time studies), decreased traffic congestion (measured by level of service analysis), improved emergency response times (tracked through fire/EMS dispatch data), and enhanced evacuation efficiency (measured through evacuation simulation modeling). Success metrics will include: signal coordination efficiency scores, reduction in intersection delay times, and emergency vehicle preemption activation frequency.

3065.organization: The School District of Palm Beach County
3065.description: The purpose is to enhance the student educational experience by providing access to innovative learning technologies, modernizing key learning environments, providing for culture building activities for students, teachers and staff, and offering diverse, enriching after school programs.
3065.purpose: The primary quantitative goal of this project is to expedite the transformation of Roosevelt Elementary from a C-Rated school to an A-rated school. In doing so, expected outcomes include filling approximately 300 surplus seats. The purpose is to enhance the student educational experience by providing access to innovative learning technologies, modernizing key learning environments, providing for culture building activities for students, teachers and staff, and offering diverse, enriching after s
3065.activities: Activities include the procurement and implementation of supplemental educational software/hardware, acquisition of modern furniture and technology for learning spaces (e.g. media center, communications studio, program spaces), school culture building activities, and the provision of diverse after school enrichment programs.
3065.direct_services: Enhanced student education experiences by providing access to innovative learning technologies, modernizing key learning environments, providing for culture building activities, and authoring diverse enriching after school programs.
3065.population: Approximately 400 economically disadvantaged and at-risk youth in grade school will be served.
3065.outcome: Enhance mental health and cultural experiences measured by surveys, attendance records, and behavioral assessments will provide quantitative and qualitative data, quantifying changes in cultural knowledge, engagement, and perspectives, surveys, cultural awareness metrics, and student reflections. Promotes education by offering an engaging, hands-on approach, measured by changes in student engagement and grades. It enables interactive, real-world learning experiences, fostering critical thinking and practical skills, measured by math, proficiency and reading literacy, increased enrollment rate, increased teacher engagement.

3514.description: Here's Help founded in 1969, and located in Miami Gardens, is a residential substance abuse facility for Juvenile and Adult males referred by DJJ and Drug Courts. It has provided services and education to thousands of otherwise incarcerated youth offenders. Request is for a multi-use building designed to expand Here's Help's vocational, educational, and treatment services. The building will provide: 1. Workforce Training Labs: Equipped for advanced trades including electrical, HVAC, and technology-focused certifications. 2.Multi-Purpose Classrooms: Construction, renovation, photography, and computer graphics. 3. Career & Transition Hub: Dedicated space for job readiness, employer partnerships, and placement programs
3514.purpose: This is a new construction project that will expand capacity and create new programs. - Workforce Demand: Florida faces a shortage of skilled workers in the construction and service trades. This project creates a direct pipeline of trained workers. - Public Safety Impact: Every youth diverted from DJJ or drug court into treatment and training represents cost savings in incarceration and a gain in workforce productivity.
3514.activities: Upon completion of construction, continuing to help residents recover from substance abuse through a transition to a preferred vocational training field such as Culinary certification, Handyman, Computer Tech, Computer Graphics, Photography, etc.
3514.direct_services: Therapeutic substance abuse treatment as well as educational / vocational courses that enhance the individual's ability to become a confident, skilled, independent, and productive man.
3514.population: Adolescents and young adult males. Thousands have completed the program successfully and we have a 82% success rate. We continue to assist all who are referred by the drug courts, DJJ, DCF and the criminal justice system. Our capacity for residential is 45.
3514.outcome: - Expansion of vocational programs. - Training and job placement -New public-private partnerships with employers in high-demand fields

3060.description: Florida Memorial University is seeking to enhance the current undergraduate degree offerings and campus resources for the Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, and Cybersecurity degrees. The establishment of the Artificial Intelligence Innovation Lab and Cybersecurity Operations Center will allow the university to expand the current research opportunities, establish certification pathways, and create workforce development opportunities. By augmenting the current offerings and resources within the Department of Computer Science and Technology, FMU will be better equipped to prepare students to enter Florida's technological and tech-adjacent workforce.
3060.purpose: The requested funding will be used to establish an AI Innovation Lab and Cybersecurity Operations Center at Florida Memorial University (FMU). The lab will be used to support current degree offerings in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, etc. Funding for this lab will be used to provide research opportunities in AI applications, establish certification pathways, and create workforce development opportunities. Funding will also be used to upgrade the university's cyber infrastructure.
3060.activities: FMU will develop and implement a series of academic and research initiatives to strengthen AI and cybersecurity pathways for students. Students will gain hands-on training using advanced technologies while faculty and staff develop comprehensive, AI-focused curriculum. Additionally, updates to the cybersecurity infrastructure will provide continuous network monitoring and cyberattack responses.
3060.direct_services: Outdated academic programs will be upgraded to meet current industry standards, providing students with useful workforce readiness opportunities. Upgrades to current cyber infrastructure will safeguard vital university information. The expansion of research and academic initiatives will enhance FMU's ability to attract, recruit, and retain top-tier faculty and staff in STEM fields.
3060.population: The target population of this project will largely include university students. It is projected that the project will serve about 400 to 800 students.
3060.outcome: There are several expected benefits or outcomes of the establishment of the lab which include, but are not limited to, the improvement of education quality The quality of education will significantly increase following the expansion of research opportunities, degree and certification offerings, and more. This method will be determined by enrollment changes in the applicable degree fields.

3396.organization: Circle of Love Empowers Women And Girls,
3396.description: To expand the youth of Valor Empowerment (YOVE) after school program by providing mentorship and STEM services to over 50 undeserved high school girls at two different program sites in Miami-Dade County. Funding will support safe and reliable transportation to attend weekly mentorship sessions, educational field trips, and STEM Enrichment activities in collaboration with Miami-Dade College North Campus. In addition funds will help to provide custom uniforms, transportations and will celebrate the girls as they graduate from high schools and moving forward to college or a career.

With your support, we can expand our current Emergency Operations Center to meet today's and tomorrow's activations.

No Dedicated Training/Classroom Space: One of the most pressing gaps

3353.description: To provide Palm Beach County, the tenth-largest school district in the United States, with a much-needed state-of-the- art Holocaust and Jewish Cultural Center in the heart of County in West Palm Beach. This center will offer essential resources to educate K–12 teachers, students and the public about the Holocaust and human rights, supporting Florida’s Holocaust education mandate. Its mission is to inspire citizens to stand against hatred and uphold human dignity.
3353.purpose: Permanent Museum facility with artifacts and culture

3353.outcome: The Holocaust Museum will serve as a vital educational resource and a center for community engagement, benefiting teachers, students, and the wider community. By fostering education, the museum will play a crucial role in combating ignorance & hate.

3515.description: This project transforms Florida's Good Dad Act (HB 775, 2023) from legislation into direct community impact by supporting fathers in the State of Florida. The initiative addresses barriers that prevent unmarried and low-income fathers from: exercising newly recognized parental rights, navigating the family-court system, stabilizing income and housing, rebuilding credit, and reducing debt. The project strengthens families, reduces repeat court involvement, and increases economic self-sufficiency.
3515.purpose: 600 fathers complete Good Dad Act Rights 101 (80% knowledge gain), 400 individualized navigation plans (60% improved co-parenting outcomes), 450 complete financial literacy (65% credit score improvement), 300 enroll in workforce training (200 credentials; 150 job placements)
3515.activities: Online Counseling and Weekly Group Sessions, In-person meeting and educational sessions, Peer Groups, Counseling, Father Child Sessions at Schools, Online Job search portal access, Online classes and Credentials; Individual Counseling
3515.direct_services: Individual Counseling (telephone, zoom, Google Meet in person), Online Counseling and Weekly Group Sessions, In person Meeting and educational sessions, Financial Literacy Sessions, workforce development, Peer Groups, Counseling, Father-Child Sessions at Schools, Online Job search portal access, Online classes and Credentials, Individual Counseling
3515.population: 600 fathers/caregivers served directly (Year 1); 900 children and 200 co-parents benefit indirectly.
3515.outcome: Advances Florida's commitment to strong families, workforce development, and financial literacy by implementing the Good Dad Act's intent through direct community engagement. Reduces public costs and strengthens economic self-sufficiency across Florida families. Outcomes will be measured by surveys and questionnaires of participants.

3405.description: The purpose of this project is to offer immediate access to direct clinical services in a brief intervention application, as well as the provision of a prevention-focused education program for parents and caregivers to acquire skill-based strategies through education, consultation, and ongoing support from experienced clinicians. Funding from the legislature to provide specialized behavioral health intervention and prevention services for children and adolescents will ensure immediate access to appropriate care, which can lead to significant savings of more costly services in the long run, reduction of recidivism, and an offer an essential step in ensuring the success and well-being of Florida's future.
3405.purpose: The purpose of this project is to provide specialized therapeutic services for youth with complex mental health needs. Immediate access to brief intervention/prevention-focused support will equip caregivers to address complex needs such as dual diagnosis of developmental disabilities and mental illness, and/or sexual exploitation. This project will ensure access to appropriate care, stabilize families, reduce recidivism, and promote the success and well-being of Florida’s future.
3405.activities: Activities and services will include professional training and clinical supervision, development of education curriculum and design, therapeutic consultation and support, and community outreach to promote access to care and collaboration. Direct services will include therapeutic case management and specialized clinical services, including therapeutic and behavioral consultation.
3405.direct_services: Services to be provided include direct clinical services, training and education, therapeutic consultation and support, and outreach with partner agencies and organizations to coordinate care for youth and families. Services made available through this project will promote safety and well-being, and enhance the quality of life for hundreds of youth with complex needs.
3405.population: The majority of the funds requested will serve target populations in support of persons with poor mental health, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, developmentally disabled, preschool/grade school/high school students, university/college students, victims of crime. Approximately 200-400 individuals are expected to be served through this project.
3405.outcome: As a result of the services provided through this project, clinical symptoms will demonstrate improvement, indicating improved mental health. A battery of clinical assessments will be utilized to track trauma-related symptoms pre and post treatment. Prevention and awareness activities, community education, and parent and caregiver support will be provided to inform the public about the vulnerability of youth with complex needs and strategies to protect and prevent harm. This project will include measurement of satisfaction survey and feedback regarding efficacy of prevention training and/or consultation and support.

3070.description: Omega Lamplighters are requesting funding to expand their year round youth mentorship program, a statewide initiative that strengthens academic pathways, improves life skills, and reduces crime committed by at-risk youth in Florida's urban core communities. Funds will be used to provide structured in-school and afterschool mentorship focused on literacy, math, and STEM readiness for students in grades 4–12, including enrichment workshops, college and career exploration, digital learning tools, and mental health supports in Duval, Escambia, Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Palm Beach, and Pinellas Counties.
3070.purpose: Primary goal of our program is to reduce the risk of youth involvement in crime and delinquency. Our year-round, statewide effort improves academic performance, support in-school and afterschool life-skills, literacy, math and STEM-focused programming that strengthens careers and college pathways for students in grades 4-12 living in Florida's urban core.
3070.activities: Expand existing in- and afterschool math and literacy mentorship programs like small-group tutoring in reading, phonics and math. Strengthening academic and pathways through expanded STEM partnerships, deepen life-skills and evidence-based mentorship to reduce crime and delinquency, and significantly improve literacy outcomes through structured, data-driven programs aligned with local school district and Department of Education priorities.
3070.direct_services: This appropriation will provide direct, face-to-face mentorship and academic support services to at-risk students in grades 4–12 living in Florida’s urban core communities. Youth will receive structured afterschool and in-school programming that delivers small-group tutoring in reading and math, STEM-focused enrichment, and ongoing life-skills coaching designed to keep them in school, improve acad
3070.population: The target population for this project is at-risk youth in grades 4–12 from low-income, high-crime urban core communities in Florida, including students who are economically disadvantaged, academically behind in reading and math, or at increased risk of gang involvement and delinquency. The program is expected to directly serve at least 800 students annually across the participating counties.
3070.outcome: The expected benefits of this project are to provide mentorship and enrichment to at-risk youth in school, raise their reading and math performance, and reduce crime and delinquency among program participants throughout Florida. Outcomes will be measured using school and program data, including changes in grades and standardized test performance, attendance and behavior records, high school graduation and postsecondary enrollment rates, and reductions in disciplinary referrals.
