3748.description: This project is a transformational investment in Florida’s Heartland that will preserve historic assets, stimulate private- sector economic activity, and create a lasting community impact in Hardee County and the region at large. Funding will continue existing efforts and specifically allow for the restoration and adaptive reuse of four historic and long-vacant buildings in downtown Wauchula, construction of a public parking lot to support increased activity, and the rehabilitation of an underutilized alleyway through the integration of public art and cultural programming.
3748.purpose: Funding will be used for the restoration and adaptive reuse of four historic and long-vacant buildings in downtown Wauchula, the construction of a public parking lot to support increased activity, and the restoration of an underutilized but vital alleyway. This activity will include: restoration of the East Main Collective, renovation of 122 West Main Street, and preservation of a currently vacant and blighted property.
3748.activities: Collectively, this appropriation will result in four market-ready commercial spaces, bringing new businesses, jobs, and foot traffic to downtown Wauchula. Improvements to parking and the addition of arts and placemaking elements in an alleyway will enhance walkability, support tourism, and create a sense of place that encourages both residents and visitors to engage with their local economy.
3748.direct_services: In addition to preserving important cultural spaces in Florida's Heartland and supporting the local economy in general, completion of this project will result in a vibrant space designed to support small businesses and entrepreneurs. Additionally, in partnership with South Florida State College, the project will launch an incubator initiative to locate and support the College’s culinary program wi
3748.population: All residents in Hardee County are expected to benefit from the completion of this project. Hardee County has a population of 26,068 according to census estimates current as of July 1, 2024.
3748.outcome: Collectively, this appropriation will result in four market-ready commercial spaces, bringing new businesses, jobs, and foot traffic to downtown Wauchula. Improvements to parking and the addition of arts and placemaking elements in an alleyway will enhance walkability, support tourism, and create a sense of place that encourages both residents and visitors to engage with downtown. Performance will be measured against local employment data, annual tourism numbers, and/or additional generated tax revenue.

3722.description: The BAF, based in Pensacola, FL is a 501(c)3, nonprofit organization. The Board of Directors is comprised primarily of former Blue Angels whose mission is to support the wounded warrior community in Florida and across the Nation. The BAF mission is to support wounded veterans by providing funding for critical services and access to the best care available as they transition back to civilian life with a focus on PTS treatment, suicide prevention and transitional housing. The BAF seeks to support veterans and their families and provide hope for the bright future they deserve.
3722.purpose: The funds requested will be used to support veterans and their families by providing access to critical care for PTS treatment and health/wellness services through our partner organization in Florida as well as capacity building support for the BAF to ensure future growth and resources for the veteran community. The level of funding requested will support 40 to 120 wounded warriors. The BAF believes this is possible with continued support through public and private partnerships.
3722.activities: Wounded warriors enrolling in the in-patient and out-patient programs provided by our partner organizations will receive evidence based treatment services for themselves and their families at no cost to them.
3722.direct_services: The program integrates evidence based psychological and pharmacological treatments, rehabilitative medicine, wellness, nutrition, mindfulness training, and family support with the aim of helping veterans thrive, not just survive. In addition, the programs are committed to serving family members with couples and family counseling.
3722.population: The target population served is the wounded warrior community from all branches of service. Florida has the second- largest veteran population in the U.S. Since 9/11, over 52,000 service members have been wounded in action, with more than 1,700 major limb amputations. An estimated 500,000 are affected by traumatic brain injuries and/or post- traumatic stress. The appropriation funding will support 40 -120 wounded warriors in Florida and create opportunity for the BAF to grow. Some warriors and t
3722.outcome: The BAF mission is to SAVE LIVES. Wounded warriors have given their all to preserve and protect our freedoms. Thousands have come home with physical injuries and the invisible wounds of war we call PTS. In resolving PTS and other traumas, these veterans find hope and purpose. Many tell us "This program saved my life." The benefits and outcomes are these funds raise awareness, provide treatment and save lives.

3807.description: The requested funds will support the redevelopment and expansion of the Arts Center, a tourism cornerstone of St. Petersburg's cultural landscape for over a century. The goal of this project is to construct a new, state-of-the-art facility at 719 Central Avenue that will integrate the internationally recognized Chihuly Collection, presented by the Arts Center, currently located across the street, into a single, cohesive campus. This redevelopment will transform the Arts Center into a premier regional hub for the arts.
3807.purpose: The funds requested will support the redevelopment and expansion of the Arts Center, including the integration of the Chihuly Collection into a single, state-of-the-art facility. The goal is to enhance public access to world-class art, expand arts education and community programming, strengthen cultural tourism, and generate lasting economic and social benefits for Pinellas County and the State of Florida.
3807.activities: The funds will support construction of a state-of-the-art facility that provides direct services to the public, including expanded gallery and exhibition space with the integrated Chihuly Collection, arts education programs and workshops for all ages, community events, and arts access for local artists, fostering cultural engagement, learning, and economic impact.
3807.direct_services: The appropriation will provide citizens with expanded access to world-class art and exhibitions, including the integrated Chihuly Collection, arts education programs and workshops for children, teens, and adults, community events, and public access to artists and art enthusiasts, fostering creativity, learning, and cultural engagement for all residents and visitors.
3807.population: The target population includes residents of St. Petersburg, Pinellas County, and the broader Tampa Bay region, as well as domestic and international visitors. Programs and exhibitions will serve all ages and backgrounds, including children, teens, adults, seniors, and underserved populations. The redeveloped Morean Arts Center is expected to serve over 200,000 visitors annually, with significant increases in attendance from new and repeat audiences.
3807.outcome: Expected Benefit or Outcome: The project will enhance cultural access, arts education, and community engagement, while increasing tourism, creating jobs, and generating measurable economic impact. It will improve mental well-being, foster creative expression, and strengthen the Morean Arts Center as a regional cultural hub. Methodology for Measurement: Outcomes will be measured using attendance tracking, ticket and program participation data, and pre- and post-program surveys. Mental well-being will be assessed through the UCL Museum Wellbeing Measure, and economic impact will be quantified via visitor spending surveys and comparisons to projections from the independent Economic Impact Study

3710.description: Provides funding to FDLE to implement a wastewater narcotics testing and analysis program to assist law enforcement in combatting drug manufacturing and trafficking and other contaminants using wastewater analysis. By using this program, law enforcement will receive real-time block-level intelligence at both the macro and micro levels to enhance surveillance efforts and support probable cause determinations for search warrants.
3710.purpose: This wastewater testing program will provide concrete, location-specific evidence of narcotics activity in communities to inform surveillance of drug manufacturing and trafficking operations. These insights help law enforcement agencies quantify the presence of opioid compounds, establish probable cause for search warrants and further improve resource allocation.
3710.activities: This funding will assist law enforcement in analyzing wastewater to quantify the presence of opioid compounds and provide precise, data-driven strategies for resource allocation and interventions. By utilizing wastewater data, law enforcement can refine efforts to combat narcotics manufacturing and trafficking in Florida.
3710.direct_services: The direct services provided to citizens would be public safety oriented. Citizens would not directly interact with this grant program, but they would receive the benefits of earlier detection of dangerous drugs, improved community safety, and population-level surveillance that improves public safety without monitoring individuals.
3710.population: Statewide law enforcement narcotics investigation and interdiction activities.
3710.outcome: Wastewater analysis provides a near-real time snapshot of narcotics manufacturing or substances, which enables law enforcement officers to identify unseen drug trends and respond proactively and with efficiency. Opioid and drug use is measured on an estimated per capita use.

3788.description: Comprehensive cybersecurity project to fortify our information security posture. This initiative encompasses a strategic integration of hardware and software tools, access controls, advanced threat detection, and a robust recovery framework.
3788.purpose: In response to the escalating cyber threats in today's digital landscape, our city is embarking on a comprehensive cybersecurity project to fortify our information security posture. This initiative encompasses a strategic integration of hardware and software tools, access controls, advanced threat detection, and a robust recovery framework. By combining strategies our goal is to create a robust, resilient, and adaptive environment for municipal government security.
3788.activities: Increased security due to completion of identified cybersecurity objectives. Physical (firewall, access control), software (data backup, offsite hosting).
3788.direct_services: Organizational backing of the governing body of the city.
3788.population: Citywide (all residents, visitors, and staff). Approximately 12,000 residents.
3788.outcome: Protect city residents, staff, and city infrastructure from cyber threats. The measurement would be the number of cybercrimes committed within the city using city resources or city information gleaned from unsecure city systems. IT professionals have access to such information and can measure based upon that and the audit logging. Also, rigorous penetration testing that identifies risk and subsequently mitigates the said risk, is a tangible metric.

Legislative funding ensures vulnerable youth receive education, mental health, and recovery services in a therapeutic, emotionally safe environment that empowers them to succeed in school, in recovery, and in life.

3725.description: Funds will be used to purchase property along Carpenter Creek for stream and wetland floodplain restoration projects that have been identified in the Carpenter Creek / Bayou Texar Watershed Management Plan. Over $6,000,000 in additional grant funds has already been allocated for construction of the stream and floodplain restoration projects. This project will reduce downstream flooding, improve water quality in impaired waters, improve riparian and aquatic habitat, improve community resilience, and increase recreational opportunities for citizens and tourists.
3725.purpose: Purchase property along Carpenter Creek so that $6,000,000 in additional grant funds can be used to construct environmental restoration projects to reduce downstream flooding, improve water quality in impaired waters, improve riparian and aquatic habitat, improve community resilience, and increase recreational opportunities for citizens and tourists.
3725.activities: State of Florida and Escambia County purchasing protocols will be followed for the property acquisition process. Two appraisals will be performed for the parcels to be purchased.
3725.direct_services: After property acquisition, $6,000,000 in allocated grant funds will be used to construct environmental restoration projects to reduce downstream flooding, improve water quality in impaired waters, improve riparian and aquatic habitat, improve community resilience, and increase recreational opportunities for citizens and tourists.
3725.population: Target populations to be served by this project include citizens of Escambia County and tourists who enjoy healthy natural resources and recreational opportunities such as fishing, swimming, and kayaking along Carpenter Creek and Bayou Texar. 50,000 individuals per year are expected to be served and enjoy the natural resources and recreational benefits of this project.
3725.outcome: Outcomes of this project include reduction in downstream flooding, improvement of water quality in impaired waters, improvement of riparian and aquatic habitat, improvement of community resilience, and increased recreational opportunities for citizens and tourists. Outcomes will be measured by quantifying reduced downstream flooding events, measuring improvements in water quality (fecal coliform bacteria and nutrients), and quantifying utilization by citizens and tourists.

3719.description: The MIMOSAS (MicroRNA-Mediated Obstruction of Stem-loop Alternative Splicing) Program, is a novel therapeutic intervention targeting Alzheimer's disease. This one-year grant supports development of the MIMOSAS platform, which seeks to modulate the gene expression associated with Alzheimer's disease to restore healthy neurological function.
3719.purpose: Alzheimer's disease is a significant driver of healthcare and long—term costs in Florida. By targeting the neurotoxic Tau at the molecular level to restore healthy protein function, the MIMOSAS platform aims to slow or halt disease progression, with potential to reduce future state expenditures related to Medicaid, assisted living, and long-term care services.
3719.activities: Research for Alzheimer's. Therapeutic intervention targeting Alzheimer's disease.
3719.outcome: The expected outcome is reliefs for patients with Alzheimer's disease.

The program convenes employer collaboratives and supports them through the six TPM strategies: organizing for employer leadership, projecting demand for critical jobs, analyzing talent supply, building talent supply chains with preferred providers, managing performance using shared measures, and continuous improvement. In Southwest Florida, this project will launch and sustain employer collaboratives in priority industries, coordinate demand planning and supply- gap analysis, and facilitate employer-provider agreements that redesign or improve training pathways to increase placement, retention, and advancement. The result is a durable, scalable system for aligning education and training partners to verif
3747.purpose: Build and sustain employer-led talent pipelines in Southwest Florida by implementing the TPM framework—producing verified, employer-defined demand signals and translating them into education and training partnerships that improve placement, retention, advancement, and employer return on investment.

3747.population: Employers in priority industries facing shared, high-volume or high-impact hiring and retention challenges Education, training, and workforce partners that supply talent into targeted pathways. 3746.description: The goal is to bring a major Olympic qualifying event to the Central Florida area. The 2027 FIVB Women's Volleyball Championship is an international volleyball competition contested by the senior women's national teams of the members of Federation International de Volleyball (FIVB), the international governing body for all forms of volleyball. Held every 2 years starting in 2025, the event is the highest level and most significant volleyball event staged outside of the Olympics. The 2027 event is particularly relevant as it would be the first time the event is held in the United States; it would take place in the year prior to the LA28 Olympics when attention on Olympic sports is at an all-time high; and it would qualify the top three (3) finishing teams for the LA28 Olympics. The event
3746.purpose: Orlando would secure host city status for the 2027 FIVB Women's Volleyball World Championship. This opportunity would foster economic development and visitor spending in the state of Florida.
3746.activities: Orlando would provide necessary resources required for the successful hosting of matches tied to the 2027 FIVB
3746.direct_services: Orlando would have the opportunity to host and welcome the world's top international women's volleyball teams to the state of Florida as they compete at the highest level for the opportunity to compete in the LA28 Olympics.
3746.population: The total combined attendance for the 2027 FIVB Women's Volleyball World Championship is forecast at approximately 60,000 - 70,000, contingent on the final number of matches staged in Orlando. Approximately 65% of attendees are projected to be non-local, traveling from at least 50 miles outside of Orlando.
3746.outcome: The 2027 FIVB Women's Volleyball World Championship is projected to generate an economic impact of more than $15 million, contingent on the final number of matches staged in Orlando. The 2027 FIVB Women's Volleyball World Championship will support the state of Florida's tourism industry, while contributing to the benefit and enjoyment of its citizens.

Businesses are attracted to the area because of the drinking water and fire flow service infrastructure in the area. Businesses bring more opportunities for new jobs to community and surrounding areas. 3. Removal of Residential wells.

3755.description: The area was built in the 1960's and has not been improved ever since developed. These improvements are necessary in order to maintain the integrity of the area, and in particular will address an aging street and sidewalk infrastructure vulnerable to the harsh local environment. These vital right-of-way improvements (street, sidewalk, curb, gutters, and stormwater conveyances) will improve infrastructure for the betterment of the community and the environment.
3755.purpose: Upgrade aging public infrastructure to modern standards, improve stormwater drainage, pedestrian access, and community resiliency.
3755.activities: Repair and replace sidewalks, pavement, curb and gutter, and stormwater inlets; bid and manage construction.
3755.direct_services: Infrastructure improvements directly benefiting property owners and residents in the South Oldsmar neighborhood.
3755.population: Elderly persons, persons with poor mental/physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantages persons, at risk youth, physically disabled persons, and students (Pre-K through college). Total served - 800 residents
3755.outcome: This project will improve stormwater drainage, reduce standing water, and enhance pedestrian and vehicle safety by upgrading sidewalks, curbs, and roadway surfaces. These infrastructure improvements will create safer, more accessible streets for residents and support healthier, walkable neighborhoods. Success will be measured by visibly reduced flooding and improved walk-ability and drive-ability after construction is completed.

3752.description: Homeless Shelter to be built on our property. The program will include homeless individuals checking in daily for showers, meals, clothing, toiletries, and a bed to sleep in each night. Shelter Workers will assist individuals with obtaining needed documents to obtain employment and housing and referring individuals that need detox or Recovery to the appropriate facilities for help. Shelter Workers will assist in referrals for free medical assistance, and mental health care. Shelter Workers will assist in referrals for free medical assistance, and mental health care. Shelter Workers will also assist individuals in finding employment.
3752.purpose: The specific purpose or goal is have a Homeless Shelter available to un-housed individuals and families in our area to have a safe place to sleep. There are currently no other homeless shelters within a 2-hour radius of our area. Also, to assist individuals and families with obtaining needed mental, medical, and drug rehabilitation treatment. To assist individuals needing detox or Rehab in getting the help they need. To assist in obtaining documents for employment and housing. The Shelters will
3752.activities: Shelter workers assist clients in referrals to the appropriate Agency or Businesses to get the help needed.
3752.direct_services: Our direct services will include food, clothing, showers, and a bed to sleep in at night. Staff will connect homeless clients to needed services.
3752.population: Homeless individuals and families and indigent individuals discharged from community hospitals.
3752.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of this project is to get homeless individuals and families off the streets and give them a safe place to shower, get food, and sleep while building trust in having a safe place to stay. We also expect to be able assist these individuals to get the help they need medically, mentally, and through helping them find employment and permanent housing. We will also direct individuals to drug rehabilitation resources when needed. Shelter Workers will document all referrals in our case files. The Shelter will also serve as a Severe Weather Shelter during inclement weather.

3785.description: This appropriation will complete the Central Florida Water Initiative's (s. 373.0465, F.S.) recommended Grove Land STA addressing the IRL freshwater discharges & expected freshwater deficit for Central Florida in 2040. This final appropriation completes the state's investment of $13m to date. https://aws.sjrwmd.com/CFWI/pdfs/CFWI_2020RWSP_FINAL_PlanDocRpt_12-10-2020.pdf (Page 75)
3785.purpose: Alternative water supply for the CFWI region, removal of excess water to tide in the Indian River Lagoon
3785.direct_services: Removal of excess water to tide in Indian River Lagoon
3785.population: East Coast Residents from Duval County down to Palm Beach County
3785.outcome: Alternative water supply for the CFWI region, removal of excess water to tide in the Indian River Lagoon

3757.description: The Citrus Center complex (buildings 3100 and 3200) has served as the home of the College's Emergency Medical Services (EMS) training program for the last 19 years. This building complex was constructed in 1996 and was built for a different purpose. The complex has undergone minor renovations to accommodate the spaces to its current purpose but has not been substantively modified since it was originally placed into service. The buildings are in need of substantive modernization to meet the modern training needs for today's first responders.
3757.purpose: Renovation of the Citrus Center complex (buildings 3100 and 3200), home of the College's Emergency Medical Services (EMS) training program. This building complex was constructed in 1996 and was built for a different purpose. The buildings are in need of substantive modernization to meet the modern training needs for today's first responders.
3757.activities: SFSC will expand Paramedic/EMS and Fire Science training by providing modern and efficient training facilities. By combining training, equipment storage, instructional, and staff spaces into one facility, student safety will be improved as they will not need to cross a busy thoroughfare when moving equipment and instructional supplies. Students will gain hands-on experience in life-saving procedures, patient care, and live-fire drills, building critical skills for public safety careers.
3757.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from highly trained Paramedic/EMS and fire professionals who respond with advanced skills in patient care, emergency services, and fire suppression. The training ensures a stronger, safer community by preparing graduates to provide critical lifesaving services in real-world emergencies.
3757.population: This project serves jobless persons, high school students, and university/college students. The number of individuals served would be in the hundreds.
3757.outcome: This project will improve physical health, education quality, and public safety by providing Paramedic/EMS and Fire students with modern and efficient training facilities. Graduates deliver rapid, skilled emergency care that saves lives and strengthens community well-being. Success measured through: improved emergency response times, increased job placement rates, higher certification exam success, enhanced retention rates, expanded community partnerships, and improved employer satisfaction surveys reflecting graduate preparedness.

3756.organization: Sherman Williams American Legion Hall Post
3756.description: Founded by Black WWII veterans excluded under Jim Crow, Post 188c became a vital hub for Delray Beach’s Black community. The 70-year-old building now faces serious structural and safety issues. With strong community support already committed, we seek state funding to restore this historic space so it can continue serving veterans, families, and community groups and preserve an essential piece of local heritage.
3756.purpose: The funds requested will be used to restore and stabilize the historic American Legion Post 188c building by addressing critical structural and safety deficiencies, bringing the facility into code compliance and improving accessibility, in order to preserve the site and ensure it can safely continue serving veterans and the surrounding community for generations to come.
3756.activities: The restored facility will be used to provide veterans’ support services, American Legion meetings, and community gatherings; host civic, educational, and youth programs; serve as a space for family and neighborhood events; and offer a safe, accessible location for outreach and assistance to veterans and residents in the surrounding community.
3756.direct_services: The appropriation project will directly provide citizens with access to a safe and accessible facility offering veterans’ assistance and support services, American Legion meetings, community and civic gatherings, educational and youth programs, and space for neighborhood events and outreach activities that serve local residents and veterans.
3756.population: The target population served by this project includes military veterans, their families, and residents of the surrounding Delray Beach community, with a particular focus on historically underserved populations. Once restored, American Legion Post 188c is expected to serve approximately several hundred individuals annually through veterans’ services, community meetings, civic events, and neighborhood programs.
3756.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is the preservation and continued operation of American Legion Post 188c as a safe, accessible, and fully functional facility for veterans and community use. This outcome will be measured by completion of the planned renovations, certification of code and safety compliance, restoration of full building occupancy, and documented increases in the number of veterans’ services, meetings, and community events hosted annually compared to pre-renovation levels.

3758.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3758.description: The Greater Hillsborough County Fairgrounds requests $4.2 million to build a new covered arena and grandstands. This project will enhance agricultural education, provide year-round space for youth and community events, improve accessibility and safety, and expand economic impact by attracting larger regional events. It creates a durable, versatile venue that strengthens our fair’s mission and benefits the entire community.
3758.purpose: The Greater Hillsborough County Fairgrounds requests $4.2 million to build a new covered arena and grandstands. This project will enhance agricultural education, provide year-round space for youth and community events, improve accessibility and safety, and expand economic impact by attracting larger regional events. It creates a durable, versatile venue that strengthens our fair’s mission and benefits the entire community.
3758.activities: The arena and grandstands will provide space for livestock shows, youth competitions, equestrian events, agricultural education, concerts, and community gatherings. With safe, ADA-accessible seating and weather protection, the venue will serve 4-H, FFA, schools, and regional events, supporting agriculture, youth development, and community engagement year-round.
3758.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with a safe, accessible, and weather-protected venue for livestock shows, youth competitions, agricultural education, equestrian events, concerts, and community festivals. These services promote learning, entertainment, and economic impact while fostering year-round community engagement.
3758.population: Target population for this project would include but not be limited to youth in Hillsborough counties and surrounding areas. This facility would be used for youth agricultural and educational events. The facility would also be used by those in Hillsborough County and surrounding counties for agricultural and equestrian events to serve as a general use and agricultural facility. In addition, the facility would be made available to the community to host community and agricultural events and functi
3758.outcome: The new arena will expand agricultural education by increasing youth participation in 4-H/FFA shows and programs by an estimated 30%, provide year-round space for school field trips and demonstrations, and allow more than 25,000 annual visitors to directly engage with agriculture, livestock, and educational exhibits. Outcomes will be measured through event attendance records, number of youth participants in 4-H/FFA programs, school field trip registrations, and surveys of visitors and exhibitors. Data will track growth in participation, educational engagement, and community use of the new arena and grandstands compared to prior years.

3764.organization: We Are All We Need, Inc.
3764.description: The Village System of Care delivers high-acuity, trauma-informed case management modeled after the Wraparound Process — an evidence-based framework recognized by SAMHSA and the National Wraparound Initiative. Designed for youth with complex, multi-system needs, this approach centers the child’s voice, builds trust with families, and coordinates services across education, justice, mental health, and community systems.
3764.purpose: Funds will be directly allocated to activities and services that - Reduce gaps and barriers for high acuity youth and families to receive proper support services - Increase mental & behavioral health screening prior to arrest or baker act - Prevent system involvement and/or further matriculation into dependency systems - Prevent Intervene or Divert participants from being arrested or re-arrested - Increase service and support infrastructure for promise/opportunity zones & BIPOC communities
3764.activities: Funds will directly provide and support: - High Acuity Case Management & Care Coordination by qualified and trained supports - LIFE Coaching & Skills development for youth, young adults and their families including caregivers - Capacity Building for grassroot programs and mentors - Street Outreach and Target Community Engagement
3764.direct_services: -Access to mental health screen prior to negative service triggers - Access to care coordination and qualified human support with lived experience - Access to virtual care, education and resources (Life skills training, Employment, Transition/Re-entry, Independent Living) - Behavioral Health Screening - Independent LIFE Plans - On-on-One & Group LIFE, Wellness & Resiliency Coaching - LIFE Skills E
3764.population: TVSOC will serve approximately 101 to 200 individuals with a target population as follows: - Youth ages 17 and under - Young adults ages 18-23 - Parents or Caregivers of enrolled youth - Youth & young adults exhibiting high risk behaviors; experiencing poverty, parent or sibling incarceration, system involvement, or chronic truancy
3764.outcome: Improve Mental Health: - Access to mental health screen prior to negative service triggers - Access to care coordination and qualified human support with lived experience - Access to virtual care, education and resources - Life skill training - Employment - Transition / Re-entry - Independent Living - Access to mental health screen prior to negative service triggers - Access to care coordination and qualified human support with lived experience Improve Quality of Education: 65% of enrolled participants will receive a completion certification in an offered education program - 80% of enrolled youth will receive GED or High school diploma Protect General Public from Harm: 65% of enrolled partic

3759.description: The Florida Department of Corrections will use funding to implement an enterprise browser to address critical operational and security challenges faced across its 143 facilities. Currently, FDC staff requires multiple security tools to access essential web-based applications for offender management, case tracking, medical records, educational programs, and inter-agency coordination. This creates workflow bottlenecks, increases IT support demands, and limits the effective deployment of emerging technologies like CLEO AI—the Department's artificial intelligence assistant for case management and operational support. The enterprise browser will provide a secure, policy-enforced web access solution to eliminate VPN dependencies while maintaining CJIS compliance and meeting stringent correctional security standards. Staff can seamlessly access approved state systems—including the Offender Base
3759.purpose: The requested funds will: enhance operational security by consolidating web access controls and eliminating VPN vulnerabilities across all 143 FDC facilities; enable secure CLEO AI deployment for predictive analytics, case management automation, and data-driven decision support without compromising sensitive offender information; reduce IT infrastructure costs by eliminating redundant security tools, VPN licensing, and associated maintenance expenses; improve staff productivity by providing seam
3759.activities: Platform Deployment: Enterprise Browser installation and configuration across 50+ correctional institutions, regional offices, and community supervision centers. Centralized Policy Management: Implementation of unified access control console enabling IT administrators to enforce consistent security policies, content filtering, and usage restrictions across all facilities. System Integration: Connection with existing FDC infrastructure including Offender Based Information System, electronic healt
3759.direct_services: Correctional Staff (15,000+ employees): Secure, streamlined access to case management tools, enabling faster incident response, improved offender supervision, and enhanced public safety outcomes. Staff will access critical systems without VPN delays, reducing time spent on technical issues and increasing focus on core correctional duties. Offenders (80,000+ under supervision): Controlled access to
3759.population: Primary Users: 15,000+ FDC staff members across 143 facilities including: Correctional officers conducting offender supervision and incident management; case managers coordinating rehabilitation programs and release planning; healthcare providers accessing electronic medical records and treatment protocols; administrative personnel managing facility operations and inter-agency coordination; and probation and parole officers supervising community-based offenders. Secondary Beneficiaries: 80,000+
3759.outcome: Primary outcomes: enhanced security and compliance; operational efficiency improvement; cost reduction; staff productivity enhancement; and improved service delivery. Baseline Establishment: Performance baselines will be documented during the first 90 days of implementation to enable accurate year-over-year comparison and outcome validation.

3793.description: Funds requested would go towards the restoration of reopening the Historic Harder Hall Hotel in Sebring, specifically major systems (electrical, life safety, plumbing). Closed since 1986, we have been renovating the resort for two years, having spent $15,000,000 and counting so far. One of the last great "pink lady" hotels in the state that has not been saved or demolished, its reopening would boost heritage tourism, create jobs, and create new tax revenue (bed, sales and property) in an economically challenged county.
3793.purpose: Restoration of major systems inside the Harder Hall Hotel (electrical, plumbing, and life safety) to aid in the reopening of a National Historic Register property in a economically depressed county. These funds will provide support to a project in which approximately $15,000,000 in private funds and counting has already been invested to save and reopen the historic resort, which was once slated for demolition.
3793.activities: Reopening of a National Historic Register property, the most iconic in Highlands County, as a destination for weddings, community gatherings, a hotel, and restaurant. It has been closed for 39 years, in which time the economy of Sebring and the County have struggled. Funds will be used for hiring of subcontractors to install new electrical, plumbing, and life safety systems) Approximately 200 new jobs will be created once opened, with the resort generating new full-time positions as well as new
3793.direct_services: Direct service will be safe, up to code, compliant electrical, plumbing, and life safety systems in the hotel, providing a place for heritage tourism, a grand community gathering place, and pride for the region. The hotel will provide jobs in hotel management, maintenance, groundskeeping, bellhop, housekeeping, bartending, restaurant staff, accounting, payroll, etc.. All jobs that are found in a r
3793.population: The reopening of this once grand hotel will bring tens of thousands of additional visitors yearly to the "heartland" of Florida, creating a massive economic impact in an economically disadvantaged County. It will also greatly benefit locals, as they will have restaurants, bar, lobby, pool, and event space to meet at, and will reduce the blight and stigma of an area that has had its most prominent building closed for 39 years. The Sebring and Highlands communities will also benefit from the resor
3793.outcome: The expected benefit of the project is to create jobs, preserve a National Register Historic asset, create tourism, boost a disadvantaged economy, and create pride in the Heartland region of Florida. Reopening the hotel, while replacing missing major systems will massively benefit all those in the surrounding areas. It will return the building to service, allowing another 100 years of residents to enjoy a building that was slated for demolition. The new bed tax, sales tax, and property tax created will boost local municipalities, and the tourism will help local businesses grow.

3763.description: To continue connecting an ever-growing community of veterans and their families, through a weekend of camaraderie and deep-sea fishing. Since most Veterans claim to miss the bond of brotherhood that serving in the armed forces forges, Hookin’ Veterans goal is to help them reconnect with other service members and re-establish this bond in an effort to combat the increase of veteran suicide. Our goal is too, and has been to partner with other non-profits to expand our wellness, mental health and resiliency.
3763.purpose: A five day all expense paid fishing excursion. Our goal is too, and has been to partner with other non-profits to expand our wellness, mental health and resiliency. We offer educational opportunities for the veteran to return home with knowledge regarding mental health resources and the skills to fish fresh water or salt water.
3763.activities: To connect to an ever-growing community of veterans and their families, through a weekend of camaraderie and deep-sea fishing. Since most Veterans claim to miss the bond of brotherhood that serving in the armed forces forges, Hookin’ Veterans goal is to help them reconnect with other service members and re-establish this bond in an effort to combat the increase of veteran suicide.
3763.direct_services: These services are for Veterans for the time being.
3763.outcome: Since most Veterans claim to miss the bond of brotherhood that serving in the armed forces forges, Hookin' Veterans goal is to help them reconnect with other service members and re-establish this bond in an effort to combat the increase of veteran suicide. Also teaching them adaptive sports skills to improve future opportunities of leisure or work.

3779.description: The Town previously received CDBG funding for much needed expansion of its potable water system. Due to unforeseen market conditions over the last couple of years, funding was exhausted before the project was completed according to the original Design. This request will allow for construction of remaining improvements, including ~1,620 linear feet of water main along Park Avenue, a vital corridor along the US Highway 231 evacuation route.
3779.purpose: Funds will be used to complete system-wide improvements to the Town's municipal water system, including the construction of ~1,620 linear feet of water main line along Park Avenue. The Town previously received CDBG funding for water system improvements, but recent market conditions left the vital Park Avenue expansion area under funded. The funds requested will allow for the completion of all originally planned improvements.
3779.activities: This is an infrastructure project. Funding will be used directly for the construction of improvements to the Town's water system, including ~1,620 linear feet of new water main line along Park Avenue.
3779.direct_services: This is an infrastructure project. These funds will improve and expand the Town's water system as a whole, benefiting nearly all of the Town's 484 residents.
3779.population: All residents within the Town of Alford will be positively impacted by the availability of adequate municipal water service. The Town's population is 484 according to the most recent Census data.
3779.outcome: The Town of Alford's municipal water system will be improved by the completion of this project. Additionally, expansion of water service along Park Avenue will allow for the better availability of infrastructure along the US 231 Evacuation Route. Benefits will be measured by year over year water customer increases, system performance, and maintenance costs.

3769.description: Pasco-Hernando State College (PHSC) seeks to renovate a former daycare on campus that is currently vacant to allow for a public-private partnership with a potential charter school. The initiative supports PHSC's mission as an approved higher education charter authorizer to establish campus-based or regionally-located charter schools. The program will enable proven, high-capacity charter operators with demonstrated student success to expand educational opportunities in Pasco and Hernando Counties, emphasizing dual enrollment, industry certifications, and postsecondary readiness.
3769.purpose: Funds support renovating an existing West Campus facility (former daycare) to create a charter school focused on grades 11-12. The college will establish infrastructure for a high-quality charter school and support proven charter operators in opening schools focused on early college pathways, STEM, health sciences, and workforce development, while increasing student access to dual enrollment, industry certifications, and postsecondary preparation in Pasco County.
3769.activities: Facilitation of coursework for grades 11-12, dual enrollment, and early college programming.
3769.direct_services: Students in Pasco County will receive access to high-quality charter schools with proven track records of success, early college opportunities in grades 11-12 with dual enrollment options, STEM, health sciences, and advanced manufacturing pathways, industry certifications and workforce preparation, college-prep education with demonstrated results, and alternative educational options for diverse st
3769.population: Initially the school will serve students with an emphasis on grades 11-12 for early college, students seeking STEM, health sciences, and workforce pathways, over-age, under-credited, or re-engaged youth, students in Pasco County seeking innovative educational options. The initial expected reach is 300-500 students.
3769.outcome: Benefits of this project will include increased student achievement as measured by state assessments, higher dual enrollment participation and college credit attainment, increased industry certification completion rates, improved high school graduation rates, enhanced college enrollment and persistence rates, measurable student success compared to district school peers. Measurements of these outcomes will include FSA results, dual enrollment credit hours, industry certification and job placement data.

3775.description: The Recovery to Reunification Program is a comprehensive, family-centered initiative designed to support parents and caregivers who are facing, or are at risk of, separation from their children due to mental health challenges and/or substance use disorders. The primary goal of the program is to promote healing, stability, and long-term recovery so families can safely reunite and remain together. This program provides integrated mental health and addiction treatment alongside parenting education, trauma-informed care, and case management services. Participants receive individualized treatment plans that address the underlying causes of substance use and mental health conditions while strengthening coping skills, emotional regulation, and healthy family dynamics. Recovery to Reunification emphasizes accountability, personal growth, and collaboration with child welfare agencies, courts, and
3775.purpose: The Recovery to Reunification Program aims to support safe and timely family reunification by providing comprehensive mental health and addiction treatment to parents and caregivers facing or at risk of separation from their children. The program focuses on stabilizing mental health symptoms, achieving sustained recovery, improving parenting skills, and strengthening family functioning. It works to reduce the risk of child removal and re-removal while promoting trauma-informed healing, accountab
3775.activities: Funds will be used to provide comprehensive, trauma-informed services that support recovery, family stability, and reunification. Activities and services will include clinical mental health treatment, substance use disorder treatment, and psychiatric evaluation with medication management. Participants will receive individual and group therapy, relapse prevention education, and coping-skills development. The program will also provide parenting education, family therapy, and reunification-focused
3775.direct_services: Licensed level 1 inpatient Res, patients receive a range of services, including individual and group therapy to address addiction and mental health issues, family therapy to improve communication and trust, and comprehensive substance abuse treatment. They also participate in life skills training for reintegration, receive case management.
3775.population: The target population for this project includes parents and caregivers living in rural areas who are facing, or are at risk of, separation from their children due to substance use disorders, mental health conditions, or co-occurring disorders. Many participants are involved with, or at risk of involvement with, the child welfare system, courts, or other social service systems and often experience limited access to behavioral health and family support services.
3775.outcome: The expected outcomes of this project include improved mental health, reduced substance use, increased parenting capacity, successful family reunification, and reduced recidivism, along with enhanced child safety and family stability. Outcomes will be measured using clinical screenings, including depression assessments (PHQ-9), suicide risk evaluations, trauma and PTSD screenings (ACE), substance use assessments (AUDIT, DAST, BAM), mental health evaluations, and functional/behavioral assessments, as well as treatment participation, reunification documentation, and reductions in crisis events, hospitalizations, and system involvement.

3770.description: NWFSC requests $3 million to create a Hospitality Training Program at the South Walton Center to meet local tourism workforce needs. Funds support hands-on equipment, industry certifications, and faculty for short-term training and pathways to certificates and degrees. The program creates a pipeline of skilled workers, reduces employer shortages, and requires no construction costs.
3770.purpose: The purpose of the program will be to address the workforce needs of the region's hospitality industry. Independent tourism and workforce reports show that Walton County's hospitality sector supports 40,000+ jobs and faces persistent staffing shortages, high turnover, and seasonality challenges. Third-party data clearly demonstrate the need for structured, industry-specific hospitality training in the county.
3770.activities: The program will offer hands-on hospitality and culinary training, industry certifications, short-term credentials, customer-service and operations instruction, employer upskilling, seasonal hiring boot camps, and pathways into NWFSC degree programs.
3770.direct_services: Citizens will gain job-focused hospitality and culinary training, certifications in guest services, front-desk, and event support. The program offers flexible schedules, hands-on equipment, employer connections, and clear pathways into NWFSC certificate, A.S., and bachelor programs.
3770.population: Walton County's hospitality industry affect over 40,000 jobs and the program will provide more training and employment opportunities.
3770.outcome: More trained workers entering hospitality roles and wage increases for certificate completions These can be measured by employer vacancy data and regional workforce reports.

3771.description: Northwest Florida State College seeks state funding to establish a comprehensive Career Services Center that will deliver career-oriented programs and support services designed to help students successfully transition from education to employment. A central component of the Center will be the development and launch of a Florida Postsecondary Comprehensive Transition Program (FPCTP) for students with unique abilities, ages 18–26. Funding will establish programming and services and will be used for construction or renovations.
3771.purpose: The funds will allow Northwest Florida State College to launch a Career Services Center and develop a Florida Postsecondary Comprehensive Transition Program (FPCTP) to support students with unique abilities as they prepare for employment and long-term career success. The project will establish staffing, program infrastructure, and resources needed to design, apply for, and implement an approved FPCTP while expanding career readiness services across the institution.
3771.activities: Activities include hiring a Director and Coordinator, developing and submitting the FPCTP application, attending required statewide FPCTP training and conferences, creating accessible academic and workforce training pathways, coordinating internships and experiential learning opportunities, building employer partnerships, and delivering individualized career readiness and job placement support.
3771.direct_services: Direct services include career counseling, academic and workforce readiness training, experiential learning opportunities, employer engagement, job placement assistance, and individualized support services for students with unique abilities transitioning into the workforce.
3771.population: The target population includes Northwest Florida State College students, and individuals in the College's service area with a specific focus on students with unique abilities between the ages of 18 and 26. Initial program development will support cohort-based enrollment as the FPCTP is approved and scaled.
3771.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved career readiness, increased workforce participation, successful completion of credentials, and job placement for students with unique abilities. Outcomes will be measured through enrollment, credential attainment, internship participation, job placement rates, and ongoing program performance reporting.

3767.description: This funding request seeks a multi-million-dollar investment by the State of Florida to establish a dedicated research program focused on Parkinson's and other neurodegenerative diseases. The program will position Florida as a national leader in biomedical innovation, attract top research talent, and stimulate high-paying biotech and healthcare jobs. By advancing scientific understanding and improving early diagnosis and treatment, this initiative will help Floridians live longer, healthier, and more independent lives—ultimately reducing the state's long-term healthcare and economic burden.
3767.purpose: The program will position Florida as a national leader in biomedical innovation, attract top research talent, and stimulate high-paying biotech and healthcare jobs.
3767.population: More than 70,000 people living with Parkinson's in Florida with the potential to impact treatments worldwide.

3776.description: This will be a joint undertaking including the Seminole Tribe of Florida and the Village of Indiantown. This project provides for the comprehensive historic restoration and rehabilitation of the Seminole Inn, a landmark structure constructed in 1925 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The project will restore the building to its original architectural character while upgrading the facility to meet current life-safety, building, and accessibility standards required for lawful occupancy and public use. The Seminole Museum will showcase priceless and irreplaceable Seminole Tribe artifacts. This funding initiative recognizes the Seminole Inn’s importance as a defining historic asset within the community and as a contributor to the Village’s heritage, identity, and economic vitality. The restored Seminole Inn will support public access and community engagement while safegu
3776.purpose: The funds requested will support the comprehensive restoration and rehabilitation of the historic Seminole Inn to ensure the facility meets current life-safety, building, and accessibility standards required for lawful occupancy. The project will preserve the Inn’s historic character while stabilizing the structure for long-term public use. This investment will safeguard a significant historic asset and support continued community benefit.
3776.activities: Activities funded through this request include structural rehabilitation, building systems upgrades, and preservation- compliant repairs necessary to restore the Seminole Inn and bring it into compliance with applicable life-safety, building, and accessibility standards. All work will be performed in accordance with historic preservation requirements to ensure the long-term stability and lawful occupancy of the facility.
3776.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with safe public access to a restored historic facility that meets current life-safety and accessibility standards. The preservation of the Seminole Inn will support community use, heritage appreciation, and local economic activity by ensuring the long-term availability of a significant historic asset within the Village of Indiantown.
3776.population: The target population includes residents of the Village of Indiantown, surrounding communities in Martin County, and visitors from across the State of Florida. As a historic property listed on the National Register of Historic Places, the Seminole Inn represents a heritage asset of statewide significance. While this specific project request is a fixed capital improvement and does not provide individual services, the restored facility is expected to serve thousands of Floridians and visitors annu
3776.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is the successful restoration of the Seminole Inn to a safe, code-compliant condition while preserving its historic integrity. The project will ensure the long-term viability of a significant historic asset and enable lawful public occupancy and use. Outcomes will be measured by completion of construction in accordance with approved plans, issuance of required certificates of occupancy, and verification that all applicable building and accessibility standards have been met.

3781.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3781.description: The proposed project is Phase 3 of the Arcadia All-Florida Championship Rodeo Mosaic Arena build plan. Phase 3 of the project includes a presentation area with kitchen amenities along with restrooms to accommodate patrons. The completion of the presentation area will open opportunities for speakers, presenters, and live demonstrations to be held in a local space. Trainings for continuing eduction credits in adults for agriculture licenses and youth agriculture leadership group meetings are examples of organizations that can utilize this area long term.
3781.purpose: The purpose of the Arcadia All-Florida Championship Rodeo expansion of a presentation area is to serve civil, community, and youth organizations to be able to host events that promote agriculture. As an economically disadvantaged and rural community this space will also provide an area for essential services and have a positive economic impact on Desoto County. It will be a centrally located area where learning and teaching can be conducted.
3781.activities: Partnering with various groups there can be educational and hands-on activities offered including youth agriculture workshops focusing on STEM activities and community focused education. The Arcadia All-Florida Championship Rodeo is dedicated to using the space for teaching and expanding the services to benefit Desoto County residents.
3781.direct_services: Citizens will have access to an area where groups in the community can meet or host events where digital media production equipment is needed or where kitchen amenities can be utilized. Another positive service this expansion could also provide is positive entertainment opportunities or learning experiences as presenting groups could now occupy this space and the rest of the Mosaic Arena.

3799.description: This is a request to revert and reappropriate funding for the same purpose. This funding will cover costs related to outfitting a specialized rescue transport vehicle with lifesaving equipment including water rescue dive equipment, marine technology, advanced life support equipment, a power load stretcher, and tow technology for personal watercraft. This is a request to revert and appropriate funding that was previously awarded, with a delay due to supply chain issues. The vehicle will be delivered in October 2026.

3799.outcome: Improved response times for marine rescue incidents, measured by length of time between call and actual response to scene

The return sludge pumping system—critical for regulating treatment biology and compliance parameters—has multiple failures. The chlorine gas disinfection system is failing to maintain charge and residual stability. 3797.purpose: Coordinated corrective action—equipment repairs, treatment process stabilization measures (including floating aeration equipment), laboratory monitoring capability, and chemical conversion work—is essential to maintain service, protect the environment, and avoid further incidents.

3796.description: Funds will support capital improvements to three (3) Guidance Care Center (GCC) facilities in Monroe County. The improvements involve updating flooring, replacing outdated and worn furniture, and building a professional-grade kitchen for food preparation and client culinary training. GCC aids thousands of Floridians yearly with quality behavioral health services. Proposed enhancements will enhance environment for those served, improve accessibility, and extend the facilities’ lifespan. GCC holds a significant position in a high-demand region of South Florida, delivering essential, trauma-focused, and evidence-based behavioral health care to individuals lacking resources and struggling with substance abuse or mental health disorders.

3800.description: The Madura Five Lift Station Rehabilitation will replace the 45 year old existing infrastructure and improve the stormwater management that impacts approximately 50 residential properties in a coastal, low-lying area.
3800.purpose: Funds will be utlized to update and replace the 45 year old existing infrastructure to improve the stormwater management in residential properties in a coastal, low-lying area.
3800.activities: Improvement of infrastructure to support residential areas.
3800.outcome: The benefit is a strengthening of infrastructure. Will help sustain infrastructure during weather storms and disasters.

3804.description: These funds would be used to create a makerspace in Lake County, as an outreach activity of the Nerds of Prey Robotics Team, with FIRST Robotics, through Lake Minneola High School. The funds would enable the team to secure a public space and purchase manufacturing equipment, computers, 3D printers, lasers, etc. which can be used to further the competitive robotics programs in Lake County and will serve as a community makerspace where lessons and workshops can be held.
